textes.Alors dis-lui cinq heures. Et qu'il se t: Then tell it five o'clock. And tell it to keep quiet.
Then tell it not to move.
Then explain to me why it itches.
textes.Alors ferme-les. Un seul, pour commencer: Then close them. Just one, to start with.
textes.Alors il faut savoir ce qui le fait batt: Then we need to know what makes it beat.
Then it was hiding in it.
textes.Alors je chanterai le premier. Deux fois: Then I'll sing the first one. Twice.
textes.Alors je chercherai seul. Comme un jagua: Then I'll search alone. Like a jaguar.
textes.Alors je collectionne les graines. Toute: So I collect seeds. All of them! Zéphyr brings me some from every island: from the jungle, from the elves, a dwarf cactus seed… I've got one thousand one hundred and eleven. I compare them to my shell, just in case. One day, I'll find the seed that looks like my hazelnut, and I'll know which tree I fell from.
textes.Alors je compte vite ! Un, deux, vingt-m: Then I'll count fast! One, two, twenty-thousand!
Then I'm going down. Don't fall asleep.
Then I'll dine at the fountain.
textes.Alors je joue doucement. Une demi-étoile: Then I'll play softly. Half a star.
Then I'll play slow, Ba Sidi.
Then I'll keep it for Nolwenn.
Then I'll save it for him.
textes.Alors je le lui ai recommandé. Chaudemen: So I recommended it to her. Warmly. “The finest novel of the year, madam. The captain, the florist, the storm in chapter twelve…” She went red as a tomato. Over a novel! I even told her the ending, to convince her. She said thank you in a tiny little voice. Mainland people are so emotional.
Then I'll keep them for my hair.
textes.Alors je les mets dans le prochain morce: Then I'll put them in the next track.
textes.Alors je lui laisse une lanterne. Pour l: Then I'll leave her a lantern. For the night.
Then I'm taking a stroll too. Twenty paces behind.
textes.Alors je me venge. Quand il pose ses cai: So I get my revenge. When he puts down his crates, I drop the price and shout: “FOR HAMID IT'S CHEAPER, THEY'VE HEARD HIS SONG!” The auction laughs. The next day, he came into port singing so loud that for a whole minute nobody heard my prices. A minute! We're even. Until tomorrow.
textes.Alors je monte la basse, Lulu. Pour là-h: Then I'll turn up the bass, Lulu. For up there.
Then I'll never drop anything for you again. Never!
textes.Alors je prépare une longue note. Au cas: Then I'll prepare a long note. Just in case.
Then I'm bringing in my beans.
textes.Alors je soigne la basse. C'est pour des: Then I'll take care with the bass. It's for royal ears.
textes.Alors je t'ai apporté une jolie pierre p: Then I brought you a pretty stone for nothing.
textes.Alors je tape plus fort aussi. Pauvre Lh: Then I'll drum louder too. Poor Lhoucine.
textes.Alors je te l'achète. Contre une questio: Then I'll buy it from you. For a question!
textes.Alors je te nourrirai couché. Comme l'hi: Then I'll feed you lying down. Like last winter.
Then I want to go there, to fairyland.
textes.Alors je viendrai le confettiser. Prudem: Then I'll come and confetti it. Carefully.
textes.Alors je viens les relâcher !: Then I'm coming to let them go!
textes.Alors joue « Marée Basse ». Les arbres l: Then play “Low Tide”. The trees like it.
textes.Alors la carte est juste. Tant mieux. Ne: Then the map is accurate. Good. Don't touch the centre.
Then the moon is a lucky moon.
textes.Alors la lune paiera son cacao elle-même: Then the moon can pay for her own cacao.
textes.Alors le courrier attendra. C'est un fai: Then the mail will wait. That's a fact too.
Then my keel's leaking, on the north side.
textes.Alors maintenant. Et ne chante pas le re: Then now. And don't sing the chorus.
Then eat standing up. But EAT.
textes.Alors mange vite, et personne ne m'enten: Then eat quickly, and nobody will hear me.
textes.Alors ne la fais pas trop attendre. Une: Then don't keep them waiting too long. A home that waits is a lantern kept lit: it burns its oil for you.
Then don't tell it; it was so touched.
textes.Alors nous sommes deux à le croire. Mais: Then there are two of us who believe it. But written doesn't mean legible. The runes always say it… a little crooked.
textes.Alors nous sommes deux à mal archiver no: Then there are two of us who archive our nights badly.
textes.Alors on se ressemble moins que je croya: Then we're less alike than I thought. Or more. One day you'll tell me what you see down there. I'll listen the way you listen to a song.
textes.Alors on échange ! Une grenouille contre: Then let's trade! One frog for three shells!
textes.Alors parle-lui. Dis-lui que c'est pour: Then talk to it. Tell it it's for your sister.
Then paint me a sky that washes out.
textes.Alors pourquoi Grignotte porte ton colli: Then why is Grignotte wearing your net collar?
textes.Alors pourquoi ai-je tant de clients ?: Then why do I have so many customers?
textes.Alors pourquoi il bat si fort quand elle: Then why does it beat so hard when she walks by?
textes.Alors pourquoi l'as-tu apportée ?: Then why did you bring it?
textes.Alors pourquoi tu les caches, ma fille ?: Then why are you hiding them, my girl?
textes.Alors prends deux pains : un pour aujour: Then take two loaves: one for today, one for courage.
textes.Alors prends le tabouret. Il t'attendait: Then take the stool. It was waiting for you.
textes.Alors prévenez le client. Il faudra fair: Then warn the guest. He'll have to make a wish!
textes.Alors préviens-le. Concert pour Tlaco !: Then tell him. Concert for Tlaco!
textes.Alors qui tient la clochette ?: Then who is holding the bell?
textes.Alors raconte-moi la fin, que je vérifie: Then tell me the ending, so I can check if you're cheating.
textes.Alors refrain au troisième temps. Comme: Then chorus on the third beat. As usual!
Then look outside your door tonight.
Then look at it for me, Ernest.
Then stay on the surface. For once.
textes.Alors réfléchis plus fort. Tlaco t'atten: Then think harder. Tlaco is waiting for you.
Then your show doesn't have an audience.
Then get it wrong loudly. I don't hear well.
textes.Alors tu aimeras le Bois-Doré. Là-bas, o: Then you'll love Bois-Doré. There, we walk ABOVE the trees, too.
textes.Alors tu as tout le temps de m'offrir un: Then you've got all the time in the world to buy me a coffee.
textes.Alors tu as un bon nez. Et ta grenouille: Then you've got a good nose. And your frog?
textes.Alors tu as vu ce que peu de gens voient: Then you've seen what few people see: the sky hesitating, just before Rê. Treasure that moment. It's the sweetest of the day.
So you arrived before you left.
textes.Alors tu es de ceux qui rêvent fort. C'e: Then you are one of those who dream strongly. That's how one finds the way to the clouds, you know. The mushroom is only a door; the dream is the key.
textes.Alors tu reviendras toujours quelque par: Then you'll always come back somewhere, that's good. But while you're here, the soup is me. And nobody turns down my soup.
textes.Alors tu sais ce que c'est, de regarder: Then you know what it is to gaze at the horizon in the morning. Remember to write to them. A letter is a drop that crosses the clouds.
textes.Alors tu seras le premier à les connaîtr: Then you'll be the first to get to know them! Look closely, listen closely, and taste Bobor's brioches closely. Then you'll tell them all about it back there.
textes.Alors un peu moins cher, pour les tilleu: Then a little cheaper, for the lime trees.
Then a little to the left. For elegance.
textes.Alors vole contre lui, Brindille. Comme: Then fly against it, Brindille. Like I taught you.
textes.Alors vous finirez bien par tomber sur l: Then you're bound to hit the right one eventually.
textes.Alors {qn} t'a raconté mes histoires ? J: So {qn} told you my stories? I hope {il} didn't tell you everything.
textes.Alors {qn} vous a raconté mes histoires: So {qn} told you my stories? I hope {il} didn't tell you everything.
textes.Alors, Brutus, ce collier pour ta fiancé: So, Brutus, how's that necklace for your sweetheart?
textes.Alors, Comète ? Qui paie les glaces ?: So, Comète? Who's paying for the ice creams?
textes.Alors, Fañch, les poissons sont bavards,: So, Fañch, are the fish chatty today?
textes.Alors, Lulu, tu reviens d'où, ce soir ?: So, Lulu, where are you back from tonight?
textes.Alors, Mathurin, combien de serpents ce: So, Mathurin, how many serpents tonight?
textes.Alors, Pépé, il pesait combien, ce matin: So, Grandpa, how much did your sea bass weigh this morning?
textes.Alors, Rachid, vendu au premier prix ?: So, Rachid, sold anything at the first price?
textes.Alors, ce lapin ? Il sort du trou, fait: So, that rabbit? Comes out of the hole, goes round the tree… You've been practising, I hope? Show me.
textes.Alors, ce nez qui ne sentait rien ? Je l: So, that nose that couldn't smell anything? I train it on every visit. Smell. … Better. Much better.
textes.Alors, ce tapis qui n'existe pas ?: So, this carpet that doesn't exist?
textes.Alors, ces pieds ? Au chaud ?: So, those feet? Nice and cosy?
textes.Alors, ces sardines au miel ?: So, how are those honey sardines?
textes.Alors, cette bulle, Basile ? Elle est pr: So, this bubble, Basile? Is it ready?
textes.Alors, cette machine pour voler ? Pensez: So, that flying machine? Think about the landing first. Achille will tell you, if he ever comes down.
textes.Alors, cette nuit, tu as volé ? Moi oui,: So, did you fly last night? I did, over the sea. I looked for you. It was very crowded.
textes.Alors, dis-moi franchement : le hamac, l: So, tell me honestly: the hammock, last time… did you sleep well?
textes.Alors, en pensée : PAF ! Confettisé ! Ro: Then, in spirit: BANG! Confetti'd! Pink, yellow, green, it's even down your collar. Come back to the stand, I'll fire you a real one. Free.
textes.Alors, franchement, entre nous, sans fla: So, honestly, between us, no flattery: what do you think of our little town?
textes.Alors, la voyante ? Ça mord, demain ?: So, seer? Will they bite tomorrow?
textes.Alors, le grand, toujours à forger pour: So, big'un, still forging for the tourists?
textes.Alors, le grand, toujours à taper trop f: So, big'un, still hitting too hard on the left?
textes.Alors, le tireur, tu as touché quelque c: So, shooter, hit anything since? Apart from Marcel's feet?
textes.Alors, le très-vite ? On verra ça sous l: So, Speedy? We'll see about that under the arches. I'll wait for you at the start. Well, I'll wait for you at the finish.
textes.Alors, ma championne, tu pointes ?: So, my champion, are you pointing?
textes.Alors, mon jeune confrère ? Du nouveau ?: So, my young colleague? Anything new?
textes.Alors, mon marchandeur ? Prêt à perdre,: Well, my haggler? Ready to lose today? My prices are hard as crystal.
textes.Alors, navigateur, on part quand ?: So, navigator, when do we set sail?
textes.Alors, petit ? Ta cabane tient debout ?: Well, kid? Your hut still standing?
textes.Alors, petit gars, ce poing ?: So, little lad, how's that fist?
textes.Alors, petit, et ces crabes ?: So, little one, how about those crabs?
textes.Alors, t'as trouvé ton endroit ? Moi, to: So, found your place yet? Mine's still the same. Shh.
textes.Alors, ta cabane ? Les planches en écail: So, your hut? Planks overlapping like scales, like I told you? The rain will thank you.
textes.Alors, tes fantômes verts ? Des lucioles: So, your green ghosts? Fireflies, I tell you.
textes.Alors, ton épée, elle t'a répondu ? Ma b: So, has your sword answered you yet? My boat hasn't either. Patience, sailor, patience.
textes.Alors, toujours des troncs ? Le mien a p: So, still tree trunks? Mine dived last night. Trunks don't dive, I'll remind you.
textes.Alors, tu as mangé, dormi, marché ? Renc: So, have you eaten, slept, walked? Met amazing people? I predicted it. I'm very good.
textes.Alors, tu as trouvé un nom pour ta lame: So, found a name for your blade? Not “Ouch”, eh. That one's taken.
textes.Alors, tu as écrit ? Non ? Mange d'abord: So, did you write? No? Eat first, write after. But write.
textes.Alors, tu l'as entendu, le petit boum ?: So, have you heard it, the little boom? The right place, I mean. I hear it every night.
textes.Alors, tu les as comptées, tes dents ? M: Tho, have you counted your teeth? Me, thith morning: one, two. Thtill two. Phew.
textes.Alors, tu nages toujours « un peu » ? So: So, still swimming “a bit”? Breathe slowly, I'm telling you. And stay where I can see you.
textes.Alors, tu nages un peu plus ? Moi je dis: So, swimming a bit more? I always say: a little is already better than… than nothing at all.
textes.Alors, tu sais maintenant qui t'attend ?: So, do you know now who's waiting for you? No? I knew, at your age. Keep looking.
textes.Alors, tu sais reconnaître un poisson fr: So, can you tell a fresh fish now? Recite: the eye, the gills, the skin. And the song.
textes.Alors, une galette pour le forgeron du g: So, a crêpe for the hinge smith?
textes.Alors, {surnom}, toi, à la taverne : tu: So, {surnom}, you, at the tavern: do you sing, do you dance, or do you listen?
textes.Alors… c'était le bouton d'un pirate. Un: Well… it was a pirate's button. A very elegant pirate.
Well then… twice upon a time.
textes.Alors… tu l'as vu, Octave. Il parle enco: So… you've seen him, Octave. Does he still talk about me?
textes.Altesse, l'ambassadeur vous attend depui: Your Highness, the ambassador has been waiting for ten minutes.
textes.Altesse, l'essayage ! Tenez-vous droite,: Your Highness, the fitting! Stand up straight, if you please.
textes.Altitude : idéale. Colis : intact. Pigeo: Altitude: ideal. Package: intact. Pigeon: annoying.
textes.Ambroise a hérité de l'atelier, de l'aut: Ambroise inherited the workshop, the automaton and the respect of the whole city. Me, the gear. He despises me, I think. He's never said so. He never says anything to me at all.
textes.Ambroise dit que son automate joueur d'é: Ambroise says his chess-playing automaton has never lost. That's because it cheats. The automaton, I mean. Ambroise, I don't know.
textes.Ambroise est le meilleur joueur d'échecs: Ambroise is the best chess player in the city, after his automaton. And the slowest, by a mile. Forty years I've been beating him on the clock.
textes.Ambroise est mon rival, un homme disting: Ambroise is my rival, a distinguished man, and the owner of an automaton that cheats. Well, the automaton does. Ambroise, I haven't made up my mind about yet.
textes.Ambroise est un juré susceptible, un hom: Ambroise is a touchy juror, a proud man, and the builder of the finest machine in the city. All three at once is exhausting. But I respect him.
textes.Ambroise m'a proposé cent fois de jouer: Ambroise has offered a hundred times for me to play against his automaton. I've always refused. “It has no watch.” Against someone without a watch, you don't play: you wait. And waiting is something I can't do. A bit much, for a clockmaker, but there it is.
textes.Ambroise. J'ai encore pensé à mes trois: Ambroise. I've been thinking about my three prizes again.
textes.Amenemhat ! Encore un poème au lieu de p: Amenemhat! Another poem instead of paying?
textes.Amenemhat ! Vous lisez dans le bon sens,: Amenemhat! Are you reading the right way round today?
textes.Amenemhat boit sa bière en lisant, il en: Amenemhat drinks his beer while reading, spills it on his papyri, and tells a story with every sip. He always pays. Late, and with a poem.
textes.Amenemhat boit sa bière en lisant. Il re: Amenemhat drinks his beer while reading. He always spills a little on the papyrus. His papyri smell of barley.
textes.Amenemhat m'a appris les signes. Il prét: Amenemhat taught me the signs. He claims to have read everything, he shows off like a river goose, and he has the most generous heart in Per-Hâpy. Only repeat the last part to him.
textes.Amenemhat mesure mon champ chaque année: Amenemhat measures my field every year with his cord. Every year, he finds it the same. Me, I find it smaller. We'll never agree. He has the cord, I have the eyes.
textes.Amenemhat prétend avoir lu tous les papy: Amenemhat claims he has read every papyrus in the House of Life. Every one. Even the ones he wrote himself. Especially those.
textes.Amenemhat ronfle à la Maison de Vie. Les: Amenemhat snores in the House of Life. The pupils call him the hippopotamus. Don't tell him.
textes.Amenemhat écrit avec des signes qui dise: Amenemhat writes with signs that each say one sound, or several, or none. It's very complicated. He talks as much as he writes. I like him very much. I only understand one sentence in two.
textes.Amenemhat, c'est le maître de la Maison: Amenemhat is the master of the House of Life. He knows seven hundred signs, and he talks even more than I do! He snores during school. The pupils call him the hippo. Don't tell him!
textes.Amenemhat. Vous avez sauté une ligne, ce: Amenemhat. You skipped a line this morning.
textes.Ami ? … Ougha réfléchit. (Ougha réfléchi: Friend? … Ougha think. (Ougha thinks very hard; it makes a noise.) All right. You friend. Smooth friend. First smooth friend of the Clan!
textes.Ami des fées ! Le royaume tout entier ch: Friend of the fairies! The whole kingdom sings your name.
textes.Ami, frère d'armes, compagnon de légende: Friend, brother in arms, companion of legend: I owe you a debt. Let me repay it with my sword. Whenever you like, just say “come with me”, and I, SIR TANCRÈDE DE TOURNEVENT, will charge at your side! One time in three, I'll fall. But the other two times… ah, the other two times!
textes.Amine m'a appris les osselets : tu lance: Amine taught me knucklebones: you throw, you pick up, you catch, all with one hand. He always wins. In exchange, I taught him to swear like a real pirate, but with no bad words: “Blistering barnacles! Thundering sardines!” Now he shouts it everywhere. His mum gives me funny looks.
textes.Amine sait où dort le chat roux. Je le s: Amine knows where the ginger cat sleeps. I know he knows! But he won't tell me. He only told Tibo, 'cause Tibo's a real pirate. It's not fair! I'm his captain. A captain has to know everything. I sulked for two days. Then he gave me a date. I stopped. A bit.
textes.Amine sait, pour les babouches de noce d: Amine knows about Rachid's wedding slippers. He saw them at the bottom of the basket. I told him: “Not a word.” He said: “Not a word.” The next day he walked past Rachid whistling the wedding tune, with enormous winks at me. He didn't say anything. Almost nothing.
textes.Amine, c'est mon matelot. Il perd toujou: Amine is my sailor. He always loses at boarding, but he's brave. He wants to be captain. That's not possible, I'm already captain.
textes.Amine, c'est mon meilleur copain de Tazi: Amine's my best mate in Tazira. He knows every roof, every crate and every secret. He wants to be a pirate. I want to be a fisherman. We should swap.
textes.Amine, mon fils. Neuf ans, des mains de: Amine, my son. Nine years old, a carpenter's hands and a pirate's head. I hand him a plane, he hands me back a wooden sabre. He takes after his mother. And a bit after me, I think.
textes.Amine, mon livreur ! Il court plus vite: Amine, my delivery boy! He runs faster than the chergui wind. He gets the wrong house one time in two, but he always comes back smiling. Paid in dates. He eats half of them on the way.
textes.Amine. Le fils de ma sœur. Il parle comm: Amine. My sister's son. He talks like the sandstorm wind. He's the only one who makes me laugh. Don't tell him: he'd talk even more.
textes.Amirale ! Vous avez vu ? J'ai redessiné: Admiral! Have you seen? I've redrawn the north coast!
textes.Ammit s'effondre et se dissout dans l'om: Ammit collapses and dissolves into the shadows. Anubis hasn't moved. You can stand before the scale again… and tell the truth this time.
textes.Ammit se ramasse… et se jette sur toi, g: Ammit crouches… and leaps at you, jaws wide open!
textes.Amoureuse. Comme au premier jour. Le onz: In love. Like on the first day. The eleventh day.
textes.Amélie m'a refusé le corail, et elle ava: Amélie refused me the coral, and she was right, I know. She knows every herb on the lookout. She couldn't find me my red.
textes.Amélie, c'est l'herboriste, et mon amie: Amélie is the herbalist, and my friend since the summer it didn't rain. I grow her thyme, she looks after my hands. We both dream of a flower nobody here has ever seen.
textes.Anne-Rose Corbeau a le plus beau galion: Anne-Rose Corbeau has the finest galleon in the archipelago and the worst temper. I offer her a swap every week: my Cod for her Shark. She refuses. She's wrong, but with panache.
textes.Annoncer la victoire à Pépin, à la Clair: Tell Pépin about the victory, at the Games Clearing
textes.Annoncer à Matthias que la Porte aux Qua: Tell Matthias that the Gate of the Four Seals is open (Carène harbour master's office)
textes.Anouk ! J'ai une drôle de douleur, là, à: Anouk! I've got a funny pain, right here, on the left.
textes.Anouk ! Regarde, je me suis pas fait mal: Anouk! Look, I didn't hurt myself today!
textes.Anouk ! Un nouveau baume, au miel des pr: Anouk! A new balm, with meadow honey this time!
textes.Anouk me soigne de tout, même de ce que: Anouk treats me for everything, even things I don't have, and she never makes fun of me. And she's been keeping a secret for me for years, without ever making me pay for it in herbal tea.
textes.Anouk ne pose pas de questions. Elle ten: Anouk doesn't ask questions. She holds out a phial of oil, she takes back the empty one. We understand each other perfectly without talking. It's the best way.
textes.Anouk soigne mes genoux. Elle grogne un: Anouk patches up my knees. She grumbles a bit, but she blows on them before putting the seaweed on, like I'm five. I like it. Don't tell anyone.
textes.Anouk soigne tout Carène avec des algues: Anouk heals all of Carène with seaweed and the patience of a limpet. She thinks I don't know she finds my hot honey stash. I know. It's our little game.
textes.Anouk soigne tout le monde avec des algu: Anouk treats everyone with seaweed, even broken legs. She thinks my desert balms are useless. I think they smell lovely. We don't have the same criteria.
Anouk treats everyone with seaweed. Even colds. Even broken legs.
textes.Anouk, ma toux est revenue. Une histoire: Anouk, my cough's back. A story and a hot honey?
textes.Anselme ? Mon vieux copain du phare. Cin: Anselme? My old pal at the lighthouse. Fifty years we've been talking, and almost never face to face. Two calls, two flashes. The longest friendship in the archipelago, and the quietest.
textes.Anselme m'a appris à reconnaître chaque: Anselme taught me to recognise every boat by its light at night. The Swallow has a slightly yellow lamp, Fernand's boat a lantern that leans. That's how I saw, from the harbour office, that the beam was trembling: the lens was cracked. I climbed up to tell him. He knew. He was waiting for someone to notice.
textes.Anselme parle moins que son phare. Mais: Anselme talks less than his lighthouse. But he watches over the whole harbour, and over me too, from up there. I take him up soup. It's our way of saying things to each other.
textes.Anselme, au phare, a vu une lueur bleue: Anselme, at the lighthouse, saw a blue glow under the water, far to the west. He doesn't believe me when I tell him what it is.
textes.Anselme, c'est le frère de Marius. Il m': Anselme is Marius's brother. He holds a net against me. All I want is for us to talk again. We're not getting any younger, him or me.
textes.Anselme, c'est ma ligne d'arrivée. Il gr: Anselme is my finish line. He grumbles, he doesn't talk, he put up a sign for me. I'm fond of him, the old owl.
textes.Anselme, le gardien du phare, a perdu qu: Anselme, the lighthouse keeper, has lost something precious. It's weighing on him.
textes.Antée, le géant, te prend dans sa grande: Antaeus, the giant, takes you in his great stone hand, very gently, like a bird. “The Cocytus is down below. It's cold. You took a coat, I hope?” He sets you down at the bottom of the well.
textes.Apaiser le Gardien du Cœur: Calm the Guardian of the Heart
textes.Apaisé. Le faisceau porte à vingt milles: At peace. The beam reaches twenty miles. Sailors sleep soundly.
textes.Apophis crache un nuage de venin noir !: Apophis spits a cloud of black venom!
Apophis is defeated. Ra is saved.
textes.Apophis s'enfonce dans l'eau noire en si: Apophis sinks into the black water, hissing… defeated! Above the barque, the sun disc lights up again, first red as dawn, then gold. Ra is saved: tomorrow, the sun will rise. And in front of the barque, something glows…
textes.Apophis siffle : des scorpions sortent d: Apophis hisses: scorpions crawl out of the darkness!
textes.Appliquée. J'ai trois robes de bal, une: Focused. I've got three ball gowns, a champion's cape and forty embroidered handkerchiefs to finish before the festival. And Tiburce dropping by every hour to criticise my hems.
textes.Apporter 2 dorades à Zohra, à la criée d: Bring 2 sea bream to Zohra, at the Tazira fish market (use a fishing rod, at the end of the jetty for example)
textes.Apporter 3 minerais de fer au professeur: Bring 3 iron ore to Professor Boum, in front of his workshop (west of Cliquetis, near the cliffs)
textes.Apporter la puce holographique et la car: Bring the hologram chip and the star chart to Ionie (in the Spaceport hangar)
textes.Apporter le miel à Bobor, au Four Éterne: Bring the honey to Bobor, at the Eternal Oven (the bakery in the Great Market)
textes.Apporter les cinq bouquets à Xóchitl (su: Bring the five bouquets to Xóchitl (on the chinampas, or at the market)
textes.Apporter les cinq fleurs à Mère Brasille: Bring the five flowers to Mother Brasille (at the Ash Gardens)
textes.Apporter les cordes et la toile à Jack (: Bring the ropes and the canvas to Jack (in the Festival Meadow, in front of the Main Stage, in the daytime)
textes.Apporter les trois champignons à Mère Sa: Bring the three mushrooms to Mother Sage (at the herb garden, south of the Academy)
textes.Apporter les trois cristaux à Violette (: Bring the three crystals to Violette (at a Guild table, or at the Upper Town lookout in the afternoon)
textes.Apporter les trois cristaux à Zigomar (à: Bring the three crystals to Zigomar (at his inventor's workshop)
textes.Apporter les trois flocons à Borée Givre: Bring the three flakes to Borée Givrelin (on the shore of Mirror Lake, north-east of the Academy)
textes.Apporter les trois fragments à Zénith (à: Bring the three fragments to Zénith (at the Observatory, on the islet to the north, across the bridge of light; he sleeps in the morning and works from evening until dawn)
textes.Apporter les trois lots de pièces à Rust: Bring the three batches of parts to Rustine (at the Spinning Mill bike workshop)
textes.Apporter les trois paniers à Lentille (à: Bring the three baskets to Lentille (at the Pay-What-You-Can Canteen, on the ground floor of the Cannery)
textes.Apporter les trois plumes à Zéphyrine Pl: Bring the three feathers to Zéphyrine Plume (at the foot of the Leaning Tower, in the south of the island)
textes.Apporter les trois touffes au Doc (Fulbe: Bring the three tufts to the Doc (Fulbert Saignée, in front of his door, near the forge)
textes.Apporter les trois éclats de lune à Auré: Bring the three moon shards to Aurélien Lumen (near the Observatory, north-west of the Academy; at the library in the afternoon)
textes.Apporter trois bûches à Pyra Flammèche (: Bring three logs to Pyra Flammèche (at the Duelling Ground, east of the Academy)
textes.Apporter un cristal de soufre à Mademois: Bring a sulphur crystal to Miss Sulfura (at the Academy; Bulle sells them at the Sulphur Baths)
textes.Apporter une galette de maïs à Kinich (I: Bring a corn cake to Kinich (Ix Chab sells them on the square of Yaxché)
textes.Apporter à Clémence un corail rouge (fon: Bring Clémence a red coral (bottom of the bay, to the west), some honey and a coconut
textes.Apporter à Hector deux bûches et trois c: Bring Hector two logs and three pebbles
textes.Apporter à Ionie trois cristaux astraux,: Bring Ionie three astral crystals, two meteorite fragments, four gears and two rolls of sailcloth (Ionie and Nébula sell them; fragments also fall on shooting-star nights) — Ionie is in the Spaceport hangar, to the east
textes.Apporter à Lord Pemberton une plume de V: Bring Lord Pemberton one of Ventaile's feathers, a naga scale or a shark tooth
textes.Apporter à Volt les trois éclats et troi: Bring Volt the three shards and three astral crystals (at the foot of the Crystal Spire)
textes.Apprendre la magie ? … Le Cristal a frém: Learn magic? … The Crystal trembled. Good sign. Listen: every apprentice starts with a spellbook. Go see Théophraste at the library: he'll give you one, brand new, with blank pages. Then introduce yourself to Pip: he's the youngest of the apprentices, and the chattiest; he'll show you everything. Then come back to me, in the courtyard of the Great Crystal.
textes.Apprendre la télékinésie avec Théophrast: Learn telekinesis with Théophraste Filandre, at the library
textes.Apprendre les six sorts des maîtres d'Ar: Learn the six spells of the masters of Arcanelle: light, fire, frost, levitation, telekinesis and healing
textes.Approche, approche ! Regarde-moi ces yeu: Come closer, come closer! Look at those shiny eyes: caught this morning. The fish, I mean, not me. I'm Zohra. My stall is the first at the auction, and the best.
textes.Approche, approche ! Tochtli, le Lapin !: Come closer, come closer! Tochtli, the Rabbit! Best merchant in the tianguis! Copal for the gods, cacao for people, obsidian for warriors! Everything you need, and even what you don't!
textes.Approche, approche ! Épices de Pandémoni: Step up, step up! Spices of Pandémonia! Fire cinnamon, ash pepper, sulphur salt, and the famous infernal chili! Zébuline, at your service. Don't sniff too hard: my last customer sneezed all the way to the harbour.
textes.Approche, approche… Assieds-toi près du: Come closer, come closer… Sit by the fire. Silas. Old Silas. The last man alive from Barbe-Sanglante's crew. Want a story? I've got a thousand. All true. Nearly.
textes.Approche, approche… Tout est garanti mag: Come closer, come closer… Everything is guaranteed magic, except what isn't. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Approche, jeune humain. Assieds-toi. Je: Come closer, young human. Sit down. I am Faelar. I watched that tree grow, and that one, and… ah, no, that one was already tall.
textes.Approche, le grand. Approche. Thorgal Ma: Come closer, big one. Closer. Thorgal Marteau-d'Or, king of Forgefer, lord of the Fire Mountain. You may bow. … Lower.
textes.Approche, matelot. Plus près. Je ne sais: Come here, sailor. Closer. I can't swim. Not a stroke. A whole life on the water, thirty years of crossings in the mist, and I sink like an anvil. That's why I know every current by heart: I'm not allowed to get it wrong. Berthe doesn't know. If she knew, she'd never let me leave again. Not even tomorrow.
textes.Approche, mon enfant, approche. Mes yeux: Come closer, my child, come closer. My eyes can't see far anymore, but my hands see everything. I am Fatima. They call me Lalla Fatima, because I'm old and I'm frightening.
textes.Approche, mon enfant, viens te réchauffe: Come closer, my child, come and warm yourself.
textes.Approche, mon enfant. N'aie pas peur : l: Come closer, my child. Don't be afraid: fire only bites those who neglect it. I am Brother Cendrin, keeper of the Ember Heart. For four hundred years, I have watched over the flame that warms the whole city.
textes.Approche, mon enfant… Dis-moi. Tu as que: Come closer, my child… Tell me. Do you have someone waiting for you, somewhere?
textes.Approche, petit, approche. Les vieilles: Come closer, little one, come closer. Old horns don't bite. They call me Grandpa Ébène. I've been telling stories on the Great Square for… oh… six hundred years? Seven? After five hundred, you stop counting candles. You count stories.
textes.Approche, petit. N'aie pas peur de mes o: Come closer, little one. Don't be afraid of my ears: they're old, but they can still hear hearts beating. I am Mère-Lune. Welcome to Ramure, the village of ears.
textes.Approche, petit. Une question de marin,: Come here, youngster. A sailor's question, a real one: can you tie a bowline?
textes.Approche, regarde. Tout vient de la mer: Come closer, have a look. Everything comes from the sea or the hold. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Approche, {surnom}, côté droit. Je n'ent: Come closer, {surnom}, on the right side. I can hardly hear anything in my left ear. Years glued to the speakers, before Bastien invented his earplugs. If Tchoum tunes the sound, it's because he hears what I can't any more. He knows — only him. The others, I don't want them to worry: a half-deaf DJ is either funny or frightening.
Come closer, {surnom}, and don't repeat this. I know I'm a bad cook. Twenty years ago, one icy winter, off a white island, I lost my sense of taste. Almost all of it. I salt because I can't taste anything any more. But Aïcha's spices… those still reach my tongue. Like a lantern in the fog. That's why I want to stay.
textes.Approche, {surnom}, et parle bas. Depuis: Come closer, {surnom}, and speak softly. Since the day of the nest, I've been afraid of heights. The high priest of Aztlán climbs the steps of the Great Temple every morning without ever looking down. I always look at the sky. People say I'm very pious. Mostly, I'm very careful. The Eagle is afraid of the drop. May Huitzilopochtli forgive me.
textes.Approche, {surnom}, et parle pas fort. M: Come closer, {surnom}, and keep your voice down. I never wanted to be mayor. I only ran because Marcel bet I wouldn't dare. His measurement was wrong, I saw it straight away: my ball was closer. And I was relieved. Since then, I cry “Thief!”, because it makes him so happy to have beaten me. He's my best friend. Don't tell him.
textes.Approche, {surnom}, et regarde sous l'ét: Come closer, {surnom}, and look under the stall. No, don't look! … All right. I never wear babouches. My feet are as flat as pancakes, and I walk better barefoot. All day long, I put shoes on Tazira, and I hide my feet under the table. The barefoot babouche seller! If this gets out, I'm ruined. Or famous.
textes.Approche, {surnom}, plus près. Cette nui: Come closer, {surnom}, closer. That night, Captain Sel asked me to leave with him. Me! A net-mender. I said no: I was waiting for Larbi. So he hid a chest in the caves, “for the day you change your mind”. I never changed my mind. I never went there. And Larbi never knew a thing. You don't know anything either.
textes.Approche, {surnom}, que je n'aie pas à c: Come closer, {surnom}, so I don't have to shout. The finest trade is Nourredine's. His. People look at the light, never at the copper. So one year, while the caïd was chasing the kids off the battlements, I engraved my name under the seventh cannon. Very small. So a bit of me would last. If Nourredine ever finds out, I'll hammer you flat.
textes.Approche, {surnom}, que personne n'enten: Come closer, {surnom}, so no one hears. I've forgotten the ending. The ending of my best story, the moon that wouldn't go to bed, the one my mother used to tell me. So when we get to the end, I start another story, and nobody notices. Except maybe Mother Moon. She always pretends to fall asleep at just the right moment. I think she knows it.
textes.Approche, {surnom}. Je ne dors pas toujo: Come closer, {surnom}. I don't always sleep at the observatory. When Kinich comes, I snore. On purpose. Then he creeps up to my tables and looks at the dots, the bars, the cycles of Venus. He learns all by himself, thinking I'm asleep. If I asked him to be my apprentice, he'd run away. Children only learn well what's a little forbidden.
textes.Approche, {surnom}. L'hymne du matin a d: Come closer, {surnom}. The morning hymn has twelve parts, one for each hour of the night. My mother joined Osiris before she could teach me the last one. So every morning for twenty years, I've made up the ending. Never the same. And every morning, the sun rises anyway. I've never told anyone. Perhaps what the gods love most is that we sing.
textes.Approche, {surnom}. La lune ne m'a pas s: Come closer, {surnom}. The moon didn't only tell me to go home. It entrusted me with a secret, at the bottom of the big pond: the seal of the mists. Where, I won't say until it has spoken to you, yourself. I'm afraid of leaving with the mist before I've passed it on. I had thought of Brume. But Brume reads tracks… and the moon, she doesn't hear it.
textes.Approche, {surnom}. La mille et unième h: Come closer, {surnom}. The thousand and first story, I've never told: I don't know it. I'm waiting to live it. And I have one regret. The Léviathan's logbook, we paid for it with semolina, to a family that was starving. That was no price. I promised little Corentin I'd give it back to whoever came looking for it. An apprentice's promise, made under a table. It's the heaviest of my life.
textes.Approche, {surnom}. Plus près. Il n'y a: Come closer, {surnom}. Closer. There is no secret. Nonna passed away one winter, before she could tell me. In her notebook, the last line just stops: “dieci pesci, zafferano, e…” And nothing. Twenty-five years I've been pretending. Sometimes I think the secret is Rosalie singing while she guts the fish. If you repeat this to her, I'll serve you soup. Real soup.
textes.Approche, {surnom}. Plus près. Mon cache: Come closer, {surnom}. Closer. My eyepatch… there's nothing under it. My eye is perfectly fine. This eyepatch was Barbe-Sanglante's. He gave it to me on the last morning, saying: “Keep it, cabin boy. It sees stories.” I've worn it ever since. I don't see anything more. But I've never been afraid of the dark again. Don't tell anyone. Especially not Sans-Dents.
textes.Approche, {surnom}. Ptahmosé, le potier: Come closer, {surnom}. Ptahmosé, the potter from Egypt, sent me a blue scarab. For two years, I've been trying to make one to send back. All my scarabs look like frogs. All of them! My hands have been making frogs for Tlaloc for thirty years, they can't do anything else any more. He must think I'm offended. I'm just hopeless at scarabs.
textes.Approche-toi et appuie sur E pour monter: Get close and press E to climb on. To call her from afar: G (or “Use” the feather in the inventory).
textes.Approche-toi et appuie sur la gâchette p: Get close and press the trigger to climb on. To call her from afar: X button (left hand).
textes.Approche. Plus près. … Mes yeux baissent: Come here. Closer. … My eyes are failing, {surnom}. For two years now. Beyond the big pond, it's all mist. The monster of the False Alarm, maybe that was it. “Nothing to report” is also because I can't see any more. Brume tells me what she smells without me asking. Nobody knows. Except that owl Hulotte. He offered me spectacles. No.
textes.Approchez ! Admirez ! Le Moteur Perpétue: Step up! Behold! Firmin Cogne's Perpetual Motion Engine: it's been running for eleven years without ever stopping! … Well, it stopped yesterday. But that was the gear's fault.
textes.Approchez ! Tout doit disparaître !: Step right up! Everything must go!
textes.Approchez, approchez ! Galettes d'algues: Step right up, step right up! Seaweed cakes! Fresh as can be! Well, fresh… wet. I'm Marée. And you are… dry! How exotic!
textes.Approchez, approchez ! Perroquet-Joe ! L: Step up, step up! Perroquet-Joe! The finest parrots in the archipelago! They talk, they whistle, they sing! A pirate without a parrot is a sailor without a sea!
textes.Approchez, {surnom}. Plus près. Depuis c: Come closer, {surnom}. Closer. Since that splash when I was seventeen, I've never set foot on a boat again. Never. The mayor of a port! I open the new quays three metres from the edge, with a big smile and knees like jelly. The village across the water, I've only ever seen from here. Fernand suspects, I think. He's kind enough to say nothing.
textes.Approche… Barbe-Sanglante a déchiré sa c: Come closer… Barbe-Sanglante tore his map in three, so his men wouldn't betray each other. One piece sleeps in the dungeon of the Cursed Fort, to the east, guarded by his old sailors, the ones who are nothing but bones now. Another in the mausoleum of the graveyard, on the western hill. The third… Sylvain, at the Shark's Tooth, keeps it up his sleeve: he only bets it against someone who beats him three times in a row. Gather all three, take them to Philémon, the mapmaker. And may the sea keep you.
textes.Approche… J'étais mousse sur la Mâchoire: Come closer… I was a cabin boy on the Black Jaw, Barbe-Sanglante's ship. The littlest cabin boy in the archipelago: smaller than Petit-Pierre, and twice as chatty. I scrubbed the deck, carried the buckets, and slept in a hammock next to the cannons. It was so long ago that the sea itself no longer remembers. I do.
textes.Approche… plus près… Je vais te dire un: Come closer… closer… I'm going to tell you a secret, {surnom}. I can't swim. A fishery cat who can't swim! I look for the King from the jetty, never in the water. Grandpa thinks I'm sensible. I'm not sensible, I'm scared. I haven't told anyone, not even Grandpa. Especially not Grandpa.
textes.Après Carène, je lui ai fait un billet s: After Carène, I made him a special ticket. In ink, with the airfield's official stamp: “One way to nowhere. Valid for life.” He looked at it for a long time, then slipped it under the lining of his hat. He's never used it. But sometimes I see him touch his hat when he walks past the Zéphyr.
textes.Après Carène, la commandante m'a fait un: After Carène, the commander made me a ticket, by hand, with the airfield stamp: “One way to nowhere. Valid for life.” I keep it in my hat, under the lining. I've never used it. But when one of my ideas turns out to exist already, I touch it with my fingertips, and I feel a little better.
textes.Après Sel, des années à terre. Puis ving: After Sel, years ashore. Then twenty years of piracy on my own account. Lou the Terrible! Three ships sunk, every crew put in the longboats: I'm no savage. And seasick my whole life, from the first day to the last. Nobody was to know. One day I threw an insolent young gunner overboard. His name was Croc.
textes.Après chaque crue, je mesure les champs: After every flood, I measure the fields with a cord to put the boundary stones back. Hapou always finds that his has shrunk. It's a field, Hapou, not a linen tunic.
textes.Après chaque plongée profonde, Lucie a m: After every deep dive, Lucie's ears hurt, and she doesn't tell anyone. So I keep a vial of warm oil for her by the stove. She comes by, takes it without a word, and leaves a shell in its place. I've got a drawer full of them.
textes.Après l'alliance perdue, j'ai raconté à: After the lost wedding ring, I told half the town that Léa didn't want to see her husband any more. She heard it from Rosalie, at the fish stall. So for a week, I folded the towels in room seven into heart shapes. On the fifth day, she left a note on the pillow: “Thanks for the hearts. Not a word.” I held out. Almost.
textes.Après l'essai, Basile m'a proposé de mon: After the test, Basile offered to get into the next bubble himself, “as ballast”. He was serious: he'd already put his hat on. I said no. I'm not going to have two men up in the air to wait for. I've only got one bench.
textes.Après l'histoire de la soupe, elle a aff: After the soup business, she pinned a sign on her kitchen door: “No pufferfish allowed”, with a crossed-out fish. The whole port laughed. Me too, at first. But the next day, she brought me a hot grog without a word, because everyone was making fun of me. That's her. Spicy and sweet.
textes.Après l'histoire de sa soupe, tout le po: After the business with his soup, the whole port was making fun of him. I hung a sign on my kitchen door: “No pufferfish allowed”, with a crossed-out fish, so everyone would laugh at the sign instead of at him. Then I brought him a hot grog. He looked at me with wet-dog eyes. We never spoke of it again.
textes.Après l'histoire du drap, il a passé une: After the bedsheet business, he spent a week in bed at my house. To keep him still, I taught him to knit. He made me a scarf, with more holes than wool. I wear it every winter. I told him the holes let the skin breathe. It's true, actually. A little.
textes.Après l'hydromel, une bière au miel et a: After the honey drink, a fizz made with honey and ember mushroom, so good the king will sing in tune. Just once! It'd be a miracle, and I'd serve it free.
textes.Après la Fête du Cristal, j'ai gardé la: After the Crystal Festival, I kept the jug, the one that froze on one side and boiled on the other between Borée and Pyra. It has a crack that goes all the way round, right in the middle. I put it on the shelf at the back. Borée always sits with his back to it: I turned his chair on purpose. He never thanked me. He understood.
textes.Après la criée, il s'assied à ma table e: After the auction, he sits at my table and eats twelve sardines. Twelve! For the voice, he says. On big auction days, thirteen. One day he ate fifteen, and that very evening he challenged Hamid on the square. A lantern fell down. I say it was because of the three extra sardines.
textes.Après la criée, je mange douze sardines: After the auction, I eat twelve sardines at his table. Twelve. For the voice. On big auction days, thirteen. The day I ate fifteen, that very evening, I challenged Hamid. Mustapha says it's the fault of the three extra. I say with sixteen, I'd have won. We've never tried.
textes.Après la grande bagarre de la saison des: After the big brawl of the rainy season, my counter was split in two. Gwen came with her tools, a plank from the Merciless and a pot of tar. She worked all night. In the morning, the counter was more beautiful than before, with a little anchor carved in the middle. She said: “Not even Gros-Louis will break this one.”

After the big brawl of the rainy season, her counter was split in two. I worked all night with a plank from the Merciless. In the morning, I carved a little anchor in the middle. Mama ran her hand over it, for a long time, without a word. Then she said: “Gaspard would have liked it.” I didn't know who Gaspard was. Now I do.
textes.Après la grande tempête, le dôme de mon: After the great storm, the dome of my Observatory had a hole in it. Berthe lent me her room under the roof, with the skylight. A month. The skylight looks straight at the North Star. I spent my nights with my head outside, my hat pulled over my ears. She brought me hot milk at midnight. The finest month of my life, along with all the others.
textes.Après la grande tempête, le dôme de son: After the great storm, the dome of his Observatory had a hole in it. He slept a month in my room under the roof, the one with the skylight. He didn't sleep, actually: he spent his nights with his head out of it. Since then, he tells everyone it's the room on the island where you dream best. So I charge more for it. Thank you, Aurélien.
textes.Après la seconde d'avance, j'ai retrouvé: After the second fast, I kept finding confetti in the works until May. In the count wheel, under the pendulum, in my cup. To make her understand what a second out of place means, I gave her a backwards watch. She hates it. She says she can't read it. That's exactly the point.
textes.Après la tempête, c'est elle qui a vu, d: After the storm, she was the one who saw, from the harbour master's office, that the beam was short. I was inside it, I couldn't see a thing. She ran up, all the way without stopping. She said nothing. She laid her hand on the cracked lens, like on a sick child's forehead.
textes.Après le combat, Fulbert est monté à not: After the fight, Fulbert came aboard with his bag, without anyone asking him. He was the king's surgeon, we were the pirates. He treated everyone, starting with the worst off. That was me. As he left, he told me: “Don't walk on the wet deck.” With only one leg. He already had a sense of humour.
textes.Après le mardi vert, mon grand-père m'a: After Green Tuesday, my grandfather wrote me a letter. Three pages, without a single comma, with words I won't repeat. At the end: “And tell your scientist that sheep are not experiments.” I took the letter to the professor. He read it to the end and said: “What a turn of phrase!” He hadn't understood a thing.
textes.Après le maïs, Pilli. Et ne vends pas me: After the maize, Pilli. And don't sell my flowers!
textes.Après le naufrage, Yasmine m'a nommé « s: After the shipwreck, Yasmine made me her “second”. I was so happy: second is like when you have seconds of tajine, it's better than the first! I celebrated all day. In the evening, my mum explained. I sulked. But I stayed second. A second gets a sabre.
textes.Après le soir du nuage, j'ai frotté le p: After the night of the cloud, I scrubbed the deck for a week, and every morning she walked past behind me saying: “Is your cloud pretty today?” On the seventh day, she gave me a wind feather for my bandana. I think it was to apologise for laughing. I still wear it.
textes.Après les plongées profondes, j'ai mal a: After deep dives, my ears hurt. I don't tell anyone. Anouk found out anyway, I don't know how. Since then, there's always a phial of warm oil in the corner by her stove, for me. I take it, I leave a shell. She must have a drawer full of them by now.
textes.Après les ressorts, j'ai boudé une semai: After the springs, I sulked for a week: not one paw in the forge. On the eighth evening I came back, all sheepish. She just said: “Hm. You're late.” She'd counted the evenings, {surnom}! That means she missed me. I think.
textes.Après les six sorts ? La cérémonie, au C: After the six spells? The ceremony, at the Moonstone Circle. You'll lay your hand on the altar, and the nine stones will decide. They've never said no. But first learn the six spells: light, fire, frost, levitation, telekinesis and healing.
textes.Après ma troisième deuxième place, Pépin: After my third second place, Pépin got out his brushes. Right at the bottom of the record board, he painted: “Grisou, almost first”. With a little arrow pointing up! I went to reread it every day for a week. My uncle came to see it too. He leaned in really close, for a really long time. He said “Hm”. He was proud, I think.
textes.Après mon premier été, je suis allé le v: After my first summer, I went to see him with two cones. I offered to go into business together: him the patter, me the ice cream. He looked at the cone, he looked at the sea, and he said: “Never.” Then he ate the whole cone, without stopping. A few days later, he opened Souvenirs d'Azur.
textes.Après sa fusée en tuyau de poêle, toute: After his stovepipe rocket, the whole square was full of smoke. Léonce was very sheepish. I told him: “Smoke is the beginning of everything!” He smiled from ear to ear. His mother looked at me the way a light bulb looks at a bucket of water. I take nothing back.
textes.Après sa troisième place de deuxième, Gr: After his third second place, Grisou had a face like a wet wolf. So I painted, right at the bottom of the record board, in neat little letters: “Grisou, almost first”. He came to read it again every day for a week, pointing it out to everyone. Even Bondi. Especially Bondi.
textes.Après tout le monde ?! À l'heure où je m: After everyone else?! By the time I get up, you've been asleep for… oh, I don't want to know. There'll only be crumbs left. And Mochi will have eaten them.
textes.Après un combat difficile, Bulle m'a pré: After a tough fight, Bulle made me a special bath, with salts from his sister Vespérine. The water turned purple and full of bubbles. I came out all purple. I kept the colour for three days. In the Arena, the crowd called me “Gorgoth the Mauve”. Bulle says it was on purpose. I don't believe him.
textes.Après un coup d'arme, garde le clic enfo: After a weapon blow, keep the button held: the blade charges up (it glows). Release: a terrible blow (×2.5). In VR: a very fast swing.
textes.Après une bagarre, c'est moi qu'on vient: After a brawl, I'm the one they come to see. And after a botched brawl, I'm the one who scrapes them off the quay. I don't ask questions. I stitch.
textes.Après une vingtaine d'années au long cou: After twenty-odd years on deep-sea voyages, I wanted to sleep in my own bed. Thirty years ago, I bought the Swallow, who was ten years old. Since then: six coats of paint, kings, newlyweds, a goat with no sea legs. My first month, a young man got off with his suitcase before we cast off. I gave him back his ticket. His name? That's for him to tell.
textes.Après ça, je dormirai sous un arbre pend: After that, I'll sleep under a tree for a year. At least. It's a fox technique.
textes.Après, il y a eu des jours affreux. Léa: After that came some awful days. Léa wasn't speaking to me. I bought a rose at Rose's: she didn't take it. I asked Inès for a ring “exactly the same”: she refused. Kiki lent me his punch ladle, I dug until midnight. In the evenings, at Paulo's, I looked at my finger and Léa looked at the sea. Ten days married, and already the longest week of my life.
textes.Après, je ne dirai rien. Je regarderai j: Afterwards, I won't say a thing. I'll just look at my uncle. And he'll sing.
textes.Après, je serai archiviste de la surface: After that, I'll be the archivist of the surface. Abyssos can look after down here, I'll do up there, and we'll share the ink.
textes.Après… je pourrai peut-être parler. Un p: After that… maybe I could talk. A little. To someone.
textes.Arbre marqué d'une entaille : il s'abat: Tree marked with a notch: chop it down with an axe
textes.Arcanelle a la plus vieille bibliothèque: Arcanelle has the oldest library in the archipelago. Three thousand volumes. Two thousand nine hundred and ninety-six, since the great gust of wind.
textes.Arcanelle n'est sur aucune carte des mar: Arcanelle isn't on any merchant's map. The mists hide it from the curious. If you're here, it's because it wanted you to come.
textes.Arcanelle, de la mer, on ne la voit qu'a: From the sea, you don't see Arcanelle until the very last moment. The mist hides it, and then all of a sudden: the Academy tower, straight as an arrow, and the crystal shining. It still does something to me, after thirty years.
textes.Archimage ! J'ai ma question du jour !: Archmage! I've got my question of the day!
textes.Aristide t'envoie ? Alors le premier ver: Aristide sent you? Then the first drink is on me! Come back tonight, Django is playing.
textes.Aristide, c'est le maire. Le maire voleu: Aristide is the mayor. The thieving mayor. He won by one centimetre, measured by Marcel. I vote for him at every election, but only so he'll feel ashamed.
textes.Arrivées et vendues, Ix Sak ! Elles ont: Arrived and sold, Ix Sak! They loved the trip!
textes.Arrr ! … Non, je ne suis pas pirate. Je: Arrr! … No, I'm not a pirate. I'm practising.
textes.Arrête ! La violence n'a pas sa place so: Stop! Violence has no place beneath these branches.
textes.Arrête ! On ne frappe personne sous l'Ar: Stop! Nobody strikes anyone beneath the Mother Tree!
textes.Arrête ! Tu vas fâcher la Reine !: Stop! You'll make the Queen cross!
Stop slowing down when he walks in.
textes.Arrêter la grande horloge. Une minute. U: To stop the great clock. One minute. Just one, on my wedding day. Let the whole city wait, let time wait, and let us have one minute all to ourselves. Then I'll wind it up again. Promise.
textes.Article 3 : la bonne humeur est interdit: Article 3: good cheer is prohibited after 6 p.m.
textes.As-tu écrit à ta moitié, là-bas ? Zéphyr: Have you written to your other half, over there? Zéphyr can carry letters. He shakes them about a bit, but they arrive.
textes.Asmodin a servi ma grand-mère, ma mère,: Asmodin served my grandmother, my mother, and now me. He's always called me “Highness”. I've asked him a hundred times to call me Ignatia. He says “certainly”, and never does.
textes.Asmodin est le majordome du palais. Il e: Asmodin is the palace butler. He's as stiff as a broomstick and talks like an etiquette book. He's written me seventeen letters complaining about my voice. I adore them.
textes.Asmodin est mon premier client, et le pl: Asmodin is my first client, and the most loyal. Every Monday, he entrusts me with his horns and says just one word: “Acceptable.” Coming from him, that's a poem. I owe him my career.
textes.Asmodin et Madame Hurla ne se supportent: Asmodin and Madame Hurla can't stand each other. He says she shouts. She says he whispers. They're both right.
textes.Asmodin m'a écrit dix-sept lettres pour: Asmodin has written me seventeen letters asking me to lower my voice. Magnificent letters, full of “I beg you” and “yours most respectfully”. I read them out on the Grand Square, aloud, one a day. The crowd applauded. Apparently they now study them at the Academy, as models of politeness. He ought to thank me.
Asmodin wrote me seventeen letters complaining about my voice. I read them all out on the square. Out loud. Everyone applauded. Except him.
textes.Asmodin ne m'a jamais pardonné la fusée: Asmodin has never forgiven me for the rocket at the ambassadors' dinner. And yet it worked perfectly! It just went in through the wrong window. And into the wrong soup.
textes.Asmodin vient chercher les brioches du p: Asmodin comes to fetch the palace brioches every day at noon. He measures them with a silver ruler. He never smiles. Well, almost never. I've found the trick.
textes.Asmodin, appelle-moi Ignatia. Et dis-lui: Asmodin, call me Ignatia. And tell him I'm coming.
textes.Asmodin, appelle-moi Ignatia. Juste une: Asmodin, call me Ignatia. Just once.
textes.Asmodin, le majordome du palais, ne m'a: Asmodin, the palace butler, has never forgiven me for the rocket in the soup. Yet it worked perfectly! It just came in through the wrong window. I admire him greatly. He's so upright. Like a rocket.
textes.Asmodin, majordome du Palais de Pandémon: Asmodin, butler of the Palace of Pandémonia, in the service of Her Highness the Archduchess Ignatia, as of her mother, and of her mother's mother. Three hundred and twelve years of service. May I take your coat? Ah. You don't have one. Unfortunate.
textes.Asseyez-vous, {surnom}. Je ne suis pas e: Sit down, {surnom}. I'm not on holiday. The university has retired me. The letters Nadine brings me ask me to clear out my office. “Officially on holiday”: it's a lie I tell myself every morning. I've spent all my savings on charts and hotel nights. If I find nothing, I'll have nothing left. Not even the excuse.
textes.Assieds-toi dans le cercle, voyageur. Ic: Sit in the circle, traveller. Here, this is the halqa: we listen, and at the end, you give what you like. I am Ba Sidi. I have a thousand and one stories, and I've only told a thousand so far.
textes.Assieds-toi, Morgane. La galette est cha: Sit down, Morgane. The crêpe is hot.
textes.Assieds-toi, assieds-toi. Je suis Tilleu: Sit down, sit down. I'm Tilleul, the storyteller. Want a story? Once upon a time… no, wait. Twice upon a time. It's a story that happened twice.
Sit down, keeper of the djinn.
textes.Assieds-toi, ma petite. La galette non p: Sit down, little one. The crêpe doesn't have time either.
textes.Assieds-toi, petit, assieds-toi. Tu veux: Sit down, little one, sit down. Want a story? Of course you want a story. Everyone wants a story. I'm Corentin, and I know a thousand of them.
textes.Assieds-toi, {surnom}, mais ne touche pa: Sit down, {surnom}, but don't touch the knots.
textes.Assieds-toi, {surnom}. Le poisson ne vie: Sit down, {surnom}. The fish won't come any faster, but there'll be two of us waiting.
textes.Assieds-toi, {surnom}. Mais d'abord, dis: Sit down, {surnom}. But first, tell me: can you at least tie a knot?
textes.Assieds-toi. Et parle moins fort, il y a: Sit down. And keep your voice down, people are eating.
Sit down. Moss, then a sweet.
textes.Assieds-toi. Quand je suis né, il n'y av: Sit down. When I was born, there was only one tree with folk living in it: the Mother Oak. My father, Frêne, had woven the wicker basket, and as a youngster I'd ride up in it to hear the old ones telling tales at the treetop. Later, I ran it myself. I talked so much that passengers took the stairs, until my son Bourru took it over. Meanwhile, the bridges had grown from tree to tree.
textes.Assieds-toi. Serre les dents. … Voilà. T: Sit down. Grit your teeth. … There. Three stitches, a little balm, and a sip of tonic (for me). You're good as new. Well, as good as second-hand.
Sit. And hands on the table.
textes.Assise sur le banc, en regardant en l'ai: Sitting on the bench, looking up at the sky. It's a compromise.
textes.Assister à la Nuit des Aurores: Watch the Night of the Auroras
textes.Assister à la Nuit des Aurores (chaque n: Watch the Night of the Auroras (every night from 10 p.m. to 2 a.m., above Astralys: watch it from the Agora, or better still, from the Observatory)
textes.Astralys — l'île flottante des Lumens (i: Astralys — the floating island of the Lumens (here, even the pebbles shine)
textes.Astralys, l'île flottante des Lumens: Astralys, the floating island of the Lumens
textes.Astralys, la cité de cristal et de lumiè: Astralys, the city of crystal and light
textes.Astuce : dis les couleurs à voix haute p: Tip: say the colours out loud while they light up. “Blue, pink, yellow…” It sticks on its own!
textes.Atteindre l'île flottante et sa citadell: Reach the floating island and its citadel
textes.Atteindre la salle du trône, au 5e étage: Reach the throne room, on the 5th floor of the dungeon
textes.Attendre. C'est ce que je fais depuis ce: Waiting. That's what I've been doing for a hundred and eighty years, on the other side. You've got patience. That's… proper. Very proper.
textes.Attends la touche… (clic : remonter): Wait for the bite…  (click: reel in)
textes.Attention ! Baisse-toi ! … Non, rien. Fa: Look out! Duck! … No, nothing. False alarm. Hello! Zigomar, inventor, pyrotechnician, and former owner of two eyebrows. Here, we invent the future of Pandémonia! Well, the future, and a few holes in the ceiling.
Look out! … Ah, no, it's nothing.
textes.Attention ! … Non, ça va. Bonjour !: Look out! … No, it's fine. Hello!
textes.Attention aux feux follets : quand ils b: Watch out for the will-o'-the-wisps: when they glow very bright, they charge. Step aside!
textes.Attention aux éclairs ! Électre Volta. C: Mind the lightning! Électre Volta. These two coils produce a million volts. What's it for? For now, making very pretty sparks. And making my visitors' hair stand on end.
textes.Attention où tu marches : des pots de pe: Watch where you step: paint pots lie all over the place. Someone is repainting the house… in two colors.
textes.Attention où tu mets les pieds, il y a d: Watch where you put your feet, there's tar everywhere. Tobias. Caulker. I plug holes. In a ship a hundred and forty metres long, there's always a hole.
textes.Attention à la peinture fraîche ! Enfin,: Mind the wet paint! Well, the wet tar.
textes.Attention à la tête : un fauteuil passe: Watch your head: an armchair is drifting over you, quite calmly.
textes.Attention à la tête, le grand ! … Ah non: Mind your head, big one! … Oh no, you're the big one.
textes.Attention à ne pas marcher sur les filet: Careful not to step on the nets! Khadija. I mend them. Every hole the sea makes, I close. The sea is patient, and so am I.
Be careful not to fall… upwards.
Mind your arms, the eggs are there.
textes.Attention, ils mordillent ! Mais gentime: Careful, they nibble! But gently! Flammèche, kennel keeper. I raise twelve hellhound puppies: Braise, Tison, Suie, Fumerolle, Pétard, Charbon, Escarbille, Flambard, Mèche, Cendre, Biscotte and Grignotte. Yes, they spit a bit of fire. Like all babies.
textes.Attention, je ne m'arrête pas. Mes frein: Warning, I do not stop. Brakes are optional.
textes.Attention, ça chauffe par ici !: Careful, it's getting hot over here!
textes.Attention, ça va tirer !: Watch out, it's going to fire!
textes.Attention… le canard… il sait voler…: Watch out… the duck… it can fly…
textes.Attentive. Les signes sont bons, le ciel: Watchful. The signs are good, the sky is clear.
textes.Attraper Grand-Mère Perche, la plus viei: To catch Grandmother Perch, the oldest perch in the river. I've seen her twice, as big as a calf. I wouldn't eat her. I'd just like her to say hello to me.
textes.Attraper le serpent de mer. Pas pour le: Catch the sea serpent. Not to keep it: to bring it to the Cauldron, put it on the counter, and see Pyra's face. Then I'll let it go. It looks friendly.
textes.Au Bois de Cendre, monsieur ! C'était de: In the Ash Wood, sir! It was natural history!
textes.Au Bois-Doré, nos maisons sont posées da: In Bois-Doré, our houses sit in the branches of trees so tall their tops touch the clouds. You'll see. I promise you.
textes.Au Cercle des Pierres-Lunes, il y a neuf: In the Moonstone Circle, there are nine stones. Each one has a name. Ysolde knows them all. She taught me three. I write them down in my journal.
textes.Au Crâne Fendu, le grog est chaud et les: At the Crâne Fendu, the grog is hot and so are the fists. At the Shark's Tooth, you lose your coins. I do both, so I go home light.
textes.Au Grand Concours du Dessert, Asmodin ét: At the Grand Dessert Contest, Asmodin was the judge. He tasted my honey cake, then Grumbald's frozen lava, then my cake, then the frozen lava… For an hour. He declared a tie. The next day, he came and bought three honey cakes “for the palace”. I saw him eat one on the way.
textes.Au Grand Concours du Dessert, j'ai prése: At the Great Dessert Contest, I entered my frozen lava, and Bobor his honey cake. Asmodin tasted for an hour and declared a tie. Since then, Bobor and I meet every month to “settle it”. We've never settled it. We've just put on weight. Bulle says we float better and better.
textes.Au Grand Concours du Dessert, j'étais le: At the Grand Dessert Contest, I was the judge. Monsieur Bobor presented a honey cake, Monsieur Grumbald his frozen lava. I tasted, tasted again, and tasted once more. I could not choose. I declared a tie, and went back to the palace with a perfectly fair stomach ache.
textes.Au Grand Temple, il y a des serpents de: At the Great Temple, there are stone snakes at the bottom of the stairs! And at the top, two houses, a blue one and a red one! I'm not allowed to go up. Neither are you, I bet.
textes.Au Grand Troc de l'an dernier, la chaîne: At last year's Great Swap, the chain reaches us: Caramel holds out a sardine, I hold out my carrot bread. She sniffs, goes “Mrrr”, and refuses. So I refused the sardine. First broken chain in twenty years! Bedaine sat down on the ground. Meanwhile, Mochi and Myrtille had already swapped their snacks.

At last year's Great Swap, the chain reached the two of us. Trèfle holds out her carrot bread. I say: “Mrrr. No.” I hold out my sardine. She says: “Certainly not.” And the chain broke. The first time in twenty years. Bedaine sat down on the ground. He still sighs when he sees me.
textes.Au bord de la Marmite: At the edge of the Cauldron
textes.Au bord du cratère, il y a un aigle. Un: On the edge of the crater there's an eagle. A REAL eagle, as big as a house. The golems chained her up. She cries at night… My goats can't sleep anymore.
textes.Au bout du chemin noir, un coffre de boi: At the end of the black path, a painted wooden chest: red feathers and bones. Odd luggage for going down among the dead…
textes.Au calmecac, on m'a confié le feu du tem: At the calmecac, I was entrusted with the temple fire, a fire that must never go out. I slept next to it, I woke up every hour to tend it. I learned the songs, the calendar, the great cycle of fifty-two years. And patience. You don't joke with a sacred fire. Nor with the priests watching over you.
textes.Au carrefour de Xibalba, il y a quatre c: At the crossroads of Xibalba there are four roads: red, black, white and yellow. The black road spoke: “I am the king's road.” And it was true: it goes down to the Lords; the other three go round in circles. The Twins sent a mosquito ahead of them. Kinich, the little boy, caught one: he keeps it in a gourd.
textes.Au carré ? Oh, je pourrais vous embrasse: Neat and square? Oh, I could kiss you! You're the guest every chambermaid dreams of. I'm reserving you a room in my guesthouse. The best one.
textes.Au cercle des contes, je répare mes file: At the storytelling circle, I mend my nets while Faelar tells his tales. One day he got a name wrong in a six-hundred-year-old story. I coughed, just once. He stopped, looked at me, and corrected himself. Since then, whenever he hesitates, he turns to me. I don't even need to look up.
textes.Au commencement, il n'y avait que la mer: In the beginning there was only the sea. A star fell, so tired that it fell asleep in the water. As it dreamed, it grew a seed… the Mother Tree. And we are its leaves.
textes.Au couronnement de Thorgal, Nori a regar: At Thorgal's coronation, Nori looked at my axe in front of the whole court and said, quietly but loud enough: “The third rune is upside down.” It was. The king kept the axe that way. He says it brings luck. Nori says it brings luck upside down.
textes.Au couronnement de Thorgal, la troisième: At Thorgal's coronation, the third rune on the axe Borin had forged was upside down. The right way up, it says “strength”. Upside down, it says “weariness”. I said so. Very quietly. But the Great Hall has a ready echo. Borin has never quite forgiven me. And the king is weary, in the mornings.
textes.Au couronnement, quand j'ai dit que la t: At the coronation, when I said the third rune was upside down, Borin turned red right up to his scalp. The next day, he came to my alcove with the axe and a chisel, and said: “Show me.” I showed him. He didn't fix the axe. But he has never carved a rune upside down again.
textes.Au cours de Yaya, je copie le chat. Il e: In Yaya's class, I copy the cat. He's really gifted, I promise: he lifts his paw right on the beat. One day Yaya told me: “Zoé, watch the cat, not me.” I watched the cat. The cat watched me. We did the crab step together. Yaya applauded. The cat left, offended.
textes.Au crépuscule, je monte l'escalier avec: At dusk I climb the stairs with Mister Hulotte, really slowly: one step, one question, one step, one question. One day I asked him if my papa was in the stars. He said he hadn't finished counting. So I gave a star a name, number four thousand two hundred and thirteen: Cerfeuil. He wrote it in his journal. I saw!
textes.Au crépuscule, on s'assoit sur mon banc: At dusk, we sit on my bench with a teapot, and Amélie has me taste her herbal teas. The thyme one, the rosemary one, the “broken heart” one, with my lavender. I tell her what's missing, she makes a note. Once, I told her: “A moonflower is missing.” She noted it down. We're waiting.
textes.Au crépuscule. J'apporte les tasses, toi: At dusk. I'll bring the cups, you bring the honey.
textes.Au dortoir, j'ai le lit près de la fenêt: In the dormitory, I've got the bed by the window. Oscar snores, Lin reads, Mirabelle boils stuff, and Gérard watches us from the roof. Mornings, lessons in the courtyard; afternoons, I watch Pyra's duels; evenings, I play in the square. I'm allowed one question a day to the archmage. I've got two hundred saved up.
textes.Au début, je vendais mal. Je disais : «: At first, I was bad at selling. I'd say: “Sword. Good. Fifty.” Customers left. One day, I said: “This one cut off a dragon's tail.” The customer bought it straight away. I understood: you sell a blade with a story. I don't like talking. But I talk about dragons. That's not the same.
textes.Au désert, il y avait du sable dans le p: In the desert, there was sand in the bread. I told my uncle. He said: “It cleans your teeth.” I ate all the bread. My teeth weren't any cleaner. But it was the best bread in the world, 'cause we ate it under the stars, sitting on a dune.
textes.Au désert, les caravaniers chantent auss: In the desert, the caravaneers sing too. The same songs as us, but slower. Sand slows everything down.
textes.Au désert, les caravaniers voyagent la n: In the desert, the caravaneers travel by night, to escape the heat. They have lanterns like mine, hung around the camels' necks. From afar, they look like walking stars.
textes.Au fait, tu connais {qn}, maintenant. Al: By the way, you know {qn} now. So, what's your verdict?
textes.Au fait, vous connaissez {qn}, maintenan: By the way, you know {qn} now. So, what's your verdict?
textes.Au fond de l'armoire, dans une chaussett: At the back of the wardrobe, in a sock:
textes.Au fond de la baie, il y a des pierres t: At the bottom of the bay, there are cut stones covered in seaweed. Steps, maybe. They go down towards the open sea. Matthias wants me to draw them. Underwater. With a pencil.
textes.Au fond de son échoppe, il y a un panier: At the back of his stall, there's a basket of yellow slippers he never sells. A caravan trader wanted to buy it: “Reserved. For a wedding.” What wedding? The only wedding in the souk is mine! I asked him if he had any gold thread. He laughed. Too fast, my brother. Much too fast.
textes.Au fond des Neuf Cercles coule le Phlégé: At the bottom of the Nine Circles flows the Phlegethon, the river of lava. It's beautiful, I promise. But don't stare at it too long: the raft won't wait for you to finish admiring.
At the bottom of the Nine Circles flows the Phlegethon, a river of lava. You cross it on rafts. Jump when the raft is right in front of you, not before, not after. Iron sinks. So do you.
textes.Au fond du coffre, gravé dans le bois :: At the bottom of the chest, engraved in the wood: “To the one who gave the Great Moai his eyes back, and the Hall of Song its voice. Thank you. — The Elders (and the little Moai, who helped carry).”
textes.Au fond du cul-de-sac, un coffre tout co: At the end of the dead end, a very sticky chest. Inside: a vial of sap, some coins… and a label: “Property of the slimes. Do not touch.” Too late.
textes.Au hibou ! Et tu t'es endormi au moment: At the owl! And you fell asleep when the wolf came in!
textes.Au large de Tazira, il y a des bancs de: Off Tazira, there are shoals of sardines so big the sea turns silver. The pirates say they've never seen anything like it anywhere else.
textes.Au large du village, on prend des daurad: Off the village, you catch sea bream this big. Paulo pays well for them for his bouillabaisse.
textes.Au lieu de m'apporter du poisson, Ahmed: Instead of bringing me fish, Ahmed brings back shells for Yasmine. Pink ones, twisty ones, ones that sing. My daughter has a whole jar of them. Me, I've got an empty pot. I scolded him, like when he was little. The next day, he came back with a basket of sardines… and five shells. He says it's Yasmine's tax.
textes.Au marché, Marley et moi, on a un stand: At the market, Marley and I share one stall: necklaces on the left, bananas on the right. One day a lady bought three necklaces from me. Marley gave her a whole bunch, “because she looked like family”. She left with more bananas than necklaces. I did the maths: that day, we lost money.
textes.Au mariage de Marius et d'Odette, j'ai a: At Marius and Odette's wedding, I lit the lighthouse in broad daylight, at noon, for them. The old keeper gave me a right telling-off. Odette, on the church steps, looked up and laughed. I'd never seen her laugh. Marius said: “See? He talks with his lamp, my brother.”
textes.Au moins, c'est honnête. Tes traces le d: At least that's honest. Your tracks already said so: they hesitate at every bridge. Stay near the lanterns. And if you get lost, stay put. I'll find you.
textes.Au moins, elle n'a pas peur des étincell: At least it's not scared of sparks.
textes.Au moins, tu le sais. C'est le début. Po: At least you know it. That's the start. Put your heel down last. Breathe through your nose. And don't talk. That's the hardest part.
textes.Au moins, vous êtes honnête. C'est un dé: At least you're honest. That's a start. Frost always begins with an impatience that calms down.
textes.Au nord de ton village, il y a un cercle: North of your village, there's a circle of standing stones. On my Ancients' map, there's a serpent drawn right in the middle. The ground sounds hollow there, {surnom}. A shovel would work wonders.
textes.Au nord, dans la jungle, il y a des serp: To the north, in the jungle, there are snakes. To the west, on the slopes of the volcano, jaguars. Real ones. Be careful.
textes.Au nord, les falaises. Le vent y est gla: Up north, the cliffs. The wind there is icy, even in summer. Borée goes up there to fetch his snowflakes. Not me. Cliffs don't float.
textes.Au nord, les ronces. Elles avancent d'un: To the north, the brambles. They advance one step every year. One day they'll eat the village. Nobody listens to me.
textes.Au nouvel an, je tire mes confettis du h: At New Year, I fire my confetti from the top of the clock tower. The wind carries it all the way to the highlands. The sheep are all colourful for a week.
textes.Au pas ! Au pas, j'ai dit !: Walking pace! I said walking pace!
textes.Au pied du phare, sous une pierre qui lu: At the foot of the lighthouse, under a glowing stone: an iron box full of coins, and a note: “For the next one who sees it. — T.”
textes.Au plaisir. La sortie est à votre gauche: A pleasure. The exit is on your left. As always.
textes.Au plus profond, dort Cipactli, le monst: Deepest of all sleeps Cipactli, the Earth monster: a crocodile with a thousand mouths. The gods made the world out of its body. Tezcatlipoca lost his foot to it. You, keep yours.
textes.Au poisson, Doc ! Mais du bon poisson, j: Fish, Doc! But good fish, I swear!
textes.Au prix de Kraxx. Moins un. Pour la Gard: At the Kraxx price. Minus one. For the Guard.
textes.Au prix de l'autre fois ? Non. L'autre f: At last time's price? No. Last time was a mistake.
textes.Au retour de Tazira, Boulon est descendu: Back from Tazira, Boulon climbed out of the gondola with a scratched nose. Three scratches. The harbour cats. He hadn't caught a single one. The commander looked at him and said: “Well. At least he came back.” Then she painted a little star on the gondola, like for the difficult flights. That's Boulon's star.
textes.Au retour, Boulon est descendu le nez ra: On the way back, Boulon got off with a scratched nose: three scratches, the harbour cats of Tazira. He hadn't caught a single one. Wilfried picked him up in his brass arm without a word, and Boulon wagged his tail anyway. I painted a little star on the gondola, like for the difficult flights. That's Boulon's star.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom} ! Graissez bien vos: Goodbye, {surnom}! Keep your gears well oiled.
textes.Au sommet des murailles de Dité, trois s: At the top of the walls of Dité, three figures spread their wings: the FURIES! “Nobody enters Dité!” they cry, diving at you.
textes.Au sommet du Grand Temple, offrir une ja: At the top of the Great Temple, offer a jar of rain to Tlaloc (blue shrine) and copal to Huitzilopochtli (red shrine)
textes.Au sommet du Mont Fusain: At the summit of Mount Charcoal
textes.Au sommet du Temple de Kukulkan, mettre: At the top of the Temple of Kukulkan, set the two calendar wheels to the date of the creation of the world (the great stele on the square shows it; Ah Kin, the astronomer, knows it)
textes.Au sommet du massif, il y a un endroit d: At the top of the massif, there's a spot where you can see both your islands at once. I mapped it. On a shell, naturally.
textes.Au stand, Momo fait les comptes sur une: At the stall, Momo does the accounts on a plank with a bit of charcoal. One evening he showed me: “Necklaces sold: nine. Bananas given away: forty-two.” He looked very sad. I gave him a banana. He laughed. And he wrote: “forty-three”.
