textes.Balam-qui-rate ! Tu as raté quoi, aujour: Balam-Who-Misses! What did you miss today?
textes.Balam. Tu as vu les jaguars, là-haut ?: Balam. Have you seen the jaguars up there?
textes.Balam. Ça veut dire jaguar. Je chasse le: Balam. It means jaguar. I hunt deer, peccary, turkey. The jaguar I leave alone: it's my name, not my game.
textes.Barbe-Sanglante… Le plus grand pirate de: Barbe-Sanglante… The greatest pirate of all time. He sank a hundred ships and never lost a battle. He did lose his treasure, though. Well, he hid it so well he never found it again.
textes.Barnabé ! Dix-sept traversées, pas un ro: Barnabé! Seventeen crossings, not one rock. A legend, oh yes!
textes.Barnabé ! Tu as encore salué la brume, h: Barnabé! You waved at the mist again last night.
textes.Barnabé ! Tu reviens mesurer la piste, c: Barnabé! Coming back to measure the dance floor tonight?
textes.Barnabé ? Le meilleur cartographe du roy: Barnabé? The best cartographer in the kingdom, according to him. The worst, according to the rock. We used to be friends. Used to is a long way back.
textes.Barnabé ? Un humain qui chante sur sa pl: Barnabé? A human who sings on his beach about exploits he never saw, to tunes he never learned. I adore it. I listen from afar. It's the right distance for Barnabé.
textes.Barnabé Coquillard ! Ta chanson a un cou: Barnabé Coquillard! Your song has one verse too many.
textes.Barnabé Coquillard… Un humain qui dessin: Barnabé Coquillard… A human who draws maps of things he has never seen. We are very fond of him. From a distance.
textes.Barnabé dessinait les cartes. Sa carte d: Barnabé drew the maps. His map said “open sea”. The sea said “rock”. I believed the map. Twenty-two years I've regretted it.
textes.Barnabé dit que sa carte des Anciens mon: Barnabé says his map of the Ancients shows “a golden eye in the east”. That's the Mother Tree. He has good eyes, for a human.
textes.Barnabé est passé hier soir. Il a fait t: Barnabé came by last night. He did three dance steps with Gaston on his shoulder and left again. Legend.
textes.Barnabé m'a donné un coin de terre contr: Barnabé gave me a patch of land for a few bunches. At night, he talks to my banana trees, he calls them his confidants. Me, I never listen. Well… almost never.
textes.Barnabé m'a prêté sa barque pour monter: Barnabé lent me his boat to build this wall, and he never asked me for a penny. Just that we say hello to Gaston. So we say hello to Gaston.
textes.Barnabé m'a tout appris des cabanes. Il: Barnabé taught me everything about huts. He talks a lot, he's sometimes wrong about the rocks, but his knots never give. Never.
textes.Barnabé parle à la mer comme à une vieil: Barnabé talks to the sea like an old friend. Humans say he's mad; the trees say he's kind. I believe the trees.
textes.Barnabé t'a parlé de moi ? Laisse-moi de: Barnabé told you about me? Let me guess: “it was Octave at the helm”. He's a broken record, that one.
textes.Barnabé, c'est une légende, frérot. Il a: Barnabé is a legend, bro. He did three dance steps at the party and swears he was measuring the dance floor. He recounts his shells when I walk past. I get it: we kind of do the same job.
textes.Bartholomé, le vieux perroquet de Joe, a: Bartholomé, Joe's old parrot, had caught a cold. He sneezed “jellyfish-head” every thirty seconds. I gave him a lukewarm honey tea, with a teaspoon. He pinched my nose so hard I saw stars. Joe said: “He likes you!” Bartholomé got better in two days. My nose, in a week.
textes.Basile ! Il a encore éternué pendant le: Basile! It sneezed again during the minuet.
textes.Basile ! Un génie du rien du tout, avec: Basile! A genius of absolutely nothing, with the prettiest machine at the Fair. He keeps me waiting for his giant bubble, but I know he's saving me the first seat. He just doesn't know it yet.
textes.Basile Pinceau, le peintre du village, a: Basile Pinceau, the village painter, saw the pot of blue (no. 1) floating on the Rubbed-Out Pond the day after the Great Downpour. It got stuck on a giant water lily, far from the bank. Basile swims like a stone.
textes.Basile avait réussi une bulle de deux mè: Basile had managed a two-metre bubble. I couldn't resist: I stuck my head inside! A silence, a perfectly round light, the smell of lavender… I talked to Basile for a minute, and my voice sounded like it was in a jar. He laughed so hard he dropped his bellows. Best minute of my week. Of my month, even.
textes.Basile est le voisin de stand idéal : il: Basile is the ideal stand neighbour: he laughs at all my shots, and he's never noticed what I put in his machine. Well, I think. He has these smiles, sometimes…
textes.Basile est le voisin de stand le plus ad: Basile is the sweetest and soapiest stall neighbour at the Fair. My piano owes him its cold. I forgive him every evening.
textes.Basile est un homme charmant, qui fait d: Basile is a charming man who blows charming bubbles. He said something about my box once. I forgave him. Almost.
textes.Basile est un juré merveilleux et parfai: Basile is a marvellous juror and perfectly useless: he thinks every invention is wonderful. Even the ones that explode. Especially those.
textes.Basile est à l'Étang Gommé, Lili sur la: Basile is at the Rubbed-Out Pond, Lili on the White Strand.
textes.Basile propose d'envoyer une bulle géant: Basile suggests sending a giant bubble to fetch Achille. I'm not sure that's a good idea.
textes.Basile s'est senti si coupable qu'il a i: Basile felt so guilty that he put up a screen between our two stalls. He painted it himself: bubbles everywhere, of every size, including one shaped like a heart. The screen doesn't stop the steam at all. But it's very pretty, and I've never had the heart to tell him.
textes.Basile veut aller chercher mon frère dan: Basile wants to go and fetch my brother in a bubble. He believes in it with all his heart, and that touches me. It terrifies me too. A lot.
textes.Basile, j'ai repêché le pot de bleu !: Basile, I fished out the pot of blue!
textes.Basile, qu'est-ce que vous regardez dans: Basile, what are you looking at in the pond?
Bastien! Your octopus says good evening.
textes.Bastien ! Tu es encore tout rouge, mets: Bastien! You've gone all red again, put your cap on!
textes.Bastien ? Un pêcheur qui se lève tôt et: Bastien? A fisherman who gets up early and doesn't haggle too much. We get along: he fishes, I pay. Not much.
textes.Bastien distribue des bouchons d'oreille: Bastien hands out earplugs. In front of MY sound. As if it were too loud. … And he was right about the crab. That's worse.
Bastien talked to me about fishing. Two hours. Tides, bait, mackerel. I said three words: “Yeah.” “Ah.” “Right.” He said it was the best conversation of his life. … He's nice. He's tiring. Nice people are tiring.
textes.Bastien m'a tirée de l'eau le jour de la: Bastien pulled me out of the water on the day of the biggest fright of my life. I owe him that. But I won't come to the five o'clock fishing. Ever. He knows it.
textes.Bastien m'invite à la pêche de cinq heur: Bastien invites me to the five o'clock fishing every evening. I say no every evening. But when he's out at sea, I sometimes dive near his boat and leave a nice shell on his bench. He pretends not to know who it is. I pretend to believe him. We're very good at this, the two of us.
textes.Bastien ne croit pas aux fées. Il dit «: Bastien doesn't believe in fairies. He says “of course” the way you shut a door, and it makes me a bit sad. But he's never painted over my octopus. So deep down, he believes a little.
textes.Bastien voulait un petit poisson sur sa: Bastien wanted a little fish on his sail. I painted a big purple octopus, a protective one. He shouted. He says the fish are scared of it. But he's never repainted the sail. And the day Sofia came up white as a sheet from the golden point, it was my octopus that made her laugh. It protects, like I said.
textes.Bastien, c'est le meilleur porteur de pa: Bastien's the best basket carrier on the island, and the only boy I've ever knocked into the water. He's sweet. He blushes a lot. Too much sun, I think.
Bastien's a grumpy big brother. He lends me everything, even when he doesn't know it yet. His cap looks better on me than on him, but I give it back. Sometimes.
textes.Bastien, ce matin, tu as trouvé quelque: Bastien, did you find anything on your bench this morning?
textes.Bastien, frérot ! Je te rends ta casquet: Bastien, bro! I'm giving you your cap back!
textes.Bastien. Combien, la sardine, aujourd'hu: Bastien. How much for a sardine today?
textes.Battre Ventaile. Une fois. D'une plume,: Beat Ventaile. Once. By a feather, that'll do me. And then carry a letter so fast it arrives before it's written. The queen says it's impossible. The queen has never raced me.
textes.Battre mon automate. Une seule fois, moi: To beat my automaton. Just once, myself, without tricks, in front of the whole Fair. Then I'll offer it a rematch. Politely. It will probably win. But I'll have had my evening.
textes.Battre son record à Dragon-Pixel: Beat your high score at Dragon-Pixel
textes.Beaucoup de piment ! Voilà quelqu'un qui: Lots of chilli! Now there's someone who knows how to drink! You have a warrior's throat. I'll make you mine, the real one, the one that makes the merchants of Aztlán cry.
Plenty of herbal tea, I know.
textes.Bedaine ? Le tanuki le plus rusé de la f: Bedaine? The craftiest tanuki in the forest. After me. He says it's the other way round. We've been squabbling over the title forever, and frankly, it's what keeps me awake at the market.
textes.Bedaine a encore troqué un caillou contr: Bedaine swapped a pebble for a feather again, a feather for a vial… One day he'll swap the Mother Oak for a hazelnut.
textes.Bedaine laisse des traces partout. Beauc: Bedaine leaves tracks everywhere. Lots of tracks means he's doing his shopping. I hold two things against him. But he makes me laugh. That almost makes up for it.
textes.Bedaine vous troque ce caillou-qui-chant: Bedaine swaps you this singing pebble.
textes.Bedaine, c'est le maître du troc ! Il me: Bedaine is the swap master! He finds me singing-stones, I give him hazelnuts and bits of rope. His great chain of swaps starts with me. First link!
textes.Bedaine, le tanuki du Marché aux trocs,: Bedaine, the tanuki of the Barter Market, wants to teach you the Great Swap: a pebble that, swap after swap, becomes a treasure.
textes.Bedaine. Le marchand de Ramure, avec sa: Bedaine. The Ramure merchant, with his tanuki tail. He talks more than Rachid. He doesn't want coins, only barter. He always wins, I think. I go back anyway.
textes.Belle matinée, oui. Il faut en profiter: Lovely morning, yes. Best enjoy it before the heat.
textes.Belle mer, ce matin. Je dis ça au vent,: Lovely sea this morning. I'm saying that to the wind, mind.
textes.Belle-Humeur ! Ce soir, je joue le tambo: Belle-Humeur! Tonight, I'm playing the drum for you!
textes.Belle-Humeur crie, grogne, tempête, et i: Belle-Humeur shouts, grumbles, storms, and his heart is as soft as the inside of a shell. Nobody sees it. I do. I shout hello to him every morning. He answers. Loudly.
textes.Belle-Humeur crie. Moi, je me tais. On s: Belle-Humeur shouts. I keep quiet. We get on well. He carried me out of the marsh. I've never thanked him. He wouldn't have heard.
textes.Belle-Humeur est furieux du matin au soi: Belle-Humeur is furious from morning till night and deaf from night till morning. But when he stands guard at the door of the Shark's Tooth, nobody comes in without saying hello. An excellent doorman. A passable gunner.
Belle-Humeur knocked me down once. Just once! He says it doesn't count. I say it counts. It's the only thing we agree to disagree on.
textes.Belle-Humeur m'a pris mes dents il y a t: Belle-Humeur took my teeth thirty yearth ago. We've never thpoken about that night thinthe. We thit at the thame bar, one at each end. We put up with each other. That'th already a lot, for him.
textes.Belle-Humeur veut que je chante son coup: Belle-Humeur wants me to sing his verse louder. Always louder. My fiddle isn't a cannon. But I've added a drum, just for him. He almost smiled. Almost.
textes.Belle. J'ai encore trouvé de la lavande: Lovely. I found lavender on my bench again.
textes.Belles ? Elles sont AFFICHE-NANTES ! … B: Nice? They're POSTER-PERFECT! ... Well. Pigment painted the rat, I printed the letters, and we argued about the colour for three hours. She wanted green, I wanted black. We went with green. The next Great Boucan has to be the biggest of all time, with people coming from everywhere! But our posters can't swim. You travel. You could carry three: one to Paulo, the cook of Port-Azur; one to Ulric, the innkeeper of Montjoie; and one to Tom the Fiddler, the musician at the Crâne Fendu, on Balafre. Great encounters start with a poster!
textes.Benvenuto, bienvenue ! Chez Paulo, la me: Benvenuto, welcome! Chez Paulo, the best bouillabaisse in the archipelago! The others are just soups.
textes.Bernard ? Soixante-sept ans, des mollets: Bernard? Sixty-seven, calves of steel and a stubbornness set in concrete. He doesn't run faster than I swim. But I admit he runs fast.
textes.Bernard court comme s'il avait un train: Bernard runs as if he had a train to catch. I'm very fond of him, and he worries me. He thinks I don't see him going round by the back alley.
textes.Bernard dit qu'il court plus vite que je: Bernard says he runs faster than I swim. Ridiculous. He runs faster than I run, that's all.
textes.Bernard défie quiconque de courir de la: Bernard challenges anyone to run from the fountain to the lighthouse in under a minute.
textes.Bernard joue avec nous l'après-midi. Il: Bernard plays with us in the afternoon. He points badly, but he runs well: every time a ball rolls too far, he sprints off to fetch it, shouting “hup hup hup”. Raymond and I don't bend down any more. Sometimes, to tease him, I pretend to run with him. Two steps. My knee goes hup too.
textes.Bernard, le coureur. Il fait trois tours: Bernard, the runner. He does three laps of the island a day, with a stopwatch. I did thousands with a satchel. Nobody ever timed me.
textes.Bernard, le coureur. Un retraité respect: Bernard, the runner. A respectable retiree who respects nothing, least of all my sign. He has the legs of a twenty-year-old and the cheek of a fifteen-year-old.
textes.Bernard. Il tape à ma porte à huit heure: Bernard. He knocks at my door at eight. I go to bed at six. Do the maths. I have.
textes.Bertha a la plus belle de toutes : une é: Bertha has the most beautiful one of all: an eight-pointed star. When it's lit, it scatters stars everywhere, on the sails, on the deck, on the first mate's face. Mâchefer covered in stars, {surnom}, that's worth the trip. I know Nourredine counts my lights in the evening from his terrace. So I light them all, for him.
Bertha is docked. At my quay.
Bertha does as she pleases, caïd.
textes.Berthe ! Deux pots de miel, et un hydrom: Berthe! Two pots of honey, and a mead.
textes.Berthe ! Le premier maquereau du jour !: Berthe! The first mackerel of the day!
textes.Berthe ! Une part de tarte, et pas un mo: Berthe! A slice of pie, and not a word about the nutmeg.
textes.Berthe ! Votre lucarne, cette nuit : éto: Berthe! Your skylight, tonight: shooting stars!
textes.Berthe et moi, on a grandi porte à porte: Berthe and I grew up next door to each other, in the village. She makes the best pie in the archipelago. Never criticise her pie in front of her. I tried once.
textes.Berthe fait la seule soupe de l'île qui: Berthe makes the only soup on the island that doesn't burn your tongue. She keeps the table at the back for me, far from the door. And far from certain people. She's a woman of tact.
textes.Berthe me sert mon petit-déjeuner à midi: Berthe serves me breakfast at noon without ever making a remark. Well, one or two. Her room under the roof is the best on the island for dreaming. I tell everyone. She's put the price up.
textes.Berthe me sert sa soupe douce, celle qu': Berthe serves me her mild soup, the kind you can eat without blowing on it. Pyra's, apparently, is full of chilli and hot as a volcano. I wouldn't taste it for the world. Berthe says the two are nothing alike. She smiles as she says it. She smiles a lot, Berthe.
textes.Berthe me vend son miel, je lui vends me: Berthe sells me her honey, I sell her my potions, and we each think the other is getting an excellent deal. She keeps my stool at the counter for me. She also keeps my tab. A long tab.
textes.Berthe met trop de sel dans sa soupe. Je: Berthe puts too much salt in her soup. I've been telling her for twenty years. She tells me I put too much honey in my herbal tea. She's not wrong.
textes.Berthe, c'est la raison pour laquelle je: Berthe is the reason I've been missing the tide for thirty years. Her pie, I mean. Her pie. She's the best woman on the island. The best pie. Well, you know what I mean.
textes.Beurk ! La grenouille t'a avalé…\n(Il fa:
Yuck! The frog swallowed you…
(It's pitch black, it smells of mud, and it's very, very sticky.)
Yuck. Course for the Skala anyway.
Good! Then you're already a little scribe. Write it for me on a potsherd one day: I'll file it with the great papyri. Right next to them. Not on top.
textes.Bien ! J'adore Tazira. Les gens sont gen: Good! I love Tazira. The people are nice, the sardines are tasty, and nobody yells at me. Except the first mate.
textes.Bien ! J'ai trouvé une veine d'argent. J: Good! I found a vein of silver. Then I lost it again. But I found it!
textes.Bien ! Tout va bien ! Tant que ma tante: Good! All good! As long as my aunt isn't looking.
textes.Bien caché, un petit sac de pièces ! Le: Well hidden, a little bag of coins! The captain's treasure! (He's asleep. He'll never know his parrot talked.)
Nice and hot, just as it should be.
textes.Bien le bonjour, caïd !: A very good day to you, caïd!
textes.Bien morte, Khéty ? Je vérifie, cette fo: Very dead, Khéty? I'm checking this time.
textes.Bien rangé, petit gars ? Pouce dehors ?: Tucked away nicely, little fella? Thumb outside?
textes.Bien sucré ! Voilà quelqu'un qui sait vi: Nice and sweet! Now there's someone who knows how to live. Sugar is tea's good manners. Here, I'll give you the highest foam of the day.
textes.Bien sûr ! Du cacao, du piment, un peu d: Of course! Cacao, chili, a little vanilla, and water. Sugar? What's sugar?
textes.Bien sûr ! On déterre, on déterre… Voilà: Of course! We dig, we dig… There! Grilled fish, coconut, and… oh no, that's a hot stone. Don't eat it. Well, if you want, but it crunches.
textes.Bien sûr que je me souviens de toi. Les: Of course I remember you. Elves forget nothing.
textes.Bien sûr que je me souviens. Les elfes n: Of course I remember. Elves forget nothing: sometimes that's a problem.
Of course, Tic. The other way round.
textes.Bien sûr, bien sûr. Je garde une place,: Of course, of course. I'll keep a spot, just in case.
textes.Bien sûr, moussaillon ! Doucement avec B: Of course, cabin boy! Gently with Bartholomé!
Of course. And I fish for whales.
textes.Bien sûr. Et ne te retourne pas en parta: Of course. And don't turn round on your way out.
textes.Bien sûr. J'ai le temps. Beaucoup de tem: Of course. I have time. Plenty of time.
Of course. On a separate sheet.
textes.Bien sûr. Un poing de fer. Avec des perl: Of course. An iron fist. With pearls, maybe?
textes.Bien, Amirale ! Neuf ! Et demi, des fois: Yes, Admiral! Nine! And a half, sometimes?
Yes, Admiral. A geographer. From very close up.
textes.Bien, bien ! Les affaires sont bonnes, e: Good, good! Business is good, and my neighbour Kraxx sneezes all day long. It's not my fault: it's the wind.
textes.Bien, bien, très bien. Le soleil, le son: Good, good, very good. Sun, beats, friends. What else is there?
textes.Bien, bien. Mes genoux craquent, mes cor: Well, well. My knees creak, my horns are heavy, but my memory's still here. Almost all of it. There's a little bit missing, around the year one thousand. Nothing important.
Good, good. A rune smiled at me this morning. That doesn't happen often.
textes.Bien, merci. Enfin… aussi bien qu'une Ar: Fine, thank you. Well… as fine as an Archduchess can be with three hundred files on her throne and a butler who sorts them by temperature.
textes.Bien, merci. La lumière est douce aujour: Fine, thank you. The light is soft today.
textes.Bien, merci. La lumière ondule joliment,: Fine, thank you. The light ripples nicely today.
textes.Bien, mon Archiduchesse. Je ne vous suiv: Very well, my Archduchess. I shall not follow you.
textes.Bien, monsieur le patron. Les vieux, à c: Very well, mister boss. The old ones, next to the chest. Not in the chest.
textes.Bien, mousse. Qu'est-ce que tu vois, à l: Good, cabin boy. What do you see on the horizon?
textes.Bien. Alors prends un scarabée. Non, je: Good. Then take a scarab. No, I'm joking. Well, not entirely. Luck needs a helping hand. A scarab helps.
textes.Bien. Alors tu peux danser jusqu'au mati: Good. Then you can dance till morning.
textes.Bien. Alors un soir, vous jouerez contre: Good. Then one evening, you'll play against me. Not against the automaton: against me. Human to human. I warn you, I think slowly. Bring patience, Tacquet doesn't lend any.
textes.Bien. C'est ce qu'il faut faire. Tu fera: Good. That's what you should do. You'd make a passable guard. For a human. … Don't take it the wrong way, it's a compliment.
textes.Bien. C'est la bonne réponse. Les lanter: Good. That's the right answer. The moon lanterns on the bridges are put there by Mère-Lune. For exactly that. For those who can't read tracks.
textes.Bien. C'est la bonne réponse. Tu montera: Good. That's the right answer. You'd come up to the Skala, say what you saw, and let the guard handle it. If one day you want a sabre, come and see me.
textes.Bien. De quoi d'autre veux-tu parler ?: Good. What else would you like to talk about?
textes.Bien. De quoi d'autre voulez-vous parler: Good. What else would you like to talk about?
textes.Bien. Il fait chaud. Il fait toujours ch: Fine. It's hot. It's always hot. That's good.
textes.Bien. J'ai compté mes rubis : il en manq: Fine. I counted my rubies: one's missing. As usual.
textes.Bien. J'ai dormi dans les branches, et u: Well. I slept in the branches, and a bird woke me up singing out of tune. It was charming.
textes.Bien. J'ai gardé les chiots de Flammèche: Good. I looked after Flammèche's puppies this morning. They climbed me like a mountain. I was a happy mountain.
textes.Bien. J'ai touché une pomme à cent pas c: Fine. I hit an apple at a hundred paces this morning. Ilyria said it was luck. It was not luck.
textes.Bien. J'ai trouvé un livre que je n'avai: Good. I found a book I hadn't read. That's rare.
textes.Bien. Le fer chante, aujourd'hui. Écoute: Good. The iron's singing today. Listen. … Hear it? No? Oh well.
textes.Bien. Le métier à tisser chante, le fil: Good. The loom is singing, the thread is soft. And the harp fell silent last night. Finally, a little quiet.
textes.Bien. Le noir, ce n'est que le jour qui: Good. The dark is only the day, sleeping. It doesn't bite.
textes.Bien. Le poisson, le vent, les gens qu'o: Good. Fish, the wind, the people we love: everything comes back to those who know how to wait. Except fish, in my case. But that's a special case.
Fine. The goats ate a barrel. An empty one, luckily.
textes.Bien. Les chèvres, c'est honnête : elles: Good. Goats are honest: they eat everything and they don't hide it. Don't tell Croâ, he'd sulk on the roof for three days.
textes.Bien. Les touristes sont polis cette sem: Fine. The tourists are polite this week. Except one, who asked for milk in his espresso. Here!
textes.Bien. Mes aiguilles sont affûtées. Mon e: Good. My needles are sharp. My ink is fresh. All I'm missing is some skin.
textes.Bien. Montre tes mains. … Hm. Pas d'ampo: Good. Show me your hands. … Hm. No blisters. You hold it wrong. Come back when you have blisters.
textes.Bien. On frappe, on attend, on dit qui o: Good. You knock, you wait, you say who you are. Like a dwarf. You knocked at my gate. I remember. Hard, too. Too hard.
textes.Bien. Sous l'eau, tout est calme. C'est: Fine. Underwater, everything's calm. It's on the surface that people talk too much.
textes.Bien. Te voilà apprenti d'Arcanelle. Éco: Good. So you're an apprentice of Arcanelle. Listen: six masters, six spells. Aurélien Lumen will teach you light, Pyra fire, Borée frost, Zéphyrine levitation, Théophraste telekinesis, and Mère Sauge healing. Each will ask you for something: magic isn't given, it's traded. When your spellbook has its six spells, come back to me.
textes.Bien. Très bien, même. J'ai vendu une pe: Good. Very good, even. I sold a shovel this morning. To you, maybe?
textes.Bien. Très bien, même. La nuit est douce: Good. Very good, even. The night is soft. Every street lamp I light is like a star I set down on the ground.
textes.Bien. Très bien. (Pyrus frappe le sol de: Good. Very good. (Pyrus strikes the ground with his pitchfork.) In the name of the Guard: thank you. Here, something to warm you up.
textes.Bien. Très bien. L'eau de la source du v: Good. Very good. Water from the village spring, I hope? It's the best, everybody knows. You can dance, then.
Good. Very good. The kick is clean.
textes.Bien. Très bien. Vous irez loin. Ceux qu: Good. Very good. You'll go far. People who don't count end up with buttons in their pockets instead of coins.
textes.Bien. Tu es bien le seul. Ewen me montre: Good. You must be the only one. Ewen shows me his scrapes three days later, once they've changed colour. Come whenever you like, I always have honey.
textes.Bien. Un bricoleur, c'est un futur clien: Good. A tinkerer is a future customer. A good tool changes everything, you'll see.
textes.Bien. Un peu trop bien, peut-être. Un bo: Good. A little too good, perhaps. A good sailor obeys. A very good sailor can recognise a bad order. Think about it.
textes.Bien. Une belle lame qui casse, c'est un: Good. A beautiful blade that breaks is a piece of jewellery. A sturdy blade is a friend. Always choose the friend. Hm. Atchoo.
textes.Bien. Vous aurez une ligne à vous dans l: Good. You'll have a line of your own in the register. And you'll respect the quay's hours, like everyone else. Even Fernand. Especially Fernand.
textes.Bien. Ça prend plus de temps, ça rate so: Good. It takes longer, it often goes wrong. But what you've mended, you know by heart. And you never throw it out again.
textes.Bien. … (Hector frappe, chauffe, frappe: Good. … (Hector hammers, heats, hammers again.) … There. A bronze cog, as precise as a captain's watch. Take it to Hortense.
textes.Bientôt ! Tu viendras ? Avec ton canon ?: Soon! Will you come? With your cannon?
textes.Bientôt… Tu parles comme un humain. Chez: Soon… You talk like a human. Where we live, “soon” means in fifty years. Well. If you say so. I'll iron my dress anyway.
textes.Bienvenue ! Chez nous, les poissons nage: Welcome! At our place, the fish swim all through the house: it's more cheerful. Want to feed them?
textes.Bienvenue ! Chez nous, on ne laisse pas: Welcome! Here, we never let a visitor leave without a glass of tea. The first glass is gentle as life…
textes.Bienvenue ! Je prépare le cacao. Le secr: Welcome! I'm preparing the cacao. The secret is the foam: you pour from one pot to the other, from very high. Want to try?
textes.Bienvenue ! Regarde tranquillement. Tu a: Welcome! Take your time and look around. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Bienvenue au Cabaret des Cailloux ! Tien: Welcome to the Pebble Cabaret! Here, listen to this one:
textes.Bienvenue au Café Feedback. Chocolat cha: Welcome to Café Feedback. Hot chocolate, three coins. Herbal tea, two coins. Melancholy is free. The jukebox only plays one song, but it's the right one.
Welcome to the Café de la Bielle! Gaston. Steam coffee, cog biscuits, and spring-loaded rooms upstairs. Service is by the butler. He's slow, but he never goes on strike.
textes.Bienvenue au Crâne Fendu, mon chou ! Mam: Welcome to the Crâne Fendu — the Split Skull — sweetie! Mama Grog. Here we drink, we play, we sing, and we brawl. But we pay BEFORE we brawl. What can I get you?
textes.Bienvenue au Fondouk ! Zineb. Ici, les c: Welcome to the Fondouk! Zineb. Here, the caravaneers sleep upstairs, the camels downstairs, and travellers wherever there's room. A room? A tea? A tajine?
textes.Bienvenue au Grand Concours de Grimaces: Welcome to the Great Grimace Contest! Watch closely, here we go: one, two, three… GRIMACE! … (All three pull… exactly the same face. The same one as always.) So? Who won?
textes.Bienvenue au Grand Hôtel des Embruns. Un: Welcome to the Grand Hotel des Embruns. A room with a sea view? They all have a sea view. That's the whole idea.
textes.Bienvenue au Perroquet Bleu ! Ici, la bo: Welcome to the Perroquet Bleu! Here the drinks are cool, the music is hot and the parrot is made of wood. What can I get you?
textes.Bienvenue au chantier, capitaine ! Ici,: Welcome to the shipyard, captain! Here we plane, nail, and tar… and dream of the open sea.
textes.Bienvenue au musée ! Enfin… chez moi. Ma: Welcome to the museum! Well… my home. But it's a museum. Have you seen my collection?
textes.Bienvenue chez le Disquaire ! Ici, il y: Welcome to the Record Shop! Here you'll find every record on the island. Vinyle lets me mind the shop when he goes out for some fresh air. Take your time.
textes.Bienvenue chez moi ! C'est petit, mais c: Welcome to my home! It's small, but it's warm and smells good.
textes.Bienvenue chez moi ! C'est tout rond, c': Welcome to my home! It's all round, it's all warm, and it smells lovely.
textes.Bienvenue chez moi ! Va dire bonjour à t: Welcome to my home! Go say hello to everyone. Even Grommelot. Especially Grommelot: he loves being ignored.
textes.Bienvenue chez un chevalier de Montjoie: Welcome to the home of a knight of Montjoie! I'm polishing my armor for the tournament. Want to help?
textes.Bienvenue dans la Guilde ! Le tableau de: Welcome to the Guild! The quest board is right behind you: four new contracts every day. Bring them back to me, I stamp them, and you go up in rank. And now that you're registered, the adventurers in the tavern might want to team up with you. Talk to Sister Pétronille, Violette and Sir Tancrède. All three of them have… a little problem.
textes.Bienvenue dans ma collection ! Deux mill: Welcome to my collection! Two thousand records. Pick one, I'll put it on the turntable.
textes.Bienvenue dans mon atelier ! Attention a: Welcome to my workshop! Watch out for the wires. And the sparks. And the cat. Want to help me test my machine?
textes.Bienvenue sur l'Île Al Dente !\nAu nord:
Welcome to Al Dente Island!
To the north: Mount Bolognese (it spits sauce).
To the west: the Colander Temple.
Please do not eat the signs.
textes.Bienvenue sur l'Île de Larsen !\nÀ l'oue:
Welcome to Larsen Island!
West: the Flower Camp.
East: Rainville (take an umbrella).
In the middle: the Main Stage.
textes.Bienvenue à Arcanelle, voyageur. Je suis: Welcome to Arcanelle, traveller. I am Séraphine Astrelune, the archmage. The Great Crystal told me a visitor would come by sea. It didn't tell me you'd look so… curious. That's a good sign.
textes.Bienvenue à Cliquetis, la cité des ingén: Welcome to Cliquetis, city of engineers! Héloïse Manivelle, chief engineer. Here, we invent in the morning, test in the afternoon, and repair in the evening. Sometimes in the other order.
textes.Bienvenue à L'Alambic ! Gustave Fiole, a: Welcome to the Alembic! Gustave Fiole, qualified alchemist, almost never exploded. Magic potions, star elixirs, syrups against shyness… The syrup against shyness is out of stock. Nobody dares ask for it.
textes.Bienvenue à La Forge du Canon ! Jos. Mon: Welcome to La Forge du Canon! Jos. My hearth is the old port-side cannon: I opened it up, filled it with bricks, and it heats better than a volcano. Need a blade?
textes.Bienvenue à bord, matelot ! Tu seras… de: Welcome aboard, sailor! You'll be… second sailor. Amine is first. No, wait, he's first mate. That's better than first, he said.
textes.Bienvenue à l'auberge de La Dernière Bor: Welcome to the inn of La Dernière Bordée! Pierrick, innkeeper, at your service. A table? A hammock for the night? The hammocks are new. Well, they're less than fifty years old.
textes.Bienvenue à la Chope Ardente ! La seule: Welcome to the Blazing Mug! The only tavern under a volcano. Ulfa Chope-Pleine. A fizz? Two fizzes? The whole barrel?
textes.Bienvenue, bienvenue ! Mange-Clous, cuis: Welcome, welcome! Mange-Clous, cook of the Requin Borgne. They call me Nail-Eater because I ate a nail once. By mistake. It was in the soup. It was MY soup.
textes.Bienvenue, bienvenue ! Mérit. Le pain, c: Welcome, welcome! Mérit. The bread is me; the beer is me; the gossip too. Some warm bread? It's fresh out of the oven.
textes.Bienvenue, bienvenue ! Souvenirs d'Azur: Welcome, welcome! Souvenirs d'Azur: postcards, painted shells, kites, and the finest snow globe collection in the archipelago. It never snows here, that's the funny part!
textes.Bienvenue, bienvenue au Marché de la Cal: Welcome, welcome to the Hold Market! Salomé, the best trader on the island. And the only one in Carène, but that changes nothing. Everything that floats, everything that shines, everything that sells!
textes.Bienvenue, bienvenue à Port-Azur, la per: Welcome, welcome to Port-Azur, the pearl of the archipelago! Aristide Bellanger, mayor for eighteen years, re-elected unanimously minus one vote. Colette's.
textes.Bienvenue, jeune ! Moi, je dansais déjà: Welcome, youngster! I was dancing on beaches back when your grandad was learning to walk.
textes.Bienvenue… Respire. Il reste un tapis, l: Welcome… Breathe. There's one mat left, the yellow one, by the door. Sit down, close your eyes, and listen to the wind on the canvas. Want to try?
textes.Bip ! Je fais comme Zéro. Bip !: Beep! I'm doing like Zéro. Beep!
textes.Bip, bip… clonk ! Synthé-Soda goût fruit: Beep, beep… clonk! Moon-fruit flavor Synth-Soda. Nobody knows what Moon fruits taste like.
textes.Bip-bip ! Le lecteur passe au vert : « B: Beep-beep! The reader turns green: “WELCOME, ROBOT NO. … ERROR … WELCOME ANYWAY.” The door sinks into the floor. Below, something very big breathes like an engine.
Beep. This furniture no longer belongs to you. Beep.
textes.Biscotte ! (Le petit rat saute de ton ép: Biscotte! (The little rat hops from your shoulder to his, nibbles his ear, then goes back to yours.) See? He chose you. He always goes back to your shoulder. (Petit-Pierre sniffles.) It's okay. He'll be better off with you, travelling, than here with Mange-Clous and his ladle. He's very clever, you know: when he disappears down a hole, he always comes back with something. A coin, a button, a pearl… Rats know where the treasures are. Here, my cabin boy's coins. And if you don't have a whistle yet to call your animals, take this one: Gwen carved it for me from a bone, with a dog, a cat, a rat and a pig carved around it. Whistle, and Biscotte will come back. And you'll come see me again, right? With him?
textes.Biscotte a léché la figure de Pépin et l: Biscotte licked Pépin's face and singed his fringe. His mother screamed. I burst out laughing. Pépin was over the moon: it was proof that Biscotte loved him. Since then, he's had one lock shorter than the rest. He calls it his Biscotte lock, and he won't let anyone cut it.
textes.Biscotte arrive en trottinant et te tire: Biscotte trots over and tugs your shoelace: “Shall we go?”
textes.Biscotte grimpe le long de ton bras et s: Biscotte climbs up your arm and settles on your shoulder, tail around your neck. He's at home.
textes.Biscotte m'a léché la figure et il a rou: Biscotte licked my face and singed my fringe. Mum screamed. Flammèche laughed. I was super happy: it proves he loves me. Since then, I've had one lock of hair shorter than the others. I call it my Biscotte lock.
textes.Biscotte saute de ton épaule et file ver: Biscotte hops off your shoulder and scurries home, zigzagging.
textes.Biscotte se dresse sur ton épaule, renif: Biscotte rears up on your shoulder, sniffing the salty air: “Ah, the smell of the hold!”
textes.Biscotte, un petit rat blanc et brun, vi: Biscotte, a little white and brown rat, lives in the hold of the Requin Borgne. He's the secret friend of Petit-Pierre, the cabin boy. But Mange-Clous, the cook, has sworn to throw him overboard: his cheeses keep disappearing. Petit-Pierre would like Biscotte to go off with someone kind before it's too late. To lure him out of the hold, you need aged cheese.
textes.Bizarre ? Hé ! Je t'interdis. … Bon. Un: Weird? Hey! How dare you. … Well. A little, maybe. But that's part of the charm.
Weird? Hey! How dare you. … Well. A little, maybe. But that's part of the charm.
textes.Bizarre, oui. C'est le mot. Je n'aurais: Weird, yes. That's the word. I couldn't have put it better.
textes.Bizarre, {nom} ? Tu ne {le} connais pas: Weird, {nom}? You don't know {le} like I do.
textes.Bizarre, {nom} ? Vous ne {le} connaissez: Weird, {nom}? You don't know {le} like I do.
textes.Bizarre… oui, peut-être. Mais qui ne l'e: Weird… yes, maybe. But who isn't, around here?
textes.Bière de Forgefer, ragoût de Dagna, from: Forgefer fizz, Dagna's stew, Hilda's cheese! And I buy honey and fruit. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Blanche… La couleur la plus difficile. L: White… The hardest colour. White doesn't exist, {surnom}: it takes the colour of everything that touches it. Maybe you do too. I like that.
textes.Bleu ciel ! C'est très chic, le bleu cie: Sky blue! Sky blue is very chic!
textes.Bleu ciel ! C'est un progrès, non ?: Sky blue! That's progress, isn't it?
Blue, Ori. All blue. Nothing to report.
textes.Bleue ! Le bleu des portes, des barques,: Blue! The blue of the doors, the boats, Samira's indigo… You have a fisherman's eye: you look at what floats and what protects.
textes.Bleu… oui. Je l'aurais deviné. Un bleu d: Blue… yes. I'd have guessed. A deep-bay blue: calm on top, deep underneath. I'll paint you into a corner of the sea, very small.
textes.Blorp ! Pour maman ! Elle est restée sur: Blorp! For Mama! She stayed on Gloop, she's too squishy to travel, so I send her photos of everything. But I'm missing the most important part: the people down below! The real Heavyfeet, on their islands! I don't dare go down. I'm green, I wobble, and the last time I said hello to a fisherman, he yelled “A GIANT JELLY!” and jumped into the water. Could you do it? Take my holo-camera. Photograph the mayor of Port-Azur, the lady from the pirate tavern, the Baron of Montjoie and the crested granny of Boucan. Four corners of the archipelago! Mama will bounce for joy!
textes.Bobor casse une brioche tous les jours à: Bobor breaks a brioche every day at four o'clock, and he leaves it on the edge of the counter. He says it's an accident. He has accidents every day!
textes.Bobor dit que ses gâteaux sont meilleurs: Bobor says his cakes are better than my frozen lava. He eats three cups every time he comes. Of my frozen lava. To check, he says.
textes.Bobor fait des brioches très honnêtes et: Bobor makes very decent brioches and honey cakes that are… all right. He claims they're as good as my frozen lava. He eats three bowls of it every time he comes. To check, he says.
textes.Bobor m'achète de la cannelle de feu pou: Bobor buys fire cinnamon from me for his brioches. One day, he put in three times too much, by mistake. The brioches were smoking. The customers loved them, and now he makes them every Friday: the “smoking brioche”. Bobor says it's our joint invention. I say it's mostly his. He insists.
textes.Bobor me donne la première brioche de ch: Bobor gives me the first brioche of every batch, in exchange for a story. It's been going on for forty years. It's the best deal of my life. And the warmest.

Bobor gives me the first brioche of every batch, in exchange for a story. It's been going on for forty years. So I owe him… let's see… fourteen thousand six hundred stories. I made half of them up along the way. He hasn't noticed a thing.
textes.Bobor, c'est le boulanger du Four Éterne: Bobor is the baker at the Eternal Oven. He's all round and smells of brioche. Every day at four o'clock, a brioche breaks by accident at the edge of his counter. It's a very good accident.
textes.Bobor, mon voisin de gauche, sent la bri: Bobor, my neighbour on the left, smells of brioche all day long. I supply him with fire cinnamon; every day at four o'clock he gives Pépin brioches broken “by accident”. We get along very well.
textes.Bof. Gaston boude, la mer est grise dans: Meh. Gaston is sulking, the sea is grey inside my head, and I've lost my favourite spoon.
textes.Bois de l'eau ! Danser au soleil, ça ass: Drink some water! Dancing in the sun dries you out. Water from the village spring is the best.
textes.Bon bois. Droit, sec, solide. Voilà ving: Good wood. Straight, dry, solid. Here's twenty coins. And… thank you, {surnom}.
Fair winds, and keep your purse shut.
textes.Bon vent, va. Assieds-toi, j'en ai une n: Fair winds, you old so-and-so. Sit down, I've got a new one.
textes.Bon vent, {surnom} ! Et méfie-toi des li: Fair winds, {surnom}! And watch out for the vines on the right.
textes.Bon vent. Et si tu vois Barnabé… ne lui: Fair winds. And if you see Barnabé… don't tell him anything.
textes.Bon, d'accord : qu'est-ce qui est gris,: All right, fine: what's grey, very tall, and doesn't move? … Me when I'm asleep. And me when I'm awake. Hee hee!
textes.Bon, par où on va maintenant ?: So, which way do we go now?
textes.Bon, pour la traversée, je prendrai peut: Well, for the crossing, maybe I'll take a rowing boat. I'll row fast. That counts, right?
textes.Bon, pour {objet}, ça fera {prix}. Clou,: Right, for {objet}, that'll be {prix}. Clou, put that away. No, don't eat it.
textes.Bon. Alors il est trop cher, comme toujo: Good. Then it's too expensive, as always.
textes.Bon. BON ! Prends-le. Gratuitement. Tu m: Fine. FINE! Take it. For free. You wore me down. But don't tell anyone: I have a reputation as a businesswoman. Well, businessman. Anyway.
Fine. Ten arches. Long ones, then.
textes.Bon. Et cette anisette, dimanche ?: Fine. And that lemonade, on Sunday?
textes.Bon. Il était une fois un hibou qui avai: All right. Once upon a time there was an owl who had lost his night…
textes.Bon. Je te le dis à toi, {surnom}. Chaqu: All right. I'm telling you, {surnom}. Every week, I write Lucas a letter. I don't sign it Lola. I sign it “The Seagull”. Sometimes I wonder if he thinks a real seagull is writing to him. That would be just like him. I don't dare talk to him, because if he said no… As long as I don't ask anything, he can't say no.
textes.Bon. Puisque c'est vous, {surnom}. Chaqu: Well. Since it's you, {surnom}. Every Friday, for two years, Hector has come to dinner at my place. In a clean shirt. The second sea bream is for him. I don't tell anyone, because here a story once told no longer belongs to those who live it: it belongs to Rosalie. This one, I'm keeping. It's the only true stone I've found here.
textes.Bon. Tiens, une brioche. Et pas de greno: All right. Here, a brioche. And no frogs in the dough trough.
Fine. A drop. A little one.
textes.Bon. Une. Petite. Et tu ne le dis à pers: Fine. One. Small. And you don't tell anyone.
textes.Bondi ? Un lapin qui court vite et qui l: Bondi? A rabbit who runs fast and says so even faster. Three carrots, not one more, but a head as big as a pumpkin. He's cute, in his vanity. Shh.
textes.Bondi est mon voisin, dans l'arbre du su: Bondi is my neighbour, in the south tree. The night before his first cup, he knocked on my door at midnight: “Pépin, your drum is making my carrots shake.” So I moved my practice behind the bakery. He won the next day. He says it was thanks to the quiet. I say it was thanks to me.
textes.Bondi mange trois carottes avant chaque: Bondi eats three carrots before every race. He says it makes you run faster. I think it just makes… three fewer carrots.
textes.Bondi, c'est le champion. Il est rapide,: Bondi's the champion. He's fast, he's nice, he's annoying. Three times I've seen his back, and it's a very fine back, I admit. This time I'll see his snout.
textes.Bondi, mon petit frère, le champion. Je: Bondi, my little brother, the champion. I'm so proud of him my apron strings could burst. But oh, is he vain! Three carrots, not one more… but four slices of toast, if you please.
textes.Bonjour ! Au Pain Doré, tout sort du fou: Good morning! At the Pain Doré, everything's fresh from the oven. Just smell that!
textes.Bonjour ! Bonjour ! C'est pour toi, ça :: Hello! Hello! That's for you: you wanted a parrot that says hello. Bartholomé is practising. Well, he's trying.
textes.Bonjour ! Café de la Place, installez-vo: Hello! The Square Café, make yourself comfortable. A coffee? This is the best seat for watching the town go by.
textes.Bonjour ! Des fleurs ? Pour quelqu'un de: Hello! Flowers? For someone special? Everyone's special, so take two.
textes.Bonjour ! Du courrier pour vous ? Non. M: Hello! Any mail for you? No. But I check every morning anyway.
textes.Bonjour ! Excuse le désordre. Enfin, l'o: Hello! Excuse the mess. Well, the order. Well… everything's on the ceiling, you know.
textes.Bonjour ! Halima, potière. Plats à tajin: Hello! Halima, potter. Tajine dishes, jugs, cups, bowls. All made from the clay of the wadi, fired in my mother's kiln. Careful when you turn around.
Hello! Dr Roux's herbal shop. A graze, a sunburn, a broken heart? I have a tea for everything.
textes.Bonjour ! Ix Sak. Je tisse, je teins, je: Hello! Ix Sak. I weave, dye and embroider the huipils of the whole village. These colours? Red from cochineal, blue from indigo, yellow from flowers. And macaw feathers, for festivals.
textes.Bonjour ! Je m'appelle Nebet ! J'ai huit: Hello! My name's Nebet! I'm eight and a half! Where are you from? Have you seen a cat? A ginger cat, with a bent ear? His name's Miou!
textes.Bonjour ! Je suis Grigri, le virus le mo: Hello! I'm Grigri, the cheapest virus in the world!
textes.Bonjour ! Je suis Pimprenelle, la plus g: Hello! I'm Pimprenelle, the greatest magician in the village! Well… when I have my wand.
textes.Bonjour ! La Poste de Port-Azur, lettres: Hello! The Port-Azur Post Office: letters, parcels and telegrams. Writing to someone?
textes.Bonjour ! Mirabelle, apprentie alchimist: Hello! Mirabelle, apprentice alchemist. Want a potion? They've all gone wrong. That's what makes them unique. This one makes you sneeze bubbles. That one turns your voice into a duck's for an hour.
textes.Bonjour ! Nenetl ! Je joue du huehuetl,: Hello! Nenetl! I play the huehuetl, the big drum, the teponaztli, the slit drum, and the clay flute. And the conch shell, when Ehécatl asks me to!
textes.Bonjour ! Pas trop de bobos aujourd'hui: Hello! Not too many bumps and scrapes today?
textes.Bonjour ! Pivoine, herboriste. Tu as l'a: Hello! Pivoine, herbalist. You look tired… No? Then you soon will be, and you'll come back to see me. Mist tea for sleeping, moon tea for dreaming.
textes.Bonjour ! Prudence Touche. Voici mon pia: Hello! Prudence Touche. Here is my mechanical piano: it plays by itself, turns its own pages, and bows at the end. Sometimes the audience applauds by itself too.
textes.Bonjour ! Reculez d'un pas. Encore un. V: Hello! Take a step back. One more. There. Miss Sulfura, flame teacher at the Infernal Academy. I don't bite, but my pupils do spit, sometimes. Sparks. By accident.
textes.Bonjour ! Samira. Soie, coton, laine du: Hello! Samira. Silk, cotton, wool from the north, desert dyes: saffron, indigo, madder. Touch it, it's soft as a cloud.
textes.Bonjour ! Tu as un bout de fromage ? Mêm: Hello! Do you have a bit of cheese? Even a small one?
textes.Bonjour ! Tu tombes bien, c'est l'heure: Hello! You've come at just the right time, it's breakfast. Are you hungry?
textes.Bonjour ! Une table ? Je vous apporte la: Hello! A table? I'll bring you the menu. There's only one menu, it's written on the blackboard.
textes.Bonjour ! Venez voir, j'ai presque fini: Hello! Come and see, I've almost finished the lighthouse.
textes.Bonjour ! Vous voulez des potins ? J'ai: Hello! Want some gossip? I've got gossip.
textes.Bonjour ! Xóchitl, la Fleur ! Je cultive: Hello! Xóchitl, the Flower! I tend the chinampas, the floating gardens. We pile lake mud onto reed mats, plant willows at the corners to hold it all together, and things grow! Maize, beans, squash, chillies, flowers!
textes.Bonjour bonjour ! Dis, toi, tu te lèves: Morning, morning! Say, are you an early riser?
textes.Bonjour bonjour ! Gaston et moi discutio: Hello, hello! Gaston and I were just talking about you. Well, mostly Gaston.
textes.Bonjour bonjour ! Gérard Dupuis, en vaca: Hello hello! Gérard Dupuis, on holiday with my wife and the little one. May I take a photo? Ah, no, I've lost my camera. What a nuisance.
textes.Bonjour bonjour ! Levée à cinq heures, f: Morning, morning! Up at five, oven lit, dough kneaded. Mochi steals the cakes… Mochi! Put that down! Pépin practises his drum behind the bakery, and the dough rises in time. And Caramel… ever since the Great Swap chain broke between us, we greet each other with the tips of our whiskers. We have to: our girls are inseparable.
textes.Bonjour bonjour ! Professeur Augustin Bo: Hello, hello! Professor Augustin Boum! Don't stand there, I'm in the middle of an experiment. Stand there. No, there. Further. Further still. Perfect.
textes.Bonjour bonjour ! Trèfle, boulangère. Pa: Hello hello! Trèfle, baker. Carrot bread, mooncake… Everything's fresh from the oven, everything's warm. Mochi! Put that cake down! … Sorry. That's my daughter.
textes.Bonjour bonjour, Pépin. Le pain est chau: Morning, morning, Pépin. The bread's hot.
Good morning first. Then three coffees.
textes.Bonjour docteur ! Mes temps sont en bais: Morning, Doctor! My times are going down!
textes.Bonjour quand même, Grommelot ! Six pièc: Good morning anyway, Grommelot! Six coins a shard?
textes.Bonjour, Amirale ! J'ai sonné neuf heure: Morning, Admiral! I rang nine o'clock on the dot!
textes.Bonjour, Archimage ! Je vous ai apporté: Good morning, Archmage! I brought you an apple.
textes.Bonjour, Basile. Vous avez cette tête… v: Hello, Basile. You've got that look… you've got a new bubble.
textes.Bonjour, Bramm. Tu as une chèvre sur l'é: Morning, Bramm. You've got a goat on your shoulder.
textes.Bonjour, Brume ! Tu sais déjà ce que j'a: Hello, Brume! Do you already know what I did this morning?
textes.Bonjour, Caelan. Tu as bien dormi ? Ah n: Morning, Caelan. Sleep well? Oh no, that's right, you were playing.
textes.Bonjour, Coquille ! Pas de récif à l'hor: Morning, Coquille! No reef on the horizon!
textes.Bonjour, Doyenne. Halo m'envoie vous sal: Hello, Elder. Halo sent me to greet you.
Good morning, Faelar. Three rays this morning.
textes.Bonjour, Fil-de-Fer ! Pas de trois-mâts: Morning, Fil-de-Fer! No three-masters in the sky?
textes.Bonjour, Frère Cendrin ! Je viens emprun: Morning, Brother Cendrin! I've come to borrow three embers!
textes.Bonjour, Gaston. Le sandwich est prêt ?: Hello, Gaston. Is the sandwich ready?
textes.Bonjour, Gorgoth. Chut. Un nouveau recue: Hello, Gorgoth. Shh. A new collection?
textes.Bonjour, Grommelot ! Un petit nectar pou: Morning, Grommelot! A little nectar to sweeten your mood?
textes.Bonjour, Grommelot… Merci pour la coquil: Morning, Grommelot… Thank you for the nutshell.
textes.Bonjour, Héloïse ! C'est déjà le printem: Good day, Héloïse! Is it spring already?
textes.Bonjour, Isaac. Le stock du mois ?: Good day, Isaac. This month's stock?
textes.Bonjour, Madame Bricolette. Mes moteurs: Good day, Madame Bricolette. How are my engines?
Good morning, Your Majesty. Your flower has had its drink.
textes.Bonjour, Marée. Les laminaires sont bell: Good morning, Marée. Is the kelp nice today?
textes.Bonjour, Maître Filandre ! Je viens just: Good morning, Master Filandre! I've just come to read.
textes.Bonjour, Maître Lumen. Vous avez respiré: Good morning, Master Lumen. Did you breathe?
textes.Bonjour, Maître Rivet. Il va très bien,: Good day, Master Rivet. Your son is doing very well.
textes.Bonjour, Maître Rivet. Je sais ce que vo: Good morning, Master Rivet. I know what you're going to say.
Hello, Moustache. I read the mud.
textes.Bonjour, Mère Sauge ! Vous portez l'écha: Good morning, Mother Sage! You're wearing the scarf!
textes.Bonjour, Mère Sauge. Rien de brûlé, rega: Good morning, Mother Sage. Nothing burnt, look.
textes.Bonjour, Mélisse… J'ai un peu de rosée d: Morning, Mélisse… I've got a little moon dew.
Good morning, Octave. Your kapok tree says hello.
Good morning, Orophin. I'm heading north.
textes.Bonjour, Perlée. Ma fleur a bu ?: Good morning, Perlée. Has my flower had its drink?
textes.Bonjour, Pimprenelle. Tu allumes toujour: Hello, Pimprenelle. Do you still light the lanterns with a snap of your fingers?
textes.Bonjour, Pip. Ta question du jour ?: Hello, Pip. Your question of the day?
textes.Bonjour, Pélagos ! Une sur trois, promis: Morning, Pélagos! One in three, promise!
textes.Bonjour, Pépin. Tu sais ta leçon d'histo: Good morning, Pépin. Do you know your history lesson?
textes.Bonjour, Rita. Toujours dans vos cartes: Good morning, Rita. Still in your cards?
textes.Bonjour, Rita. Vous n'avez rien vu, j'es: Good morning, Rita. You haven't seen anything, I hope?
textes.Bonjour, Thalion. Non, je ne te dirai pa: Good morning, Thalion. No, I won't tell you.
textes.Bonjour, amiral des mouettes ! Elles t'o: Hello, admiral of the gulls! Do they obey you now? They still don't obey me.
textes.Bonjour, bonjour ! Aurélien Lumen, maîtr: Hello, hello! Aurélien Lumen, master of light, astronomer, and incidentally the only one here who sleeps during the day. Did you see the sky last night? No? What a shame. It was magnificent.
textes.Bonjour, bonjour ! Bobor, boulanger du F: Hello, hello! Bobor, baker of the Eternal Oven! My oven hasn't gone out in four hundred years: my great-great-grandfather lit it with an ember from the Ember Heart. An ember brioche? It's just out of the oven. It's hot. Always.
textes.Bonjour, bonjour ! Ernest, gardien du té: Hello, hello! Ernest, cable car keeper. Two cabins, one cable, forty seconds from the port to the city. Get in when the cabin is in the station, and don't lean out. Above all, don't lean out.
textes.Bonjour, bonjour ! Lumina, la lanternièr: Hello, hello! Lumina, the lantern-maker! Every lantern in Pandémonia, I make it: the little ones, the big ones, the round ones, the pointy ones, and the city's seven Great Lanterns. Look: this one's shaped like a horn!
textes.Bonjour, bonjour ! Philémon Lunette, car: Hello, hello! Philémon Lunette, cartographer. I draw the islands that others discover. It's less dangerous. Although… this island cost me three quills and a toe.
textes.Bonjour, bonjour… Yum Kab, gardien des a: Hello, hello… Yum Kab, keeper of the bees. My bees have no sting. They're gentle, like me. Want to taste the honey? It tastes of jungle flowers.
textes.Bonjour, jeune homme. Une demi-taille, t: Good morning, young man. Still half a size?
textes.Bonjour, jeune personne. Quelle heure es: Good day, young person. What time is it? Oh, forgive me. Nobody knows any more, around here.
textes.Bonjour, les abeilles ! … Elles m'ont en: Hello, bees! … Did they hear me?
textes.Bonjour, madame Colette ! Et ce pot, auj: Good day, Madame Colette! And that jar, today?
textes.Bonjour, maître. Le corail mord toujours: Good morning, master. Does the coral still bite?
textes.Bonjour, maître. Vous avez l'air en form: Good day, master. You look well.
textes.Bonjour, mon petit ! Attention où tu met: Hello, dear! Watch where you step: there's a cat everywhere.
textes.Bonjour, mon petit. Fais attention où tu: Hello, little one. Mind where you step: there are my ash peppers, and there my sulphur roses. Mother Brasille, gardener. I've tended these gardens for three hundred years. They're the only gardens in the world you water with hot water.
textes.Bonjour, mon petit. Je tricote des pulls: Hello, dear. I knit plaid sweaters for the whole street. When it rains, you need to be warm. And when it doesn't rain… it rains anyway, here. Want a pair of socks? I have too many.
textes.Bonjour, mon petit. Mère Sauge. Tu as un: Hello, little one. Mother Sage. You look a bit peaky, you do. Are you eating enough? Here, chew this mint leaf. It's good for everything, except hiccups.
textes.Bonjour, monsieur Échec. Votre automate: Hello, Mr Checkmate. Is your automaton well?
textes.Bonjour, petite étoile. Combien de quest: Good morning, little star. How many questions today?
textes.Bonjour, professeur ! Vos sourcils vont: Good day, Professor! How are your eyebrows?
textes.Bonjour, professeur. Toujours pas monté: Good morning, Professor. Still haven't gone up to see my grandfather?
textes.Bonjour, prêtresse ! Je cours, je cours: Good morning, priestess! I'm running, I'm running!
textes.Bonjour, s'il te plaît, merci : trois mo: Hello, please, thank you: three more words, Ursule.
textes.Bonjour, voyageur ! Bienvenue chez nous: Hello, traveller! Welcome to our home!
textes.Bonjour, voyageur. Citlali, l'Étoile. J': Hello, traveller. Citlali, the Star. I teach at the calmecac, the school where you learn the songs, the calendars, writing in pictures. Our books unfold like a folding screen. We call them codices.
textes.Bonjour, {surnom}. J'ai fini le chapitre: Hello, {surnom}. I've finished chapter twelve. There's a chapter thirteen. I'm very happy.
textes.Bonjour, {surnom}. La table du coin est: Hello, {surnom}. The corner table is free.
textes.Bonjour, {surnom}. Tu viendras danser, c: Hello, {surnom}. Will you come and dance tonight?
textes.Bonjour-bonjour ! Brindille, factrice !: Hello-hello! Brindille, postwoman! I fly, I deliver, I'm off again! Letters, parcels, postcards, love notes, bills, and once a cheese, but I don't talk about that any more. Got any post? No? Shame. Right, see you! … No, wait, I'll stay a bit. You look nice.
textes.Bonjour. Ambroise Échec. Mon automate n': Hello. Ambroise Échec. My automaton has never lost a game. Would you like to try? No? Wise choice.
textes.Bonjour. Anouk, la guérisseuse. Mon infi: Hello. Anouk, the healer. My infirmary is on the lower deck, between the hammocks. Seaweed, honey, and plenty of patience. Are you hurt?
textes.Bonjour. Driss. Je ne parle pas beaucoup: Hello. Driss. I don't talk much. Neither does the sea. We get along.
textes.Bonjour. Hapou. Je cultive l'orge, le bl: Hello. Hapou. I grow barley, wheat and flax on the south bank. And I chase crocodiles out of my fields. Mostly that, these days.
textes.Bonjour. Je m'appelle Ortie, j'ai neuf a: Hello. My name is Ortie, I'm nine, and I'm going to be the greatest inventor in Pandémonia. After Zigomar. No: before Zigomar. You can write that down.
textes.Bonjour. Margot. J'ai huit ans et demi e: Hello. Margot. I'm eight and a half and I'm an engineer. Well, an apprentice. Léonce does the rockets, I do the calculations. Without me, his rockets would make even more smoke.
textes.Bonjour. Nolwenn, voilière. Tu vois les: Hello. Nolwenn, sailmaker. See the red and blue awnings all over Carène? Those are my old sails. I re-sew them, re-cut them, give them a second life.
textes.Bonjour. Nourredine, lanternier. Toutes: Hello. Nourredine, lantern maker. Every lantern in Tazira, in the souk, on the square, in the houses, comes out of my workshop. In the evening, the town lights up thanks to me.
textes.Bonjour. Perles, pierres, or ancien. J'a: Hello. Pearls, gems, antique gold. I buy too, if you have any treasures.
textes.Bonjour. Tiyi. Je tisse le lin, le plus: Hello. Tiyi. I weave linen, the finest on the river: so fine you can see the light through it. My daughter, Nebet, is running around somewhere. She's always running around somewhere.
textes.Bonjour. Toujours une demi-taille de tro: Good morning. Still half a size too big?
Good morning. Three coffees. Thank you.
textes.Bonjour. Tu as réfléchi au problème du m: Hello. Have you thought about the perpetual motion problem? I have. It's impossible. Don't tell Mr Cogne.
textes.Bonjour. Vespérine, apothicaire. Potions: Hello. Vespérine, apothecary. Sap potions, magic potions, star elixirs. Everything labelled, dated and tested. On me. Don't worry about the green of my eyes: it's natural. Well, I think so.
textes.Bonjour. Wilfried Ressort. Et voici Boul: Hello. Wilfried Ressort. And this is Boulon, man's best friend… mechanical edition. He fetches, he gives his paw, he sits up and begs. He doesn't pee everywhere: that's his big advantage.
textes.Bonjour. Épicerie fine. On touche avec l: Good day. Fine groceries. Look with your eyes, not your hands.
textes.Bonjour. … Bonjour ! Bonjour, bonjour, b: Hello. … Hello! Hello, hello, hello! Sorry. It's been so long. (His voice is a little deep, a little crackly, like an old radio.) Thank you, my friend. Mio will be so happy. And Cargo… he kept it for me, didn't he? He keeps everything, that big softie. Here: these are the two sodas I had in my treasure hatch. For twenty years. They still sparkle.
textes.Bonjour… Attention où tu marches, chaque: Hello… Watch where you step, every dewdrop has a name.
textes.Bonjour… Pardon, je ne suis pas de très: Hello… Sorry, I'm not very good company. Hugo. I'm… on my honeymoon. Well, I was.
textes.Bonjour… Philibert Vis. Inventeur. Enfin: Hello… Philibert Vis. Inventor. Well, almost. Every idea I have, someone's already had it. Yesterday, I invented the wheel. It already existed.
textes.Bonne ! Le four chauffe bien, la pâte lè: Good! The oven is hot, the dough is rising. What more could you ask?
textes.Bonne ! Les maquereaux mordent, et aucun: Good! The mackerel are biting, and no gargoyle raided my stall this morning. Touch basalt.
textes.Bonne ! On est sortis à cinq heures, ren: Good! We went out at five, came back at ten, holds full. Now I'm asleep on my feet.
textes.Bonne garde, Thalion ! Je te joue quelqu: Good watch, Thalion! Shall I play you something?
Have a nice day! Enjoy the sunshine.
textes.Bonne nouvelle : mer d'huile aujourd'hui: Good news: sea like glass today, just how you like it. Even the goat would have held on.
textes.Bonne nuit, mon petit veilleur. Tiens, t: Goodnight, my little night watchman. Here, your mint.
textes.Bonne nuit. Dors au chaud : les lanterne: Good night. Sleep warm: the lanterns watch over the city.
textes.Bonne nuit. Le Grand Cristal veille sur: Good night. The Great Crystal watches over us.
textes.Bonne nuit. Le Léviathan craque, mais il: Good night. The Léviathan creaks, but it holds.
textes.Bonne nuit. Le soleil voyage sous le mon: Good night. The sun travels beneath the world, but it will return.
textes.Bonne nuit. Si vous entendez une explosi: Good night. If you hear an explosion, it's Professor Boum. Go back to sleep.
textes.Bonne nuit. Écoute bien : ce sont les ta: Good night. Listen closely: those are the moon drums. They'll rock you till morning.
textes.Bonne nuit. Écoute la fête, elle dure ju: Good night. Listen to the party, it goes on until midnight.
textes.Bonne route ! Et si tu te perds dans la: Safe travels! And if you get lost in the mist, follow the lanterns.
textes.Bonne réponse. On alerte d'abord, on dis: Right answer. Alarm first, talk after. Even if it's Hulotte. Especially if it's Hulotte.
textes.Bonne réponse. Tiens : un accord de ré,: Right answer. Here: a D chord, just for you. Tonight, at the Perroquet, I'll play you three more.
textes.Bonne réponse. Un équipage fidèle te ram: Right answer. A loyal crew will bring a ship home, even in pieces. The reverse isn't true. You'd make a good first mate.
textes.Bonne soirée. Et couvrez-vous : il fait: Good evening. And wrap up warm: it's chilly, barely fifty degrees.
textes.Bonne, Capitaine ! Et pas une gargouille: Good, Captain! And not a gargoyle in sight!
textes.Bonne, tant que Chak garde sa balle loin: Good, as long as Chak keeps his ball away from my pots.
textes.Bonne, tant que les chiots de Flammèche: Good, as long as Flammèche's puppies don't come digging in my flowerbeds. They bury bones under my lava begonias. I've dug up eleven bones this month. And a shoe.
textes.Bonne. J'ai sorti une fournée parfaite c: Good. I took a perfect batch out of the kiln this morning. Not a single crack.
textes.Bonsoir ! Il me reste deux croissants, j: Good evening! I've got two croissants left, you can have them half price.
textes.Bonsoir, Amélie. Toujours pas de corail: Good evening, Amélie. Still no coral?
textes.Bonsoir, Basile. Il reste de la place po: Good evening, Basile. Any room left for nothing wrapped in wood?
Good evening, Berthe. The table at the back.
textes.Bonsoir, Ernest. Un café, comme d'habitu: Good evening, Ernest. A coffee, as usual.
textes.Bonsoir, Gaston. La bouteille de nuit ?: Good evening, Gaston. The night bottle?
textes.Bonsoir, Gorgoth. Un poème pour toi, sur: Good evening, Gorgoth. A poem for you, on the bench.
textes.Bonsoir, Lilas ! Prête pour la lune ?: Evening, Lilas! Ready for the moon?
textes.Bonsoir, Lulu. Nos champignons brillent: Good evening, Lulu. Are our mushrooms glowing nicely?
textes.Bonsoir, Mama. Votre soupe était parfait: Good evening, Mama. Your soup was perfect last night.
textes.Bonsoir, Maître Filandre. Je rapporte le: Good evening, Master Filandre. I'm bringing back volume three.
textes.Bonsoir, Mère-Lune ! Votre cape va bien: Good evening, Mère-Lune! How's your cloak?
textes.Bonsoir, Mère-Lune. Vous m'avez regardée: Good evening, Mother Moon. Did you watch me?
textes.Bonsoir, Nausicaa. La marée est haute ?: Good evening, Nausicaa. Is the tide high?
textes.Bonsoir, Nox ! Je joue ta valse ?: Good evening, Nox! Shall I play your waltz?
textes.Bonsoir, Nox ! Ta valse, ce soir ?: Good evening, Nox! Your waltz, tonight?
textes.Bonsoir, Nox ! Tout est allumé ?: Good evening, Nox! Is everything lit?
textes.Bonsoir, Nox. Rayon sept. Un nouveau rec: Good evening, Nox. Shelf seven. A new collection.
textes.Bonsoir, Philibert ! Vous m'avez gardé m: Good evening, Philibert! Did you save my seat?
textes.Bonsoir, Sylvain. Bonne table, ce soir ?: Good evening, Sylvain. Good table tonight?
textes.Bonsoir, Triton. Je chante la haute ?: Good evening, Triton. Shall I sing the high tide?
textes.Bonsoir, Ursule ! Juste des fers un tout: Evening, Ursule! Just horseshoes a teeny bit lighter?
textes.Bonsoir, Ysolde ! Les pierres brillent b: Good evening, Ysolde! The stones are shining nicely tonight.
textes.Bonsoir, Ysolde. Je peux leur lire le ch: Good evening, Ysolde. May I read them chapter eight?
textes.Bonsoir, Ysolde. Ta journée de demain se: Good evening, Ysolde. Tomorrow will be a calm day for you.
textes.Bonsoir, capitaine sans cloche. Par la q: Good evening, captain without a bell. By the keel, still afloat?
textes.Bonsoir, la patronne ! Le poêle tient le: Evening, boss! Is the stove holding up?
Good evening, my girl. It smells good tonight.
textes.Bonsoir. Mon voisin humain trouve que je: Good evening. My human neighbor finds me good company.
Good evening. Stay away from the lake.
textes.Bonsoir. Sylvain. On m'appelle Doigts-d': Good evening. Sylvain. They call me Doigts-d'Argent — Silver-Fingers. Here, at the big table, we play big and lose everything. Do take a s… sorry: sit down. The dice are waiting for you.
textes.Bonsoir… ah non, bonjour. Pour une music: Good evening… ah no, good morning. For a musician, it's always a little bit evening. Calcine, violinist of the Great Square. I play for the dancers, for the storyteller, for the passers-by. And for the lanterns, when nobody's around. They adore waltzes.
textes.Bonsoir… ou bonjour ? J'ai perdu la noti: Good evening… or good morning? I've lost all track of time, that's a good sign.
textes.Bon… avant le Zéphyr quand il a le vent: Well… before the Zéphyr when it's sailing into the wind. Still counts. Hop.
textes.Bon… parce que c'est toi. Un petit geste: Well… because it's you. A little something off.
textes.Bon… parce que tu as une bonne tête. Un: Fine… because you have a nice face. A little discount. But don't tell anyone, I have a reputation.
textes.Bon… pour le premier visiteur depuis mil: Well… for the first visitor in a thousand years, a little discount.
textes.Bon… pour toi, un petit rabais. Les arbr: Well… for you, a small discount. The trees saw nothing.
textes.Bon… si tu changes d'avis, tu sais où me: Well… if you change your mind, you know where to find me.
textes.Borin Barbe-de-Fer ? Un nain qui croit q: Borin Barbe-de-Fer? A dwarf who thinks good iron grows under his mountain. Good iron is made by the arm. He forges well. I'll never tell him so.
textes.Borin a encore volé une louche de ragoût: Borin pinched another ladle of stew before noon again. I saw him. I see everything.
textes.Borin dit qu'il est le meilleur forgeron: Borin says he's the best blacksmith on the mountain. Borin says a lot of things.
Borin is the best blacksmith in the world. He says so, and it's true. He shouts a lot. But when I get it wrong, he shows me. Every time. Even while shouting.
textes.Borin et Grimli se disputent depuis cent: Borin and Grimli have been arguing for a hundred years over who has the finest beard. It's me.
textes.Borin forge bien, je ne dis pas. Mais il: Borin forges well, I'll grant you. But he talks about his beard as if it were the city gates. Mine burnt because of him, and it grew back finer. That's a fact.
textes.Borin grave trois runes sur ta lame et l: Borin engraves three runes on your blade and feeds them at the heart of the magma. They light up, blue, and never go out again. “A king's blade, lad.”
textes.Borin rive des écailles de bronze sur ta: Borin rivets bronze scales onto your mail, like the skin of a dragon. “Dwarves wore these in the days of the Great Mines.”
textes.Borin tape fort et parle fort. Il croit: Borin hits hard and talks loud. He thinks I look down on him because I correct his runes. I correct them because his steel deserves to be well written.
textes.Borin vole une louche de ragoût tous les: Borin steals a ladleful of stew every day, says it needs salt, and goes back for thirds. The best smith on the mountain. And the worst liar.
textes.Borin. Le meilleur forgeron de la Montag: Borin. Best blacksmith in Fire Mountain. Grumpy. Chatty. A blade I can't improve any more, I send to him. He'll grumble. That's a good sign.
textes.Borin. Mon maître. Le meilleur forgeron: Borin. My master. Best blacksmith in the world, and he knows it. I still hold the coal against him. A bit. I owe him everything else.
textes.Borée ! Tu entends ? Il chante en ré !: Borée! Do you hear? It's singing in D!
textes.Borée Givrelin m'apprendra le gel si je: Borée Givrelin will teach me frost if I bring him three everlasting frost flakes from the northern cliffs. Then I'll have to cross the Mirror Lake to the Frost Crystal.
textes.Borée est têtu comme un caillou, et tu s: Borée is as stubborn as a pebble, and you know what I think of pebbles! We never agree about the north wind. And yet I'm fond of him, that old icicle. A little. A lot, on windless days.
textes.Borée et Pyra ne se parlent plus depuis: Borée and Pyra haven't spoken since the winter she melted his lake to take a bath. They'll make up eventually. In a hundred years.
textes.Borée et moi, on est deux vieux au bord: Borée and I are two old men by the water. Him his lake, me my sea. He doesn't talk, I talk for two. We get on very well. He thanks me for wood I never gave him.
textes.Borée et moi, on n'est pas d'accord sur: Borée and I don't agree about the north wind. He says it whistles. I say it sings. Out of tune, but it sings.
textes.Borée mange à la table du fond, loin de: Borée eats at the table at the back, far from the door and far from Pyra. He doesn't talk, he never blows on his spoon, he always says thank you. A perfect customer. A bit chilly, but perfect.
textes.Borée me boude depuis douze hivers pour: Borée has been sulking at me for twelve winters over a bath. A bath! He's old, he's stiff, he's slow. And he makes the finest ice in the archipelago. That annoys me even more.
textes.Borée me demande ma soupe douce, celle q: Borée asks me for my mild soup, the one that doesn't burn. Pyra asks me for my strong soup, the one with character. It's the same soup, sweetie. The same pot. I blow on one a little, I pepper the other over the counter, and there you go. Never tell them. They'd fight over who copied whom.
textes.Borée prétend que la glace est plus élég: Borée claims ice is more elegant than fire. Ice melts. Just saying.
textes.Borée était déjà là quand je suis arrivé: Borée was already here when I arrived. He's as stubborn as a glacier, and just as slow to melt. I'm very fond of him. I rarely tell him so: he freezes up.
Borée, Pyra was asking after you.
textes.Borée, c'est mon plus vieil ami. Il parl: Borée is my oldest friend. He talks little, freezes a lot, sulks for ages. But he's never forgotten a Sunday. He's a faithful man, like his lake.
textes.Borée, ta soupe douce, comme d'habitude: Borée, your mild soup, as usual?
textes.Bouge encore une fois, et ce sera une lo: Move one more time, and it'll be a ladle.
textes.Bouge pas… bouge PAS… (Ocre tire la lang: No move… NO move… (Ocre sticks out his tongue. Ocre scratches, dabs, blows red ochre onto a flat stone.) There! It you! … Well. It you in squares. Ocre did best. Take. Ocre paint another on cave wall.
textes.Bouleversée ? Je suis… je suis… (Elle tr: Upset? I'm… I'm… (She trips over nothing.) Sorry. My sun rosary! Father Clotaire gave it to me for my fifteenth birthday. I was praying by the lake for Monsieur Yvon, and an enormous, ENORMOUS frog stuck out its tongue and… slurp. It swallowed it. Monsieur Yvon calls it the Duchess. Frogs spit out what they swallow when you beat them, apparently. Would you please… ? I'll pray. From afar. From very far.
textes.Boulon a fait l'aller jusqu'à Tazira en: Boulon flew all the way to Tazira barking at every cloud. Every cloud! I could hear the Zéphyr barking from the airfield, and through my binoculars I could see a spring tail sticking out of the window. Gustave said he'd never had a better-guarded flight. The clouds didn't say a word.
textes.Boulon a un cœur. Un vrai petit moteur q: Boulon has a heart. A real little engine that beats faster when you pet him. I made it that way on purpose.
textes.Boulon est allé à Tazira en Zéphyr. Il a: Boulon went to Tazira on the Zéphyr. He barked the whole flight. Not at the passengers: at the clouds. Every single cloud. Gustave said he'd never had a better-guarded flight. The commander, who stayed on the ground, swears she could hear him from the airfield. The whole way, Boulon defended the Zéphyr against the entire sky.
textes.Boulon est déjà allé à Tazira en dirigea: Boulon has already been to Tazira by airship. He chased the cats at the port. He didn't catch a single one. They caught him.
textes.Boulon remonte à bord, demain ?: Can Boulon come aboard again tomorrow?
textes.Boulon voudrait savoir, et moi aussi : v: Boulon would like to know, and so would I: do you prefer dogs or cats?
textes.Boulon vous a reconnu. Regardez sa queue: Boulon recognised you. Look at his tail!
textes.Boum ! Boum-boum ! Boum fait parler tamb: Boum! Boum-boum! Boum make drum talk. Drum say: everybody dance! You dance too?
textes.Boum ! Dis-moi, {surnom} : tu as le ryth: Boom! Tell me, {surnom}: have you got rhythm?
textes.Boum ! Excellent choix. Zigomar dit que: Boom! Excellent choice. Zigomar says every great breakthrough starts with a boom. Mum says every great boom ends with a ceiling to fix. They're both right.
textes.Boum, ba-da boum ! Le djembé résonne aut: Boom, ba-da boom! The djembe echoes around the fire… and, somewhere in the camp, another drum answers you.
textes.Boum, ta-ka, boum ! Omar. Je joue du ben: Boom, ta-ka, boom! Omar. I play the bendir, the round drum. All day long, I drum on tables. In the evening, they finally let me drum on something made for it.
textes.Bourru ? L'autre tambour. Le grand, le l: Bourru? The other drummer. The big one, the slow one. He sends the party to sleep, I wake it up, and Lilas says together it's the right rhythm. A mystery. I say he slows me down.
textes.Bourru ? Oh… il tape le grand tambour, i: Bourru? Oh… he beats the big drum, he minds the basket lift, and he says “Hrmm”. That's all. But his drum, I'd know it among a thousand.
textes.Bourru a encore oublié de remonter la na: Bourru forgot to bring the basket lift back up again. Three rabbits waited at the bottom all morning. They ended up taking the stairs. Did them good.
textes.Bourru m'a sauvé la vie, il y a dix ans,: Bourru saved my life ten years ago, with his bare hands. I owe him everything. And yet I no longer ride in his basket lift. It hurts his feelings. I'm ashamed of it. Hoo.
textes.Bouton n'est PAS dans ton pétrin. Pas au: Button is NOT in your dough trough. Not today.
Bramm! Your mug's waiting. The dented one.
textes.Bramm a un cœur grand comme sa porte, et: Bramm has a heart as big as his gate, and just as firmly shut. I've been bringing him a bowl at noon for a hundred and fifty years. He says “Hmph”. That means thank you.
textes.Bramm dit que je garde un tapis. Je gard: Bramm says I guard a rug. I guard a king. He guards a gate that never moves. We'll see who has the harder job.
textes.Bramm est fâché contre moi depuis cent v: Bramm has been cross with me for a hundred and twenty years. I don't quite remember why. Something about a floor. I smile at him anyway. It annoys him, I think.
textes.Bramm n'a pas souri depuis cent ans. La: Bramm hasn't smiled in a hundred years. The last time was when a barrel of fizz fell on an elf.
textes.Bramm vient boire ici après sa garde, to: Bramm comes in for a drink after his watch, every evening for a hundred and eighty years. He doesn't talk, he doesn't smile. Sometimes he does. Don't tell anyone.
textes.Bramm vient boire ici après sa garde. Il: Bramm comes for a drink here after his watch. He smiles, sometimes. Don't tell anyone.
textes.Bramm, c'est le meilleur rocher de la mo: Bramm is the best rock on the mountain: he doesn't move, he keeps you warm, and the goats adore him. He loves them too. He'll never say so.
textes.Bras de fer ? Ce samedi, je gagne, le Mu: Arm-wrestling? This Saturday, I win, Silent One!
textes.Bravo ! Et la calebasse reste fermée pen: Well done! And the gourd stays closed during my matches.
textes.Bravo ! Tu as tenu… presque une minute !: Bravo! You lasted… almost a minute! Next time, we'll tackle sit-ups.
Well done. The river owes you seven.
Bricolette thinks it's bad luck. Seven dates, seven excuses: a storm, a clock to repair, a second fast… It's me, {surnom}. Every time. I'm afraid that once I'm happy for good, time will start going faster. I know. For a clockmaker, it's ridiculous. Time passes at the same speed for everyone. I've measured it.
textes.Bricolette, c'est ma fiancée depuis tren: Bricolette has been my fiancée for thirty-one years. She's always on time, the other way round. And she sells my presents. With my consent. Well, almost.
textes.Brigadier Lefort, garde municipal. Circu: Constable Lefort, town watch. Move along… no, wait. You look resourceful. I may need you.
textes.Brigadier Lefort. Rien à signaler. Enfin: Constable Lefort. Nothing to report. Well, almost.
textes.Briller la mer… Je l'avais oublié. Merci: Makes the sea sparkle… I had forgotten. Thank you, {surnom}.
textes.Brindille ! Du courrier pour la capitain: Brindille! Any post for the harbour office?
textes.Brindille ! J'ai un nouveau sort pour te: Brindille! I've got a new spell for your drops!
textes.Brindille ! Tu as de la rosée de lune po: Brindille! Have you got moon dew for me this morning?
