I / Tab: bag   •   J: quests   •   M: map   •   P: characters   •   H: heroes   •   1-5: tabs   •   Esc: close
Controller: D-pad or stick to aim   •   A: select   •   B: close   •   LB / RB: tabs   •   right stick: scroll
textes.Ianthé ! Tu danses sur ma marée, ce soir: Ianthé! Are you dancing to my tide tonight?
textes.Ianthé ! Une petite danse ? Je te paie e: Ianthé! A little dance? I'll pay you in crackers!
textes.Ianthé danse comme je chante, en plus vi: Ianthé dances the way I sing, only faster and wetter. She says she's the one people watch. I'm the one people listen to.
textes.Ianthé danse devant mon étal et le clien: Ianthé dances in front of my stall and the customers come all by themselves. I pay her in crackers. She says she'd prefer coins. Everyone says that.
textes.Ianthé danse sur le pont sud tous les so: Ianthé dances on the south bridge every evening. I… I happen to pass that way. For the mother-of-pearl. The light's better there. That's all.
textes.Ianthé m'a demandé un jour pourquoi je n: Ianthé once asked me why I never taste my own crackers. I said I wasn't hungry. She smiled, as if she knew. Since then, when she dances in front of the stall, she pretends to bite into one and pulls a face, a tiny one, just for me. We laugh, the two of us, without a word.
textes.Ici ? Ta première ? Alors souviens-toi b: Here? Your first? Then remember this night well, kid. You tell the story of your firsts your whole life. And you polish it a little each time.
textes.Ici c'est la teuf, là-bas c'est la valse: Here it's the party, over there it's the waltz. The two islands are made for each other.
textes.Ici, j'ai découvert le tajine. Zohra m'a: Here I discovered tajine. Zohra taught me. Well, she watched me make one and she cried. For joy, I think.
Here, I almost have a landlubber's life. At dawn, I row with Driss. In the afternoon, I teach knots to the harbour kids, and little Yasmine already beats me. I tease the caïd about his sleeping cannons. In the evening, I dance on the square. And above my cannons shine Nourredine's lanterns. I won't say how they got there.
textes.Ici, j'ai tout ! Zohra qui m'a appris le: Here, I have everything! Zohra who taught me tagine, Mustapha who gave me his recipe, Hassan and his slightly bland tea, Saïd who sold me forty kilos of sardines for a sneeze. In the evening, Lhoucine plays me the whale dance. Tibo peels my potatoes. And in the souk, there's Aïcha. Ho ho. Above all, Aïcha.
textes.Ici, je loge chambre douze, au Grand Hôt: Here, I stay in room twelve at the Grand Hotel. Six croissants from Madame Margaux every morning. A snow globe from Victor every week. Fernand's sea dragon tooth, under a glass dome. Toni's divine punch, paid in gold. Madame Colette's jar of figs, which she refuses to sell me. And Edmond's moustache, which I covet in silence. Well, almost in silence.
textes.Ici, je ne fais rien. Rien du tout. Depu: Here, I do nothing. Nothing at all. For three days, I've been sunbathing, reading, watching my two children from my towel, and in the evening we dine at Paulo's. The grocer recommended her favourite novel, the fortune-teller made me a prediction, and one evening I passed some chocolate to the young bride next door, who was crying. For someone who does nothing, I'm very busy.
textes.Ici, sous terre, impossible de voler : t: Here, underground, you can't fly: you land.
textes.Ici, tout se règle à la pétanque. Les ma: Here, everything gets settled with pétanque. Weddings, inheritances, elections. The mayor won at pétanque.
textes.Ici, une bagarre éclate pour un rien. Un: Around here, a brawl breaks out over nothing. A look, a wrong word, a spilled grog. I like it. Livens things up.
textes.Ignace Bouche-d'Or a des dés pipés. Je l: Ignace Bouche-d'Or has loaded dice. I know it. He knows I know. That's why he never plays at MY table with them.
textes.Ignace Bouche-d'Or a gagné son sloop aux: Ignace Bouche-d'Or won his sloop at dice. Against a governor. With loaded dice, if you ask me.
textes.Ignace Bouche-d'Or triche aux dés. Tout: Ignace Bouche-d'Or cheats at dice. Everybody knows it. Nobody's ever proved it. That's talent.
textes.Ignace est le meilleur capitaine du mond: Ignace is the best captain in the world when he's not gambling. The problem is, he gambles all the time. He's already bet our sloop. He won. That time.
textes.Ignace parle pour deux. Ça tombe bien. I: Ignace talks for two. That suits me. Maybe he cheats. That's not my question. He hired me without asking any. I owe him that.
textes.Ignace parle trop, joue trop et sourit t: Ignace talks too much, gambles too much and smiles too much. All those gold teeth blind me. But he pays me, and he lets me guard the door. I like guarding doors. Nobody mumbles in doorways.
textes.Ignatia est née un soir de grande érupti: Ignatia was born on the night of a great eruption, and she kept something of that fire. She carries the city the way you carry a flame: without squeezing it too tight.
textes.Il a accroché une clochette à ma chaise,: He hung a little bell on my chair in the library, so he knows when I move. So I hold the bell with one hand so it won't ring. Which means I can't turn the pages. I always read the same one. I know it by heart: page forty-two of the herbarium. Nettles.
textes.Il a aimé ton histoire d'hier, Faelar. C: It liked your story yesterday, Faelar. The one about the hedgehog.
textes.Il a apporté son chronomètre de Cliqueti: He brought his Cliquetis stopwatch to the bakery. Now he times the baking: “Twenty-two minutes, Trèfle! Record broken!” It's not a race, Pépin, it's bread! But I have to admit: since then, I haven't burnt a thing. Cerfeuil would have laughed. He burnt every loaf, and without a stopwatch.
textes.Il a baptisé sa glace coco « Bruno-Loco: He named his coconut ice cream “Bruno-Loco”, in my honour, he says. The day I went to taste it at the beach hut, he didn't make me pay: “It's your recipe, brother.” Then he made me pay for the glass of water. He's sharp, that boy.
textes.Il a bien reçu mon pot ?: Did he get my jar all right?
textes.Il a bien tourné les pages ? Toutes ?: Did it turn the pages properly? All of them?
textes.Il a bien tourné les pages, ce soir ?: Did it turn the pages properly tonight?
textes.Il a construit un château à quatre tours: He built a castle with four towers and a moat. I photographed it from every angle: front, back, from above, lying in the sand. Sixty-two photos. When I looked up, the sea had carried off a tower. Théo said: “You didn't even look at it, Dad.” But I've got sixty-two photos of it.
He's got style. That's better than a neck.
textes.Il a dit « peut-être ». C'est mieux qu'h: It said “maybe”. That's better than yesterday.
He's said “jellyfish-head” three times. Excellent mood!
textes.Il a dormi trois ans ! Il doit avoir fai: It's slept for three years! It must be hungry.
textes.Il a encore oublié de remonter la nacell: He forgot to bring the basket back down again. Three rabbits waited at the bottom a whole morning. I found him asleep at the treetop, nose in the sun. I growled. He said: “Hrmm. They took the stairs? Serves them right.” He was right. I didn't tell him.
textes.Il a entendu parler des chaussures à res: He heard about the spring shoes in Cliquetis. He begged me. Three evenings. “Just two springs, Ursule!” No. I told Pépin. Pépin said: “Cheating.” Grisou sulked for a week. The forge was quiet. Lovely week. Since then, he asks for lighter shoes. “Just in case.”
He's hungry, that's a good sign.
textes.Il a fait six huit dans le ciel depuis t: He's done six figures of eight in the sky since earlier!
textes.Il a goûté une de mes galettes par jour: He tasted one of my crackers a day for forty days, taking notes, to find the recipe. On the forty-first, he came to read me his scroll, all proud. I said: “Wrong. All wrong.” He was so disappointed I gave him a cracker. Free! He wrote that down too, of course.
He seems to regret your quarrel.
textes.Il a le bon nombre de poils !: He has just the right amount of hair!
textes.Il a mangé, au moins, ton pirate ?: Has he eaten, at least, your pirate?
textes.Il a marchandé une heure pour vingt plum: He haggled for an hour over twenty macaw feathers. I let him have his price, for peace's sake. At the next fair, I saw my feathers on his stall: I recognise my knots. Three times my price! He told me: “They've travelled, they're tired, that costs extra.” So I tripled my prices. He pays without arguing now.
textes.Il a mes pattes, ton crabe sentimental !: Your sentimental crab has my legs!
textes.Il a montré mon tapis rouge et il a dit: He pointed at my red carpet and said: “How much?” I named a starting price, a joke price. He said: “Paid.” And he left with it. I had a fever for three days. Samira put wet cloths on my forehead, and I kept repeating in my sleep: “Haggle… haggle…”
textes.Il a parié que je ne toucherais pas sa b: He bet I couldn't hit his ball in the air with my blowgun. He sent the ball very high, with a flick of the hip. I blew. The dart stuck in the rubber. The ball fell back down with my dart in it. It's still there. Chak plays with it. He says it's a lucky ball. He lost the bet.
textes.Il a passé une nuit à mesurer la lueur d: He spent a night measuring the glow of the stones with his instruments. At dawn, he came to tell me, all proud, that they shine a tenth brighter when Lin reads them a story. I said: “I know.” He looked disappointed. I didn't want to disappoint him. But I knew.
textes.Il a posé un doigt sur une pierre, pour: He put a finger on a stone, to see if it was cold. I was behind him. I said: “I know.” Nothing more. He ran off so fast his hat stayed on the ground. I brought it back to him the next day, at the dormitory. He turned it over every which way before taking it. He was checking it wasn't a pigeon.
textes.Il a posé une pièce d'or sur mon comptoi: He put a gold coin on my counter, a big one, with his great-grandfather's head on it. “For the oldest jar in the shop, madam.” I pushed it back with my fingertip. He took a goat's cheese instead, and paid for it with the same coin. I didn't have change. I gave it to him in honey. Six jars.
He promised. Well, he wagged his tail.
textes.Il a rapporté de Per-Hâpy un scarabée bl: He brought back a blue scarab from Per-Hâpy, from Ptahmosé. I spent an hour wondering whether it was a compliment or an insult. Tochtli told me that in Egypt, a scarab brings luck. I was relieved. Later, I learned he'd made it up on the spot. And that it was true anyway. With Tochtli, even the lies hit the mark.
textes.Il a revendu un tapis de l'oasis à un vo: He resold an oasis carpet to a traveller, claiming it had been woven for a sultan's wedding. I know the weaver. An old woman who weaves for her grandsons, in her tent. No sultan. I was there. The traveller looked at me. I said nothing. Afterwards, Rachid bought me a tea. He'd understood.
It shrank. The night was cold.
textes.Il a révisé. Votre piano tousse toujours: It revised. Is your piano still coughing?
He has a very nice camel.
textes.Il a un chronomètre de Cliquetis, et il: He has a stopwatch from Cliquetis, and he times everything: the race, the warm-up, the nap, even my carrots. “Forty-three seconds for three carrots, Bondi, a record!” I hear the tick-tock even in my dreams.
textes.Il a vendu au tianguis du « copal béni p: At the tianguis, he sold “copal blessed by the high priest”. I hadn't blessed anything at all. I went to see him. He held out a piece and said: “Bless it now, then it'll be true.” I did. I still don't know why. He doubled his price that same day.
textes.Il a voulu attirer un dictionnaire par t: He tried to summon a dictionary by telekinesis. Without permission. The whole B shelf followed: bestiaries, botany, biographies. He disappeared underneath. I dug him out book by book, putting each volume back in its place. Two hours. He didn't move a toe. It's the only time he's ever been perfectly still.
textes.Il a voulu compter les marches du temple: He wanted to count the temple steps, like me at his age. He got to the top, out of breath: “Three hundred and sixty-four!” I told him to start again. He started again four times. The fifth time, he got three hundred and sixty-five, and shouted so loudly that the macaws flew off. He had forgotten the platform.
textes.Il a voulu deviner le trente-troisième i: He wanted to guess the thirty-third ingredient of my ras el hanout. He sniffed, tasted, closed his eyes, and said, very sure of himself: “Fish!” Fish! In my ras el hanout! I laughed so hard I knocked over the paprika. It's the only time he's ever made me laugh. Well. One of the only times.
textes.Il a voulu garder ma chinampa, une nuit,: One night, he wanted to guard my chinampa against vegetable thieves. Around midnight: splash! I ran with a lamp. Mixtli was in the canal, with his whole jaguar skin soaked on his head. He said: “The canal moved.” I held out an oar. I laughed until morning. So did the herons.
He wanted to barter for my indigo cheche. For a pot of honey, then two, then a cloth of mist, then a singing hat. He talked a whole afternoon. I said nothing. In the evening he sighed: “Your silence is worth more than your cheche, my friend.” I kept both.
textes.Il a échangé deux pains à la brasserie,: He swapped two loaves at the brewery, mine and Mérit's, while I was looking the other way. I tasted. I said it was mine. It was hers. The whole brewery laughed. I paid for my beer and left. I didn't speak to him for a month. He didn't notice straight away. He talks a lot.
textes.Il a écrit dans ses rouleaux que la prem: He wrote in his scrolls that grandmother's first cracker was “dreadful”. Dreadful! I went to the archives to scratch the word out myself. He sat on the scroll. We stayed like that for an hour. In the end he added “eaten while weeping for joy”. I accepted the deal.
textes.Il a écrit mon nom au tableau des cogneu: He wrote my name on the brawlers' board, in chalk: “Bel-Humeur”. Letters were missing! I rubbed it out with my sleeve and wrote it again, big, in cannon-sized letters. Now my name takes up half the board. Gros-Louis and the Mute have little names, at the bottom. It's better that way. It's fairer.
textes.Il avait dix ans, des genoux écorchés et: He was ten, with scraped knees and the nerve of a government minister. He took the finest apple off my stall, bit into it in front of me, and said: “I'll pay you when I'm mayor.” I wrote it in my notebook. Page one. He's been mayor for eighteen years. The page hasn't changed.
textes.Il avait douze ans. Une nuit, à trois he: He was twelve. One night, at three o'clock, there was a knock at my door in the Tower: Aurélien, barefoot, a tiny trembling light in his hands. His first. He wanted to know if it shone brighter than the stars. I told him it did. It wasn't true, and it was the most beautiful light I've ever seen.
textes.Il avait peur des échelles. Alors chaque: He was afraid of ladders. So every year, for his birthday, I leave a ladder in front of the library, with a ribbon. Forty ladders. He gives them all to Mathurin, who's turned them into planks for the jetty. When I walk on the jetty, I count the years.
textes.Il avait quatorze ans quand il m'a suppl: He was fourteen when he begged me to take him on the Bahja. The first day, he was sick over the side all morning. He got up, all green, and said to me: “That was to feed the fish, uncle. So they'll come.” That day, I knew he'd make a fisherman.
textes.Il avait quatre ans. Un crabe vert, gros: He was four. A green crab, big as a date, pinched his finger on the quay. He screamed. And how he screamed! The seagulls flew off, a guard came running down from the Skala. I unhooked the crab, I blew on the finger. He went quiet at once, and looked at me as if I'd slain a dragon. Ever since, he carries my balls of twine.
He was sixteen and thought he was a poet. He recited me a poem about seagulls, rhyming on “-ay” everywhere: gull at play, girl so gay, sock of grey. I said: “That's bad.” He left, red as a brick. I still know it by heart. When he gets too proud, I recite it to him. He turns modest straight away.
textes.Il avait six ans, il courait sur la plag: He was six, running along the beach knocking over the parasols, and banging on two coconuts and a conch. I taught him to count with his feet. I named him Mistral, because he blew through like the wind. Now he gets the whole village dancing. I tell people he learned on seashells. It's true. More or less.
textes.Il avait six ans. Il a lancé la balle d': He was six. He hit the ball with his hip, very high, over the wall of the court. I was looking at Venus. The ball landed on my head, bounced, and came down on his. Two identical bumps. He tells everyone I was the one who saw stars. He saw them too. I heard him say: “Oh, Venus.”
textes.Il avait six ou sept ans, et un turban t: He was six or seven, with a turban too big for him. He'd come to the end of the jetty to steal my fishing worms from the tin box while I pretended to sleep. I let him. The next day he'd come back with three little fish and give them to me “to pay”. Already a man of honour. Already a thief.
textes.Il avait une jarre fêlée, invendable. Je: He had a cracked jar, unsellable. I took it anyway. At the tianguis, I presented it as “the jar where Tlaloc keeps the thunder”: when you tapped it, it rumbled, because of the crack. I sold it for three times its price. Coyotl wanted his share. I gave it to him. He cracked other jars on purpose. They didn't rumble.
textes.Il balaie ! Colle-toi à ses chenilles, o: It sweeps! Stick close to its tracks, or back away out of reach.
textes.Il boit un seul rhum par soir. Un seul,: He drinks one rum a night. Just one, in silence, at the end of the counter, back to the wall. He talks to nobody. He watches the captain. A sailor who drinks like that is a sailor who's calculating. That worries me more than a brawl. Brawls, I can handle. Calculations, I watch.
It's sulking, Thalion. It has its moods.
textes.Il brille au soleil. Un marchand en voud: It shines in the sun. A merchant might want it.
It shines, Coralin. Just like yours.
textes.Il cachait le dessert dans le canon de p: He used to hide the dessert in the stern cannon, so I wouldn't find it. The stern cannon! I found it by the smell, like a hunting dog. Since then, he hides it somewhere else. I'm still looking. I think it's in the captain's cabin. I'm not going in there.
textes.Il cache un sablier derrière la pile d'e: He hides an hourglass behind the pile of encyclopaedias, to know how long I take to read. I see it reflected in his glasses. So now I read more slowly, so he keeps his record. He looks worried. He offered me a lamp. I took it. It made him happy.
textes.Il caresse le cuivre. Ce grand ours, ave: He strokes the copper. That big bear, with his hands full of burns, runs his finger over a new tray, ever so gently, like on a cat's back. I pretend not to see. A pirate stroking copper, that should stay between the copper and him.
textes.Il chante si tu joues de la flûte !: He sings if you play the flute!
It sings too loud. Clou can't sleep any more.
textes.Il chante « Marée Basse » ! Il chante «: It's singing “Low Tide”! It's singing “Low Tide”!
textes.Il cherchait la chaleur, Dagna. Comme to: It was looking for warmth, Dagna. Like everyone.
textes.Il cherche sa carte partout : dans les g: He's looking everywhere for his map: in the caves, under the barrels, in his crew's pockets. Everywhere except up high. Cats climb. I've told him three times. He says a captain doesn't climb on roofs. The truth is, he's scared of heights. I saw him stand on a chair to take down a lantern. He was green.
textes.Il connaît ! Tête de méduse, pile au tro: He knows! Jellyfish-head, right on the third!
textes.Il croit que je ne l'ai pas vu, la nuit,: He thinks I didn't see him, at night, behind the lanterns, watching me run. … I saw him. So one morning I left my tracks on purpose. On his training path. Nice and clear. Fourteen laps. So he'd count. … He counted.
textes.Il croit que je ne le vois pas, la nuit,: He thinks I don't see him at night, under my windows, with his mother-of-pearl lamp and an empty scroll. He's waiting for my lamp to go out so he can finally write something cheerful. Some nights I blow it out on purpose, even if I'm not sleeping. He goes home delighted.
textes.Il croit que je ne vois pas les haricots: He thinks I don't see the beans he slips into my right pocket to cheat on his hot honeys. I see them. Once, I let him: I served him his five hot honeys, and made him pay for all five. He paid in stories, five stories. Good deal. But I sewed my pocket shut all the same.
textes.Il croit que je triche aux osselets. Je: He thinks I cheat at jacks. I don't cheat: I just blow on the shells a tiny bit, to make them spin. Blowing is my job. He says it's cheating. Coralin used to say the same. I'm starting to think it's a city-wide affliction.
textes.Il crépite, mon enfant. Il t'a entendue: It's crackling, my child. It heard you coming.
textes.Il danse le dos bas, les yeux fixes, en: He dances crouched low, eyes fixed, creeping forward slowly, as if he were hunting. The others step aside. Me, I laugh so hard I have to sit down. He never stops. One evening, I asked him why he kept going. He said: “You laugh.” It's the longest sentence he's ever said to me. I embroidered it in my head.
He dances better than Haldir now.
textes.Il dit qu'avant Barbe-Sanglante, la Bala: He says that before Barbe-Sanglante, Balafre was called the Green Island, and that the rain dug the ravine. We argued a whole afternoon on the bench. In the end, he asked me if I was here a hundred years ago. I said: “Yes.” He was left speechless. For a man who whistles, that's quite a feat. I won. I think.
textes.Il dit que je chante faux. J'ai chanté u: He says I sing off-key. I sang once, at the Dawn Festival, a hundred years ago, because I'd been asked to. Nobody has asked me again. That's perfectly fine. But I don't see why he has to remind everyone of it at every festival.
textes.Il dit que je l'ai jamais affronté. Je l: He says I've never faced him. I tell him: “What about the salt night?” He says: “You didn't even have your fists up, it doesn't count.” So I offer him a rematch, fists up. He says: “WHAT?!” I say it again. He says: “WHAT?!” We've been stuck there for two years.
He says your map was wrong.
textes.Il dit toujours : « C'est la mer. » Quan: He always says: “It's the sea.” When it crackles. Once it was a crab, inside Raoul. … Fine. Most of the time, it's true, it's the sea. But I check. He never checks. He trusts me. Trust is heavy. It's good.
He says that to everyone. He's lying.
textes.Il dort depuis trois ans ! Il devrait êt: She's been asleep for three years! She should be in top shape.
textes.Il déteste la noix de coco. Pas le goût: He hates coconut. Not the taste: he can't bite it. So I grate it very fine, cook it in milk, and tell him it's semolina. He loves my semolina. It's been going on for six years, and he keeps asking for more. Never tell him. A cook has the right to his secrets.
textes.Il déteste ma tisane de lune. Alors, les: He hates my moon tea. So on nights when he can't sleep, I serve it to him in an old sailor's mug with a spoonful of honey at the bottom, and say it's the captains' hot honey. He downs it in one, goes “aaah” like Corentin, and sleeps like a rock.
It has one hundred and fourteen.
He makes them. That's already a lot.
textes.Il en manque un, Hapou ! Je plaisante !: There's one missing, Hapou! Just kidding! Just kidding!
Is one missing? I'll pierce it tomorrow.
textes.Il en manque {manque}. Les araignées de: {manque} still missing. The spiders in the western cave. Go.
There was some. Before you showed up.
textes.Il en vaut une. Et la moitié de ton chat: It's worth one. And half of your cat.
textes.Il essaie tous les jours de deviner ce q: Every day he tries to guess what I'm making at the back of the stall. Yesterday he asked me, all casual: “Got any gold thread, you?” I said: “Gold? For slippers? You've had too much tea, Rachid.” He left. I heard him muttering all the way back to his carpets.
textes.Il est 23 heures… Les projecteurs s'étei: It's 11 PM… The spotlights go out for a moment. At the side of the stage, Clapotis holds Bouton-d'Or's hand, and doesn't take his eyes off the sky. FFFIIIIIIUUU… BOOM!
He went to ask Octave for nails. He came back saying Octave's shacks are better. I sulked for three days. On the fourth, I taught him the clove hitch, which Octave doesn't know. We have our weapons too.
textes.Il est arrivé à Forgefer avec des bras d: He turned up in Forgefer with big'un arms and a mule's head. I gave him sacks of coal. Three years of sacks. He came back every morning. On the first day of the fourth year, I handed him a hammer. He looked at it like the king's crown. I went to fetch a mug of fizz, so I wouldn't have to see his face.
textes.Il est arrivé à l'aérodrome et m'a deman: He came to the airfield and asked me for a ticket “to a place where nobody has ever invented anything”. Gustave dropped him at Carène. He came back on the next flight, very sheepish, hat in hand. “They have cider, commander.” I offered him a tea. He asked if anyone had already invented it. I didn't have the heart to answer.
textes.Il est au crayon. Je l'effacerai le jour: It's in pencil. I'll rub it out the day I see it.
textes.Il est beau sur toi, en foulard, Lalla A: It looks lovely on you, as a scarf, Lalla Aïcha.
textes.Il est beau, Hapou. Pas de chaton dedans: It's fine, Hapou. No kitten in it this time?
textes.Il est en bois. Et il ne sert pas les pu: It's made of wood. And it doesn't serve punch.
textes.Il est entré dans ma tente, il s'est ass: He came into my tent, sat down, pointed at his heart, then his arm, and made a tiny heart with his two index fingers. He put a pearl on the table. I tattooed. Three hours, not a shiver. At the end, he looked at his arm for a very long time. I thought he didn't like it. Then he shook my hand so hard I couldn't tattoo for two days.
textes.Il est entré et il a posé sa main sur mo: He came in and laid his hand on my counter like a piece of evidence. “Exactly the same,” he said. Then, very quietly: “Half a size smaller, without it showing.” A ring too big that slips off in the waves… I didn't need my loupe to understand.
textes.Il est frais, il est beau mon poisson !: Fresh and lovely, my fish! Come closer, come closer! I'm Rosalie, and here we only sell this morning's catch.
textes.Il est gros comment ? Il est gros commen: How big is it? How big is it?
textes.Il est monté un soir, sans prévenir, ave: He came up one evening, unannounced, with two cups of coffee. At the two hundredth step, I heard him puffing like a whale. He got to the top with one empty cup and one half-full. He handed me the half. I drank it. I didn't say thank you. He came back anyway.
textes.Il est parfait. Mes filles ont butiné le: It's perfect. My girls have been foraging the lime trees.
textes.Il est parfait… Attendez… Écoutez ! Tic,: It's perfect… Wait… Listen! Tick, tock… and… DONG! It chimes! After so many years! Thank you, thank you… You've given the square its heart back.
textes.Il est parti par là-bas, vers la colline: It went over there, towards the hill, above the houses in the west! It got stuck in a tree, I'm sure of it!
It's been down for an hour.
textes.Il est rentré de son voyage avec un coqu: He came back from his voyage with a shell from Port-Azur, all pink inside, like an ear. He gave it to me on the quay, without a word, his hands trembling. I pierced it and hung it round my neck. It's still there. When Larbi is at the end of the jetty, I hold it to my ear. You can hear the sea, and it's a little bit him.
textes.Il est revenu de Cliquetis, autrefois, a: Long ago, he came back from Cliquetis with a compass that points south. South! For a tracker, that's a treasure: you always know where you're not going. By the time I went to ask him for it, he'd swapped it in Carène, for a telescope. I haven't quite forgiven him.
textes.Il est revenu me demander une selle pour: He came back to ask me for a saddle for his horse. I couldn't put a saddle on an octopus. So I drew a little hat on the octopus's head. A tricorn, a tiny one. He was delighted. Now he says it's a captain's horse. I can't take any more. But it's my finest octopus.
textes.Il est tard, oui. Mais la nuit a ses sec: It's late, yes. But the night has its secrets.
textes.Il est tombé, Léonce. Ce n'est pas parei: He fell, Léonce. It's not the same.
textes.Il est tout petit, Grégoire ! C'est de l: It's tiny, Grégoire! It's called rigour!
textes.Il est venu me demander de garder la Gra: He came and asked to guard the Great Gate with me. I looked at him for an hour without saying a thing. He talked the whole hour. I said: “No. You smile too much.” He went off to guard the hall. He still smiles. He even smiles on duty. Hmph.
textes.Il est venu me saluer dans la clairière,: He came to greet me in the clearing, Gaston on his shoulder and only one boot on. He asked me if elves ate shells. I said we mostly ate flowers. The next day, he brought me a bouquet. Of shells. I kept it.
textes.Il est venu un matin, sans un mot, et il: He came one morning, without a word, and tugged me by the sleeve all the way to a great ceiba. In the trunk, a wild swarm, enormous. He hadn't touched it. We brought it back together, slowly. He carried the log, I talked to the bees. When we arrived, he said: “You talk too much.” Then: “They like it.”
textes.Il existait. Mais le vôtre a de très jol: It did. But yours has very pretty ribs.
textes.Il existera quand tu m'auras donné la cr: He will exist once you've given me the crust.
textes.Il fait bon. Les heures passent tranquil: It's pleasant out. The hours drift by.
textes.Il fait ce qu'il peut. Comme toi. Viens: It's doing what it can. Like you. Come and sit down.
textes.Il fait noir… Tu entends ce bruit ? C'ét: It's dark… Do you hear that noise? That was my tummy. I think.
textes.Il fait nuit. Je reste tout près de toi,: It's night. I'll stay right next to you, if you don't mind.
Everyone has to be kept covered.
textes.Il faut posséder au moins un des quatre: You must own at least one of the four seals.
I need to tighten his bolts.
textes.Il file par la fenêtre de derrière dès q: He slips out the back window as soon as he sees me coming. One evening, I searched the whole Shark's Tooth for him. His wooden leg was sticking out from under Sylvain's big table. I could have pulled him out by it. I didn't. A man hiding under a table is ashamed enough already. But I gave him time to get cramp.
textes.Il finit quand, l'abordage ?: When does it end, this boarding?
textes.Il grandit tous les soirs, ton doigt, je: That finger of yours grows every night, if you ask me.
textes.Il grince ?! C'est un violon de Crémone: Squeaks?! It's a Cremona violin! Well, from Cremona-on-Sea! It weeps, it laughs, it sings! It does NOT squeak! (He hugs his violin, offended.)
textes.Il hoche la tête. Ça prend trois semaine: He nods his head. It takes three weeks.
textes.Il l'a traversée, Ix Kanul. Comme chaque: It made it through, Ix Kanul. Like every night.
It found it. In my cauldron.
He has it… under his arm. It's a start.
textes.Il laisse des miettes de gomme partout s: He leaves eraser crumbs all over my table. He draws, he rubs out, he draws again: a city, a crystal, columns. The day he finally spoke, it was to explain the crystal to me. A whole hour. I closed the terrace late. I didn't understand a thing. It was very beautiful, all the same.
textes.Il laisse toujours un pourboire « munici: He always leaves a “municipal” tip. One coin, set down nice and straight on the saucer, with a little speech: “For the staff of the Square, on behalf of the town.” The staff is me. One day, I gave him the coin back: “For the broken cups, on behalf of the café.” He laughed about it for a week.
textes.Il lisait le codex des Soleils devant ma: He was reading the codex of the Suns in front of my class. He said “wind” instead of “water”. I coughed, just a little. He reread it, he corrected it. That evening, he thanked me. I said I had a frog in my throat. He looked at me: “Frogs don't cough.” I said: “Then it was a xolo.”
textes.Il lui a fallu onze essais pour réussir: It took him eleven tries to get my needles right. Eleven! He never grumbled. On the eleventh, he held them out to me on his big palm, and I said: “Perfect.” He blushed to the ears. To thank him, I tattooed a little anvil on his forearm. He didn't move for three hours. I think he was asleep. He says he was thinking.
It's a finger short. I measured.
textes.Il m'a acheté trois pommes. Je les ai em: He bought three apples from me. I wrapped them in paper, as I do for everyone, and I charged him for the paper. One penny. He looked at the paper, he paid. The next week, I took him my cheese knife to sharpen. He charged me for the sharpening. To the penny. I said nothing. Hm.
textes.Il m'a apporté mes quatre cents clous da: He brought me my four hundred nails in a bucket, still hot. I counted them one by one, in front of him, on a plank. It took an hour. He didn't move. At four hundred, I nodded. He nodded. He left. That was the best conversation I've had on this island. And one of the longest.
textes.Il m'a apporté un bouquet. Du persil et: He brought me a bouquet. Parsley and coriander, tied with a bit of ship's string. I said: “It's parsley.” He said: “I know. You can't eat roses.” I put it in a pot, on the stall. In the evening, I sold it. But it stayed there all day.
textes.Il m'a appris une chanson du désert, une: He taught me a desert song, a slow song that walks like a camel. He played it to me three times. I sing it twice too fast, and he looks at me as if I were pushing a caravan along. He says sand slows everything down. Me, I come from the sea: the sea pushes.
textes.Il m'a appris une vieille coutume : glis: He taught me an old custom: slipping a coin under the foot of the mainmast, for the ship's luck. He says Barbe-Sanglante did it on all his ships. I put a silver coin under the mast of the Merciless. Silas looked, and he said: “She'll float again.” He's the only one, besides me, who says it without laughing.
textes.Il m'a appris à faire un poing : le pouc: He taught me how to make a fist: thumb outside, or it hurts. I tried it on one of Mange-Clous's flour sacks. The sack didn't feel a thing. I did. Gros-Louis blew on my hand and said it was a very good fist, but flour is a fearsome opponent. Since then, my fist stays in my pocket.
textes.Il m'a arrêté sur le quai, carnet à la m: He stopped me on the quay, notebook in hand: “Running on a public thoroughfare.” I asked him to read me the regulations. He read them: “No bicycles on the quay.” I looked at my legs, I looked at the sergeant. No wheels. The next day, there was a slate: “Runners: walking pace.” I overtake it with a salute.
textes.Il m'a commandé un crocodile en argile,: He ordered a life-size clay crocodile from me, to scare the real ones. I made a very handsome crocodile, with every one of its teeth. Hapou set it up at the edge of his field. The next morning, a real crocodile was sleeping beside it, with its head resting on mine. Hapou says they were fighting. I say they'd found each other.
textes.Il m'a commandé une jarre pour garder se: He ordered a jar from me to keep his fish alive. He put a perch in it, and it still lives there, apparently. He calls it Ptah. Ptah! Like the god! Like me! I went to see it, to check the jar. The jar is perfect. The perch has a crooked face. I don't see the resemblance.
He asked me how many stars there are. I told him: “Count them.” He came back the next morning, red-eyed: “One thousand and eleven! Plus Xan, who flew in front of the moon.” I wrote the number in my tables. With Xan. For science. A mosquito in front of the moon is an observation.
textes.Il m'a demandé comment Rê vainc Apophis: He asked me how Rê defeats Apophis every night. I told him. He told me that for them, the sun fights the stars. We thought for a long while, and we agreed on just one thing: being a sun is an exhausting job. He laughed. I don't think that happens to him often.
textes.Il m'a demandé de lui rapporter quelque: He asked me to bring him something “really from the bottom”. I brought him up an old copper button from the Léviathan, with an anchor on it. He sewed it onto his hat, crooked, with fishing line. He says it's his captain's medal. He shows it to everyone.
textes.Il m'a demandé de mettre en couleur sa c: He asked me to colour his map of Port-Azur, the one the mayor gives to visitors. I painted the sea in six blues: the port blue, the bay blue, the open-sea blue… He held the map at arm's length, eyes shining: “It's the first map that looks wet.” I nearly cried.
textes.Il m'a demandé les plans de son auberge,: He asked me for plans of his inn, with real beds and a sign. I drew twelve rooms. He added in pencil, in a corner: “My aunt's room, with a stove.” He thinks I didn't see. I went over it in ink.
textes.Il m'a demandé pourquoi je n'arrive pas: He asked me why I can't paint the pink. I explained the light, the sad tubes, the evening that keeps moving. He thought about it, then said: “Pink is when blue and red give each other a kiss.” I tried it. It didn't work. But I've never heard a better theory.
textes.Il m'a demandé pourquoi je pleurais en é: He asked me why I cried when peeling onions, and he didn't. I told him it was because I was old. The next day, he cried over the onions, and asked me, all worried, if he was old now. I told him no: they were grown-up onions. He was delighted.
textes.Il m'a demandé pourquoi les jarres de Tl: He asked me why Tlaloc's jars have fangs. I told him: to guard the rain, like a dog guards the house. He looked at Tlaco, hairless and without very terrible fangs, and said: “So Tlaco is a jar.” Since then, he calls him “my little jar”. Tlaco seems to agree.
textes.Il m'a demandé quel jour il fallait hono: He asked me on which day the Serpent should be honoured. I gave him the date from our calendar. He took out his. It wasn't the same. We called Ah Kin Pech, who calculated on his fingers all afternoon. He concluded that both dates were right. Nobody was happy.
textes.Il m'a demandé s'il pouvait porter mon b: He asked if he could carry my shield. I lent it to him. He disappeared behind it. All you could see were his feet and the tip of Tlaco's tail. He said, from behind the shield: “I'm invincible!” He stepped forward and fell into a basket of chillies. Invincible, but not very nimble.
textes.Il m'a demandé trois fois de voir le tab: He's asked me three times to see the galleon painting. The first time as the caïd, the second out of curiosity. The third time, he came with tea. I drank the tea. I didn't show the painting: I promised. But the tea was delicious, and he was so embarrassed. That memory, I'm keeping.
textes.Il m'a demandé un jour : « Amirale, si j: He once asked me: “Admiral, if I repair the Léviathan, can I be captain?” I answered: “If you repair it, you'll be admiral.” He thought about it, and said: “No. Captain's better: you're on the ship.” He's right. I didn't tell him.
textes.Il m'a demandé un sac de sel, pour son c: He asked me for a sack of salt, for his cook. I sold him one. Lovely sand from the east beach, nice and dry, nice and white. He paid without looking. Sixty years after the first sack! His grandfather, at least, had tasted it before paying. I told him: “You have his eyes. Not his nerve.” He didn't speak to me for three days. He came back.
textes.Il m'a dessiné une carte du Bois-Doré sa: He drew me a map of Bois-Doré without ever having been there. Everything's wrong: the trees, the walkways, the number of moons. Except the Mother Tree, exactly in its place. I hung it at home, above my bed.
textes.Il m'a dessiné une rose des vents à seiz: He drew me a sixteen-point compass rose, with a mermaid in the north and a whale in the south. I tattooed it on an old helmsman's arm, smaller, without a single mistake. Philémon came to look. He looked for a long time, with his magnifying glass. He said: “It's better than the original.” He was offended. The next day, he drew me another one. Even more beautiful.
textes.Il m'a dicté la ballade du roi Atlas. Le: He dictated the ballad of King Atlas to me. The next day, I was singing it in the square, and in the third verse, Protée stood up in the front row: “No, no, now it's a queen, and she has an octopus!” Everyone laughed. I carried on with the octopus. I'm a professional.
textes.Il m'a dicté un jour : « Par ordre du ro: One day he dictated: “By order of the king, fizz is a royal treasure.” I wrote: “Fizz is a treasure.” He shouted: “Where did royal go?” I said: “Ulfa would never have put it up.” He thought about it, he laughed, he signed. The decree still hangs above the counter at the Mug.
textes.Il m'a donné jusqu'à la fin de l'été pou: He's given me until the end of summer to find the chest. Otherwise, the crew will vote. Every morning, he says to me: “Hm. End of summer.” The way other people say good morning. I answer: “I can count.” I can count. There are… plenty of days left. Enough. Well. A few.
textes.Il m'a donné ses lunettes d'aviateur, se: He gave me his flying goggles, his real ones! They're too big, so Dad tied them behind my head with a shoelace. I wear them all the time, even to sleep. Mum says I've got a mark round my eyes, like a raccoon. It's an inventor's mark.
textes.Il m'a donné un crayon enduit de cire et: He gave me a wax-coated pencil and a little board, to draw underwater. I tried. My drawing looked like a poorly octopus. He framed it. It hangs in the harbour master's office, next to the big map. When people ask him what it is, he says: “A discovery.”
textes.Il m'a emmené en pédalo, « pour voir la: He took me out in a pedalo, “to see the coast from below”. He pedalled, I looked. After three metres, I felt the sea rising in my throat. After four, I was leaning over the side. He turned round, singing. I've never been so far from home.
textes.Il m'a emprunté l'Atlas des étoiles fixe: He borrowed my Atlas of the Fixed Stars. He returned it eleven years later, with corrections in ink in the margins: three stars moved. He told me, delighted, that they had shifted. Fixed stars! In ink! I had to buy a new atlas. He wrote corrections in that one too. In pencil, this time. He's making progress.
textes.Il m'a envoyé mon nom en hiéroglyphes :: He sent me my name in hieroglyphs: a star and a little sun. I answered with a drawing: a bald old man, with a reed, and a hippopotamus head. Nebet, the little girl from Per-Hâpy, had told me the nickname. He wrote to me that it was the finest portrait anyone had ever made of him. And the only one.
textes.Il m'a eue. Il m'a bandé les yeux pour m: He got me. He blindfolded me to make me taste “a spice blend on bread”. I tasted. I said: “Delicious. What cumin!” He took off the blindfold. A sardine. A SARDINE! I left shrieking, and Saïd heard everything. But it was my cumin. The cumin was delicious, so there.
textes.Il m'a fallu dix ans pour tisser le lin: It took me ten years to weave royal linen, the kind you can see through. The day I managed it, I held the cloth up to the sun, and I saw Ra through it, all soft, as if behind a cloud. I cried, I think. Since then, the temple orders its linen from me. And Néferet wears only my robes.
textes.Il m'a fallu huit ans pour le finir. Qua: It took me eight years to finish it. Four hundred gears, thousands of punch cards. First public match at the Fair, fourteen years ago: it beat Héloïse in twenty-three moves. Since then, it has never lost a game of chess. Three Cogs of Honour in a row. As for the stone game of the mist people… we shan't speak of it.
textes.Il m'a frappé ! Vous avez vu ?!: He hit me! Did you see?!
textes.Il m'a gagné ma boussole d'argent à la D: He won my silver compass from me at the Shark's Tooth: three sixes against my three fives. He wears it round his neck, like a medal. Every time I pass, he opens it and says: “North is that way, captain.” Since then, the Widow sails by the sun and the stars. She sails very well. Hm. Better, even. But that's not the point.
textes.Il m'a invitée à l'Observatoire pour voi: He invited me to the Observatory to watch a comet go by. I brought a book, just in case. He talked all night: about the stars, his grandfather, fireflies. I didn't read a single page. The comet went by at three o'clock. It was nice. I didn't need the book.
textes.Il m'a mis au défi d'aller voir ses lumi: He dared me to go and see his green lights in the graveyard, at night. I went! Well, as far as the gate. I heard a little noise, clack clack, like bones. I ran back, to check something at the harbour. And I still say they're fireflies. Fireflies with bones, maybe.
textes.Il m'a montré son premier poème : un chi: He showed me his first poem: a puppy, rhymed with “puppy”. I read it three times. He was looking at me with such hopeful eyes that I said: “That's a rich rhyme.” He smiled like a child. Later, Ombreline explained to him what a rich rhyme is. He came back to tell me: “Thank you for lying kindly.”
textes.Il m'a offert un cornet en cuivre, pour: He gave me a copper ear trumpet, to hear better. I put it to my ear. He talked into it. I understood nothing: he mumbles even into a trumpet! So I use it to pour powder into my cannons. Doesn't spill. Best present of my life. I never told him. He knows. He knows everything, that man.
textes.Il m'a peint une enseigne : « Pain chaud: He painted me a sign: “Hot bread”. He put the sign for cat instead. A whole week of “cat bread”! The children came to see if the loaves meowed. Nebet ordered one with a tail. I made it, with ears too. I've never sold so much. I kept the sign behind the oven. For bad days.
textes.Il m'a percé une lanterne spéciale. Quan: He pierced me a special lantern. When it's lit, there's a sultan on the wall, a sardine, and a little djinn coming out of the sardine. The children in the circle shriek when I turn it. So do I, a bit. I asked him what I owed him. He said: “The end of the story. I've never heard it.”
textes.Il m'a proposé un jour de jouer sa Morue: One day he offered to bet his Cod against my Shark. A sloop against a galleon! I told him: “A shark against a cod, my friend, we know who eats whom.” He laughed so hard all his teeth shone. The next day, he offered again. He offers again every week. It's become his way of saying hello.
textes.Il m'a prêté sa longue-vue en cuivre, ce: He lent me his copper spyglass, the one with a star engraved on it. I put it on a crate to look for my glasses, and Gros-Louis sat on the crate. The spyglass has a little bend in it now. Philémon says it can see behind rocks. He was very nice about it. He only cried a little.
textes.Il m'a raconté le grand feu des dieux, à: He told me about the great fire of the gods, at Teotihuacan: Tecciztécatl, covered in gold and feathers, who backs away from the fire, and little Nanahuatzin who jumps. I said I would have jumped first. He asked me: “With your feathers, or without?” I didn't know what to answer. I'm still thinking. My feathers are very beautiful.
textes.Il m'a raconté qu'il avait avalé un clou: He told me he'd swallowed a nail, for real, and that's why he's called Mange-Clous, Nail-Eater. I wanted to try it with a nail made of breadcrumb. It was tasty! Mange-Clous said I was the first cabin boy to eat a nail without ending up at Doc's. He called me “Crumb-Eater” all day.
textes.Il m'a rapporté de sa grande traversée u: He brought me back a black pebble from the highlands after his great crossing, telling me it was ore. It was coal. I said nothing: I put it in the forge, and on its fire I forged him a pair of compasses for his maps. He still doesn't know his ore was coal.
textes.Il m'a signalé un jour une île au nord,: He once reported an island to the north, shaped like a three-master. I added it to my big map, in dotted lines: “Probable island, sighted by Fil-de-Fer”. The next day, Captain Anne-Rose informed me it was a cloud. I left the island. I just drew a tiny sheep on it. He doesn't hold it against me. I think.
textes.Il m'a taillé un peigne dans une branche: He carved me a comb from a branch that fell from his kapok tree. He repeated three times: “Fallen. Not cut.” I wear it every day. In Bois-Doré, people ask me which elf carved it. I answer: a bear.
textes.Il m'a vendu des graines de courge « qui: He sold me squash seeds “that give squash as big as canoes”. They gave normal squash. I went to complain. He measured a squash with his arms, very seriously, and he said: “A little canoe. For a child.” I laughed. He refunded me half. That's a lot, for Tochtli.
textes.Il m'a vendu une « plume de quetzal », t: He sold me a “quetzal feather”, very expensive, for my festival headdress. It ran at the first rain. A parrot feather, painted. I went to the tianguis and gave it back to him, on his head, in front of his customers. He said it was a test, to see if I could recognise a real one. Me, I recognise a real cousin.
textes.Il m'a vendu une « tisane en fiole », to: He sold me a “herbal tea in a vial”, ready-made, blue. I tasted it, then poured it on my tomatoes. They turned blue. Huge, blue, and delicious. I gave him a basketful, without a word of explanation. He didn't ask. He'd be quite capable of selling them.
textes.Il m'a vendu « la conque d'Ehécatl ». J': He sold me “the conch of Ehécatl”. I blew into it in front of the whole square. It squeaked! Like a frightened mouse! It was a snail shell from the lake. I laughed so hard I fell back onto my drum. Boom. I kept it. It makes the children laugh. My best purchase. Don't tell him, he'd put up the price of his snails.
textes.Il m'apporte le minerai des pentes rouge: He brings me ore from the red slopes, and every time he forgets a sack somewhere on the mountain. Once, he forgot Fundin. Fundin came back the next day, black as soot, with the sack and a bat in his hood. I paid Grimli anyway. The ore was good.
textes.Il m'arrive de m'endormir à ma table l'a: Sometimes I fall asleep at my table in the afternoon, my cheek on my star charts. When I wake up, there's always a cushion under my head, and the coffee machine has stopped whistling. Gaston turns off the whistle for me. The whole café drinks in silence. Nobody complains. It's the only café on the island where people whisper for an astronomer.
textes.Il m'avait dit que 13 Ahau était un jour: He told me 13 Ahau was an excellent day for my match. I lost, three balls to nil. I went to see him, furious. He opened his tables, read for a long time, and said: “Excellent for the other team.” Now I always ask him: “Good for whom?” He says that's an excellent question.
textes.Il m'en a parlé trois fois. Ton bras gra: He told me three times. Is your arm itching?
I still need {manque}, {surnom}. My cauldron is waiting.
textes.Il m'en manque {manque}. Elles brillent: I'm still missing {manque}. They shine like tiny little moons lying on the ground.
textes.Il m'envoie des corbeaux à minuit avec d: He sends me crows at midnight with very important messages. “The king is hungry.” “The king requests cheese.” “The king asks whether the cheese is asleep.” One night, I sent Croâ back with a cheese tied to his leg. Croâ ate it on the way. The king thanked me for the crow.
textes.Il m'échange une lampe de nacre chaque s: Every week he trades me a mother-of-pearl lamp for my crackers. He thinks I resell them. I've kept them all. Thirty-seven lamps, lit, in my house. At night it looks like a little crystal. If you tell him, I'll charge you double for life.
textes.Il m'écoute moi, ou il t'écoute toi ?: Is he listening to me, or is he listening to you?
textes.Il manque encore {manque_liste}. Ne te p: We're still missing {manque_liste}. Don't hurry: the Tree is patient, even when it's ill.
textes.Il manque encore {manque} Perles de Lumi: {manque} Pearls of Light are still missing. The crystal is waiting patiently. So am I.
textes.Il manque la mer. Elle ne rentre pas dan: The sea is missing. It doesn't fit in your speakers.
textes.Il manque un pêcheur, Fernand !: What's missing is a fisherman, Fernand!
There's a ruby missing tonight, Ulfa.
textes.Il manque un truc. Je te dirai quand je: Something's missing. I'll tell you when I know.
textes.Il me fallait la pointure exacte de Rach: I needed Rachid's exact shoe size. I know it, of course, but Samira wanted to measure herself. So one afternoon, while he napped on his own carpets, she tiptoed over with a ribbon. He snored the whole time. That evening, he told everyone he'd dreamt of a cat tickling his feet.
textes.Il me faut du bois droit pour mes flèche: I need straight wood for my arrows. Bring me {manque} good straight sticks and I'll pay you. Honestly.
textes.Il me faut du bois, oui. Une voie d'eau: I need wood, yes. A leak has opened under the forge, on the port side: nothing serious, but if I don't plug it, Jos will end the week with his feet in the water. Four logs. Good wood, not driftwood. An axe, a tree, and back you come.
textes.Il me faut du fer. Toujours du fer. Les: I need iron. Always iron. The northern shepherds have hills full of it and sell it one drop at a time.
I need more of your ochre.
textes.Il me faut encore {manque_liste}. Courag: I still need {manque_liste}. Courage: the Tree is waiting for you. It never complains, but I can hear it sigh.
textes.Il me faut encore {manque} dents de requ: I still need {manque} shark teeth. Keep going!
textes.Il me faut {manque} runes. Pas une de mo: I need {manque} runes. Not one less. A gate doesn't open halfway.
textes.Il me manque des fleurs de braise pour m: I'm short of ember flowers for my flowerbeds. They only grow on the slopes of the volcano, where the ground smokes. I'd need five to make a fine bed. My old legs don't climb up there any more. Yours, perhaps?
I'm out of wild honey, {surnom}. Could you find me {manque} combs? In the hollow trees on your island, when you chop wood. I'll bake you bread in return!
textes.Il me manque encore {manque_liste}. La f: I'm still missing {manque_liste}. The moonflower only grows at the top of the little jungle peak, the one that looks over the bay. The water: draw it with the vial from the pool of the big waterfall, in the north-east of this island. And the golden seed… the waves carried it off long ago. Perhaps a collector picked it up?
textes.Il me manque encore {manque} champignons: I still need {manque} mushrooms. Patience: the forest is full of them.
textes.Il me manque encore {manque} minerais. P: I still need {manque} ores. No iron, no sword. That's the law of the anvil.
textes.Il me manque encore {manque} rayons de m: I still need {manque} honeycombs. Keep going, my oven is waiting for you!
textes.Il me manque {manque} éclats d'obsidienn: I still need {manque} obsidian shards. The runes are waiting.
textes.Il me paie en fèves et il les compte lui: He pays me in beans and counts them himself, out loud, very fast. I count again after him: one is missing. Always one. He told me it was the moon's fault, it had a day less that month. The moon doesn't drink cacao! Since then, he gives me an extra bean, “for the moon”. I put it aside. The moon owes me a lot.
textes.Il me paie en plumes de corbeau pour vér: He pays me in raven quills to check his old maps. Nine times out of ten, it's a fake. Once, just once, he brought me a real portolan chart, very old, with a whale drawn in one corner. My hands were shaking. Isaac saw. He sold it to me for the price of one quill. I still don't understand why.
textes.Il me raconte tout ce qu'il entend sur l: He tells me everything he hears on deck: the islands, the winds, the rumours. Even the seasick goat: “She saw the elves' island, and she threw up.” I wrote it all down. In the margin of my map, near the Bois-Doré, there's a tiny little goat. She's my most reliable source.
textes.Il me rapporte des choses : un coquillag: He brings me things: a shell, a parrot feather, a pearl, a dried starfish. Without a word. He puts them on my table and leaves. My tent is full of them. I don't know who the heart on his arm is for. I've never asked him. Tattooists are like doctors: you don't ask the wrong questions.
textes.Il me reproche d'écrire des histoires mo: He accuses me of writing dead stories. “A true story is a story that has lived.” I asked him for proof. He held a shell to my ear and said: “Listen.” All I heard was the sea. He said: “There. It's all in there.” For once, I didn't write anything down.
textes.Il me reste un pain au chocolat à deux b: I've got one two-bar pain au chocolat left. Quick, before Nina gets back from the fountain!
textes.Il ment. Comme tous les arbres. Et tous: It's lying. Like all trees. And all customers.
textes.Il n'arrive qu'une bouteille de rhum de: Only one bottle of rum from the Murène reaches Berthe's each month. Just one. Pyra and I bet on it: if I saw a serpent before midnight, it was mine. At a quarter to midnight, I saw three. She said they were seaweed. We never settled it. We drank the bottle together, so as not to fall out.
It's not for sale. Same as yesterday.
textes.Il n'est que onze heures et soixante min: It's only eleven o'clock and sixty minutes, Moulay Brahim.
textes.Il n'y a eu qu'une autre exception, il y: There's only been one other exception, a hundred and twenty years ago: “The Pearl of the avenue has vanished. Black ship sunk to the west.” The handwriting shook that evening too. I asked him how it had happened. He said: “I didn't see anything.” Then he looked at his feet for a very long time. I didn't write that down. That's rare.
textes.Il n'y a jamais de détails dans « rien »: There are never any details in “nothing”. That's what saddens me.
textes.Il n'y a jamais eu de dragon, petit. Il: There never was a dragon, lad. There was a very big dwarf.
textes.Il n'y a même pas d'orage, Héloïse !: There isn't even a storm, Héloïse!
There isn't even a storm, Héloïse.
textes.Il n'y a pas d'arbres au désert. Mon boi: There are no trees in the desert. My wood comes from Carène, and they sell it dear. One year, the wood didn't come at all, and the whole fleet had holes. So I went all round town and bought up the old blue doors, one by one. I repaired every boat with them. Even today, some boats have a lock.
There are no trees at the market, Pépin.
textes.Il n'y a pas de rythme pour la dorade. B: There's no rhythm for sea bream. Boom.
textes.Il n'y a personne. Le parquet craque sou: There's nobody. The floorboards creak under your steps. Especially near the rug.
textes.Il n'y a personne. Une maison bien rangé: There's nobody here. A tidy house that smells of wax and bread.
textes.Il n'y a personne… juste une théière sur: There's nobody here… just a teapot on the low table. A teapot with… a bushy tail?
textes.Il n'y a plus rien sous le coussin. Just: There's nothing left under the cushion. Just a bit of cat fur.
textes.Il n'y a rien dans mes poches ! … Enfin,: There's nothing in my pockets! … Well, nothing that goes croak.
textes.Il n'y avait pas de loup dans cette hist: There was no wolf in that story.
There aren't any under my windows.
textes.Il n'y en a pas. J'ai cherché sur toutes: There isn't one. I've looked on all my maps.
textes.Il n'y en a pas. Mais votre billet reste: There isn't one. But your ticket is still valid.
textes.Il nageait près de la paillote du Coco L: He was swimming near the Coco Loco beach hut, where the waves meet the sand. It must be buried there. But you can't get it out with your hands.
textes.Il naît : tout s'éveille.\nIl règne : to:
It is born: everything awakens.
It reigns: everything blazes.
It dies: everything sheds its leaves.
Where it never goes, everything sleeps.
It doesn't move. Its cannons do.
It isn't smoking. You're the one fuming.
textes.Il ne s'est pas effacé. Il dort. Viens t: It hasn't faded. It's sleeping. Come and sit at the Circle on a clear night. The stones sometimes wake what sleeps. Not always.
It doesn't know how to share. It knows how to win.
textes.Il ne va pas mettre le feu à ta poche ?: Won't it set your pocket on fire?
textes.Il ouvre une noix de coco d'un seul coup: He opens a coconut with a single stroke of the machete, like his grandfather. The first day, he did it in front of my kiosk, to impress me. Whack! Two perfect halves. The juice squirted over my window, my cones and the sergeant. Lefort wanted to fine him for “splashing”. He got an ice cream instead.
textes.Il paie chaque histoire d'une noisette,: He pays for each story with a hazelnut, set nice and straight on my knee, and takes it back when he leaves, “for next time”. One evening, I was the one who fell asleep before him. When I woke up, he'd finished the story by himself, for the other little ones. With a dragon. There's always a dragon, with Gland.
textes.Il paie son ardoise en potions. « Pour l: He pays his tab in potions. “For coughs”, “for low spirits”, “for goats' hooves”. I don't have a goat! I've got a whole shelf of them behind the counter. Once, I opened one by mistake: my saucepans sang all evening. In tune. More in tune than him, anyway.
textes.Il paraît qu'il y a cent ans, un tonneau: They say that a hundred years ago, a barrel rolled off a cart onto an elf who'd come to sell wood, and Bramm smiled. I was in the kitchen. I didn't see a thing. I've been watching out ever since. With every bowl, I look at his beard. It twitches, sometimes. I note it all down on my kitchen wall, in chalk.
textes.Il paraît qu'il y a des ruines sous les: They say there are ruins under the roots of the great kapok trees. Stairs that lead nowhere. Or else very far away.
textes.Il paraît qu'il y a un fantôme dans la C: They say there's a ghost in the Rune Crypt! Oscar said so. But Oscar says lots of things.
textes.Il paraît qu'il y aura de la daurade, ve: I hear there'll be sea bream on Friday.
textes.Il paraît qu'on peut voir le Grand Spagh: They say you can see the Great Spaghetti through the holes in the ceiling. I'm looking for the right hole.
textes.Il paraît qu'on trouve des petites croix: They say you can find little wooden crosses on the beaches. Castaways more far-sighted than me buried their savings there.
textes.Il paraît qu'à Cliquetis, ils ont des ch: Apparently in Cliquetis they have spring-loaded shoes. If I had some… No. Pépin would say it's cheating. Pépin's right. But still.
textes.Il paraît qu'à Port-Azur, Django joue de: Word is that in Port-Azur, Django plays waltzes at the Perroquet Bleu. One day we'll do a track together: waltz-techno!
textes.Il paraît qu'à Port-Azur, ils font des c: Apparently in Port-Azur they make croissants. That means “crescent” — bread shaped like a crescent moon! Like ours! But only half.
textes.Il paraît que Faelar a raconté l'histoir: I hear Faelar told the story of the first seed. Again.
textes.Il paraît que Hulotte a vu une étoile to: Apparently Hulotte saw a star fall into the great pool. Me, I think it was a firefly that had drunk too much moon tea.
textes.Il paraît que Mistral prépare un morceau: Word is Mistral's working on a track with whale songs. It's going to be huge.
textes.Il paraît que dans le désert, il y a des: They say that in the desert there are painted stones. Very old ones. Hunters, animals, and a great round door. I'd so love to see them.
textes.Il paraît que de l'autre côté de l'île v: They say on the other side of the island lives an old loon who talks to seashells. Barnabé, his name is. Don't believe a word he says about me.
textes.Il paraît que je suis « un peu bizarre »: Apparently I'm “a bit weird”, according to you. It was {qn} who told me. I'll think about it. Or not.
Apparently I'm “a bit weird”, according to you. It was {qn} who told me. I'll think about it. Or not.
textes.Il paraît que la Porte aux Quatre Sceaux: Apparently the Gate of the Four Seals is made of stone, but its hinges are metal. A metal nobody knows. I'd love to see a bit of it.
textes.Il paraît que tu as aidé {qn}. {Il} aura: I hear you helped {qn}. {Il} could have managed on {son} own, but there you go.
textes.Il paraît que tu as frappé {qn}. Je ne d: I hear you hit {qn}. I shouldn't laugh. I laughed anyway.
textes.Il paraît que tu as offert {objet} à {qn: I hear you gave {objet} to {qn}. {Il} talked my ear off about it all day. Thank you on behalf of {lui}.
I hear you gave {objet} to {qn}… {Il} hates that! Don't worry, I said it's the thought that counts.
textes.Il paraît que tu as soigné l'Arbre sacré: They say you healed the sacred Tree on your island. Thank you, human.
textes.Il paraît que tu fais des cadeaux à {qn}: I hear you've been giving presents to {qn}. That's nice of you.
textes.Il paraît que tu me trouves sympathique: I hear you think I'm nice? It was {qn} who told me. Well, that warms my heart.

textes.Il paraît que {qn} t'a parlé de moi. Ne: I hear {qn} told you about me. Don't believe everything {il} says.
textes.Il paraît que {qn} t'a parlé de moi. Tou: I hear {qn} told you about me. All good things, I hope.

textes.Il passe au souk, il entend mon tac-tac,: He comes by the souk, hears my tac-tac, and drums along on my stall with his fingertips: tac-tac-boom. One evening, he played the whole festival on my rhythm, and told the whole square where it came from. From Abdellah's, the coppersmith. I was miffed. A little. Then Hnia saw me tapping my foot. She counted.
textes.Il passe parfois une barque, loin, à l'o: Now and then a boat goes by, far off, to the west. It comes from the village islands and the elves. I count them. This year: three. Including you.
textes.Il passe à chaque ronde, les mains dans: He comes by on every patrol, hands behind his back, all casual. He looks at the beach, he looks at the sea, he looks at the vanilla. I hold out a cone. He takes it without a word, like a piece of evidence. Three times a day. Rosalie shouts it all over the port. He says he's “keeping an eye on the kiosk”. Of course he is.
textes.Il penche depuis quatre ans, ton comptoi: Your counter has been sloping for four years.
textes.Il peut me redire le gros mot ?: Can he say the rude word again?
It's crying, more like. It's wet.
textes.Il pleut ? Votre chocolat des jours de p: Is it raining? Your rainy-day hot chocolate is ready. The machine grumbled, but it made it.
It rains inside, it's the atmosphere.
textes.Il pleut, vous êtes content ? Le bras de: It's raining, are you happy? Wilfried's arm is itching. I've sent him his ointment. I'm keeping a little for you, just in case.
textes.Il pousse à l'ombre des grands arbres. R: It grows in the shade of the tall trees. Restores half a heart.
textes.Il prend le limon de mon champ pour ses: He takes the silt from my field for his jars, and he pays me in jars. I've got forty. Full of barley, flax, seeds, nothing at all. Once, I tried to give him one back. He tapped it, listened for a long time, and said: “It's perfect, keep it.” He taps everything, that potter. Even people.
He promises. Well, he's wagging his tail.
textes.Il pétille sur la langue comme une poign: It fizzes on the tongue like a handful of stars.
textes.Il pêche au pied du phare, maintenant, a: He fishes at the foot of the lighthouse now, at the end of the jetty, just when I go up for my watch. He says it's the best spot. It's true. That annoys me all the more. He whistles. Out of tune. To needle me. One evening I threw a handful of coarse salt at him through the skylight. He said thank you, and salted his sardine.
textes.Il racontait le naufrage du Léviathan de: He told the wreck of the Léviathan standing up, rolling like a ship: left for the wave, right for the wind, and the whole circle rolled with him. When the ship hit land, he dropped down onto the sand. Three old folk of Tazira got seasick. I applauded. I've never dared tell a story lying down.
textes.Il raconte partout que j'ai gagné la Mor: He tells everyone I won the Cod with loaded dice. So I told everyone he'd married his brig because no lady would have him. He went as red as his Widow. Then he said, very quietly: “Just one.” I never made that joke again. We all have a spot where you mustn't press.
textes.Il raconte partout que l'idée de faire f: He tells everyone the idea of making the gunports smoke, against the Murène Noire, was his. It's possible: he whispered it to me at the rail, between two hot honeys. But I was the one who got into the boat. An idea, Corentin, doesn't go and parley with a pirate.
textes.Il raconte qu'il a crié « Récif ! » de t: He says he shouted “Reef!” at the top of his lungs the night we hit. Me, I heard nothing. Nor did Ignace. The only one who heard it was Belle-Humeur, who hears nothing! Does that make sense to you? Belle-Humeur said “WHAT?!”. That's all we know. Fil-de-Fer says it's proof.
textes.Il raconte qu'il a gagné la Morue aux dé: He claims he won the Cod at dice from an admiral. The week before, it was from a governor. The month before, from a prince. I say it was the same dice every time. He smiles at me with his twenty-two carats. It's the most expensive and the falsest smile in the archipelago.
textes.Il raconte que les dents de crocodile, c: He says the crocodile teeth are for a necklace. For a fiancée. I have no fiancée. I told him. He smiled. He still says it. I bent an iron bar. He still says it. I don't know how you stop Mange-Clous. Nobody knows.
textes.Il reflottera ! Il reflottera quand je l: It will float! It'll float when I say so! I've replaced forty planks, caulked the whole side and set the keel straight! One more word about my ship and it's YOU I'll caulk!
textes.Il refuse d'enlever son képi pendant les: He refuses to take off his cap during massages. “A sergeant does not uncover on duty.” We're alone, in the back room, door shut. He keeps the cap on. He walks out stiff as a post, and gives me a regulation salute on the threshold of the back door.
He regrets your quarrel, I think.
textes.Il reste Pixel, quelque part dans la cit: Pixel is still out there, somewhere in the city…
textes.Il reste Quark… écoute bien : il fredonn: Quark is still out there… listen carefully: he hums when he hides.
textes.Il reste une chose que je n'ai jamais di: There's one thing I've never told anyone. Someday, maybe. When I trust you.
There's one thing I've never told anyone. Someday, maybe. When I trust you.
textes.Il revient tous les ans. J'écris « sorti: It comes back every year. I'm writing “out”.
textes.Il s'appelle Moustache ! Regarde ses mou: His name is Moustache! Look at his whiskers!
textes.Il s'entraîne même la nuit, quand il n'y: He even trains at night, when nobody's around. One evening, his ball came through my window and landed on my loom. Three threads broken. He came to fetch it, all sheepish. I made him retie the three threads himself. It took him an hour. He says it was harder than a match.
textes.Il s'est arrêté net au bord de la plate-: He stopped dead at the edge of the platform! Strike!
textes.Il s'est assis devant ma forge pendant t: He sat in front of my forge for thirty days so I'd take him on as an apprentice. Ash was raining down, he stayed. On the thirtieth day, I handed him a broom. He took it as if it were the king's axe. Twelve years later, he's still sweeping. Not as well, but with pride.
textes.Il s'est assommé contre la paroi ! C'est: He knocked himself out against the wall! Now's the moment!
textes.Il sait sourire, c'est déjà ça. Yo, capi: He knows how to smile, that's something. Yo, captain!
textes.Il se doute de tout. Il ne sait juste pa: He suspects everything. He just doesn't know what.
textes.Il se moque de moi, je l'ai vu ! Il fait: He makes fun of me, I've seen him! He pretends to drink, then to fall, and he laughs without a sound. Hic! I told him that wasn't nice. So he did it again: drink, fall… and this time he caught himself by the collar, like the night of the bay, and gave me a wink. I didn't understand it all. But I think it was nice.
textes.Il se souvient de quoi ? Il ne veut pas: Remembers what? He won't tell me!
textes.Il se tient toujours derrière ma chaise: He always stands behind my chair when I play, and taps the table with the tip of his hook, tick, tick, out of habit. Sylvain says it's a signal. I swear it's a tic. Crochet swears nothing at all: he doesn't like questions. So nobody knows. Me, I love it when nobody knows.
It's whistling in nothing at all.
It's just out of the boiler, Tic.
textes.Il sort une lame ! Le lâche !: He's drawing a blade! The coward!
textes.Il sort, tout au fond, un disque dans un: From the very back, he pulls out a record in a handmade sleeve: a sun and a cloud holding hands. “Vinyle kept this one for the day the two villages made peace. That day has come.” The music starts: djembes, a fuzzy guitar, and two girls' voices… those of Granny Sunflower and Mother Downpour, fifty years ago.
textes.Il t'a dit quelque chose ?: Did he say anything to you?
textes.Il t'a dit quelque chose, celui-là ?: Did that one say anything to you?
textes.Il t'a touché ? Avec son Appendice Nouil: He touched you? With his Noodly Appendage? (The Reverend takes off his golden colander, presses it to his heart, and puts it back on crooked.) My child… In forty years, he has touched only three people. A fisherman, a baker, and Nonno Tortellini, in 1987 — he says it was a wink, but it was a noodle. You are the fourth. Here: two plates of Mamma's spaghetti, two focaccias fresh from the oven, and a title, which I'll write myself in the great book. Ramen, my child. Ramen!
textes.Il t'en reste combien, des dents ?: How many teeth have you got left?
What you mostly need is gloves.
textes.Il te manque des pièces… Bon. Je te l'of: You're short of coins… Fine. It's on me. But don't tell Spleen, he'd say I'm too nice. He'd be right.
textes.Il te manque quelques pièces. Reviens qu: You're a few coins short. Come back when you've got enough to pay.
textes.Il te manque toufours qu'une dent ? Gard: Thtill only one tooth mithing? Keep the otherth. Teeth are like friendth: you count them when they leave.
textes.Il te réveille d'un coup : endurance au: It wakes you up in one go: stamina at maximum.
textes.Il te suit ! Regarde-le, le groin collé: He's following you! Look at him, snout glued to your shoes! (Père Gaubert laughs, then blows his nose loudly.) It's the pollen. Listen carefully, lad: he eats anything, but not the golden turnips, no, those are my little ones. In the woods and meadows, let him sniff around: he'll find you truffles, and sometimes some old buried thing, a coin, a ring… He has a golden snout, I'm telling you. Here, two truffles he found for me yesterday, and a few coins. And if you don't already have a whistle to call your animals, take my father's, carved from bone: a dog, a cat, a rat and a pig all around it. Whistle, and your pig will come back. Gently with my little one, all right!
textes.Il tient depuis deux cents ans, Jos. Et: It's held for two hundred years, Jos. And so has your hinge.
textes.Il tient. L'autre aussi, celui qui dort: It's holding up. So is the other one, the one that sleeps next to it.
It flows the other way, the current.
textes.Il tourne tous les jours, le vent, Matth: The wind turns every day, Matthias.
He'll come round to my side one day.
textes.Il tousse encore ? Je vais tourner le so: Still coughing? I'll turn the bellows round.
Then it even cheats in its sleep.
textes.Il va battre son record… Non… Si… NON !: He's going to beat his record… No… Yes… NO!
textes.Il va encore me faire un bisou ?: Is he going to give me a kiss again?
textes.Il va très bien ! Enfin, il tourne un pe: It's very well! Well, it spins a little when I think about it.
textes.Il va, il vient ! C'est un toit très voy: It comes, it goes! It's a well-travelled roof.
textes.Il veut des dents de crocodile. Il dit q: He wants crocodile teeth. He says it's for an iron fist. I say it's for a necklace for his sweetheart. He looks at me, picks up an iron bar, and bends it. He says nothing. He hasn't got a sweetheart. But every time I bring it up, his ears turn red. I'm keeping an eye on it.
textes.Il veut que ma tour devienne le « Minist: He wants my tower to become the “Ministry of Geography”. He came and put a plaque on my door. I agreed, on condition he never again asks me to draw an avenue. He swore. The next day, he wanted a trading port. I drew him a trading port. On a separate sheet.
textes.Il veut savoir où sont les grottes de so: He wants to know where his grandfather's caves are. I told him: “Under the feet of the one who guards.” He went crawling under the Skala, at night, and the caïd picked him up. He thinks I'm making fun of him. I'm not. I'm answering. He doesn't know how to listen yet.
textes.Il veut une revanche. Il dit qu'on ne l': He wants a rematch. He says we never did it for real. He offers it every evening, at the counter. He talks softly, I hear nothing, I say “WHAT?!”, he repeats, I still hear nothing. It's been two years. He's patient. I'm not. One of these days, I'll end up understanding. And then he'll be sorry.
He'll come anyway. He likes you.
textes.Il vient me voir tous les deux jours ave: He comes to see me every other day with a rhyme for “large”. “Barge”, “charge”, “marge”. I explained that “Large-Louis on the charge” didn't mean much. He said: “It means here I come!” He's not wrong. I wrote it in my notebook, just in case.
textes.Il vient toutes les semaines demander qu: He comes every week to ask when the flagship will be ready. I answer: “When I say so.” He writes the answer down in a little official notebook. He has forty pages of “When I say so”. One day, he brought me honey, to speed up the work. I ate the honey. The work goes at the same speed.
textes.Il vise mes engrenages ! Je vais te fair: It aims at my gears! I'll take you to court!
textes.Il voulait interdire les bagarres le dim: He wanted to ban brawls on Sundays. Nobody listened to him. So one Sunday, I climbed up on my counter with my rolling pin and said: “Today, the Governor has spoken.” Not one brawl all day. The next day, he gave a speech on the success of his policy. I let him. It was sweet.
textes.Il voulait partir chasser les jaguars du: He wanted to go and hunt the jaguars of the Smoking Mountain. I consulted the calendar: a day worth nothing for hunting. I forbade it. He obeyed, but he spent the day sharpening his weapon outside my door. Very noisily. In the evening, I told him: “Your weapon is ready. Your patience, not yet.”
textes.Il voulait une louche solide. Je lui ai: He wanted a sturdy ladle. I forged him a ladle. A handle as long as an arm. A bowl big enough for a whole soup. He lifts it with both hands. He complains. But it doesn't break. A ladle that breaks is soup on the floor. Soup on the floor is a hungry crew. I thought about the crew.
textes.Il voulait vendre des places au premier: He wanted to sell front-row seats for my festivals. I told him music is like the wind. He said: “The wind, I can sell.” He came back the next day with fans: “Wind of Ehécatl, two beans.” He sold one. To his mother. She said it was hot.
textes.Il voulait voir les étoiles « d'un peu p: He wanted to see the stars “a little closer”. I levitated him above the Observatory. At three metres, he clung to my arm shouting: “They're fine from a distance!” The master of light is afraid of heights. I haven't told anyone. Except you. And the wind.
It's waiting for you. It lives up to its name.
textes.Il vous fait des bisous de lumière ?: Does it give you light kisses?
textes.Il vous manque quelques pièces. Revenez: You're a few coins short. Come back when you can pay.
He thanks you. As for me, I sigh.
