textes.Il y a aussi la route, à l'est, qui desc: There's also the road, to the east, that winds down to the port. The robot porters take it. They get dizzy in the cabin.
textes.Il y a cent ans, Glaucos a ramolli des c: A hundred years ago, Glaucos softened some shells in the crystal's heat and blew into them through a reed. A round lamp, in three minutes. It takes me three weeks to carve one. I said: “That's cheating.” He packed up his tools, very politely, and left that same evening. He kept the apron.
A hundred years ago, Orsik never laughed. He counted. So one evening, I took a ruby from him. Just one. Then another the next day. At the Forge Festival, I gave him back a full mug: three hundred and sixty-five rubies. The face he made… I thought he was going to cry. He laughed. For the first time.
textes.Il y a cent ans, Yggdrasil a cessé de do: A hundred years ago, Yggdrasil stopped giving its seeds. That same winter, Églantine, queen of the root fairies and my friend, wrote to me: “Something is growing under my throne. Come.” When I went down, the brambles were already closing off the north. I called to her for three nights. The brambles answered. She didn't.
textes.Il y a cent ans, le grand tremblement a: A hundred years ago, the great quake split the old gates of Forgefer. The old king told me: “Forty days.” I took thirty-nine. Grimli hauled the ore up for me on his back. On the last evening, a spark singed off half his beard. He says it grew back finer. He's lying. The gates, though, haven't budged. Now that's solid.
textes.Il y a cent ans, les ronces ont poussé a: A hundred years ago the brambles grew in the north, and they took our Queen Églantine. I cried for a whole month. And one morning I saw that my tears weren't drying: they shone, perfectly round, like moon dew. Since then, when I lose my drops… I make more. It's not very practical.
textes.Il y a cent ans, un automne, j'ai trouvé: A hundred years ago, one autumn, I found a black shoot up north, in the old root. It smelled of iron. I warned Queen Églantine. I warned everyone. They said: “You're always grumbling, Grommelot.” Yes. That time I had good reason to grumble. When winter came, the brambles were everywhere. And the queen, inside them.
textes.Il y a cent ans, à la fête de l'Aube, en: A hundred years ago, at the Dawn festival, in the middle of a ballad, my G string snapped. A blue-eyed elf climbed onto the stage and replaced it with a golden thread, without a word. Then she stepped down again. I forgot the rest of the ballad. I forgot Celebrë singing. I forgot my own name, I think.
textes.Il y a cent ans, à la fête de l'Aube, je: A hundred years ago, at the Dawn festival, I was singing the “Ballad” with Caelan. A string broke, Ilyria came up to replace it, and Caelan ran off after her. Mid-verse! I sang alone for a whole hour, making up the words. They say it was my finest hour. Mostly it was my longest.
textes.Il y a cent ans, à la fête de l'Aube, un: A hundred years ago, at the Dawn festival, a string on Caelan's harp snapped in the middle of the ballad. I had a golden thread in my pocket, I can't remember why. I went up, tied it, came back down. He looked at me as if I'd brought him the moon. He's played under my window every night since. I should have kept my thread.
textes.Il y a cent cinquante ans, le volcan a t: A hundred and fifty years ago, the volcano coughed all winter long. The ash fell like grey snow, and the terrace forges mustn't go out. So we brought the big cauldron out of the city, Bramm carried it on his back, and I fed a hundred dwarves with a cracked ladle. Borin forged me a spoon. I still have it.
textes.Il y a cent quatre-vingts ans, les genou: A hundred and eighty years ago, my father's knees gave out. He handed me the spear without a word. The first visitor that day was a goat. I made it wait three hours, on principle. It ate the hem of my cloak. I didn't move. You don't move.
textes.Il y a cent vingt ans, j'ai chanté la ma: A hundred and twenty years ago, on the steps of the Gate, I sang the high tide so softly that Triton fell asleep. I saw him. He looked so peaceful that I didn't want to wake him. The next day, the Pearl of the avenue had vanished. I've never said a word, {surnom}. Least of all to him.
textes.Il y a cent vingt ans, je suivais une ve: A hundred and twenty years ago, I was following a vein of iron, happy as can be, and I came up a little too far. My head popped out through the floor of the guardhouse, between Bramm's boots. I asked him if he'd moved house. He's never forgiven me. Me, I've forgotten why he's cross. Almost.
textes.Il y a cent vingt ans, le sol de ma loge: A hundred and twenty years ago, the floor of my guardhouse cracked open. A head popped out, between my boots. A helmet, a grey beard: Grimli. “Sorry, I was looking for my tunnel.” The gate was never forced. The floor was. That doesn't count. I filled the hole myself. With a gate stone, and my fist.

A hundred and twenty years ago, the floor of my guardhouse heaved up and his head came out between my boots. He said: “Oh, Bramm. Have you moved house?” I hadn't moved house. I filled the hole with a gate stone. It's still there. I stand guard on it, every day.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, Cerfeuil est parti avec: Five years ago, Cerfeuil left with the mist. That's how we say it, here. The night before, he made me promise to look after Trèfle and Mochi, my goddaughter, who wasn't even one. I said “Promise, boom!” to make him laugh. Since then, every morning, I run to the bakery with the flour sacks. I say it's training. Trèfle pretends to believe me.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, Cerfeuil, le mari de Tr: Five years ago, Cerfeuil, Trèfle's husband, left with the mist. Trèfle couldn't sleep any more: I could smell her tiredness through the bakery door. One dawn, I gathered the mist off the big pond and sealed it in a vial, with a moon feather from Plumette. Trèfle slept. The vial of mist was born. Ursule buys it for the silver; I don't ask bears questions.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, Philibert est entré au: Five years ago, Philibert came into the Bazaar with an empty box, apologising at every step. He was going to throw it away. I bought it for eight coins. He went bright red, he wanted to pay me back on the spot, and I pushed him out the door so he couldn't. Since then, I order twenty a month from him. My best seller.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, Pivoine m'a vendu ma pr: Five years ago, Pivoine sold me my first vial of mist. I dipped a little bell in it. The silver sang clearer. Much clearer. Since then, I quench silver and blades in a trough of cold mist. Not even Borin knows. Charbon forged a little bell for every pair of ears born. So do I. They sing better now.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, au Perroquet, la nouvel: Five years ago, at the Perroquet, the new waitress spilled a punch on me. The whole glass. She was all red, she kept saying sorry, sorry. I said: “It's nothing, it smells nice.” It was true. Since then, I play cards there every evening. Against Victor. I lose. I look somewhere else.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, elle m'a acheté sa prem: Five years ago, she bought her first vial of mist from me. She took a little silver bell out of her pocket, dipped it in, right there on my counter, and shook it. The bell sang, clear as a dewdrop. Ursule said: “Hm.” Then she bought the whole shelf. I didn't ask anything. You don't ask bears questions.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, j'ai acheté une fiole d: Five years ago, I bought a vial of mist. On her counter, I dipped a silver bell in it. It sang. Clear, like never before. Pivoine raised her nose. She didn't ask anything. I bought the whole shelf. Good. She doesn't ask questions. I don't answer.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, j'allais jeter une boît: Five years ago, I was about to throw away an empty box. I used to make them back then, pretty wooden boxes to keep my ideas in. They stayed empty: my ideas all existed already. Madame Bricolette saw me with that one in my hand. She bought it from me for eight coins. It's my only invention ever sold, and the Bazaar's best seller. Basile doesn't like it. Well… he's entitled to.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, j'avais dix-huit ans. J: Five years ago, I was eighteen. I bought a return ticket “for the day”. In the evening, when Léon rang for departure, I stayed on the quay. He shouted: “Coming aboard?” I shouted: “I'm staying!” He kept my return ticket. That same evening, I helped carry crates into the Perroquet without being asked, and Toni hired me.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, la grande tempête a fra: Five years ago, the great storm hit the library head-on. The wind came in through the top window and took four books, the way you pick fruit. I watched them go off into the night, pages open like wings. I called with all my might. The wind called louder. I had never lost a book. Not one.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, une petite est descendu: Five years ago, a young girl stepped off L'Hirondelle with a bag and a return ticket she never used. That very evening, she helped me carry my crates down to the cellar, without me asking. One, two, three, four. At the fifth, I told her: “You start tomorrow.” She answered: “I'm starting now.” That was Lola.
textes.Il y a cinquante ans, Orsik a voulu desc: Fifty years ago, Orsik wanted to go down the mine and pick his stones himself. I guided him. We got lost, of course, and he dropped a ruby on the way. Last year, I found it in a tunnel and sold it to him. He recognised his own stone. He paid for it anyway, in tears.
textes.Il y a cinquante ans, j'ai voulu choisir: Fifty years ago, I wanted to pick my stones myself, deep in the mine. Grimli guided me. We got lost for two days, and I dropped a ruby in the dark. Last year, he came to sell it to me, very proud. MY ruby. With my mark on it. I paid for it anyway. So he wouldn't sell it to someone else.
textes.Il y a de la houle au large, aujourd'hui: There's a swell out at sea today. Your favourite. I'm keeping the bow for you. Bring an oilskin.
textes.Il y a des années, on se volait les clie: Years ago, we stole each other's customers every night. So we signed a treaty, on a Crâne Fendu napkin: at my place, you bet small and eat well; at his, you bet big and don't eat. The napkin is framed behind my counter. He signed in beautiful handwriting. Me, with a cross. He didn't say anything. He's polite.
textes.Il y a des chats à Tazira aussi. Des cha: There are cats in Tazira too. Whole cats, with no people around them. They steal maps from pirates. I like them.
textes.Il y a des coquillages magnifiques au bo: There are gorgeous shells at the end of the beach, just behind the sound wall.
textes.Il y a des lumières dans les grottes, so: There are lights in the caves, under the cliff, behind us. At night. I don't have the men to go and look.
textes.Il y a deux ans, au nouvel an, un confet: Two years ago, at New Year, a piece of confetti slipped into the escapement of the great clock. Just one. Blue. Result: one second fast. The only one in its life. I scolded the clock. Then I scolded Capucine. The clock, at least, seemed to understand.
textes.Il y a deux ans, au nouvel an, un de mes: Two years ago, at New Year, one of my confetti got stuck in the escapement of the great clock. It went one second fast. The only time in its whole history! Tic scolded the clock, then he scolded me, in exactly the same voice. He was finding confetti in the works until May.
textes.Il y a deux ans, elle m'a apporté un paq: Two years ago she brought me a parcel. I won't tell you more. Neither will she: she promised. Since then, when she runs into my uncle, she looks at her feathers. A postwoman says nothing. But a postwoman carries heavy loads, sometimes.
textes.Il y a deux ans, en pleine nuit : « ALER: Two years ago, in the middle of the night: “ALERT!” Croc-Gris had seen a monster. Everyone ran out in their nightshirts! Me, I took the Lookout zip line, in my pyjamas, for the first time in my life. Wheeeee! It was SO cool! The monster was Hulotte with her lantern. Since then I do one alert a day. Croc-Gris growls. That means he's happy.
textes.Il y a deux ans, quand Éclair est tombée: Two years ago, when Éclair fell at the root bend, Grisou shouted “you OK?” as he went by. Me, nothing. I jumped. I tell myself that's racing. But Grisou, he shouted. It bugs me sometimes. In the evening. Not for long. Hop.
textes.Il y a deux ans, Éclair menait la course: Two years ago, Éclair was leading the race. Ahead of me up to the root bend. Then a wet root, and she slipped. I jumped over her. Hop. Without stopping. I won. Everyone says that's racing. I say that's racing. I say it often. Maybe a bit too often.
textes.Il y a deux ans, Éclair menait, et elle: Two years ago Éclair was leading, and she fell at the root bend. Bondi jumped over her like an arrow, without a glance. Me, as I went by, I shouted “you OK?”. I didn't stop, mind, it was the race. But I shouted. Him, nothing. I'm not saying that makes me a better runner. I'm just saying.
textes.Il y a deux ans. La Grande Course. J'éta: Two years ago. The Great Race. I was in front. In front of Bondi. Up to the root bend, before the Lookout. A wet root. … I fell. Bondi jumped over. Without looking. Grisou went past. He shouted: “You OK?” … Third. I finished third. The root is still there. So am I.
textes.Il y a deux ans. Pleine nuit. Une forme: Two years ago. Dead of night. A shape climbs the Mother Oak. A long-necked monster, with a fiery eye at the end. I sound the alarm. All of Ramure comes down, in nightshirts, by the stairs and the zip line. It was Hulotte. His lantern. His long telescope. … It was a drill. Very successful. The whole village down in four minutes.
textes.Il y a deux chutes d'eau ici. L'eau de l: There are two waterfalls here. The water of the bigger one, in the north-east, comes from very deep under the ground. It tastes of stars.
textes.Il y a deux mois, ma tante m'a offert un: Two months ago, my aunt gave me a week here. One week! The first morning, I climbed up to the lookout with my sketchbook. The light fell over the port all at once, like a tablecloth being shaken out. I forgot to draw. I sat there till noon. And I decided to stay. A little. A lot.
textes.Il y a deux mois, à trois heures du mati: Two months ago, at three in the morning, the blue glow of Stoneheart pulsed twice a minute instead of once. Just one night. The next day, at the Crankshaft, Prudence told me her piano had played a tune she'd never taught it. Same night, same hour. We compared our notebooks, very quietly. We haven't told anyone.
textes.Il y a deux siècles, Taeron m'a dit que: Two centuries ago Taeron told me my sail between Fil-d'Aube and the Mother Tree would last a year. He's replaced his planks four times since. My sail hasn't budged. Every time he replaces a plank, I bring him up a cup of herbal tea and say nothing. He hates that.
textes.Il y a dix ans, Grumbald a inventé la la: Ten years ago, Grumbald invented frozen lava and said it was the best dessert in Pandémonia. I answered with my honey cake. The Grand Dessert Contest took place on the Great Square, with Asmodin as judge. He tasted, tasted again, and tasted again. He declared a tie. Grumbald says it wasn't.
textes.Il y a dix ans, Héloïse a construit le t: Ten years ago, Héloïse built the cable car, and she made me its keeper. Me! Soon after, a cabin stopped in the middle of the cable, with the mayor of Port-Azur inside. An hour. He wrote a poem about the clouds, all rhyming in “-ation”. And it was my little Écrou, fifteen years old, who climbed along the cable to release the brake. My palms still sweat thinking about it.
textes.Il y a dix ans, en traversant le Bois To: Ten years ago, crossing the Twisted Wood, a wheel broke on a root. Prune stopped dead and refused to move another step. The old oaks leaned over to look. The mushrooms lit up all around us. I got the message. I never fixed the wheel. It's still there, propped against an oak.
textes.Il y a dix ans, j'étais dans la nacelle: Ten years ago I was in the basket lift with the mailbag. Halfway up, snap: the rope broke. Bourru held it all with his bare hands. I clutched the bag to me and waited, counting. I've never ridden in it since. I tell the children I fly. I take the stairs. Two years later I handed the mailbag to Plumette.
textes.Il y a dix ans, tante Sésame est partie: Ten years ago, Aunt Sésame left for the longest swap of her life: “this bell for a trip round the world”. With the family bell at the tip of her tail, she went down the stairs jingling. Since then, Plumette sometimes brings me a card from some impossible place: a town on stilts, a singing desert, a floating island. I've got nine.
textes.Il y a dix ans, un matin de brume, la Mu: Ten years ago, one misty morning, the Murène sailed past our boat. I didn't think. I jumped. I swam and swam, with my boots on. Halfway there, I thought I'd sink. And then a rope dropped in front of my nose. It was the lookout, Gaspard, who'd spotted me before anyone else. He said nothing. He pulled me in.
textes.Il y a dix ans. La cinquième corde. Elle: Ten years ago. The fifth rope. It snapped halfway up. Hulotte inside, with the mail bag. I grabbed the rope. Bare hands. It burned. I held on. Ursule jammed the pulley with an iron bar. Pivoine tended my paws. Pomme-de-Pin and her grandmother wove the sixth rope in one night. Hulotte never got back in. Hrmm.
textes.Il y a dix jours, la Grande Averse (une: Ten days ago, the Great Downpour (a shower of clear water from a pure white cloud) washed over Sketched Island: the Stone Palette overflowed, and the island's nine pots of colour were carried off by the water to the four corners of the island. Since then, everything has been black and white. Grandma Aquarelle, the village elder, has entrusted you with the island's Brush. You need to find the nine pots and pour each one into its numbered paint well.
textes.Il y a dix-huit ans, je me suis présenté: Eighteen years ago, I ran for mayor. A perfect tie with Aristide! We settled it with pétanque, on the square, in front of the whole town. Last ball, Marcel takes out his tape measure, measures, and announces: “Aristide, by one centimetre.” ONE centimetre! They stole the town hall from me, that's what. Marcel measured like a postman.
textes.Il y a dix-huit ans, égalité parfaite av: Eighteen years ago, a perfect tie with Raymond, the baker. Not one vote between us! So, as we do round here, we settled it with pétanque. Marcel got out his tape measure, knelt down, measured for a long time. “One centimetre. To Aristide.” I won. Between you and me… I've never been entirely sure about that centimetre.
textes.Il y a douze ans, Margaux est entrée dan: Twelve years ago, Margaux walked into the shop, saw the “for sale” sign and said: “I'll take it.” Just like that! We signed on the kneading trough, with the flour pencil. She was shaking so much her signature took up three lines. I kept the paper. You can still see the pencil mark on the trough.
textes.Il y a douze ans, c'est moi qui ai vu la: Twelve years ago, I was the one who spotted the Murène Noire first, at daybreak, black sails on a grey sea. I rang three times, the old signal. The Admiral was on the poop deck before the third. She asked: “How many cannons?” I said: “Twenty-two.” She said: “Good. We have forty.” They don't fire, but still.
textes.Il y a douze ans, j'ai chargé une barque: Twelve years ago, I loaded a boat with shovels and axes and rowed all the way to the Fire Reefs. The beach guard wouldn't let me in. Borin came down, struck one of my axes on a rock and said: “Not bad, for a tall one.” He bought the lot, in gold. To melt it down.
textes.Il y a douze ans, je suis arrivée ici po: Twelve years ago, I came here for a week's holiday. On the third day, outside Au Pain Doré, I saw the “For Sale” sign. Raymond was stopping after forty years at the oven. I breathed in the smell of bread through the open door, and I bought it. With all my savings. I never took the boat home.
textes.Il y a douze ans, je suis devenue postiè: Twelve years ago, I became a postwoman. Marcel was in his last year as postman. He taught me the round: every dog, every step, every box that sticks. “The villa at the end, a sugar lump for the dog. High Street, the third step creaks. At Hortense's, you knock even without a letter.” I wrote it all down. I still have the notebook.
textes.Il y a douze ans, la Murène Noire est en: Twelve years ago, the Murène Noire sailed into the bay, twenty-two cannons run out. Croc-de-Sel wanted to “visit our holds”. I had every gunport on the Léviathan smoking with tar, and I went to see him in a rowing boat. I told him our forty cannons were loaded. He left. He still doesn't know they've been cold for two centuries.
textes.Il y a douze ans, la veille de la fête d: Twelve years ago, on the eve of the flood festival, my oven suddenly cracked, like an eggshell. The whole village was waiting for my bread. Ptahmosé arrived with clay, without a word. He worked all night by lamplight. At dawn, I had a new oven. We had bread for the festival. And we've been arguing ever since.
textes.Il y a douze ans, le four de Mérit s'est: Twelve years ago, Mérit's oven cracked on the eve of the flood festival. No oven, no bread; no bread, no festival. I took some clay and worked all night. By morning, the oven was hot, the bread was baking, and my hands were burnt. Mérit said the oven smoked a little on the left. It doesn't.
textes.Il y a douze ans, quand la Murène Noire: Twelve years ago, when the Murène Noire sailed into the bay, I'm the one who had the idea of making smoke pour out of the old cannons' gunports. Morgane had the idea of saying it was hers. She was right: an old storyteller's idea, nobody would have followed it.
textes.Il y a douze hivers, je suis rentrée des: Twelve winters ago, I came back from the northern cliffs frozen to the bone. I saw the Mirror Lake, all flat, all white, and I thought: the biggest bath in the world. I heated it. A bit too much. At midnight, the lake was steaming and I was in it, with my woolly hat. Borée arrived in his nightshirt. He hasn't spoken to me since. Well, he has: “Madam.”
textes.Il y a du vent aujourd'hui, ça va secoue: It's windy today, it's going to be bumpy.
textes.Il y a huit ans, j'ai construit la paill: Eight years ago, I built the beach hut with my own hands: palm leaves, bamboo, rope and lots of songs. The first night, I had three customers and a crab. The crab stayed the longest. He didn't order anything, but he danced. I called him Mister Pincer. He still comes back sometimes, on party nights.
textes.Il y a huit ans, les méduses sont arrivé: Eight years ago, the jellyfish arrived at the same time as the tourists. Sixty stings in one week! I invented a vinegar and aloe balm in my kitchen, holding my nose. The bravest of my patients was Sergeant Lefort, stung on the calf while keeping watch on the beach. He's been coming back ever since. For his back. Through the back door.
textes.Il y a huit ans, mon père a commencé à l: Eight years ago, my father started delivering to the wrong trees. He walked with his nose in the air, looking for stars in broad daylight. Tilleul got Bedaine's accounts for a whole month! He thought it was a very long story, with lots of numbers. So I took the satchel, and my father went up to count the stars. Everyone was happy. Especially Bedaine.
textes.Il y a huit jours, j'ai eu trente ans. A: Eight days ago, I turned thirty. Achille arrived at dawn with a big parcel in flowery paper: steam-powered wings. He wanted to “just try them, two minutes”. He took off from the airfield at twelve minutes past nine; Tic Tacquet noted the time. I didn't even have time to hand him an umbrella. He never came back down.
textes.Il y a longtemps, j'ai empêché Jos de fa: A long time ago, I stopped Jos from doing something very silly with his cannon. We promised never to talk about it. So I don't. But when he bangs too hard, I cough, very loudly, on the stairs. He gets it. He bangs more softly. For an hour.
textes.Il y a longtemps, les Anciens vivaient s: Long ago, the Ancients lived beneath your islands. A people of stone and serpents. They chained Nâga, then they vanished. We stayed in the trees.
textes.Il y a longtemps, un pirate a caché un t: Long ago, a pirate hid a treasure in the caves behind the Skala. Another pirate, his grandson perhaps, has come back to look for it. Stories always come back.
textes.Il y a neuf ans, un dimanche, le cœur d': Nine years ago, one Sunday, Albert's heart stopped. Just like that, between two spoonfuls. On the Monday, I opened up again. You don't close a grocery: there are people who need salt. On the top shelf, I left the last jar of fig jam he made. I dust it in the mornings. That's all.
textes.Il y a plus de cinquante ans, sur ce qua: More than fifty years ago, on this quay, a little cabin boy came up to me, twisting his cap in his hands. He was crying so hard he couldn't finish his sentence. I was the one who comforted him, if you can believe it. That day I learned you can have a heart in pieces and still wipe someone's nose.
textes.Il y a quarante ans, j'ai fait une parti: Forty years ago, I played a game against the baker, Raymond. He said his ball was closer. It wasn't. We argued, and we never stopped. Eighteen years ago, at the election, Raymond and Aristide were tied. We settled it with pétanque. And I was the one who measured. One centimetre. For Aristide.
textes.Il y a quarante ans, j'étais charpentier: Forty years ago, I was a carpenter and went looking for timber out towards the mists. I got lost for three days. A big bear found me under a tree, carried me to his village and told me, under the full moon, the tale of the moon that fell into the pond. He fell asleep in the middle. I had to finish it myself.
textes.Il y a quarante ans, je suis arrivé ici: Forty years ago, I arrived here as assistant to old Anatole, the librarian. The same autumn as a young woman who made light with her hands: Séraphine. Anatole showed me the shelves, very tall, and the ladder. I went pale. He smiled: “Then the books will have to come down.” I learned telekinesis in one winter.
textes.Il y a quarante ans, la grande grille du: Forty years ago, the great grate of the Heart cracked in the middle of the night. Embers were rolling across the flagstones. I ran to fetch Ferronde, who came in her nightgown, hammer in hand. She forged a new grate before dawn. I've never thanked her out loud. I leave her a jar of candied chilli every week.
textes.Il y a quatorze ans, au premier match pu: Fourteen years ago, at the automaton's first public match, it was Héloïse who sat down opposite. She lost in twenty-three moves. And she was the first to applaud, even before the crowd. She stood up, put her monocle back in and said: “Well played, both of you.” I've never forgotten it. I'll never tell her.

Fourteen years ago, at the automaton's first public match, I was the one sitting opposite. Twenty-three moves. I never saw it coming. When the wooden hand laid down my king, I was the first to applaud. Ambroise has never forgotten. Nor have I: I still have my notes from the game. They're very short.
textes.Il y a quatre ans, Yaya m'a traînée à la: Four years ago, Yaya dragged me to the party. I set the camera on the sand, left the shutter open for a long time, and someone walked past with a glow stick. In the photo, there was a ribbon of light, like a dancing snake. Since that night, I've never taken a single photo in daylight.
textes.Il y a quatre ans, je me suis inscrite a: Four years ago, I entered the big Port-Azur waltz contest. In front of everyone, I slipped and fell. People laughed. Walking home that night, I heard the kick at the end of the beach. I went to look. Nobody was watching anybody, everybody was dancing. I danced till morning. The week after, I was dragging Lila along.
textes.Il y a quatre cents ans, Coralin m'a tai: Four hundred years ago, Coralin carved me a ring of pink coral. Twelve coins, friend's price. I offered nine, fiancée's price. A week of haggling! Afterwards we didn't speak for ten years. Now we're talking again. We still haggle. I think that's our way of being married.
textes.Il y a quatre cents ans, je lui ai taill: Four hundred years ago, I carved her a ring of pink coral. I gave her a friend's price: twelve coins. She offered nine, fiancée's price. We haggled for a whole week. By the end, we weren't speaking. The ring's in my drawer. Price: still twelve.
textes.Il y a quatre étés, Gaspard est tombé co: Four summers ago, Gaspard went down like a plank, at high noon, on the dance floor. I lifted him, at my age, and carried him to the spring singing “The Pretty Seagull” to keep the rhythm. My knees sang along with me. I poured the water over his head. He opened one eye and said: “You're singing off key.”
textes.Il y a quatre étés, j'ai dansé à midi, e: Four summers ago, I danced at noon, in full sun, without drinking, for five hours. I woke up in Nono's arms; he was carrying me to the village spring with his creaky knees. He poured water over my head, singing out of tune. Since then, I drink. And I tell everyone to drink. I know, it annoys Sofia.
textes.Il y a quatre étés, je me suis effondré: Four summers ago, I collapsed on the dance floor at high noon. Nono lifted me up, at his age, and carried me to the spring singing an old sea shanty. His knees creaked at every step. Afterwards, he said: “You weigh as much as a dwarf's barrel.” I still don't know if that's a compliment.
textes.Il y a quatre-vingt-dix ans, Thorgal all: Ninety years ago, Thorgal was about to be crowned. He ordered a crown from me: gold from the Royal Forge, eight rubies, “and not too dear”. I worked forty nights. On coronation day, it shone so bright that half the court wept. The king paid me half. He still owes me the other half.
textes.Il y a quatre-vingt-dix ans, on m'a cour: Ninety years ago, I was crowned. Borin had forged the axe, Orsik the crown, Nori read the runes. I trod on my cloak, fell flat in front of the whole court, and the crown rolled all the way to Ulfa's counter. I got up and said: “I was testing it.” They applauded. That's what being king is.
textes.Il y a quelques années, une partie a dur: A few years ago, a game lasted an hour and forty minutes. Ambroise had victory at his fingertips. He thought. He thought some more. And my brass chess clock went “clack”: time's up, one second before his move. He froze with his hand in the air. I wrote it down in the score book. He says it's the finest defeat of his life.
textes.Il y a quelques jours, j'ai vu quelque c: A few days ago, I saw something golden roll off the top of the cliff and bounce on the quay, near the crane. It was shining. I didn't have time to pick it up.
textes.Il y a quelques siècles, il a voulu refa: A few centuries ago, he decided to redo the nose on King Atlas's statue, chipped by the flood. He carved a new nose, a very handsome one. His own. Since then, in profile, my great-grandfather looks like Coralin, and Coralin walks past the statue with his head held high.
textes.Il y a quinze ans, j'ai débarqué avec un: Fifteen years ago, I landed here with an ice-cream churn, a bag of coarse salt and not much else. Victor was already selling ice creams on the beach. His melted before they reached your mouth: you drank them through a straw. I set up my kiosk. In one summer, all of Port-Azur was queuing at mine. Poor Victor. He got over it. More or less.
textes.Il y a quinze ans, j'ai entendu un gamin: Fifteen years ago, I heard a kid playing guitar on the jetty for three fishermen and a seagull. It gave me goosebumps. I offered him a stage, a meal and a wage. He looked at the wage like an insult, and at the meal like a gift. He took all three. He's never said thank you. He plays — that's better.
textes.Il y a quinze ans, j'en avais vingt. Je: Fifteen years ago, I was twenty. I played at the end of the jetty for the fishermen coming home. They paid me in sardines. One evening, Toni stopped to listen. He offered me a stage, a meal and a wage. I said yes. Ever since, I've wondered whether my grandfather would be proud or sad. Both, maybe.
textes.Il y a quinze ans, je suis arrivée à Por: Fifteen years ago, I arrived in Port-Azur with a folding table, a purple scarf and a deck of cards so dog-eared that the king of hearts had lost his crown. I set up the table on the promenade, facing the sea. I live on Rue Haute, next door to Hortense, who said hello to me for the first time after three years. The cards had foreseen it.
textes.Il y a quinze ans, on cousait l'envelopp: Fifteen years ago, we were sewing the Zéphyr's envelope on the giant sewing machine. My sleeve got caught in it. I lost my right arm. Master Rivet spent the night with me, over the plans for a new arm. I made it in brass. It's stronger than the old one. It itches when it rains. The old one never itched. You can't have everything.
textes.Il y a quinze ans, un grand chef du cont: Fifteen years ago, a big-shot chef from the mainland arrived with a chef's hat as tall as the lighthouse and copper pans. He said our bouillabaisse was “rustic”. RUSTIC! We held a contest on the quay, in front of the whole harbour. He put butter in it. Butter, in a bouillabaisse! I won. Since then, it's written on my door: the others are just soups.
textes.Il y a quinze ans, un éboulement a coupé: Fifteen years ago, a landslide cut the line. It was never repaired. The Bielle was going to the scrapyard. I bought her with all my savings and had her hoisted to the top of the cliff. On the way up, a wheel came loose and fell all the way down to the harbour; Gonzague kept it. As for the Bielle, she became my coffee machine. She just changed jobs.
textes.Il y a seize ans, Marius est tombé sur l: Sixteen years ago, Marius collapsed on the quay, beside me, the net in his hands. Since then, Anselme doesn't speak to me. Odette, my neighbour, saves me the best mooring. I have my boat, the “Marguerite”. My sea bream go to Paulo's and to Rosalie's. And I sold a sardine bone to a lord. A man has to laugh a little.
textes.Il y a seize ans, un matin de juin, Mari: Sixteen years ago, one June morning, Marius was untangling old Vasseur's net with Fernand, on the quay. He sat down. He didn't get up again. His heart, the doctor said. Since then, Anselme and Fernand don't speak. As for me, I leave Fernand the best spot on the quay. He was the last one to talk to Marius. That's worth a mooring ring.
textes.Il y a seize ans. Je finissais ma veille: Sixteen years ago. I was finishing my watch, up there. I saw my brother fall on the quay, next to Fernand, the net in his hands. Three hundred and twenty steps. I came down them like never before. It was over when I got there. Since then, the net has been at Fernand's. And I'm up top.
textes.Il y a sept ans, quand l'horloge s'est a: Seven years ago, when the clock stopped, Hortense looked so lonely on her bench. The next morning, I left a sprig of lavender there. And the next. And every morning since. She thinks it's Marcel. I don't set her straight. She's been waiting for someone for fifty years, {surnom}. I only wanted her to find something when she arrived.
textes.Il y a sept ans, toute la plage était là: Seven years ago, the whole beach turned out for our race. Me on the sand, him in the water, from the beach hut to the rocks. I had my new shoes on, he was warming up his shoulders. And then the red flag went up. “Rules,” he said. I ran anyway, all on my own, to the rocks. Nobody was counting.
textes.Il y a sept ans, un retraité en short es: Seven years ago, a retired man in shorts turned up on my beach: Bernard. On the first day, he told me he ran faster than I swim. We organised a race, him on the sand, me in the water, the whole beach watching. At the start, the wind picked up: red flag. And I'm the one who raises the flag. Race cancelled. Never settled.
textes.Il y a sept ans, un rouage a cassé. Le j: Seven years ago, a cog broke. On the anniversary of Jules's departure, if you can believe it. Since then, I still go up to oil it twice a day. Hector “never has the time”, the mayor makes promises. In the mornings, on my bench, young Django plays and I keep the beat. Every day I find a sprig of lavender there: Marcel, I'm sure of it. And my neighbour Rita foretells a stranger. Nonsense.
textes.Il y a sept ans, à la retraite, je suis: Seven years ago, newly retired, I came on holiday to do three laps of the island. I never left. The first year, I did fountain-to-lighthouse in seventy-eight seconds. A record! And I challenged Kevin: me on the sand, him in the water. The red flag went up before the start. We're still waiting for the rematch.
textes.Il y a six ans, Salomé m'a vendu « une c: Six years ago, Salomé sold me “an ancient map of Stoneheart, brought back from the desert”. I paid three months' work for it and studied it for a whole week. It was an embroidered tablecloth from Tazira. Stoneheart was a tea stain. She swears she didn't know. She always knows everything.
textes.Il y a six ans, je lui ai vendu une cart: Six years ago, I sold him an ancient map brought back from the desert. I swear I thought it was a map. Well, a little less once he'd walked off with it. It was an embroidered tablecloth, and Stoneheart was a tea stain. He still holds it against me. But he kept the tablecloth: it's on his bedside table.
textes.Il y a six ans, le volant d'un de mes vi: Six years ago, the flywheel from one of my old prototypes fell off the cliff. Gonzague picked it up. He refuses to give it back: “What falls belongs to the crane.” It's a harbour law, apparently. Apparently he also greases it every month. I don't know whether to be cross or flattered.
textes.Il y a six ans, on inaugurait le centièm: Six years ago, we were unveiling the hundredth sweeper on the Grand Square. Half his, half mine. I had slipped a little cylinder inside that sang his song, the shepherds' one. The sweeper sang, out of tune, in front of the whole city. The crowd laughed. Rivet left without a word. The next morning, the sweeper had vanished. We haven't spoken since.
textes.Il y a six ans, un drôle de type a monté: Six years ago, some odd fellow set up speakers at the end of the beach. The next day, not a single mackerel left in the bay. I came over, very cross, to ask him to turn it down. Mistral handed me a coconut: “One track, and I'll turn it down.” I danced till morning. He never turned it down. The mackerel came back anyway.
textes.Il y a soixante ans, une barque de grand: Sixty years ago, a boat of big folk came close to the Reefs. I was on the beach. I raised my hand. I meant to say hello, {surnom}. I don't know how to say hello. They took it for something else and turned back. I watched them go for a long time. You're the first big'un who's come back.
textes.Il y a soixante-dix ans, j'ai mené mon c: Seventy years ago, I led my clan to the foot of the Mother Oak, the only inhabited tree. Up there, the rabbits were trembling. To avoid a quarrel, I suggested a race around the tree: the first Great Race. A rabbit won, and the wolves became the guardians of the Lookout. That evening, a young bear, Tilleul, told me a story. I fell asleep before the end.
textes.Il y a surtout de la brume, Faelar. J'en: What there mostly is is mist, Faelar. I've just come back from there.
textes.Il y a trente ans, après une nuit à bouc: Thirty years ago, after a night plugging a leak under the stern, I found the Admiral, very young, white as Nolwenn's canvas. I said: “She'll hold a hundred years.” She believed me. Since then, I can't say anything else. If I ever say ninety-nine, she'll never sleep again.
textes.Il y a trente ans, au Crâne Fendu, f'ai: Thirty yearth ago, at the Crâne Fendu, I had a little dithcuthion with Belle-Humeur. He wath already in a foul mood. One thingle punch, and all my teeth went off travelling, ekthept two. It wath Gathpard, Mama'th huthband, who got me back on my feet with a grog and a thong. Thinthe then, I'm fond of grogth. And I whithtle when I talk.
textes.Il y a trente ans, j'avais la fièvre. Qu: Thirty years ago, I had a fever. Forty degrees, for once I'm not exaggerating. Marguerite went out to haul in the nets in my place. A squall came down. The boat came back on its own, empty. The new one bears her name. I've never forgiven the fever, {surnom}. Nor myself for staying in bed.
textes.Il y a trente ans, on m'a payé pour livr: Thirty years ago, someone paid me to deliver six barrels to Arcanelle. An island nobody can find. I found it, following a scrap of light in the mist. I unloaded, Berthe served me her pumpkin pie, and I missed the tide. The next day, the mist. The day after, the pie. I've been leaving tomorrow for thirty years.
textes.Il y a trente ans, quelqu'un m'a appelé: Thirty years ago, somebody called me “Belle-Humeur” at the Crâne Fendu. The whole room laughed. I didn't see who'd said it. I thumped whoever was laughing closest. It was Sans-Dents. He's whistled ever since. I still don't know who came up with that name. If I knew… BOOM. But I don't.
textes.Il y a trente ans, une voie d'eau s'est: Thirty years ago, a leak opened under the stern, in the dead of night. I plugged away till dawn. Coming back up, I found the new Admiral, very young, white as a sheet. I said: “She'll hold a hundred years, Admiral.” I had no idea. I've said it again every spring since. Somebody has to say it.
textes.Il y a trente ans, une élève aux cheveux: Thirty years ago, a pupil with orange hair set fire to my beard in her very first lesson. I said: “Excellent! Now, put it out.” It took her three minutes. I gave her the best mark of the year, for enthusiasm. Today, Sulfura is our best flame teacher. I keep my beard short.
textes.Il y a trente ans, {surnom}, j'avais un: Thirty years ago, {surnom}, I had a ticket for the school of cartography on the mainland. I boarded the Swallow. I sat down. And I got off again, before Léon cast off. It wasn't seasickness: the boat hadn't moved. Léon gave me my money back without a word. He's never told anyone. Nor have I, until you.
textes.Il y a trente ans. Brume épaisse, on ne: Thirty years ago. Thick mist, you couldn't see the end of your rod. And there, just at the surface, a golden fish. Big as a rabbit. It looked at me. It laughed. I ran home, which never happens to me. Nobody believed me. Except little Caramel. She believed me until she was twelve. That's long, twelve years. I'm grateful to her.
textes.Il y a trente et un ans, je suis entrée: Thirty-one years ago, I walked into the clockmaker's to sell him a silent alarm clock. Tic Tacquet looked at me, said “good morning” three times, and went back to work without listening to me. That evening, he handed me a watch that ran backwards. He'd made it without realising, while thinking of something else. Of me, I hope. We've been engaged ever since. I still wear it.
textes.Il y a trente et un ans, une dame est en: Thirty-one years ago, a lady came into my shop to sell me a silent alarm clock. She talked and talked… and I listened while making a watch. Absent-minded. When she stopped, the watch was running backwards. I gave it to her. She said: “It's perfect.” It was Bricolette. Every year, on that date, I make her a new one.
textes.Il y a trois ans, Héloïse nous a confié: Three years ago, Héloïse put us in charge of lighting the Grand Square for the Fair. His steam lamp exploded: a shower of soot over the whole jury. My bulbs set fire to the garlands. Héloïse put the oil lamps back without a word. The professor said: “A draw!” I've never forgiven him for being right.
textes.Il y a trois ans, Héloïse nous a demandé: Three years ago, Héloïse asked us to light up the Grand Square for the Fair. Électre with her bulbs, me with my steam lamp. My lamp exploded: a shower of soot over the whole jury. Her bulbs set fire to the garlands. Héloïse put the oil lamps back without a word. Électre and I looked at each other, both black as coal. A draw!
textes.Il y a trois ans, j'ai annoncé que mes y: Three years ago, I announced that my eyes were getting tired. They made me commander of the airfield, with a new helmet, a medal and an office that doesn't move. Gustave took the stick. Since then, I stay on the ground, binoculars glued to my eyes, counting the minutes of delay. They told me it would be more restful. It's worse.
textes.Il y a trois ans, j'ai laissé Lulu peind: Three years ago, I let Lulu paint the sail of my boat. I pictured a nice fish. She painted a purple octopus, huge, with eyes that follow you while you row. Since then, the fish run away from me, I'm sure of it. She says the octopus protects me. From what? I ask. From nothing, she says — proof that it works.
textes.Il y a trois ans, la tempête a couché to: Three years ago, the storm flattened my whole banana grove. I smiled anyway, because I always smile, but inside it hurt. Gaspard turned up with ropes, without a word. We stood every plant back up, one by one, for two days. Only three died. I planted three new ones, and I called them Gaspard.
textes.Il y a trois ans, le bateau du cirque a: Three years ago, the circus boat stopped at Port-Azur and never left again: no money, no big top, the director sold everything. Everyone went home. Me, I didn't have a home any more. I hopped on the Swallow at random, heard the kick from the deck, and thought: hey, a ring!
textes.Il y a trois ans, papi Nono m'a écrit :: Three years ago, Grandpa Nono wrote to me: “There's a beach here where the music never stops. Come.” I took three boats. He was waiting on the jetty in his orange beanie, dancing all by himself. That very night, I fell asleep against the speakers. I'd never slept so well in my life.
textes.Il y a trois ans, un matin, le gros croc: Three years ago, one morning, the big crocodile came out of the river and crossed my field the way you'd cross your kitchen. He flattened the wheat, ate a goat, and left without hurrying. I named him Sobek, like the god. He doesn't deserve it. He's been coming back ever since. He knows the way. So do I: I run the other way.
textes.Il y a trois ans, une tempête est tombée: Three years ago, a storm hit the bay in the middle of the party. Nobody left. We made a human chain, from the dance floor to the top of the dune, and all twenty-four speakers went from hand to hand, with Tchoum at the front, talking to them to calm them down. By morning, the sand had covered everything except us. We plugged back in, and we danced.
textes.Il y a trois cent cinquante ans, il y a: Three hundred and fifty years ago there was the grey winter: the Mother Tree hadn't flowered, the bees were asleep, we were hungry. Faelar told the children about banquets to comfort them. That made it worse! The next day I went to knead with my mother. I swore nobody would ever go hungry here again.
textes.Il y a trois cents ans, avant que la por: Three hundred years ago, before the door of the Mother Tree closed, an elf, already old and very chatty, used to come down to trade stories for riddles. Faelar. One evening he left me one I've never solved. Then the door closed. Three centuries of searching, {surnom}. Imagine how annoyed I am.
textes.Il y a trois cents ans, grand-mère s'est: Three hundred years ago, Grandmother fell asleep beneath the Mother Tree, the way very old elves do, to become one of its leaves. The next day, I was the herbalist of the Bois-Doré. The first to knock on my door was a little Lyra, her mouth all blue. The berries, of course.
textes.Il y a trois cents ans, un courant noir: Three hundred years ago, a black current struck the dome, and the sharks came with it. The tower shook, the three Pearls fell from the crystal's crown, and the sea carried them away. That night, Coralin carved a trident in one hour, and I put it in the hands of a young man who was trembling less than I was. It was Triton.
textes.Il y a trois cents ans, un soir d'orage,: Three hundred years ago, one stormy evening, I was telling stories at the circle to three children. Lightning struck in the middle of my finest sentence. The next day, the firefly spirits had gone and the door of the Mother Tree had closed. I've told that story ever since, but it has no ending. I'm waiting for someone to bring me one.

Three hundred years ago, one stormy evening, the door of the Mother Tree closed. The firefly spirits flew off into the forest. I was on watch that night. Since then, I've been guarding a closed door. Three centuries. Faelar says it's pointless. Faelar doesn't stand guard.
textes.Il y a trois semaines, je me suis offert: Three weeks ago, I treated myself to a weekend at the Grand Hotel in Port-Azur. On the Saturday night, on the beach, I heard a kick coming from across the water, from the other island. I took the last boat over to take a look, “just for an hour”, with my little bag. My suitcase is still at the hotel, I think. I haven't dared ask.
textes.Il y a très, très longtemps, le Grand Mo: A very, very long time ago, the Great Moai had eyes. Two eyes of white coral that saw everything: the sky, the sea, and what sings beneath the earth. Beneath him, a staircase leads down to the Hall of Song, where the island's memory sleeps.
textes.Il y a un an, la Murène Noire s'est arrê: A year ago, the Murène Noire stopped at our place to take on water. At night, I left a note on the kneading trough for my mum: “I'm off to see the world. I'll be back. Tibo.” And I climbed aboard, hidden in a flour barrel. In the morning, the first mate found me, all white. He said: “Hm. A ghost. Give him a brush.” Since then, I've had a brush.
textes.Il y a un arbre si grand que ses racines: There's a tree so tall that its roots drink from every island. The fairies call it Yggdrasil.
There's a charming caravan trader upstairs.
textes.Il y a un chat roux qui vole sur les éta: There's a ginger cat that steals from the stalls. They say he even stole something from the pirates. Not fish. A paper.
textes.Il y a un coffre sur le dais de mousse…: There's a chest on the moss dais… I'm not allowed to touch it. You are!
textes.Il y a un dirigeable qui vient se poser: There's an airship that lands north of the village, the Zéphyr. The engineers of Cliquetis. They wanted to sell me a steam-powered basket. Hrmm. No.
There's a new collection. Shelf seven.
textes.Il y a un palmier en pot près de ma port: There's a potted palm by my door. The healthiest in Tazira. Fronds like sails. People ask me my secret. My secret is Hamid: every evening he takes his rum, says “Thanks, Mama Lou!”, and as soon as I turn my back, he pours it into the pot. The palm thanks me. Hamid thinks he's being discreet.
textes.Il y a un trou dans le mur. Et des caill: There's a hole in the wall. And pebbles everywhere. And a very pleased-with-himself dwarf.
textes.Il y a un trésor enterré quelque part su: There's a treasure buried somewhere on this island. The Stubborn Seagull's pay chest. It was never found. Dig, {surnom}. Dig.
textes.Il y a une autre Lumi, en bas, chez les: There's another Lumi, down below, with the root fairies. One day, I got mixed up: I gave the one up here a letter meant for the one down there. She wrote back! Now the two Lumis write to each other every week, and I'm the one who carries it all. Twice the work. For one mistake. Just one.
textes.Il y a une dizaine d'années, j'ai entend: About ten years ago, I heard about Port-Azur, the island of sunshine. I came with my board, all excited. First morning, I look at the sea: one foot. One foot! A bathtub wave. So I put the board away and bought six boats and some pedalos. “Wave 1” to “Wave 6”. That way, I still get six waves.
textes.Il y a une histoire que je ne change jam: There's one story I never change, {surnom}. When I was little, my father left the dome to follow the whale. He never came back. So I make up all the others, differently every time, so that one isn't left all alone. And in my other stories, he always comes back. By a different road each time.
textes.Il y a une ligne fausse dans mes dix mil: There's one false line in my ten thousand scrolls, {surnom}. Day 3,207: “Nothing to report.” That day, my master Themis fell asleep forever, and I couldn't write it. I never could. A thousand years of exact history, and the only day that truly mattered to me, I left blank.
textes.Il y a vingt ans, Sigrun est arrivée sur: Twenty years ago, Sigrun arrived on the terrace with a sack of barley, red eyes and no roof. She'd just left Ulfa's cellar. I gave her my old bread oven, the one that only heats on one side. She's brewed there ever since. Warm side, the fizz. Cold side, she sleeps.
textes.Il y a vingt ans, j'ai débarqué à Port-A: Twenty years ago, I landed in Port-Azur with my savings in a sock and a blue parrot in a cage. I'd bought it from a sailor; it knew three words, one of them not polite. I rented the old hall on the quay. Hector forged me an iron sign, a parrot with its wings spread. I paid him in dwarven fizz. I'm still paying, actually.
textes.Il y a vingt ans, j'ai ouvert La Murène: Twenty years ago I opened La Murène Ivre in the old salt warehouse. Fishermen on one side, pirates on the other, and me in the middle with my club. On the first day, an old woman mending on the quay said, without looking up: “You still walk like a cabin girl.” Fatima. And three weeks ago, Croc walked in, wearing a captain's hat.
textes.Il y a vingt ans, j'ai ouvert l'Enclume: Twenty years ago, I opened the Blue Anvil, on Lighthouse Street. Problem: Port-Azur is too quiet for an armourer. No dragons, no pirates. Tourists. So I sell souvenir swords. Pays for the coal. Same year, I forged the Perroquet's sign for Toni. Paid in fizz. Hm. I'm still drinking it off.
textes.Il y a vingt ans, j'ai voulu que Port-Az: Twenty years ago, I wanted Port-Azur to be more cheerful. I planted bougainvilleas along the house fronts, one per house, with nobody's permission. They took. Oh yes, they took. They climbed, overflowed, swallowed two balconies and the post office letterbox. Nadine opens it with secateurs. They're gorgeous. And a little greedy.
textes.Il y a vingt ans, pendant le dîner des a: Twenty years ago, during the ambassadors' dinner at the palace, I tested a rocket on the roof opposite. It came in through the window and dived into the soup tureen. Asmodin served the soup flambéed. The ambassadors loved it. Asmodin banned me from the palace. I came back. Through the window. With a cup, to apologise.
textes.Il y a vingt ans, une femme est passée s: Twenty years ago, a woman walked along the quay with a bag on her shoulder. My eyes were already failing. But that step… A cabin girl's step, light in front, heavy behind, as if the quay were rolling. Without raising my head, I said: “You still walk like a cabin girl.” She sat down on a crate. I think she was crying. A pirate! I never told anyone.
textes.Il y a vingt-cinq ans, Grumbald a dit qu: Twenty-five years ago, Grumbald said my fish wasn't fresh. I threw a sardine at his head. The next day, he came back to apologise with a bunch of ember flowers. The day after, he bought my whole stall. The sardine is framed above his counter. He says it was our first date.
textes.Il y a vingt-cinq ans, Moloka a lancé un: Twenty-five years ago, Moloka threw a sardine at Grumbald's head, on my quay, right in front of me: he'd said her fish wasn't fresh. I separated them. A year later, I married them, on the same quay. The sardine was framed, set on a table. Grumbald still has it, above his counter.
textes.Il y a vingt-cinq ans, il a servi un moi: Twenty-five years ago, he served a month on my ship. A young gunner with a mouth bigger than the cannon. One morning he gave me one cheeky answer too many. I won't repeat it, it was a good one. I threw him overboard. He swam back like a wet dog and climbed the ladder. I kept him till the end of the month.
textes.Il y a vingt-cinq ans, j'ai dit à une po: Twenty-five years ago, I told a fishmonger her fish wasn't fresh. She threw a sardine right in my face. The sardine was fresh. Very fresh. I came back to apologise the next day, and I bought her whole stall the day after that. Moloka married me a year later. The sardine is framed above the counter.
textes.Il y a vingt-cinq ans, je suis descendu: Twenty-five years ago, I stepped off the boat with a cooking pot, an apron and my nonna's notebook, tied with a red ribbon. That's all. No chair, no table. I made my first bouillabaisse on the quay, over a fire of old crates. That very evening, the fishermen were queuing with their mess tins. Chez Paulo was born.
textes.Il y a vingt-cinq ans, la sardine est pa: Twenty-five years ago, the sardines left. Three months. The boats came back empty, the town was hungry. My caravan arrived with dates. I told the amin: “Take them. You'll give them back.” The whole town took. And every date was given back to me. Every one. Since then, in Tazira, people greet me. … The desert lends. The sea gives back.
textes.Il y a vingt-cinq ans, les bancs ont dis: Twenty-five years ago, the shoals vanished. Three months without a single sardine. I set the price at zero, opened the stores of the drying shed and shared everything out, house by house. Then a young caravan man arrived from the desert, Mbarek, and gave the whole town dates on credit. Every date was paid back to him. I've never forgotten it. Nor has he, I think.
textes.Il y a vingt-cinq ans, un gros tavernier: Twenty-five years ago, a big tavern keeper walked past my stall and said: “Your fish isn't fresh.” I threw a sardine at his head. He smelled it: it was fresh. He came back to apologise the next day, and bought the whole stall the day after. A year later, I married him. Grumbald has never criticised my fish again.
textes.Il y a écrit « piment », Vespérine ! C'e: It says “chili”, Vespérine! That's clear enough!
textes.Il y a écrit « piment ». C'est clair, no: It says “chili”. That's clear, isn't it?
textes.Il y avait encore un confetti dans ma so: There was another confetto in my soup!
There's just the right amount, my dear.
textes.Il y en a plusieurs ? … Je ne veux pas s: There are several? … I don't want to know. Mind the lemons.
textes.Il écoute toujours. Il ne comprend jamai: He's always listening. He never understands.
textes.Il était deux fois une louve… Pourquoi p: Twice upon a time there was a she-wolf… Why not a sardine.
textes.Il était deux fois… Jeune ours, j'ai mar: Twice upon a time… As a young bear, I walked three days along the coast to Tazira. Or four. There was a big circle, tea, and Ba Sidi, the storyteller of the square. And a young sailor from Carène who told stories better than he fished: Corentin. Ba Sidi told a thousand, Corentin a thousand, me just one… twice. Nobody won. It was summer. Or winter.
textes.Il était offert. Comme mon amitié. Presq: He was a gift. Like my friendship. Almost.
textes.Il était petit prince quand je l'ai trou: He was a little prince when I found him hiding behind my big barrel, dodging his lessons. I taught him to pull a fizz. He knocked the whole barrel over. The old king punished us both: a week scrubbing the cellar. We laughed all week. We still laugh about it, on the quiet.
textes.Il était une fois un boulanger tout rond: Once upon a time, there was a very round baker…
textes.Il était une fois une étoile très fatigu: Once upon a time there was a very tired star…
textes.Il était une fois, sous la cité, neuf ce: Once upon a time, beneath the city, there were nine circles dug by the ancients to lock away the cold of the earth. At the very top, the gate and its inscription. Then the Acheron, a dark river, and Charon the ferryman, with his boat and his lantern. He only takes one obol. Not two. He's very particular about his accounts.
textes.Il éternue, Basile. Des bulles. En mesur: It sneezes, Basile. Bubbles. In time, at least.
textes.Il éternue. Ce n'est pas pareil. Et lui,: It sneezes. That's not the same. And at least it doesn't cheat.
textes.Il éternue. Votre automate a bien dormi: It's sneezing. Did your automaton sleep well?
textes.Ils bougent, mon gars. Ils dorment, mais: They're moving, lad. They're asleep, but they're moving. Soon, Mélusine will ring her bell, and they'll all run off at once! The Great Turnip Alert! With my knees, I can't catch a single one anymore. Germaine can, with her net, but she keeps them to annoy Babette. When the bell rings, run to the fields and catch five for me. Just a light touch, no more! They turn golden when you catch them. Gently with my little ones.
textes.Ils dorment. Un treizième pour ma vitrin: Sleeping. A thirteenth for my window?
textes.Ils grincent en rythme, petit. C'est déj: They creak in rhythm, kid. That's something.
textes.Ils n'aiment pas la musique. Moi non plu: They don't like music. Neither do I, at midnight.
textes.Ils n'ont pas fondu. Vous avez marché do: They haven't melted. You walked gently. Good. Hold your palm open. Blow on it, slowly, like on a soup that's too hot. … There. The cold listens to you. Now, the lake. On the islet sleeps the Frost Crystal. Ask the lake to harden beneath your steps, and go and touch it.
textes.Ils ont le sourire. C'est presque pareil: They've got smiles. That's almost the same.
textes.Ils rient encore de leur dispute de la d: They're still laughing about their last quarrel.
textes.Ils ronflent, caïd. Je les entends d'ici: They snore, caïd. I can hear them from here.
textes.Ils sont déjà bien bordés. L'un d'eux so: They're already well tucked in. One of them smiles in his sleep.
They keep watch. That's their job.
textes.Ils tapent à l'huile de la Fabrique, on: Looks like they type with Works oil!
textes.Ils te reconnaissent ! Amiral te fait un: They recognize you! Admiral winks at you. Well, I think so.
textes.Ils vont très bien ! Ils sont juste… un: They're fine! They're just… a bit green.
textes.Ils éclatent de rire tous les deux. « Me: They both burst out laughing. “Thanks, referee! Here, for your trouble.”
They listen. That's already a lot.
textes.Ils écrivent avec votre machine, oui !: They write with your machine, yes!
Ilyria! Your golden ribbon, I tangled it. A little.
textes.Ilyria ? Elle tisse la lumière du matin: Ilyria? She weaves the morning light and she laughs like a brook. She doesn't know I love her. Well… I think she doesn't know. She doesn't know, does she?
textes.Ilyria est venue un jour pour une piqûre: Ilyria came in once with a golden spider bite, the only one of her life. She hid her hand, offended: “They're usually so gentle.” She'd pulled too hard on the thread, the morning after Caelan played until dawn. I said nothing. I just thought it very loudly.
textes.Ilyria m'a dit un jour que mes planches: Ilyria once told me my planks creaked in “B flat”. I spent a month planing them. They still creaked. Caelan came by, listened, and said: “It's Ilyria's thread vibrating, in B flat.” Ilyria laughed for a month. Without Caelan, I'd still be planing.
textes.Ilyria me tisse des rubans, de plus en p: Ilyria weaves me ribbons, longer and longer. I tangle them everywhere. She pretends to be cross, then she weaves me a longer one. It's our game.
textes.Ilyria tisse les voiles de mes passerell: Ilyria weaves the sails for my walkways and leaves threads everywhere. I trip over them. She says it's my planks that move. My planks do not move.
textes.Ilyria voit tout depuis sa plate-forme,: Ilyria sees everything from her platform, and she thinks I see nothing. The anonymous flowers on my counter are from her. The golden thread around the bouquets gives her away.
Ilyria sees everything from her platform, and she thinks that makes her a guard. It doesn't. And that apple wasn't luck. It's never luck.
textes.Ilyria, tu n'aurais pas vu qui a laissé: Ilyria, you wouldn't have seen who left flowers on my counter, would you?
Ilyria. Your threads, on my railing.
textes.Ilyria. Tu as encore laissé un fil sur m: Ilyria. You've left a thread on my arrow again.
textes.Ilyria… belle lumière, aujourd'hui, non: Ilyria… lovely light today, isn't it?
textes.Immense ! Plus grande que la Porte ? Plu: Enormous! Bigger than the Gate? Bigger than the obelisk?! … No, don't answer. I'd rather imagine. When you're on guard, imagination is all you've got.
textes.Immense ? Plus grande que le Grand Moaï: Immense? Bigger than the Great Moai? … BIGGER?! … I don't believe you. Do I? Oh my. Oh my oh my.
textes.Impatiente ! La graine d'Yggdrasil… je r: Impatient! The seed of Yggdrasil… I dream of seeing it sprout.
textes.Impossible de creuser ici : il faut du s: You can't dig here: it needs sand or soil.
textes.Inquiet. La montagne gronde, la nuit. Ce: Worried. The mountain rumbles at night. It's not a normal rumble.
textes.Inquiet. Ma bouillabaisse a besoin de po: Worried. My bouillabaisse needs fresh fish, and Rosalie sold me yesterday's sea bream. YESTERDAY'S!
textes.Inquiet. Mon phare n'éclaire plus aussi: Worried. My lighthouse doesn't shine as far anymore. A boat could break up on the jetty.
textes.Inquiet. Sans mon engrenage d'or, le jur: Worried. Without my golden gear, the jury will never believe me.
textes.Inquiet. Un crocodile a encore piétiné m: Worried. A crocodile trampled my wheat again. And ate my dog. No, just kidding, it ate the kennel. The dog had a close shave.
textes.Inquiète, oui. Yggdrasil n'a plus donné: Worried, yes. Yggdrasil hasn't given a seed in a hundred years. A bramble has crept into its heart, and all the plants of the tree have turned nasty. Without a seed, no new World Tree… and one day, the islands will wither. We fairies are too small for this fight. You, perhaps… If you accept, the tree will open its door to you. Climb to its crown, and bring us back the seed.
textes.Inquiète. Chaque jour, une branche de pl: Worried. Every day, one more branch turns grey. But you're helping me: I'm starting to hope again.
textes.Inquiète. Chaque nuit, le Grand Cristal: Worried. Every night the Great Crystal grows a little paler, and the dome with it.
textes.Inquiète. Une chèvre est montée trop hau: Worried. A goat climbed too high, towards the golems. She came back down. Running.
textes.Inquiète. Yggdrasil ne donne plus de gra: Worried. Yggdrasil hasn't given a seed in a hundred years. No seed, no new tree; no new tree, and the islands will wither in the end.
textes.Inquiète… Chaque matin, je salue Rê qui: Worried… Every morning, I greet Ra being reborn. For moons now, he has risen pale, as if he had slept badly. I think Apophis harasses him at night, deep in the Duat. The Pyramid of Ra, across the river, guards the path of the night; but its door is sealed, and the Sphinx opens only to those who know how to answer. Go and see it. Think before you speak. And if you go down… protect the barque of the sun.
textes.Inscrit au registre, et le thé bu jusqu': Registered in the register, and the tea drunk down to the last sparkle? Then welcome, little star. Welcome for real. (She pins a round badge on your chest: it shines and goes “beep-beep”.) Your visitor's badge. It says: “Heavyfoot, but kind.” Ecliptic chose the words. He wanted to put in forty. Here, also, a little tea for the road, and a few discs. I don't know what they're for, but they say that down below, they're very much appreciated.
Cheeky! You'll get a double helping.
textes.Inspiré ! J'ai trouvé une rime à « Ilyri: Inspired! I found a rhyme for “Ilyria”: “harmon-ia”. It's not quite there yet.
textes.Inspiré ! Le ciel est clair. De ma tour,: Inspired! The sky is clear. From my tower I can see all the way to Arcanelle when the mist lifts.
textes.Inspirée ! Avec vos pigments, ma toile c: Inspired! With your pigments, my canvas sings.
textes.Installe-toi près du feu. Je te réveille: Make yourself comfortable by the fire. I'll wake you for supper.
textes.Installez-vous. Un café ? Dites-moi, vou: Have a seat. A coffee? Tell me, how do you take it?
textes.Interroger Bruno, le glacier de la prome: Question Bruno, the ice-cream seller on the promenade
textes.Inventer ? MOI ? J'ai navigué avec Barbe: Make them up? ME? I sailed with Barbe-Sanglante! I saw the Kraken! I danced with a mermaid! … She was a bad dancer, by the way. Are you calling me a liar, cabin boy?
textes.Inventer la potion parfaite : celle qui: Invent the perfect potion: one that gives you magic, cures colds and tastes like Berthe's pumpkin pie. Three drops, and presto, you're happy. I'm working on it. It still explodes a little.
textes.Inventer le parfum que tout le monde che: To invent the flavour everyone's looking for without knowing it. You taste it and you think: “Ah, so that's what it was!” I've been searching for fifteen years. I tried tomato. No.
textes.Inventer une chose qui n'existe pas enco: To invent something that doesn't exist yet. Even something tiny. Even something useless. And hear someone say, when they see it: “I hadn't thought of that.” Just once. It would be… well, you know.
textes.Inès ! Regardez celui-là. Authentique !: Inès! Look at this one. Authentic!
textes.Inès ! Un coquillage authentique, rien q: Inès! An authentic shell, just for you!
textes.Inès est la seule personne de Port-Azur: Inès is the only person in Port-Azur who can keep a secret. She said no to me, and she was right. It's rare, someone who says no for your own good.
textes.Inès, la bijoutière, a un amoureux secre: Inès, the jeweller, has a secret admirer. I know because she buys two sea bream on Fridays.
textes.Inès, la bijoutière. Belle, discrète, et: Inès, the jeweller. Beautiful, discreet, and two sea bream every Friday. Two! She has a sweetheart, I can feel it right down to my boots. I'll find out who sooner or later.
textes.Inès, la bijoutière. Une femme de goût,: Inès, the jeweller. A woman of taste, very demanding, who thinks my shells are “authentically painted”. Which is true. But she doesn't have to say it so loudly.
textes.Inès. Bonne bijoutière. Elle voit le déf: Inès. Good jeweller. She spots a flaw in a blade from three paces. She buys obsidian from me, I forge her prongs. Hm. Nothing else.
textes.Ionie, la mécanicienne du Spatioport, rê: Ionie, the Spaceport mechanic, dreams of turning the hero's aircraft (the Albatros, built in Cliquetis) into a Star Glider: a fast little saucer that can climb very high and land on Astralys. She needs materials, a hologram chip for navigation (which flew off from Professor Quasar's laboratory) and a star chart drawn by Sextant.
textes.Ionie, vous pourriez améliorer ma machin: Ionie, could you upgrade my flying machine?
textes.Isaac Cinq-Doigts a vendu plus de fausse: Isaac Cinq-Doigts has sold more fake maps of Barbe-Sanglante than there are real islands in the archipelago. Now he has me check them. I say “fake”. Nine times out of ten. He sighs.
textes.Isaac Cinq-Doigts m'achète mes coquillag: Isaac Cinq-Doigts offers me two coins for my shells. TWO COINS! For shells from two hundred beaches! I'm not selling. He asks again every week. He's stubborn. So am I.
textes.Isaac Cinq-Doigts vend des dés trafiqués: Isaac Cinq-Doigts sells loaded dice to anyone who wants them. I buy them all back from him, every month, and throw them into the bay. He makes more. We both do good business.
textes.Isaac achète les dents de crocodile. Moi: Isaac buys crocodile teeth. I want them too. He sells sabres he didn't forge. Some of them, I forged. He didn't know. Now he knows.
Isaac. My mark, in your window.
textes.Ix Chab ! Chak est passé, ce matin ?: Ix Chab! Did Chak come by this morning?
textes.Ix Chab ! Un cacao bien mousseux, s'il t: Ix Chab! A nice frothy cacao, please?
Ix Chab! A cacao, and here are my beans.
textes.Ix Chab ! Un petit cacao, pour faire la: Ix Chab! A little cacao, to make peace?
textes.Ix Chab ! Un pot de miel, comme d'habitu: Ix Chab! A pot of honey, as usual?
textes.Ix Chab fait le meilleur cacao de Yaxché: Ix Chab makes the best cacao in Yaxché. She always recounts my beans. She says I make mistakes in my favour. It's a lunar error. It happens to the best astronomers.
textes.Ix Chab fait le meilleur cacao de l'île,: Ix Chab makes the best cacao on the island, and she's been chasing me since the business with the pots. It wasn't me. It was the ball. She serves me anyway. With a bit less froth.
textes.Ix Chab me poursuit encore pour ses pots: Ix Chab is still chasing me about her pots. It wasn't me. It was the ball.
textes.Ix Chab trouve que je vends mon miel tro: Ix Chab thinks I sell my honey too cheap. She doesn't have any honey. She says it's a matter of principle. I like her. She grumbles the way other people sing.
textes.Ix Chab vend un cacao mousseux et amer,: Ix Chab sells a frothy, bitter cacao full of chilli, which the Mayas drink the way we drink beer. She's been yelling at me since the honey business. She still buys my dates, though.
Ix Chab has been my friend forever. Her tongue is as spicy as her cacao, and her heart as sweet as… well, as honey cacao. But don't tell her I said honey.
textes.Ix Chel, la déesse de la lune, a appris: Ix Chel, the moon goddess, taught women to weave. My loom ties to my waist and to this tree. When I lean back, the threads go taut. I weave with my whole body.
textes.Ix Kanul connaît toutes les histoires de: Ix Kanul knows all the stories of Xibalba! She's a bit strict. She never laughs. Well, once, with Yum Kab. But she tells the best stories in the world.
textes.Ix Kanul est sérieuse comme le Cénote, e: Ix Kanul is as serious as the Cenote, and just as deep. I bring her balché honey for the festivals. Once, I made her laugh. The gods didn't hold it against me. I even think they laughed too.
textes.Ix Kanul est sérieuse comme une stèle, e: Ix Kanul is as serious as a stela, and almost as patient. She scolds me for my one-day errors. I remind her that her mother believed me when nobody else did. That calms her down. A little.
textes.Ix Kanul garde le temple du Serpent à Pl: Ix Kanul keeps the temple of the Feathered Serpent. She's as solemn as a stele, and I like her. Every year, at the fair of the longest day, we greet our suns together.
textes.Ix Kanul m'a raconté le Popol Vuh, et le: Ix Kanul told me the Popol Vuh, and the Twins' mosquito. So I went to the Cenote in the evening with a gourd. The mosquitoes bit me everywhere, everywhere! I counted thirty bites. And then, whoosh, I caught one! I named him Xan, like the real one. I had bumps right up to my ears. It was worth it.
textes.Ix Kanul ne rit jamais. Enfin, presque j: Ix Kanul never laughs. Well, almost never. She doesn't like it when I talk about beating the Lords of Xibalba. She says it attracts them. I talk a bit more quietly now.
textes.Ix Kanul sert le Serpent à Plumes. Elle: Ix Kanul serves the Feathered Serpent. She calls him Kukulkan. We call him Quetzalcóatl. She says he's hers. He's ours. Well… maybe he belongs to everyone. Don't tell her.
textes.Ix Kanul. Ton serpent a toujours ses plu: Ix Kanul. Does your serpent still have its feathers?
textes.Ix Sak ! Mes plumes sont toujours les pl: Ix Sak! My feathers are still the finest!
textes.Ix Sak ! Tes couleurs sont toujours auss: Ix Sak! Are your colours as loud as ever?
textes.Ix Sak ! Tes plumes ont fait un beau voy: Ix Sak! Your feathers had a lovely journey!
textes.Ix Sak ! Ton chasseur s'est décidé ?: Ix Sak! Has your hunter made up his mind?
textes.Ix Sak coud mes plumes de champion. Elle: Ix Sak sews my champion's feathers. She laughs at everything, especially me. She has a cape of a hundred and twelve red feathers, and she won't say where they come from. I know. Everybody knows.
textes.Ix Sak tisse avec tout son corps, attach: Ix Sak weaves with her whole body, tied to a tree, and her colours sing. Me, I only make white. She says my white is the most beautiful of colours. She's kind. Maybe she's right.
textes.Ix Sak tisse toutes les couleurs de la f: Ix Sak weaves all the colours of the forest. She laughs loudly. She talks for two. That works out. I don't talk.
textes.Ix Sak vend les plus belles plumes d'ara: Ix Sak sells the most beautiful macaw feathers in Yaxché. I resell them in Aztlán. She raised her prices when she found out. She learns fast. She'd make an excellent merchant. Don't tell her.
textes.Ix Sak, c'est mon amie depuis qu'on a de: Ix Sak has been my friend since we had teeth. She weaves wonders, she laughs at everything, and she's waiting for a certain hunter to make up his mind. I say nothing. I watch. Like the whole village.
textes.J'AI SOURI ! Une fois ! En 1702 ! Quand: I HAVE SMILED! Once! In 1702! When a cannon blew up next to the governor! … The governor didn't make me laugh. Neither do you.
textes.J'achète le minerai, l'obsidienne et les: I buy ore, obsidian and magma hearts. And I sell steel. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.J'achète les perles, les rubis, les écla: I buy pearls, rubies, crystal shards, scales… anything that sparkles. Dwarves pay better than tall folk. Well, I do.
textes.J'achète mon café aux caravaniers de Taz: I buy my coffee from the Tazira caravan traders, who buy it from other caravan traders. It travels more than I do.
I adore %s. Everyone here knows it.
textes.J'adore attendre le bateau. C'est déjà l: I love waiting for the boat. It's already part of the trip.
textes.J'adore cette place. Il y a de l'ombre,: I love this square. There's shade, flowers, and a signal.
I love the sound of the leak.
textes.J'adore ton carnet. Je vais m'installer: I love your journal. I'm going to move into the bag.
textes.J'ai accroché une clochette à sa chaise,: I hung a little bell on his chair, to know when he moves. Since then, he holds it with one hand so it won't ring, and he no longer turns the pages. He's been reading page forty-two of the herbarium for three months. He must know it by heart. It's a good page. Nettles.
textes.J'ai affiché le prix des cruches au mur,: I put up the price of jugs on the wall, right next to the price of rum. Broken jug: double price. Two jugs: four times the price. A pirate who breaks things: the door. Since then the pirates read the wall before they quarrel. Not all of them can read. The ones who can read for the others. It calms things down.
textes.J'ai aidé maman à pétrir. J'ai tapé, rou: I helped Mummy knead. I patted, rolled, patted again. And when the bread came out of the oven, it was shaped like a rabbit! With floppy ears. It was me! Nobody dared eat it, because it was me. Then Uncle Bondi bit off an ear. I shouted “Ouch!” as a joke.
textes.J'ai analysé l'huile à cornes de Tiburce: I analysed Tiburce's horn oil, in public, on my stall. Result: nine tenths perfume, one tenth vanity. I posted the figures. The next day, Tiburce wrote underneath: “And one hundred percent happiness”. His sales doubled. Mine didn't. I don't understand customers at all.
textes.J'ai appris chez les nains, sur la Monta: I learnt from the dwarves, on Fire Mountain. Three years hauling coal before I touched a hammer.
textes.J'ai appris deux mots à l'Amiral : « BER: I taught the Admiral two words: “BERTHA! FIRE!” He shrieked them one morning on the quay, right in the middle of the fish auction. Everyone threw themselves flat. Saïd fell off his platform, Zohra dropped a crate of sardines. Gaspard looked at me for a long, long time. Then he smiled. That's Gaspard.
textes.J'ai appris la télékinésie pour attraper: I learned telekinesis to reach the books on the top shelves without a ladder. I was afraid of ladders. I'm not afraid of ladders any more. I don't need them any more.
textes.J'ai appris le métier avec Papa : le chê: I learned the trade with Papa: the oak, the iron hoops, the fire to bend the staves. One day, I made my masterpiece. The merchant filled it with rum, and to check it didn't leak, I had a taste. Then I checked again. Papa told me not to come back until I understood the difference between checking and emptying. I went to sea to think it over.
