textes.J'ai appris le métier avec un nain de Fo: I learnt the trade from a dwarf from Forgefer who came here on a raft. He left again after a year. He said there was too much water.
textes.J'ai appris les runes pendant cent ans,: I studied runes for a hundred years, at my grandmother's, in the very alcove where I still live. Three thousand signs, and each has three meanings, depending on the light. She made me read by lava-glow alone. She used to say: “A rune read in sunlight always lies.” Since then, I hardly ever go out in the sun.
textes.J'ai appris mes signes en recopiant le m: I learned my signs by copying the same tale three hundred times. I still know it by heart. Want to hear it? … Another time, then.
textes.J'ai appris tout seul, avec les cartes d: I taught myself, with my father's maps and the sailors' stories. At sixteen, I drew my first map of Port-Azur. Very beautiful. Three hundred metres out: I'd put the lighthouse in the water. My father framed it anyway. When he died, I took over the bookshop. And I put the lighthouse back on dry land.
textes.J'ai appris à lire avant de parler. Ma m: I learned to read before I learned to talk. My mother says my first word was “shh”. I don't believe her. I think it was “page”.
textes.J'ai appris à nager avant de marcher. Ma: I learnt to swim before I could walk. My mother dived, and her mother too. They say we have gills hidden behind our ears. That's not true. I think.
textes.J'ai appris à parler aux perroquets avan: I learned to talk to parrots before I learned to talk to people. Parrots are easier: they repeat everything, they never argue.
textes.J'ai balayé 14 kilomètres aujourd'hui. J: I swept 14 kilometers today. I only found one coin. I kept it.
textes.J'ai bu mon thé, j'ai posé la tasse, et: I drank my tea, I put the cup down, and when Agathe opened her mouth, I set fire to the leaves. Pfft. No more future. She looked at the ashes, and she smiled. She'd already read it all, of course. A smile like that is worse than a future.
textes.J'ai bu une noix de coco, mon frère. C'e: I drank a coconut, my brother. Same thing, only better.
textes.J'ai bâti ma cabane avec les planches de: I built my shack from the planks of the Seagull that the sea gave back to me one by one; the last one arrived nine years ago. I have four thousand three hundred and twelve shells, every one of them named. Marley grows his bananas in my corner, Mistral set up his sound wall thanks to my rowing boat, and young Gaspard comes to learn about shacks. For a hermit, I get far too many visitors.
textes.J'ai caché du grog dans ses algues penda: I hid my hot honey brew in her seaweed for years. Last week she swapped it for herbal tea. I drank it and shouted “What a brew!” so as not to give her the satisfaction. The next day I found a real bottle in its place, with a note: “For your cough. Just one.” That's Anouk for you.
textes.J'ai caché le dessert partout : dans le: I've hidden the dessert everywhere: in the stern cannon, in the sail locker, in a bucket under Petit-Pierre. He finds everything, by the smell! Now, I hide it in the captain's cabin. He doesn't dare go in. The only problem is that the captain, she does dare eat the dessert.
textes.J'ai caché trois cents noisettes dans le: I hid three hundred hazelnuts in the Mother Oak. Three hundred! In the holes, under the bark, behind the lanterns, everywhere. And then I forgot where. I found one! There are two hundred and ninety-nine left. That way, winter won't find them either! Clever, huh? Pomme-de-Pin says it's very clever. She giggles when she says it.
textes.J'ai calculé que le Zéphyr met trois min: I calculated that the Zéphyr takes three minutes and twelve seconds to get from Cliquetis to Tazira. With the wind behind it, three minutes. With Achille in front, four.
textes.J'ai calculé que papa souffle trente et: I calculated that Dad blows thirty-one per cent of his bubbles for himself. Not for the audience. For him. I can tell: he watches them rise, he doesn't watch the people. I showed him the result on a sheet of paper. He said: “Is that a lot?” I said: “It's just the right amount.” He blew me a square bubble.
textes.J'ai chronométré la cuisson de ses miche: I timed how long her loaves bake: twenty-two minutes, on the dot. I shouted “Twenty-two minutes, Trèfle, record broken!” She asked me what the old record was. There wasn't one. Since then, that's the record, and she breaks it every morning. It makes her happy, I think. Me too.
textes.J'ai cloué une casserole au plafond de m: I nailed a saucepan to my workshop ceiling, right under his anvil, so he'd hear what I hear. He hung one under his. Now the two ring together, and Ewen calls it “the lower-deck music”. The guests at the inn think it's a bell. I can't sleep any more.
textes.J'ai collé mon oreille contre Jojo, le p: I pressed my ear against Jojo, the little one right at the bottom, and told Tchoum: “He's sad, he's lonely.” Tchoum didn't answer. That night, Jojo was up top, next to Raoul. He sounded louder, happier. Tchoum never told me it was for me. He doesn't need to.
textes.J'ai commencé docker à seize ans. Toute: I started as a docker at sixteen. Crates all day long. To pass the time, I gave them names. Number twelve is called Gertrude. My rowboat too, I called her Gertrude. But saying “Gertrude” to Odette, for her register, that I struggle with. She'd look at me. With her glasses.
I started out as a cabin boy on a three-master. Now I run the ferry, and I sleep in my own bed every night. That's true wealth.
textes.J'ai compté les marches du temple, comme: I counted the temple steps, like she did when she was little. Three hundred and sixty-four! She told me to count again. Four times! The fifth time, I got it: I'd forgotten the platform at the top! Three hundred and sixty-five, like the days of the year! The temple is a calendar! I shouted, and the macaws flew away.
textes.J'ai confié à Haldir deux cent quatre-vi: I've given Haldir two hundred and eighty letters for Ilyria. Two hundred and eighty times I've run after him to take it back before he knocked. Once, he was already on the last walkway. I jumped. Taeron had to repair the railing, and I kept the letter.
textes.J'ai connu Firmin, son père, quand Sylva: I knew Firmin, his father, when Sylvain was just a kid counting chips under the table. Firmin kept me a seat by the fire on rainy evenings. Sylvain still keeps it for me. I tell the gamblers that the ghosts of a crew play at the Tooth at night. He pretends not to like it. He leaves three dice on the table when he goes.
textes.J'ai construit la cabane de Marley au-de: I built Marley's hut above his banana trees, near Barnabé's place. He paid me in bunches: one per plank. Eighty-three planks. I ate bananas for three months. Jam, fritters, bread, grilled bananas. I can't look at one any more. I've never told him.
textes.J'ai convaincu Roux de courir une Grande: I talked Roux into running a Great Race. Just one. He set off last, whistling. At the sixth arch, no more Roux! We looked everywhere. He was asleep underneath it, a leaf on his nose. He said he was saving his strength for the end. There was no end.
textes.J'ai couru la Grande Course pendant dix: I ran the Great Race for ten years. Never won. So now I organise it. It's almost the same, and I win every time.
textes.J'ai couru le marathon du continent quar: I've run the mainland marathon forty times. I won once. The other runner got lost.
textes.J'ai cousu des patins de feutre aux geno: I sewed felt pads onto the knees of his armour, for his night rounds. The first evening, he came home without a sound and suddenly appeared in the kitchen. I got such a fright I threw my hammer at him. He caught it in mid-air. Since then, he always makes a little clang on the landing.
textes.J'ai cousu à Calcine une robe de scène a: I sewed Calcine a stage dress with ember sequins that light up when she plays fast. The first evening, she played so fast that a sequin flew off and shot straight into the mouth of Madame Hurla, who was shouting next to her. Total silence on the square, the longest in its history. I sewed the sequins back on. More firmly. A little regretfully.
textes.J'ai creusé sous toute la montagne. Il y: I've dug under the whole mountain. There are tunnels even the king doesn't know about. Neither do I, come to that. I've forgotten them.
textes.J'ai dansé avec un dauphin, là, au bout: I danced with a dolphin, right there, at the end of the beach. I did, I did. Ask Zoé.
textes.J'ai demandé au Zéphyr de m'emmener là o: I asked the Zéphyr to take me somewhere nobody had ever invented anything. Gustave, the commander's brother, dropped me off at Carène. I took three steps along the quay and saw a man drinking sparkling apple. Sparkling apple! They invented it a hundred years ago. I came back on the next flight. The commander was waiting for me with a cup of tea.
textes.J'ai demandé au Zéphyr de m'emmener quel: I asked the Zéphyr to take me somewhere nobody had ever invented anything. It dropped me at Carène. They invented cider. No luck.
textes.J'ai demandé aux élèves de dessiner leur: I asked the pupils to draw their animal in a codex. Pilli drew Tlaco… with fur. Lots of fur, everywhere, like a cloud. I asked him why. He said: “So he won't be cold in Mictlan.” I didn't correct anything. I hung the drawing on the wall. It was the most beautiful in the class.
textes.J'ai demandé un slow à Mistral. Un vrai,: I asked Mistral for a slow dance. A real one, like on my father's boat. He gave me a slow dance at a hundred and forty-five beats per minute. I told him it was a disgrace to humanity. I danced it to the very end. And I ask him again every Saturday, because somebody has to protest.
textes.J'ai demandé à Coyotl pourquoi les jarre: I asked Coyotl why Tlaloc's jars have fangs. He told me it's to guard the rain, like a dog guards the house. So Tlaco is a jar! A jar that guards the house. Now I call him “my little jar”. He likes it. I think.
textes.J'ai demandé à Fernand de m'apprendre le: I asked Fernand to teach me the bowline knot. Very useful for a collector: you tie everything down. He showed me three times. On the fourth, I tied myself to the bench on the quay, very securely. Fernand laughed so hard that two seagulls took off. It took half an hour to untie me. Splendid knot.
textes.J'ai demandé à Joe d'amener Bartholomé s: I asked Joe to bring Bartholomé on stage one evening, just to see. At the chorus of the whalers' jig, Bartholomé shrieked “Jellyfish-head!” on the third beat, exactly. The room exploded. I rewrote the whole chorus around his cry. Joe was so proud he wept into his beard. Bartholomé, for his part, demanded a seed.
textes.J'ai demandé à Jos une aiguille courbe,: I asked Jos for a curved needle, as long as a hand, for thick canvas. He asked what canvas. I said: “A canvas.” He didn't ask anything else. Three days later, the needle was on my workbench, wrapped in a rag, with a note: “For the canvas.” He'd engraved a little star on it.
textes.J'ai demandé à Matthias quel était l'end: I asked Matthias where the stillest place on the island was. He searched for three weeks, with his compasses. He drew me a meadow above the bay, behind the north point, between two oaks. I asked if it moved. He said no. I keep the map in my apron. I look at it when my aunt's back is turned.
textes.J'ai demandé à Moloka de garder deux chi: I asked Moloka to look after two pups for a day. In the evening, when I came to fetch them, they were asleep in a fish basket, one on top of the other, and Moloka had made them little collars out of fishing net. She told me: “They ate my shoe.” Her eyes were wet when she handed them back.
textes.J'ai demandé à Momo un collier avec une: I asked Momo for a necklace with a single pearl, found near the golden point. I didn't tell him why it mattered. He asked me only one question: “Blue thread or gold thread?” I said blue. I still wear it, under my scarf. He never asked again.
textes.J'ai demandé à Octave si je pouvais cons: I asked Octave if I could build a little hut in his kapok tree, below his. He said: “To spy on me with Barnabé?” I said I just wanted the view. He said: “The view costs extra.” So I build somewhere else. Lower down. With less view.
textes.J'ai demandé à Perlée de donner mon nom: I asked Perlée to give my name to a drop. She said every drop already had its own. The next day, on a flower, there was a drop resting right under a firefly. It was glowing. Perlée said ever so softly: “This one is called Lumi.” I shrieked so loudly that the drop fell off.
textes.J'ai demandé à Pépin une course qui fass: I asked Pépin for a race that goes round the whole island. He got out his stopwatch, counted on his fingers, scratched his ears, counted again. “Three weeks, Grisou.” I said: “Perfect, wolves are all about stamina!” He put his stopwatch away. He didn't say no, mind. He didn't say yes either.
textes.J'ai demandé à Sofia si on pouvait aller: I asked Sofia if we could go and see Atlantis together, just the two of us. She stopped swimming all of a sudden. She said “one day”, in a small voice. I didn't push. That evening she gave me a pearly shell, found really deep down. I think it was a serious “one day”.
textes.J'ai demandé à chaque juré d'écrire son: I asked each juror to write their favourite on a slip of paper. Basile handed me a list. Capucine, Ambroise, Prudence, Firmin… everyone. And himself, very small, in a corner. I asked him to choose just one. He looked so miserable that I withdrew the question.
textes.J'ai demandé à Écrou de négocier le prix: I asked Écrou to negotiate the price of iron ore with her family. I offered to pay in free explosions: one a month, your choice, with fireworks. She looked at me for a long time and said: “Go up and apologise. In person. On foot.” I'm getting my shoes ready. I've been getting them ready for a month.
I asked. They all said Marcel.
textes.J'ai deux enfants, des jumeaux : Bulle,: I have two children, twins: Bulle, at the Baths, and Vespérine, at the market. One laughs all the time, the other almost never. And yet I raised them the same. Well, I think so. Maybe I tickled Bulle a bit more.
textes.J'ai dicté à Ori un décret magnifique :: I dictated a magnificent decree to Ori: “By order of the king, fizz is a royal treasure.” He wrote: “Fizz is a treasure.” I asked where “royal” had gone. He said: “Ulfa would never have put it up.” He was right. The decree still hangs above the counter at the Mug.
textes.J'ai dit au jury que je ne savais pas co: I told the jury I didn't know how my machine made heart-shaped bubbles. That's not true. I know. They come when I think of Lise. I blow more gently without realising it, and the soap does the rest. Don't tell Margot, {surnom}. She already counts everything else.
I said a coffee. Not a question.
textes.J'ai dit à Pyra que j'avais brûlé Bertra: I told Pyra I'd burnt Bertrand on purpose, for fun, like you. She didn't laugh.
textes.J'ai dit à Sylvie que son mari retrouver: I told Sylvie her husband would find his camera thanks to “someone who walks a lot”. She smiled the way you smile at a pupil who's making things up. Then she said: “You saw him come down from the lookout empty-handed, didn't you?” I didn't answer. A fortune-teller doesn't answer. She smiles harder.
textes.J'ai donné des noms à mes trois mannequi: I gave names to my three dummies: Bertrand, Hubert and Germaine. Oscar has burnt Bertrand eleven times, Hubert six. Germaine, only once, but she was behind him, at the other end of the Ground. I still don't know how. Neither does he. I restuff her with fresh straw while staring at him.
textes.J'ai donné un champignon des fées à Bast: I gave Bastien a fairy mushroom, in front of everyone. He put it in his pocket, rolling his eyes. A few days later, I saw fish glowing a little, around his boat. I didn't ask him anything. He didn't tell me anything. But he doesn't say “of course” quite the same way any more.
textes.J'ai donné une semaine de cours à Fanny: I gave Fanny a week of lessons so she'd dance “smaller”, elbows tucked in. She lasted two tracks. On the third, her arm flew out, and me with it. I landed in Tchoum's arms. I never told Fanny it was my best night of the year. She's still wondering if she passed the exam.
textes.J'ai dormi trois jours. Ce n'est rien :: I slept for three days. That's nothing: last time it was three years.
textes.J'ai droit à une question par jour. Une: I'm allowed one question a day. Just one! So I write them in a notebook so I don't lose them. I've got two hundred in reserve. One day, I asked her if she'd ever been little. She thought about it for three days. Then she said: “Yes. Not for long.” I don't understand, but it's a good answer.
textes.J'ai découvert une étoile qui n'était su: I discovered a star that wasn't on any map. I named it “Cliquetis”. It blinks. Like everything here.
textes.J'ai développé ta photo. Tu as une aile: I developed your photo. You've got a blue wing instead of an arm. It's in my box of important people.
textes.J'ai embarqué il y a un an. Je voulais v: I signed on a year ago. I wanted to see the world. Mostly I've seen the deck. Up close. With a brush.
textes.J'ai emmené Félix en pédalo, pour lui mo: I took Félix out on a pedalo to show him the sea up close. Three metres. Not one more. He went green, then white, then green again, and begged me to go back. On the jetty, he lay down and said: “I'll be your navigator. From here.” I gave him a bucket, for the big voyage. He kept it.
textes.J'ai emprunté la barque de Bastien pour: I borrowed Bastien's rowing boat to go find my dolphin. I rowed far, really far. No dolphin. And I dropped both oars waving big hellos at a seagull. I swam home pushing the boat. I made him a necklace to say sorry. He says he doesn't wear it. He wears it.
textes.J'ai emprunté les six derniers bâtons lu: I borrowed Lila's last six glow sticks to juggle her a rainbow. It was magnificent for three seconds. Then one went into the sea and another into Nono's hair. Lila said nothing. She just wrote something down in her journal. I think I owe her six sticks. And an apology.
I still feel like eating flies.
textes.J'ai entendu dire que tu avais aidé {qn}: I heard you'd helped {qn}. Good. We need people like you.
textes.J'ai entendu dire que vous aviez aidé {q: I heard you'd helped {qn}. Good. We need people like you.
textes.J'ai entendu un cœur battre, au fond d'u: I heard a heart beating, at the end of a tunnel. Boom… boom… Don't tell the king.
textes.J'ai enterré un os en 2019. Je cherche e: I buried a bone in 2019. Still looking.
textes.J'ai envoyé des jarres jusqu'à Per-Hâpy,: I've sent jars all the way to Per-Hâpy, to the Egyptians. Their potter, Ptahmosé, sent me back a scarab. I think it was a compliment.
textes.J'ai essayé de compter combien de temps: I tried to count how long Lucie stays underwater. I got to a hundred, and then I skipped seventy. So I started again with pebbles: one pebble every ten seconds. When she came up, there were nineteen pebbles. She said: “You put two down at once.” It was true.
textes.J'ai essayé de le faire rire pendant un: I tried to make him laugh for a month: faces, Mange-Clous's jokes, the crab dance. Nothing. One day, I slipped on a sardine and fell into the washerwoman's laundry basket. That's when he laughed. Not a sound, but his shoulders were shaking like a bridge in a storm. Since then, I always keep a sardine in my pocket.
textes.J'ai essayé de lui poser des énigmes plu: I tried setting her easier riddles. “I'm blue, I'm up high, and there are clouds in me.” She got it! I clapped. Too loudly, apparently: she realised. Now she asks me for “real” ones. I don't dare any more.
textes.J'ai essayé de ne pas finir un livre, co: I tried not finishing a book, like you. I held out until the second-to-last page. It's very hard.
textes.J'ai essayé de photographier Titou trois: I've tried to photograph Titou three hundred and twelve times. In every one, he's a pink streak with dark glasses. One day he promised to stay still for just one second. He managed it. And then he sneezed. I sighed so hard the camera moved too. He wants all his photos: he calls them “my ghost portraits”.
textes.J'ai essayé le tambour. Les voisins ont: I tried the drum. The neighbors signed a petition. Then the trumpet: they moved away. Two are left, and I'll get them too.
textes.J'ai essayé ta potion pour voler ! Mes c: I tried your flying potion! My socks floated. I didn't. It's a start, right?
textes.J'ai essayé une fois de lui parler en fa: Once I tried to talk to her face to face, at the fountain. I'd prepared a four-page speech. I said: “Lovely day.” She said: “Very.” And I ran off. Haldir says it's the longest conversation we've had in a century.
textes.J'ai eu des jumeaux, une fille et un gar: I had twins, a girl and a boy, three minutes apart. Vespérine came first, frowning. Bulle arrived laughing. I raised them among the peppers and the sulphur roses. At five, she was labelling my jams; he was blowing bubbles in my watering can. My little root and my little soap bubble.
I had an apprentice once. Glaucos. Gifted, patient, three hundred years without one word louder than the next. Then one morning he softened some mother-of-pearl under the crystal and blew into it, like a bubble. A lamp in three minutes! I said: “That's cheating.” He packed up his tools, politely. That was a hundred years ago. The workshop's too quiet.
textes.J'ai fabriqué pour Brindille un « sac po: I built Brindille a “jet-powered mailbag”. On the first try, it caught fire above the port, and she crossed the Harbour backwards, smoking like a chimney. Every letter reached its destination! A little toasted, but people said they smelled of fresh bread. For me, it's a total success. Brindille disagrees.
textes.J'ai fabriqué pour Céleste une petite la: I made Céleste a little red battery lamp. White light dazzles an astronomer's eye for twenty minutes; red doesn't. She reads her notes without losing a single star. She wears it around her neck at night. When I look towards the observatory from my tower, I see a little red dot moving about. It reassures me.
textes.J'ai fabriqué pour Lucie un crayon de ci: I made Lucie a wax pencil and a little board, to draw underwater. Her first drawing looked like a poorly octopus. She gave it to me with a shrug. I framed it, next to the big map. It may not be a drawing of a stone, but it's the first drawing ever made underwater. It's historic.
textes.J'ai fait cent fois l'aller-retour entre: I've gone back and forth between the tables a hundred times. My feet hate me, but I'm fond of them.
textes.J'ai fait comme vous m'avez dit : je ne: I did what you told me: I only believe in the good signs. Yesterday, a rainbow over the hotel. I kept it.
textes.J'ai fait la liste des suspects. Le maît: I've made a list of suspects. The lifeguard? I asked Kevin: he laughed so hard he swallowed his whistle. The bookseller? Félix gets seasick just eating fish. The professor? He wouldn't notice a sea bream in his bed. I've got names left. I'm trying them one by one.
textes.J'ai fait les jarres de la Maison de Vie: I made the jars of the House of Life, the ones in the temple, and the big jar where Mérit brews her beer. My jars don't leak. Not every potter can say that.
textes.J'ai fait poser sur la porte de sa tour: I had a copper plaque put on the door of his tower: “Ministry of Geography”. He made me promise never to ask him for avenues again. I promised. The next day, I asked him for a trading port. He drew it for me on a separate sheet. I keep it in a separate drawer. For later.
textes.J'ai fait six ans de médecine. Un dimanc: I studied medicine for six years. One Sunday, at a second-hand bookseller's, I found an old collection of remedies from the archipelago, with dried leaves pressed between the pages. I read it that night, cover to cover, twice. Fifteen years ago I landed here with a trunk of jars that clinked with every wave. The next day I opened the herbalist's shop.
textes.J'ai fait ta blague sur la place, celle: I did your joke on the square, the one about problems. The parents laughed. A kid asked me what a problem was. Lovely day.
textes.J'ai fait toutes les fêtes de l'archipel: I went to every party in the archipelago, kid. Every one. Except my daughter's. Her birthdays, her first dance, her wedding: I was always somewhere else, dancing for strangers. Now she writes me two letters a year. Lulu is my second chance, {surnom}. I don't miss a single one of her parties any more. Not even her naps against the speakers.
I've been to every party in the archipelago. Even one at the dwarves', in a mine. The echo was incredible.
textes.J'ai fait un rêve avec un dragon !: I had a dream with a dragon!
textes.J'ai fait un tour en Zéphyr ! On voit to: I went for a ride on the Zéphyr! You can see everything from up there! I spat out of the window. It's not allowed. Don't tell.
textes.J'ai fait une potion pour qu'elle lise e: I made a potion so she'd read even faster. She didn't want it. So I drank it myself. All day, the letters danced in front of my eyes, in every book, round and round. I didn't read a single word. Lin says I read a waltz. Lin doesn't laugh often. That day, she did.
I ended up sleeping on the floor.
textes.J'ai fondé la Fabrique. Balayeurs, porte: I founded the Works. Sweepers, porters, the Bielle's butler. Simple, solid machines. And two apprentices who mattered. Héloïse, at fifteen: a clockmaker's hands, a head too full. Then Wilfried: patient, solid, a bit of a dreamer. The others, I've forgotten their names. Not those two. Hm.
textes.J'ai formé des mousses. Le premier dont: I trained cabin boys. The first one people remember is little Aristide: on the second day, he fell in the water while telling a story. Fished out with the boathook, by his belt. He became mayor, which goes to show. After that, there was Marius Vasseur. Fifteen years on my boat. The best. Him, his knots, and his father's net.
textes.J'ai glissé une banane dans le panier de: One evening I slipped a banana into Fanny's basket, so her boss could taste it. She never told me what became of it. But a week later, she let slip, all casual: “Banana croissants, still no. But a little banana bun… maybe.” Maybe! I danced till morning.
textes.J'ai grandi au-dessus de la boutique de: I grew up above my aunt's flower shop, on the mainland. At eight, I knew the names of a hundred flowers, in Latin and for real. I fell asleep to the smell of hyacinths. But I'd never seen the sea. My aunt said it looked like a field of lavender that moves. She was right. In blue.
textes.J'ai grandi chez ma grand-mère, qui avai: I grew up at my grandmother's, who had an old upright piano with a candle on each side. I played it for hours. Very well, in fact, false modesty aside. But always alone, door closed. My grandmother listened from the kitchen, pretending to shell peas. In the middle of winter.
textes.J'ai grandi chez mon oncle Bedaine, au m: I grew up at my uncle Bedaine's, surrounded by swaps: I slept between a carpet that doesn't fly and a pile of singing pebbles. When I was little, I followed the jingle of my aunt Sésame's bell everywhere, at the tip of her tail. Ding, here I came. Ding, off I went. So they called me Grelot — that means little bell. Better than Pebble.
textes.J'ai grandi dans le jardin de ma grand-m: I grew up in my grandmother's garden, on the hill, behind the olive trees. I talked to the plants all day long. I told the thyme to grow straight, the mint to leave the tomatoes alone, and they listened to me. My grandmother said I had green fingers and the gift of the gab. That was before the bougainvilleas.
textes.J'ai grandi dans les copeaux. Mon père c: I grew up among wood shavings. My father built boats, I held the nails. I was eight when he made the Mabrouka, Driss's boat. He let me drive in a nail. Just one. It went in crooked. My father said: “It'll hold.” It still holds. Forty years. Driss still shows it to me.
textes.J'ai grandi dans une famille de bergers,: I grew up in a shepherd family, in the highlands. At eight, I took the village mill apart. At nine, they sent me to Cliquetis. Everyone was happy.
textes.J'ai grandi dans une maison de gardes, p: I grew up in a family of guards, near the North Gate. My father guarded the bridge, my mother guarded the house, and I guarded my little sister Flammèche, who brought home every lost animal in the city. One day, she brought home a lava crab. I guarded it too. It was called Mister Pincer.
textes.J'ai grandi derrière son étal, à compter: I grew up behind her stall, counting coins before I could count fish. On her nine hundredth birthday, grandmother took my hands and passed me the recipe, move by move. “Not a word written down. It's handed on through the fingers.” That very evening, Abyssos came to ask if he could archive it. He's still waiting, poor thing.
textes.J'ai grandi ici. Je plonge depuis que je: I grew up here. I've been diving since I could walk. I can hold my breath for two minutes. OK, a minute and a half.
textes.J'ai grandi maison 1, au bord du grand c: I grew up in house 1, at the edge of the big field that became the airfield. With my little brother, Gustave, we flew kites there that were bigger than us. One very windy day, a kite lifted Gustave a good metre off the ground. I caught him by the belt. Ever since, he's the one who flies and I'm the one who worries. That's where it started.
textes.J'ai grandi près de la porte du nord, là: I grew up near the north gate, where the caravans come into town. I made my first guembri at eight: an iron sardine tin found behind Mustapha's grill, a stick, and three bits of string. It sounded like a cat with a cold. Omar, next door, was already drumming on every table. We had an orchestra.
textes.J'ai grandi sur le continent, chez une g: I grew up on the mainland, with a very proper grandmother who hid romance novels under the kitchen tea towels. I found every one of them. I read them in the broom cupboard, with a torch. At twelve, I knew everything about moonlit duels and kisses in the rain. About fractions, on the other hand, nothing.
textes.J'ai grandi à Port-Azur, dans la ruelle: I grew up in Port-Azur, in the little street behind the harbour, with my three brothers. At home, we talked loud, ate fast and danced in the kitchen while doing the washing-up. My mum says I broke more plates dancing than washing them. She exaggerates. A bit.
textes.J'ai grimpé jusqu'à la troisième passere: I climbed up to the third footbridge with no hands, and I fell into a blackberry bush. Aëlwen put moss all over me and asked: “How many hands?” I said: “Zero.” She sighed so hard her jars rattled.
textes.J'ai huit ans et demi. À quatre ans, je: I'm eight and a half. At four, I was already counting my dad's bubbles. My mum was called Lise, she was a glassblower. She died when I was two. I don't remember her, but I have her glass marbles in a box. I've counted them all: a hundred and twenty-seven. There's a green one with a bubble inside. It's my favourite.
textes.J'ai interrogé Bruno officiellement, ave: I questioned Bruno officially, with my notebook. He offered me a vanilla during the interrogation. He was talking about a little white shadow, over by the quay… and my ice cream was melting onto my notebook. By the end, the statement was illegible and sticky. I had to rewrite it all from memory. It still smells of vanilla. The statement.
textes.J'ai inventé la lave glacée à la brioche: I invented brioche frozen lava: one of Bobor's brioches, frozen, with fire syrup. It was horrible. Bobor told me so. I tasted it, and I said: “It's horrible.” And we ate three each, laughing, unable to stop. I've never put it on the menu. But once a year, I make one, in secret, for the two of us.
textes.J'ai inventé le crabe amoureux un matin,: I invented the lovestruck crab one morning, all alone on the beach. That evening, Yaya saw it. Two days later it was in her class, under the name “sentimental crab”. I'm demanding my name on her poster. She offered me a teeny little line at the bottom. I said: “Thank you, Miss.” She couldn't tell if that was mean. Neither could I.
textes.J'ai inventé le téléphérique, le monorai: I invented the cable car, the monorail and half the sweeper robots. The other half is Master Rivet's. We haven't spoken since the business of the singing sweeper.
textes.J'ai inventé un baume pour ses vieilles: I invented a balm for her old paws: arnica, hazelnut butter, and a bit too much pond mint. The first evening, it smelled so strong that up in the crow's nest of the Watchtower, Croc-Gris sneezed. Three times! Mother Moon said: “My guard has caught my aches.” I cut down the mint. A bit.
textes.J'ai inventé une machine qui ramasse les: I invented a machine that picks up bolts in Zigomar's workshop. It worked really well: it picked up all the bolts, then the broom, then one of Zigomar's shoes. He shouted “Eureka!” and ran after the machine to get his shoe back. He said I was a genius. And that it needed an off button.
textes.J'ai joué dans toutes les tavernes de la: I played in every tavern on the coast, then in castles. One day, a king summoned me for his wedding. I played a lament so beautiful that he wept. Then someone whispered to him that it was his old sweetheart's song. He had me thrown out, fiddle and all. The fiddle survived. My career as a court musician, much less so.
textes.J'ai joué pour un roi, une fois. Il a pl: I played for a king once. He cried. Then he threw me out because at his wedding I'd played his ex-fiancée's song. Kings have no sense of humour.
textes.J'ai joué. J'ai JOUÉ ! (Il tapote ton ép: I played. I PLAYED! (He taps your shoulder in rhythm, not even noticing.) Rouille asked me if I wanted to come back tomorrow. And the day after. And every night. Clou nodded at me. Mouette did her seagull thing. Tapage cried, he said it was the dust. And Dad... Dad was at the back of the hall. He tapped his foot. The whole concert. He says it was a cramp. (He laughs.) I'm the drummer of the Bilge Rats. And the “Son” of Lisse & Son. Both. Thank you. Here: my first musician's coins. I don't have many yet. But these, I earned by playing.
textes.J'ai laissé Margot et Léonce installer l: I let Margot and Léonce set up their robot in the cellar, between the soap barrels. It's called Bidule. It doesn't work, but it looked like its head was cold. So I made it a hat out of hardened bubble. Margot said it wasn't regulation. She's never taken it off.
textes.J'ai laissé Ortie allumer une petite fus: I let Ortie light a small rocket, just one, on the jetty. Her hand shook as she brought the match to the fuse. The rocket went up, made a little “pop”, and drew a very crooked star. Ortie looked at me with shining eyes. I said it was the most beautiful crooked star I'd ever seen. It was true.
textes.J'ai laissé ma place dans la passe à Dri: I gave my spot in the channel to Driss, my old cabin boy. Now I fish at the end of the jetty, and I catch nothing. In the evening I light the green lighthouse and salute the caid three times. In the afternoon, little Youssef comes to tell me about his whales, and a mute pirate sits beside me with his parrot. The three of us catch nothing. It's very restful.
textes.J'ai laissé tomber à l'eau le couteau de: I dropped my grandfather's knife in the water, the one with the whalebone handle. Ten fathoms deep. Lucie dived three times. The third time, she came up with the knife between her teeth, like a pirate. She said: “There was a crab on it. He didn't agree.”
textes.J'ai laissé une petite main bleue sur Ge: I left a little blue handprint on Gertrude one morning. Sort of on purpose: she looked sad. Tchoum scrubbed for an hour, sighing. The next day, the hand was still there. He'd stopped scrubbing. I think he also finds Gertrude happier that way.
textes.J'ai le mal de mer rien qu'en le regarda: I get seasick just looking at it.
textes.J'ai les pieds en compote, mais le cœur: My feet are killing me, but my heart is light.
textes.J'ai lu sa tasse, une fois, très sérieus: I read her cup once, very seriously. I saw “a long life and lots of herbal tea”. She laughed so hard she spilled the cup on my embroidered tablecloth. I looked at the stain and said: “That confirms it.” She's been bringing me her verbena ever since. The stain is still there. I don't wash it. It's a prediction.
textes.J'ai lu un jour dans le carnet de Tréphi: One day I read the name of a whale disease in Tréphine's notebook, and I was sure I had it. Anouk made me drink warm water while holding my hand, very serious, and told me I was saved. Only just. I thanked her all week. I know now it was water. It worked anyway.
My back hurts. Coal is heavy.
textes.J'ai mangé le gâteau très proprement !: I ate the cake really neatly!
textes.J'ai mangé une histoire, ma petite. Très: I ate a story, my dear. Very nourishing.
textes.J'ai marchandé une heure pour ses plumes: I haggled for an hour over her macaw feathers, and I won. At the next fair, she saw the same feathers on my stall, three times dearer. She recognised her knots. I told her: “They've travelled, they're tired, that costs extra.” She laughed. Then she tripled her prices. I pay without arguing. She made me pay for my own arguments.
textes.J'ai marché jusqu'à Tazira, une fois, en: I walked all the way to Tazira once, following the coast. Three days. Over there they drum all night long, on a square full of sand. I taught their rhythms to Pépin.
textes.J'ai mené mon enquête, figurez-vous. Je: I conducted my investigation, if you please. I went to Rose's and asked her who bought lavender from her before eight o'clock. She thought for a long time, arranging her buckets. Then she said: “Everyone, Madame Hortense.” Very well. So Marcel is part of everyone.
textes.J'ai mesuré la lueur des Pierres-Lunes t: I measured the glow of the Moonstones for a whole night, with my instruments. It rises by a tenth when Miss Lin comes to read them a story. Exactly a tenth! I went to announce it to Ysolde, very proud. She answered: “I know.” She always knows. It's rather vexing.
textes.J'ai mis des noisettes dans les caisses: I put hazelnuts in the fishery crates, to keep them cool, next to the sardines. And Caramel found them IN the sardines. Myrtille laughed so hard she fell off the bench! She said it was the best joke of the year. It wasn't a joke, it was a hiding place. But okay.
textes.J'ai mis la danse de Nono dans mon spect: I put Nono's dance in my show: “the elegant seal”. The kids love it, they clap like flippers. One day Nono came to watch, very dignified, in his beanie. He said I was forgetting the shoulder move. The next day he came back to show me. He stayed an hour. He got more applause than me.
textes.J'ai mis ma plus belle passoire, aujourd: I put on my best colander today. The Sunday one.
textes.J'ai mis un nœud papillon à mon majordom: I put a bow tie on my butler. Black silk, it gives him style. Master Rivet spotted it the very first lunchtime. He said: “Hm. A robot has no neck.” He took it off. The next day I put it back on. It's been going on for years. The butler says nothing. He's a diplomat.
textes.J'ai modifié l'itinéraire de ma ronde po: I changed the route of my rounds so as not to pass her stall. I take the alley behind, it adds four minutes. On the first day, at the corner of the alley, Rosalie was waiting for me with a bucket. She shouted: “The ice-cream stand's on the left, sergeant!” The whole quay laughed. I went back to the old route. On principle.
textes.J'ai mon grimoire, et Pip m'a tout montr: I have my spellbook, and Pip showed me everything.
textes.J'ai neuf ans ! J'habite la maison 9, av: I'm nine! I live in house 9, with my dad Wilfried and Boulon. Nine years old and house 9, I think that's on purpose. My mum is Électre, she lives at the Volta lab, with the lightning. On Wednesdays I eat at her place, in the middle of the sparks. The pasta tastes of thunder. It's so cool.
textes.J'ai noté dix-sept versions de sa légend: I've recorded seventeen versions of his legend of the flood. In one, the sea was jealous of the queen. In another, it was an octopus. In the latest, I save everyone with my quill. I archived it like the others. I reread it once. Well. Three times.
textes.J'ai offert un collier à Barnabé, trente: I gave Barnabé a necklace, thirty shells. He went all pale: in the middle there was a tiger cowrie he'd lost to a tide six years ago. Her name is Hortense. He bought her back off me for a bunch of bananas. Marley's bananas, on top of that. It all stays in the family.
textes.J'ai offert à Léonce mes premières lunet: I gave Léonce my first aviator goggles, the ones from my Academy years. They're too big: he ties them behind his head with a bit of string. He never takes them off. Wilfried says he sleeps in them. When he looks at me through them, I feel like I'm seeing myself at nine. Only cleaner.
textes.J'ai oublié de remonter la nacelle. Une: I forgot to bring the basket up. One morning. Three rabbits at the bottom. Ursule growled. Loud. Hrmm. The three rabbits took the stairs. Good for them. They got to the top all pink. Fit. I did them a favour. Ursule disagrees.
textes.J'ai oublié mon chapeau. Tant pis !: I forgot my hat. Oh well!
textes.J'ai ouvert la porte de l'Arbre-Mère !: I opened the Mother Tree's door!
textes.J'ai ouvert le Crâne Fendu avec mon défu: I opened the Crâne Fendu with my late husband, Grog. That's why they call me Mama Grog. His name was Gaspard, but he loved grog so much…
textes.J'ai ouvert le Perroquet il y a vingt an: I opened the Perroquet twenty years ago with my savings and a parrot. The parrot flew away. I kept the name.
textes.J'ai ouvert mon étal sur la place de Por: I opened my stall on the square of Port-Coutelas, because a pirate without a parrot is a sailor without a sea! I sold parrots to the whole port. They all talk, they're all polite. Almost all. Rhubarbe, the red one I sold to Captain Anne-Rose, called her an old sardine in the very first second. I thought my career was over. She paid double!
textes.J'ai parié qu'il ne toucherait pas ma ba: I bet he couldn't hit my ball in mid-flight with his blowgun. I threw it very high. Fffft. The dart stuck in the rubber. It's still there! Now it's my lucky ball. I lost the bet, but I won a one-of-a-kind ball. Balam says that's not how bets work.
textes.J'ai pas sommeil. Les apprentis n'ont ja: I'm not sleepy. Apprentices are never sleepy. That's the rule.
textes.J'ai pas vu, Momo ! Encore une fois !: I didn't see, Momo! One more time!
textes.J'ai passé trois soirées à lui tailler u: I spent three evenings carving him a set of walnut dentures, by the light of my lantern: file, try, file again. The day he put them in, he smiled in front of my mirror, for the first time in thirty years. That very evening, he lost them in Mange-Clous's stew, and Gros-Louis bit into them. I put my file away. I'm proud all the same.
textes.J'ai payé mes babouches en deux fois. La: I paid for my slippers in two goes. The first, with all my cabin-boy savings. The second, with a gold coin all green, found at the bottom of the hold, under a plank. Karim looked at it really close, he said it was the coin of a king with big feet. He kept it. I don't know where it came from. The hold's full of mysteries.
textes.J'ai peint des bulles sur le paravent, p: I painted bubbles on the screen, so it would look less sad. Thirty-eight bubbles, one for each day of sniffles since the start of the Fair. Prudence looked at it for a long time. Then she said: “You could have painted fewer.” But she left it there. And she smiled. I saw her.
textes.J'ai peint le galion pirate. Le capitain: I painted the pirate galleon. The captain wanted to buy the painting. I asked him for one gold coin. He gave me three, and asked me never to show it to anyone.
textes.J'ai peint le sac de l'appareil de Lila: I painted Lila's camera bag while she was asleep: eyes everywhere, so her camera could see even better. She screamed when she woke up. Then she laughed. Then she said the eyes were watching her. Then she kept the bag. She takes it every night. It sees a lot, now.
textes.J'ai peint trois graffitis, Pigment !: I painted three graffiti pieces, Pigment!
textes.J'ai peint un sourire sur le casque de P: I painted a smile on Dad's helmet while he was asleep. He did his whole patrol with it! All the guards saluted him with a smile, even Kraxx, who never smiles. Dad thought the city was very friendly that day. It was the Archduchess who showed him his reflection. He didn't wipe off the smile. He just hid it a little.
textes.J'ai pensé à vous ce matin, en défaisant: I thought of you this morning, untangling a ball of sheets. Do you still sleep like a hurricane?
textes.J'ai perdu mon bras droit dans une machi: I lost my right arm in a giant sewing machine. I made myself this one, out of brass. It's stronger, but it itches when it rains.
textes.J'ai photographié Nono avec l'obturateur: I photographed Nono with the shutter open for a whole track. In the photo, his orange beanie left a big curve, like a rolling wave. I gave it to him. He looked at it for a long time and said: “You see. A very elegant seal.” He keeps it folded in his beanie.
textes.J'ai piloté le Zéphyr pendant dix ans. M: I flew the Zéphyr for ten years. Now my brother flies it, and I stay on the ground worrying. It's worse.
textes.J'ai pisté jusqu'au pied du Cœur-de-Pier: I tracked all the way to the foot of Stoneheart, in the middle of the island. The tracks of all four peoples lead there. Then nothing, for a long time now. As if everyone had forgotten the way.
textes.J'ai porté le courrier de Ramure pendant: I carried Ramure's post for thirty years. Every morning I took the bag up to the treetop in the basket lift, then came down tree by tree. I delivered well. Almost always. Sometimes, with my nose in the air, I'd slip a letter into the wrong tree. Nine hundred and four lost letters in thirty years. Forgive me: I counted that too.
textes.J'ai porté sa première jarre à Per-Hâpy,: I carried his first jar to Per-Hâpy, to Ptahmose the potter. He looked at it for a long time, without a word. Then he gave me a blue scarab to take back. Coyotl turned it every which way: “Is it a compliment or an insult?” I said: “Over there, a scarab brings luck.” I'd made it up. It turns out it was true.
textes.J'ai pris la garde à trente ans. Sept ca: I took command of the guard at thirty. Seven bronze cannons, a tower, six guards, and a red lighthouse. I light it myself, every evening. That job I leave to no one. Opposite, at the end of the jetty, Si Larbi lights the green one. When both are burning, I cover my light three times. He answers. The channel is guarded. I can breathe.
textes.J'ai pris la mer à dix ans, comme mousse: I went to sea at ten, as cabin boy on a black-sailed brig, the Firebrand. The first day, I scrubbed the deck, the second day too; on the third, they let me take the helm while the captain slept. I sailed a full circle around the Harbour. The captain woke up in the same spot. He made me a sailor, for my nerve.
textes.J'ai pris la mer à dix ans, sur un brick: I went to sea at ten, on a brig with black sails. I saw the islands of the east, the ice of the north, and a whale that sang out of tune. Then the Archduchess put me in charge of the harbour. I put away my telescope. Well, almost: I take it out every morning.
I had my bath this morning, thank you.
textes.J'ai proposé à Basile un savon explosif,: I offered Basile an explosive soap, for bubble propulsion. One drop in a thimble, to try it out. Pfft! No more thimble. Pink smoke, delightful. Basile put the bottle on the highest shelf in his workshop. He thinks I don't know which one. With a stool, I'm two metres tall.
textes.J'ai proposé à Edmond d'acheter sa moust: I offered to buy Edmond's moustache, to put next to the admiral's at the manor. One gold coin per hair! He replied, standing very straight: “It is not for sale, milord. It is on duty.” Since then, whenever I cross the lobby, he checks it in the mirror. I think he's afraid I'll make off with it in passing.
textes.J'ai proposé à Inès de monter mes coquil: I suggested to Inès that she set my painted shells into necklaces. “Victor and Inès, jewels of the sea!” She took a shell, looked at it through her magnifying glass, and scratched a corner with her fingernail. The blue came off. She said: “No.” Just “no”. I repainted the shell. It's even bluer now.
textes.J'ai prédit à Félix qu'il traverserait l: I predicted Félix would cross the sea before he turned sixty. He's fifty-eight, and gets seasick just looking at a pedalo. He comes every month to remind me how much time he has left. I just smile. Two years is a long time. People have been known to change in two days.
textes.J'ai quatre cent douze ans. Je lis les r: I'm four hundred and twelve years old. I read the runes our ancestors carved into the mountain. They tell the future. Badly, often. But they tell it.
textes.J'ai racheté les onze premiers moteurs p: I bought Firmin's first eleven perpetual motion engines, all stopped. They're in the window, lined up in a neat row, under a sign I painted myself: “Almost Perpetual”. Firmin walks past every day with his head down. One morning, I caught him dusting number seven with his sleeve.
textes.J'ai raconté des histoires à sa grand-mè: I told stories to her grandmother, to her mother, and to her. She's the best of the three. She still comes to listen to me under a hood. She thinks no one recognises her. With horns like those!
textes.J'ai raconté des histoires à trois Archi: I told stories to three Archduchesses when they were little. The last one, Ignatia, still comes to listen, with a hood over her head. Her crown of horns pokes out of the hood. Everyone pretends not to recognise her.
textes.J'ai raconté à Ondine que la reine avait: I told Ondine the queen was a thousand years old. It was a joke! Well, to explain the hair. The next day, the queen smiled at me as she passed, a long smile, and said: “Good morning, Triton. I'm a little older than that.” I didn't sleep a wink for three nights.
textes.J'ai rapporté à Momo un coquillage nacré: I brought Momo a pearly shell as big as a hand, found really deep down. He made his finest necklace with it, sold it, and wanted to give me the six coins. I refused. He insisted. I threw them into the sea, for the fish. He yelled “Sofiaaa!” for quite a while. It was worth six coins.
textes.J'ai refusé de lui faire la copie. On ne: I refused to make him the copy. You don't fool a woman with a ring, even out of love. But I lent him my old jeweller's loupe, to search the sand. He gave it back three days later with a bouquet. The bouquet didn't surprise me. The sand stuck in the loupe did. I still find some.
textes.J'ai refusé la rose qu'Hugo avait acheté: I refused the rose Hugo had bought at Rose's. A beautiful red rose, cut on the slant, as it should be. The next day, I was ashamed: for a florist, refusing a flower is like a baker throwing away bread. I went to apologise. She'd put the rose in a vase, “in the meantime”. I melted.
I was looking at my cards.
textes.J'ai regardé ses étiquettes, une fois. L: I looked at her labels, once. The honey. The goat's cheese. I said: “Prices to scare a dwarf.” She said: “You know dwarves?” I said: “Yes.” Next day, the honey had gone up a penny. Just for me, I think.
textes.J'ai regardé son livre, une fois. Une pa: I looked at her book, once. A whole page of “hmphs”. With the date. And the time. Nobody's ever listened that well. I told her one was missing. The loudest one. She added it. Without laughing. Felt funny.
textes.J'ai remarqué que Marée ne mange jamais: I've noticed Marée never eats her own crackers. Never. So when I dance in front of the stall, I pretend to bite into one and pull a face, a tiny one, just for her. She laughs without a sound. We have a secret, the two of us. I don't know exactly what it is, but it's definitely a secret.
textes.J'ai remarqué que le brigadier s'arrête: I noticed the sergeant stops at Bruno's kiosk on every round. So I mentioned it. To a customer. Who mentioned it to another. Now he takes a big detour so as not to pass my stall. The other day, I saw him turn right, and I shouted: “Sergeant! The ice cream's to the left!” The whole market laughed. He didn't.
textes.J'ai remarqué une chose bizarre. Chaque: I've noticed something odd. Every time Caramel walks past my bakery, there's one mooncake missing from the display. Just one, never two. And she walks past looking the other way, tail held high, like a cat who's never tasted a cake in her life. I don't say anything. I make a note. She didn't have a tab with me. She has one now.
textes.J'ai remonté une perle grosse comme un p: I brought up a pearl as big as a pea, almost pink. Salomé examined it through her eyeglass for ten minutes, sighing, saying it had a little blemish. I took the money. That same evening, she was selling it to a caravanner as “the pearl of the Lady of the Prow”. Blemish and all. For three times the price.
textes.J'ai rencontré Brunna en creusant. J'ai: I met Brunna while digging. I broke through her kitchen floor, right under her table. She knocked me out with a pair of bellows. When I woke up, I had a bandage, a bowl of soup and a fiancée. I never found out in what order.
textes.J'ai rencontré Brunna en sortant par le: I met Brunna by coming up through her kitchen floor. She knocked me out with a pair of bellows, then she nursed me, then she married me. These days, she works the bellows at Borin's forge, and I sleep in the mine. She snores. She says she doesn't. The bats say she does.
textes.J'ai rencontré Grumbald en lui lançant u: I met Grumbald by throwing a sardine at his head. He'd said my fish wasn't fresh. The sardine certainly was: he felt it. We got married the year after. Twenty-five years. He never criticises my fish any more.
textes.J'ai rencontré Pélagos dans les jardins: I met Pélagos in the gardens: he scolded me for cutting his seaweed without permission. The next day, I came back with a scarf woven from that very seaweed. He blushed right down to his fins. On our wedding day, he wore it. It's gone a bit green since. So does he, when he's moved.
textes.J'ai rencontré Wilfried le jour où son b: I met Wilfried the day his brass arm got magnetised and stuck to my big coil. A whole hour. We had time to get to know each other. We got married, Léonce was born. When he was four, we separated, without a quarrel. Two currents that didn't connect. I live at the lab, Léonce at his father's, and on Wednesdays, he has lunch with me.
textes.J'ai rencontré Électre parce que mon bra: I met Électre because my arm, magnetised, stayed stuck to her coil for an hour. We got married. Léonce was born. Then we separated, without a quarrel. Léonce was four. So he'd have someone in the evenings, I built Boulon. Today, I have stand 4 at the Fair, a son, and a dog who chases the cats of Tazira.
textes.J'ai rendu l'Atlas des étoiles fixes au: I returned the Atlas of Fixed Stars after eleven years. With a few corrections in the margins, in ink: three stars had moved! It was a discovery! Théophraste didn't see things that way. He bought a new atlas. I put corrections in that one too, but in pencil. He says it's progress.
textes.J'ai repris l'atelier à cent ans. Depuis: I took over the workshop at a hundred. Since then, I lay the planks, Ilyria weaves the sails, and we argue about which holds up what. I've rebuilt the Fil-d'Aube walkway four times. Her sail has never budged. That's not proof. But she says it as if it were.
textes.J'ai repris la taverne il y a deux cents: I took over the tavern two hundred years ago, when my mother hung up her apron. The first night, I screwed a bung in too tight. The barrel exploded! The fizz shot up to the ceiling and stayed stuck there for a week. The customers drank with their heads tipped back. Packed house. By my beard, what a triumph!
textes.J'ai rien touché ! … Bonsoir, madame Yso: I didn't touch anything! … Good evening, Madam Ysolde.
textes.J'ai rêvé que je cueillais. C'est presqu: I dreamt I was picking. It's almost the same.
textes.J'ai salué Lentille, Rustine et Sirène !: I said hello to Lentille, Rustine and Sirène!
textes.J'ai sculpté l'enseigne du Chaudron dans: I carved the Cauldron's sign from a plank of my old boat. I made the cauldron a bit small, and the smoke… I was inspired. It takes up the whole plank. Berthe says I'd been drinking. A little. She's never wanted to change it. When the wind blows, the sign creaks. Berthe says it creaks just like me.
textes.J'ai servi trois Archiduchesses. La gran: I have served three Archduchesses. The grandmother, who talked to volcanoes. The mother, who counted the spoons. And Her Highness Ignatia, who hid in the chandelier. Each taught me something. The first, patience; the second, order. The last taught me to climb a ladder.
textes.J'ai signé un décret de réquisition pour: I signed a requisition decree for the Merciless, with red ribbon and a wax seal. Madame Calfat read it, thanked me, and slipped it under a plank of the hull. She explained that my decree was holding the side together. I didn't quite understand. But I'm proud: my decree is now part of the ship.
textes.J'ai six ans ! C'est pas un bébé, six an: I'm six! Six isn't a baby!
textes.J'ai six ans ! Et c'est moi le chef du c: I'm six! And I'm the boss of the castle!
textes.J'ai six ans ! Et des oreilles qui tombe: I'm six! And I've got floppy ears, like Mummy. You've got teeny tiny ears, that's so funny! I've got a silver bell at the Mother Oak, with a little moon on it: Ursule engraved it. And I know what all the cakes taste like. Especially the ones that aren't for me. Shh!
textes.J'ai six ans. Quand je serai grand, je s: I'm six. When I grow up, I'll be a sandcastle builder. And a kite pilot.
textes.J'ai soigné tout le monde, ici. Les brûl: I've treated everyone here. Pyra's burns, Borée's chilblains, Oscar's bumps. Especially Oscar's bumps.
textes.J'ai taillé ma flûte dans un bambou du C: I carved my flute from a bamboo from the Circle, with seven holes, the proper way. One day, I left it on a bench, and little Gland, who was teething, chewed on it all afternoon. He made an eighth hole. Since then, it plays one note more than every other flute in the world: the squirrel note. Gland wants royalties. In hazelnuts.
textes.J'ai taillé son trône de nacre en neuf a: I carved her mother-of-pearl throne in nine years. On delivery day, she sat down, closed her eyes and said: “It's shaped like a wave.” That's all. No purse, not one coin. A wave! I wrote on my invoice: “paid in compliments”. It's still outstanding.
textes.J'ai tissé un tablier à Marée, avec son: I wove Marée an apron, with her name embroidered on it. Since then, she slips a cracker into my basket every morning, without asking for anything. I don't know how to say no. Ondine makes them into boats for the canal. They float very well, actually. Whatever you do, don't tell Marée.
textes.J'ai touché une Pierre-Lune. Juste un do: I touched a Moonstone. Just one finger, to see if it was cold. Ysolde was behind me. She wasn't there before! She just said: “I know.” I ran all the way to the dormitory without stopping. My hat stayed there. She brought it back the next day. I checked it wasn't a pigeon.
textes.J'ai toujours trop de lettres et pas ass: I've always got too many letters and not enough wings! If you ever want to help me carry some, I won't say no. Grumbald at the Diable Repu, Ombreline at the Library, Gorgoth at the Arena: that's my longest round, from the port to the Upper Town, and back.
textes.J'ai toussé pendant des siècles. Aëlwen: I coughed for centuries. Aëlwen gave me a hundred herbal teas, and I poured every other one into my fern's pot. The day she found out, the fern was two metres tall. Aëlwen looked at the fern, then at me. And she charged me for a consultation. For the fern.
textes.J'ai transcrit l'air sur un petit cylind: I transcribed the tune onto a little music-box cylinder. Céleste asked me to come and play it at the observatory, under the stars, facing Stoneheart. We wound up the box and waited. Nothing happened. But since then she hums it while she observes. Out of tune. With a lot of heart.
textes.J'ai transformé le grand soufflet de Mam: I turned Mum's big bellows into a fire-bubble machine. There were flaming bubbles right up to the forge ceiling! Mum shouted so loud the bells rang. Then she put the bellows back together. But I saw her smile as she watched the last bubble float away. I saw it.
textes.J'ai trouvé son appareil sur le banc du: I found his camera on the bench at the lookout, one evening. I didn't touch it. A camera left lying there might be a camera waiting for someone. Its owner was bound to come back. He didn't. Apparently he'd have preferred me to take it down to the hotel. I didn't know it was his! Well… I had an inkling.
textes.J'ai trouvé un appareil photo près du ba: I found a camera near the bench, last night. No, I didn't take it. I left it where it was. Someone may be looking for it.
textes.J'ai trouvé un bâton. Il est à toi. Non,: I found a stick. It's yours. No, mine. No, yours.
textes.J'ai trouvé une plume de héron doré !: I found a golden heron feather!
textes.J'ai un carnet rien que pour les histoir: I've got a notebook just for Corentin's stories, the thirteenth. I note, I compare. Over twenty evenings, his whale has had between two and seven trees on its back. But it was always north-west of the point. Always. So I drew a little whale on the map, to the north-west. With a question mark, of course.
textes.J'ai un frère jumeau, Bulle, le maître d: I have a twin brother, Bulle, the master of the Baths. I was born three minutes before him. He laughs all the time, I don't. Our mother says we split our personalities at birth: he took all the laughter, I took everything else.
textes.J'ai un petit carnet noir. Sur chaque li: I have a little black notebook. On each line, a date, a place, and the mayor's sentence: “Before the end of the year!” Fourteen lines. I showed it to him once, on Gisèle's terrace. He said it was a very pretty notebook. Then he promised to give me another one.
textes.J'ai un pot d'onguent à l'arnica avec so: I have a pot of arnica ointment with his name written on it: “Oscar”. I refill it every week. Once, it stayed full for eight days. Oscar came to show me, all proud. On the way out, he bumped into my gate. I opened the pot. We both laughed.
textes.J'ai un sixième sens pour les trésors. L: I have a sixth sense for treasure. The seventh is for fish.
textes.J'ai un tiroir à son nom, dans mon burea: I have a drawer with his name on it, in my office. Three hundred and twelve patents. The umbrella, the sock, the spoon… I read them all in the evening, and every time I hope to find the first one that doesn't exist. Last month, the drawer wouldn't close any more. I had a second one made, just underneath. It's empty. For now.
textes.J'ai une fille, Ortie, et une petite sœu: I have a daughter, Ortie, and a little sister, Flammèche, who raises hellhound puppies. Between the two, I don't know who gets up to more mischief. The puppies, at least, sit when you say “sit”.
textes.J'ai une question. Tu préfères les chiff: I have a question. Do you prefer numbers or letters? Think carefully. I'm writing it down.
textes.J'ai une sœur jumelle, Vespérine, l'apot: I have a twin sister, Vespérine, the apothecary. She was born three minutes before me, and she never lets me forget it. She says in those three minutes she had time to take all the family's seriousness. I took the rest. The best part!
textes.J'ai une vieille botte, ça vous intéress: I have an old boot, are you interested?
I have a real curiosity for you.
textes.J'ai vendu la boulangerie à Margaux il y: I sold the bakery to Margaux twelve years ago, and usually I still deliver her bread in the morning, to Paulo's, to Gisèle's and to the hotel. But right now I'm limping: a sprain, a misstep while pointing. After that, it's pitch number one, mine. And Nina calling me “Grandpa Raymond”. Me, a grandpa! The lost jack, on the other hand, is Marcel's fault.
textes.J'ai vendu un sabre de Jos à un caravani: I sold one of Jos's sabres to a caravan trader, telling him it had belonged to the terrible Captain Floc'h. The trader paid a fortune for it. Jos found out, he came to the stall in his apron, bright red, shouting. I gave him half. He left a lot less red. Captain Floc'h has been in great demand ever since.
textes.J'ai voulu accrocher une clochette au bo: I wanted to hang a little bell at the end of the fourth-floor corridor, so the ghost would trip over it. Monsieur Edmond took it down the next morning: “Hotel regulations.” I hung it back up. It vanished again. That ghost has accomplices, I'm telling you.
textes.J'ai voulu acheter le plumeau de Pauline: I wanted to buy Pauline's feather duster. A duster that has touched so many wonders is a wonder itself, surely! One gold coin. She refused: “And what would I do your room with, milord?” Unanswerable logic. So I sat her in the armchair, with her duster, and drew the two of them. The duster came out better.
textes.J'ai voulu aider Cardamome en faisant jo: I tried to help Cardamome by making her crystal bells play by themselves. They played all night, faster and faster. Incredible music! It took Cardamome a month to retune them. She says it was noise. I say it was ahead of its time.
textes.J'ai voulu apprendre le pas du crabe à T: I tried to teach Tchoum the crab step. He tried, very serious, without stopping nodding. A crab that says yes to everything! I laughed so hard I fell in the sand. He held out his hand to help me up and said: “Again?” It was adorable.
I tried to teach Mochi to climb. I showed her: paw there, tail there, hop! She got up onto the first branch. And she sat on it all afternoon, eating a cake, saying it was very high. It was the first branch. Rabbits aren't made for climbing.
textes.J'ai voulu attirer un dictionnaire par t: I tried to summon a dictionary by telekinesis, just one. The whole B shelf came. I was buried under bestiaries, botany and biographies. Master Filandre dug me out one book at a time, without a word, putting them back in order. It took two hours. I didn't move.
textes.J'ai voulu faire des bulles avec une pot: I tried to make bubbles with one of my sister's sap potions. The potion made bubbles. So did I: for two days, every time I spoke, a bubble came out of my mouth. I opened the Baths anyway, and talked to the customers in bubbles. They loved it. Vespérine filled three notebooks. She smiled twice.
textes.J'ai voulu instaurer un impôt sur le com: I tried to introduce a tax on trade, to fund the new pontoon. Monsieur Cinq-Doigts took out his scales and billed me a tax on the scales. I did the sums: the city owed him money. I abolished the tax and made a speech on free trade. One of my best. He applauded.
textes.J'ai voulu leur faire donner une leçon c: I wanted them to give a joint lesson, fire and frost, to show the apprentices steam. There was so much steam that the courtyard vanished for an hour. When it came back, Pyra and Borée were each at one end, and Oscar was nowhere to be found. He'd gone to bed: he thought it was night.
textes.J'ai voulu lui présenter un jeune scribe: I wanted to introduce her to a young scribe from Amenemhat's school. Very well brought up. He only spoke in proverbs: “Patience is a thread of gold”, “The river does not flow back to its source”… At the fifth proverb, Tiyi stood up: “The loom does not wait.” Now that was a Tiyi proverb. He left.
textes.J'ai voulu monter voir les deux maisons,: I wanted to climb up and see the two houses at the top of the Great Temple. Halfway, Cuauhtli was coming down. I thought he was going to shout. He sat down on a step, looking only at the sky, and told me about Nanahuatzin, the little god covered in spots who became the sun. I went back down to listen better. It was a trap. A good trap.
textes.J'ai voulu poser ma boule sur l'autel du: I wanted to set my ball on the altar of the Circle, just for a minute, to see what would happen: the future on top of the past. Ysolde said no before I'd finished my sentence. The ball had warned me. I went anyway: I wanted to see her face when she said no. It was worth the trip.
textes.J'ai voulu présenter Xan aux abeilles de: I wanted to introduce Xan to Yum Kab's bees, so they'd become friends. I opened the gourd in front of the hive. All the bees came out and flew around Xan! And Xan went back into the gourd all by himself. He was shy. Or maybe the bees told him something.
textes.J'ai voulu retrouver sa recette en goûta: I tried to work out her recipe by tasting one cracker a day and noting everything. After forty days, I had a whole scroll and a historic stomach ache. She read over my shoulder and said: “Wrong. All wrong.” Then she gave me a cracker, free. I noted that too.
textes.J'ai voulu verbaliser Bernard pour « cou: I tried to fine Bernard for “running on the quay”. He jogged on the spot while I looked for the article, then pointed out that the regulations ban bicycles, not runners. I reread the regulations. He was right. I wrote on a sign: “Runners: walking pace.” He overtakes it every morning, saluting me.
textes.J'ai voulu écrire un livre sur les coqui: I wanted to write a book about seashells. But I just couldn't come out of my shell.
textes.J'ai voulu être archer, mais je racontai: I wanted to be an archer, but I told the deer stories instead of aiming at them. Old Ithilwen, the storyteller in those days, took me by the ear: “Since your talking makes the game run away, come and make the children stay.” I learned three thousand stories with her. I've forgotten two. I can't remember which.
textes.J'ai vu ! Cinq braseros, et pas un sourc: I saw! Five braziers, and not an eyebrow singed! You're more gifted than Oscar. Well, it's not hard. Here, some coins, and a piece of advice: you never throw fire at someone you love. Except Borée. Borée doesn't count.
I've seen the Door of the Four Seals.
I saw your line. It's moving.
textes.J'ai vu un jour sur l'étal de Salomé un: One day I saw a red canvas bag on Salomé's stall, with a label: “Fragment of the Léviathan's great sail”. It was an offcut from my awning on the square. I nearly knocked over the stall. She told me: “But Nolwenn, it's almost true! All the canvas in Carène comes from the Léviathan!” The worst part is she was right.
textes.J'ai vu un tapis rouge. J'ai dit : « Com: I saw a red carpet. I said: “How much?” He named a price. I said: “Paid.” He went white as a sheet. He said it wasn't possible. He was ill for three days, apparently. I sleep on that carpet. In my cabin. It's thick. Hm. Good price.
textes.J'ai vu une petite lumière danser au-des: I saw a little light dancing above a ring of white mushrooms in the forest! Faelar says it's a firefly spirit. I wasn't allowed to follow it.
textes.J'ai vu une étoile tomber dans la grande: I saw a star fall into the big pond, forty nights ago. It never came back out. Since then, Brume has seen round tracks. I'm doing calculations.
textes.J'ai vu. Elle pousse comme tes galeries: I saw. It grows like your tunnels: any which way.
textes.J'ai écrit une chanson sur elle : « La B: I wrote a song about her: “The Ballad of the Town Crier”. There's a part where the violin imitates her voice. It's very lifelike. The children sing it in the streets, shouting. She pretends to be offended. But the other day, I heard her humming it at the market. Off-key. But loud.
textes.J'ai écrit une chanson sur son pain : «: I wrote a song about her bread: “O golden crust, O crumb of moon…”. Sylwen listened without stopping her kneading, then she said “pretty”. In two hundred years, I'd only ever heard her say “pretty” to a brioche. That night I slept like a king.
textes.J'ai écrit « LABORATOIRE INTERDIT » en g: I wrote “LABORATORY: KEEP OUT” in big letters on the cellar door. Then, underneath, smaller: “except Mirabelle”. She underlined her name twice, in pink. Since then, before going down, she knocks three times on the ceiling, so I know there's going to be noise. She's a professional.
textes.J'ai épousé Ardoise, un chat gris, pêche: I married Ardoise, a grey cat, a pond fisherman. The finest float in Ramure. Three years ago, he went off to fish at sea, on the blue boats of Tazira. He asked me to come. I stayed. He writes every month, and Plumette brings me the letters. I read them at the end of the jetty. Seven times each. Like my stretches.
textes.J'ai épousé Driss. Le jour du mariage, i: I married Driss. On our wedding day, he said “yes”. And nothing else all day. My mother thought he was ill. That was thirty years ago. He still doesn't talk. But every time he comes back from fishing, he puts a shell on my chair, the prettiest one in the net. Without a word. Thirty years of silences, and of shells.
textes.J'ai épousé Joseph, mon Jojo, pêcheur de: I married Joseph, my Jojo, a tuna fisherman. He goes out to sea six months a year and comes back with a beard down to his belly and stories about whales. We had Kevin, who was diving before he could walk, and Clara, fifteen now, who does pirouettes on the stall crates. A dancer, that's what she wants to be. A dancer! In a family of fishmongers, can you imagine?
textes.J'ai épousé Margaret, la plus jolie pers: I married Margaret, the loveliest person in the county, and the only one who laughed at my hats. She collected shells: two hundred and seven, sorted by colour. And every morning, she went down to our village jetty to feed the seagulls. She gave them names. The biggest one was called the Admiral. Splendid times, my dear. Splendid.
textes.J'ai épousé Marguerite, qui pêchait mieu: I married Marguerite, who fished better than me and sang more off-key than a seagull. On the boat, she sang, I laughed, and the sardines fled. She'd tell me: “Fernand, one day the sea will keep you.” I'd answer: “It hasn't got room.” We laughed like that for years, bless us.
textes.J'ai épousé Marius Vasseur, le petit frè: I married Marius Vasseur, Anselme's little brother. He was a deckhand on Fernand's boat. He laughed at everything, I laughed at nothing: between us, it made a decent average. Twenty years ago, when the old harbour master retired, Marius pushed me to apply. “You already know everything, Odette. All you're missing is the cap.”
textes.J'ai épousé Sennefer, un batelier qui tr: I married Sennefer, a boatman who carried stones on the river. He laughed loudly and sang out of tune. Nebet was born the year of the great flood. When she was two, Sennefer left for the Field of Reeds, where the righteous go, to Osiris. I wove his shroud myself. The finest linen of my life. I don't often talk about it.
textes.J'ai étudié la médecine sur le continent: I studied medicine on the mainland. Then I discovered the plants of the archipelago. The elves know more than all my professors put together.
textes.J'ai étudié la médecine trois ans à Mont: I studied medicine for three years in Montpellier! And the saw is a MEDICAL instrument! … OK, I also use it to cut wood. But I wash it in between. Sometimes.

I studied medicine for three years in Montpellier. I was the best at bandages and the worst at exams: I knew everything, but I talked too much, and I ended every answer with an anecdote. In the third year, I answered a question about the heart with a story about a whale. The professor advised me to join the navy. I took the advice.
textes.J'ai été cuisinier au palais d'un gouver: I was a cook at a governor's palace, on a southern island. He loved complicated dishes: stuffed peacocks, jellies shaped like castles. One evening, I served a roast under a silver cloche so shiny that when he lifted it, he saw himself inside, among the potatoes. He ran off. So did I: I'd set the tablecloth on fire.
textes.J'ai été garde, avant. Trente ans sur le: I used to be a guard. Thirty years on the ramparts. One day my sword broke on a gargoyle. I said to myself: we need better blades. So I started selling them. The gargoyles are still there. But my blades don't break any more.
textes.J'ai été percepteur des impôts du roi, s: I was the king's tax collector, on a ship that made the rounds of the islands. I went ashore with my register, my stamp and my finest smile, and I came back with chests. People didn't much like me. I didn't understand why: I was so polite. I even had a welcome speech, in three parts, with a conclusion.
textes.J'ai été professeur de gymnastique trent: I was a PE teacher for thirty-five years. “Hop hop hop” comes from there: the pupils dawdled, I pushed them on. On the side, I ran forty marathons on the mainland. Only one win, the twenty-third: the other runner followed a brass band down the wrong road. I've still got the medal. I take it out on rainy days.
textes.J'ai été rat de cale, rat de quai, maint: I've been a ship's rat, a dock rat, and now I'm a shoulder rat.
textes.J'aime l'aube : tout le monde dort encor: I love dawn: everyone's still asleep, except the birds.
textes.J'aime quand le ciel devient orange. On: I love it when the sky turns orange. It looks like it's blushing.
textes.J'allume les réverbères en rythme, penda: I light the street lamps in rhythm while Calcine plays. I borrow poems from the library through the window; Ombreline leaves a candle. I leave poems in Lumina's boxes, and one on Gorgoth's bench. At dawn, I meet Mother Brasille, who gives me mint to help me sleep. They're beautiful nights.
textes.J'appelle ces trois jours ma « visite d': I call those three days my “state visit aboard the Morue Enragée”. In my speeches, I talk about the treaty of friendship we signed. In reality, we signed an IOU for his honey. But a treaty is a treaty. I had it framed at the residence, under my portrait. It's very well written. By me.
textes.J'apporterai des nouvelles. Je veux dire: I'll bring news. I mean… cakes.
textes.J'apprends les nœuds à Pépin sur le quai: I teach Pépin knots on the quay: the bowline, the clove hitch, the figure-eight. He listens, he nods, he tries, and he always ties a shoelace knot. One day, he tied a rowing boat to the quay with a shoelace knot. It held all night. I've never understood how. I didn't tell him.
textes.J'apprends à danser en observant Kira. P: I'm learning to dance by watching Kira. Progress: four percent.
textes.J'archive tout : les marées, les naissan: I archive everything: the tides, the births, the whale songs… And Coralin's mistakes. Those are the thickest scrolls.
textes.J'arrive ! Je vais pleurer comme un gran: Coming! I'm going to cry like a grown-up!
textes.J'arrive, Grumbald ! Prépare trois coupe: On my way, Grumbald! Get three bowls ready!
textes.J'arrive, Joe ! Bartholomé est de bonne: Coming, Joe! Is Bartholomé in a good mood?
textes.J'arrose, je taille, je parle aux fleurs: I water, I prune, I talk to the flowers.
textes.J'attends le bateau. Il est en retard. O: I'm waiting for the boat. It's late. Or maybe I'm early. Or there's no boat.
textes.J'attends le gros poisson. Ça fait trois: I'm waiting for the big fish. It's been three years.
I wait for someone to open.
I wait for it to pass.
textes.J'attends quelqu'un. Ou rien. Je ne sais: I'm waiting for someone. Or nothing. I've forgotten.
textes.J'attends toujours qu'elle ait fini de l: I always wait till she's finished reading, in case there's a reply. Every other time, there is, and it smells of grilled fish. One day, Caramel gave me a skewer with her reply: “So it flies faster.” I ate it on the way back up the stairs. The letter went off very fast.
