textes.J'attends. Je suis très doué pour attend: I'm waiting. I'm very good at waiting.
textes.J'avais attrapé un poisson, tout petit,: I'd caught a fish, a tiny one, and I took it to Mange-Clous. He got out the frying pan! I told him it was going to grow. He put the pan away, and we went to release it together at the jetty. Now, when I fish, I say hello to it. It's always the same one, I'm sure: it has a little spot on its fin.
textes.J'avais cent ans quand la baleine m'a ré: I was a hundred when the whale answered me for the first time. I was singing the high tide on the north bridge, and the whole sea hummed above the dome: a note deeper than the world. Since then, I sing to her whenever she passes. I don't know what I'm saying to her. Nor does she, I think. That's fine just as it is.
textes.J'avais dix ans quand ma mère a embauché: I was ten when my mother took on a tall lad of seventeen, still pale from his dunking the day before: Aristide. On the first day, he broke twelve cups. I counted them. At the thirteenth, I showed him how to hold a tray. He became mayor. I took over my mother's café. To each his own counter.
textes.J'avais dix-huit ans quand la jeune Mère: I was eighteen when young Mother Moon arrived with her clan. The rabbits were trembling, the wolves were growling, and she suggested a race round the Mother Oak. The first Great Race! That evening, I told her my very first story. She fell asleep in the middle, smiling. That night, I decided to be a storyteller: so folk fall asleep happy.
textes.J'avais dix-huit ans quand un nain de Fo: I was eighteen when a dwarf from Forgefer washed up on the beach, on a raft made of barrels. Master Hrolf. He stayed a year, grumbling about the water, the salt and the seagulls. He taught me to listen to iron: “It sings when it's ready, lad.” One morning, he left again on his raft. He said there was too much water. He was right.
textes.J'avais dix-neuf ans, et j'étais reine d: I was nineteen, and I'd been queen for a single spring. That night, the sea reared up higher than the tower. I laid my hands on the Great Crystal and asked it for one thing only: “Keep them.” By morning, we were under the sea, in a bubble of air. And my hair was as white as foam.
textes.J'avais dix-neuf ans. Je cherchais une a: I was nineteen. I was looking for a lost anchor under the hull, in the sand. I dug with my hands, and I touched stone. Carved. Covered in signs, circles and lines. Too old to be from the castaways. The Léviathan didn't run aground on rocks. It ran aground on something somebody had built.
textes.J'avais dix-neuf ans. Ma mère priait au: I was nineteen. My mother was praying at the valley temple. During the morning hymn, the sun began to darken from one side, like a flatbread someone bites into. The village cried: “Apophis is eating Rê!” I kept on singing, all alone on the terrace, my voice trembling. And the sun came back, piece by piece. Since that day, people listen to me.
textes.J'avais douze ans, au jour de l'équinoxe: I was twelve, on the day of the equinox. My mother sat me at the foot of the great staircase. The sun sank, and the shadow of the tiers drew a serpent of light on the balustrade, slowly coming down towards the stone head, right at the bottom. My mother whispered: “Kukulkan is coming to see us. One day, you'll be the one to welcome him.”
textes.J'avais douze ans, j'ai couru pieds nus: I was twelve, I ran barefoot to the Tower to show her my first light, at three in the morning. She opened the door in her nightcap. She looked at my light very seriously and said: “Brighter than the stars.” It wasn't true. She knew it, I knew it. She made tea anyway.
textes.J'avais douze ans, j'étais l'élève de Sé: I was twelve, I was Séraphine's pupil, and I couldn't get anything right. One night, on the dormitory roof, looking at the stars, I opened my hand and a little light came out. Very little. I ran barefoot to the Tower to wake Séraphine, at three in the morning. She told me it shone brighter than the stars. I pretended to believe her.
textes.J'avais eu l'idée des « galettes royales: I'd had the idea of “royal crackers”, with the queen's portrait on them, twice the price. She said no. So I made “almost royal” ones, with a lady who looks like her, but with a different nose. She walked past the stall, looked, and bought one. She paid for it. The only time ever.
textes.J'avais huit ans. Elle m'a fait un nœud: I was eight. She tied me a knot in a scrap of net twine, a knot nobody else knows how to tie, and said: “For when you're grown up.” I still have it, on my key ring. It's nearly sixty years old, and it's never budged. Like her.
textes.J'avais huit ans. Un soir de brume épais: I was eight. One evening of thick mist, I found she-wolf tracks at the edge of the path, and I followed them. For a long time. Slow, steady steps, one paw dragging a little. They led me to a door. Mère-Lune opened it before I knocked. She looked at my muddy paws. She said: “Come in, little one. You start tonight.”
textes.J'avais mis sur l'étal un petit sac de t: I'd put a little red canvas bag on the stall: “Fragment of the Léviathan's mainsail”. Nolwenn nearly knocked everything over. I explained that all the canvas in Carène comes from the Léviathan, so it was almost true. She repeated “almost” in a terrible voice. I changed the label: “Almost a fragment”. It sells even better.
textes.J'avais ouvert le chenil à côté des Jard: I'd opened the kennel next to the Ash Gardens. Bad idea: my pups dug up Mother Brasille's flowerbeds to bury bones in them. She came to see me with her broom and asked me, very nicely, to move. I set up in the Artisans' Quarter. She still comes for the bones they bury at her place. She keeps them.
I was afraid you'd say that.
textes.J'avais pris un coup de soleil sur le cr: I'd got sunburnt on my scalp. Gaspard said nothing. Next day he put this beanie on my head. Green. Knitted in Port-Azur. He said: “For the sun.” I said: “Yeah.” We didn't say anything else. We said everything.
textes.J'avais quatorze ans l'hiver où la mer n: I was fourteen the winter the sea gave nothing. Not one herring, not one sardine. My grandfather took the logbook of the Léviathan, which had always slept at our house, and we walked all the way to Tazira. He sold it to a young storyteller for six sacks of flour. We ate all winter. Me, I cried the whole way home.
textes.J'avais quatorze ans quand je suis monté: I was fourteen when I signed on as cabin boy on the Fair Star, a three-master that sailed far to the south. On board was a sailor from Port-Azur, Jules. He taught me knots, the stars, and not to be sick into the wind. Every night on watch, he talked to me about Hortense. I knew his fiancée by heart before I'd ever seen her.
textes.J'avais quinze ans, j'étais mousse, j'av: I was fifteen, a cabin girl, and I hadn't eaten for three days. While the women were selling their sand to the pirates, a girl of twenty put a bowl of harira in my hands, without a word. Hot, thick, with lemon. The best meal of my life. I've had it in twenty ports since. None comes close to that one.
textes.J'avais quinze ans. Le téléphérique d'Hé: I was fifteen. Héloïse's cable car was brand new, and it stopped in the middle of the cable, with the mayor of Port-Azur inside. After an hour, I'd had enough of hearing him declaim. I climbed along the cable with a twelve-millimetre spanner and released the brake. Héloïse offered me a place at the Academy. I chose the harbour. It smells better.
textes.J'avais seize ans quand le vieux Gaudenc: I was sixteen when old Gaudence handed his staff to Séraphine. My mother sang the song that wakes the stones. I held the lantern. The stones lit up one after another, like eyes opening. I didn't blink. I didn't want to miss anything. It's the only time I've heard it sung.
I was sixteen, I thought I was a poet. I recited her a poem about seagulls, with rhymes in “-ette” everywhere. She listened to the end and said: “It's bad.” She was right. The worst of it is she still knows it by heart. She recites it to me when I get too proud. I become very modest very quickly.
textes.J'avais seize ans. La corde de la nacell: I was sixteen. The basket's rope snapped halfway up, with Hulotte and the mailbag inside! Bourru held the whole thing with his bare hands. That very evening, Granny Faîne and I braided the sixth rope. All night, no sleep, fingers on fire. By morning, it was ready. It was my first real job. It still holds! Obviously.
textes.J'avais sept ans quand j'ai collé l'orei: I was seven when I pressed my ear against a pillar in the Great Hall. It was whispering. Everyone laughed. My grandmother Ragna, the rune-reader in those days, didn't laugh. She took me by the hand and said: “At last.” I only understood that word three hundred years later.
textes.J'avais trente ans quand les jambes de m: I was thirty when my mother's legs said no. The first night I ran the tavern on my own, I burned three crêpes and broke a mug. And then Corentin told stories, Fañch sang off-key, somebody spilled sparkling apple on the Admiral of the day, and everybody laughed. I knew I was home.
textes.J'avais un chapeau de paille. Un beau. L: I had a straw hat. A nice one. My uncle's camel ate it. In one go! I cried a bit, and my uncle laughed. Really laughed, with his mouth open. Mum says nobody's ever seen her brother laugh like that. So the hat was worth it.
textes.J'avais une jarre fêlée. Il l'a vendue c: I had a cracked jar. He sold it as “the jar where Tlaloc keeps the thunder”, because it rumbled when you tapped it. Three times its price! I wanted my share. He gave it to me. So I cracked other jars on purpose. They didn't rumble. You can't order a crack. Tochtli says you can't order thunder either.
textes.J'avais vingt ans quand Garance est part: I was twenty when Garance left with the mist: that's how we say it here, when someone dies. She left me the shop, halfway up the Mother Oak: three hundred jars, and not a single label. Not one! She said a nose doesn't need to read. I spent a whole winter sniffing everything. I still haven't put labels on. Garance was right.
textes.J'avais vingt ans quand la fièvre est mo: I was twenty when the fever rose from the harbour basin, one foggy winter. Tréphine fell ill first. After that, there was only me. Seventeen patients in a month, herbal teas on every stove in Carène. Fifteen got back on their feet. Some evenings I still count the other two.
textes.J'avais vingt ans, c'était la Saint-Jean: I was twenty, it was Midsummer. Fañch got down on his knees in the sand in front of everyone. I panicked, I laughed, and I said: “The day a fish tells you yes.” A silly thing. He's never forgotten it. Since then, he's been asking the mackerel. And I listen at the window to what they answer.
textes.J'avais vingt ans, j'étais apprenti chez: I was twenty, an apprentice to old Si Moussa, the souk's lantern-maker. One day a young coppersmith turned up with a hideous lantern, heavy as a cooking pot. It was Abdellah. Si Moussa told me: “Pierce it, so we can have a laugh.” I pierced it all night. By morning, nobody was laughing. For forty years he's shaped and I've pierced. And for forty years we've argued.
textes.J'avais vingt ans. Le septième toit est: I was twenty. The seventh roof went off all at once, and I found myself sitting in the soot, without eyebrows, more frightened than I'd ever been. I decided to keep the idea of exploding, take away the danger and keep the colours. The professor gave me the barrel of his old engine as a farewell present. It became my first confetti cannon.
textes.J'avais vingt ans. Un capitaine est entr: I was twenty. A captain sailed into port disguised as a salt merchant, with a red beard and a thief's smile. With the women of the port, we sold him sacks of sand for salt, at a high price. They left poorer. And that night, a little cabin girl, skinny as a herring, was hungry. I gave her a bowl of harira. It was Lou.
textes.J'avais vingt-quatre ans quand ma mère m: I was twenty-four when my mother gave me Katell's copper compass, saying: “The helm doesn't turn any more, but we hold it.” The next day, I was admiral of a town of two hundred souls, of a ship that doesn't float and forty cannons that don't fire. I learned fast. I had no choice.
textes.J'avais écrit son nom au tableau, à la c: I'd written his name on the board in chalk, a bit hastily: “Bel-Humeur”. He saw it. He rubbed it out with his sleeve and rewrote his name in enormous letters that take up half the board. Gros-Louis and the Silent One are tiny underneath. I didn't dare correct it. Even the chalk was scared.
textes.J'avais écrit « Recommandé par l'infirme: I'd written “Recommended by the infirmary” next to the desert balm, because Anouk had treated a customer who'd used some. That's a kind of recommendation, isn't it? Next morning, the chalk had been wiped off, and in its place, in Anouk's hand: “No.” She has very pretty handwriting, Anouk.
textes.J'avais écrit « pas pour Pip » sur l'éti: I wrote “not for Pip” on the label, on purpose. OK, the “not” was a bit small: there wasn't much room left. He drank it anyway. He had green ears for a whole day! The whole class called him Pip-the-Frog. He says it's my fault. I say you have to read to the end.
I'm bringing jam for my aunt.
textes.J'empruntais tout le temps la longue-vue: I was always borrowing the Captain's telescope to look at the sea from the post office roof. One morning, he gave me his old cabin-boy telescope, all dented. He said: “That way, you'll leave me mine.” I wear it round my neck, always. It saw the ash storm, apparently.
textes.J'en ai cent autres qui attendent !: I've got a hundred more waiting!
I counted a hundred last night, Silas. A hundred!
textes.J'en ai dix. Sous l'eau, ça en fait troi: I've got ten. Underwater, that makes three.
textes.J'en ai six ! « Vague 1 », « Vague 2 »…: I've got six! “Vague 1”, “Vague 2”… up to “Vague 6”. Handy, isn't it? Oh, and the pedalo is called “Gérard”. Like the tourist. He doesn't know.
I'll take good care of it.
I always find one. It's my job.
textes.J'en vends, des plumes d'ara. Quatre suf: I sell them, macaw feathers. Four would be enough for a Dark House, I'd say. For a festival, you need a lot more.
textes.J'enseigne ici depuis quarante ans. J'ai: I've been teaching here for forty years. I've seen hundreds of apprentices come and go. Some became mages, others pastry cooks. Both work wonders.
textes.J'espère que les grenouilles dorment, à: I hope the frogs are asleep at this hour.
textes.J'essaie toujours de lui faire dire ce q: I'm always trying to get her to tell me what's in the letters. “This one smells of salt and sardines: is it for Caramel?” Plumette answers: “A postmistress says nothing.” I can smell I'm right. But I'll never know more. An owl keeps her beak shut.
textes.J'essaie. « La cascade d'encre pleure sa: I'm trying. “The waterfall of ink weeps without colour…” I'm missing the rhyme. Most of all I'm missing the orange: pot number seven. I saw it! It got stuck at the very top, on the Lip, at the water's edge, where the waterfall hesitates before falling. Me, I get dizzy. From heights, and from rhymes. Would you climb up? The mountain path goes right above it.
textes.J'habite sur le continent, dans une mais: I live on the mainland, in a house with stairs. Mummy's a teacher, but not at my school. Daddy counts numbers all day, even on Sundays, in his head. I'm six. And I've got a bear, he's called Captain. He's only got one eye, because he went to war. Well, the washing machine.
textes.J'habite une maison ronde avec un toit v: I live in a round house with a green roof, by the canal. Mum weaves seaweed, Dad looks after the gardens, and I look after the window! It's the best window in the dome: you can see the turtles go by. I've counted forty-three. Well, maybe it was the same one, forty-three times.
I live next to my dad's boatyard. It smells of wood and glue, and in the morning it goes tap-tap-tap. My mum, Itto, she comes from the desert. She says I was born the day the whole fleet came home full. “That's lucky,” she says. I say the sardines came to watch me be born. Same thing.
textes.J'invente mes pas sous la plate-forme d': I make up my steps beneath Ilyria's platform. The sound of her loom gives me the rhythm: clack, swish, clack. One day she stopped weaving to watch me, and I fell over, because there was no more music. She laughed. Now she weaves more slowly when I dance.
I'd go and take a closer look.
textes.J'ouvre à huit heures, je déjeune sur un: I open at eight, have lunch on a bench in the square, and in the evening I pick my herbs in the hotel garden. I look after Lefort's back, keep an eye on Bernard's heart, comfort Léa with Rose's lavender. And every morning, I taste a berry from the jungle. For science. Somebody's got to do it, as they say round here.
textes.J'y compte bien, mon ami. J'y compte bie: I'm counting on it, my friend. I'm counting on it.
I'm listening. The pond says nothing.
textes.J'écris des poèmes. Ils ne sont pas très: I write poems. They're not very good. The last one rhymed “puppy” with “puppy”. Nox says that's a perfect rhyme. I think he's being kind.
textes.J'écris des poèmes. Sur la nuit, les fla: I write poems. About the night, flames, people sleeping. I leave them in Lumina's lantern boxes. She doesn't know it's me. … She knows? Oh no.
textes.J'écris mon nom avec un pot, une jambe e: I write my name with a pot, a leg and a loaf. Amenemhat says the pot is a basket, and the leg is no use. But I need a leg: I'm always running! So I'm keeping it. He said “almost right”. And then he smiled behind his hand. I saw him!
textes.J'écris ses lettres pour l'ours de Ramur: I write his letters to the bear in Ramure, because his hand shakes. He says things like “it was raining”. I write “it was raining herrings”. The bear wrote back that it was the best letter of his life. Corentin pretended to be cross, and then he gave me a coin. A real one.
textes.J'écris tout ce que dit Grommelot dans m: I write everything Grommelot says in my big book. Everything. One day he came to look. He leafed through a page full of “hmphs”, each with the date and time beside it. He stood in front of it for a long while. Then he said: “One's missing. The loudest.” I added it.
textes.J'écris à quelqu'un chaque semaine. Il h: I write to someone every week. He lives ten metres from here. I don't dare talk to him. Silly, huh?
textes.J'étais apprenti chez la vieille Garance: I was apprenticed to old Garance, the herbalist of the Herb Shop, along with Pivoine. She could tell a hundred herbs apart; I could tell every tart in Ramure, and I mixed up sage and nettle. Nettle stings, stranger. Garance ended up sending me out to pick outdoors. I never really came back in. Fox technique: wander off far enough that people come looking for you.
textes.J'étais assise dans sa tente, le bras te: I was sitting in her tent, arm held out, very calm. A fly landed on my nose. I sneezed. Coralie says I'm the one who moved. I say it was the fly. The knife became a spoon, with a pretty handle. The whole port laughed for a week. Gros-Louis asked me if I threw forks too.
textes.J'étais au cirque. Lanceuse de couteaux,: I was in the circus. Knife thrower, with a partner on a spinning wheel. One day he asked for a raise in the middle of the show. I changed jobs. So did he. He became careful.
textes.J'étais au sol, les jumelles sur le Zéph: I was on the ground, binoculars on the Zéphyr, as always. And I see a little curly head poke out of the gondola window, take aim, and spit. On the island. From a hundred and sixty metres. When it landed, I was waiting for him at the foot of the gangway. I said: “Nice spit.” He went bright red. He polished the whole railing the next day.
textes.J'étais bûcheron, avant. Un jour, j'ai c: I was a woodcutter, before. One day, I cut down a tree that fell on the king's boat. They offered me prison or the navy. I chose the pirates.
I was a surgeon in the royal navy. One day I treated a pirate. Then two. Then the navy threw me out. The pirates kept me.
textes.J'étais cuisinier au palais d'un gouvern: I used to be cook in a governor's palace. One day I served the governor instead of the roast. … No, just kidding. But he ran off anyway.
textes.J'étais en train de creuser sous une vie: I was digging under an old root, happy as anything, when Grommelot burst out with a broom. He was shouting: “Thief! Root thief!” I'd only taken one seed! A teeny one! He chased me all the way to the garden. I was laughing so hard I was flying sideways.
textes.J'étais facteur. Trente ans à marcher. M: I was a postman. Thirty years of walking. Now I stay put and throw boules. That's balance.
textes.J'étais fille de pêcheur, sur une île du: I was a fisherman's daughter, on an island in the north. One day, the Moray sailed by. I jumped aboard. That was ten years ago.
textes.J'étais jeune quand j'ai connu sa grand-: I was young when I met his grandmother, Lalla Mennana. She wove without speaking, for days on end. I offered her my best djinn tale. In exchange, she told me the story of the walking dune, in ten words, without looking up from the loom. I still repeat them to myself, without being sure I understand them. Those curious about the seal, these days, I send to her grandson.
I was young, a gunner on her ship. One morning, she gave me an order, and I answered back with some cheek. Magnificent cheek. She grabbed me by the collar and threw me overboard, without even putting down her pipe. I swam back, climbed the ladder and went back to my cannon. She kept me on till the end of the month. I think she liked me.
textes.J'étais le dernier de sept enfants. Aux: I was the last of seven children. At marbles, at jacks, at racing, I lost. By twelve, I had lost three hundred games of chess in a row against my big brother. Three hundred. I counted them. That evening, I swore that one day I would build someone who never lost. I did it. My brother never agreed to play against him.
textes.J'étais mousse, il y a… longtemps. Puis: I was a cabin boy, oh… a long time ago. Then a fisherman, then a carpenter, then nothing at all. Now I tell stories. Best job there is: you never get wet.
textes.J'étais percepteur d'impôts. Un jour, de: I was a tax collector. One day, pirates boarded my ship. They took all the money, then found me so talkative they dropped me off here. I decided that since nobody was governing, it would be me.
textes.J'étais petit prince, je fuyais mes leço: I was a little prince, dodging my lessons behind the big barrel at the Blazing Mug. Ulfa found me. Instead of marching me back to the throne, she taught me to pull a fizz. I knocked the barrel over. My father punished us both: a week scrubbing the cellar. We laughed all week.
textes.J'étais pisteuse, autrefois, comme Brume: I was a tracker once, like Brume. I followed the moon's trail to the edge of the world. She told me: go home, Ramure needs you. So I came home.
textes.J'étais tonnelier. Je faisais des tonnea: I was a cooper. I made barrels. Then I tasted what was inside. Ever since, I empty them.
textes.J'étais venu à la Dent du Requin inspect: I had come to the Shark's Tooth to inspect the games of chance, on behalf of the city. Monsieur Malaterre invited me to play. I had no coins: I wagered my person for a week. He rolled three sixes. I rolled a two, a one and a four. I spent three days on the Cod polishing boots. Then he returned me to the city. He claims I ate too much.
textes.J'étais étudiant à l'Académie, et très d: I was a student at the Academy, and very gifted! At blowing things up, mostly. One Tuesday, the chemistry room went boom. The whole room. As my old master used to say: “Augustin, out!” He had soot right into his ears. So I built my workshop far to the west, on the edge of the cliffs, far from everyone. First roof. It lasted three weeks.
textes.JE RÊVE… pardon. Je rêve qu'un jour, l'A: I DREAM… sorry. I dream that one day, the Arena will be so full that people climb onto the roofs to see Gorgoth. And that the whole city shouts his name with me. He'd blush right to the tips of his horns.
textes.JUSTE UN CHAT ?! Elle t'a entendu ! Rega: JUST A CAT?! She heard you! Look, she's turning her back on you! It's the worst insult among sacred cats!
textes.Jack, Mamie Tournesol dit que le festiva: Jack, Granny Sunflower says the festival is coming back!
textes.Jack, voilà les cordes de Galet et la to: Jack, here are Galet's ropes and Lune's canvas!
textes.Jacquot ? Il renifle mes épices comme un: Jacquot? He sniffs my spices like a hunting dog, he buys cumin by the kilo, and he looks at me like I'm a tajine. Ridiculous. A little touching. Mostly ridiculous.
textes.Jacquot achète tout le poisson dont pers: Jacquot buys all the fish nobody wants, at sneezing prices. A customer like that only comes along once in a crier's life. Thankfully.
textes.Jacquot est gentil comme un gros chien,: Jacquot is as sweet as a big dog, and he cooks like a dog too. He thinks I taught him the tagine. I didn't have the heart to tell him the truth.
textes.Jacquot me raconte souvent comment il a: Jacquot often tells me how he lost his two fingers. A shark, a lobster, a soup… I made a list, carved with a knife under the galley table. There's already nine versions. And he's only missing two fingers! I showed him the list. He said: “Ho ho! There's one missing, the best one.” And he told me the tenth.
textes.Jacquot, c'est mon chef. Sa cuisine, ell: Jacquot's my boss. His cooking is… let's say brave. But he always saves me the best bit, and he tells stories. He's the nicest one on the whole Murène.
textes.Jacquot, le cuisinier des pirates, est m: Jacquot, the pirates' cook, is my pupil. I gave him my recipe. A fake one. He follows it to the letter, so seriously… I'm a bad teacher. And a man who laughs too much.
textes.Jaguar, Vent, Pluie de Feu, Eau, puis Mo: Jaguar, Wind, Fire-rain, Water, then Movement. The codex of the Legend of the Suns is there, on the lectern: look, the dots give the order.
textes.Jaguar, Vent, Pluie de feu, Eau ! Tam ta: Jaguar, Wind, Rain of fire, Water! Boom boom!
textes.Jaguar, Vent, Pluie de feu, Eau : les qu: Jaguar, Wind, Rain of Fire, Water: the four suns, in order! The Sun Stone lights up with gold, and beneath it, the door of the Fifth Sun sinks into the floor.
textes.Jamais ! C'est ça, les pirates !: Never! That's what pirates are like!
textes.Jamais ! Et toi, tu as une nouvelle pair: Never! And you, got a new pair hidden away, Karim?
textes.Jamais ! Par les cendres de la Rade, tu: Never! By the ashes of the Harbour, you've got sea legs! I can tell by the way you walk on the quays: you don't look at your feet. One day, I'll take you out to sea.
textes.Jamais ! Tu as de la chance, ou tu cours: Never! You're lucky, or you run fast. Here, you're in no danger: my bees have no sting. They have opinions, that's all.
textes.Jamais ! Tu l'as dit ! Je vais le répéte: Never! You said it! I'm going to tell everyone! Even the crystal. That way, it's official.
textes.Jamais ? Ah… Dommage. Moi non plus, enfi: Never? Oh… Too bad. Me neither, well, almost. But it doesn't matter, we'll look together. I've already got a shovel. Well, a spoon.
textes.Jamais ? Alors la prochaine est pour toi: Never? Then the next one's for you. Promise. I'll call you, I'll shout, and this time you'll look in the right place.
textes.Jamais ? Alors nous sommes deux. Ne vous: Never? Then there are two of us. Don't worry: you can live very well without singing in front of people. You sing in your head. A head echoes a lot.
textes.Jamais ? Alors tu as peut-être la main v: Never? Then maybe you have a green thumb without knowing it! Come to the chinampas, I'll give you a seed. Just one. We'll see.
textes.Jamais ? Alors tu n'as jamais vraiment m: Never? Then you've never really eaten! Come back tonight, I'll let you taste my jungle chilli stew. Weird, but good. Mostly good.
textes.Jamais ? Assieds-toi. Une promesse, ça n: Never? Sit down. A promise isn't something you throw overboard like an insolent gunner. You keep it. Even when it's heavy. Especially when it's heavy. Got it? I won't say it twice.
textes.Jamais ? Bienvenue au club ! Moi, dix co: Never? Welcome to the club! Me: ten races, zero cups, and I'm the happiest rabbit in Ramure. Winning is overrated. Well… a bit overrated.
textes.Jamais ? C'est reposant, quelqu'un comme: Never? That's restful, someone like you. You can put a watch down next to you and find it in one piece. That doesn't happen to me often.
textes.Jamais ? Ce n'est pas grave ! Moi, je pe: Never? That doesn't matter! I lose too. Sometimes. Fine, often, when I bet against Balam. Come and play, we'll win together.
textes.Jamais ? Essaie ce soir. Commence par un: Never? Try tonight. Start with one corner of the sky. You'll see: after a hundred, you can't think of anything else. It's very restful. Or very annoying.
textes.Jamais ? Ha ! Alors on est deux. Ça me r: Never? Ha! Then that makes two of us. That's a relief. I was starting to think it was avoiding me on purpose.
textes.Jamais ? Hm. Je te promets une chose : u: Never? Hm. I promise you one thing: one evening, without you knowing it, your foot will move. Just one. I'll play a note, and it will move. You'll see.
textes.Jamais ? Hm. Tu as tort. Mais je ne vais: Never? Hm. You're wrong. But I won't force you. Me, I'd have given a lot for one last ball.
textes.Jamais ? Hmm. Vous ne savez pas ce que v: Never? Hmm. You don't know what you're missing. Or else you're lying, like everyone. I won't say a word. I'm a vault. A vault on holiday.
textes.Jamais ? Hou… Monte à la cime un soir. A: Never? Hoo… Climb to the treetop one evening. Lie down. Start with one. The first is the easiest. After that it gets tricky.
textes.Jamais ? Il n'est jamais trop tard ! Je: Never? It's never too late! I'll keep a little explosion aside for you. A tiny one. A beginner's explosion, eyebrows guaranteed.
textes.Jamais ? Inch'Allah, ça va changer. Je t: Never? Inch'Allah, that'll change. I promise you: before the festival is over, you'll sing. A verse. A word. A “ho”. But you'll sing.
textes.Jamais ? Ma doue, mais c'est merveilleux: Never? Good heavens, how marvellous! My favourite customer! … No, I'm joking. Do haggle a little, though. Otherwise I'll feel bad.
textes.Jamais ? Mais comment tu te souviens des: Never? But then how do you remember places? Here, a postcard. Just one. It weighs nothing. Two pennies. Well, a penny and a half.
textes.Jamais ? Même pas un tout petit peu ? …: Never? Not even a teeny bit? … You're lucky. Or else you keep them all inside. That's not good, you know. It makes storms.
textes.Jamais ? Oh là… Ça, ça m'inquiète. Même: Never? Oh dear… Now that worries me. Even parrots sleep, you know. Sit down, I'll make you a herbal tea. Yes, I have some. For serious cases.
textes.Jamais ? Oh, mon pauvre… Viens au bout d: Never? Oh, you poor thing… Come to the end of the quay in the morning, with me. You mustn't make any noise and you mustn't blink. That's the secret.
textes.Jamais ? Oh, quel dommage ! Ce soir, ava: Never? Oh, what a shame! Tonight, before you sleep, think of a feather. Just one. It'll do the rest, you'll see.
textes.Jamais ? Oh… Tu passes à côté de la mer: Never? Oh… You're missing out on the sea talking to you! Here, take this one. No, not that one. This one. All right, I'm lending it to you.
textes.Jamais ? Oh… alors viens au Cercle ce so: Never? Oh… then come to the Circle tonight. Not to dance: just to watch. Nobody watches for long before their feet start on their own.
textes.Jamais ? Parfait. Exactement ce que j'at: Never? Perfect. Exactly what I've been waiting for these twenty-two years. I'd note you down in my notebook, but it only has one column: “Suspects”.
textes.Jamais ? Personne ne t'a jamais joué la: Never? Nobody's ever played you the right music, that's all. Come tonight. You won't dance. But your foot will tap the beat. Just like Asmodin's.
textes.Jamais ? Peuchère. Assieds-toi. Le lapin: Never? Dear oh dear. Sit down. The rabbit comes out of the hole, goes round the tree, goes back down the hole. There. Now you know. Well, almost.
textes.Jamais ? Peuchère. C'est ce que disent t: Never? Bless you. That's what everyone says before I end up treating them. Stick out your tongue… No, I'm joking. Well, half joking.
textes.Jamais ? Soit tu fais très attention, so: Never? Either you're very careful, or you've never tried anything. We'll soon find out which. Come closer to the brazier.
textes.Jamais ? T'as de la chance ! Ou alors, t: Never? Lucky you! Or maybe you've just never gone far enough. The Ash Wood is really big, you know. There are places where even Gérard doesn't go.
textes.Jamais ? Tant mieux. Vraiment. Garde ça: Never? Good. Really. Keep it that way, {surnom}. A goodbye you never said weighs more than a cannon.
textes.Jamais ? Tiens. Un rabot. Tu pousses, do: Never? Here. A plane. You push, gently, with the grain. … There. You've built a wood shaving. It's a start.
textes.Jamais ? Tu devrais. Une barque à qui on: Never? You should. A boat that gets talked to leaks less, everybody knows that. Ask Tobias. No, don't ask him, he'll sigh.
textes.Jamais ? Tu dis les choses vraies avec t: Never? You say true things with your true face? How brave. You'll have to teach me. I can't do it.
textes.Jamais ? Vous êtes sage. Comme moi, avan: Never? You're wise. Like me, before. Keep your feet on the ground: someone has to hold the spare umbrella.
textes.Jamais ? Waouh. Ça, c'est du courage. Ou: Never? Wow. Now that's brave. Or else you've never seen real dark. The dark under the clouds is very dark, you know.
textes.Jamais ? … Bien. Très bien. Vous pourrez: Never? … Good. Very good. You may borrow the little blue book, on the left-hand shelf. Nobody ever borrows it. It will be delighted.
textes.Jamais ? … Comme ça, ils ne s'arrêtent j: Never? … That way, they never stop. I hadn't thought of that. It's maybe wiser than me.
textes.Jamais ? … Hm. Moi non plus, avant. Dans: Never? … Hm. Me neither, before. In the marsh, watch the water. Not the sky. The water.
textes.Jamais ? … Oh. C'est triste. Bon, ce n'e: Never? … Oh. That's sad. Well, never mind: we can do one together! A little one. With just a bit of smoke. I know where there's a stovepipe.
textes.Jamais ? … Tiens. (Il te met un marteau: Never? … Here. (He puts a hammer in your hand.) Heavy, eh? Strike. Not on your fingers. There. Now you know.
textes.Jamais ?! Devant mon étal ? Tu veux ma m: Never?! In front of my stall? Are you trying to kill me? Fine. Come on a Friday. My tajine has converted pirates, it'll convert you too.
textes.Jamais ?! Mais c'est un drame ! Vous ne: Never?! But that's a tragedy! You don't know what you're missing. The sound of an envelope being opened… Right. I'll convert you. I have time, I'm a postwoman.
textes.Jamais ?! Même pas une petite ? Même pas: Never?! Not even a little bit? Not even a frog? … You're fibbing. The leaves said so. Oh, all right, I believe you. A bit.
textes.Jamais ?! Pas de chiens savants, pas d'a: Never?! No performing dogs, no acrobats, no knife-thrower? You poor thing. Right. I'll give you a demonstration. Not on you, don't worry.
textes.Jamais ?! Vous êtes de ceux qui laissent: Never?! You're one of those who leave the sheets in a ball and the towel on the floor… I know your type, I get twelve a day. Oh well. Nobody's perfect.
textes.Jamais assez ! Comme Roux. Ordonnance :: Never enough! Just like Roux. Prescription: fewer adventures, more naps. Under a tree, if you like, but only if you pick herbs at the same time. He can't manage that.
textes.Jamais assez ! Mais j'ai un plan !: Never enough! But I have a plan!
textes.Jamais de monnaie ? Alors c'est vous, le: Never any change? So you're one of those people who pay for a jar of honey with a big coin. I hate you a little. I'll serve you anyway.
textes.Jamais essayé ? Alors tiens, prends cett: Never tried? Then here, take this sulphur rose seed. Plant it wherever you like, water it with hot water, and sing it something. You'll see.
textes.Jamais essayé ? Mais qu'est-ce qu'on app: Never tried? What are they teaching young people these days! An adventurer without a bowline is a boat without a mooring. Tomorrow, lesson. Six o'clock.
textes.Jamais fait attention ? Dix mille coups: Never paid attention? Ten thousand blows per tray, and you never paid attention. Tac. Next time you come by, you listen. That's the rule of the workshop.
textes.Jamais plus, monsieur Malaterre ! La cit: Never again, Monsieur Malaterre! The city needs me!
textes.Jamais pris la mer ? Mais tu es venu jus: Never been to sea? But you came all the way here! … Flying? Swimming? Ha! You'll tell me all about it. Around here, we go to sea for any old reason. Even to go fishing for a dream.
textes.Jamais rien ? Ici, ça ne durera pas. Je: Never anything? Here, that won't last. I give you three weeks on Balafre. I'll set a compress aside for you, just in case.
textes.Jamais, Ix Sak. Elle dort dans un coffre: Never, Ix Sak. It sleeps in a chest.
textes.Jamais, capitaine ! Bartholomé dit « têt: Never, captain! Bartholomé says “jellyfish-head”, that's all.
Never. That's what makes it funny.
textes.Jamais. Hm. Courageux, ou imprudent. Je: Never. Hm. Brave, or reckless. I haven't decided yet. In the meantime, I'll look behind me for you.
Never. I sleep like a log.
textes.Jamais. Tu as du miel dans les poches, j: Never. You've got honey in your pockets, I can smell it.
textes.Jamais. … Bon, une. Coco. Petite. Gratui: Never. … Fine, one. Coconut. Small. Free?
textes.Jambe-de-Bois est au tapis. Quand il se: Jambe-de-Bois is down. When he's back on his feet, talk to him: he owes you a purse.
textes.Je bavarde, je bois un jus. La belle vie: I'm chatting, sipping a juice. The good life.
textes.Je bouge pas ! Mais fais vite, j'ai une: I'm not moving! But be quick, I've got crab cramp!
textes.Je brasse la bière de Forgefer depuis de: I've been brewing Forgefer fizz for two hundred years. Dark, frothy, and it warms your ears.
textes.Je bricole. Il y a toujours quelque chos: I'm tinkering. There's always something to fix.
textes.Je cache mon sablier derrière la pile d': I hide my hourglass behind the pile of encyclopedias, to time her. Four hundred pages in an afternoon. I recounted three times. For a few weeks now, she's been reading more slowly. Much more slowly. I'm worried. Perhaps her eyes hurt. I offered her a lamp.
I'd turn someone into a frog.
textes.Je chante pour mes poissons. Pas pour le: I sing for my fish. Not for grumblers.
textes.Je chasse à l'aube. Je vends au marché d: I hunt at dawn. I sell at the maize market. I hunt again in the afternoon. The meat, I share with those who need it. Yum Kab first. In the evening, I go to the Venus platform. Ix Sak dances. Me too. She says I do the jaguar. Kinich follows me into the jungle, with his dog. The game hears them too.
I look it up in a book.
textes.Je cherche depuis des années le trente-t: For years I've been hunting for the thirty-third ingredient of her ras el hanout. I sent her a list of fifty guesses on the Zéphyr. She answered “no” to every one, in pencil. Except the forty-seventh, “patience”, where she wrote: “Almost.” I haven't slept since.
textes.Je cherche toujours ta potion pour plus: I'm still looking for your potion to not be scared. So far, I've found something that gives you hiccups. It helps you forget, a bit.
textes.Je cherche toujours votre thé. Les carav: I'm still looking for your tea. The Tazira caravaners offered me mint. I said no. For you, I said no.
textes.Je cherche une énergie nouvelle, propre,: I'm looking for a new energy, clean, powerful. I've found it eleven times. It has exploded eleven times.
textes.Je collectionne les coquillages. Chacun: I collect shells. Each one has a story. This one, for instance, saw a whale sneeze.
textes.Je collectionne les coquillages. Un de c: I collect shells. One from every beach I've landed on. I've got two hundred and twelve. My crew calls me Coquille — Shell. Before, they called me Periwinkle. I protested.
textes.Je collectionne les graines. J'en ai de: I collect seeds. I have some from every island: jungle, elves, even a cactus seed from the dwarves. I'm only missing the most beautiful one.
textes.Je commence : « Plus j'ai de gardiens… »: I start: “The more guardians I have…” Pimprenelle shouts: “A frog!” I try another: “I run without legs…” “A frog!” By the tenth, I changed the answer on purpose so it would be a frog. She said: “Too easy.” I didn't speak to her for the rest of the day.
I trade with the southern caravanners. They're thieves. I adore them.
textes.Je compose tout moi-même. Celui-là s'app: I make all the tracks myself. This one's called “Low Tide”. A hundred and forty-five beats per minute, like your heart when you run along the beach.
textes.Je comprends. Moi non plus, je ne me cro: I understand. I wouldn't believe me either. So come and look, one clear night. Not to believe me. To see.
textes.Je compte les versions de la fête de Non: I count the versions of Nono's party in the dwarves' mine. I'm up to seventeen. In number seven there was a dragon. In twelve, the dwarf king danced on a table. In the latest, Nono played the drum on an anvil. I prefer twelve. So does he, I think. His eyes sparkle when he tells it.
textes.Je compte sur Tibo pour me donner la poi: I'm counting on Tibo to get me the captain's shoe size. He says he can't get near the boots: the captain sleeps in them. Still, he brought me a charcoal drawing of a boot print on the wet deck. Size forty-six. A captain's foot. I've already started the black pair.
textes.Je connais l'adresse de tout le monde. C: I know everybody's address. It's very handy and a little bit scary.
textes.Je connais la chanson qui réveille les p: I know the song that wakes the stones. I will sing it once, for the next archmage. That will be the day Séraphine lays down her staff. Every night, I rehearse it in silence so as not to forget it, {surnom}. And every night, I wish I never have to sing it. Both are true. The stones know.
textes.Je connais la fin. Elle fait récurer le: I know the ending. She makes the storyteller scrub the deck.
textes.Je connais les Neuf Cercles mieux que pe: I know the Nine Circles better than anyone. I've never been down there, of course. But I've listened to everyone who spoke of them: the old keepers, the founders' books, and even a former ferryman. Charon and his obol, Cerberus and his three heads, the bridges of Malebolge… It's all in my stories. The truth, and a little bit of make-believe, for flavour.
textes.Je connais tous les courants autour de l: I know every current around the island. The mist, the reefs, the whirlpools. Wizards can fly. Me, I know how to get back to port.
textes.Je connais tous les trous de l'île. Tous: I know every hole on the island. Every one. Even the tiny ones.
textes.Je connais toutes les cachettes du villa: I know all the hiding places in the village! There's one under the fountain. But it's a secret. Oops.
textes.Je construis des cabanes dans les arbres: I build tree houses. Barnabé taught me. OK, Octave says his are better.
textes.Je cours ! Trois tours tous les jours. E: I'm running! Three laps every day. Well, two and a half.
textes.Je crache tout près, maintenant ! Regard: I spit really close now! Look!
textes.Je crois qu'une page de ma partition est: I think one page of my sheet music went towards the beach, another towards the square, and the last one… somewhere along the quay, to the east.
textes.Je crois que j'ai attrapé la fièvre des: I think I've caught seagull fever.
I think I saw a dolphin.
I crunch the chili pepper in front of the jury.
textes.Je cueille le nectar au cœur des fleurs: I gather nectar from the heart of the giant flowers and bottle it. Fairies adore it. Humans too, apparently.
textes.Je cuisine en chantant. Le safran aime l: I sing while I cook. Saffron loves opera.
textes.Je cuisine. Ça sent bon, hein ?: I'm cooking. Smells good, doesn't it?
textes.Je cultive des bananes dans la jungle. B: I grow bananas in the jungle. Barnabé lets me have a patch near his hut, in exchange for a few bunches.
textes.Je cultive les algues dans les jardins d: I grow seaweed in the dome gardens, dry it under the crystal and press it into cakes. My grandmother's recipe. She was nine hundred years old.
textes.Je cultive mes fleurs sur la colline, de: I grow my flowers on the hill, behind the olive trees. Lavender, roses, and bougainvillea that never listens to me.
textes.Je danse comme un spaghetti dans l'eau b: I dance like a spaghetti in boiling water. It's the right technique.
textes.Je danse sur toutes tes chansons. Même c: I dance to all your songs. Even the ones you hide.
textes.Je demande à Sofia tous les soirs si ell: Every evening I ask Sofia if she's coming to the five o'clock fishing. She says no. But when I get back at noon, there's often a pretty shell sitting on the bench of my boat. I pretend not to know where it came from. She pretends to believe me. That's her way of coming along.
textes.Je dessine les cartes de l'archipel. Vot: I draw the maps of the archipelago. The map in your journal is a bit mine too: I fill it in thanks to travellers.
textes.Je devais repartir le lendemain de mon a: I was supposed to leave the day after I arrived. The mist was too thick. Berthe served me more pie. The next day too: the mist, the pie. After a month, I understood: it's the pie that brings the mist. She doesn't believe me. But she keeps making it. So I stay. Somebody has to eat it.
textes.Je dis partout que je battrais les Seign: I tell everyone I'd beat the Lords of Xibalba. But I'll tell you, {surnom}: at night, I don't dare go near the Cenote. The bats… And before every big match, at dawn, I go and see Ix Kanul, without saying anything, so she'll pray for my hips. I say I'm out running. She pretends to believe me. I think.
textes.Je dis que je fais tout à pied, que j'ai: I say I go everywhere on foot, that I like walking. The truth, {surnom}, is that I'm scared of boats. Scared stiff. Even Bastien's rowboat, even moored, I won't get in. I've never seen Port-Azur up close. That's why I want so badly to go to Lulu's fairies: it's the only trip you can take without a boat.
textes.Je dis toujours que la sardine me manqua: I always say I missed the sardines. It's true: the sardines over there had no taste. I came home a year early, without telling anyone. Fatima was on the quay, mending. She looked up and said: “There you are.” As if I'd left the day before. The year after, we got married.
textes.Je dis toujours que personne n'est jamai: I always say nobody has ever come. That's almost true. A hundred and twenty years ago, one night with no sharks, Nausicaa was singing so softly that I closed my eyes. One minute. When I opened them again, the Pearl no longer shone at the foot of the obelisk, and a black hull was speeding off westward. I've never told anyone. Nobody. Not even her.
textes.Je dis à Lucas d'écrire à Lola. « Une le: I keep telling Lucas to write to Lola. “A letter, Lucas! Women love letters!” I even gave him a postcard with a lighthouse on it, to get him started. He went bright red: “Letters aren't my thing.” He put it in his pocket all the same. He never sent it. I'll give him another one. At cost price.
textes.Je dis à mon peuple que nous attendons q: I tell my people we are waiting for the sea to give us back our island. Here is the truth, {surnom}. Five hundred years ago, one night, the crystal shone so brightly it could have lifted the dome all the way to the sun. I felt it under my hands. I was afraid of what lay above, of what the world had become without us. And I said no. For everyone.
textes.Je dois rentrer, sinon Maman va faire de: I have to go home, or Mum will start blowing smoke out of her ears. She really does that when she's cross.
textes.Je dois rentrer. Papa va encore faire cl: I have to go home. Dad's going to go clang clang on the stairs again, and Mum's going to laugh. Same thing every evening.
textes.Je dois à Bobor une histoire pour chaque: I owe Bobor a story for every brioche. That's more than fourteen thousand stories. I made up half of them walking to his stall. One day, he said to me: “You've already told me that one.” I answered: “Yes, but the ending is new.” He laughed, and gave me two brioches.
textes.Je donnais mon cours à cinq heures, Tito: I gave my class at five, and Titou his show too, on the other side of the fountain. He did my crab step backwards while falling over, and all the kids went over to him. The cat stayed. I moved my class to four. The kids came back. The next day, Titou had moved his show to four.
I give dance lessons in the village. The only serious student is the cat from the little house.
textes.Je donne des noms aux caisses. Ça passe: I give the crates names. It passes the time. Don't tell Odette.
textes.Je dors comme une chauve-souris, la tête: I sleep like a bat, upside down. The dreams are much better: they just fall right into your head.
textes.Je dors de six à neuf heures. Bernard ta: I sleep from six to nine. Bernard knocks at my door at eight. At noon, I eat at the Perroquet, my back to Fernand. On Sundays, Odette brings up soup. At night, Léon flashes me twice, I answer with two beams. One stormy night, the lens cracked. And to the west, sometimes, the blue glow. I write it down. I say nothing.
textes.Je dors jusqu'à ce que le soleil soit ha: I sleep until the sun is high. Then I play at the halqa, near Ba Sidi's circle: when his tale crosses the desert, I lay down a low note. In the evening, on the square, Omar gives the camel's step, Hamid sings too loud, and I hold the wave. And when the pirates' cook gets up, I play him his whale dance.
textes.Je dors toujours, Khéty. Parle aux héron: I always sleep, Khéty. Talk to the herons, don't mind me.
textes.Je déborde d'énergie ! Il faut que ça so: I'm bursting with energy! It's got to come out.
textes.Je décharge les bateaux. Toute la journé: I unload the boats. All day. In the evening I play cards at the Perroquet. I lose, but I play.
textes.Je déjeune au comptoir à midi. Pour surv: I lunch at the counter at noon. To keep an eye on the butler. He's slow: I built him never to spill a drop. He never has. And one morning Gaston put a bow tie on him. Under the chin. There is no chin. The bow is held on with a magnet. Hm. It holds well, I'll admit.
I make shell necklaces. By day I sell, by night I dance. Perfect balance.
textes.Je fabrique tout ce qui sert sous la mer: I make everything you need under the sea: mother-of-pearl lamps, combs, flippers… Flippers! With them, you swim like a dolphin.
textes.Je fais compter les coquillages à Théo,: I get Théo to count shells — occupational hazard. He counts very well up to twenty. After that, he makes it up: “Twenty, twenty-ten, twenty-thousand!” I tried to correct him. He looked at me, very serious: “Mummy, these are holiday shells. They don't count the same.” I couldn't think of an answer. A schoolteacher beaten by a six-year-old.
textes.Je fais des barques, pas des montagnes :: I make boats, not mountains: the whole port laughed. The truth, {surnom}, is that I was scared. I've never touched a big ship. If I fail, everyone will see. So at night, I draw their hull in charcoal, on planks, and I look for where the leak is. I think I know. I don't dare go and tell them.
I take photos of the party at night. The glow sticks leave gorgeous trails.
I'm taking a nap. Well, I was.
textes.Je fais le pain du village depuis deux c: I've been baking the village's bread for two hundred years, ever since my mother fell asleep under the Mother Tree. Gilwen brings me her honey, Thalion the wild honey from up top, Nimiel brings frogs. Caelan sings songs to my brioche. The oven sulks one day in three. It's enough for me, {surnom}. Have a loaf.
I've baked the village bread for two hundred years. Nobody has ever gone hungry in Bois-Doré. Except Thalion, who forgets to eat.
textes.Je fais les chambres depuis cinq ans. On: I've been doing the rooms for five years. You learn everything about people by making their bed.
textes.Je fais les clochettes d'argent pour les: I make the silver bells for the big festivals. One little bell for every ear born in Ramure. There are a lot of them on the Mother Oak.
textes.Je fais les jarres de la Maison de Vie,: I make the jars for the House of Life, the temple and the houses. My jars don't leak. I also make scarabs for travellers: they bring luck. The merchant from Aztlán, Tochtli, sometimes takes my pots to Coyotl, the lake potter. Coyotl sends me back his fanged jars. We talk through jars. That's enough.
textes.Je fais ma fameuse soupe aux cailloux. L: I'm making my famous pebble soup. My great-great-grandmother's recipe. All I'm missing is… a pebble. Or something that stings.
textes.Je fais mes glaces moi-même, la nuit, av: I make my ice cream myself, at night, with milk from the hill goats and ice that comes in by boat. The constable eats three a day. It's a state secret.
textes.Je fais mille nœuds par jour. Fatima, à: I tie a thousand knots a day. Fatima, next to me, ties two thousand. She's eighty. I don't know how she does it.
textes.Je fais partie du groupe, moi aussi. Je: I'm part of the band too. I play the triangle.
textes.Je fais pousser les fleurs d'un coup de: I make flowers grow with a flick of my wand, I light up the houses, I turn Grommelot into a frog when he's too grumpy. Well, I used to.
textes.Je fais rire tout le monde avec mes gale: I make everyone laugh with my lost tunnels. At first, it was for fun. But the other morning, {surnom}, I watched Brunna butter her bread and, for a whole minute, I couldn't remember her name. One minute. I didn't tell her. I sleep in the mine so she won't see.
textes.Je fais une coiffe pour la fête du Solei: I'm making a headdress for the Sun festival! I'm missing the last feather, the one in the middle. Which would you choose?
textes.Je fais une pause. Les androïdes ont dro: I'm taking a break. Androids have the right to breaks, ever since the mayor's law.
I'm taking a break. A little one.
textes.Je fermais la paillote quand j'ai vu une: I was closing the beach hut when I saw a lantern moving at the water's edge. It was Hugo, on his knees, digging and talking to himself: “Sorry, Léa. Sorry, sand. Give it back, please.” I brought him a consolation punch and stayed a while. You don't leave someone talking to the sand all alone.
textes.Je garde chaque brin. Je les glisse entr: I keep every sprig. I slip them between the pages of a big almanac of my father's, one sprig a day, for seven years. The book won't close any more, it smells like a bride's wardrobe. I told Rose about it, one evening. Her eyes went all wet. The pollen, no doubt. A florist must breathe in a great deal of it.
textes.Je garde l'entrée du village. Depuis que: I guard the village entrance. Since the mist opened for you, I mostly keep an eye on you.
textes.Je garde la forme. Tu veux faire un tour: I'm keeping fit. Want to do a lap with me?
textes.Je garde la mémoire du royaume : les his: I keep the kingdom's memory: the stories, the songs, the riddles. A riddle is a story in hiding.
textes.Je garde la porte. Contre les requins, s: I guard the gate. Against sharks, mostly. They can't get under the dome — there's no water — but they try. Silly things, sharks.
textes.Je garde le Cercle de l'aube jusqu'au mi: I watch over the Circle from dawn until the middle of the night. I know who passes, who touches, who picks things up. Lin comes to read to the stones. Aurélien picks up the shards, saying thank you. Pip gave his blanket to the smallest one. Agathe prowls with her crystal ball. Séraphine comes up in the evening. It isn't a job. It's a way of being there.
textes.Je garde le temple depuis la mort de ma: I have kept the temple since my mother died. Every morning I pour cacao and copal into the Cenote. The rain gods live there.
textes.Je garde les racines depuis quatre cents: I've guarded the roots for four hundred years. Before the fairies, before the elves. Nobody ever thanks the roots. Nobody.
textes.Je garde une boîte de poudre de fer derr: I keep a tin of iron powder behind the counter, just for the professor. One lunchtime he put in so much that his spoon was pulled by the machine's magnet. It flew off and stuck to the boiler, ding! It took me an hour to get it off. It hangs above the counter now, with a label: “The Professor's Reflection”.
textes.Je garde une porte. Elle ne bouge pas. M: I guard a gate. It doesn't move. Neither do I. All is well.
I'm keeping it. I'm keeping everything. Even you.
textes.Je garde. Le jour, la porte. La nuit, le: I guard. By day, the gate. By night, the golems coming down. Kalda, my niece, reports what she sees on the slopes. Dagna brings me a bowl at noon. Hilda's goats climb on me. In the evening, a mug of fizz at Ulfa's. All is well. More or less.
textes.Je glisse les plans du bateau-robot sous: I slide the plans for the robot boat under her door. Every month. They come back the next day under mine. Annotated. In red. “No.” “No.” And at the bottom, once: “The rudder is good. Still no.” Hm. The rudder is good. I know.
I taste a lot, Mother Sage.
textes.Je guide les lucioles. Le soir, je les e: I guide the fireflies. In the evening, I send them to draw paths in the air for fairies who come home late.
I'm gardening. Plants are patient. I'm trying to be, too.
I throw it out and get a new one.
textes.Je jongle, je danse, je fais le clown su: I juggle, I dance, I clown around on the village square for the kids. The party is my own show.
textes.Je joue ! Tu veux jouer avec moi ?: I'm playing! Want to play with me?
textes.Je joue aux boules. Tu sais pointer, toi: I'm playing boules. Can you roll one close?
textes.Je joue depuis que j'ai six ans. Mon gra: I've been playing since I was six. My grandfather played in town squares, with a hat at his feet. Me, I've got a boss and a wage. Would he be proud or sad? I don't know.
textes.Je joue derrière les tambours, alors j'e: I play behind the drums, so I hear things. When Bourru drums, he slows down just as Lilas raises her arms. And she dances slower just when he slows down. I don't say anything. A fox knows when a joke would be one too many. Rarely. But this time, I know.
textes.Je joue pour l'Arbre-Mère, pour le vent…: I play for the Mother Tree, for the wind… and above all for one window, up there. Ilyria's.
textes.Je joue un peu de musique. Ça fait du bi: I'm playing a little music. It does everyone good.
textes.Je joue, c'est le plus important de la j: I'm playing, it's the most important part of the day!
textes.Je jouerai plus lentement. Rien que pour: I'll play slower. Just for your feet.
textes.Je l'ai composé moi-même ! Il s'appelle: I composed it myself! It's called “Symphony for a Sneezing Cat.” Want to hear it?
textes.Je l'ai connu haut comme trois noix de c: I knew him when he was knee-high to a coconut, and I'm the one who gave him his name. His music goes way too fast… and yet my heart keeps up. I don't know which of us is wrong.
textes.Je l'ai demandée en mariage comme on ven: I proposed to her the way you sell a carpet: “One husband, very handsome, very chatty, special fiancée price.” She said: “Too expensive.” I lowered it. “Still too expensive.” I lowered it. At the third price, she said yes. I ran through the whole souk shouting: “She haggled! She loves me!” Karim knocked over his slippers.
textes.Je l'ai emmené sur les falaises du nord: I took him to the northern cliffs to listen to the wind with me, for a whole hour. I sang along with it, so he'd hear the tune. Borée said: “You sing off-key. So does it.” That proves it sings, doesn't it? On the way down, he took my arm. He says I took his. He took mine.
textes.Je l'ai entendue ! Toute l'île l'a enten: I heard it! The whole island heard it! Even Borée looked up! Here, some coins for you. And come levitate with me at sunset: from up high, the sea turns all pink.
textes.Je l'ai entendue quatre cents fois. Elle: I've heard it four hundred times. It's still beautiful.
textes.Je l'ai envoyé sur le toit du Fondouk ch: I sent him up on the Fondouk roof to look for the ginger cat. “Don't come back without him!” He came back an hour later with… a nightcap, taken off a washing line. “No cat, captain, but it was cold up there.” I took the nightcap back myself, to an old lady. She hit me with it.
textes.Je l'ai laissé peindre le ciel d'une pet: I let him paint the sky on a little canvas. Blue everywhere, really hard, tongue sticking out. Then, right in the middle, he painted a red, yellow, blue and green diamond, with a long knotted tail. His kite. I didn't say anything. I kept the canvas. It's above my bed, at the hotel.
textes.Je l'ai laissée inventer un parfum. Elle: I let her invent a flavour. She thought about it for a week, looking very scientific. Then she said: “Strawberry, and a pinch of sea salt. For the dolphin.” I pulled a face. I tasted it. My oh my… it was good! The strawberry-dolphin sells better than my coconut. Don't tell Kiki.
At least I washed it. The sock.
I ate it. Half of it.
textes.Je l'ai presque ! Presque presque !: I've almost got it! Almost almost!
textes.Je l'ai senti. Toute l'île l'a senti. (L: I felt it. The whole island felt it. (The bridges of light shine, the fountain finally chooses its planet, and way up there, the Spire beats like a happy drum.) For a thousand years the Heart has carried us, and it was a Heavyfoot who healed it. The elders of Ondelune wouldn't believe it. I do. (She stands up, very straight, and places both hands on your shoulders.) In the name of the Council, of Tempo who cried at exactly the right hour, of Écliptique who is preparing a two-hour speech, and of Volt who says it's nothing: you are now the Friend of the Lumens. The first one. Hee hee. Here, some washers, since you all like those, and three cosmic jellies from Gloubi. He cried into them. They're a little salty.
textes.Je l'ai tenu contre moi pendant toute la: I held it close the whole crossing.
textes.Je l'ai trouvé sur un radeau, au large,: I found him on a raft, far out at sea, years ago. He had nothing. Not a word, not a name. Just a drawing folded in his pocket: a white house, a laughing woman. I had him brought aboard. He took a rope and did the work of three. He's never asked me for anything. I've never asked him anything either.
textes.Je l'ai vu ! La couleur est sortie de la: I saw it! The colour came out of the Palette like a drop of ink on blotting paper, and the clearing got back its brown, its grass, its old tree trunks. (She wipes her eyes: they run a little.) Now, the Brush: dip it in the Palette, and it will drink the colour. Then hold it in your hand, and paint what you like, where you like. For the other eight pots, ask the families: Basile is looking for the blue at the Rubbed-Out Pond, Rosalie the green in the Hatching Wood, Capucine the red in the White Meadows, Lili the yellow on the Strand, Gaspard is watching for the purple from the top of the Lookout, and Achille dreams of the orange at the foot of the waterfall. The last two… you'll have to hunt for them. Augustin surely has an idea: he always does.
I saw it too. Keep watching.
textes.Je l'ai vu, patron. Je ne suis pas aveug: I saw him, boss. I'm not blind.
textes.Je l'ai vue lancer ses couteaux au cirqu: I saw her throwing knives at the Tortuga circus, the night her partner demanded a raise in the middle of the show. After the show, I went to see her: “On my brig, nobody asks for a raise.” She laughed. She signed. She's never asked for one. She keeps the cash box. I don't dare check.
textes.Je l'ai écrit quelque part… sur un coqui: I wrote it down somewhere… on a shell, I think.
textes.Je l'ai élevée au milieu des plus beaux: I raised her among the finest swaps in Ramure, and she sells for coins! Where did I go wrong, my friend? And her apples are delicious. That's the worst part.
textes.Je l'avais ramassée en passant, sa noise: I'd picked up her hazelnut in passing, because it was shining a bit. I dropped it on the steps of the throne. The next day, a little fairy was climbing out of it demanding seeds. Ever since, every week, she asks me which island. I really do think hard, you know. I see trees. Lots of trees.
I can hear it, girl. I can hear it.
textes.Je la croyais endormie au fond de la bar: I thought she was asleep at the bottom of the boat. I was explaining to a heron, very quietly, that the flood comes from the rain in the mountains. And her voice, behind me, eyes closed: “And the rain, Khéty, who sends it?” I dropped the oar, the oar fell in, I dived in to catch it. She didn't even open her eyes.
textes.Je la garde depuis trois mois !: I've been holding it for three months!
textes.Je la regarde avec les doigts, Ptahmosé: I'm looking at it with my fingers, Ptahmose!
I'd give it back to its fairy.
textes.Je la vois ! Elle est toujours là ! Elle: I see it! It's still there! It moves all the time! Doesn't it ever get tired? … Thank you, friend. Thank you.
textes.Je laisse des poèmes dans ses boîtes à l: I leave poems in her lantern boxes. One evening, coming out of her workshop, I ran right into her. I pretended to check a street lamp. There was no street lamp in front of her workshop. She didn't say anything. The next day, there was one. She'd had it put in. It's called Poem.
I'd just tell them, simple as that.
I'll keep it. Your mother sends her love.
textes.Je le mets dans mon cours. Le chat va ad: I'm putting it in my class. The cat will love it.
I'll put it on your tab, then.
I'll put it here. Away from the carpet.
textes.Je le regarde ! Avec mes yeux ! C'est tr: I'm watching it! With my eyes! It's very… bright, without a camera.
textes.Je le savais ! C'est comme ça qu'on trou: I knew it! That's how you find what's on no map. And then people tell me about it, and I draw it. You're my best informant.
I knew it! Nobody will believe us.
I knew it! You've got good taste, you.
textes.Je le savais ! Tu as une tête à bêtises: I knew it! You've got a mischief face! Tell me! No, wait, Aëlwen's listening. Later. But I knew it!
I knew it! You have good taste.
textes.Je le savais ! Vous avez une tête de bul: I knew it! You've got a bubble face. That's a compliment. Look at that one, it looks like you: round, light, a bit lopsided.
I knew it! Xan knows his. When I say “Xan”, he buzzes. OK, he buzzes all the time. But louder!
textes.Je le savais ! … Attends. Tu te moques d: I knew it! … Wait. Are you making fun of me?
textes.Je le savais. Ce matin, Rê s'est levé ro: I knew it. This morning, Ra rose red and gold, like a young man. (She lays her hand on your forehead.) May his light follow you wherever you go. Here: bread from Mérit, and enough to fill your purse. And the Eye of Horus, keep it well: in the highlands, in the middle of the island, a niche awaits it.
textes.Je le savais. Je demandais pour la forme: I knew it. I was only asking for form's sake.
I knew it. I missed you, big girl.
I can feel it in my whiskers.
textes.Je le sens jusqu'au bout de mes cornes :: I feel it down to the tips of my horns: it's warm! (The Archduchess laughs, and the whole throne room laughs with her.) Pandémonia owes you her fire, little flame. From today, you're at home here. Here: buns from the Eternal Oven, and enough to fill your purse. And this title, which will be engraved on the great door.
I suspect he laughs under his chèche. While I haggle, the cloth moves a little, right there, around the mouth. Once, I pretended to faint halfway through the price, just to see. The chèche moved a lot. He still said “No”. But he was laughing, I swear it on my carpets.
textes.Je les ai ! Regardez : caoutchouc, jusqu: I've got them! Look: rubber, up to the knees!
textes.Je les ai ! Une question, une seule !: I've got them on! One question, just one!
textes.Je les ai bien emmêlés, hein ?: I tangled them up nicely, didn't I?
textes.Je les ai vus ! (Elle a des étoiles dans: I saw them! (She has stars in her eyes. And a bit of green paint.) They're... alive! You've got the touch! The supple wrist, the bold pschhht! The wall says thank you. So do I. Here, a little reward, and know this: on the water tower, there's a spot for your name. I'll write it tonight. In green. Don't argue.
textes.Je les fais. Mais sans bateau brodé, cet: I'll make them. But no embroidered boat this time.
I keep every one of them.
textes.Je les laisse là. Au cas où il serait pr: I'll leave them here. In case it's clean and loud.
I'm painting them, caïd. With my eyes.
textes.Je les prends toutes, Marée. Ondine gran: I'll take them all, Marée. Ondine's still growing.
I've got them, Yaya! I've got them… Oops. Sorry, Momo!
I see them. I won't tell you where.
I'll check them myself. Every one.
textes.Je leur dirai. Elles ne m'écoutent pas t: I'll tell them. They don't always listen to me.
textes.Je lis des histoires aux pierres, à voix: I read stories to the stones, in a low voice, sitting against Nacre. Once, I skipped a page without meaning to. From the other side of the Circle, Ysolde said: “You skipped a page.” She didn't have the book. I went back. The stones prefer stories in order.
textes.Je lis en buvant sa bière, et il m'arriv: I read while drinking her beer, and sometimes I spill a little. My scroll of the Hymn to Hapy smells of barley now. The pupils sniff it before reading it. Mérit says it's the only papyrus on the river that makes you thirsty. I think she's proud of it.
I'll read a little longer. Just one chapter. Or two.
textes.Je lis un peu. Les livres, ça fait voyag: I'm reading a bit. Books let you travel without moving.
I'm reading. Well, I was reading.
textes.Je lui achète mes sardines chaque samedi: I buy my sardines from her every Saturday. She always picks the finest, the shiniest, and puts it aside for me, laughing. I suspect her of trying to bribe an officer. I've noted it in my notebook. But they really are very fine sardines.
textes.Je lui achète trois paniers de dattes pa: I buy three baskets of dates from her a year. For my flatbreads. Egyptian dates are the best, I have to say. We swapped recipes: I gave her my cacao without the chilli, she gave me her beer without the dates. We both lied. I know it. She knows it. We respect each other.
textes.Je lui achète un pot de miel chaque sema: I buy a pot of honey from him every week, for my flatbreads. He looks at me with a funny little smile, as if he knew something. He doesn't know anything. He can't know anything. I put a pot of honey a week in my flatbreads. They're very… very sweet. There.
textes.Je lui ai acheté la potion qui change la: I bought the potion that turns your voice into a duck's. I talked to the wind like a duck for an hour, on the cliffs. It laughed, yes, it did: it made a little whirlwind. Mirabelle says it's the first time one of her potions has made the wind laugh. She wrote it in her notebook.
textes.Je lui ai acheté trois flacons et je l'a: I bought three bottles from her and paid with a riddle. A very good one, worth double. She's been looking for the answer for ten years. The day she finds it, she'll realise she's the one who owes me change. I'm in no hurry.
textes.Je lui ai acheté un bouclier pour la Gar: I bought a shield from him for the Guard. It was so heavy it took two guards to carry it. Together. When I went to complain, Kraxx told me: “Nothing gets through it.” It's true. Nothing gets through. Not even the guards carrying it.
I brought her a tale from Cliquetis.
textes.Je lui ai appris la cochenille. Son lin: I taught her about cochineal. Her linen stayed white, her hands turned red. She looked at them, amazed, as if she were seeing her hands for the first time. I gave her a red and yellow belt. She said: “I'll never wear it.” She held it close all afternoon.
textes.Je lui ai appris la vieille coutume : un: I taught her the old custom: a coin under the foot of the mainmast, for the ship's luck. Barbe-Sanglante put a gold coin under each of his masts. Gwen put a silver coin: it was all she had. I looked, and I said: “She'll float again.” She smiled. I mean it. Boats can tell when you believe in them.
textes.Je lui ai appris la vieille façon de pêc: I taught him the old way to fish for light: you stretch the crystal net above the fountain, you wait for the first ray to get caught in it, and above all, you don't talk. It took him a hundred years to manage it. He says it's because I was talking the whole time, right beside him.
textes.Je lui ai appris le nœud de chaise à la: I taught him the bowline the Barbe-Sanglante way: the rabbit comes out of the hole, goes round the tree and goes back down the hole. He practises every evening, eyes closed. His rabbit always gets a bit lost round the tree. Mine got lost too, at his age. The captain used to say the best rabbits get a bit lost.
textes.Je lui ai appris le nœud de huit. Le soi: I taught her the figure-of-eight knot. That same evening, she'd taught it to her mother, to Lucas, to Raymond and to the little white dog, who does it very badly. Since then, there are figure-of-eight knots all over the quay: on the benches, on the bins, on Fernand's walking stick.
textes.Je lui ai appris trois noms : Doyenne, N: I've taught her three names: Doyenne, Nacre, Petite-Ourse. One per full moon, no more. I asked her not to write them down. She writes them in lemon ink, which can only be read over a flame. I said nothing. Neither did the stones. She's a child who finds solutions. I like that.
textes.Je lui ai appris à faire de l'ocre avec: I taught her to make ochre from the wadi clay: you dry it, crush it, sift it. She wanted to do it all with her bare hands. Her hands were red for a whole week; at the Fondouk, my aunt thought she'd been in a fight. With that ochre, Selma painted birds on my jugs. The whole series sold in a day.
textes.Je lui ai appris à faire un poing. Le po: I taught him how to make a fist. Thumb outside, not inside, or it hurts. The captain said the cabin boy doesn't fight. So he keeps it in his pocket, his fist. Sometimes he takes it out to show me. It's a good one. I'm proud.
textes.Je lui ai appris à lancer une ligne. Au: I taught her to cast a line. With her first fish, she shouted for joy. Then she looked at it, and put it back in the water: “Maybe it has children.” She put the next six back too. In the evening, we came home with an empty basket and the faces of champions. Tiyi made lentils.
textes.Je lui ai commandé des pots pour mes fle: I ordered pots for my flowers from him. He put Tlaloc's round eyes on them, out of habit. My cempasúchil look surprised in them. Pilli says they watch people go by. Coyotl says Tlaloc watches over my flowers. It does rain a lot on my pots, that's true.
textes.Je lui ai commandé la carte officielle d: I commissioned the official map of the city from him. I wanted something dignified: an avenue, a square, an opera house. He drew it all, with columns and fountains. It's magnificent. Visitors get a little lost looking for the opera house, but they see the city as it will be. That's what a map is for. I believe.
textes.Je lui ai commandé un crocodile en argil: I ordered a clay crocodile from him, to scare off the real ones. He made it very well. Too well. The next day, Sobek was sleeping next to it, with his head on it. Ptahmosé told the whole brewery that my crocodile had found love. It's not funny. Fine. It's a bit funny. But not for me.
textes.Je lui ai commandé un tablier brodé de d: I ordered an apron embroidered with sea bream from her. Calm ones, I said. She embroidered six sleeping sea bream, eyes half-closed. I wore it to the fish market and planted myself under Saïd's platform: “Look, Saïd! Here's a happy sea bream!” He shouted louder. But he looked at the apron. For a long time.
textes.Je lui ai commandé une jarre pour garder: I ordered a jar from him to keep fish alive. It holds water so well that a perch has been living in it for weeks. I don't have the heart to eat her. I named her Ptah. Ptahmosé pretended to be offended. But one evening I saw him lean over the jar and say hello to the perch.
textes.Je lui ai confié ma carte de Port-Azur,: I entrusted her with my map of Port-Azur, the one the mayor gives to visitors, to colour it in. She gave it back with the sea in six blues. Six! The port, the bay, the open sea, the lighthouse's shadow… I held the map up to the sun and said: “It's the first map that looks wet.” She blushed right up to her beret.
textes.Je lui ai confié ma graine de cactus des: I trusted her with my dwarf cactus seed. Perlée gives it one drop a month. Not one more, even when I beg. In spring, it grew a yellow flower! I cried for joy. Perlée gave me a funny look. As if she wanted to cry too, but didn't know how.
textes.Je lui ai conseillé de chanter aux abeil: I advised him to sing to the bees before taking the honey. He sang. Once. They stung him twice as much. I explained that it wasn't the song, it was the tuning. He didn't speak to me for a month. My girls buzzed with laughter all week.
textes.Je lui ai cousu dans l'ourlet un fil dor: I sewed a golden thread into her hem, the only one I have, kept from my own mother. I told her it was a ray of sunshine. She checks every evening that it's still there. So do I, when she's asleep.
textes.Je lui ai cousu un chapeau de capitaine: I sewed her a captain's hat from an old apron, with a sea bream embroidered on the front. She looked at the sea bream for a long time. Then she said: “That one looks calm.” Since then, she wears it every day. Even to sleep, when she thinks I'm not looking.
textes.Je lui ai cousu une cape rouge à paillet: I sewed him a red cape with ember sequins for the Arena. The first time, the crowd shouted so loud that he froze, and the sequins went out. Madame Hurla shouted “MOVE!”. He moved, and the cape shone like a bonfire. Since then, before every fight, I murmur to him: “Move gently, but move.”
textes.Je lui ai demandé ce qu'ils mangent en m: I asked him what they eat at sea, on the Murène. He brought me one of their biscuits. Hard as wood. I tried to bite it, nearly lost a tooth. Now I use it as a sinker for my line. It sinks very well. Better than lead.
textes.Je lui ai demandé cent fois de me rappor: I've asked her a hundred times to bring me back the caravan folk's cream recipe from the south. Every time, she tells me she's almost got it. Two years ago she brought me a little “authentic” pot, with a ribbon. It was goat fat. Again.
textes.Je lui ai demandé combien de trous il fa: I asked him how many holes you'd have to plug for the Léviathan to float. He opened an old black journal full of numbers and said: “Four thousand three hundred and twelve. Plus tomorrow's.” I said: “Oh well, that's not so many.” He sighed so hard the lantern swung.
textes.Je lui ai demandé combien il y a d'étoil: I asked him how many stars there are. He told me: “Count them.” So I counted all night long, on the roof. One thousand and eleven! And Xan flew in front of the moon, so that made one thousand and eleven plus Xan. He wrote it all in his tables. I'm in Ah Kin Pech's tables! Well, Xan is.
textes.Je lui ai demandé d'arrêter. Il a promis: I asked him to stop. He promised. The next day, the octopus had fifty arms, and I beat it with one hand, holding my cup of hot seaweed tea in the other. “See, I've made you more modest,” he told me. I don't see.
textes.Je lui ai demandé de m'écrire depuis l'A: I asked him to write to me from Atlantis once he's found it. A card, with a stamp from there. He promised, hand on heart.
