He always opens the caramel before the letter, and he often doesn't finish the letter. But my card, I'm sure he'll finish it. I'm waiting for it. I think I'm waiting for it more than he is.
textes.Je lui ai demandé de me faire léviter, p: I asked her to make me levitate, to see the stars up close. Three metres above the roof, I discovered I was afraid of heights. I clung to her arm shouting that the stars were very nice from far away. She brought me back down without laughing. She laughed afterwards. For a long time.
textes.Je lui ai demandé de quelle couleur étai: I asked her what colour the sun was. She said yellow. I asked yellow like what, because there's nothing yellow here. So she took off her crown and put it on my head! I ran all the way to the canal to look at myself in the water. I had a sun on my head. She took it back afterwards. Shame.
textes.Je lui ai demandé où étaient les grottes: I asked her where my grandfather's caves were. She said: “Under the feet of the one who guards.” The one who guards: the Skala! I went there at night, with a lantern, on my knees in the pebbles. And I came face to face with the caïd Hamza, sabre drawn. I said I was admiring the cannons. Fatima laughed about it for three days.
textes.Je lui ai demandé pourquoi les scarabées: I asked him why scarabs push balls of poo. He told me it's like Khepri, who pushes the sun in the morning. So the sun is a ball of poo? I asked Néferet. She laughed really loudly. Ptahmosé went all red. I still don't know the answer.
textes.Je lui ai demandé un jour, très poliment: One day I asked her, very politely, if she could “lose a little” of the university's letters. Just a little. A week or two. She refused, looking at me the way you look at a child who won't go to the dentist. The next day, with the envelope, there was a caramel. Since then, there's always one. I open the caramel first.
textes.Je lui ai demandé une louche solide. Il: I asked him for a sturdy ladle. He forged me an iron one, with a handle as long as an arm and a bowl that holds a whole soup. I can only lift it with both hands. He said: “That way, it won't break.” It doesn't break. My arms ache, but it doesn't break.
textes.Je lui ai demandé une robe avec des poch: I asked her for a dress with pockets, to keep roasted chestnuts in during audiences. She let out a shriek, as if I'd asked for a dress made of straw. Three days later, she delivered a magnificent dress, with pockets hidden in the folds. She made me swear not to tell anyone.
textes.Je lui ai demandé. Il porte tes sandales: I did. He's wearing your sandals.
textes.Je lui ai dit qu'il y avait cent squelet: I told him there were a hundred skeletons at the Cursed Fort. He went to count, with his spyglass. He came back very proud: “Ninety-seven!” I replied: “The other three are out.” He thought about it. Then he drew them in dotted lines on his map. That day, I knew we'd be friends forever.
textes.Je lui ai dit, devant tout le monde, que: I told him, in front of everyone, that his horns shone brighter than his conversation. The whole square laughed. Tiburce smiled, bowed very low, and answered: “Then I shall keep quiet, and let you play.” He stayed until the very last note, without a word. It may be the most beautiful answer anyone's ever given me.
textes.Je lui ai dit, un jour, ce que disent le: One day I told her what the old ones say: that Yggdrasil grows on the other side too, beneath the clouds. She replied: “Perhaps all the way down to your sister.” Since then, every morning, I set one extra drop at the foot of the Tree. In case its roots reach all the way down.
textes.Je lui ai donné des graines de maïs à pl: I gave him maize seeds to plant. He planted them all upside down, tip in the air, “so they can see the sun”. They grew anyway. A bit crooked. Like his father's first maize. I didn't tell him why my eyes were wet. I just watched the maize dance.
textes.Je lui ai donné ma première balle, celle: I gave him my first ball, the one my father made me, the size of a mango. He sleeps with it. He has bruises everywhere. He's happy. His mother came to complain to me. I explained that it's the path of champions. She didn't look convinced.
textes.Je lui ai donné sa première vraie leçon: I gave him his first real lesson: stepping back. “Further. More. A bit more.” He backed up all the way to the Crankshaft. Perfect! Then I let him pull the lever on a tiny little explosion. A teeny pop. He still talks about it as the greatest day of his life. So do I, a bit.
textes.Je lui ai donné un champignon qui brille: I gave her a glowing mushroom, so she wouldn't need a candle when she marks papers. She said it wasn't allowed. But she kept it! It's on her desk, I saw it through the window. It's called Henri.
textes.Je lui ai fabriqué un cerf-volant avec u: I made him a kite out of an old dormitory sheet. I told him: “That way, the sheet flies, and you hold the string.” He flies it every evening in the square, higher than the roof, higher than Gérard. Pip watches it with eyes as big as saucers. As long as he's holding the string, I can breathe.
textes.Je lui ai fabriqué une lanterne spéciale: I made him a special lantern, cut out with dragons, princesses and volcanoes, that casts shadows on the walls when he tells his stories. The first night, I used the wrong cut-out, and a dragon appeared in the middle of a love story. Grandpa improvised. It became his most famous story.
textes.Je lui ai fabriqué une étagère pour ses: I made her a shelf for her shells, with planks from the Merciless too damaged for the hull. Two hundred and twelve slots. Plus one, empty, at the top in the middle, for the one she hasn't found yet. She didn't say anything. She just took a nail and drove it in straight. First try. The only time.
textes.Je lui ai fait ma tisane « pour chagrin: I made her my “broken heart” tea: lime blossom, lemon balm, and a hint of Rose's lavender. She drank, thought about it, and said: “It doesn't cure anything, but it smells nice.” Best compliment I've ever had on a herbal tea. The next day she asked for two more.
textes.Je lui ai fait une cruche incassable. Ex: I made her an unbreakable jug. On purpose. Three fingers thick, a handle like an arm. It's so heavy it takes two pirates to fill it, and nobody can drink from it. Mama Lou uses it to prop open the tavern door. It's never broken. It's my best jug. I'm proud.
textes.Je lui ai fait une flûte en terre, en fo: I made her a clay flute, shaped like a bird. The first time she blew into it, a real hummingbird came and perched on the edge of the roof, to listen. She cried. So did I. It's the smallest thing I've ever made. The only one that ever drew a bird of the gods.
textes.Je lui ai fait une potion de légèreté. E: I made her a lightness potion. She drank it in front of her whole class. She didn't float at all, but her hair stood straight up, like a big white feather, all day long! She taught like that. She said the apprentices had never paid so much attention. I wrote it in my notebook: success.
textes.Je lui ai forgé des protège-cornes pour: I forged him horn guards for the Arena, in steel lined with leather. He came to collect them with a bouquet of ember flowers, and a poem. The poem rhymed “Ferronde” with “Ferronde”. I nailed it above the anvil. The apprentices make fun of it. Me, I reread it often.
textes.Je lui ai interdit de grimper au premier: I forbade her to climb up to the first platform without the stairs. She obeyed. She takes the stairs, at full speed, four steps a bound, shouting “I'm obeying!”. The whole fishery shakes. I can't say a thing: it's exactly what I asked for. Mrrr. She'll go far, that one. Running.
textes.Je lui ai laissé tenir le pot de goudron: I let him hold the tar pot once, the way my father let me. He got it up to his elbows, but he didn't let go of the pot. I said “not bad”. He ran off to tell all of Carène. Since then, everyone looks at me as if I'd made a speech.
textes.Je lui ai laissé un pot d'onguent pour l: I left her a pot of ointment for the injured owl in the Twisted Wood, in case it lets her come near. Agathe put it on her table, next to the crystal ball. She told me the ball and the ointment were waiting for the same thing. I don't know what that meant. Neither does she, I think.
textes.Je lui ai laissé une pierre rouge sur so: I left a red stone on his anvil. A beautiful one, picked up at the edge of the crater. He took it for ore and put it in the fire. It shattered. I walked off without a word. That evening, I heard him asking everyone what he'd done. Nobody told him. I won't tell him either.
textes.Je lui ai mis des piquants, à ton oursin: I put spines on your sea urchin. It looks happier. So do I, funnily enough.
textes.Je lui ai montré l'arête dans le creux d: I showed him the bone in the palm of my hand, lowering my voice: “Sea dragon's tooth, milord. Torn out at the risk of my life.” He went pale and took out his purse: “I'll pay you double. For the danger.” Double! For a fishbone! I accepted. Then I bought a round of lemonades at the Perroquet, to be forgiven. By whom, I don't know.
textes.Je lui ai montré l'œil de la Zahra, celu: I showed him the Zahra's eye, the one that watches over. The next day, he'd drawn one on his hammock, in charcoal. He says that way, if he falls asleep, the hammock will bring him back to port. I didn't have the heart to tell him hammocks don't float.
textes.Je lui ai montré ma carte des Anciens. E: I showed her my map of the Ancients. She put her finger on the stain I'd taken for coffee and said: “That's my home.” Since then, I've gone over the stain in gold leaf. Well, in mango juice. It's what I had.
textes.Je lui ai montré mon premier poème. Il p: I showed him my first poem. It was about a pup and rhymed “pup” with “pup”. Nox read it three times, in silence. Then he said to me: “That's a rich rhyme.” I was so proud! Ombreline explained to me later what a rich rhyme was. It wasn't that. But I'm keeping the compliment.
textes.Je lui ai offert un bloc de colophane po: I gave her a block of rosin for her bow, carved into the shape of a horn and polished with ember oil. Perhaps I put in a little too much perfume: her violin smelled of roses for a month. She only said thank you after three days. Three days! I counted them, hour by hour. Then she said thank you. It was worth the three days.
textes.Je lui ai parlé du cœur qui bat, au fond: I told him about the heart that beats, at the end of a tunnel. Boom… boom… He didn't laugh. He asked me to draw the way there. I drew it. He looked at it for a long time, then he said: “Forget this path, Grimli. For once, forget it on purpose.” I'm doing my best.
textes.Je lui ai peint une enseigne pour son ét: I painted her a sign for her stall: “Hot bread”. My eyes… well, my hand slipped, and I put the sign for cat instead of the one for hot. For a week, Mérit sold “cat bread”. The children queued up to see if it meowed. She never sold so much. She bought me a beer, and gave me a new sign to paint.
textes.Je lui ai percé une lanterne spéciale :: I pierced him a special lantern: when you light it, a sultan and a sardine chase each other all round the circle. Three weeks of work. On the first evening, Ba Sidi forgot to tell his tale. He was watching the sardine run. He said it was the first time a story had told itself without him.
textes.Je lui ai posé une énigme sur lui-même :: I set him a riddle about himself: “I grumble in the morning, I grumble at night, and I guard what no one keeps in sight.” He thought for a long time, very seriously, and said: “A bear.” I laughed for three days. He didn't speak to me for the rest of the season. No great loss, he hardly talks.
textes.Je lui ai promis de lui montrer Bertha d: I promised to show her Bertha up close. Not from the quay: on deck, hand on the bronze. But first, the clove hitch. She practises on everything: ribbons, washing lines, Amine's hair. Last week, she almost got it. I've started shining Bertha for the visit.
textes.Je lui ai promis une vraie sortie en mer: I promised her a real trip out to sea the day she eats a raw sardine without pulling a face. She tries every Friday. She pulls a face before she even sees it. I think she pulls a face as soon as she wakes up, just in case.
textes.Je lui ai proposé cent fois une partie c: A hundred times I've suggested he play against the automaton. He always refuses: “It has no watch, Ambroise. I don't play against someone who has no watch.” One evening, I tried to stop the clock to think. He looked at me as if I'd insulted his mother. I never did it again.
textes.Je lui ai proposé d'échanger nos recette: I offered to swap recipes: my salted grog for his tea. A fair deal, between artists. He put down his teapot, looked at me for a long time, and said: “Go away, pirate, before I pour the tea on your head from a great height.” I think that was a no. But the corner of his moustache was smiling.
textes.Je lui ai proposé de vendre des places a: I suggested she sell front-row seats for her festivals. She said music is like the wind: you don't sell it. I told her I could sell the wind. She told me to try. I tried, with fans: “Wind of Ehécatl, two beans.” I only sold one. To my mother. She won, that time.
textes.Je lui ai proposé quatre cents pièces po: I offered her four hundred coins for her whole collection. A fortune! She thought for a second, a tiny little second, and said no. “Everything's for sale, my girl,” I told her. She answered: “Not this.” I felt something odd, right here, in my chest. I think I was happy. That's very bad for business.
textes.Je lui ai proposé un jour d'échanger son: Once, I offered to trade potions for her honey. She refused: her bees don't like the smell of sap. Since then, I pay her in coins, and she counts them one by one, out loud, in front of me. Like I do. We have great respect for each other.
textes.Je lui ai proposé une barque neuve. Pres: I offered him a new boat. Practically a gift: the wood at cost, my work for nothing. He listened to the end. He said: “No.” Then he left. The next day, he brought me a sardine, to thank me for offering. So every winter, I re-caulk the Mabrouka. She thanks me in her own way: she holds.
textes.Je lui ai prêté ma longue-vue de cuivre,: I lent him my copper spyglass, the one with an engraved star, a gift from my first captain. He gave it back with a kink in it: Gros-Louis had sat on it. I wept a little, for form's sake. Then I looked through it: it sees slightly round the corner, behind the rocks. Very handy for hidden coves.
textes.Je lui ai prêté ma longue-vue pour qu'il: I lent him my spyglass so he could watch for his father's ship. He looked at the sea for an hour without moving. I told him ships are like mushrooms: they turn up when you stop looking for them. He went off looking for mushrooms. I watched him go. Then I picked up the spyglass again. For him.
textes.Je lui ai raconté le grand feu de Teotih: I told him about the great fire of Teotihuacan: proud Tecciztécatl, covered in gold, who backs away four times, and humble Nanahuatzin who jumps. Mixtli listened to the end. Then he said: “I'd have jumped first.” I asked him: “With your feathers, or without?” He thought about it for a very long time.
textes.Je lui ai raconté le soir du trois-mâts: I told him about the night of the cloud three-master. He took it very seriously. On his big map, in the north, he added a little dotted island: “Probable island, seen by Fil-de-Fer”. I was so proud. Then I saw he'd drawn a sheep on it. A tiny one. He says it's a detail.
textes.Je lui ai raconté qu'en mousse, j'avais: I told him that as a cabin boy I'd seen a whale as big as the Skala, which soaked me right up to my cap. Big mistake. Since then he tells the whole harbour: “Even Si Larbi said so!” Moulay Brahim came to ask me if it was true. I said yes. It is true. But I didn't know I'd have to repeat it a hundred times.
textes.Je lui ai raconté qu'un monstre vivait d: I told him a monster lived in the harbour basin, under the pontoons. He searched for it a whole afternoon, with a lantern and a shrimping net. He came back with an old boot, put it on my knees and said: “Your monster lost this.” I kept it. It's where I keep my odds and ends.
textes.Je lui ai raconté une version du déluge: I told him a version of the flood where he saves the city with his quill. He pulled a face. The next day I heard him in the archives, all alone, reading it aloud. He even changed a word, to improve it. Got him, the old liar.
textes.Je lui ai rapporté de la Plage des Os un: I brought him back a big shell from Bone Beach, pink inside. He said: “WHAT'S THAT?!” I said: “For you.” He grunted and stuffed it under his arm. I thought he'd thrown it away. But one evening, I saw the shell in his hammock, right by the pillow. I didn't say anything. I smile when I think about it.
textes.Je lui ai rapporté un coquillage de la p: I brought her back a shell from the humans' beach, and told her you could hear the sea in it. She slept with it against her ear for a month. Since then, she asks everyone for one. That's a bit my fault.
textes.Je lui ai rapporté un harpon tordu en fo: I brought him back a harpoon bent into an S. A gargoyle had bitten it. I put it on his stall, saying: “Your harpoon ties knots.” He answered: “Your gargoyle eats iron.” We laughed. He swapped it for me. I kept the bent one: it hangs above my fireplace. The children think it's a snake.
textes.Je lui ai rapporté une graine de cactus: I brought her back a cactus seed from the dwarves, from Fire Mountain. For transport, I took the cactus along too. Bad idea. I sat on it when I landed. Noisette pulled out thirty-two spines. I went “fffwoosh” every time. It was very brave.
textes.Je lui ai taillé un peigne dans une bran: I carved her a comb from a branch of my kapok tree. Fallen, not cut. Free. It's the only free thing I've made in twenty-two years. She wears it in her hair. It pleases me. A little.
textes.Je lui ai tourné une cruche avec une bal: I threw him a jug with a whale in relief, spout and all. He doesn't use it. He doesn't fill it, he doesn't drink from it: he looks at it. It's on his windowsill, facing the sea. “So she can see the others,” he says. He's silly. She's pretty, my whale.
textes.Je lui ai vendu des graines de courges g: I sold her giant squash seeds. They gave normal squash. She came to complain. I measured a squash with my arms: “A little canoe. For a child.” She laughed. I refunded half. I'd never refunded anyone. I don't know what came over me. It was the laugh, I think.
textes.Je lui ai vendu mes cartes des fonds mar: I sold him my charts of the seabed one by one, one a day. He came back every morning, pretended to browse, then: “And that south-west one, there, how much?” In the end, he had them all. My window was empty. I never told him I'd kept the drafts. To read them over with him.
textes.Je lui ai vendu un bouclier pour la Gard: I sold him a shield for the Guard. The sturdiest one on the stall. It took two guards to carry it. Pyrus came back to complain. I told him: “Nothing gets through it.” He answered: “Not even the guards.” I offered him a lighter, less sturdy model. He preferred to keep the first.
textes.Je lui ai vendu une conque, « la conque: I sold her a conch, “the conch of Ehécatl, the one that set the sun turning”. She blew into it, in front of the whole square. It squeaked. Like a mouse. It was a lake snail shell. She laughed so hard she had to sit down on her drum. She kept it. She never asked me for a refund. I don't understand.
textes.Je lui ai vendu une potion pour que sa p: I sold her a potion to make her dough rise faster. I'd written “three drops” on the label. She read “three spoonfuls”. The dough rose up to the kitchen ceiling, and she served a pie as tall as a stool. She says it's my fault. I say my potion works very well.
textes.Je lui ai vendu une tisane en fiole, tou: I sold her a herbal tea in a vial, all ready to drink, a magnificent blue. She told me she'd found it “interesting”. That summer, her tomatoes were blue. Huge and blue. She gave me a basketful, without a word. I didn't ask anything. They were delicious. I'm thinking about it, for the shop.
textes.Je lui ai écrit dix-sept lettres pour la: I wrote her seventeen letters begging her to lower her voice. Mademoiselle Brindille delivered them one by one. Madame Hurla read them out on the square, aloud, with feeling. The whole town knows my prose. I am quoted at the market. I have never been so embarrassed, nor, I confess, so widely read.
textes.Je lui apprends le départ comme une flèc: I'm teaching her the off-like-an-arrow start, in Mum and Dad's vegetable garden. We get into position between the carrot rows, I say “Hop!”… and she's already gone. Before the hop. Every time. Mum yells that we're squashing the leeks. Mochi yells “I win!”. And me, I'm running after a six-year-old bunny. That's new.
textes.Je lui apprends le métier : compter les: I'm teaching him the trade: counting sails, telling a brig from a sloop, smelling rain before it comes. The other day, he shouted “Whale!” and the whole crew ran to port. It was a whale. A real one! I was so proud I nearly fell. Me, it took me three years to see one.
textes.Je lui apprends à attendre le virage. Ne: I'm teaching her to wait for the bend. Don't start too fast. Wait. Then give everything. … She said: “Like Grandpa with the float?” … Yes. Like Grandpa. … I'd never thought of that.
textes.Je lui apprends à retenir son souffle, p: I'm teaching her to hold her breath, for the day she goes out. We count together in front of the Gate. She's up to forty. I told her I could last three hundred. It's… a goal. Yesterday, at a hundred and twelve, I pretended I had sand in my throat.
textes.Je lui avais annoncé une traversée avec: I'd foretold him a crossing with a beautiful stranger with golden eyes. He shaved, he put on a clean shirt. It was a goat, for Sauge's garden. With magnificent golden eyes, I stand by it. I never said it was a woman. He didn't speak to me for a week. The goat adores him.
textes.Je lui avais demandé un poisson, sur ma: I'd asked her for a fish, on my sail. A small, discreet one. She painted a three-metre purple octopus, with eyes that follow you while you row. That month, I caught two sardines. She says the fish just need to get used to it. They've been getting used to it for three years.
textes.Je lui avais garanti que Rhubarbe était: I'd guaranteed her that Rhubarbe was perfectly trained. He opened his beak, looked at her, and said: “Old sardine.” I thought I'd end up in the bay. The captain smiled. A tiny little smile, on the side of her scar. She paid double. Since then, Rhubarbe has learned all her curses. He says them in her accent.
textes.Je lui avais prédit une grande découvert: I'd predicted a great discovery for him. The next day, he searched the whole island for his glasses. They were on his nose. I told him: for a man who looks so far away, seeing what's under his nose is a very great discovery. He thought about it for a long time. Then he thanked me. He's an honest man.
textes.Je lui commande des rythmes « pour faire: I order rhythms from him “to bring in the sea bream”. He says there's no rhythm for sea bream. I say he just hasn't found it yet. So every afternoon he tries a new one on the table, and every morning I sing it at sea. So far, only sardines. But we're working on it.
textes.Je lui dis tous les jours. Il n'écoute p: I tell it every day. It doesn't listen.
textes.Je lui dois le « Traité des flammes douc: I've owed her the “Treatise on Gentle Flames” for sixty-three years. Every year, on the same date, I receive a little card in her hand: “Dear Professor, the book awaits you. No hurry.” I keep them all in a drawer. There are sixty-three. Each one is a little funnier than the last.
textes.Je lui garde un tabouret près de l'enclu: I keep a stool for him by the anvil. He tells stories, I hammer, the customers stay for both. I forged him a walking stick, with a moon on the handle. Left it against his door, without a word. He told the story of the walking stick to the whole village. Three days. Hm.
textes.Je lui grille toujours des « sardines sp: I always grill her “special sardines”, just for her. She watches them, she counts them. They're exactly the same as the others, out of the same crate. But I put them in the left corner of the grill. The captains' corner. That changes everything.
textes.Je lui laisse mes noix de coco vides sur: I leave her my empty coconuts on the low wall, and she makes flowerpots out of them. Now there are flowering coconuts all along the street, right down to the ferry terminal. The tourists think it's an old Port-Azur tradition. We don't set them straight.
textes.Je lui porte le minerai des pentes rouge: I've been bringing him ore from the red slopes for two hundred years. He weighs it, sniffs it, says “Hmph, that'll do”, and pays me three coins less than agreed. In the evening, at the Mug, he buys me a fizz. Three coins, the fizz. We never talk about it.
textes.Je lui rapporte des tisanes du village,: I bring her herbal teas from the village, verbena from the hills, in a paper cone. I put them on her bench and slip away. Why? You can't give back a fiancé with verbena, I know. But you try anyway, for fifty years.
textes.Je lui rapporte le miel sauvage d'en hau: I bring her the wild honey from the top of the Mother Tree. The bees don't like it. Neither do I. But when I come down, she's already set the first loaf aside. The best one. She thinks I don't notice she gives me the best one. I notice everything.
textes.Je lui répondrais : pour un matelot qui: I'd answer: for a sailor who laughed just right. Then I'd go and have my herbal tea, at the exact hour, like a well-regulated lady.
textes.Je lui tends des pièges. « Deux daurades: I set traps for her. “Two sea bream, Inès? Does your guest like lemon?” She answers: “I'm very hungry on Fridays.” “What time does he come?” “I eat early.” She never blushes, never! A stone, that woman. A beautiful stone, but a stone. If it were me, I'd have confessed everything by the second fish.
textes.Je m'appelle Ix Sak : la Blanche. Mais t: My name is Ix Sak: the White One. But all through my childhood, I had blue fingers! My mother dyed with indigo, and I dipped my hands in all her pots. The children called me “Ix Sak the Blue”. My mother laughed: “She has the name of one colour and the hands of another.” Today, my hands are every colour. The name, I kept.
textes.Je m'appelle Kinich, comme Kinich Ahau,: My name is Kinich, like Kinich Ahau, the sun god! Well, I'm a little sun. My parents work in the milpa, the maize field, all day long. So I go everywhere in Yaxché: the ball court, the market, the temple, the bees. Mum says I shine brightest when I'm up to mischief.
textes.Je m'assois un instant. La foudre, ça fa: I'll sit down for a moment. Lightning is tiring.
textes.Je m'assois, je m'assois. Il était une f: I'm sitting, I'm sitting. Once upon a time…
textes.Je m'en doutais : tu as les yeux de quel: I suspected as much: you have the eyes of someone who counts stars. Moon tea, three drops of honey, and put your thoughts down beside the bed. They'll wait for you.
I thought so. The horns, probably. Then tell them about Pandémonia: our lanterns, our cakes, our puppies that breathe fire… just a little. They won't be afraid of us any more.
textes.Je m'en doutais. Tous les joueurs disent: I suspected as much. All gamblers say that, and they all end up the same way: here, at my table, with empty pockets. Do sit… sit down. I was expecting you.
textes.Je m'ennuie. Thalion ne veut pas m'appre: I'm bored. Thalion won't teach me archery. He says Sylwen's door never recovered.
textes.Je m'entraîne la nuit, quand tout le mon: I train at night, when everyone's dancing. Bondi thinks nobody knows. Everybody knows.
I train at night. During the party. In secret. … Everybody knows. I live with Brume. We don't talk. It's good. Before every race, Caramel saves me a skewer. The biggest. Myrtille wants to run like me. She counts my laps on her fingers. She gets it wrong. I don't correct her.
textes.Je m'entraîne le matin, je bois un cacao: I train in the morning, I drink a cacao at Ix Chab's at noon, if she'll serve me, and I go back to the court. In the evening, I dance at the Venus platform with my blue hips. Kinich copies all my moves. Ix Sak sews my feathers. Balam looks at me sideways. And Ah Kin Pech counts my bumps.
textes.Je m'entraîne à l'aube, je fais ma ronde: I train at dawn, I do my rounds at the tianguis, I train again. In the evening, I dance in the square when Nenetl plays. Up there, on the slopes of Smoking Mountain, two jaguars took one of Xóchitl's animals. I want to hunt them. The high priest says to wait for the right day. I'm waiting. I don't like waiting.
I'm practising scrubbing for your ship. That way, the day you take me on as cabin boy, I'll be ready.
textes.Je m'entraîne. Le souffle, c'est comme l: I'm training. Breath is like friendship: you have to keep it up.
textes.Je m'occupe du jardin. Il me le rend bie: I'm looking after the garden. It pays me back nicely.
textes.Je m'échappe parfois du palais par le ja: Sometimes I slip out of the palace through the garden to buy fire cinnamon at Zébuline's. Pyrus follows twenty paces behind, pretending to inspect the cobblestones. Clang, clang, clang. The merchants nudge each other. I pretend not to hear him. It's our little play, and the whole market knows the lines.
I mostly fight with my bare hands.
textes.Je me demande parfois si ce n'est pas un: Sometimes I wonder if it isn't a jar of fig jam. Don't tell Madame Colette. She'd raise the price. Or worse: she'd sell it to me.
textes.Je me lève avant Rê, je chauffe le four,: I get up before Rê, I heat the oven, I sell the bread, I brew the beer, and in the evening I serve the whole village. Amenemhat reads and spills things, Khéty tells his fish stories doubled, Hapou pays in onions. And me, I listen. That's how I know everything. People tell a brewer everything. Especially after the second jar.
textes.Je me lève avant l'aube. Je croise Nox q: I get up before dawn. I pass Nox on his way to bed, and I give him his mint. Some mornings, I go and pick mushrooms in the Ash Wood. I sing to my peppers, I chase Flammèche's puppies with my broom, and at noon I have a nap. At my age, a nap is like any other plant: it needs tending.
textes.Je me lève à cinq heures, je pêche au po: I get up at five, I fish off the pontoon, I sell at the slipway, I mend my nets on the beach, and in the evening we light the fire with the others. Sometimes, when I wake up, there are shells laid on my boat. The mist folk, Lucie says. I say thank you out loud. You never know who's listening.
textes.Je me lève à cinq heures. J'inspecte l'a: I rise at five. I inspect the silverware, I count the candles, I have my horns polished on Mondays at Monsieur Tiburce's, and I fetch the brioches from Monsieur Bobor at noon. I measure each brioche with a silver ruler. They are all the same height. Except one. Always one. I suspect Monsieur Bobor.
textes.Je me lève à trois heures. Je pétris, je: I get up at three. I knead, I sing, I taste. At dawn, I give the first brioche to Grandpa Ébène in exchange for a story. At noon, Asmodin measures my brioches with his silver ruler. At four o'clock, a brioche breaks by accident for Pépin. In the evening, I go and float at the Baths. I float very well.
textes.Je me pose une question depuis des jours: I've been asking myself a question for days. Do you think you can forgive everything?
I'm moving. In the name of the city.
textes.Je me repose au soleil. Ne me fais pas d: I'm resting in the sun. Don't block my light.
textes.Je me repose un peu. Les jambes, ça s'us: I'm having a little rest. Legs wear out, you know.
textes.Je me réveille doucement. Le matin, je s: I'm waking up slowly. I'm slow in the mornings.
textes.Je me souviens de toi. Tu es le premier: I remember you. You're the first visitor in a thousand years.
textes.Je me suis assis devant la forge de Bori: I sat down in front of Borin's forge and never left. Thirty days. Ash rained down, I stayed put. On the thirtieth, he handed me a broom. Twelve years later, I'm allowed to hold the tongs. And to hammer, sometimes. When he's not looking. Or when he pretends not to look.
textes.Je me suis endormi contre la stèle, un m: One morning I fell asleep against the stela. I woke up with the date of creation printed on my cheek. Nobody said a thing. I gave my lesson all morning. In the evening, Ix Kanul came by and said: “Lovely lesson, Ah Kin. Very… visible.” I only understood when I washed my face.
textes.Je me suis endormi un jour au milieu de: One day I fell asleep in the middle of the story of the owl who had lost his night. When I woke up, there was a flower on my nose, and Nimiel had finished the story for me, in front of the whole circle. Her ending was better than mine. That's how I tell it now.
textes.Je me suis réveillé à minuit : le lac fu: I woke up at midnight: the lake was steaming like a cooking pot. She was in the middle, in hot water up to her chin, with a woolly hat on, and all the fish huddled round her. She waved at me. Waved. I stood on the bank in my nightshirt. It took three days to freeze the lake again.
textes.Je me suis un peu perdu dans le Bois de: I got a little bit lost in the Ash Wood the other day. Not a lot! Just a little. Now Mum holds my hand at the market. So embarrassing. But kind of nice, too.
textes.Je me tiens derrière sa chaise quand il: I stand behind his chair when he plays. I tap the table with my hook. Tick, tick. Out of habit. Sylvain thinks it's a signal. Ignace swears it's a tic. Me, I say nothing. People wonder. I like it when other people are the ones asking questions.
textes.Je me trompe exprès, Fatima. Pour t'ente: I get it wrong on purpose, Fatima. To hear you.
textes.Je mets mes babouches que pendant le qua: I only wear my slippers on night watch. One night, the captain was pacing the deck and stepped on a slipper in the dark. He yelled “THE CAT!” and pulled out his sabre. I crawled over and got the slipper back. The next day, he was telling everyone he'd nearly caught the ginger cat with his bare hands. I didn't say anything.
textes.Je mets un peu d'argent de côté pour ouv: I'm putting a bit of money aside to open a little guesthouse, one day. With just three rooms. And I won't make the beds.
I'll put in a dotted line, meanwhile.
I'll come up tonight. I'll bring the tea.
textes.Je monte parfois au phare avec deux tass: Sometimes I climb up to the lighthouse with two cups of coffee. Three hundred and twenty steps: at the two-hundredth, I sit down. He lets me in without a word. One night, he beckoned me over to the lantern and pointed west. Nothing at first. Then, very far off, under the water, a blue dot. He didn't say a word. Neither did I. For once.
textes.Je mouds le maïs avant l'aube, je fais l: I grind the maize before dawn, I make the flatbreads, and I sell my cacao all day. Chak comes by at noon with his ball: I keep an eye on him. Ah Kin Pech pays me one bean short. Yum Kab sells his honey far too cheap. In the evening, I sit in the square with Ix Sak and tell her everything. It rests the arms.
textes.Je n'achète plus rien chez toi. Depuis l: I'm not buying anything from you any more. Not since the tablecloth.
textes.Je n'ai aucune photo de ma mère. Elle es: I don't have a single photo of my mother. She left when I was four, and her face fades a little more every year. I still have her laugh, just about. So I photograph everyone, all the time. So that nobody here ever fades. Don't tell the others, {surnom}. They'd pose far too seriously.
textes.Je n'ai jamais dit le contraire. Plus ja: I never said otherwise. Never again.
textes.Je n'ai jamais dit à la reine Oriane que: I never told Queen Oriane I'd lost her branch. And the worst thing, {surnom}… is that without it, I don't even know if I really have a gift. Maybe the wand was the magician. Not me. Don't tell anyone. Not even me.
textes.Je n'ai jamais dormi dans aucune de nos: I've never slept in a single one of our rooms. Yet I know them all by heart.
textes.Je n'ai jamais eu de petits, et pourtant: I never had cubs, and yet all of Ramure calls me Mother. I took Brume as my pupil, I knitted Croc-Gris's red scarf, and every spring I put the moon lanterns back on the bridges. This year, my paws won't take me to the edge of the ponds any more. So in the evening, on my moss, at the Circle, I watch Lilas dance. That's my way of lighting lanterns now.
textes.Je n'ai jamais pris le bateau, alors je: I've never taken the boat, so I give Fanny my messages for the other island. “Say hello to the harbour.” “Tell the lighthouse it blinks nicely.” She comes back the next day and tells me, very seriously: “The lighthouse thanks you.” I know she's making it up. But she says it so seriously that it does me good.
textes.Je n'ai jamais vendu un tapis au premier: I've never sold a carpet at the first price. Never. Once, a pirate paid without haggling. It made me ill for three days.
textes.Je n'ai jamais vu Zélie, alors je l'imag: I've never seen Zélie, so I imagine her. Tall, with aviator goggles on her forehead and a pencil behind her ear. She sends me “theoretical” timetables. I correct her addresses: “Ramure has no streets, Commander: it has trees.” She replied: “Noted. Which tree?” We're making progress.
textes.Je n'ai pas de fils, {surnom}. Le bâton: I have no son, {surnom}. The amin's staff, one day, will have to be handed on. I'd like it to be Ahmed. He laughs, he listens, the fleet loves him, and he always comes home. But I've never told him. Saying it would be admitting I'm old. So I watch him pass the jetty every morning, and I keep quiet. Like Driss.
I don't have an octopus, Protée.
textes.Je n'ai pas encore sommeil. Alors je tra: I'm not sleepy yet. So I'm hanging about a bit.
I didn't need to knock, then.
I don't have time to sleep.
textes.Je n'ai pas le temps, Bulle. J'étiquette: I don't have time, Bulle. I'm labelling.
I didn't say anything about the watering can.
I have nothing better to offer you.
textes.Je n'ai rien demandé, ma petite ! … Quat: I didn't ask anything, my girl! … Four hundred and ten?
I didn't say a thing! Yellow, size thirty-seven.
I didn't say a thing, my dear.
I said nothing. I saw nothing.
textes.Je n'aime pas les chiens, Flammèche ! Pa: I don't like dogs, Flammèche! Not one bit!
textes.Je n'archive pas les versions, Protée. J: I don't archive versions, Protée. I archive facts.
textes.Je n'avais ni père ni mère, seulement le: I had neither father nor mother, only the port. In the evening, I'd sit at the edge of the great Sidi Belaïd's halqa, so close he trod on my feet. I gave nothing at the end: I had nothing. When I was twelve, he stopped in the middle of a tale and said to me: “You. Tomorrow, you carry my stool.” I carried his stool for thirteen years.
I've only got one good one.
textes.Je n'ose pas vous le demander. Je vous l: I don't dare ask you. I'm asking you anyway. Can I come with you? I'll read during the journeys, I'll hardly talk, and I'll zap the monsters. Especially the monsters. Almost always the monsters. If you'd like, just tell me. I'll be at the Guild.
textes.Je n'oublie jamais. Mais d'accord pour l: I never forget. But I'll take the fizz.
I don't know anything about it.
I had nothing to do with it. I swear.
textes.Je ne chante pas. Je ne me bats pas. Je: I don't sing. I don't fight. I guard.
textes.Je ne cours pas, Frère Cendrin ! Je marc: I'm not running, Brother Cendrin! I'm walking fast!
I don't run. I patrol quickly.
textes.Je ne crois pas à ses cartes. Mais depui: I don't believe in her cards. But since then, when a stranger crosses the square, I watch him. His hands, mostly. The other day, I followed a tourist with my eyes all the way to the fountain. He turned round. I pretended to look for my glasses. They were on my nose.
I won't say a word, my dear.
textes.Je ne dis ça qu'à toi. Une nuit, au-dess: I'm only telling you this. One night, above a ring of white mushrooms, I saw a little light dancing. When I told Thalion, he went quite pale and forbade me to shoot. He's never said why. He's been hiding something for a long time. I could look into it. I don't. For once.
textes.Je ne dors jamais. À cause de toi, juste: I never sleep. Because of you, as it happens.
textes.Je ne dors pas bien dans le silence, {su: I don't sleep well in silence, {surnom}. In Cliquetis, everything goes tick-tock, all night long. Here, nothing. My father gave me a little mechanical bird when I left. I wind it up every evening, under my pillow. It ticks until morning. Nobody knows. Mirabelle thinks it's one of her potions making noise.
textes.Je ne dors pas, maîtresse ! Je réfléchis: I'm not asleep, miss! I'm thinking with my eyes closed!
textes.Je ne dors pas. Je surveille la ville av: I'm not sleeping. I'm watching the town with my eyes closed.
textes.Je ne dors plus beaucoup. Je regarde le: I don't sleep much any more. I watch the crystal grow pale, and Nausicaa sings me my mother's lullaby. Abyssos keeps an eye on my lamp from under my windows; he thinks I don't see him. In the morning, Marée brings me a warm cracker. It tastes of the first night. Strange, the things that can comfort a queen.
textes.Je ne fais que du blanc, {surnom}. Tout: I only make white, {surnom}. Everyone knows that. But in my chest, under the sheets, there's a red and yellow belt that Ix Sak wove for me, in Yaxché. In the evening, when Nebet is asleep, I put it on. And I dance a little, all alone, between the looms. White is my work. Colour is my secret. Keep it safe.
textes.Je ne fais que passer. À bientôt !: I'm just passing through. See you soon!
textes.Je ne l'ai avoué à personne, {surnom}. P: I've never admitted it to anyone, {surnom}. Not even to Léa. The ring was too big: she got the size wrong, and she was so proud that I didn't dare tell her. I'd wedged it with a cotton thread, wound round the inside. In the waves, the thread gave way. It was my fault, and not my fault at all. Both at once. Inès guessed, I think. Nobody else.
textes.Je ne l'ai dit à personne, {surnom}. Ce: I've never told anyone, {surnom}. That morning, near the sunken rooftops, I heard singing. Not a whale. A voice. A woman singing the way my grandmother sang underwater. That's what scared me. Not the dark, not the depth: that someone down there was singing my grandmother's song.
textes.Je ne l'ai dit à personne, {surnom}. J'a: I haven't told anyone, {surnom}. I still have my return ticket in my pocket. Every morning I touch it. I'm scared it'll be like the piano and the pottery: that one day I'll get bored and leave. I don't want to. For the first time in my life, I don't want to. So I keep the ticket. To check that I'm not using it.
textes.Je ne l'ai dit à personne, {surnom}. L'é: I've never told anyone, {surnom}. The star “Cliquetis”, I wasn't the first to see it. It was Margot, at the telescope. She said: “That one's twinkling.” I announced it to the Academy on my own. In my notebook, it isn't called Cliquetis. It's called Margot. I've never told her. I'm ashamed of it, every clear night.
textes.Je ne l'ai dit à personne, {surnom}. La: I've never told anyone, {surnom}. The night the lightning struck the crater, I was up there. It came from the south, from the sky, not from the mountain. I saw the golems open their eyes, one by one. And I ran. A scout who runs. My uncle thinks I was down below. I let him think so.
textes.Je ne l'ai dit à personne, {surnom}. Pas: I haven't told anyone, {surnom}. Not even Rachid. I wove a copy of the captain's carpet, tiny, the size of my hand. It's sewn into a cushion on my bench. I don't know why I made it. I tell myself it's curiosity. But in the evening, I'm afraid it's something else. A longing for gold.
textes.Je ne l'ai jamais dit à personne, {surno: I've never told anyone, {surnom}. Not even Gaston. The day before the shipwreck, on my draft, there was a tiny black dot, right on our course. I thought it was a biscuit crumb. I didn't copy it out. Twenty-two years I've been shouting that my map was right. It was. Give or take a crumb.
textes.Je ne l'ai jamais raconté, {surnom}. Une: I've never told anyone, {surnom}. One night, after two days on watch, I fell asleep standing up, leaning on my shield. The king walked by. In the morning, I had his red cloak around my shoulders. He never mentioned it again. Since then, I never sleep on watch. Never. For him.
I haven't forgotten it. I'm keeping it.
textes.Je ne le dirai qu'une fois, {surnom}. Le: I'll only say this once, {surnom}. The day after the shipwreck, the sea left a leather case at the foot of my kapok tree. Inside: the helm's map. It's been under my anvil for twenty-two years. I've never unrolled it. If the rock is on it, I'm to blame. If it isn't, he is. I don't know which would hurt me more.
textes.Je ne le vise pas, capitaine. Je l'entra: I'm not aiming at it, captain. I'm training it.
textes.Je ne les compte plus. C'est eux qui me: I don't count them anymore. They're the ones who count me, in the evening.
I can't read maps, I get lost.
textes.Je ne lui ai pas encore demandé. Hm. Bie: I haven't asked her yet. Hm. Soon. Maybe.
textes.Je ne lui parle pas beaucoup de son papa: I don't talk to her much about her dad. I'm afraid of crying into the dough, and the bread would be too salty. She has his wooden spoon, Cerfeuil's, all black at the end. At night, she holds it tight to fall asleep. I pretend not to see. I can do that too.
textes.Je ne lui vends plus de camomille. La de: I don't sell him camomile anymore. Last time, he made a “sleeping” potion out of it that blew the door off L'Alambic. The whole village woke up. Camomile is for sleeping, little one, not for waking up the village. Now I sell him lemon balm. It explodes less. A bit less.
textes.Je ne mange pas. Je viens pour l'odeur d: I don't eat. I come for the smell of ginger. It's very highly rated.
textes.Je ne me bats jamais. J'ai des amis pour: I never fight. I have friends for that. (Two pirates stand up.)
textes.Je ne me bats pas, moi. La capitaine l'a: I don't fight. The captain said so: “The cabin boy doesn't fight.” So when there's a brawl, I count the punches. Yesterday I counted forty-three.
textes.Je ne me bats pas, moi. Mais j'ai des am: I don't fight, me. But I've got friends who do. Lots of friends.
I never get tired of this view.
I'm staying out of your business.
textes.Je ne me perds JAMAIS. Je fais des détou: I NEVER get lost. I take detours.
I don't turn around anymore. I walk backwards.
textes.Je ne note rien ! Je… respire. Avec une: I'm not writing anything! I'm… breathing. With a quill.
textes.Je ne pars qu'avec un aventurier inscrit: I only go with an adventurer registered at the Guild. It's the rule! (Églantine made me sign it. Twice.)
textes.Je ne promets rien, chère amie. Vous bri: I promise nothing, dear friend. You shine.
textes.Je ne rate jamais un sort. Mais je les l: I never botch a spell. But I cast them slowly. Pyra says I throw fireballs the way you write a letter. I think it's a compliment.
I'm not laughing! Here, a sugared petal. For the road.
I don't know what that means.
I don't know how to run slowly.
textes.Je ne sais pas encore, Calcine. On verra: I don't know yet, Calcine. We'll see as we go.
I don't remember where I come from.
textes.Je ne savais pas qu'elle tenait taverne: I didn't know she ran a tavern here. I walked into La Murène Ivre like a conqueror and ordered a rum. The landlady served me and said: “Still swim like a wet dog?” I dropped my glass. Since then, she serves me in an old glass kept aside, engraved with an “S”. I asked her why. She poured me another.
textes.Je ne suis pas d'humeur à plaisanter. Ma: I'm not in the mood for jokes. But I'll make one anyway: you. Hmph.
textes.Je ne suis pas difficile. Une conversati: I'm easy to please. A chat is enough for me.
textes.Je ne suis pas gros. Je suis rempli d'am: I'm not fat. I'm full of love. And apples.
textes.Je ne suis pas petit ! Je suis capitaine: I'm not little! I'm a captain!
textes.Je ne suis pas sorcière, moi. Le seul so: I'm no witch, me. The only spell I know is pumpkin tart. But believe me, it bewitches everyone.
I'm not your master anymore, Glaucos.
I'm not your master any more.
textes.Je ne t'ai pas oublié : la prochaine bal: I haven't forgotten you: the next whale is yours. Keep your eye on the Skala.
textes.Je ne t'ai rien demandé. Un nain demande: I didn't ask you for anything. A dwarf rarely asks.
I didn't ask you anything… not yet.
textes.Je ne te suis pas. Je vais dans la même: I'm not following you. I'm going in the same direction as you. There's a difference.
textes.Je ne triche jamais. Je n'en ai pas beso: I never cheat. I don't need to. The dice know who feeds them. (He snaps his fingers. Two burly fellows stand up at the back of the room.) I'd advise you to take that back.
I don't want to know, Agathe.
textes.Je ne vois pas mon dos, alors j'ai deman: I can't see my back, so I asked Scarlett what Coralie had drawn on me. She looked for a long, long time, and she said: “A magnificent horse.” I was so proud I bought a round for the whole Crâne Fendu. Coralie was shouting “It's an octopus!”, but nobody listened. Hic! Jealous, the lot of them.
textes.Je ne vois rien de tel dans ton sac. Une: I don't see anything like that in your bag. A Ventaile feather, a naga scale, a shark tooth… that's all I'm interested in.
textes.Je ne vous ai jamais inscrit au registre: I've never entered you in the register. So, for the record: are you moored here, passing through, or lost?
textes.Je ne vous ai rien demandé ! … Pas encor: I didn't ask you anything! … Not yet today.
I didn't ask you for anything.
textes.Je note : une mouette-voile. Par la quil: Writing it down: one seagull-sail. By the keel!
I'm writing: “The king is in a good mood.”
textes.Je note : « un rubis, sorti ». Comme hie: I'm writing: “one ruby, out”. Same as yesterday. And my thank you?
textes.Je note toutes ses prédictions dans un p: I write all her predictions in a little red notebook, with the date, to catch her out one day. Thirty-seven predictions. Thirty-four wrong. Three right. Including one about me. I won't say which. Three is too many. It keeps me awake at night.
textes.Je note « bleu ». Tu as les sourcils int: I'm writing “blue”. Your eyebrows are intact.
textes.Je note « gris ». Avec un point d'interr: I'm writing “grey”. With a question mark.
textes.Je note. Mais elle est toujours au nord-: I'm writing. But is it still to the north-west?
textes.Je note. Mais je mets un point d'interro: I'm writing it down. But with a question mark.
textes.Je nourris toute la terrasse. Cent nains: I feed the whole terrace. A hundred dwarves, a hundred stomachs, a hundred opinions about the salt.
textes.Je paie Pomme-de-Pin en pièces, comme to: I pay Pomme-de-Pin in coins, like everyone. Except she doesn't know what to do with them. So she drilled holes in them and hung them under the west bridge, where they jingle in the wind. When my uncle saw that, he threw a fit: “Coins! Under a bridge!” Me, I think it's the prettiest safe in Ramure.
textes.Je paie l'Amiral une graine de tournesol: I pay the Admiral one sunflower seed per rhythm he gets right. He's already earned forty-three. Gaspard keeps the seeds in a little bag on his belt and raises a finger each time: one seed. One day, the Admiral managed a rhythm I can't play myself. I gave him two. And my pride along with them.
textes.Je paie ma bière en oignons, une botte p: I pay for my beer in onions, one bunch per jar. One evening, one was missing. I went back to my field, on the other side of the river, in the middle of the night, with the crocodiles. I found it, I brought it back. Mérit said I was mad. No. A debt is a debt. Even an onion.
textes.Je paie mes punchs avec les pièces de mo: I pay for my punches with my great-grandfather's coins. Toni never has change. So he opened a “gold” tab, where he notes what he owes me. To thank him, I gave him a cork from my collection: the one from the bottle opened at a king's coronation. He put it on the shelf, next to the parrot.
textes.Je paie mon cacao en fèves, et je les co: I pay for my cacao in beans, and I count them myself: it's my job. Ix Chab recounts them after me. There's always one missing. Just one! I explained that the moon, that month, had one day less. She replied that the moon doesn't drink cacao. Since then, I pay one bean extra. For the moon.
I'd bet my wooden leg… er, no.
I bet it came from an airship.
textes.Je parie que oui. Hou… Je l'espère. Si e: I bet it is. Hoo… I hope so. If it weren't, I'd tell no one. Except you, perhaps.
I bet you can't even swim.
I was talking to the mackerel, me.
I was talking to the fish, me.
textes.Je parle à mes poissons. Ils ne réponden: I talk to my fish. They don't answer. Well, hardly ever.
textes.Je pars à l'aube, je vends à midi, je re: I leave at dawn, I sell at noon, I fish again in the afternoon. In between, I ferry Néferet across to the other bank, to the valley temple. In the evening, I drink a beer at Mérit's and tell the story of my day, doubling it. And one day in ten, on the rest day, I teach Nebet to cast a line. She throws everything back.
textes.Je partage la maison de l'arbre des mare: I share the house in the pond tree with Grelot, my best friend; she dances behind me at the Circle and makes me laugh. Pépin drums too hard, Bourru too slowly: together, it's just the right rhythm. Roux plays the flute. And Mother Moon watches me from her moss. When I dance, I feel all their eyes on me, like lanterns.
textes.Je passais au large, sur un bateau de pê: I was passing offshore, on a fishing boat. Going somewhere, I forget where. I heard a speaker crackling, from out at sea. It bothered me. I asked them to drop me off. I fixed the speaker. With a fishbone. And I stayed. That was six years ago. The boat, I still don't know where it was going.
textes.Je passe devant son étal en revenant de: I walk past her stall on my way back from the jetty. I tell her my whale of the day, and as I leave, I turn back to smile at her. Once, turning back, I knocked over three bowls. Three! I paid in sardines. Since then, when I walk by, she says: “Careful when you turn around.” But she smiles.
textes.Je passe mes journées au bord du lac. J': I spend my days by the lake. I teach the young ones not to fear the cold, and not to run on the ice. At noon, I eat on my bench. In the evening, at Berthe's, my mild soup, at the table at the back. Once a year, Mathurin takes me out to sea. On Sundays, Sauge brings me herbal tea. I let it cool. A lot.
textes.Je passe mes journées derrière mon burea: I spend my days behind my desk, from eight in the morning to seven at night. I tidy, I catch, I say “shh”. Miss Lin reads at the back table, young Oscar holds his little bell, Mr Lumen snores on the atlas. In the evening, I dine at Berthe's, table four. And I reread. I've never finished rereading.
textes.Je passe toutes les semaines demander qu: Every week, I drop by to ask when the city's fleet will be ready. She answers: “When I say so.” I note the answer in my official notebook. I'm up to forty pages. One day, I brought her honey to encourage the work. She ate it. I considered it an agreement in principle.
textes.Je peins ce que je vois. Enfin, ce que j: I paint what I see. Well, what I'd like to see.
textes.Je peins des fresques sur les voiles des: I paint murals on boat sails. The one on the sound wall is mine. Well, the one that isn't done yet.
textes.Je peins des paysages. Je suis venue pou: I paint landscapes. I came for a week, two months ago. Every morning the light is different, so I stay.
textes.Je peins du matin au soir. Théo vient me: I paint from morning till night. Théo comes to watch me, Félix gets me to colour in his maps, and I pay Edmond for my room in paintings. In the evening, at the Perroquet, I draw Django, who's played in profile ever since I offended him. And there was that camera, near the bench. I left it there. Its owner might have been looking for it.
textes.Je peins. Ne regarde pas, ce n'est pas f: I'm painting. Don't look, it's not finished.
textes.Je pense encore à tes noix pleines d'eau: I'm still thinking about your nuts full of water. A nut you can drink! I can't sleep for it, {surnom}.
textes.Je pense souvent à lui dire la vraie rec: I often think about telling him the real recipe. No honey, no cinnamon, no three hours: embers, six minutes, and cumin. One day I'll tell him. The day he stops coming to ask me “a bit more honey?” with his shining eyes. In other words… never, maybe. He looks so happy.
textes.Je perce chaque motif à la main, trou ap: I pierce every pattern by hand, hole after hole. When you light the candle, the patterns settle on the walls. It's like taking the stars home with you.
textes.Je peux avoir du gâteau quand même ?: Can I have some cake anyway?
textes.Je peux courir la Grande Course ?: Can I run the Great Race?
textes.Je peux donner un coup de pioche ?: Can I take a swing with the pickaxe?
textes.Je peux essayer le casque ?: Can I try on the helmet?
textes.Je peux faire le crabe amoureux ?: Can I do the Crab in Love?
textes.Je peux t'aider pour la fièvre ?: Can I help with the fever?
textes.Je peux te prendre en photo ? Rien qu'un: Can I take your photo? Just one. I promise I won't show it to anyone.
textes.Je peux vous aider pour la fête ?: Can I help you with the festival?
textes.Je peux vous aider pour le tajine ?: Can I help you with the tagine?
textes.Je peux vous demander quelque chose ? Vo: Can I ask you something? Do you believe in signs?
textes.Je peux écouter un disque ?: Can I listen to a record?
textes.Je photographiais chaque assiette avant: I photographed every plate before eating it. Monday's bouillabaisse, Tuesday's… Paulo asked me why. I said: “So I don't forget.” He wiped away a tear with his apron. Since then, he arranges my plate like a work of art, with a sprig of fennel on top. My trousers don't forget anything either.
textes.Je plaisante ! Je les ai payés ! … Presq: I'm joking! I paid for them! … Almost all of them.
textes.Je pleure pas, c'est le sable. Et c'est: I'm not crying, it's the sand. And I'm the boss of the castle.
I'll dive. But you owe me a crêpe.
textes.Je porte les lettres d'arbre en arbre, d: I carry letters from tree to tree, from cabin to cabin. I know every door in Ramure. And every secret. But a postmistress never tells. Hoo.
textes.Je porte les messages entre les îles. Si: I carry messages between the islands. If one day you hear the wind whistle your name, that's me.
I carry her letters to her sister, down below. On the way there, they're heavy with advice; on the way back, Brindille's are heavy with tears. Once, to practise reading fast, I read hers out loud while flying. Every seagull heard it. She didn't speak to me for a whole season. I didn't notice straight away.
textes.Je porte. Tu portes. Il porte. Je suis l: I carry. You carry. He carries. I'm the only one who carries, actually.
textes.Je pose encore un chapeau devant la scèn: I still put a hat in front of the stage, like my grandfather. In the evening, it fills up. A bit too much. I know it's Toni slipping coins into it when I close my eyes during a solo. He thinks I don't see a thing. So I play with my eyes closed, on purpose, so he can. We both pretend.
textes.Je pose une gourde d'eau de source sur l: I put a bottle of spring water on Mistral's table every hour. He pretends not to see it. So I stand there, I look at him, I nod. One night, it went on for four minutes. He drank it in one go, laughing, and played me a track he called “Water Bottle”. Not funny. I danced to it anyway.
textes.Je prenais le bateau chaque semaine pour: I used to take the boat every week for the Port-Azur croissants. The little apprentice danced behind the counter while giving change, and the coins flew everywhere. I did the crab step for her all the way to the door and told her: “Tonight, village beach.” She came. Now she only leaves to sleep.
textes.Je prends l'air avant de commencer ma jo: I'm getting some fresh air before starting my day.
textes.Je prends un jus de fruits, tranquilleme: I'm having a fruit juice, nice and easy.
I'm enjoying the cool evening air.
textes.Je profite du banc. Il est à tout le mon: I'm enjoying the bench. It belongs to everyone, but right now, it's mine.
I prefer to say so in advance.
I'd rather talk face to face.
textes.Je prépare le repas. Si tu restes, il y: I'm making a meal. If you stay, there'll be some for you.
textes.Je prépare les notes froides, Grand-père: I'm getting the cold notes ready, Grandpa Ébène.
textes.Je prépare ma robe pour la fête de l'Aub: I'm making my dress for the Dawn Festival. I'd need {manque} pearls to embroider it like dew. You find them in the sea, don't you?
textes.Je prépare un éclair… Reculez un peu, pa: I'm preparing a bolt… Stand back a little, just to be safe.
textes.Je pète la forme ! Regarde, je saute enc: I'm buzzing! Look, I can jump even higher than yesterday.
textes.Je pêche avec mon oncle Hamid. Il crie b: I fish with my uncle Hamid. He shouts a lot, he sings off-key, but he always finds the fish.
I fish what the sea gives.
textes.Je pêche à l'aube, je vends le matin, je: I fish at dawn, sell in the morning, watch the Arena fights in the afternoon, and reopen the stall until evening. I give the fish scraps to Flammèche's puppies and shout good morning to the Captain. In the evening, I sit at the Diable Repu, my husband's place, and tell him about my catch. He pretends to listen.
textes.Je pêche. Enfin, j'attends. La pêche, c': I'm fishing. Well, waiting. Fishing is mostly waiting.
textes.Je rachète le poisson de la surface ! Ic: I buy fish from the surface! Down here we don't fish: we talk to the fish. But a grilled mackerel… mmh.
textes.Je rachète les champignons, les baies, l: I buy mushrooms, berries, honey. Everything that grows ends up in a vial, sooner or later.
textes.Je racontais qu'un cercle de champignons: I used to tell how a ring of white mushrooms in the forest drew the firefly spirits. Orophin laughed. Then he went to look, seven nights in a row, without telling anyone. On the eighth, he came back quite pale: “There was a little light.” Since then he doesn't laugh at my stories. He takes notes.
textes.Je raconte aux enfants que les Neuf Cerc: I tell the children that the Nine Circles were dug by a giant with a spoon. Then Malachar comes along to explain the pickaxes, the plans and the thousand years of work. The children ask him: “So where's the spoon?” He doesn't know what to answer. I do: it's in the story.
textes.Je raconte ma fête de la mine à Gaspard: I tell Gaspard about my party in the mine; he sighs, he says he knows it by heart. But he never leaves before the end. He nods. Even when I add things. Especially when I add things. Gaspard likes stories more than he lets on. Like water.
textes.Je raconte à tous les touristes que le m: I tell every tourist that the mayor won at pétanque. They think I'm joking. So I pull my tape measure out of my pocket, show a centimetre between two fingers, and say: “That's democracy.” And I wink. Aristide, if he's around, laughs very loudly. A bit too loudly.
textes.Je raconte à tous mes clients que Margau: I tell all my customers that Margaux steals my croissants. Then that I'm the one stealing hers. Then that it's a joke. It makes them laugh. Except since that business with the night-time croissant thief. The first time, she looked at me with her bread peel in her hand. I stopped the joke. For a whole week.
textes.Je rapporte à Anouk les algues du fond,: I bring Anouk seaweed from the deep, the kind the tide never uncovers. Once, I brought her up a red seaweed that only grows on the carved stones. She smelled it for a long time and said: “It smells of rain.” She's still trying to work out what it's for. I think it's not for anything. Like beautiful things.
I mess up on purpose, for fun.
textes.Je rate tous mes sorts. Mais je les rate: I botch all my spells. But I botch them in original ways! The archmage says that's already a kind of talent. I think she's being kind.
textes.Je recommence à cent ! Comme d'habitude: I start again at a hundred! Like always!
textes.Je regardais seulement, grand prêtre ! A: I was only looking, high priest! With my eyes!
textes.Je regardais… le perroquet. Il est beau,: I was looking at… the parrot. It's a lovely parrot.
I am looking! Through the lens.
textes.Je regarde ce qui se passe. Il se passe: I'm watching what's going on. Something's always going on.
textes.Je regarde la mer. Elle est rouge, là-ba: I'm looking at the sea. It's red over there, by the waterfall. You get used to it.
textes.Je regarde le jour se lever. Ça ne se la: I'm watching the sunrise. Never gets old.
I'm looking at yours. It's pretty.
textes.Je regarde les étoiles. Tu connais leurs: I'm looking at the stars. Do you know their names?
textes.Je regarde passer les gens. C'est le mei: I'm watching people go by. It's the best show on the island, and it's free.
textes.Je regarde vos fiches…: Let me look at your files…
textes.Je regarde, mon grand ! Avec mes deux ye: I'm looking, big guy! With both my eyes!
I'm looking. I promise, I'm looking.
textes.Je remonte l'horloge depuis cinquante-de: I've been winding the clock for fifty-two years. My father did it before me. And his father before him.
textes.Je remplace Croc-Gris au Guet l'après-mi: I take over from Croc-Gris at the Watchtower in the afternoons. I watch the forest. OK, mostly I watch the Games Clearing. To see how Bondi trains.
textes.Je rends toujours la monnaie en objets i: I always give change in useless objects, that's the rule. One day, Firmin bought a spring from me, and I gave him a fan-hat as change. He left with it, baffled. The next day, he was wearing it at his stand. He said it cooled the engine. The engine, or Firmin, I didn't ask.
textes.Je rends toujours les livres avec une fl: I always return the books with a dried ember flower between two pages, to say thank you. One day, Ombreline showed me a big herbarium kept on the poetry shelf: all my flowers were there, pressed, with the date and the title of the book. Forty flowers. I couldn't say a thing. Neither could she. It was a very beautiful silence.
textes.Je rentre à la Guilde raconter nos explo: I'm off back to the Guild to tell of our exploits. I'll embellish them only a little.
I'll come back tomorrow for the reply.
I'll come back. With my shield.
textes.Je repense à ce que je t'ai confié l'aut: I keep thinking about what I told you the other day, my dream… You haven't told anyone, I hope?
textes.Je repense à ce que je vous ai confié l': I keep thinking about what I told you the other day, my dream… You haven't told anyone, I hope?
textes.Je reprends toujours deux assiettes de s: I always have a second bowl of her soup. To check if it's still too salty. It's always too salty. Sometimes I have a third, to be sure. Berthe says nothing. She smiles as she fills it. That woman smiles far too much.
I'll pick up where I left off.
textes.Je respire ! Je respire en parlant, c'es: I am breathing! I breathe while I talk, it's a talent!
textes.Je respire par la bouche depuis treize a: I've been breathing through my mouth for thirteen years!
textes.Je reviens chaque jour sur sa terrasse r: I go back to his terrace every day for another glass, to check. I bring my little bag of salt, just in case. Hassan hides the salt cellar when he sees me, as if I were going to steal it. But I don't need it, I've got my own! One day he'll understand. Salt is life. Even in coffee. Especially in coffee.
textes.Je reçois des lettres de Port-Azur, appo: I get letters from Port-Azur, brought by the boats. Postcards with a blue sea. Here the sea is grey with mist, but it's ours.
I'll laugh. Promise. I'm already laughing.
textes.Je ronronne, mais c'est pour moi, pas po: I'm purring, but it's for me, not for you.
textes.Je règle le son. Si tu entends quelque c: I do the sound. If you hear something off, it means my back was turned.
textes.Je règne sur les fées du ciel depuis que: I have reigned over the sky fairies since the world was young. My task is simple: watch over the Tree, and the Tree watches over everything else.
textes.Je réfléchis. Tu m'as interrompu, mais c: I'm thinking. You interrupted me, but never mind.
textes.Je réfléchis. Vous m'avez interrompu, ma: I'm thinking. You interrupted me, but never mind.
textes.Je répare, je façonne. Un objet bien fai: I mend things, I make things. A well-made object lasts a lifetime.
textes.Je répète. Tu aimes ce morceau ?: I'm practising. Do you like this tune?
textes.Je rêvais d'une elfe qui traversait la b: I was dreaming of an elf crossing the mist. Lovely dream.
textes.Je rêve d'habiller toute la cité pour la: I dream of dressing the whole city for the Night of Lanterns: every demon in a hand-sewn outfit, with ember sequins that sparkle when they dance. Seen from above, the Great Square would be an embroidery.
textes.Je rêve d'ouvrir le plus beau salon de l: I dream of opening the finest salon in the archipelago, with mirrors everywhere, oils from every island and a red velvet armchair. The elves would come to shine their ears, the dwarves their beards. Why not?
textes.Je rêve d'un grand bazar des épices où v: I dream of a great spice bazaar where merchants would come from every island: saffron from Tazira, cacao from Yaxché, cinnamon from the elves… And in the middle, my infernal chili, the king of the party.
textes.Je rêve d'un grand parc pour tous les ch: I dream of a big park for all the hellhounds on the island, mine and the wild ones, with bones everywhere and pools of warm lava to roll around in. They'd all be good, I know it. You just have to talk to them.
textes.Je rêve d'une Académie où chaque diablot: I dream of an Academy where every little devil could light their flame without burning their neighbour's. One flame each, and everyone warm. It's a bit like life, really.
textes.Je rêve d'une bibliothèque où chaque liv: I dream of a library where every book would be returned on time. … No. I dream of a library where every book would be read. Returned late, but read. That's already a lot.
textes.Je rêve d'une grande fête où tout l'arch: I dream of a great party where the whole archipelago would come and dance on our Grand Square: the elves, the dwarves, the pirates, the people of Port-Azur. So they'd finally see that you can have horns and a tender heart.
textes.Je rêve d'une lame qui ne casse jamais,: I dream of a blade that never breaks, not even on a gargoyle. Ferronde says it doesn't exist. I tell her that if we forge it together, it will. She laughs. She doesn't say no.
textes.Je rêve d'une nuit où toutes les lantern: I dream of a night when all the lanterns of the archipelago would light up at the same time: here, in Port-Azur, among the elves, among the dwarves… You'd see them from the sky. A constellation made by us.
textes.Je rêve d'une semaine sans rien à signal: I dream of a week with nothing to report. A real one. I'd sit on a bench on the Grand Square, without armour, with Ferronde, and we'd watch Ortie invent something that doesn't explode.
textes.Je rêve d'écrire la grande Histoire de P: I dream of writing the great History of Pandémonia, in twelve volumes, with footnotes, and footnotes to the footnotes. Ébène says no one will read it. I will. Several times.
textes.Je rêve d'écrire le grand Herbier de Pan: I dream of writing the great Herbarium of Pandémonia: every plant on the island drawn, named, labelled. With the date. My mother would say I'm too serious. She'd also say she's proud.
textes.Je rêve d'écrire un vrai livre de poèmes: I dream of writing a real book of poems. Not very long, because of my big fingers. Just enough for someone to read it one evening, under a lantern, and feel less alone.
textes.Je rêve de brasser un hydromel. Mais ici: I dream of brewing a honey drink. But there are no bees here: too hot. If you brought me {manque} honeycombs from your island… I'd give you the first tankard!
textes.Je rêve de construire des Thermes sur ch: I dream of building Baths on every island in the archipelago! Imagine: dwarves in the bubbles, elves in the steam, pirates singing in the bath! Nobody would ever be cold again. Ho ho!
textes.Je rêve de coudre une voile neuve pour u: I dream of sewing a new sail for a boat and setting off to see the other islands. One day.
textes.Je rêve de distribuer le courrier dans t: I dream of delivering mail across the whole archipelago: the village, the jungle, the elves, the dwarves… They even say there are people under the sea.
textes.Je rêve de faire une brioche si grande q: I dream of making a brioche so big the whole city could have a piece, on the Night of Lanterns. We'd have to enlarge the oven. I'll ask it nicely.
textes.Je rêve de forger une cloche si grande q: I dream of forging a bell so big it could be heard from every island in the archipelago. On festival day, I'd ring it, and everywhere people would look up wondering where the noise was coming from. From Pandémonia, that's where!
textes.Je rêve de jouer un soir avec des musici: I dream of playing one evening with musicians from every island: a drum from Tazira, an elven flute, bagpipes from Carène. It would be the biggest party in the archipelago. And I'd be the one playing the melody. Obviously.
textes.Je rêve de livrer une lettre dans chaque: I dream of delivering a letter to every island in the archipelago in a single day: the village, Port-Azur, the elves, the dwarves… I'd fly so fast people would take me for a shooting star. A shooting star with a bag.
textes.Je rêve de planter un jardin sur les pen: I dream of planting a garden on the slopes of the volcano, where the ember flowers grow. A garden nobody sowed, except the volcano and me. It's very slow, but so am I.
I dream of catching the golden sunfish. The real one, the legendary one. I'd show it to the whole city, then let it go. Well… I'd show it for a long time. Then I'd let it go.
textes.Je rêve de raconter une histoire si bell: I dream of telling a story so beautiful that even the Frost Titan, at the bottom of the Cocytus, would warm up listening to it. But someone would have to go down and tell it to him. I'm a bit old for stairs.
textes.Je rêve de reprendre la mer une dernière: I dream of going to sea one last time, with Pépin at the helm and Zébuline… on the quay, waving a handkerchief. Sailing around the archipelago, and coming home in time for the Night of Lanterns.
textes.Je rêve de voir la Flamme Éternelle de m: I dream of seeing the Eternal Flame with my own eyes, once, before I put down my broom. They say it burns at the bottom of the Nine Circles, near the Cocytus, since the city's very first day.
textes.Je rêve de voler, une nuit, juste une fo: I dream of flying, one night, just once, over the city, to see all my street lamps lit from above. Like a sky laid on the ground.
textes.Je rêve du plus grand feu d'artifice de: I dream of the biggest firework display in the island's history: rockets shaped like a volcano, a dragon, a lantern, a brioche! And one, the last, shaped like a heart. A successful one. Just once. For her.
I dream with my eyes open.
textes.Je rêve que des voyageurs de tout l'arch: I dream of travellers from all over the archipelago coming to the Diable Repu, just to taste my frozen lava. Elves, dwarves, pirates, everyone at the same counter. Bobor's face would be a picture!
textes.Je sais ce que tu as fait à {qn}. Je ne: I know what you did to {qn}. I won't forgive you any time soon.
textes.Je sais ce que vous avez fait à {qn}. Je: I know what you did to {qn}. I won't forgive you any time soon.
textes.Je sais compter, Mâchefer. Je sais compt: I can count, Mâchefer. I can count.
textes.Je sais grimper jusqu'au premier planche: I can climb up to the first floor without the stairs. Mum doesn't want me to. So I take the stairs. Running.
I know where the door is. Drink.
textes.Je sais qui a gagné rien qu'à sa façon d: I know who won just from the way he sits down. If he wins, he sits astride the chair and orders for everyone. If he loses, he pulls the chair out slowly, perches right on the edge, arms folded, and says: “A coffee.” He doesn't drink it. I serve it anyway. That's our arrangement.
I know who. He denies it, that old postman.
textes.Je sais un secret de Karim : au fond de: I know one of Karim's secrets: at the bottom of his basket, there are wedding babouches, for Rachid. I didn't say anything. I just whistled the wedding tune when I walked past Rachid. With winks. Whistling isn't telling.
textes.Je sais écrire mon nom en hiéroglyphes !: I can write my name in hieroglyphs! A pot, a leg, a loaf. That makes Nebet. Amenemhat says it's almost right.
textes.Je sais, Grimli. Elle fait boum depuis m: I know, Grimli. It's been going boom for a thousand years.
textes.Je sais, Hurla. Tout le monde sait. Tu l: I know, Hurla. Everyone knows. You've already shouted it.
textes.Je sais, Marley. Ton ventre, il va mieux: I know, Marley. How's your tummy, better?
textes.Je sais, Maître. C'est vous qui me l'ave: I know, Master. You're the one who taught me.
textes.Je sais, Tochtli. Elles me l'ont dit. El: I know, Tochtli. They told me. They want their share.
textes.Je sais, je sais, cinq heures, ce n'est: I know, I know, five o'clock is never for you. I won't ask any more. I'm just telling you, in case.
textes.Je sais, je sais, je te l'ai déjà demand: I know, I know, I've already asked you. I'm asking again. Have you had a drink?
I know, my dear. The ball told me.
textes.Je sais, mon vieux glaçon. Trois cuillèr: I know, you old icicle. Three spoonfuls of honey?
I know. So I'm singing for the Gate.
textes.Je sais. C'est pour ça qu'elle est libre: I know. That's why it's free.
I know. This one's for no reason.
I know. And I never cheat.
I know. I can smell it. Clang.
textes.Je sais. Je t'entendais frotter d'en bas: I know. I could hear you scrubbing from downstairs.
I know. The little stone slept well.
textes.Je sais. La tienne penche toujours ?: I know. Is yours still leaning?
I know. We'll see on Friday.
I know. The whole village can smell it.
textes.Je sais. Toute l'île le sait : Bourrasqu: I know. The whole island knows: Bourrasque shouted it from the garage roof. (He smiles, which rarely happens to him.) Then it's time. The stage is ready, I tightened the last bolt this morning. I'm missing two things. Galet's ropes, to stretch the backdrop: he said they'd be at the Ropeworks, near the spinning wheel. And the canvas itself, which Lune has been weaving for three years. She says she'll finish it “when the two villages talk to each other”. They're talking. Go and see if she's finished. Me, I'm not moving: if I leave, someone will move an amp.
textes.Je sens l'ours et la forge. Bonjour, Urs: I smell bear and forge. Hello, Ursule.
textes.Je sens que je peux te le dire, {surnom}: I feel I can tell you, {surnom}. Roux's three proposals… I knew they were serious. The riddle, the flower, and the moon song: I knew it was for me. I said no because I was afraid he'd stop being funny if I said yes. Silly. Next time, I'll say yes. Even if he's joking.
textes.Je sens surtout mes pieds. Ça fait six h: Mostly I feel my feet. They've been in the sand for six hours.
textes.Je serai la plus grande inventrice de Pa: I'll be the greatest inventor in Pandémonia. I'll invent a machine that relights lanterns all by itself, a machine to warm up horns, and a machine to do Pépin's homework. He asks me for that one every day.
