textes.La Reine des Ronces… on n'en parle pas t: The Bramble Queen… we don't speak of her too loudly here. Her brambles have eaten half our kingdom.
textes.La Reine hurle : « Mes enfants, à moi !: The Queen howls: “My children, to me!” Crystal spiders burst from the brambles!
textes.La Reine se relève, et son bouclier d'ép: The Queen gets back up, and her thorn shield grows back! The roses of light close again…
textes.La Rose des Sceaux. Une salle ronde comm: The Rose of Seals. A hall as round as a square, four columns, four doors. On the floor, an engraved compass rose, and at the centre a round seal beneath four dark crystals. Under the vault, a red crystal hangs and beats like a heart.
textes.La Râpe d'Or… Arrr. Bon. Je vais te dire: The Golden Grater… Arrr. Well. I'll tell you the truth, matey. I buried it thirty years ago, so nobody would steal it from me. And then I forgot where. (Pesto shouts: “RAMEN!”) … No, wait. I remember the phrase: “where the mast's shadow touches the sea at noon”. My mast is the Houseboat's. Take a shovel, and dig on the sand, between the mast and the water. You don't have a shovel? I sell one. Cheap. I'm a pirate, not a thief.
textes.La Salle de la Sève. À l'ouest, une sour: The Sap Hall. To the west, an amber spring from which golden light flows. Three flowers with polished silver hearts, like mirrors. To the east, a big knot of dark wood: the heart of the tree?
textes.La Salle des Deux Vérités. Anubis, le di: The Hall of the Two Truths. Anubis, the jackal god, and Thoth, the ibis god, before a great golden scale. Along the walls, the forty-two judges.
textes.La Salle des Pièges. À l'est, un champ d: The Trap Room. To the east, a field of tiles (some are dark and cracked…); to the west, a campfire and goblins; to the south, a closed door, and three unlit lamps above it. Three levers to find!
textes.La Salle des Prismes est au bout du coul: The Prism Hall is at the end of the corridor. The sun comes down through a crack… but it no longer reaches the Door Flower.
textes.La Salle des Saisons. Quatre fleurs de p: The Hall of Seasons. Four stone flowers, one at each cardinal point, and a carved stele right next to you… And leaves that move all by themselves!
textes.La Salle du Cœur. Le grand cristal bat d: The Heart Chamber. The great crystal beats gently, with a golden light. All is calm.
textes.La Salle du Cœur. Une caverne immense, r: The Heart Chamber. An immense, round cavern, veins of fire in the floor. In the middle, hanging from chains, a red crystal larger than a house… that beats. And beneath it, something is rising.
textes.La Salle du Trône Gélatineux. Le sol col: The Jelly Throne Room. The floor sticks to your soles, a jelly throne wobbles at the far end… and a smell of green apple hangs everywhere.
textes.La Skala, avec les canons, c'est le meil: The Skala, with the cannons, is the best place to play. But the guard chases us away. He says cannons aren't horses.
textes.La Terrasse du Ciel — à 150 mètres au-de: The Sky Terrace — 150 meters above the streets: the whole city, the sea, and the archipelago in the distance
textes.La Tomateraie — des tomates grosses comm: The Tomato Grove — tomatoes as big as fists, red, warm from the sun
textes.La Tour Axiome — 265 mètres de verre ; s: The Axiom Tower — 265 meters of glass; its elevator goes up to the Sky Terrace
textes.La Tour Penchée, autrefois, c'était la t: The Leaning Tower used to be the tower of the winds, standing straight. I was given my class there at twenty-five. There was a bench on every floor, one for each wind, and the bell, right at the top, that rang when they arrived. Sometimes I taught upside down, so the apprentices would see the world differently. They did. They got dizzy.
textes.La Tour Penchée, là-bas, c'était la tour: The Leaning Tower, over there, used to be the tower of the winds. It's been leaning since the great storm. Its bell is still up there, but the staircase collapsed. There's only one way left to get up…
textes.La Tourmente : un couloir au bord d'un g: The Tempest: a corridor on the edge of a fiery chasm, and a wind that never stops blowing, in gusts. The pillars against the wall make good shelters.
The Waltz plays when it wants to. Serve first.
textes.La Veuve Écarlate, c'est ma femme, ma ma: The Veuve Écarlate is my wife, my home, my country. I named her after a lady who dropped a flowerpot on my head in Tortuga. I married the ship. It was safer.
textes.La bague en corail rose, il me l'a laiss: The pink coral ring, he offered it at twelve coins, friend's price. I offered nine, fiancée's price. A week of haggling! In the end he said “eleven”, I said “ten”, and we looked at each other. Neither of us gave in. The ring's still in his drawer. I know: I check when his back is turned.
textes.La bague est dans ma poche depuis des jo: The ring has been in my pocket for days. I'm waiting for the right moment. The right century, maybe.
textes.La baguette de Pimprenelle ! Son étoile: Pimprenelle's wand! Its crystal star crackles between your fingers. She'll be delighted to have it back, in the Fairy Village.
textes.La bague… Tu en as trouvé une ? Avec une: The ring… Have you found one? With a blue stone, mind. Not red. Red is for declarations of war.
textes.La baie devant la plage descend doucemen: The bay in front of the beach slopes gently. At the bottom there are orange starfish. Bringing them up to the surface is my challenge for the tough ones.
textes.La baie est poissonneuse, abritée par le: The bay is full of fish, sheltered by the two points. Further out, there are the big ones. And to the north, under the highland cliffs, lobsters the size of dogs.
textes.La balance penche lourdement : ton cœur: The scale tips heavily: your heart weighs more than the feather! In the shadows behind the judges, something growls… AMMIT THE DEVOURER bursts out!
textes.La balance s'équilibre : ton cœur est au: The scale balances: your heart is as light as Ma'at's feather! Thoth writes on his tablet: “True of voice.” Your heart returns to your chest… and at the far end of the hall, the door to the Duat opens.
textes.La balle est lourde, en caoutchouc plein: The ball is heavy, solid rubber. One ball on the head and you see stars. Ask Ah Kin Pech: that's how he became an astronomer.
textes.La balle roule, rebondit sur le talus… e: The ball rolls, bounces off the slope… and falls back into the alley. The Lords snigger. Aim for the stone ring, on the wall.
textes.La bannière ! LA BANNIÈRE ! (Il la brand: The banner! THE BANNER! (He waves it, trips on his cape, falls, and is still waving it, lying down.) A real feat! With a witness! With sunshine! Bertrand! BERTRAND! We need a song! And not a single cloud in it!
textes.La barque de Rê glisse sur le fleuve de: The barque of Ra glides over the river of night… and drops you off in the sunlight, in front of the pyramid door.
textes.La betterave. Ma vie d'artiste est un dr: Beetroot. My artistic life is a tragedy.
The Montjoie library is that way. Just for your information.
textes.La bijouterie le matin, le déjeuner chez: The jeweller's in the morning, lunch at Paulo's, the shop, a stroll in the evening. Victor drops by to offer me “authentic” shells that smell of paint. A young newlywed asked me for a ring “exactly the same”. And Rosalie counts my Friday sea bream with saucer eyes. A quiet life, as you can see. In Port-Azur, nothing stays quiet for long.
textes.La bière épaisse et douce de Mérit, fait: Mérit's thick, sweet barley drink, made with barley bread and dates. The Egyptians drank it like liquid bread. Restores one heart.
textes.La boisson du Diable Repu, sans alcool :: The house drink of Au Diable Repu, alcohol-free: honey, fire cinnamon, a pinch of sulphur from the springs (for the colour). It smells of eggs, and it warms you right through. Restores one heart.
textes.La botte de Barnabé ! Je vais la clouer: Barnabé's boot! I'll nail it above my door. Like a trophy.
textes.La botte, c'était une botte de pêcheur,: The boot was a fisherman's boot, size thirteen, full of mud. Agathe came to look at it on the jetty. She took it, carried it off to her caravan, and planted thyme in it. Now it sits in pride of place by her door, with a label: “Prediction fulfilled”. I walk past it grumbling. The thyme is doing well.
textes.La boule ajoute : « Évitez les grenouill: The ball adds: “Avoid the frogs.” Nobody knows why. Everybody listens.
textes.La boule devient rose une seconde. D'apr: The ball turns pink for a second. According to Églantine, that means “hidden talent”. Very hidden.
textes.La boule embue sa propre vitre. Elle a b: The ball fogs up its own glass. It needs a moment.
The ball makes a little satisfied noise. Églantine notes: “The ball is happy.”
textes.La boule m'avait annoncé une traversée a: The ball had foretold me a crossing with a beautiful stranger with golden eyes. I shaved, I put on my clean shirt. It was a goat. A goat for Mère Sauge's garden, with magnificent yellow eyes, I'll grant you. Agathe says she never mentioned a woman. It's true. I hate it when it's true.
textes.La boule ne ment jamais. Elle exagère, p: The ball never lies. It exaggerates, sometimes.
textes.La boussole que je t'ai donnée ne montre: The compass I gave you doesn't point north. It points to what you're really looking for. Usually, that's north.
textes.La boutique est FERMÉE. Pour toi. Revien: The shop is CLOSED. To you. Come back when I've got over your punches.
textes.La boîte aux lettres jaune devant la pos: The yellow postbox outside the post office? If you slip a wish into it, I won't read it. Promise.
textes.La brioche du Four Éternel de Bobor, dor: The brioche from Bobor's Eternal Oven, golden, split on top, baked over the embers that never go out. Still warm, at any hour. Restores two hearts.
textes.La brume ? C'est le souffle de l'Arbre-M: The mist? It's the Mother Tree's breath. It opens for those it loves. It seems to like you. It has strange tastes.
textes.La brume est calme… Tu as fait tout ce q: The mist is calm… You've done everything there was to do. The stars salute you. So do I.
textes.La cachette est vide : tu as déjà pris l: The hiding place is empty: you've already taken the treasure. The parrot gives you a knowing look.
textes.La caisse vient se caler contre le quai: The crate slides up against the loading dock: a nice step! Jump on it, then onto the dock… then onto the mezzanine.
textes.La caisse à outils du chauffagiste ! Une: The boiler technician's toolbox! A wrench, some patches… and coins. On the lid: “Do not open during steam bursts.”
textes.La capitaine Anne-Rose a le perroquet le: Captain Anne-Rose has the worst-behaved parrot in my catalogue and the most loyal heart in the port. She adores him. He adores her. They swear together. It's beautiful!
textes.La capitaine m'a trouvé en haut d'un mât: The captain found me at the top of a mast and left me there. It's the nicest thing anyone's ever done for me. She's got a good eye, too. Not as good as mine, but nearly.
textes.La capitaine, c'est la meilleure. Elle d: The captain's the best. She says “jump”, I jump. She says “hit”, I hit. She says “eat”… well, she never says that one. But I eat anyway.
textes.La capitaine, c'est la plus forte de tou: The captain is the strongest in all of Balafre! She says the cabin boy doesn't fight. And she says “almost” when I mess up my knot. It's my favourite word.
textes.La capitaine. Elle voit tout, elle note: The captain. She sees everything, she writes everything down. She scares me a bit. But she's fair. I respect her.
textes.La carte d'Églantine montre la passe ent: Églantine's map shows the pass between the Fire Reefs, to the west. The dwarves of Fire Mountain live over there.
textes.La carte de Barbe-Sanglante ? Elle exist: Barbe-Sanglante's map? It exists. I've seen it, young man: torn into three pieces. Bring them together and I'll piece it back for you. I can read pirate maps: they always lie, but always in the same way.
textes.La carte des Récifs de Feu ! Les nains d: The map of the Fire Reefs! The dwarves of the Fire Mountain… They forged the finest blades in the world. My grandfather sold them moonwood, eight centuries ago. He came back with an axe and without his beard. Head towards the sunset, beyond the jungle. And knock hard: dwarves are a little deaf, from all that hammering on anvils.
textes.La carte du trésor ? Barbe-Sanglante l'a: The treasure map? Barbe-Sanglante tore it in three, so his men wouldn't betray each other. One piece is in the mausoleum, in the graveyard. Another in the keep of the Cursed Fort. The third… they say Sylvain, the croupier, keeps it up his sleeve.
textes.La carte frémit dans ton sac. Le sable d: The map quivers in your bag. The sand of the Circus rises… bones come up and fit together: CAPTAIN SANS-CHAIR!
textes.La carte officielle de Port-Coutelas, si: The official map of Port-Coutelas, signed with my name and his seal, hangs in his residence. It shows Lagrange Avenue, Constitution Square, a columned opera house and a botanical garden. In reality, there's a quay, a well and a gallows. He paid me in honey. Visitors get lost with it, but elegantly.
textes.La cascade de lumière descend des racine: The waterfall of light flows down from the Mother Tree's roots. It's its sap. Don't drink it: you'd glow for a week.
textes.La casquette de Bastien, je l'ai repêché: I fished Bastien's cap out of the water the night Fanny sent him flying into the sea. I put it on so it could dry. It dried on my head for three days. He found it and gave me an hour-long lecture. I listened with the cap on my head. He didn't dare take it back during the lecture.
textes.La chambre de la terrasse. Laisse la fen: The terrace room. Leave the window open: you'll fall asleep to the party, and wake up to the seagulls.
textes.La chambre du dessus. Le lit est à resso: The room upstairs. The bed has springs: if you bounce off the ceiling, that's normal. The alarm clock rings at seven; it plays the trumpet.
textes.La chambre du haut, celle avec la lucarn: The top room, the one with the skylight. If the cauldron sings tonight, that's normal: it's dreaming.
textes.La chance ! Ah, tu me plais. La chance e: Luck! Ah, I like you. Luck is a lady, my friend. You must greet her, smile at her… and sometimes show her your teeth.
textes.La chapelle d'Isis. Deux gros blocs de g: The chapel of Isis. Two big granite blocks, and two bronze slabs engraved with an ankh. Near the entrance, a bronze ring on the wall.
textes.La chapelle de Khépri, le scarabée. Un s: The chapel of Khepri, the scarab. A floor of slabs above a pit of sand. Some are engraved with a tiny scarab.
textes.La chapelle de Serket, la déesse au scor: The chapel of Serket, the scorpion goddess. Something is scratching in the corners…
textes.La chapelle obscure. Pas une torche. Jus: The dark chapel. Not a single torch. Just a green glow at the very back… and shuffling footsteps.
textes.La charpentière. Trop bruyante. Ses pont: The carpenter. Too noisy. Her bridges dance too much. But they hold. I respect that. I don't say so.
textes.La chaudière ronronne, la cheminée fume,: The boiler purrs, the chimney smokes, the propeller churns: your boat has a steam engine! Careful, it starts with a jolt.
textes.La chaîne d'os ne bouge pas. Dehors, que: The chain of bones won't budge. Outside, something still guards the treasure… (Captain Sans-Chair, in the Circus)
textes.La chaîne d'os tombe en poussière. Le co: The chain of bones crumbles to dust. The lid creaks… BARBE-SANGLANTE'S TREASURE! (
textes.La chaîne tombe ! Ventaile pousse un cri: The chain falls! Ventaile lets out an immense cry that echoes through the crater… but she is too weak to fly. She is hungry: bring her fish (three).
textes.La chorale te remercie avec ce qu'elle a: The choir thanks you with what it has.
textes.La chèvre qui est montée trop haut, vers: The goat that climbed too high, towards the golems? Kalda saw her come back down. She told me: “She was running so fast her horns arrived before she did.” Then, more quietly: “The golems didn't follow her. They didn't even turn their heads.” That scared me.
textes.La cime du Chêne-Mère : la Poste des cho: The top of the Mother Oak: the Owl Post Office.
textes.La cinquième corde a cassé. Hulotte deda: The fifth rope snapped. Hulotte inside, the mail bag clutched to him. He was counting the wickers. Out loud. Me, I held on. He counted up to a hundred and twelve. Then the pulley locked. He got out. He said thank you. He never got back in. Hrmm.
textes.La cité s'étend sous toute la montagne :: The city stretches under the whole mountain: the great hall, the Royal Forge, the mines, the dormitories… and my cellar. The biggest room of all.
textes.La cloche de la Cathédrale sonne douze c: The Cathedral bell strikes twelve… THE NIGHT OF LANTERNS BEGINS! From every street, the demons pour into the Great Square, laughing and singing. Calcine strikes up a wild jig.
textes.La cloche de la Tour Penchée: The bell of the Leaning Tower
textes.La cloche de la Tour Penchée a sonné !: The bell of the Leaning Tower has rung!
textes.La cloche de la Tour Penchée sonne sur t: The bell of the Leaning Tower rings out over the whole island! Zéphyrine must have heard it.
textes.La clé d'argent tourne. Les hiboux cisel: The silver key turns. The engraved owls all open an eye (“hoo”) and the silver door sinks into the floor. Further down, it smells of green apple… and jelly.
textes.La clé d'or de la ville, remise par le m: The golden key to the town, given by the mayor to the honorary citizen. It opens no doors, but every heart.
textes.La clé de cuivre entre dans la bouche de: The copper key slides into the mouth of the frog lock, which goes “ribbit” (yes, really). The copper door sinks into the floor.
textes.La commandante Zélie Hélice, à Cliquetis: Commander Zélie Hélice, in Cliquetis! We write each other a little note in every bag. I've never seen her. But I recognise her handwriting: it leans forward, like an airship.
textes.La commandante Zélie est la seule person: Commander Zélie is the only person who ever sold me a trip to nowhere. Free, what's more. A very precise woman, and a very kind one.
textes.La commandante Zélie est une amie. Chaqu: Commander Zélie is a friend. Every time the Zéphyr takes off, she gives me a little wave. She never forgets who she owes the envelope to.
textes.La commandante Zélie m'apporte le monde: Commander Zélie brings me the whole world in a mailbag. She doesn't like my headlines about her delays. I don't like her delays. We're even.
textes.La commandante, elle voit tout avec ses: The commander sees everything with her binoculars. Even spitting. She's strict, but she knows the sky by heart. When I'm older I'll be a pilot, like she used to be.
The rope snapped. I held the basket. Bare hands. It slipped. It burned. And Ursule arrived. An iron bar. In the pulley. Clack. Done. We never talked about it. Never. Ten years. Hrmm. No need. That evening, she gave me her honey pot. Her own. Whole.
textes.La couchette, c'est pour la nuit (à part: The bunk is for the night (from 7 p.m.)… For now, the sun is winking at you!
textes.La cour des Seigneurs de Xibalba. Douze: The court of the Lords of Xibalba. Twelve thrones, twelve motionless figures. A dry voice: “Greet the Lords then, traveller… the greatest first.”
textes.La couronne des Rois-Ciel : or blanc, sa: The crown of the Sky Kings: white gold, sapphires and cloud pearls. Proof that you defeated Lord Storm. It's worth a fortune… but who would dare sell it?
The crown is heavy. Especially in the morning.
textes.La course passe sous les dix arches : la: The race goes under the ten arches: the Games Clearing, the north, the western pools, the Circle, the south, the forge, the Watchtower… and back. Don't cut through the trees: the arches count.
textes.La course, Ahmed ! Si ta Zahra trouve la: Race you, Ahmed! If your Zahra can find the channel.
textes.La criée, c'est le cœur de Tazira. Tout: The fish auction is the heart of Tazira. Everything that comes out of the sea passes through my cries. Then the fish goes to the souk, to the grills, to the drying racks, or into the desert caravans.
textes.La cuisine des petits Moaïs : un four cr: The little Moai's kitchen: an oven dug into the ground, gourds, and a lot of patience.
textes.La dalle glisse dans un raclement. Une é: The slab slides away with a scrape. A ladder descends into the dark… and a cool breath rises up.
textes.La dalle ne bouge pas d'un cheveu. Il ma: The slab doesn't budge an inch. Something is missing to open it. The little Moai might know…
textes.La dalle s'enfonce sous ton poids !: The slab sinks under your weight!
textes.La danse de la lune raconte l'histoire d: The moon dance tells the story of the she-wolf who saved the moon when it fell into the pond. The moment she lifts it out of the water… that's when everyone raises their arms. You'll see.
textes.La date de la création du monde: The date of the creation of the world
textes.La dernière Furie s'enfuit en hurlant («: The last Fury flees, screaming (“We'll be back! We never come back.”). The great iron gate of Dité creaks, glows red… and opens.
textes.La dernière fois, c'était pour une toute: Last time, it was for a tiny little anchor.
textes.La dernière fois, cela ressemblait à un: Last time, it looked like a mushroom.
textes.La dernière fois, il est venu payer. Une: Last time, he came to pay. One coin, with great ceremony, in front of witnesses. I got out my notebook and calculated the interest since the day of the apple: four hundred and twelve coins and change. He went pale. I refused his coin. A debt doesn't get paid back at a discount.
textes.La dernière fois, j'ai enfin aperçu mon: Last time, I finally caught sight of my treatise. It was under one foot of his big still. To level it. Mr Fiole explained it was “so as to always have it to hand”. I left without finishing my cordial. I walked all the way to the lake. Borée looked at me and said: “Hm.” That was exactly it.
Last time, I told you about %s.
Last time, I told you about %s.
textes.La dernière fois, tu n'avais pas assez b: Last time, you hadn't drunk enough. So, today? Show me your water bottle.
textes.La dernière pluie d'étoiles filantes a f: The last shower of shooting stars cracked three lenses of Zénith's great telescope. To cast new ones, he needs three meteorite fragments that fell on the island that night. After that, he'd like to show you the Night of the Auroras through the repaired telescope.
textes.La dernière vanne ! L'eau monte jusqu'au: The last sluice! The water rises to the brim, and the chinampas form a floating path to the opposite shore. Just like in the time of the Sun of Water, when men became fish…
textes.La dernière, la plus belle !: The last one, the most beautiful!
textes.La deuxième borne. Des chameaux sont gra: The second marker. Camels are engraved on its sides, in a line. The arrow still points northeast.
textes.La deuxième fois que je suis montée là-h: The second time I went up there, Queen Oriane told me the tree was sick. She asked me if I'd have the courage to go inside it, into the great trunk. I said no. I was so scared, {surnom}. Since then, I give my mushrooms to people who look braver than me. I watch them go. I'm a bit ashamed.
textes.La deuxième, la Perle de l'Épave, est l': The second, the Wreck Pearl, is the age of humans: sailors stole it, and their ship, “The Black Mermaid”, sank to the west. It stayed in the captain's chest.
The management approves of the cloud.
textes.La direction ne fait pas de commentaire,: The management has no comment, madame.
textes.La direction vous remercie. Le sujet ?: The management thanks you. The subject?
textes.La docteure Électre, c'est un million de: Doctor Électre is a million volts and the best source in the city after Professor Boum. She bans me from the lab without boots. With boots, she puts up with me.
textes.La faim. J'ai toujours faim. Mange-Clous: Hunger. I'm always hungry. Mange-Clous says I've got a hole in my stomach. I say he's got a hole in his recipe.
textes.La fameuse tourte de Mamie Rissole, la c: Mamie Rissole's famous pie (she's the Guild's cook): a golden crust, vegetables, mushrooms, melted cheese, and a secret she has never told anyone. Master Hugues eats three a day. Restores three hearts.
textes.La femme de chambre. Une personne très…: The chambermaid. A very… observant person. Too much so. She has turned my work into a topic of conversation. I remain polite. It is difficult.
textes.La fierté de Gustave Fiole, à L'Alambic: The pride of Gustave Fiole, at L'Alambic: moon dew, three drops of honey and a kind thought. It restores six points of magic.
textes.La fin… Ah. Tu veux savoir comment ça se: The end… Ah. You want to know how it finishes. So do I, little one. So do I. But the best stories have an ending that opens another one.
textes.La fièvre des marais a couché la moitié: Marsh fever has laid up half the crew of the Veuve Écarlate. The Doc needs three tufts of feverweed, which grow at the water's edge in the Drowned Marsh.
textes.La flamme prend. Rien d'autre ne se pass: The flame catches. Nothing else happens… for now.
textes.La flamme prend… puis toutes les flammes: The flame catches… then all the flames snuff out at once, in a puff of sand. That was not the course of the sun.
textes.La flamme, elle, ne fait pas la différen: The flame can't tell the difference.
textes.La fleur de cristal frémit… et les cloch: The crystal flower trembles… and the bells start singing on their own. Listen closely, and watch which ones light up.
textes.La fleur de lune ! Ses pétales brillent: The moonflower! Its petals glow softly between your fingers, like a piece of night.
textes.La fleur de lune… l'eau de la source… la:
The moonflower… the spring water… the golden seed! Come, {surnom}, look. I place the seed at the foot of the Tree, the flower among its roots, and the water… there.

Can you feel it? The sap is rising. It's breathing. IT'S BREATHING!

Here: my elven compass. Its crystal needle cuts through the mist of Bois-Doré. Take your boat east… and come and see me at home.
textes.La flotte sort à l'aube, la criée à dix: The fleet goes out at dawn, the fish auction is at ten, and in the afternoon I'm asleep on my feet. My big sister Zohra wants sea bream, I bring her sardines. My niece Yasmine commands the Zahra at the quay. Every morning, I race Youssef to the channel. And I'm teaching the pirates' cabin boy, Tibo, to fish. A pirate who fishes! Now I've seen everything.
textes.La fontaine a chanté cette nuit. Tu l'as: The fountain sang last night. Did you hear it?
textes.La fontaine est ronde, Yaya. Elle n'a pa: The fountain is round, Yaya. It doesn't have sides.
textes.La fontaine, c'est la meilleure. Si tu j: The fountain is the best. If you throw in a coin, your wish comes true. I wished for a dog.
textes.La fontaine, elle coule de la sauce ! De: The fountain, it flows with sauce! REAL sauce!
textes.La forge des pistons : d'énormes marteau: The piston forge: enormous cast-iron hammers pounding the floor in rhythm, and between them, conveyor belts that carry you backward. Count the beats…
textes.La forge le jour, la bière naine au Perr: The forge by day, dwarven fizz at the Perroquet by night. Colette finds my blades frightening and charges me for the wrapping paper. Madame Hortense looks at me the way you look at a clock. On Friday nights, I put on a clean shirt. Don't ask why. Hm. Nobody asks. That's what's good about Port-Azur.
textes.La forêt du Bois-Doré est une pharmacie: The forest of Bois-Doré is a pharmacy: bark for fever, moss for wounds, dew for tired eyes.
textes.La forêt est grande. Ne t'éloigne pas du: The forest is big. Don't stray from the path at night: the roots move. Well… so they say.
textes.La fosse est vide. Un gobelet en plastiq: The pit is empty. A plastic cup rolls along all by itself. Come back tonight, from 9 o'clock: that's when things happen.
textes.La foudre qui a réveillé les golems ne v: The lightning that woke the golems didn't come from the mountain. It came from the sky, from the south. From a floating castle… The runes say: “Fire guards fire, but the storm guards the sky.”
textes.La fête bat son plein ! Les ballons, la: The party is in full swing! Balloons, music, cake crumbs everywhere.
textes.La fête des morts approche. Il me faudra: The festival of the dead is coming. I need five cempasúchil bouquets for the temple altars. They grow on the southern chinampas, along the canals. Would you help me pick them?
textes.La galerie relie les deux îles ? Barnabé: The tunnel links the two islands? Barnabé could walk over to see me now. How horrible.
textes.La galette complète de Mère Gwenola : sa: Mother Gwenola's complete galette: buckwheat, salted butter, an egg in the middle, cooked on the billig griddle at La Dernière Bordée. Restores two hearts.
textes.La garance, c'est une racine. On la déte: Madder is a root. You dig it up, you grind it, and it gives all that red. People who love red have courage. Or character. Often both.
textes.La glace craque. Au fond du lac, quelque: The ice cracks. At the bottom of the lake, something very big rises: THE FROST TITAN, a crown of crystals, a club of frozen water. He clutches the Eternal Flame in his cage of ice.
textes.La gloire ! Hm. Le grand prêtre te racon: Glory! Hm. The high priest would tell you the story of Tecciztécatl. He tells it to me often. I'm starting to understand it. A little.
textes.La gorge, au milieu, va jusqu'au grand m: The gorge in the middle runs all the way to the great massif in the north. One day a river will flow through it, I'm sure. I can hear it dreaming.
textes.La graine… Elle respire ! Cent ans que n: The seed… It breathes! We've waited a hundred years for it. We'll plant it in the clearing, and in a thousand years, a new Yggdrasil will watch over the islands. To thank you, I give you the most precious thing fairies have: the magic of travel. Think very hard of a place you've already seen… and you'll be there.
textes.La grande carte de l'archipel, {surnom}: The great map of the archipelago, {surnom}! Bois-Doré, the sunken city, the dwarves' island, the floating island… And this time, it'll fit in a pocket. With your name on it. Very small, but on it.
textes.La grande course : retrouver Comète au-d: The great race: meet Comète above the Spaceport, aboard the Star Glider, and fly through all the sky rings around Astralys before she does
textes.La grande dalle s'est enfoncée dans le s: The great slab has sunk into the ground. Behind it, a stone staircase spirals down into the dark… and, far below, something is singing.
textes.La grande lanterne de la place, on l'a f: The big lantern in the square, we made it together. He signed it on one side, me on the other. Now people argue about which side to admire it from. I always walk past on mine. Him, on his. In the evening, we pass each other underneath without looking. Each to his own side.
textes.La grande lanterne de la place, on l'a s: The big lantern on the square, we both signed it: him on the souk side, me on the sea side. Since then people walk round it before admiring it, to pick their side. The fishermen look at it from the sea side, the merchants from the souk side. The children run round it laughing. They're the ones who've got it right.
textes.La grande lentille du phare a perdu un m: The lighthouse's big lens has lost a piece, which fell into the sea at the foot of the point.
The great iron door is locked. “Ye who enter here, keep hope (and bring a coat).” Brother Cendrin, the keeper of the Ember Heart, holds the Brasier key.
textes.La grande toile que Lune a mis trois ans: The great canvas that Lune spent three years weaving, rolled up like a carpet. Inside, you can make out a sun, a cloud and a rainbow. It's as heavy as a sleeping donkey.
textes.La grande voile, là-haut, sous la vergue: The big sail, up there, under the yard, is the Léviathan's last original sail. Nobody's allowed to touch it. Not even me. It's falling to shreds, and I watch it go.
textes.La grande île de l'est — Carène, le port: The great eastern island — Carène, the port inside the wreck of the Léviathan
textes.La grenouille fait la grimace et te recr: The frog makes a face and spits you out: apparently, you weren't to her taste!
textes.La grenouille fait « blurp »… et recrach: The frog goes “blurp”… and spits out a copper key, all slimy! (It had taken it for a fly. A very hard fly.)
textes.La grenouille l'a mangé ! Rends-le-nous,: The frog ate it! Give it back, you naughty frog!
textes.La grille, c'est déjà loin. Pour un bûch: The gate's already far. For a lumberjack.
textes.La grue le jour, la pêche le soir, au bo: The crane by day, fishing in the evening at the end of the quay, next to Écrou. Madame Bricolette comes down to ask for my piano; I say no, and we swap boots. Ernest, at the bottom station, asks me what's fallen. And the other day, something golden bounced near the crane. It was shining. By the time I'd climbed down from the cab, I couldn't see it any more. The quay keeps its secrets.
textes.La guerre a commencé avec les auvents. I: The war began with the awnings. He put up an awning that shaded my saffron jars. I put up a higher one. He put up an even higher one. After a week, both our awnings stood taller than the roofs. Captain Pyrus had to come and ask us to lower them.
textes.La guerre des prix : Victor vend ses car: The price war: Victor sold his postcards a penny cheaper than mine. The next day, I dropped mine by a penny. The day after, so did he. After a month, we were selling our cards for zero pennies. We made peace over a coffee at Gisèle's. He insisted on paying for the coffees. That was unfair too.
textes.La guitare électrique de Clou, rouge cer: Clou's electric guitar, cherry red, covered in stickers and scars. One string is a little rusty; that's on purpose. Clou hardly ever talks. But to her guitar, he does.
textes.La hache ! Bien en main, le fil vers l'a: The axe! Grip it firmly, edge forward. It cuts wood… and everything else. Mind your feet.
The harp went quiet at four.
textes.La haute, Majesté. Et la basse pour vous: The high one, Majesty. And the low one for you, if you can't sleep.
textes.La herse retombe derrière toi… L'eau du: The portcullis drops behind you… The water in the well bubbles. KARKINOS, THE KING CRAB, surges from the depths!
textes.La herse retombe. L'eau noire se soulève: The portcullis drops. The black water heaves… NÂGA, THE SERPENT OF THE ABYSS, rises from the depths!
textes.La houle ! Ha ! Un vrai marin. Tu auras: The swell! Ha! A real sailor. You'll have your place at the bow on windy days. I'm warning you: at the bow, you get soaked. That's the price of the show.
textes.La journée est finie. Les crocodiles, eu: The day is over. The crocodiles are just starting theirs.
textes.La journée se termine. On se raconte ce: The day is ending. We tell each other what we've been up to.
textes.La jungle, c'est mon garde-manger : bana: The jungle is my pantry: bananas, coconuts, chillies, mushrooms. But watch out for the crocodiles in the marsh: they're looking for dinner too.
textes.La lave glacée, c'est mon invention : un: Frozen lava is my invention: a sorbet of fire fruits, served in an obsidian cup. Cold outside, hot inside. Demons pretend to be shocked. Then they have seconds.
textes.La leçon de tajine, je m'en souviens com: I remember that tagine lesson like a shipwreck. He put in the fish, the lemon, my saffron… then a splash of rum, then two spoonfuls of sugar. I said nothing, I couldn't. When he lifted the lid, I cried, standing there with my spoon in my hand. He thinks they were tears of joy. I let him think so.
textes.La limonade maison de Sirène, au bar de: Sirène's homemade lemonade, from the bar at the Howling Hall: lemon, ginger, and a secret (very chatty bubbles). Alcohol-free. Restores one heart.
textes.La longue-vue ne se tient pas avec un ca: You can't hold the spyglass with a headset on… Just move closer instead!
textes.La louve et la lune, je la raconte encor: The wolf and the moon, I still tell it here, my way. In my version, the moon falls into the harbour, and the she-wolf fishes it out with a sardine for bait. Tilleul would be outraged. Or delighted. With a bear, you never know: he falls asleep in the middle of his own anger.
textes.La luciole replonge dans le bassin. À to: The firefly dives back into the pool. Your turn: touch the stones in the same order (E on each stone).
textes.La lumière ! Le premier des sorts ! Écou: Light! The first of the spells! Listen: to learn it, you must first hold a little real light in your hand. Moon shards: three have fallen this season. One near the altar of the Moonstone Circle, one in the Twisted Wood, one on the western shore. Bring them to me, and I'll teach you to bring forth your own.
textes.La lumière de Rê frappe le disque d'or d: Ra's light strikes the golden disc on the door! It blazes… and the slab slowly sinks into the floor.
textes.La lumière de la sève passe par les troi: The sap's light passes through the three mirror-flowers, brighter and brighter… and strikes the wooden heart! It lights up like a golden ember, and the whole hall begins to pulse gently. The staircase roots draw back.
textes.La lumière des sages court de miroir en: The light of the wise runs from mirror to mirror… and strikes the crystal, which blazes up in gold! To the south, the gate of Limbo sinks into the floor.
textes.La lumière des sages, de miroir en miroi: The light of the wise, from mirror to mirror.
textes.La lumière tombe de la couronne, toute r: Light falls from the crown, perfectly round, onto poufs of every color.
textes.La lumière touche le cœur de bois… mais: The light touches the wooden heart… but it stays almost dark. The light is too weak: it would have to pass through all three flowers.
textes.La lumière, c'est le premier sort qu'on: Light is the first spell you learn and the last one you master. A little flame in your hand, and suddenly the dark isn't the same dark any more.
textes.La lune au-dessus de Ramure est toujours: The moon over Ramure is always full. I've checked for three thousand nights. Elsewhere it gets thinner, then fatter. Not here. I have no explanation. It's the most beautiful thing I know.
textes.La lune touche la pierre… le croissant d: The moon touches the stone… the silver crescent lights up, and a pale disc slowly rises from the stone, in the mist: the Seal of Mists! Moonglow awakens within you (key 4, then X; in VR: B). And the mist around the pond takes shapes…
textes.La lune, Ix Chab. Elle a soif, ce mois-c: The moon, Ix Chab. She's thirsty this month.
textes.La lune, encore. Elle a soif, ce mois-ci: The moon again. She's thirsty this month.
textes.La légende des yeux du Grand Moaï: The legend of the Great Moai's eyes
textes.La légende des yeux du Grand Moaï : un œ: The legend of the Great Moai's eyes: one eye in “the water that looks at the sky,” the other “beneath the heads that look at the clouds.”
textes.La lévitation, Archimage. La chaise a vo: Levitation, Archmage. The chair flew. I didn't.
textes.La machine à café, c'est un ancien moteu: The coffee machine is an old locomotive engine. It makes forty cups a minute, and it whistles when it's ready. The customers jump. They come back anyway.
textes.La magie, ce n'est pas un pouvoir, c'est: Magic isn't a power, it's a way of listening. Fire, ice, wind, light: everything speaks. A wizard is someone who has learned to answer politely.
textes.La magie, ça fatigue. Un sorcier qui lan: Magic is tiring. A wizard who casts too many spells gets shaky hands and a spinning head. One magic potion, and hop! Off you go again.
textes.La mairie le matin, le serré de Gisèle à: The town hall in the morning, Gisèle's espresso at noon, Paulo's bouillabaisse, pétanque at five. At every election, all of Port-Azur votes for me. All of it, minus one vote: guess whose. The clock? I've promised fourteen times to have it fixed before the end of the year. Hortense keeps count. And in the shower, I sing. Django says something about seals. Jealous.
textes.La maison de la doyenne : des calebasses: The elder's house: gourds, mats, and engravings all over the walls.
textes.La maison est vide, mais il fait bon : q: The house is empty, but it's cozy: someone has just left, the fire is still burning.
textes.La maman te glisse un petit cadeau, sans: The mother slips you a little gift, without a sound.
textes.La meilleure patronne de l'archipel !: The best landlady in the archipelago!
textes.La meilleure réponse. Un ordre vaut ce q: The best answer. An order is worth what the person giving it is worth. I try to be worth something. I don't manage it every day.
textes.La menthe pousse dans les jardins de l'o: The mint grows in the gardens of the wadi, north of the town, beyond the ramparts. It's the only green place within three days' walk.
textes.La mer ? Encore plus d'eau que le fleuve: The sea? Even more water than the river? And more crocodiles, surely. You're braver than me. Or less careful.
textes.La mer d'huile ! Un passager comme je le: A sea like glass! Just the kind of passenger I like. You sit down, you look, you don't spill anything. The seagulls will love you, and so will I.
textes.La mer est bonne, le poisson est bête. Q: The sea is good, the fish are daft. What more could you ask?
textes.La mer est plus profonde au large de la: The sea is deeper beyond the bay. Much deeper. It's pitch black from ten fathoms down.
textes.La mer est à côté. Elle n'est pas sourde: The sea is right there. It isn't deaf.
textes.La mer m'entend pas, sinon !: Otherwise the sea can't hear me!
The sea. That's a beautiful first memory. The sea never stops, just as the stones never move. Now you have both.
textes.La mer. Hmm. Ça brille, mais ça ne se se: The sea. Hmm. It shines, but you can't set it. And you can't resell it. You're a poet, you are. Poets never pay cash.
Mine does. It loves the sea.
The mine. Yes, Nono. Forty times.
textes.La montagne est notre mère, notre forge: The mountain is our mother, our forge and our fortress. The reefs and the ash hide us from the tall folk. You came with Églantine's map. She always did have good taste.
textes.La montre qui tourne à l'envers, au Baza: The watch that runs backwards, at the Bazaar? I made it. On an absent-minded day. It keeps perfect time, just in the other direction.
textes.La musique de Tazira, c'est le désert et: The music of Tazira is the desert and the sea mixed together. The drum is the camel's step. The guembri is the wave.
textes.La musique me prend les pieds. Je n'y pe: The music grabs my feet. I can't help it.
textes.La musique, c'est comme la mer. Tu ne pe: Music is like the sea. You can't hold it in your hands, but it carries you.
textes.La méduse de ciel ramenée à la Serre: The sky jellyfish brought back to the Greenhouse
textes.La mélodie entière résonne dans la salle: The whole melody rings through the hall! To the north, the grille of roots slowly unties… and a golden light passes through the opening.
textes.La même qu'hier, Caelan. Tu disais déjà: Same as yesterday, Caelan. You said that yesterday too.
textes.La même, Bramm ! Et un sourire avec ?: The usual, Bramm! And a smile on the side?
The usual, Ulfa. Nice and cool. Nice and… pure.
textes.La même. Mettez-y une faute, ça marche m: Same as ever. Put a typo in it, it works better.
textes.La nacelle, c'est mon grand-père qui l'a: My grandfather wove the basket. The wicker's been changed four times. The rope, six times. But it's still my grandfather's basket.
textes.La nouvelle version ! Tu vas voir, elle: The new version! You'll see, it's much better.
Night! At last! My stars are rising.
textes.La nuit ! Quand on l'entend sur le toit,: At night! When you hear it on the roof and you're nice and dry. Ah, that's the best rain. Tlaloc sings, and we sleep.
textes.La nuit appartient à Xibalba, le monde d: The night belongs to Xibalba, the world below. The Lords of Death never sleep.
textes.La nuit après l'accident, Maître Rivet e: The night after the accident, Master Rivet stayed with me until morning, at the workbench, with the plans for my arm. He showed me his own, piece by piece. He didn't say one word of comfort. Just “Hm”, and “there, a size-five screw”. The next day, the giant sewing machine was gone. Dismantled. He never spoke of it again.
textes.La nuit après l'accident, on a dessiné s: The night after the accident, we drew his arm. He and I. On the Works bench, until dawn. I showed him mine, every part, every screw. He chose brass. Not iron. “Iron is yours, Master.” Hm. By morning, we had the plans. And I took the machine apart.
textes.La nuit d'orage où mes ruches se sont af: The stormy night my hives went wild, I came home covered in stings. Aëlwen put balm on every one, counting out loud. Three hundred and four. The next day she sent me the bill: “Balm, three hundred and four. On the house.” I had it framed.
textes.La nuit de la crue, elle portait les pet: The night of the flood, she carried the little scrolls one by one, gritting her teeth, more serious than a judge. At dawn, I found her asleep on the roof, on a pile of papyri, like a mummy in a bed of letters. I covered her with my shawl. She slept on the Book of Hours. She's known them all ever since.
textes.La nuit de la grande crue, j'avais sept: The night of the great flood, I was seven. Water was coming into the House of Life, and Amenemhat was carrying the scrolls up to the roof, two at a time. I carried the smallest ones, one at a time, very serious. At dawn, I fell asleep on a pile of papyri. He covered me with his shawl and carried on without me. He thanked me for a week.
textes.La nuit de la grande tempête, Zéphyr s'e: On the night of the great storm, Zéphyr got lost in the clouds. He says he didn't. He was lost. I sent all my fireflies, every one, even the little ones, to write a path in the sky: “THIS WAY, SILLY”. He came home soaked. He said he was taking a detour. My fireflies know what they saw.
textes.La nuit de la grande tempête, Zéphyr s'é: On the night of the great storm, Zéphyr got lost in the clouds. Lumi sent all her fireflies to draw a path across the sky. I saw it from my window: they had written, in letters of light, “THIS WAY, SILLY”. Zéphyr came home. He never said thank you.
textes.La nuit de la grande tempête, elle voula: The night of the great storm, she wanted to relight my cauldron with a snap of her fingers. I slapped her hand: no magic in my inn, not even to save the cauldron. Especially not to save the cauldron. We blew all night with the bellows, on our knees, singing out of tune. The finest night of our friendship.
textes.La nuit de la grande tempête, j'étais to: The night of the great storm, I was right at the top of the tower. I asked the wind to calm down, politely, as always. For the first time in my life, it said no. The tower leaned, the staircase fell, and I floated out of the window. Since then, I levitate everywhere, {surnom}. Everywhere. Except up there. I've never been back up.
textes.La nuit de la grande tempête, la lantern: The night of the great storm, the mast lantern went out, and I couldn't climb any more. I saw a little shadow scrambling up the shrouds, in the rain. I shouted his name, the wind swallowed it. The lantern came back on. When he came down, I hugged him so hard he said “ouch”. Then I scolded him. In that order.
textes.La nuit de la grande tempête, le vent es: The night of the great storm, the wind came down the Cauldron's chimney and almost put out her grandmother's cauldron. I wanted to relight it with a snap of my fingers. Berthe slapped my hand: “No magic in my inn.” So we blew with the bellows, the two of us, until dawn. It didn't go out.
textes.La nuit de la grande tempête, le vent s': The night of the great storm, the wind rushed down the chimney, and the cauldron's flame lay flat, all blue, all tiny. Pyra was there. She wanted to relight it with magic. Not in my house! We took the two bellows and blew, on our knees, all night long, singing to keep our courage up. At dawn, it was still burning.
textes.La nuit de la grande tempête, mes luciol: On the night of the great storm, my fireflies wrote “THIS WAY, SILLY” in the sky to bring Zéphyr home. He came back soaked and said he was “taking a detour”. Ever since, whenever he sets off, I ask him if he's planned a detour. He goes “Fffwoosh” and flies off, sulking.
textes.La nuit de la lanterne. Je suivais une é: The night of the lantern. I was following one of old Fatima's riddles, on my knees at the foot of the Skala. A shadow, a sabre: the caïd. “What are you doing here?” “Admiring the cannons.” “In the dark? From underneath?” “They have lovely undersides.” He walked me back to the quay. I admired them the whole way, to stay consistent.
textes.La nuit de la soupe, j'ai soigné trente: The night of the soup, I treated thirty sailors with herbal teas, buckets and a lot of patience. In the morning, I went and lifted the lid of his pot. I sniffed. Sunfish, badly prepared. I put the lid back and told no one. A doctor keeps his patients' secrets. And their cooks'.
textes.La nuit de la tempête, je n'étais pas pe: On the night of the storm, I wasn't lost. I was taking a detour. A long detour. In the dark. In the rain. Fine. Lumi wrote “THIS WAY, SILLY” in the sky with her fireflies. It helped a bit. The “silly”, though, was not necessary.
textes.La nuit de la tempête, la lanterne du gr: The night of the storm, the mainmast lantern went out. Before I'd finished giving an order, Ewen was in the shrouds. He relit it, three boats came home. I punished him: three days of deck duty, rules are rules. On the third evening, I put my childhood hat on his bucket. The rules say nothing about hats.
textes.La nuit de la tempête, la lentille s'est: The night of the storm, the lens cracked. The beam wouldn't reach, and the Swallow was at sea. I stayed up there all night wiping the glass, as if that did any good. Léon came home by guesswork, by ear, by memory. He made it. The next evening, two flashes, as usual. Nothing else.
textes.La nuit de la tempête, les enceintes pas: The night of the storm, the speakers were passed from hand to hand up to the dune. They were scared. They were. So I talked to them. To talk to someone, you need a name. Gertrude, the oldest. Raoul, the big subwoofer. Germaine, who runs hot. Jojo, the little one. Twenty-four names in one night. I'd never talked so much.
textes.La nuit de la vague, tout le monde coura: The night of the wave, everyone was running. Me, I ran to fetch a quill. In the morning, under the bubble, I asked the queen what this day was called. She looked at me as if I were mad, then said: “The first, I suppose.” I wrote “Day 1”. I haven't skipped a single day since.
textes.La nuit de mon premier éclair en bouteil: The night of my first lightning in a bottle, I ran to Héloïse's house. It was midnight. She opened the door in her dressing gown, monocle on her eye, as if she slept in it. I held up the bottle: it was crackling blue against the glass. She said nothing for a minute. Then: “Come in. I'll make tea. We'll talk about it until morning.” We did.
textes.La nuit de son arrivée, il y a soixante-: The night she arrived, seventy years ago, she had mud up to her knees, leaves in her ears, and eyes… lovelier than the moon. Yes, yes. I sat down next to her, I started a story, and she fell asleep in the middle. I finished the story anyway. For the moon.
textes.La nuit des requins, elle m'a tendu le t: On the night of the sharks, she handed me the trident and said: “Guard the Gate until I come back.” She hasn't come back yet. She's very busy. But one day she'll come, and I'll be able to tell her: “Nothing to report, Majesty. Three hundred years.” I've rehearsed the line.
textes.La nuit des requins, il y a trois cents: The night of the sharks, three hundred years ago, I wrote the page I'd been dreading: “The three Pearls are lost.” My hand shook so much the ink made a blot shaped like a whale. I kept it. Since then, I've searched my scrolls for a way to bring them back. I've found where they are. Not how to fetch them. It needed someone like you.
textes.La nuit des requins, j'avais deux cents: On the night of the sharks, I was two hundred and good for nothing. The queen crossed the square with a trident Coralin had just carved, and she gave it to me, because I was the closest. “Guard the Gate until I come back.” I'm still here. She's very busy, the queen.
textes.La nuit des requins, je lui ai mis le tr: On the night of the sharks, I put the trident in his hands and said: “Guard the Gate until I come back.” A thousand things kept me busy, and I never came back. He's still there, three hundred years later. I no longer dare tell him it was just a figure of speech.
textes.La nuit du Fidèle, il a ficelé vingt mar: The night of the Faithful, he trussed up twenty of the king's sailors with his lumberjack knots. By morning, they couldn't undo them. Neither could we. We left them on the beach with a bread knife and a week's supplies. If you ask me, they're still untying.
textes.La nuit du bain, quand Borée est arrivé: The night of the bath, when Borée arrived at the edge of the lake, in his nightshirt and woolly nightcap, I was in the middle, in hot water up to my chin, and all the fish had huddled around me to warm up. I waved at him. Apparently, waving was not the thing to do.
textes.La nuit du chergui, le vent a arraché la: The night of the chergui, the wind tore the bar off the great door. The doors were banging, sand was blowing in, the camels were bellowing. Mbarek came down, and he held the door. Alone. All night. In the morning, he had sand in his beard and red eyes. He said: “Tea.” That's all. I served him the best of my life.
textes.La nuit du chergui, quand j'ai vu la cou: The night of the chergui, when I saw the courtyard full of frozen caravan traders, I thought I'd never manage. And Hassan arrived, teapots under his arms, without anyone calling him. He poured all night. He gave away the fourth glass, of course. That evening, I said nothing. That evening only.
textes.La nuit du chergui, quarante caravaniers: The night of the chergui, forty caravan drivers stuck in the courtyard, we served together until dawn. She carried the trays, I poured. Not one argument. In the morning, the wind dropped, and she said to me: “Thank you, Hassan.” Once. She never said it again. I keep it, the way you keep a rare coin.
textes.La nuit du marais, il m'a soigné jusqu'à: The night of the marsh, he tended me till dawn. He talked the whole time: about the stars, about Montpellier, about a parrot with a cold. I didn't answer. But I listened. I think that's why he talked: so I'd listen to something other than my arm. That chatterbox did me a favour. Don't tell him.
textes.La nuit du récif, il y avait une brume à: The night of the reef, the fog was thick enough to cut with a sabre. Coquille asked me: “Where are we going, captain?” I had a game going in the cabin, so I answered: “Straight ahead.” It's an answer that almost always works. Not that night. She says it's my fault. I say she was asleep. We're both right.
textes.La nuit du récif, il y avait une brume é: The night of the reef, there was fog as thick as milk. I asked: “Where are we going, captain?” He shouted from his cabin: “Straight ahead!” He had a game going. Straight ahead, there was a reef. On no map! All right, maybe I had my eyes closed for a second. But straight ahead was his idea.
textes.La nuit est belle. Écoute… la place comm: The night is beautiful. Listen… the square is starting to beat.
textes.La nuit où Belle-Humeur l'a ramené du ma: The night Belle-Humeur brought him back from the marsh, I worked until dawn. He said nothing. So I talked for two: about Montpellier, the stars, a parrot of Joe's that sneezed swear words. I think he was listening. In the morning, Brutus came to look at his arm, without a word. In the evening, there was a hook. This port has funny ways of loving each other.
textes.La nuit où il a eu peur des chauves-sour: The night he got scared of the bats, at the Cenote, I found him under a tree, all trembling. I didn't scold him. I put him on my back and carried him home. At the door, I told him: “Next time, call me first.” He looked at me very seriously. He said yes. I believe him.
textes.La nuit où il a joué la « Ballade de l'A: The night he played the whole “Ballad of the Dawn” under my window, three hours of it, I didn't open the shutters. Before dawn, while he was asleep on his bench, I crept down and tied a blue ribbon to his harp. He's never taken it off. He's never asked. I won't say anything either.
textes.La nuit où j'ai eu peur des chauves-sour: The night I got scared of the bats at the Cenote, it was Balam who found me, hiding under a tree. He didn't scold me. He put me on his back and walked without a sound all the way home. At the door, he just said: “Next time, call me first.” I will. First.
textes.La nuit où j'ai joué jusqu'à l'aube, Ham: The night I played until dawn, Hamid sang with me to the very end. Not one break. When the sky turned white, he slung his father's oud over his shoulder and went straight to his boat, still singing. We heard him pass the channel. He came back without a single sardine. But he was still singing.
textes.La nuit où j'ai joué la « Ballade de l'A: The night I played the whole “Ballad of the Dawn” under her window, three hours, her shutters stayed closed. In the morning I found a blue ribbon tied to my harp. I've never taken it off. I've never asked her if it was her. If it wasn't, I don't want to know.
textes.La nuit où je suis tombé dans la baie, j: The night I fell into the bay, I was floating on my back without meaning to. I saw a big hand come out of the dark and grab me by the collar. It was the Silent One. He laid me on the quay like a fish, looked at me, and nodded once. Since then, I buy him a drink every evening. He downs it in one, and carries me home.
textes.La nuit où l'eau est entrée sous la tave: The night the water came in under the tavern, I worked lying in cold water till morning. When I'd finished, Gwenola was waiting for me with a hot drink and a blanket. She didn't say a word. She just straightened my collar, like a mother. I didn't sigh. I couldn't: I had a lump in my throat.
textes.La nuit où la Morue s'est posée sur le r: The night the Cod sat down on the reef, I was at the bow of the Shark, at the mouth of the bay, in the fog. I saw the breakers before anyone and shouted “Reef!” with all my strength. Coquille didn't hear me: she was asleep. Nor did Ignace: he was playing dice. Belle-Humeur heard me. He shouted “WHAT?!”. Too late.
textes.La nuit où la capitaine a pris le Fidèle: The night the captain took the Faithful, I was asleep in the crow's nest. When I woke up, everyone had been tied up and put ashore, and me, they'd forgotten. Two days up there, with one biscuit. I thought it over. Down below, pirates singing out of tune and laughing loudly. I came down and asked for work. Nobody's ever asked me anything else.
textes.La nuit où la corde a cassé, il fallait: The night the rope snapped, we needed new hooks for the sixth rope. Ursule forged them while Granny Faîne and I braided. All night, side by side, without a word. She hammered, I braided: tap, tap, knot, tap. At dawn, everything was ready. She looked at me and said “Hm. Good.” I still remember it.
textes.La nuit où la grande grille du Cœur s'es: The night the great grate of the Heart cracked, Brother Cendrin hammered on my door shouting my name. I'd never heard his voice so loud. I forged until dawn, and he held the lantern for me all night without saying a word. The next day, there was a jar of candied chilli in front of my forge. There's been one every week since.

The night the great grate of the Heart cracked, I ran all the way to Ferronde's. She arrived in her nightgown, hammer in hand, hair full of soot. She forged until dawn while I held the lantern for her. The next day, I put a jar of candied chilli in front of her forge. There's been one every week for forty years.
textes.La nuit où la passerelle de l'est s'est: The night the east walkway started swaying, I held my lantern above Taeron for three hours in the rain. He worked muttering the names of his planks, the way you talk to children. In the morning he asked me not to say anything: he didn't want anyone to know he'd been scared. I'd been scared too.
textes.La nuit où le cristal a clignoté, ses al: The night the crystal flickered, her seaweed was curling up. I sat down among her rows, hands on the soil. I fell asleep there. In the morning, she gave me a cracker. I don't like crackers. I ate it.
textes.La nuit où le cristal a clignoté, toutes: The night the crystal flickered, all my seaweed curled up at once. I thought I'd lose everything. In the morning I found Pélagos asleep in the middle of my rows, hands on the soil, as if to warm it. He said he just happened to be there. I gave him a cracker. He sighed, and he ate it.
textes.La nuit où le cristal s'est éteint un in: The night the crystal went out for a moment, Mum hugged me so tight I had the marks of her shell necklace on my cheek. The next day she said it was nothing. But since then, she weaves at night, without stopping. Mum weaves when she's scared.
textes.La nuit où le vent a soufflé toutes les: The night the wind blew out every candle at the festival, Nourredine ran from one lantern to the next with a single wick, and relit the square one star at a time. I made a tale of it: the lantern-maker who gave back the stars. He pretends he's never heard it.
textes.La nuit où mon piano a joué cet air inco: The night my piano played that unknown tune, it was three in the morning. The next day, at the Bielle, I told Céleste about it in a whisper. She took out her notebook, leafed through it and went pale: that night, the blue glow of Stoneheart had pulsed twice a minute instead of once. Same hours. We've told no one. Well, except you.
textes.La nuit tombe, mes étoiles se lèvent. Je: Night is falling, my stars are rising. I'm the happiest man in Arcanelle.
textes.La nuit vient. Rê entre dans la Douat, l: Night is coming. Ra enters the Duat, the world below. Twelve hours of travel, twelve gates, and Apophis lying in wait.
textes.La nuit, beaucoup rentrent chez eux. Si: At night, many people go home. If you want to talk to someone, come during the day.
textes.La nuit, c'est encore mieux : les lumièr: At night it's even better: the lights, the moon on the water… and the kick echoing across the bay.
textes.La nuit, c'est l'heure du jaguar. Mon he: Night is the jaguar's hour. My hour.
textes.La nuit, des lumières vertes bougent au: At night, green lights move in the graveyard. Gros-Louis says they're fireflies. Gros-Louis has never been to the graveyard at night.
textes.La nuit, il y a de la lumière dans les g: At night, there's light in the caves behind the Skala. Not fishermen. Lanterns moving about.
textes.La nuit, j'allume la lanterne, là-haut,: At night I light the lantern up there, at the top of the mainmast. The boats find their way home by it.
At night, I steer by Anselme's lighthouse. When it works.
textes.La nuit, je raconte aux petits l'histoir: At night, I tell the little ones the story of the moon who didn't want to go to bed. They always fall asleep before the end. So does the moon.
textes.La nuit, je regarde la mer et je compte: At night, I watch the sea and count the lights. The village's, the jungle's… and sometimes a blue glow, under the water, far to the west. I've never told anyone.
textes.La nuit, je turbine mes glaces avec le l: At night, I churn my ice creams with milk from the goats on the hill. At ten, I open the kiosk in front of the beach. Nina wants to be an ice-cream maker, she watches me like an inspector. Kiki pinched my coconut recipe. And the other evening, as I was closing, I saw a little white shadow dash off with a croissant in its mouth. My oh my, what a life!
textes.La nuit, l'Arbre-Mère brille. Maman dit: At night, the Mother Tree glows. Mum says it watches over us. I think it's only pretending to sleep.
textes.La nuit, l'île est plus calme. On entend: At night, the island is quieter. You can hear the sea.
textes.La nuit, la brume monte des mares. C'est: At night, the mist rises from the ponds. That's my hour. That's why my name is Brume. It means mist.
textes.La nuit, la cité est différente. Les rue: At night, the city is different. The streets are empty, the lanterns purr, and you can hear the lava of the Circle of Fire whispering. I know every street lamp by name. The one by the market is called Gustave. It flickers when it's happy.
textes.La nuit, la jungle appartient aux jaguar: At night, the jungle belongs to the jaguars. I'm going home.
textes.La nuit, la lampe de Nolwenn reste allum: At night, Nolwenn's lamp stays lit till midnight. She's sewing something big, I can hear her pulling the canvas. One day, I found a bit of silver thread on the deck, glowing in the dark. I put it in my pocket, without asking. Secrets are like leaks: if you press on them, they get bigger.
textes.La nuit, la mer brille quand on marche d: At night, the sea glows when you walk in it. Mistral says it's the plankton dancing too.
textes.La nuit, les oreilles de tout le monde b: At night, everyone's ears glow a little. Even mine! Look when it gets dark.
textes.La nuit, les pierres brillent un peu. Je: At night, the stones glow a little. I stay close to them. They don't like being alone in the dark.
textes.La nuit, les étoiles se battent contre l: At night, the stars fight against the sun. We pray that it wins.
textes.La nuit, mes herbes sentent plus fort. L: At night, my herbs smell stronger. So do foxes, says Roux. He talks nonsense.
textes.La nuit, mes éclairs se voient de très l: At night, my bolts can be seen from very far away. It's pretty.
textes.La nuit, on compare nos oreilles. Elles: At night, we compare our ears. They both glow a little. Mochi says hers glow more because they're longer. I say that's cheating, because they droop, so they glow on the ground. We asked Grandpa. He said “Shh”. That means it's a draw.
textes.La nuit, quand je m'entraîne, elle me re: At night, when I train, she watches me from her window. She counts my laps. On her fingers. … She only has ten fingers. After ten, she starts again at one. In the morning she says: “Auntie, four laps!” I did fourteen. … I say: “Yes. Four.”
textes.La nuit, quand je rentre, j'entends des: At night, on my way home, I hear bones clacking over by the graveyard. I play louder. It doesn't work, but it reassures me.
textes.La nuit, quand la mer est calme, on ente: At night, when the sea is calm, you can hear the hull singing. The young ones say it's the wood shifting. I say the Léviathan remembers.
textes.La nuit, quand tata s'entraîne, je compt: At night, when Auntie trains, I count her laps from the window, on my fingers. One, two, three… ten. And then I start again. In the morning I tell her: “Auntie, four laps!” She says: “Yes. Four.” I'm super good at counting.
textes.La nuit, sous sa couverture, j'entends G: At night, under her blanket, I hear Grelot counting her coins. Very quietly. One, two, three… Sometimes she stops in the middle and sighs. I say nothing. I pretend to be asleep. A friend also knows how not to hear.
textes.La nuit, sur le Cœur-de-Pierre, il y a u: At night, on Stoneheart, there's a blue glow that pulses, very slowly. Once a minute. Like a heart. I've recorded it two hundred nights in a row.
textes.La nuit, un chevalier veille. Et grignot: At night, a knight keeps watch. And nibbles a little.
textes.La nuit, à Ramure, les oreilles brillent: At night, in Ramure, ears glow a little. All of them! So Myrtille and I compare. Mine are floppy, so they glow downwards, like lanterns. Hers are pointy, they glow upwards. Together they light up the whole path to the bakery. Mummy says we'd do better to sleep.
textes.La nuit, à la belle étoile, Amine a voul: At night, under the stars, Amine wanted to count the walking stars. “One… two… three…” He fell asleep at four, mouth open, sand in his hair. I kept counting for him. Until morning. He doesn't know.
textes.La paix ! Demain, j'irai prendre un thé: Peace! Tomorrow, I'll go and have tea at her place. In the rain, with my new umbrella. And you know what? We decided together: the Larsen Festival is coming back this summer, on the Main Stage. Both villages, together. It will be sunny AND it will rain, and it will be perfect. Thank you, my messenger. You've given this island its rainbow back.
textes.La partie de l'élection, je la raconte t: I tell the story of the election game every year. The two balls, the jack, the whole square holding its breath. I got down on my knees with my postman's tape measure, measured, and said: “Aristide. By one centimetre.” Raymond cried robbery. He's still crying it. Me, when I tell it, I wink. Nobody knows why.
textes.La passe entre les deux jetées est étroi: The channel between the two jetties is narrow. A galleon like the Murène Noire had to be towed in by ten boats. The pirates rowed. That made me happy.
textes.La patronne. Elle m'a sorti de sa tavern: The landlady. She threw me out of her tavern. By the ear. Nobody had ever done that to me. I respect her. Hm. A lot.
textes.La peintre de l'hôtel, Clémence, cherche: The painter at the hotel, Clémence, is looking for natural pigments. She asked me for red coral. I don't sell coral!
textes.La peintre. Elle s'installe sur mes crén: The painter. She's been setting up on my battlements every morning for four months. She disturbs the guard. … She paints well. She disturbs it all the same.
textes.La peinture de la coque : huit couleurs: The hull paint: eight colours to choose from, and you can change it for free whenever you like.
textes.La petite Ignatia vient m'écouter sur la: Little Ignatia comes to listen to me on the square, with a hood over her head. Her crown of horns pokes through the hood like two towers. So I announce: “Tonight, a story for a little stranger.” Everyone turns towards her, then pretends nothing's going on. The whole city plays along with me. It's our finest show.
textes.La petite Lou. Elle a soixante-quinze an: Little Lou. She's seventy-five, she's sunk three ships, she carries a club. To me, she's the little cabin girl who was hungry. She knows it. She lets me say it.
textes.La petite Margot est la seule à avoir fa: Little Margot is the only one who has ever made my automaton think. Eleven minutes on a single move. I'd never seen that. Neither had it, I believe.
textes.La petite Nebet a perdu son chat. Elle p: Little Nebet has lost her cat. She cries all day long. The cat must be strolling quietly among the dead, up on the plateau. Cats love tombs: it's nice and cool in there.
Little Ortie wants to be my apprentice. She invented a machine that picks up bolts. The machine ate my broom. I was very impressed. And a bit worried about my shoes.
textes.La petite Yasmine ne mange pas de poisso: Little Yasmine doesn't eat fish. Except her mother's tagine, and my sardines. Because my sardines aren't fish. They're sea birds.
textes.La petite boule de buis de Raymond et Ma: Raymond and Marcel's little boxwood ball. Without it, there's no pétanque on the square.
textes.La petite cuillère se met à tourner. Pui: The teaspoon starts to turn. Then faster. Then the cup turns too. You put it down, carefully.
textes.La petite lanterne de Lumina, la lantern: Lumina the lantern-maker's little lantern: a living ember flame that never goes out. With it, you light the seven Great Lanterns of Pandémonia.
textes.La petite lumière recule dès que tu tend: The little light backs away as soon as you reach out your hand, then comes back to dance above the mushrooms. It needs a shelter… Faelar, the Village Elder, might know.
textes.La petite pluie… Wilfried la sent avant: Light drizzle… Wilfried feels it before anyone else: his brass arm itches. I send him graphite ointment. You don't have anything that itches, I hope?
The girl fixes everything she touches. That's good, generally. But I wish she'd leave the Petit Piston alone. She's sleeping. You don't wake what's sleeping.
textes.La petite-fille de mon amie Garance. Ell: The granddaughter of my friend Garance. She has her nose, her tongue and her way of scolding me. I pretend to obey, she pretends to believe me. She's the one who sews the fox ears I give away.
textes.La peur, je connais. Mieux que vous ne c: Fear, I know all about. Better than you'd think. It's not a flaw, it's a flight instrument. Go up when you're ready. I'll stay down below, waving to you.
textes.La pierre chante, toute seule, une note: The stone sings, all by itself, a low soft note… but no one answers it.
textes.La pierre gravée qui animait un golem de: The carved stone that brought a highland golem to life. Bramm, the gate guard, asks for it as proof of your worth.
textes.La place, c'est le cœur de Port-Azur. Le: The square is the heart of Port-Azur. Mornings, the market; afternoons, pétanque; evenings, sweethearts on the benches.
textes.La place, c'est le plus beau terrain de: The square is the finest pitch in the archipelago. The gravel is perfect, and so is the shade of the plane trees.
textes.La place, le quai, la promenade. Un arrê: The square, the quay, the promenade. A regulation stop at Bruno's kiosk: three ice creams a day, state secret. My back, which Doctor Roux treats via the back door. Rosalie shouting my ice-cream stops to the whole harbour. Bernard running on the quay despite my sign. And the case of Margaux's croissants, the most serious of my career. Croissants. Can you imagine.
textes.La plage de Port-Azur, c'est la plus bel: Port-Azur beach is the most beautiful in the archipelago. The sand sings when you walk on it. Listen closely.
textes.La plage est divine. L'eau est si claire: The beach is divine. The water's so clear you can see the starfish on the bottom. The lifeguard says you can pick them up, if you hold your breath.
textes.La plage est la plus belle du monde. Et: The beach is the most beautiful in the world. And the cruellest: it swallows wedding rings.
textes.La plage est parfaite : le sable pour da: The beach is perfect: sand for dancing, sea for cooling off, and nobody to wake up except the seagulls.
textes.La plage, à l'est du port, c'est là qu'o: The beach, east of the port, is where we haul up the boats that aren't going out. In winter, they all sleep there, keel in the air.
textes.La plage… Le sable chaud, le bruit des v: The beach… The warm sand, the sound of the waves. Yes, I understand. A little.
The name board, I've already carved it. Ahead of time. Nobody knows. And in the corner, I carved a little whale, with its spout. I'll bring it out the day of the hull, I want to see his face. … What? Why are you smiling? He doesn't know. Eh? He doesn't know, I'm sure of it.
textes.La pluie et le soleil ont reçu leur offr: The rain and the sun have received their offering! The temple drums begin to beat all by themselves, and the great round slab slides aside: a staircase leads down beneath the Great Temple.
The quetzal feather? It was a trial run. A very well-painted parrot feather, I admit. I wanted to see if he'd recognise a real one. He didn't notice a thing. The rain noticed. He came to give it back to me, on his head, in front of my customers. My customers applauded. That day, I sold twice as much. Thanks, cousin.
textes.La plus authentique de l'archipel, milor: The most authentic in the archipelago, milord! Painted… er, snowed this very morning!
textes.La plus authentique de la semaine, milor: The most authentic one this week, milord! Hand-snowed!
textes.La plus belle Nuit des Lanternes depuis: The most beautiful Night of Lanterns in a thousand years! (Lumina still has sparks in her hair.) You're one of us now. Keep the lantern: it will always know you.
textes.La plus belle pour la loi !: The finest one for the law!
textes.La plus noire, pour l'amin !: The blackest one, for the amin!
textes.La poignée de la tyrolienne était trop h: The zip line handle was too high for him. He'd jump. Miss. Jump again. One day, he nearly went over the edge of the platform. So I shortened the handle rope. For safety. Purely for safety. He catches it without jumping now. He says thank you every time. I answer “Halt.”
textes.La pointe est battue par les vents. Les: The point gets battered by the wind. The agaves like it. So do I.
textes.La poissonnerie est sur le quai, à côté: The fish stall is on the quay, next to old Charbonnel's harbour master's office. In the Harbour the water is warm, because of the volcano. The fish there are fat and lazy. The best kind.
textes.La porte ! Le poste le plus important. T: The gate! The most important post. Everyone walks past you, you say hello to everyone, and you only let the nice ones in. Easy. Except when the Archduchess wants to go out.
textes.La porte de l'Arbre-Mère est ouverte… Tr: The Mother Tree's door is open… Three centuries I kept it shut, and a human opens it in a week. Well. Bravo.
textes.La porte de l'Arbre-Mère s'est ouverte !: The Mother Tree's door has opened! The whole village is talking about nothing else.
textes.La porte de mon poêle avait un gond cass: The door of my stove had a broken hinge, and it had to be fixed without letting the fire die down. Jos came one evening after closing, with leather gloves and pincers, and worked all night in the heat, his beard singed. By morning, the hinge was new and the fire hadn't budged. He wouldn't take anything for it. Just breakfast.
textes.La porte de sécurité, au sud, s'enfonce: The safety door, to the south, sinks into the floor with a hiss. The stairs lead down to the Automated Warehouse.
textes.La porte des Neuf Cercles: The door of the Nine Circles
textes.La porte des Neuf Cercles dit « prenez u: The gate of the Nine Circles says “bring a coat”. I take that sentence very seriously. Down at the bottom, in the Cocytus, the cold is so sharp it freezes hems. Wear several layers. One layer is elegance. Three layers is wisdom.
textes.La porte des Neuf Cercles porte une insc: The gate of the Nine Circles bears an inscription: “All ye who enter here, keep hope (and bring a coat)”. The part in brackets was added by Her Highness's great-grandmother. She felt the cold. I approved.
textes.La porte du milieu est murée par une dal: The middle door is sealed by a stone slab. On either side, two stone wheels are carved: numbers in dots and bars, and the twenty days of the sacred calendar. “When the date of the world's creation returns, Kukulkan will open his door.”
textes.La porte du temple, en haut de Kukulkan,: The temple door, at the top of Kukulkan, only opens on the day of creation. The two stone wheels must show the date when the present world was born.
textes.La porte est ouverte ! Derrière, un esca: The door is open! Beyond it, an immense staircase plunges into the dark, beneath Stoneheart. A warm breath rises from it. (E: go down)
The door creaks. I prefer the window.
textes.La poste est au Port de Cendre, à côté d: The post office is at the Ash Port, next to the harbour master's office. All the island's mail goes through my hands. And my wings. I know every address, every door, and every dog. Especially the dogs.
The post office sells postcards too. Unfair competition, that is. Nadine is lovely, mind you.
textes.La postière. Elle sourit trop. Je crois: The postwoman. She smiles too much. I think she knows things. Postwomen know everything.
textes.La potion Gérard avance ! Pour l'instant: The Gérard potion is coming along! For now, it just makes you coo. But that counts: cooing is speaking pigeon.
