textes.La potion d'Aëlwen, l'herboriste du Bois: The potion of Aëlwen, the herbalist of Bois-Doré: golden sap and moon herbs. Restores three hearts.
textes.La potion de magie, c'est ma fierté : de: The magic potion is my pride and joy: moon dew, three drops of honey, and a kind thought while you stir. Without the kind thought, it tastes of cabbage.
textes.La potion devient violette et sent le ch: The potion turns purple and smells of cabbage. The frog sneezes. Failed!
textes.La potion fait « plop » et sent la tarte: The potion goes “plop” and smells of pie. The frog looks interested, but stays a frog.
textes.La potion fume, une odeur terrible envah: The potion smokes, a terrible smell fills the room. The frog holds its nose. Well, it tries to.
textes.La potion se met à hululer. La grenouill: The potion starts to hoot. The frog blinks, very worried.
textes.La prairie est pleine : des fleurs dans: The meadow is full: flowers in hair, checked shirts, holey umbrellas. Everybody is dancing.
textes.La première année, je lui ai offert un s: The first year, I gave her a faience scarab by Ptahmosé. She gave me a jade bead, green as the river in spring: for them, jade is the breath of life. I wear it under my necklace. The scarab, I'm told, guards the altar in her house.
textes.La première année, les requins fonçaient: The first year, the sharks charged at the dome every night. Nobody knows how to fight, where we come from. So I taught myself, outside: wait, wait some more, and strike at the last moment. I left a bit of fin out there, and all my fear. Since then, they circle. They don't come in. Dumb, but not that dumb.
textes.La première fois qu'elle a fait une soud: The first time she made a perfect weld, she was sixteen. Eight months I'd been making her redo everything. I ran my thumb over it. Nothing to say. I said nothing. I put my lamp next to hers. She understood. She always understood everything. Too fast. Hm.
textes.La première fois qu'elle est entrée chez: The first time she came into my place, she shook her wings. Glitter everywhere. On the table, in the soup, in my beard. I was finding it till spring. Hence the name. She earned it. Every bit of glitter.
textes.La première fois qu'elle est entrée à la: The first time she came into the forge, she looked at my best sword, the one in the window. One second, no more. “There's a flaw, there, near the guard.” There was. I'd seen it. Nobody else had ever seen it. I took the sword out of the window and melted it down. There.
textes.La première fois qu'elle est montée chez: The first time she came up to my place, I hid my axe behind my back. She smiled, put her hand on my kapok tree and said: “It's happy with you.” Happy! A tree! I told her I don't give discounts to elves. She laughed. So did Clou, the traitor.
textes.La première fois qu'il est passé, trois: The first time he came by, three of my parrots shouted “Landlubber!” at him. I know who taught them that: Rhubarbe, the day he boarded with me. I told Petit-Pierre it was a compliment. He believed me. I gave him a green feather. He still wears it in his bandana. It tugs at my heart.
textes.La première fois que Brindille est venue: The first time Brindille came to deliver a letter, she flew in through the big window and knocked over two shelves of dictionaries. Pages flew all over the room. She helped me tidy everything up, whispering apologies every ten seconds. The next day, I put up a sign: “Here, we whisper. And we don't fly.”
textes.La première fois que Capucine m'a confet: The first time Capucine confetti'd me, I was coming out of the workshop with a notebook. Poof! Pink, yellow, green. I looked at my notebook, all speckled, then at the sky, and I applauded. She thought I'd get cross. Get cross at an explosion that comes down in colours? That's all I've been looking for for forty years!
textes.La première fois que Gorgoth est entré d: The first time Gorgoth came into the library, he had to get on his knees to fit through the door, and he whispered so loudly that three readers jumped. He wanted poems “not too long, because of the big fingers”. I picked him a collection of three-line poems. He read it in an hour. He came back the next day, with tears in his eyes.

The first time Gorgoth got into the big pool, the water rose all at once, and a wave swept all the customers over the edge. Me included. We all ended up sitting on the flagstones, soaked, laughing. Gorgoth kept saying “sorry, sorry”. The next day, I started building the Gorgoth Bath.
textes.La première fois que Lulu est revenue de: The first time Lulu came back from her fairies, she had golden pollen on her cheeks and eyes as big as saucers. I didn't ask her if it was true. I asked her what the music was like. She brought me back a glowing petal. I keep it in my beanie, with my treasures.
textes.La première fois que Lumina est venue ch: The first time Lumina came to fetch a flame, she was eight. She ran. The flame went out on the way. She came back crying. I told her: “You carry a flame like a secret: gently, and without running.” She set off again with tiny steps, and she made it. Since then, she's never run with a flame again.
textes.La première fois que Silas est passé dev: The first time Silas walked past my stall, Bartholomé cried: “The skull, the skull!” Silas stopped dead. He went all pale. Then he took off his tricorn and bowed to the parrot, very low, the way you salute a captain. Bartholomé spread his wings wide. I'd never seen either of them do that.
textes.La première fois que j'ai laissé Nina so: The first time I let Nina ring the departure bell, she rang it too early, with all her might. I cast off by reflex. Three passengers were left on the quay with their suitcases, and a gentleman with a cake. We turned back. The gentleman gave me a slice of cake to console me. Nina got two.
textes.La première fois que j'ai livré une lett: The first time I delivered a letter to the library, I flew in through the big window and knocked over two shelves of dictionaries. Pages flew everywhere. I helped Ombreline tidy it all up, whispering sorry every ten seconds. The next day, there was a sign. I know it's meant for me.
textes.La première fois que j'ai porté la robe: The first time I wore Grisette's sequinned dress, I played so fast that a sequin came loose and shot straight into the mouth of Madame Hurla, who was shouting next to me. Hurla stopped dead: the longest silence in the history of the square. Grisette sewed the dress back up that very evening, with better-attached sequins.
textes.La première fois que j'ai posté ma lettr: The first time I posted my letter “To L.”, Nadine looked at the envelope, then at me, and blurted out: “It's Lucas, isn't it?” I nearly took my letter back. I made her swear silence, hand on the yellow postbox. She swore. The week after, a tourist smiled at me and said: “Good luck with Lucas.”
textes.La première fois que j'ai pris le Zéphyr: The first time I took the Zéphyr to Tazira, I had a trunk of sparkling apple juice and a single idea: cheap saffron. Lalla Aïcha received me at the souk. We haggled for three hours and four teapots. In the end, I had her saffron, she had my apple juice, and we'd both lost money. The finest day of my life as a merchant.
textes.La première fois que j'ai vu Bartholomé,: The first time I saw Bartholomé, he looked at me with his round eye and said: “The skull, the skull.” In Barbe-Sanglante's voice. Exactly. It knocked me off my feet. I took off my tricorn and saluted him, the way you salute a captain. On board, we called him Cannonball. He spread his wings. He recognised me, I'm sure of it.
textes.La première fois que j'ai vu une clochet: The first time I saw a little silver bell above the forge door, I asked where it came from. Borin grunted: “From a she-bear.” I didn't dare ask which one. Now, every time I run in, it rings, and I stop dead. I think that's the whole point.
textes.La première fois que je l'ai changé en g: The first time I turned him into a frog, he caught a moth with his tongue, first go. He looked so proud! When he turned back into a goblin, he said: “Hmph, disgusting.” But afterwards I saw him watching the moths go by. Longingly.
textes.La première fois que je l'ai vu, il desc: The first time I saw him, he was getting off the jungle boat with a bag, a machete and the look of a kid lost at the market. He asked me where the coconut palms were. I told him: “There are three here, and they belong to the mayor.” He sat down on his bag and looked at the sea for a very long time.
textes.La première fois que je suis entré dans: The first time I went into the Ash Wood, I was six. I saw a mushroom that glowed, then another, then a hundred! I decided to give them all names. I've named forty. The biggest is Gérard. The smallest is Pétunia. Mum says I must always go with someone. I say yes.

The first time I got into the big pool at the Baths, the water rose all at once, and all the other bathers went over the edge, on a wave. Bulle laughed so hard he fell into the water too. The next day, he had the Gorgoth Bath built. Just for me. With a step my size.
textes.La première fois que je suis entré à la: The first time I went into the library, I had to go through the door on my knees, and I whispered so loudly that three readers jumped. I asked for poems “not too long, because of my big fingers”. Ombreline didn't laugh. She brought me a little collection of three-line poems. I cried on the fourth page. It was about a cloud.
textes.La première fois que je suis entrée chez: The first time I went into his place to sell my nectar, I shook my wings a bit too hard. He was sweeping up glitter for a week. He still had some in his beard come spring. That's when he started calling me “glitter-gnat”. You have to admit I sort of deserved it.
textes.La première fois que je suis entrée dans: The first time I went into Zigomar's workshop, a rocket whizzed over my head, the ceiling went boom, and Zigomar came out of the smoke shouting “Eureka!”. I knew straight away it was my calling. Now I go and sweep up at his place every day. I count the bolts. I'm learning.
textes.La première fois que je suis monté en ha: The first time I climbed to the top of the mainmast, I didn't know how to get down. Fil-de-Fer came to fetch me. He told me: “Don't look down, look far away.” I looked far away, and I saw the Pic du Borgne with a cloud on top, like a hat. I wasn't scared any more. Since then, I always look far away.
textes.La première fois que je suis passé devan: The first time I walked past his stall, three parrots shouted at the same time: “Landlubber!” Joe went bright red and said it was a compliment, that land is very precious on an island. Afterwards, he gave me a green feather. I put it in my bandana. I think it was to say sorry.
textes.La première fois, Madame Rita m'a regard: The first time, Madame Rita looked at me for a long while, and said: “I see a house. Three rooms. And beds you won't be making.” I spilled my cup. I'd never told her about it! Well, I think. I talk a lot, so I'm never sure.
textes.La première fois, c'était devant le jury: The first time, it was in front of the jury. My finest waltz. On the third beat of the repeat, the piano went “atchoo” and a bubble came out from under the lid. Then two. Then twelve. Basile's soap steam had been creeping into the cylinder all afternoon. The jury applauded the bubble. Not the waltz. The bubble.
textes.La première fois, elle a regardé mon ass: The first time, she looked at my plate and said: “I don't eat fish.” I said: “That's lucky. These aren't fish, they're sea birds. They fly underwater.” She looked at me for a long time, then: “All right.” She ate six. She pretends to believe me. I pretend she believes me.
textes.La première fois, il est arrivé au milie: The first time, he arrived in the middle of the night, with dark rings under his eyes: the galleon's pump was creaking too loud to sleep. He stood in front of me without a word. It was the Admiral who spoke: “A ROOM, NOT TOO STEADY!” I gave him the one above the stable. The camels shift about, it rocks a bit. He slept like a child.
textes.La première fois, je n'avais rien à offr: The first time, I had nothing to offer the queen. So I painted a moonflower on the back of her hand, with blackberry juice. She looked at it for a long time. Nobody had ever painted anything for her, she said. Since then, I bring her real moonflowers. But I've heard she didn't wash her hand for two days.
textes.La première fois, je suis entré dans sa: The first time, I wandered into his shop by chance and saw a Barbe-Sanglante map in the window. I sniffed it: the ink still smelled of fresh cuttlefish. I said so out loud. The customers heard. By evening, there was a queue all the way to the well, and everyone wanted a refund. He didn't speak to me for a month.
textes.La première fois, je suis entrée à La Mu: The first time, I walked into La Murène Ivre to make a delivery, jugs in my arms. A pirate tried to help me and broke one. Mama Lou banged her club on the counter: “Girlie, how much?” I said double. She paid. Then she turned to the pirate. He paid triple.
textes.La première fois, je suis venue acheter: The first time, I came to buy two bowls. I stayed three hours watching her throw. Then I wanted to try. My bowl became a plate, the plate became a pancake, and the pancake fell off. Halima said: “You paint. I throw.” We've never argued over roles since.
textes.La première fois, le Lord a pris une bou: The first time, the Lord picked a snow globe off the shelf — a lighthouse in the snow, the cheapest one. He shook it, stood there a whole minute without a word, and asked: “How much?” I doubled the price. He paid without arguing, in gold. Then he said: “This will be the favourite piece in my collection.” I felt ashamed. Not for long. But I felt ashamed.
textes.La première goutte, Majesté. Comme chaqu: The first drop, Your Majesty. Like every morning.
textes.La première nuit de Lulu, elle a marché: Lulu's first night, she walked into the sea and her feet lit up blue. She shouted “The sea is dancing!”. I came down to explain plankton to her. She nodded very seriously and said: “Yes. Plankton dances.” We were both right, so it became official.
textes.La première nuit sous le dôme, il ne res: The first night under the dome, there was no wheat left, nothing. Salicorne, Marée's grandmother, pressed seaweed between two hot stones and handed me the first cracker. It was dreadful. I wept as I ate it, and it was the best meal of my life. Marée makes exactly the same one.
textes.La première nuit, il ne voulait pas de m: The first night, he didn't want me in the workshop: “Nobody paints in a lantern maker's.” I stayed outside, on the doorstep, painting what I could see through the door. The second night, there was a stool on the doorstep. The third, the stool was inside. He never said a thing. Neither did the stool.
textes.La première nuit, j'ai cru que l'île ava: The first night, I thought the island had a sick heart. Then I understood it was music. I hid behind a kapok tree to listen, and my feet started moving on their own. Elves don't dance to that kind of music. Officially.
textes.La première nuit, j'ai cru voir une comè: The first night, I thought I'd seen a comet. It was coughing. It was Achille. Since then, I've followed him in the great telescope, and every morning I slip a note under Adèle's door: the time, the coughs, the heading. One night, he saw me. He came and flew right in front of the lens and waved at me in the eyepiece. I knocked over my bottle of coffee.
textes.La première nuit, j'ai trouvé la fenêtre: The first night, I found the library window ajar. I borrowed a collection, brought it back at dawn, and wrote “Thank you” in the ledger. The next evening, there was a lit candle near the window. I wrote “Thank you for the candle”. Since then, there's always a candle. I don't know how to thank her enough.
textes.La première nuit, j'avais si peur que j': The first night, I was so scared I cried in my hammock. Barbe-Sanglante came by. The most terrible pirate of all time. He sat down on a barrel and told me a story, until I fell asleep. The next day, another. He used to say: “A story, cabin boy, is a lantern you light in the dark.” I've never put mine out.
textes.La première plongée de Zoé, elle a bu la: On Zoé's first dive, she drank half the bay. She came up coughing and shouted: “It's like dancing, but you can't shout!” I laughed, really laughed, for the first time in a long time in the water. Since then, whenever I go down, I think of what she said. I'm a little less scared.
textes.La première sardine de chaque saison, je: The first sardine of each season, I bring it to him. At the end of the jetty. I put it on the stone, next to his line. He says nothing. I say nothing. I leave. Every year. In the evening, Fatima grills it. Hm. It's the best of the season. I know. I chose it.
textes.La première t'attend peut-être sous le v: The first one may be waiting for you under the village…
textes.La première, la Perle du Jardin, est l'â: The first, the Garden Pearl, is the age of life: it sleeps in the giant clam of the coral reef, to the north-east. Go up to it and open it gently; the sharks guard it.
textes.La prochaine fois, tu tiendras ta langue: Next time you'll hold your tongue.
textes.La puce et la carte ! (Elle glisse la pu: The chip and the chart! (She slides the chip into the dashboard; the chart unrolls by itself and becomes a hologram spinning above the controls.) Navigation… connected. Astral engine… warm. Hull… (She taps it.) Clack. Perfect. The Star Glider is ready! Call it the same way you called your old machine, climb aboard, and go see the sky from way up high. And be careful: it's fast. Really fast. Comète is going to be jealous.
textes.La pêche, c'est de la patience et du sil: Fishing is patience and silence. Two things tourists don't have.
textes.La quinzième année de mon mandat, je lui: In the fifteenth year of my term, I had the town medal presented to him, “for saving a future mayor”. Speech, brass band, the lot. He climbed onto the platform in his boots, took the medal, and said: “I should've left him one more minute, he'd have learned to swim.” The whole square laughed. So did I. A little.
textes.La rafale t'a emporté dans le gouffre !: The gust swept you into the chasm! You wake up at the start of the corridor, a little singed. Wait behind a pillar for the wind to die down, then run.
textes.La rafale t'a emporté dans le vide… tu t: The gust swept you into the void… you wake at the entrance of the hall, aching all over. Wait under cover, in the bends of the walkways, until the wind dies down.
The net-mender. Her net. My anchor. Hm. She sends me papers. Every week. With numbers that keep growing.
textes.La recette de Mamie Silex : des crosses: Granny Silex's recipe: crushed fern fiddleheads, toasted on a flat stone by the fire. Nice and crispy, a little smoky. Restores two hearts (and "extra squares", says Granny).
textes.La recette de Mustapha : trois heures de: Mustapha's recipe: three hours of cooking, with honey and cinnamon. I follow it to the minute. My sardines come out black and sticky, like polished boots. If you ask me, it still needs more honey. I went to ask him. He looked at the sea for a long time, his shoulders shaking, with emotion, and he said: “Yes. More honey.”
textes.La reine ? C'est elle qui m'a ramassée s: The queen? She's the one who picked me up off the throne steps. She lets me plant everywhere. Almost everywhere. She smells like summer rain, and she always knows what the Tree is thinking.
textes.La reine ? C'est la plus gentille du mon: The queen? She's the nicest in the whole world! She's the one who told me I didn't need to glow. And she laughs at all my jokes. Well, half of them.
textes.La reine ? Je la sers depuis la première: The queen? I've served her since the first line of my first scroll. She carries the city the way the crystal carries the dome. And she no longer sleeps. It's on record, and it worries me.
textes.La reine ? La seule à qui j'obéis. Enfin: The queen? The only one I obey. Well, almost always. She's patient with me. Too patient. Sometimes I wonder what she knows.
textes.La reine ? Une grande dame. Avec une pet: The queen? A great lady. With a short memory for debts: the mother-of-pearl throne, I'm still waiting to be paid. Six hundred years.
textes.La reine Oriane ? La plus belle fée que: Queen Oriane? The most beautiful fairy I've ever seen, and she's the one who gave me my wand. I admire her so much I'm scared of disappointing her.
textes.La reine Oriane est douce comme la lune,: Queen Oriane is as gentle as the moon, and a little sad, like it. She watches over the tree that drinks from all our islands. She calls me “little painter”.
textes.La reine Oriane pose deux doigts sur ton: Queen Oriane places two fingers on your forehead… A warmth, a golden spark, wings of light around you: you know teleportation magic! You can return in an instant to any place you've already visited: press T on PC, or open the journal, Map tab, “Teleport”.
textes.La reine Oriane écoute l'Arbre, et moi,: Queen Oriane listens to the Tree, and I listen to the queen. She often comes to sit at the edge of my pond. She thinks I don't see when she's worried. I see.
textes.La reine a les cheveux tout blancs parce: The queen's hair is all white because she's a thousand years old. Well, that's what Triton says. Don't tell her!
textes.La reine a vite compris qu'un vent comme: The queen soon realised that a wind like me needed keeping busy. She gave me a letter. Ever since, I've carried messages between the islands. Fairies travel in the blink of an eye, poof, somewhere else. I know how to do it. But I don't. Where's the fun if you don't see the scenery? And the scenery, I'm the one who ruffles it.
textes.La reine attend les trois Perles. Le cri: The queen is waiting for the three Pearls. The crystal grows weaker every night.
textes.La reine est la seule personne du dôme q: The queen is the only person in the dome who really likes my crackers. I bring her one every morning. She doesn't pay. For her, I don't keep count. Almost not.
textes.La reine m'a confié la Porte. Je ne l'ai: The queen entrusted me with the Gate. I've never left it. Well… almost never. For her, I'd stand guard a thousand years more.
textes.La reine ne dort pas, la nuit. Je le sai: The queen doesn't sleep at night. I know because sometimes I don't either. One night I saw her on the palace steps, all alone, looking at the crystal. I sat down beside her without saying anything. After a while she said: “You should be asleep.” I said: “So should you.” We stayed anyway.
textes.La reine ne dort plus. Elle regarde le c: The queen doesn't sleep anymore. She watches the crystal all night. The pearls, {surnom}… the pearls.
textes.La reine ne dort plus. Je lui chante, le: The queen doesn't sleep anymore. On sleepless nights, I sing her her mother's lullaby. She pretends she isn't crying. I pretend I don't see.
textes.La reine, elle est très belle et très vi: The queen is very beautiful and very old, a thousand years I think! She answers all my questions, even the silly ones. Especially the silly ones.
textes.La rive sud est fertile, mais le plateau: The south bank is fertile, but the plateau behind it is desert. The realm of the dead. Nothing grows there, except silence.
textes.La rivière ! Tu es plus malin que tu en: The river! You're cleverer than you look. Not that that's hard, mind you.
The red one is very pretty, you know.
The hive is falling asleep. So am I.
textes.La réclame du Bazar dit : « Ici, rien ne: The Bazaar's advert says: “Here, nothing is good for anything.” One morning, the press dropped a letter: “Here, nothing is good for anyting.” I ran to the Bazaar to apologise. Too late: the queue stretched all the way to the Grand Square. Everyone wanted to see what an “anyting” was good for. Sales tripled. Now she asks me for a typo every week.
textes.La salle chante, grâce à toi. Écoute : m: The room sings, thanks to you. Listen: even the drops fall in rhythm now.
textes.La salle d'Osiris. Au milieu, un sarcoph: Osiris's chamber. In the middle, an open sarcophagus… empty. Four doors lead to the chapels of Isis.
textes.La salle de Thot. Un dieu à tête d'ibis: Thoth's chamber. An ibis-headed god before a great papyrus; in front of the door, three stone drums covered in signs. And in the shadows, bandages that move…
textes.La salle de la Pierre du Soleil. Un disq: The Sun Stone chamber. An immense stone disc above the south door, and four empty niches beneath it. Four doors, each marked with a sun. Near the entrance, a painted codex.
textes.La salle des Saisons ! Il y a une stèle: The Hall of Seasons! There's a stone tablet that says in what order the seasons bloom. The flowers change colour when you touch them.
The throne room falls silent again. Behind the throne, on the right, a door leads to the Tower of Storms…
textes.La salle du trône. Des vitraux, des bann: The throne room. Stained glass, banners, and at the far end the throne of the Sky Kings… Two suits of armour break away from the pillars!
The blowpipe is the Twins' weapon. Hunahpu and Xbalanque hunted birds with it. So do I. But I miss more often than they did.
textes.La sauvegarde a échoué (disque plein ou: Saving failed (disk full or protected folder?). Your previous game is intact.
textes.La semaine dernière, Fañch a fait sembla: Last week, Fañch pretended to sleep in the bottom of the boat so I could steer alone to the north point. I came about all by myself, cleanly. On the way back, he said: “Not bad, for a sailmaker.” I threw a bucket of water at him. He laughed like a seal. He'd earned both.
textes.La semaine dernière, Kevin a ramené un t: Last week, Kevin towed back a tourist in a straw hat, clinging to “Wave 4” like a lifebuoy. Yannick was waiting on the pontoon, arms wide open: “So, how was the ride?” The gentleman rented a second hour. I said nothing. I wrote three pages in the register.
textes.La semaine dernière, Tibo a pris sa prem: Last week, Tibo caught his first sardine. He shouted so loud that half the quay came to look. Then he wanted to keep it alive in a bucket, “so it can see the world”. It saw the world for an hour. Afterwards, we grilled it at Mustapha's. He said thank you to the sardine before eating it.
textes.La semaine dernière, Tobias m'a laissé t: Last week Tobias let me hold the tar pot. He says it was his first job too, at seven. I got it all the way up to my elbows. He didn't say anything for a long time. Then he said: “Not bad.” I think it's the nicest compliment he's ever given anyone.
textes.La semaine dernière, Victor m'a fait une: Last week, Victor made me a one-of-a-kind globe: inside, a little lord in a top hat, in the snow, with a croissant in his hand. The nose is a bit big. I wept. The price was a bit big too. I wept twice.
textes.La semaine dernière, il a trempé une lam: Last week, he quenched a red-hot blade in Dagna's cauldron. PSSSHHH! Dagna came out with her spoon raised. I swore it was an accident. It was. But the stew had a little taste of iron, and the whole terrace said it was better.
textes.La semaine dernière, j'ai pris ma premiè: Last week, I caught my first sardine! All by myself, on the end of my line, all shiny. I wanted to keep it alive in a bucket. I called it Bertha Two. Ahmed told me a sardine in a bucket is a sad sardine. So I had it grilled at Mustapha's. The best sardine of my whole life. Sorry, Bertha Two.
textes.La semaine dernière, j'ai trouvé trois b: Last week I found three bottles under my kelp. I swapped his honey brew for seaweed tea, and waited. That evening, at the tavern, Corentin took a big secret gulp, pulled a terrible face, and said very loudly: “Ma doue, what a brew!” He never complained about it.
textes.La semaine dernière, je l'ai laissée seu: Last week, I left her alone at the helm all the way to the north point, and pretended to sleep. She came about all by herself, neat as you like, like an old hand. On the way back, I said: “Not bad, for a sailmaker.” She threw a bucket of water at me. Among sailmakers, that means thank you.
textes.La semaine dernière, une de mes bulles a: Last week, one of my bubbles swallowed a star-shaped confetto. It rose above the square with its star inside, like a little sky. Capucine watched it go with the look of a delighted culprit. I said nothing. It's the most beautiful bubble I've ever made. Well, that we've ever made.
textes.La semaine où elle a dansé les pas de Ta: The week she danced the Tazira steps, I put a sign on my stall: “Apples blessed by the dancer”. Two coins extra per apple. Sold out before noon! Lilas laughed for a week. She never blessed a single apple. Well, she walked past them. That counts.
textes.La semaine où j'ai dansé les pas de Tazi: The week I danced the Tazira steps, Grelot sold “apples blessed by the dancer”. Two coins extra per apple! I laughed for a week. The worst part is it worked: Bedaine wanted one, for a pebble, and he swore it tasted of moon.
textes.La semaine suivante, Colette m'a raconté: The following week, Colette told me the end of the novel, without my asking. The duel on the cliff, the letter found again, the kiss in the storm. Her eyes were wet. “She writes well, this Delarive. She must have suffered a great deal.” I bought peaches, nodding. A lot of peaches. Gérard still doesn't understand why.
textes.La septième Grande Lanterne s'allume ! D: The seventh Great Lantern lights up! From one end to the other, Pandémonia shines like a necklace of embers. Lumina is going to be over the moon. And when night falls, in the Great Square… the party!
textes.La seule fois où elle m'a laissé être ca: The only time she let me be captain, I sank the ship in the fountain on the square. The ship was the bench next to it. We jumped into the fountain, that was the shipwreck. She shouted: “Captain overboard!” And she took back the hat. Forever, I think.
textes.La seule forgeronne qui parle moins que: The only smith who talks less than Bramm. Good hands, a grindstone that sings. When she sends me someone, they're worth the trouble.
textes.La seule interview de l'histoire faite p: The only interview in history conducted during an explosion: that was us! Rosette was asking me about my new boiler when the boiler answered for itself. We both ended up under the table, her with her pencil, me with my goggles. She kept taking notes. Next day's headline: “The Professor Speaks Out”. Magnificent.
textes.La seule interview de toute l'histoire d: The only interview in the whole history of the Gazette conducted during an explosion. The professor said: “One second, I'll finish my sentence.” Then: “Under the table!” We finished the interview under the table, covered in soot. Question: “Professor, what are you looking for?” Answer: “My roof!” Excellent quote.
textes.La soupe aux cailloux, c'est surtout les: Pebble soup is mostly about the vegetables around it. The pebble is for the flavor. And for tradition. Come back tomorrow, I'll make more.
textes.La spécialité de Marée : des algues du d: Marée's speciality: seaweed from the dome, dried under the crystal and pressed. It tastes of the sea. A lot. Restores two hearts.
What comes next? All right, listen.
What comes next? All right, listen.
textes.La suite ? Le Cœur-de-Pierre, au milieu: What happened next? Stoneheart, in the middle of the island, and the Gate of the Four Seals. They say each of the island's peoples guards one. The highlands' one, the mists' one, the desert's one… and the fourth. Ours. Nobody knows what became of it.
textes.La suite… on ne se connaît pas encore as: The rest… we don't know each other well enough yet, {surnom}. Come back and see me.
The rest… we don't know each other well enough yet, {surnom}. Come back and see me.
A surprise! The wisest of answers. The ball is offended, but I approve. The future is like a present: you don't shake the parcel.
textes.La surprise… Sage, très sage. Les cartes: The surprise… Wise, very wise. The cards don't like to be rushed. I'll turn them face down on the table, and we'll say no more about it. But they know.
textes.La table trois est libre… enfin, presque: Table three is free… well, almost.
Table three is the best one.
textes.La tarentelle, ça fait tourner la tête e: The tarantella makes your head and your feet spin at the same time!
textes.La tarte de Berthe Chaudron, qui « ensor: Berthe Chaudron's pie, which "bewitches everyone". Melting, spiced, still warm. Restores three hearts.
textes.La taverne est dans le château arrière,: The tavern is in the sterncastle, under the poop deck. The big windows, there, at the back — that's the old captain's gallery. The finest sunset on the island, and you get to sit down.
textes.La terre de Tazira est rouge, comme les: The earth of Tazira is red, like the ramparts. It's the same earth: the ramparts are just very big jugs.
textes.La terre du cimetière remue… Des mains d: The earth of the graveyard stirs… Bony hands emerge from the graves!
textes.La terre ferme ! Un terrien ! Bon. On ne: Dry land! A landlubber! Well. You don't choose your passengers. Sit in the middle, look at the horizon, and don't do what the goat did.
textes.La tisane de Pivoine, à la sauge et à la: Pivoine's herbal tea, with sage and meadowsweet. They say it makes you sleep like a dormouse. Restores one heart.
textes.La toute première teuf, il y a six ans,: The very first party, six years ago, nobody came. Just me, four speakers and the sea. Around three in the morning, a bald guy with a long beard sat down in the sand. He listened for an hour, got up, fixed the crackling speaker with a fishbone, and sat back down. He never left.
textes.La troisième borne. Sa flèche montre une: The third marker. Its arrow points to a big crescent dune, very close… The dune seems to have moved since the arrow was engraved: it has advanced at least ten paces.
textes.La troisième semaine, je n'avais plus de: In my third week, I couldn't pay for my room any more. I went down to the desk with a canvas under my arm, red with shame. Edmond looked at it for a long time, smoothed his moustache, and said: “The management accepts.” I asked to thank the management. He replied: “The management is very busy.”
textes.La troisième, la Perle de la Fosse, est: The third, the Trench Pearl, is the age of the deep: on an altar at the bottom of the Jellyfish Trench, north of the city. Jellyfish sting your skin: slip between them, slowly.
textes.La tyrolienne du Guet, c'est trop bien !: The zip line at the Lookout is the best! Croc-Gris says it's for emergencies. I have an emergency every day.
textes.La tyrolienne du Guet, mon oncle dit qu': The Lookout zip line, my uncle says it's mostly for kids. And for me. Once, I went down it with one of Caramel's skewers between my teeth, to save time on snack time. I dropped it halfway. It landed right on my uncle's head. He looked at it, ate it, and said: “Nothing to report.”
textes.La tyrolienne, je l'ai tendue pour les a: The zip line, I strung it up for alarms. The children use it every day. And Grisou. A grown-up. A wolf. A relief guard. Once, he had a skewer between his teeth. It fell on my head. I ate it. He never asked for it back. He learned something that day.
textes.La tyrolienne, là-haut ? C'est pour desc: The zip line up there? It's for getting down fast, in case of alarm. Truth is, it's mostly the kids who use it. And Grisou.
textes.La télékinésie ne trouve rien à attraper: Telekinesis finds nothing to grab over there.
textes.La tête te tourne un peu. (+1 de force): Your head spins a little. (+1 strength)
textes.La vague t'emporte ! Abrite-toi dans une: The wave sweeps you away! Shelter in an alcove, on the sides, when you hear it rumble.
textes.La vase bouillonne… Une gueule énorme so: The slime bubbles… An enormous maw rises from the black water: VIEILLE-DENT!
textes.La vasque frémit… puis se tait. Ce n'est: The basin shivers… then goes quiet. That is not the order of the world.
textes.La veille d'une course, je lui ai vendu: The day before a race, I sold him an apple pie I'd made myself. With a bit of grated carrot inside. Quite a lot, actually. He ate the whole thing, he ran, he won anyway. Ever since, he's suspicious of all my pies: he sniffs them, flips them over, taps them. It makes me laugh every single day.
textes.La veille de chaque mesure, Hapou m'appo: The day before each measuring, Hapou brings me a basket of barley, “for nothing, just like that, between neighbours”. I thank him, I measure, I leave him exactly the same field. The next day, he comes to take his basket back. It's been twelve years. It's become a sort of festival. A festival where nobody laughs, but a festival.
textes.La veille de chaque mesure, je lui porte: The day before each measuring, I bring him a basket of barley. Just like that, between neighbours. He thanks me, he measures, he leaves me the same field. The next day, I take my basket back: it was no use. It's been twelve years. He never eats the barley. He keeps it for me. We're polite, where I come from.
textes.La veille de la dernière fête de l'Aube,: The day before the last Dawn festival, a tall, absent-minded elf trod on my violets. I scolded him for an hour. He smiled. The next day I invited him to dance, so he'd understand what it's like to be trampled on. He danced terribly. I married him at dawn. Elandor still treads on my violets.

The day before the last Dawn festival, an elf came out of a bush with a basket and scolded me for an hour because I'd trodden on her violets. The next day, she asked me to dance with her. To make amends, she said. I dance terribly. She married me anyway.
textes.La veille du sacre, en sertissant le hui: On the eve of the coronation, as I was setting the eighth ruby, my tweezers slipped. A crack. Too late to find another. So I cut a shard of red glass, all night, by candlelight. By morning, the crown was perfect. Almost. Nobody noticed a thing. Ninety years of nobody noticing a thing. Shh.
textes.La vie au camp ? On se lève avec le sole: Life at the camp? We get up with the sun, we garden, we weave, we play music, and in the evening we gather around the fire. The only problem is that we miss Rainville a little. We used to party together.
textes.La vieille Fatima. La seule de Tazira qu: Old Fatima. The only one in Tazira who really remembers my grandfather, and she answers me in riddles! She's making fun of me. With great talent.
textes.La vieille bibliothécaire qui m'a tout a: The old librarian who taught me everything knew the Nine Circles from books. She made me learn by heart what Minos, the judge, asks: what you've seen along the way. She used to say: “A traveller who knows how to look has nothing to fear from a judge.” I've never been down there. But I know all the answers.
textes.La vieille boussole de marine de Barnabé: Barnabé's old ship's compass. It shows what you're really looking for. Usually, north.
textes.La vieille canne de Barnabé. Équipe-la,: Barnabé's old fishing rod. Equip it, go up to the water and hold the click to cast.
textes.La ville ? Avec ses scribes, ses marchan: The town? With its scribes, its merchants, its gossip? Hm. Each to their own. Me, I prefer my boundary stones. Even when Amenemhat measures them.
textes.La vingt-quatrième enceinte. Celle de dr: The twenty-fourth speaker. The one on the right, right at the top. The clearest. The one that stays in tune even when the wind turns. I named her Yaya. … Yaya doesn't know. She asks me her name every week. I say: “Later.” You won't say anything, {surnom}. Right.
textes.La vitrine des îles est complète ! Les L: The Showcase of the Islands is complete! The Lumens will queue all the way to the Spire to see it. I wrote the labels myself. The seashell is labelled “little house of the sea.” The turnip, “running vegetable, not to be left unattended.” Here: a nebula flower, the most beautiful one in the Bazaar, and a few of those discs you like so much. And come back! There are other islands. There are always other islands.
textes.La voie d'eau est bouchée. Le Léviathan: The leak is plugged. The Léviathan thanks you, and so do I. Here, some coins, and the galette Gwenola gave me this morning. I'm not hungry any more, I'm happy.
textes.La voilà, toute chaude ! Et mon histoire: Here it is, piping hot! And my story?
textes.La voix de Zéro… Oui. Sa puce a grillé l: Zéro's voice… Yes. His chip burned out last week. A Z Series, the very first series of androids. Nobody has any left. Except maybe… Cargo. The big dockworker on the Drone Quay. He keeps all the old parts in the containers at the end of the quay. Go and ask him, and bring me the chip.
textes.La voyante de la promenade m'a dit que G: The fortune-teller on the promenade told me Gérard would find his camera thanks to “someone who walks a lot”. Is that you?
textes.Lac Napolitain\nBaignade interdite : la:
Neapolitan Lake
No swimming: the sauce is hot,
and they say you come out all red.
textes.Lac des Long-Cous. Eau calme, Long-Cou b: Long-Neck Lake. Water calm, Long-Neck drink, Long-Neck eat big trees. Before, Old Flint swim there. Before being old. Very long ago. Yesterday, maybe.
textes.Laisse-le dormir, petite. Il est fatigué: Let her sleep, girl. She's tired.
Give him a chance. And a cup.
Let me explore the island first.
textes.Laisse-moi deviner… Rien à signaler ?: Let me guess… Nothing to report?
Let me sleep one more bar.
textes.Lait de coco, jus de mangue et une ombre: Coconut milk, mango juice and a paper umbrella. Toni's recipe (or Kiki's, depending on who you ask). Restores two hearts.
textes.Lalla Aïcha a le meilleur safran de l'îl: Lalla Aïcha has the best saffron on the island, and she knows it. She sells it to me too dear, every week. And every week, she sneaks in an extra pinch. We only argue for show.
textes.Lalla Aïcha déteste la sardine. L'odeur,: Lalla Aïcha hates sardines. The smell, she says. But she says my cumin is the only cumin in Tazira put to good use. Coming from her, that's a medal.
textes.Lalla Aïcha me vend du safran en me rega: Lalla Aïcha sells me saffron while looking at me like a criminal. For her, saffron is for eating. For me, it's for wearing. We'll never agree, but we're fond of each other.
textes.Lalla Aïcha, la marchande d'épices de Ta: Lalla Aïcha, the spice merchant of Tazira. A magnificent thief. Forty spices on her stall, and she beats me at every haggle. I adore her.
textes.Lalla Fatima ? Soixante-dix ans qu'elle: Lalla Fatima? Seventy years she's been listening to me, and seventy years she's been correcting me. When I tell the tale of the pirate of the caves, she says: “That's not how it was. I was there.” And nothing more.
textes.Lalla Fatima a ramendé les filets de mon: Lalla Fatima mended my father's nets, then mine. She's the only one who still calls me “the little one”. In front of my fishermen. I respect her more than anyone. And I blush.
textes.Lalla Fatima m'a tout appris. Quatre-vin: Lalla Fatima taught me everything. Eighty years old, nearly blind, and two thousand knots a day. Me, a thousand. I admire her, and I worry about her. She never rests.
Lalla Fatima, do rest a little.
textes.Lalla Fatima… devant mes pêcheurs !: Lalla Fatima… in front of my fishermen!
textes.Lance loin, là où l'eau devient bleu som: Cast far, where the water turns dark blue. Big fish like the deep, like philosophers.
textes.Laquelle ? … Euh. Je connais pas de Gert: Which one? … Er. I don't know any Gertrude.
textes.Laquelle ? … Je veux dire : quelle Gertr: Which one? … I mean: what Gertrude?
textes.Larbi ne prend plus rien au bout de la j: Larbi doesn't catch anything any more at the end of the jetty. Nothing. So, some evenings, I stop at Zohra's before him, buy a nice fish, and slip it into his basket while he puts away his rod. He comes home proud. He says: “Not bad, today.” I say: “Not bad.” He doesn't know. Well… with Larbi, you never know what he knows.
textes.Larbi, mon mari. Cinquante-huit ans de m: Larbi, my husband. Fifty-eight years married, and he still hasn't managed to beat me at knots. He fishes without catching anything. He lights his lighthouse. He's a good man.
textes.Le BADGE DE L'USINE GRISE ! Une photo de: The GREY FACTORY BADGE! A photo of a smiling robot, and the words: “ACCESS TO ALL FLOORS — even -5”. With this, the door at the bottom should open.
textes.Le Baron Barthélemy a perdu son plus bea: Baron Barthélemy has lost his finest hat, the plumed one: the wind carried it over the castle wall. It was seen flying over the rooftops of the Middle Town… then nothing more.
textes.Le Belvédère des Couleurs, en haut du Gr: The Lookout of Colours, at the top of the Great Oak — the whole island, all white; it will take a lot of colours!
textes.Le Bois Tors est le plus vieil endroit d: The Twisted Wood is the oldest place on the island. The trees there have been twisting for a thousand years to look at the stars through the leaves. The mushrooms glow at night. It's pretty, and a little unsettling.
textes.Le Bois Tors, au sud du Cercle, n'est pa: The Twisted Wood, south of the Circle, isn't wicked. It's old. Old trees twist round to see who's passing.
textes.Le Bois de Cendre, au sud-est, est plein: The Ash Wood, to the south-east, is full of wonders and paths that all look alike. Pépin runs off there the moment my back is turned. If you ever see a little imp with ivory horns over there talking to mushrooms… tell him his mother is waiting for him.
textes.Le Bois de Cendre, c'est le plus bel end: The Ash Wood is the most beautiful place in the world! The trees are black, the leaves are embers, and the mushrooms glow like lanterns! Mum says I must never go there on my own. Never ever.
textes.Le Bois des Hachures — des chênes et des: The Hatching Wood — oaks and birches drawn in ink, stroke by stroke
textes.Le Bois des Riffs — des chênes et des bo: The Riff Wood — oaks and birches; the wind plays guitar in the leaves
textes.Le Bois-Doré. Des arbres si grands que l: Bois-Doré. Trees so tall their crowns are lost in golden light… A path of lanterns winds toward the elves' village.
textes.Le Bois-Doré… Des arbres de soixante mèt: The Bois-Doré… Trees sixty metres tall? That'd make a lot of shovel handles. No, I'm joking. Half joking.
textes.Le Borgo des Coquillettes — le hameau de: The Borgo of the Macaroni — the followers' hamlet: houses of every colour, a trellis, a long table, and a smell of warm bread
textes.Le Boulevard des Néons — la grande avenu: The Neon Boulevard — Neopolis's great avenue, from the quay to the south of the city
textes.Le Cabaret des Cailloux. Ce soir : le pl: The Pebble Cabaret. Tonight: the funniest of the little Moai. (He wrote that on the poster himself.)
textes.Le Café Feedback : une odeur de chocolat: Café Feedback: a smell of hot chocolate and wet wool, a jukebox glowing pink, a cat sleeping on an amp… and a drip falling, drip, drop, into a cup placed on table three.
textes.Le Café Feedback est fermé. Sur la porte: The Feedback Café is closed. On the door: “We open when we wake up.” Through the window, cups, an old jukebox… and a cat sleeping on the amp.
textes.Le Camp des Fleurs — des yourtes en rond: The Flower Camp — yurts in a circle around the fire, pennants, painted buses, and drums that never sleep
textes.Le Campement du Clan — un feu, un totem,: The Clan Camp — a fire, a totem, drying racks… and square eyes watching you from behind the rocks
textes.Le Capitaine Charbonnel a sa table au Di: Captain Charbonnel has had his table at the Diable Repu for thirty years. He orders a hot sulphur punch and tells the story of the ash storm. I know it by heart. The waves grow every evening.
textes.Le Capitaine Charbonnel m'a appris à vol: Captain Charbonnel taught me to fly. Without him, I'd still be wearing a big coat to hide my wings. He lends me his telescope, he tells me about his storm, and he's never made fun of my too-big wings.
textes.Le Capitaine Charbonnel m'a rapporté un: Captain Charbonnel brought me back a twisted harpoon. A gargoyle had bent it with its teeth. He said: “Your harpoon ties itself in knots.” I answered: “Your gargoyle eats iron.” A draw.
textes.Le Capitaine Charbonnel m'achète des har: Captain Charbonnel buys harpoons from me against the gargoyles. He brings them back bent and asks me why. I tell him his gargoyles eat iron. We laugh. We start again.
textes.Le Capitaine Charbonnel raconte la même: Captain Charbonnel has told the same ash storm every evening for thirty years. Every time, the waves get higher. Now they're the size of the volcano.
textes.Le Capitaine Charbonnel veille sur le po: Captain Charbonnel watches over the port as if it were his own children. He tells the same storm story every evening, and each time, the waves get bigger. He's the one who married Grumbald and me, on his quay.
Captain Floc'h is me, Salomé. And I'm not a captain.
textes.Le Capitaine Rigatoni m'a promis de m'ap: Captain Rigatoni promised to teach me to fish. That was twelve years ago.
textes.Le Capitaine Sans-Chair lève son sabre :: Captain Fleshless raises his sabre: “Up, lads!” Skeletons rise from the ground!
textes.Le Capitaine Sans-Chair s'effondre en un: Captain Sans-Chair collapses into a heap of bones. The eyes of Skull Rock go dark… The mouth of the skull awaits you.
textes.Le Capitaine Sel, le grand-père de Croc: Captain Sel, Croc's grandfather? I knew him. A real rogue. He came here, yes, with a chest. He left without it. I'll say no more.
textes.Le Capitaine fait tournoyer son sabre to: The Captain whirls his sabre all around him!
textes.Le Cercle t'a vu arriver avant moi. Je s: The Circle saw you coming before I did. I am Ysolde Lunevoile. I keep the Moonstones. Nobody touches them without my knowing. Nobody.
textes.Le Cinquième Soleil tourne, et Cipactli: The Fifth Sun turns, and Cipactli sleeps for good.
textes.Le Cinquième Soleil. Un grand feu, deux: The Fifth Sun. A great fire, two altars: gold and jade on one side, reeds and thorns on the other. On the wall, a fresco: gods around the fire, and one of them leaping.
textes.Le Cirque des Os — des os partout. Et, q: The Bone Circus — bones everywhere. And, somewhere, an enormous breath
textes.Le Clan te couvre de cadeaux (surtout de: The Clan showers you with gifts (mostly shiny coins found in the river).
textes.Le Cocyte, au fond des Neuf Cercles, c'e: The Cocytus, at the bottom of the Nine Circles, is the opposite of our nights: a night without any light at all, cold as a silence. If you go down there, take a flame. A small one is enough. A small flame in the great cold is already a poem.
textes.Le Cocyte, le lac gelé, le Neuvième et d: The Cocytus, the frozen lake, the Ninth and last Circle. It snows, under the earth. Far at the bottom, a throne of ice.
textes.Le Colosse a peur du tonnerre. J'ai dit: The Colossus is afraid of thunder. I said it was a flaw. Wilfried said: “A robot that's afraid, Master, is a robot with a heart.” Hm. I didn't answer. I didn't fix the flaw either.
textes.Le Colosse fait peur aux enfants. Il ne: The Colossus frightens the children. He wouldn't hurt a fly. In fact, he's scared of flies.
textes.Le Colosse lâche un jet de vapeur brûlan: The Colossus lets out a jet of scalding steam all around it!
The Colossus waved at me. I swear. With his big iron hand.
textes.Le Colosse, c'est mon chef-d'œuvre. Il d: The Colossus is my masterpiece. It was meant to guard the city against storms. It's afraid of thunder. I think it gets that from me. Hm. The rest of the time, I look for a sweeper that sings. I don't speak to Héloïse any more. In the evening, I sit on the bench on the promenade. So does she. Each at our own end.
The Colossus is my masterpiece. He was meant to guard the city against storms. He's afraid of thunder. I haven't worked out why yet.
textes.Le Cratère du Lac — une eau immobile, co: The Lake Crater — still water, the color of the sky, at the bottom of the volcano
textes.Le Cristal de Givre s'illumine sous ta m: The Frost Crystal lights up under your hand: you've crossed the Mirror Lake. Borée will be proud of you.
textes.Le Cénote sacré, au nord-ouest, c'est un: The sacred Cenote, to the north-west, is a door to the world below. In the evening, bats come out of it by the hundred. Camazotz, the death bat, commands them, they say.
textes.Le Cœur de la Flèche, le grand cristal q: The Spire's Heart, the great crystal that keeps Astralys afloat, is growing weak: three shards have broken off and fallen onto the island. Volt, the energy engineer, can weld them back with three astral crystals, but then the Heart's light must be restored, right at the top of the Spire.
textes.Le Cœur de la Montagne bat sous nos pied: The Heart of the Mountain beats beneath our feet. It's growing weak. When it stops, the lava will wake. Not today. Not tomorrow. But one day.
textes.Le Cœur de la Montagne… Une pierre de fe: The Heart of the Mountain… A fire stone, big as a barrel, that beats deep in the volcano. It keeps the lava asleep. Since the golems woke, its beat has grown weak. Nori will tell you more. One day, perhaps, we'll need you, big one.
textes.Le Cœur du Volcan rallumé: The Heart of the Volcano rekindled
textes.Le Cœur ronronne de nouveau comme au pre: The Heart purrs again as it did on the first day, my child. I'm no longer cold inside. I think I'll take a little nap beside it. To celebrate.
textes.Le Cœur va bien, Frère Cendrin ?: Is the Heart all right, Brother Cendrin?
textes.Le Cœur-Brasier brûle haut et clair, grâ: The Ember Heart burns high and bright, thanks to you. The whole city is warm. Even Asmodin smiled. Twice. I counted.
textes.Le Cœur-Brasier n'est plus qu'une petite: The Ember Heart is now nothing but a small blue flame. It needs the Eternal Flame, lost deep in the Nine Circles.
textes.Le Cœur-Brasier, c'est le grand feu sous: The Ember Heart is the great fire under the Forge Cathedral. As long as it burns high, Pandémonia is warm, the lanterns shine, the bread rises. When it grows pale, the whole city shivers. And a shivering demon is a sad sight.
textes.Le Cœur-Brasier, le grand feu de la Cath: The Ember Heart, the great fire of the Forge Cathedral that warms all of Pandémonia, grows paler by the day. A chill is rising from the Nine Circles beneath the cathedral: they say the Frost Titan has carried off the Eternal Flame.
textes.Le Cœur-de-Pierre, au centre, c'est un p: Stoneheart, in the centre, is a perfectly round plateau ringed by cliffs. Nobody goes up there. At the foot of its western face, there's a giant gate: the Gate of the Four Seals.
textes.Le Deuxième Cercle. Sur un trône de bron: The Second Circle. On a bronze throne, MINOS, judge of the underworld, crowned, his long tail coiled around him. He waits for you to present yourself.
textes.Le Diable Repu est au Port de Cendre, su: The Diable Repu is at the Ash Port, on the quay. Sailors come for the punch, merchants for the news, and the news for the merchants. Everything that gets said in Pandémonia gets said here first.
textes.Le Disquaire : des milliers de pochettes: The Record Shop: thousands of sleeves, a smell of cardboard and old paper, and a turntable spinning softly.
textes.Le Disquaire est fermé. Une affiche, col: The Record Shop is closed. A poster, stuck on crooked: “Back after rehearsal. Do not touch the records. Or the cat.”
The Dungeon of a Thousand Steps.
textes.Le Fieux Filas raconte des hiftoires dep: Old Thilas hath been telling thtorieth for fifty yearth. Half of them are true. The problem ith knowing which half. Me, I believe the half that thuitth me.
The Cursed Fort, on the eastern point. The cannons are still there. I go and see them sometimes. The skeletons leave me alone. They find me scary.
textes.Le Four Éternel, c'est mon arrière-arriè: The Eternal Oven was lit by my great-great-grandfather with an ember from the Ember Heart, four hundred years ago. It has never gone out. When he handed it over to me, my father said: “Bobor, you can botch a brioche. You can botch a batch. But never let the oven get bored.” I sing it lullabies at night.
textes.Le Four Éternel, c'est mon trésor. Quatr: The Eternal Oven is my treasure. Four hundred years without going out. At night I sing it lullabies so it doesn't get bored. The neighbours say it's the oven singing. I don't correct them.
textes.Le Garde-Marée bascule sur le dos ! Vite: The Tide Warden flips onto its back! Quick, strike it!
textes.Le Garde-Marée se remet sur ses pattes !: The Tide Guard gets back on its feet!
textes.Le Gardien du Cœur est apaisé ! La Lame: The Guardian of the Heart is calmed! The Heart Blade, 200 coins, one more heart, and a title: “Hero of the Four Peoples”. The circle of light, north of the hall, will take you back to the surface.
textes.Le Gardien du Cœur s'effondre… Les veine: The Heart Guardian collapses… The veins of fire fade. Above, the great crystal stops beating so hard; its red light turns golden, soft as an evening sun.
textes.Le Gardien frappe le sol : des créatures: The Guardian pounds the ground: creatures from all four wings come running!
textes.Le Glisseur stellaire des Lumens (Ionie,: The Lumens' Star Glider (Ionie, at the Astralys Spaceport)
textes.Le Goff est le meilleur cartographe que: Le Goff is the best cartographer Carène has ever had. He's also the only one who wants to open a gate our ancestors closed. I respect him. I keep an eye on him.
textes.Le Gouverneur Lagrange est l'homme le pl: Governor Lagrange is the most talkative man I've ever won at dice. I gave him back after three days. He ate all my honey and gave me speeches at breakfast.
textes.Le Gouverneur Lagrange s'est proclamé go: Governor Lagrange proclaimed himself governor all on his own. Nobody voted. Nobody protested either. He buys the rounds.
textes.Le Gouverneur interdit les bagarres ! …: The Governor forbids brawling! … on Sundays.
textes.Le Gouverneur m'a commandé la carte offi: The Governor commissioned the official map of Port-Coutelas from me. He wanted boulevards, an opera house and a statue of himself. I drew them. They don't exist. My finest map since the continent.
textes.Le Gouverneur m'achète tout ce qui brill: The Governor buys everything that glitters from me: his gold tricorn, his chain, his medals. He pays in official promises. I have a drawer full of promises. They're very well written.
textes.Le Gouverneur veut faire du Sans-Pitié l: The Governor wants to make the Merciless the flagship of the Port-Coutelas navy. Port-Coutelas has no navy. And the Merciless isn't his. She belongs to the sea. And a little to me.
textes.Le Gouverneur, mon chou, c'est un grand: The Governor, sweetie, is a big child with a gold tricorn. He makes speeches, he promises pontoons, and he buys the rounds. The port likes him. So do I. But I'm the one who decides.
textes.Le Grand Boucan restera dans les mémoire: The Great Boucan will be remembered: Granny Barricade raises her fist on the mezzanine, Clou smiles (really, he does), and the whole pit chants your name. Go and see Rouille afterwards!
textes.Le Grand Cristal faiblit. Il se nourrit: The Great Crystal is fading. It feeds on three Pearls of Light, one for each age of the sea… They were scattered when the sharks came. Bring me back the {manque}, and the dome will live another thousand years. I'll give you the trident of our kings.
textes.Le Grand Marché est au nord-est de la Ba: The Great Market is in the north-east of the Lower Town: my spices, Kraxx's weapons, Vespérine's potions and Bobor's bread. It smells of fire, sugar, iron and sulphur. It's the smell of home.
textes.Le Grand Moaï te voit, avec ses yeux de: The Great Moai sees you, with his coral eyes. He looks pleased. Well… for a mountain.
textes.Le Grand Spaghetti Volant entrouvre un œ: The Great Flying Spaghetti half-opens an eye, looks at you, and closes it again. It's still sulking. (Reverend Father Farfalle, at the temple, might know why.)
textes.Le Grand Spaghetti Volant redescend douc: The Great Flying Spaghetti slowly comes back down… A long noodle stretches toward you and touches your shoulder, very gently. You have just been Touched by His Noodly Appendage. (It tickles, and it smells good.) Go and see Reverend Father Farfalle!
textes.Le Grand Spaghetti Volant te fait un pet: The Great Flying Spaghetti gives you a little noodle wave. (Nobody knows how it stays up in the air. The followers say: “by the sauce!”)
textes.Le Grand Temple a deux sanctuaires. Celu: The Great Temple has two shrines. Tlaloc's, the blue one, wants water: a rain jar. Huitzilopochtli's, the red one, wants fire: burning copal. Bring both, and the door of the Fifth Sun will open between them.
textes.Le Grand Troc ! Ici, pas de pièces : on: The Great Swap! No coins here: we trade. One thing for another, and everyone goes home happy. Today, I'll take:
textes.Le Grand Troc, le vrai, c'est une chaîne: The real Great Swap is a chain: you give a pebble, you get an acorn, then a feather, then a vial… At the end, there's always something beautiful. I'll show you, if you like.
textes.Le Jardin Zen — des cerisiers en fleurs,: The Zen Garden — cherry trees in bloom, raked gravel… and silence, at last
textes.Le Lac Napolitain — un lac de sauce toma: The Neapolitan Lake — a lake of tomato sauce, calm and steaming (no swimming)
textes.Le Lac Souterrain. Des pierres plates fo: The Underground Lake. Flat stones form a ford… and giant frogs, big as barrels, stare at you. One of them, on the western islet, has a belly that glows with a copper sheen. It swallowed something.
textes.Le Lac des Long-Cous — des cous si longs: The Long-Neck Lake — necks so long they graze on the treetops
textes.Le Lord ! Six croissants par matin, depu: The Lord! Six croissants every morning, ever since he arrived. He eats one, the seagulls get the rest. It's crazy. And a bit beautiful, I think.
textes.Le Lord Pemberton, chambre douze, collec: Lord Pemberton, room twelve, collects strange objects. He pays well, and very dearly.
textes.Le Lord a voulu acheter mon perroquet en: The Lord wanted to buy my wooden parrot. For his collection. He offered three gold coins for it! I said no: without it, the Perroquet Bleu would just be plain Bleu — blue, and nothing else. He sighed, ordered a punch, and clinked glasses with the parrot. Since then, every evening, he says good evening to it as he comes in. The parrot doesn't answer. It's polite, but wooden.
textes.Le Lord a voulu m'acheter mon plumeau. I: The Lord wanted to buy my feather duster. He said a duster that had touched so many wonders was a wonder itself. He offered a gold coin for it! I refused: what would I have done room twelve with? He sighed. The next day, he asked if he could at least draw it. The duster. Not me.
textes.Le Lord anglais commande six croissants: The English Lord orders six croissants every morning. He only eats one. The rest he gives to the seagulls.
textes.Le Lord anglais de l'hôtel achète n'impo: The English lord at the hotel buys any “exotic” trinket. I sold him a sardine bone as a “sea dragon tooth”.
textes.Le Lord anglais paie toujours avec des p: The English Lord always pays in gold coins. I never have enough change.
textes.Le Lord de la douze paie bien, et très c: The Lord in twelve pays well, and very handsomely. He would also like my moustache. It is not for sale. It is not even for rent.
textes.Le Lord est un brave homme, riche comme: The Lord is a decent man, rich as the sea and gullible as a cabin boy. I sold him a sardine bone. I laugh about it. A bit less at night.
textes.Le Lord secoue chaque boule à neige cont: The Lord shakes every snow globe next to his ear before he buys it. “To hear the snow,” he says. I asked him what you can hear. He said: “Listen.” I listened. Nothing. Then a tiny whisper, like sugar falling. Ever since, I listen to all of them in the evening, when I close up. Don't tell anyone. They'll think I'm turning English.
textes.Le Lord vient tous les jours me demander: The Lord comes every day to ask for my jar of figs. It's not for sale. He's unbearable. He's polite. That's worse.
textes.Le Lord, c'est mon client en or. Littéra: The Lord is my golden customer. Literally: he pays in gold coins. Charming, generous, a bit mad. I never have change, and he never has anything else.
textes.Le Marché de Nuit — des lanternes, des m: The Night Market — lanterns, steaming pots, and a robot making noodles
textes.Le Marché de Nuit, c'est mon rituel. Un: The Night Market is my ritual. A bowl, a tea, and off to bed.
textes.Le Masque de Jade ! Le visage des rois d: The Jade Mask! The face of the kings of Yaxché, hundreds of little green squares. 150 coins, one more heart, and a title: “Victor of Xibalba”. A secret staircase, behind the altar, climbs back to the top of the temple.
textes.Le Mont Bolognaise — un volcan de sauce: Mount Bolognese — a tomato sauce volcano; the path winds up to the Cooking Pot
textes.Le Mont Fumant — il fume, il gronde, il: The Smoking Mountain — it smokes, it rumbles, it spits red. Don't step on the red!
textes.Le Mont Fusain\npar ici, le sentier du s:
Mount Charcoal
this way, the path to the summit
textes.Le Mont Fusain — une grosse colline rond: Mount Charcoal — a big round hill; the path climbs to the summit
textes.Le Muet ! Ce soir, tes quatre temps, com: Silent One! Tonight, your four beats, as always!
textes.Le Muet ! La cible est prête ?: Silent One! Is the target ready?
textes.Le Muet a parlé, une fois. Personne ne s: The Mute spoke once. Nobody knows what he said. Everyone who was there forgot. Strange, isn't it?
textes.Le Muet est le seul homme qui me compren: The Silent One is the only man who understands me without my opening my mouth. I'm the only one who understands his hands. Between the two of us, we make a whole conversation.
textes.Le Muet est mon client préféré. Il ne bo: The Mute is my favourite customer. He doesn't move, he doesn't talk, he doesn't complain, and he pays me in pearls. He has a little heart on his arm. Don't tell him I told you.
textes.Le Muet et Gros-Louis se disent les meil: The Mute and Gros-Louis say they're the best brawlers in port. They've never taken me on. They're scared. They're right.
textes.Le Muet n'a pas de couplet dans ma chans: The Silent One doesn't have a verse in my song. He has a silence. Four beats. The whole room goes quiet, and he nods. It's the finest part. Everyone says so.
textes.Le Muet ne dit rien, et c'est l'homme le: The Silent One says nothing, and he's the most reliable man in the archipelago. If I had to trust someone with the Widow's helm, it would be him. He wouldn't argue.
textes.Le Muet se dit champion. Il ne m'a jamai: The Mute calls himself champion. He's never faced me. He looks at me, I look at him, and nobody throws a punch. At least he doesn't mumble. He makes gestures. Gestures, I hear very well.
textes.Le Muet, c'est le seul qui me fait peur: The Silent One is the only one who scares me and makes me laugh at the same time. He doesn't talk, but he hits like a tide. We've never fought for real. We respect each other too much. And we're a bit scared, too.
textes.Le Muet, c'est mon meilleur copain. Il n: The Silent One is my best pal. He never contradicts me! He carries me back to the Widow every evening, on his shoulder. Hic! I see the port upside down. It's pretty, the port, upside down.
textes.Le Palais de l'Archiduchesse se dresse a: The Archduchess's Palace stands at the top of the Citadel, above the Circle of Fire. Four bridges lead to it. I beg you not to run on them: the lava has never cared for people in a hurry.
textes.Le Perroquet à midi et le soir, la plage: The Perroquet at lunch and in the evening, the beach in the afternoon, on my red towel. I'm the one who writes the menu on the board, with spelling mistakes on purpose to make Toni laugh. Lucas plays cards and loses. Django, my neighbour, slows the music down as soon as Lucas walks in; I've told him to stop. And Nadine, at the post office, has guessed everything. In short, everybody knows. Except him.
textes.Le Phlégéthon, une rivière de lave bouil: The Phlegethon, a river of boiling lava. Basalt rafts cross it all by themselves, in no hurry. On the other bank, an enormous beast with a man's face waits: Geryon.
textes.Le Plat de la Grande Réconciliation ? En: The Dish of the Great Reconciliation? At last! I've been telling him for a week: a sulking spaghetti is a hungry spaghetti! (She takes a nest of golden tagliatelle out of a basket, freshly made.) Here. I made them this morning, by hand, singing. Don't crush them, don't break them, and don't eat them on the way. I know you.
textes.Le Plateau des Anciens et le Grand Moaï: The Elders' Plateau and the Great Moai
textes.Le Plateau des Anciens — le Grand Moaï,: The Elders' Plateau — the Great Moai, and the circle of Moai with a door
textes.Le Popol Vuh, notre livre du conseil, ra: The Popol Vuh, our book of counsel, tells how the gods made people: first out of mud, which melted; then out of wood, and they had no heart; and at last out of maize. We are people of maize.
textes.Le Port de Cendre, c'est la Rade, au nor: The Ash Port is the Harbour, in the north-east of the island: the basalt quays, my black-sailed ships, Moloka's fish stall, Brindille's post office, the Diable Repu and the red-lit lighthouse. Everything that comes to Pandémonia passes through here. You too, as it happens.
textes.Le Professeur Malachar est le lecteur le: Professor Malachar is the most learned reader in the city, and the most overdue. He's owed me a book for sixty-three years. I write to him every year. It's become a correspondence.
textes.Le Professeur Malachar me doit un livre: Professor Malachar has owed me a book for sixty-three years. I write to him every year. Every year he replies that he's on chapter three. It's coming along.
textes.Le Professeur Malachar parle trop, digre: Professor Malachar talks too much, always digresses, and corrects the spelling mistakes on the canteen menus. He's the best teacher I ever had. He's the one who taught me that a mistake is a lesson.
textes.Le Professeur Malachar propose de passer: Professor Malachar offers to let you sit the Infernal Academy exams: the trial of flames, the trial of the contract and the trial of sparks. The jury is strict, but fair (and a little singed).
textes.Le Puits des Géants. Tout en bas, la gla: The Pit of the Giants. At the very bottom, ice. All around, stone giants, in chains. One of them, Antaeus, has no chains: he reaches his hand toward the landing.
textes.Le Quartier des Arcades — des écrans, de: The Arcade District — screens, games, and music made of little beeps
textes.Le Quatrième Cercle, celui des Avares. D: The Fourth Circle, that of the Misers. Two enormous weights, heaps of gold, two golden slabs in the floor. Push the weights (standing behind them) onto the slabs. The lever near the entrance puts everything back in place.
textes.Le Requin Borgne s'appelait le Fidèle, a: The Requin Borgne used to be called the Faithful: a king's galleon, brand new, that had been chasing us for a week. One moonless night, we boarded her from the stern. Gros-Louis trussed up the crew with his lumberjack knots, and we set them down on a beach with supplies. The figurehead, a golden shark, had lost an eye in the boarding. I renamed her that very morning.
textes.Le Requin Borgne, je l'ai pris à la mari: The Requin Borgne, I took her from the royal navy. They gave her up with all their hearts. Well… their hands were tied, but their hearts were in it.
textes.Le Rocher du Crâne, au bout de la Balafr: Skull Rock, at the end of the Balafre… I wanted to draw it up close. Its eyes lit up. I drew very fast.
textes.Le Roi Champignard tape du pied : « Mes: The Mushling King stamps his foot: “My little ones!” Three mushlings pop out of the moss!
textes.Le Roi Gélatineux tremble de toute sa ge: The Jelly King quivers all over… and splits! Little slimes break off from him!
textes.Le Roi Gélatineux tremble, gargouille un: The Jelly King trembles, gurgles one last time (“My crown… it was too small anyway…”) and spreads into a great puddle that smells of green apple. In the middle shines a jelly heart, like a giant candy.
textes.Le Roi des mares est doré, gros comme un: The King of the Pools is golden, big as a rabbit, and he looks at me. I swear it. He looks at me and he laughs. Fish laugh underwater, you just can't hear it.
textes.Le Rouage prend dans le moteur ! Les eng: The Cog catches in the engine! The jammed gears come loose, turn… and the platforms start moving above the chasm. For how long?
textes.Le Royaume des Racines était grand, avan: The Kingdom of Roots used to be big. There were gardens all the way to the sea. Now there are brambles.
textes.Le Royaume des Racines. L'air sent la te: The Kingdom of Roots. The air smells of earth and honey; everywhere, roots as thick as tree trunks, and dancing lights…
textes.Le Royaume des Racines… Cela faisait tro: The Kingdom of Roots… No one had gone down there for three hundred years. Fairies love games: beware of their riddles, and never lose sight of the sun.
textes.Le Ruisseau Pointillé — il file vers la: The Dotted Stream — it runs to the sea in little waves traced in ink
The Sans-Pitié will never float again.
textes.Le Sceau d'Airain ! Il se met à tourner: The Bronze Seal! It starts spinning on its own in your hand, its teeth clicking… A mechanism awakens within you: the Cogwheel (key 3, then X; in VR: B). Behind you, a sound of metal: the two statues are moving!
textes.Le Sceau des Sables est chaud dans ta po: The Seal of Sands is warm in your pocket… The Flame (key 2, then X)?
textes.Le Sceau des Vents : une stèle gravée d': The Seal of Winds: a stele engraved with a compass rose, with two empty slots. The great door of the keep doesn't budge. Missing:
textes.Le Scorpion-Roi frappe le sol de sa queu: The Scorpion King slams its tail on the ground: scorpions crawl out of the sand!
textes.Le Sixième Cercle : des rangées de tombe: The Sixth Circle: rows of open tombs, from which flames burst, each in its turn.
textes.Le Sloop : six mètres et demi, une petit: The Sloop: six and a half metres, a little cabin with portholes, a tall mast, a mainsail and a jib on its bowsprit. Steadier, faster (10 m/s under sail), and you can bring your four-legged friends along.
textes.Le Soleil de Pluie de feu. Le plafond es: The Sun of the Rain of Fire. The ceiling is split with embers. At times, the floor glows red… then fire stones fall. Two stone shelters, in the middle.
textes.Le Soleil de l'Eau. Un grand bassin pres: The Sun of Water. A large, nearly empty basin, chinampas stranded at the very bottom, and three bronze wheels on the walls.
textes.Le Soleil des Jaguars : le premier monde: The Sun of the Jaguars: the first world, which the jaguars devoured. Growls between the pillars…
textes.Le Soleil du Vent : des passerelles étro: The Sun of the Wind: narrow walkways above the void, and a wind that rises in gusts. In the bends of the walkways, the wind blows the right way… Shelter and wait; then run.
textes.Le Sphinx du plateau pose trois devinett: The Sphinx of the plateau asks three riddles. The first is as old as the world: what walks on four legs in the morning, two at noon, and three in the evening? Think of a whole life, not a single day.
textes.Le Sphinx gronde, et le sable tremble :: The Sphinx rumbles, and the sand trembles: “No. Go, think, and come back when you know.”
textes.Le Sphinx ne bouge pas. Mais tu jurerais: The Sphinx doesn't move. But you could swear that, for an instant, its stone lips smiled.
textes.Le Sphinx, il pose des devinettes ! Moi: The Sphinx asks riddles! I know the one about the man: on four legs in the morning, that's the baby! On two at noon, that's the grown-up! On three in the evening, that's the old man with his stick! Easy!
textes.Le Styx, un marais de boue tiède. Des da: The Styx, a marsh of lukewarm mud. Basalt slabs form a path… but some of them bubble. At the far end, the red walls of Dité.
textes.Le Séchoir à pâtes — des rideaux de spag: The Pasta Drying Shed — curtains of spaghetti drying in the sun
textes.Le TOUR des maisons ?! Ce n'est pas un m: A TOUR of the houses?! This isn't a museum! OUT!
textes.Le TROISIÈME fragment de l'amulette, gra: The THIRD fragment of the amulet, engraved with a moon! With the other two, the Serpent Gate awaits you, on the village side…
textes.Le Temple englouti. Des siècles de silen: The Sunken Temple. Centuries of silence… and somewhere, water dripping.
textes.Le Temple-Passoire — le soleil passe par: The Colander Temple — the sun shines through all the holes of the colander and rains down little spots of light
textes.Le Titan de Givre vacille… se fige… et v: The Frost Titan wavers… freezes… and bursts into a thousand shards of ice! On the altar at the back, a golden flame lights up in a crystal pillar: the Eternal Flame.
textes.Le Titan frappe la glace de sa massue :: The Titan strikes the ice with his club: the lake trembles!
textes.Le Titan rugit : des spectres de givre s: The Titan roars: frost specters rise from the lake!
textes.Le Titan souffle un vent de givre !: The Titan blows a freezing wind!
The Tournament of Horns has four rounds. In the last one, I'm the one you have to beat. I'm not mean, but I'm heavy. Don't stand in front of me when I charge: I'm not very good at turning.
textes.Le Troc des Sept Jours ! Roux m'a vendu: The Seven-Day Swap! Roux sold me a “phoenix feather”. A painted pheasant feather, my friend! I swapped it back to him the next day, disguised as a moon feather. He sold it back to me, repainted. Seven days! On the seventh, little Mochi bought it for a mooncake. Nobody won. Except Mochi. And the cake was good.
textes.Le Troc des Sept Jours, l'étranger ! Je: The Seven-Day Swap, stranger! I sell Bedaine a phoenix feather: a pheasant feather, painted by yours truly, very nice work. Next day, he swaps it back to me, disguised as a moon feather. I repaint it, I sell it again. Seven days! On the seventh, Mochi bought it for a mooncake. She wears it in her hair. She's the craftiest one.
textes.Le Vestibule des Quatre Peuples. Quatre: The Vestibule of the Four Peoples. Four stone statues: a sailor, a caravan woman, a shepherd, a fox woman. Above the staircase, a fresco. Before you, a balcony… and below, an immense hall where a red light pulses.
textes.Le Vieux Silas a connu mon père, et peut: Old Silas knew my father, and perhaps my grandfather. He tells stories I don't believe, and I listen to him anyway. On rainy evenings, he sits near my table. I never charge him for his seat.
textes.Le Vieux Silas jure que Bartholomé a nav: Old Silas swears Bartholomé sailed with Barbe-Sanglante. Bartholomé doesn't deny it. He says “the skull, the skull”. Silas says that says it all. Me, I don't know.
textes.Le Vieux Silas jure que la carte du trés: Old Silas swears that Barbe-Sanglante's treasure map exists, torn into three pieces: one in the dungeon of the Cursed Fort, one in the mausoleum in the graveyard, and the third up the sleeve of Sylvain, the croupier. Philémon Lunette will know how to put it back together.
textes.Le Vieux Silas raconte que le trésor de: Old Silas says Barbe-Sanglante's treasure is hidden in a skull-shaped rock. He also says he danced with a mermaid. So…
textes.Le Vieux Silas s'assoit près du feu de l: Old Silas sits by the fire on the shore every morning and tells me ship stories while I work. Half of them are made up. But he knows boats. That, he doesn't make up.
textes.Le Village des Arbres-Maisons\nLes habit:
The Treehouse Village
The villagers have gone to find their colours. Come on up and see!
