textes.Le professeur est mon meilleur client et: The professor is my best customer and my best friend. He's looking for Atlantis, I'm looking for the world. Neither of us has ever left.
textes.Le professeur m'a appris à écouter une c: The professor taught me to listen to a boiler. We'd put our ears to it, the two of us, without speaking. “Is it singing, Capucine?” “It's singing.” “Then we stay.” One day, it went quiet. He grabbed my hand and we ran. We were at the end of the path when the roof went off. He was laughing. So was I, back then.
textes.Le professeur m'a proposé un savon explo: The professor offered me an explosive soap, “for bubble propulsion”. I agreed to try one drop, just one, in a thimble. There was a little noise, a little pink cloud, and no more thimble. The professor applauded. Me, I put the bottle away very, very high up.
textes.Le professeur prend trois cafés chaque m: The professor has three coffees every morning and says nothing. Nothing! One single thank-you in two months. I counted. And the day he did talk…
textes.Le public te lance des pièces (et un coq: The audience throws coins at you (and a seashell).
textes.Le pédalo qui s'appelle « Gérard », c'es: The pedalo called “Gérard”, I'm the one who swam it back, pushing it in front of me. The tourist inside had been going round in circles for an hour photographing the lighthouse. He photographed me too, while I pushed. Yannick named the pedalo after him. The tourist doesn't know. Shh.
textes.Le pêcheur est là. C'est l'assiette qui: The fisherman's here. It's the plate that's missing.
textes.Le quai de sept heures à dix-neuf heures: The quay from seven in the morning to seven at night. Lunch at Paulo's. Evenings, cards at the Perroquet. Sometimes a little white dog sleeps behind my crates, at the end of the quay. I don't say anything. Little Nina doesn't either. And every week, Nadine slips a letter into my letterbox on High Street. A letter. For me. I read it at night, sitting on Gertrude. The crate.
The quetzal one is the most precious.
textes.Le ragoût de Mama Grog : poisson, banane: Mama Grog's stew: fish, plantains, red beans, chilli and a ladle of molasses. Nobody asks what else is in it. Restores three hearts.
textes.Le ras-el-hanout, c'est « la tête de la: Ras el hanout means “head of the shop”: the merchant's best blend. Mine has thirty-two spices. The thirty-third ingredient is a secret.
textes.Le rat ? Ce voleur ? Ce brigand à mousta: The rat? That thief? That whiskered bandit? (He bangs his ladle on the table.) Three cheeses! My three finest aged cheeses, the ones that smell so strong even the seagulls faint! Gone! I saw him dash off into the port with a piece bigger than he is. He's hidden them somewhere, the wretch! (He grumbles.) … Well. If you take him far from my kitchen, I'll say no more. Find my cheeses: wherever he hid them, he'll come back. Put them near the hold, and he'll come out. That rat would do anything for cheese. So would I, come to think of it. Maybe that's why we don't get along.
textes.Le rat du Requin Borgne: The rat of the Requin Borgne
textes.Le rayon de soleil frappe la Fleur-Porte: The sunbeam strikes the Door Flower! Its petals quiver… and slowly open, like on the first morning of the world.
textes.Le rayon te repose, tout doucement, sur: The beam sets you back down, very softly, on the buoy. Your rowboat is waiting, a little surprised.
textes.Le rayon te soulève, doucement, comme un: The beam lifts you, gently, like a soap bubble… 380 metres higher up, the Lumens wave hello.
textes.Le rempart ? Tout en haut, au vent, à gu: The ramparts? Way up high, in the wind, watching for gargoyles. That's the post for the brave. Or the dreamers. Often, they're the same.
textes.Le requin s'enfuit dans les profondeurs…: The shark flees into the depths… It lost a shark tooth (picked up).
textes.Le reste, c'est un secret. Je ne le conf: The rest is a secret. I only share it with a friend. A true one, {surnom}.
textes.Le rhum brun du Crâne Fendu, vieilli dan: The brown tonic of Le Crâne Fendu, aged in barrels from a sunken ship. It smells of wood, molasses and a little of gunpowder. Restores one heart.
textes.Le rhum de Mama Lou adoucit tout. Même l: Mama Lou's rum softens everything. Even cats.
The rum is good tonight. Hm.
textes.Le rhum noir de La Murène Ivre. Les pira: The dark tonic of La Murène Ivre. Pirates say it warms the heart; Anouk would say otherwise. Restores one heart.
textes.Le rocher était MAL PLACÉ !: The rock was in the WRONG PLACE!
textes.Le roi a encore commandé un tonneau de b: The king ordered another barrel of fizz from Ulfa. To “taste” it. Three times this week.
textes.Le roi a encore perdu sa couronne. Elle: The king has lost his crown again. It was on his head.
textes.Le roi dicte des décrets très longs et t: The king dictates very long, very royal decrees. I shorten them. He protests, then he signs. I think he's glad to have someone who dares.
textes.Le roi m'a envoyé dessiner les mers du s: The king sent me to chart the southern seas, my grandfather's seas, aboard the Stubborn Seagull. Octave was the ship's carpenter: we played cards every evening, he cheated, I measured his beard. Then one moonless night, the rock. I woke up on a raft of rolled-up maps, one boot short, and a parrot said “Shipwreck” to me from the top of a tree. Great barnacles, what a night.
textes.Le roi perd sa couronne sur sa tête, cha: The king loses his crown while it's on his head, sings off-key and pays his bills late. He's the best king in the world. I'd give my life for him. Or at least, I'd stay awake.
textes.Le rouage, je l'ai dessiné. Cent fois. S: The cog, I've drawn it. A hundred times. On my workbench, in chalk, at night, when the forge cools down. The teeth, the axle, the thickness. In the morning, I wiped it off with my sleeve. Nobody's ever seen it. If you tell, I'll say you're lying.
textes.Le rouge ! (Elle le tient à bout de bras: The red! (She holds it at arm's length, in the sun.) My poppies will be able to blush again. With joy, this time. Hurry and pour it in: paint cup number three. And here: a bunch of sunflowers. They're white for now, but they won't stay that way for long.
textes.Le rouge ! La couleur des aras, de la co: Red! The colour of macaws, of cochineal, of the heart! You have fire in you. I'd weave you a red belt, if you stayed long enough.
textes.Le royaume a trois parties : les racines: The kingdom has three parts: the roots, the village… and the Bramble Queen's domain, to the north. No one has been there for a hundred years.
textes.Le royaume des fées ! Une prairie en fle: The fairy kingdom! A flowering meadow floats above a sea of golden clouds. Fireflies dance in broad daylight… and to the north stands an immense tree, so tall its crown touches the sky: Yggdrasil, the World Tree. Fairies are waiting for you in the glade, to the south.
textes.Le sable t'avale… Tu te débats, et tu re: The sand swallows you… You struggle free and come out, out of breath, at the entrance of the hall.
textes.Le sac qui contenait la lettre de Pépin: The bag with Pépin's letter in it was going “tick-tock”. Zélie had slipped a note on it: “Do not shake. Theoretically, it isn't alive.” Theoretically! I carried the bag at arm's length all the way to Pépin's door, very slowly. It was a stopwatch. Pépin timed how long I'd taken. Too long, according to him.
textes.Le safran ! La couleur la plus chère du: Saffron! The most expensive colour in the world, and Lalla Aïcha sells it to me with a sigh. People who love yellow love a party. So you'll dance at my wedding.
textes.Le sanctuaire bleu de Tlaloc, le dieu de: Tlaloc's blue shrine, the god of rain, with round eyes and fangs. In front, a chacmool holds an empty bowl on its belly. Tlaloc is thirsty… for a jar of rainwater, no doubt. Coyotl, the potter, makes lovely blue jars.
textes.Le sanctuaire rouge de Huitzilopochtli,: Huitzilopochtli's red shrine, the warrior hummingbird, the sun that fights every night to return. In front, an unlit brazier. You burn copal in it, the white incense; Tochtli sells some at the market.
textes.Le sandwich d'Achille, c'est Gaston qui: Achille's sandwich was Gaston's invention: ham, gherkin, tied up with a little lead weight so it flies straight. Free “until landing”. The first morning, I threw it as hard as I could, and Achille caught it one-handed, mid-loop. I ran into the café shouting. Gaston pretended his eyes weren't wet.
textes.Le sandwich d'Achille, c'est jambon, cor: Achille's sandwich is ham and gherkin, tied up with a little fishing weight so it flies straight. On the second morning it was too windy: Adèle threw it, the wind caught it, and it dropped straight down Professor Boum's chimney. We heard a little “boom”. The professor came to tell me it was his best lunch in weeks.
textes.Le savon, sûrement. C'est mystérieux, le: The soap, surely. It's mysterious stuff, soap.
textes.Le scarabée pousse sa boule de fumier co: The scarab rolls its ball of dung the way Khepri rolls the sun up in the morning. Small, dirty, stubborn… and it makes the day dawn. I like scarabs.
textes.Le sceau du désert ? … Qui t'a parlé de: The desert seal? … Who told you about that? The elders say it sleeps under the walking dune. But the dune walks, that's the thing. Nobody knows where it is today.
textes.Le sceau du nord ? On raconte que les be: The northern seal? They say the shepherds keep it in a cave, under the highest ridge. They won't talk about it. I understand them: if I had it, I'd take it apart.
textes.Le sceau roule sur le côté. Un escalier: The seal rolls aside. A staircase plunges into the dark, around a bottomless well…
textes.Le seau d'eau ? Il l'a vidé par la fenêt: The bucket of water? He emptied it out of the window, right next to me. Next to me! A man who aims that badly is a man who aims very well, you see? I said “thanks, very refreshing”. It was true, too. It was eight o'clock, I'd done my lap.
textes.Le second de Barbe-Sanglante, le Capitai: Barbe-Sanglante's first mate, Captain Sans-Chair, swore to guard the treasure for all eternity. He kept his word. He's still out there. Well, what's left of him.
textes.Le second, il crie tout le temps sur moi: The first mate yells at me all the time. Only at me! With the others, he just goes “Hm”. I'm a bit scared of him. But when he bends an iron bar with his bare hands, that's so cool.
textes.Le secret de la forme ? Cent pompes le m: The secret to fitness? A hundred push-ups in the morning, a hundred in the evening, and a pie at noon. Want to join in?
textes.Le secret de la pêche ? Garder la ligne: The secret of fishing? Keep the line taut, but not too taut. Like a conversation with Gaston.
textes.Le secret, c'est la braise. Pas de flamm: The secret is the embers. No flames. Flames burn, embers cook. It's the same with people.
textes.Le secret, c'est le départ. Je pars comm: The secret is the start. I shoot off like an arrow, and after that, the others are chasing an arrow. It's discouraging.
textes.Le septième toit, je m'en souviens comme: The seventh roof, I remember it like yesterday: a flash, a huge bang, and Capucine sitting in the soot, without eyebrows. The next day, she told me she was leaving to “keep the colours without the danger”. I gave her the barrel of my old engine, the only one that had never exploded. She made it into her first cannon. Every time it fires, my eyes sting a little.
textes.Le serpent-naga des profondeurs… une éca: The naga serpent of the depths… a scale from that creature would be the jewel of my collection.
textes.Le silence ?! Mais… Ha ! Tu sais quoi ?: Silence?! But… Ha! You know what? You're right. The finest moment in a song is just before the first note. The Silent One would agree with you.
textes.Le silence. Au milieu de la pièce, quelq: Silence. In the middle of the room, someone with a very pale face makes big gestures… without a sound.
textes.Le silence… Respect. C'est la note la pl: Silence… Respect. It's the hardest note to play. Listen. … There. That one was for you.
The sixth, I'm charging you for.
textes.Le soir (à partir de 21 h), retrouver Gé: In the evening (from 9 p.m.), meet Gédéon at the entrance to the Howling Hall and walk him to the drum kit: let him play his first concert with the Bilge Rats
textes.Le soir de la carte. Il la pose sur un t: The night of the map. He puts it on a barrel while he lights his pipe. A ginger cat jumps, grabs the map, darts over the crates, then onto a roof. The captain stays down below. He yells. He's scared of heights. A captain scared of a cat and a roof. Hm. Three dead captains, and this one.
textes.Le soir de la démonstration, j'ai trouvé: On the evening of the demonstration, I found a pink confetto in my hat. I waved it in front of the whole Crankshaft: the proof! Capucine said it was last year's confetti. How does she know? How can you tell what year a confetto is from? And the next day at lunch, there was one in my soup. I don't say anything any more. I take notes.
textes.Le soir de la foudre, Kalda est venue di: The night of the lightning, Kalda came to dictate her report, paler than my paper. I asked her: “And the sky?” She said: “Nothing.” Her eyebrows still smelled singed. I didn't write anything. I left the line blank. She'll fill it in when she's ready.
textes.Le soir de la fête du port, il n'y a plu: On the night of the harbour festival, there isn't a free table at Paulo's. And yet, every year, when I turn up at ten, a plate is waiting for me at the end of the counter, under a tea towel, with the spoon on top. I taste it. I say: “Something's missing.” He slaps me on the back. It's our tradition.
textes.Le soir de la tempête où sa lentille s'e: The night of the storm when his lens cracked, the lighthouse was only half lit. I came in by guesswork, by compass and by ear. As I came alongside, I saw a figure right up top, on the gallery, in the full wind, following me with a lantern in his hand. We've never talked about it.
textes.Le soir de ma nomination comme professeu: On the evening I was appointed teacher, he took me to the top of the Academy tower. He spread his wings, showed me the whole city lit up, and said: “Each of those lights was lit by someone who learned.” Then he added: “Don't burn the tower. It has suffered enough.”
textes.Le soir de ma nomination, Corentin a rac: The evening I was appointed, Corentin told the tavern the story of “the admiral who commanded a bathtub”. Everyone laughed, me too, out of politeness. The next day, he came to the harbour office and told me, just me, about the night Katell held the helm to the very end. Not a single joke. I've never forgotten it.
textes.Le soir de ma première coupe, Trèfle a f: The evening of my first cup, Trèfle baked a cake shaped like a cup. With a handle. Magnificent. I ate the handle before anyone else, before the speeches even. She yelled. I said: “A champion tastes his cup.” She said: “A champion waits.” Fine. She's right. But the handle was delicious.
textes.Le soir de ma première leçon, quand la T: The evening of my first lesson, when the Tower started shining in the middle of the night, Berthe thought it was dawn. She opened the inn and served eggs to wizards in their nightshirts. I came to apologise. She served me eggs too. I said thank you, and good night. She said: “Good morning, more like.” She was right.
textes.Le soir de mes soixante-dix ans, toute l: On my seventieth birthday, the whole tavern called for the shipwreck. At the end, Gwenola put out the lanterns, all but the glow of the stove, and everyone sang the old topmen's song, in Breton. Off key. So off key. I've never heard anything more beautiful.
textes.Le soir de mon arrivée, il y a soixante-: The evening I arrived, seventy years ago, a young bear sat down beside me and said: “Twice upon a time…” I had walked for a whole moon. I fell asleep in the middle. He never got over it: since then, nobody hears the end of his stories. I think it's partly my fault.
textes.Le soir de mon arrivée, trempé, sans cha: The evening I arrived, soaked, hatless, I walked into the Crâne Fendu and made a speech on the importance of taxation. A big pirate wanted to throw me out. Mama Grog rapped his hand with her rolling pin and served me soup. I ate it to the last spoonful. The best soup of my career.
textes.Le soir de sa demande, après mon oui au: The evening he proposed, after my yes at the third price, he ran through the whole souk shouting: “She haggled! She loves me!” Karim knocked over a basket of slippers. The next day, Rachid sold a carpet at the second price. The only time in his life. He says it was an accident. I say it was love.
textes.Le soir de sa première leçon de maître,: The evening of his first lesson as a master, he wanted to do things properly. The Astrelune Tower started shining like a golden sun, in the middle of the night. The whole town thought it was dawn: Berthe opened the inn and served eggs to wizards in their nightshirts. Aurélien apologised for a week.

The evening of his first lesson as a master, the Astrelune Tower started shining gold, in the middle of the night. I thought it was dawn! I opened the inn, heated the milk, cooked eggs. Wizards in nightshirts turned up rubbing their eyes. Aurélien came to apologise, red as a tomato. He had some eggs.
textes.Le soir de sa première victoire, j'ai fa: The evening of his first win, I made a cake shaped like a cup, with a handle and everything. I put it on the table for the party, I turned round to get the knives: he'd already eaten the handle. “I was checking it was sturdy.” The champion! He had a tummy ache until the next evening.
textes.Le soir des funérailles de mon père, je: On the evening of my father's funeral, I went down to the tavern. One fizz, two, three. The fourth tasted like spring water. I looked at Ulfa. She was wiping a mug, very busy. I said nothing. She's kept it up ever since, and I've kept up not noticing. A king needs someone to watch over his mug.
textes.Le soir des funérailles du vieux roi, Th: On the evening of the old king's funeral, Thorgal came down to the tavern. One fizz, two, three. The fourth, I filled with water. He drank it without a word. For ninety years now I've been watering down his fizz whenever he looks sad, and he never notices. Well… I think.
textes.Le soir des golems, il est venu boire mo: The evening of the golems, he came to drink some of my moon water. He pulled a terrible face and said “Delicious”. Since then, every time he comes by, I pour him a little glass, and every time he says “Delicious” with the same face. It's our ritual. Rituals are runes too.
textes.Le soir des pots cassés, j'ai poursuivi: The evening of the broken pots, I chased Chak all the way to the Cenote. On the way back, I found Ix Sak outside her house, at her loom, dying of laughter. She'd botched three rows. She kept them: she says it makes a pattern. She calls it “Ix Chab in a temper”. It's a very pretty pattern. I hate that it's pretty.
textes.Le soir des pots, j'ai entendu crac, cra: The evening of the pots, I heard crack, crack. Two pots, my finest, painted by my mother. Chak was there, ball in hand, looking as innocent as a jaguar next to a plucked turkey. I came out with my pestle. He ran all the way to the Cenote. So did I. At the water's edge, I had no breath left to shout. So I charged him double. He paid.
textes.Le soir des pots, ma balle a rebondi sur: The evening of the pots, my ball bounced off the wall and broke two of Ix Chab's pots. Bonk, crack, crack. She came out with her pestle. I ran all the way to the Cenote along the sacbé, shouting: “It was the ball!” At the water's edge, she caught me. She looked at me, out of breath, and said: “Tomorrow, double price.” I paid double for a month.
textes.Le soir des quarante-trois coups, j'étai: The night of the forty-three punches, I was on his shoulders, at the Crâne Fendu. I counted out loud, and at the last one I shouted “Forty-three!” so loud that the two brawlers stopped to clap for me. Gros-Louis said I'd stopped a fight all by myself. I'm the only cabin boy who's done that. I think.
textes.Le soir des résultats, on proclame : « U: On results night, they announce: “Unanimous minus one vote.” The whole square turns towards the grocery. Colette, behind her window, raises her pencil. Every time. Eighteen years I've given my victory speeches looking at that pencil. It keeps a man modest.
textes.Le soir du dauphin, Zoé était sur la pla: The night of the dolphin, Zoé was on the beach. I was dancing in the water, the dolphin jumped, I turned to her and yelled. She gave me two thumbs up. The next day she was telling everyone “almost”. But right then, bro, she gave me two thumbs up. I remember it really well.
textes.Le soir du jour où je l'ai ramené à la b: The evening of the day I brought him back at the helm, he told the story at the party, standing on a table. In his version, the channel was full of reefs, there was fog, a storm and a shark. There was none of that. I let him tell it. It was nice, being the hero of a song.
textes.Le soir du nuage, il a hurlé « Trois-mât: The night of the cloud, he yelled “Three-master to port!”. I had the cannons loaded, the whole crew on deck, Petit-Pierre hidden under a bucket. The three-master stretched out, then turned into a sheep. Fil-de-Fer scrubbed the deck for a week. Ever since, when a cloud goes by, the crew salutes it.
textes.Le soir du punch, elle m'a renversé le v: The punch night, she spilled the glass right down my shirt. She grabbed a tea towel, she was scrubbing, saying sorry, sorry, all red. I didn't move. I said: “It's nothing, it smells nice.” I didn't wash that shirt for a week. It smelled of coconut. Then it rained. Oh well.
textes.Le soir où Barnabé est passé à la teuf,: The night Barnabé dropped by the party, he did three steps, right on the kick, Gaston on his shoulder. Three! Everyone cheered. He says it was cartography, that he was measuring the dance floor. Bro, I saw his shoulders. That was dancing. Legend.
textes.Le soir où Doc lui a taillé un dentier e: The evening Doc carved him a set of walnut-wood dentures, Sans-Dents came to dinner wearing them, all proud. On the third mouthful, the dentures stayed in the stew. I didn't see. I served it to Gros-Louis. He bit into it and said: “Good stew, but a bit tough.” Sans-Dents never put them back in.
textes.Le soir où Fanny m'a envoyée valser d'un: The night Fanny sent me flying with one big gesture, I landed in Tchoum's arms. He didn't let go right away. He just said: “… You okay?”, and went bright red under his beanie. The whole dance floor saw. Nobody has ever mentioned it again. Me, I think about it.
textes.Le soir où Lyra est partie veiller l'arb: The evening Lyra left to watch over the tree for good, I gave her my old blanket and a single piece of advice: “Talk to the humans.” It took her two centuries to follow it. She still sleeps under the blanket. My feet have been cold ever since. It's a cold that makes me happy.
textes.Le soir où Léa n'a pas voulu de ma rose,: The evening Léa didn't want my rose, I took it back to Rose's. I didn't know what to do with it. She put it in a vase on her counter, with a label: “In the meantime.” Every time I go by, it's still standing, much longer than a normal rose. I think Rose talks to it.
textes.Le soir où Léa pleurait sur le balcon vo: The evening Léa was crying on the next balcony, I passed her a square of chocolate over the railing. She took it without a word. Then a second. At the fourth, she told me about the ring. At the sixth, I told her: “Husbands get lost and found again.” There was no chocolate left. But she was smiling.
textes.Le soir où Marcel a réclamé son augmenta: The night Marcel asked for his raise, a man in the front row was clapping by banging his wooden leg on the bench. After the show, he offered me a place on his brig. I asked him why me. He said: “Because you put the knife down.” I followed him for that answer.
textes.Le soir où des pirates l'ont déposé sur: The night some pirates dropped him on the quay, he had nothing left, not even his hat. He came into the Crâne Fendu, soaking wet, and gave the customers a speech on the importance of taxes. Gros-Louis wanted to throw him out. Me, I served him a soup. The next day, he was governor. I still wonder if it was my soup.
textes.Le soir où il a chanté mon couplet pour: The night he sang my verse for the first time, the whole Crâne Fendu stamped their feet. I was so happy that I lifted him up, him, his stool and his fiddle, and put him on the counter. He played the ending up there. Mama Grog said if the counter broke, I'd pay for it. It didn't break. Almost.
textes.Le soir où il a dansé sur la grande tabl: The night he danced on the big table, after the Forge Festival, the table cracked in the middle of a verse. The king stayed standing on one half, mug raised, and finished his song. Nobody dared laugh until the end. After that, they did. The table still wobbles. I won't replace it: it's a monument.
textes.Le soir où il a débarqué sur le quai, il: The evening he landed on the quay, he had an axe and a loaf of bread. I asked him what he could do. He said: “Chop.” I said: “We board tomorrow.” He asked: “And when do we eat?” I hired him for the second answer.
textes.Le soir où il a fini les portes, je me s: The evening he finished the gates, I leant in to look. Poof! One spark, and half my beard was gone. Borin laughed so hard he dropped his hammer on his foot. We both limped for a week, him from his foot, me from my chin. We've been arguing ever since. It's our way of being friends.
textes.Le soir où il a misé la Morue contre un: The night he bet the Cod against a barrel of rum, I took the helm apart and hid it under my hammock. If he lost, the others would have got a sloop that went round in circles. He won. The next day, I put the helm back, whistling. Now, when he bets big, I sit next to him with a screwdriver. He gets it.
textes.Le soir où il a perdu son alliance, je l: The night he lost his ring, I lent him my big punch ladle to dig with. It was the sturdiest tool in the beach hut. He dug until midnight and found two bottle caps, a sandal and a furious crab. The next day, I served the punch by the cup. The ladle smelled of sand for a month.
textes.Le soir où j'ai chanté son couplet pour: The night I sang his verse for the first time, he was so pleased that he lifted me, my stool and my fiddle, and set me down on the bar. I finished the song up there, my head among the lanterns. Mama Grog shouted that he'd pay for the bar. The bar creaked, but it held. So did I. Just about.
textes.Le soir où j'ai compris ce que voulait l: The evening I understood what the captain wanted, I told only one person: Zohra. “A carpet that doesn't exist, can you imagine? Don't tell a soul.” That very evening, Hassan was asking me how the carpet was going. Then Saïd. Then the amin. Zohra swears she only told Halima. Halima swears she told no one.
textes.Le soir où j'ai débarqué avec ma hache,: The evening I turned up with my axe, she asked me what I could do. I said “chop”. She said “we board tomorrow”. I asked when we ate. She smiled. Just once, but I saw it. The next day, we took the Shark. The day after, I had my soup.
textes.Le soir où j'ai fini les portes de la ci: The evening I finished the city gates, Grimli leant in to admire the work. A spark jumped. Half his beard went up in smoke, poof, just like that. He said: “It'll grow back finer.” He's been saying it for a hundred years. We've been arguing for a hundred years. Hilda says she's winning.
textes.Le soir où j'ai misé la Morue contre un: The night I bet the Cod against a barrel of rum, Coquille took the wheel apart and hid it under her hammock: “If you lose, they'll get a sloop that can't turn.” I won, of course. The next day, she put the wheel back on, whistling. Since then, when I bet big, she sits next to me with a screwdriver.
textes.Le soir où j'ai perdu toutes mes gouttes: The evening I lost all my drops, Mélisse laughed. And then, that night, I found an empty bottle outside my door, with the words: “For the next ones.” I put it on my windowsill. I've never put anything in it. It's lucky that way, empty.
textes.Le soir où j'étais enroué, plus de voix,: The night I was hoarse, no voice, no “boom-boom”: if I can't sing it, I can't play it! I stayed on the bench, and Bourru played all alone. The whole village danced in slow motion, like they were wading through mud. I stamped my foot to help them. Nobody listened. Bourru, though, looked very pleased.
textes.Le soir où je l'ai mis au défi, il est p: The evening I dared him, he set off for the graveyard whistling very loudly. I followed him through the spyglass from the bow. I saw him reach the gate, stop, scratch his head… and come back so fast he overtook a dog. When he got back, he said: “Saw nothing. Fireflies.” He was white as a sheet.
textes.Le soir où je pleurais sur le balcon, un: The night I was crying on the balcony, a hand came over the railing, holding a square of chocolate. Then a voice: “Gérard arrived late to our own wedding. He was photographing the church.” I laughed between sobs, it made a noise like a seal. She passed over a second square. “For the seal,” she said.
textes.Le soir où je suis partie veiller l'Arbr: The evening I left to watch over the Tree, he gave me his old blanket and a single piece of advice: “Talk to the humans. They live shorter lives than we do, but they go further.” The blanket smelled of moss and old books. I still sleep under it.
textes.Le soir où la Perle de l'avenue a dispar: The evening the avenue's Pearl vanished, he asked me how it had happened. I said I hadn't seen anything. That was true, in a way. He looked at me with his scroll eyes, and he didn't write anything. I think it's the only time Abyssos has ever written nothing.
textes.Le soir où la baleine est passée au-dess: The evening the whale passed over the palace, I ran all the way to the Gate to tell him. He took one step, then he stayed put. So I sang him the whale, the whole whale, for an hour, so he could see her anyway. His eyes were closed. He was smiling.
textes.Le soir où la balle de Chak a cassé ses: The evening Chak's ball broke two of her pots, Ix Chab chased him across the whole square, then along the white sacbé, all the way to the Cenote. With her pestle! Chak ran shouting: “It was the ball! It was the ball!” I was weaving in front of the house. I missed three rows, I was laughing so hard. I kept them. They make a pretty pattern.
textes.Le soir où la peau de son bendir a crevé: The night his bendir skin split, in the middle of the festival, he ran to my table, grabbed a tray and played on it until midnight. The square danced twice as hard. The tray came back dented all over. I never wanted to straighten it. It's on the wall, next to Mâchefer's. Its dents are in rhythm.
textes.Le soir où le Zéphyr a débarqué douze vo: The evening the Zéphyr landed twelve travellers, I offered seaweed beds at the breach, “no risk of falling”. I got eight, Pierrick four. The next day, my eight had sea fleas and all went over to him. He charged them double. I was proud of him. I didn't tell him.
textes.Le soir où les golems se sont réveillés,: The evening the golems woke up, Bramm came in without a word, grey as his gate. I didn't ask anything. I set down his mug, sat across from him, and kept quiet. A whole hour! Everyone thought I was ill. On his way out, he said: “Thanks.” A whole word. A record.

The evening the golems woke, I walked into the Blazing Mug without a word. Ulfa asked nothing. She set down my mug, sat across from me, and kept quiet. Ulfa. Quiet. A whole hour. It's the kindest thing anyone has ever done for me.
textes.Le soir où ma mère m'a passé la boussole: The evening my mother handed me the compass, I went to the Bordée alone, in a uniform too big for me. I didn't know what to say to anyone. Gwenola served me a sparkling apple and sat beside me until closing, without a word. I've never had better advice.
textes.Le soir où mon bendir a crevé, j'ai fini: The night my bendir split, I finished the festival on one of his trays. I dented it. A lot. I wanted to pay for it. He said: “Tap. No.” And he never hammered it straight. When people ask him what that dent is, he answers: “It's a festival.”
textes.Le soir tombe. C'est l'heure où les gens: Evening is falling. It's when people get together.
textes.Le soir, Joe me laisse donner les graine: In the evening, Joe lets me give out the seeds. Bartholomé, the oldest, always pinches my finger a bit. Joe says it's a kiss. One evening, Bartholomé stared at me and said: “The skull, the skull.” I got shivers all over. Joe says he says that to everyone. I still slept with the lantern on.
textes.Le soir, Kevin s'accoude à mon comptoir: In the evening, Kevin leans on my counter and, instead of having a quiet drink, he does push-ups on it. Push-ups on the counter, between the glasses! Once, he knocked over a pineapple. The customers clap, the glasses shake, and I count. He cheats: he barely bends his elbows.
textes.Le soir, Lumi me prête trois lucioles po: In the evening, Lumi lends me three fireflies to sort my seeds. I named them Pip, Acorn and Peanut. Peanut glows the brightest, but she steals the other two's honey. That's normal, she's a peanut. Peanuts are greedy.
textes.Le soir, Léonce s'assoit sur mon bras de: In the evening, Léonce sits on my brass arm and I lift him up to my shoulder. From up there, he reports on the Fair like Rosette: “Professor Boum still has his eyebrows!” He says it's his very own airship. I tell him the airship creaks. He says that's its charm.
textes.Le soir, Mademoiselle Sulfura me donne d: In the evenings, Miss Sulfura gives me lessons in secret. I asked her how to make a blue flame. She said I was too little. So the next day, I made a green flame, with a bit of sulphur salt from Zébuline's. You should have seen her face! I didn't tell her about the salt.
textes.Le soir, Maman me raconte des histoires: In the evening, Mum tells me stories about Dad. That he carried stones as big as cows on his boat. That he sang so out of tune the fish jumped out of the water so they wouldn't have to hear him. I think the fish jumped to hear him better. Mum says it's possible. She smiles with wet eyes.
textes.Le soir, Ortie me fait réciter ses leçon: In the evening, Ortie makes me recite her lessons from the Academy. She knows the answers, I don't. She gives me marks. Yesterday I got four out of twenty in the history of flames. She wrote in the margin: “Dad must work harder.” I had it framed. It hangs in the barracks.
textes.Le soir, Zineb monte un thé à ma chambre: In the evening, Zineb brings tea up to my room, “on her way past”. She sits on the edge of the bed to look at the day's canvas. She stays an hour without a word, except: “The sky is too pink.” The next day, I paint it even pinker. She comes back. She stays two hours.
textes.Le soir, c'est la fête. Les tambours, le: In the evening, it's party time. Drums, dancers, stars. Come!
textes.Le soir, c'est le meilleur moment. Les p: Evening's the best time. The fishermen come home, Corentin tells his tales, and someone always ends up singing.
textes.Le soir, c'est mon heure ! Les lanternes: Evening is my time! The lanterns light up, Nox does the rounds of the street lamps, and the whole city turns into a big jewellery box.
textes.Le soir, depuis la plage, on voit le pha: In the evening, from the beach, you can see the Port-Azur lighthouse blinking. As if it were dancing with us.
textes.Le soir, depuis le balcon, je regarde le: In the evening, from the balcony, I watch the lanterns light up one by one. It's my favourite moment: my city breathing.
textes.Le soir, en cachette de sa mère, je donn: In the evenings, without her mother knowing, I give Ortie extra lessons in the Academy courtyard. She asked me how to make a blue flame. I told her she was too young. The next day, she turned up with a green flame. I still don't know how she did it.
textes.Le soir, il descend un peu, pour que je: In the evening, he comes down a little so I can talk to him. He says the view is marvellous and that he needs a wee.
textes.Le soir, il raconte. J'écoute. Tout. San: In the evening, he tells stories. I listen. To everything. Without sleeping. He thinks I'm asleep. I know all his stories. And their endings. Except one: the moon that didn't want to set any more. That one, never heard the end. Nobody has. Hrmm. Strange.
textes.Le soir, j'allume une seule bougie et je: In the evening I light a single candle and read until it goes out. It always goes out at the best part. That's candle spite.
textes.Le soir, j'interroge Papa sur mes leçons: In the evenings, I test Dad on my Academy lessons. He never knows anything. Yesterday, he got four out of twenty in the history of flames. I wrote in the margin: “Dad must work harder.” He had the paper framed and hung it up at the barracks. He says it's his medal.
textes.Le soir, j'écoute la fête depuis mon ban: In the evening, I listen to the festival from my bench. I don't dance any more. But when Lhoucine plays a fast tune, my knees dance all by themselves. Not in time. I folded my arms, to look stern. Lhoucine saw me. He played the same tune three times in a row. I suspect that boy of being a cheat.
In the evening, I listen to the party from my bench. I don't dance anymore. My knees dance on their own, and not in time.
textes.Le soir, je bois un grog de soufre au Di: In the evening I have a hot sulphur punch at the Diable Repu. No spices. I asked.
textes.Le soir, je chante sur la place, et Nene: In the evening, I sing in the square, and Nenetl follows me on the drum. One evening, she sped up, and up, to see if I could keep up. I did. She sped up again. In the end, I was singing so fast that the dancers sat down on the ground. We laughed until midnight. Just in time for the song to the stars.
textes.Le soir, je chante à la fête. Pas pour v: In the evening, I sing at the party. Not to sell. Just for the fun of making the lanterns shake.
textes.Le soir, je compte mes trocs de la journ: In the evening, I count up the day's swaps. I've never gained anything, never lost anything… and yet I'm richer every day. That's swapping for you.
textes.Le soir, je danse avec mon Pyrus sur la: In the evening, I dance with my Pyrus on the Great Square. He dances like a drawbridge. I adore him.
textes.Le soir, je danse sur la Grand-Place. Et: In the evening I dance on the Great Square. And I don't set anyone on fire. Well, hardly anyone. Zigomar doesn't count.
textes.Le soir, je danse sur la plateforme de V: In the evening, I dance on the Venus platform. With Balam, when he isn't busy playing jaguar.
textes.Le soir, je descends au Cercle. Même un: In the evening, I come down to the Circle. Even a guard has the right to listen to the drums. Grisou takes over. Well, he tries.
textes.Le soir, je donne à boire aux plantes et: In the evening, I give the plants a drink and say goodnight to them. The sulphur roses close up on their own. The peppers, you have to sing them something.
textes.Le soir, je fais le tour du palais et j': In the evening, I go round the palace and snuff out the unnecessary candles. Her Highness says they cost nothing. The principle, {surnom}. The principle.
textes.Le soir, je fais mes expériences les plu: In the evening, I do my quietest experiments. The neighbours have signed a petition.
textes.Le soir, je fais sécher mes herbes au-de: In the evening, I dry my herbs over the fire. The whole house smells of lavender and thyme.
textes.Le soir, je goûte les potions du jour. P: In the evening, I taste the day's potions. To check them. That's why I sing on my way home.
textes.Le soir, je laisse reposer ma voix. Enfi: In the evening I rest my voice. Well, I try. It won't let me.
textes.Le soir, je lis sur mon banc, sous la la: In the evening I read on my bench, under the lantern. Nox goes by and says good evening. Sometimes he gives me a poem. It's the best moment.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois au Cercle, je regar: In the evening, I sit at the Circle, watch the fire, and I'm already thinking about tomorrow's bread.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois au Diable Repu et j: In the evening, I sit at the Diable Repu and tell Grumbald about my catch. He pretends to listen while drying his glasses. One evening, I told him I'd caught a whale. He answered: “That's nice, dear.” The next day, he bought a bigger cauldron. He was listening, after all. A little.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois au Diable Repu, che: In the evening I sit at the Diable Repu, my husband's place. He serves me a frozen lava, and I tell him about the fishing. He pretends to listen. I pretend not to notice.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois sur ma mousse, près: In the evening, I sit on my moss, near the fire, and watch the young ones dance. My paws still dance, in my head.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois sur un banc de la p: In the evening, I sit on a bench in the square and watch people go by. Not for the people: for what they're wearing. You learn a lot by looking at sleeves.
textes.Le soir, je m'échappais pour écouter Gra: In the evenings, I'd slip out to listen to Grandpa Ébène on the Grand Square. My favourite story was the one about the princess who wanted to see snow. She crossed the Nine Circles to touch a snowflake, and came back saying that the cold is mostly there so we'll love the fire. It took me a long time to understand.
textes.Le soir, je m'étire au coin du feu. Sept: In the evening, I stretch by the fire. Seven times. It's the perfect number of stretches.
textes.Le soir, je monte au Cercle écouter les: In the evening, I go up to the Circle to listen to the Moonstones. They speak slowly. You have to be patient.
textes.Le soir, je monte en haut de la tour, j': In the evening, I climb to the top of the tower, open my wings and look at the city. From above, Pandémonia looks like a birthday cake. With lots of candles.
textes.Le soir, je monte sur la dunette. De là-: In the evening, I climb up to the poop deck. From up there, you can see Stoneheart turn red at sunset. It calms me.
textes.Le soir, je pose mon sac et je danse sur: In the evening, I put down my bag and dance on the Great Square. It's the only time I'm not flying. Well, I hop. That's almost flying.
textes.Le soir, je prends ma table au Diable Re: In the evening I take my table at the Diable Repu and tell the tale of the ash storm. Grumbald knows it by heart. He mouths the words along with me.
textes.Le soir, je promène les chiots dans les: In the evening, I walk the puppies through the streets. They bark at the street lamps. Nox says good evening to them. They adore him: he smells of lamp wick.
textes.Le soir, je prête trois lucioles à Noise: In the evenings, I lend Noisette three fireflies to sort her seeds. She's given them names: Pip, Acorn and Peanut. Peanut is the brightest, but she eats the other two's honey. Noisette says that's normal, she's a peanut.
textes.Le soir, je raconte ma journée à Maman a: In the evening, I tell Mum about my day before bed. Three times. The first time, I tell it fast. The second, I tell the mushrooms. The third, I tell it yawning. Mum says the third is her favourite, because I fall asleep in the middle.
textes.Le soir, je range mes fioles par couleur: In the evening, I sort my vials by colour. Then by smell. Then I mix them.
textes.Le soir, je regarde la cité s'allumer de: In the evening, I watch the city light up from the promenade. All those windows are people still inventing.
textes.Le soir, je regarde la mer. Des fois, je: In the evening, I watch the sea. Sometimes I see a sea serpent. Sometimes it's a log. Sometimes it's the honey drink.
textes.Le soir, je teste mes fusées sur la jeté: In the evening, I test my rockets on the jetty, near the lighthouse. Captain Charbonnel says I scare the fish. The fish have never said anything to me.
textes.Le soir, je vais flotter aux Thermes. Je: In the evening I go and float at the Baths. I float very well. Bulle says I'm the only customer who never sinks. It's thanks to the brioches.
textes.Le soir, je vais m'asseoir aux Jardins d: In the evening I go and sit in the Ash Gardens, near my mother's herbs. It's the only place in the city where nobody asks me for a potion against hiccups.
textes.Le soir, je vais écouter Calcine jouer s: In the evening, I go and listen to Calcine play on the Great Square. In the front row. Eyes closed. I sigh at the right moments. Well, I think they're the right moments.
textes.Le soir, je venais pleurer dans le jardi: In the evenings, I'd come and cry in the hotel garden, among the thyme. A lady arrived with a basket and scissors. She sat down beside me and said: “Lime blossom, lemon balm, and a pinch of Rose's lavender. For a broken heart.” The next evening, there was a steaming cup waiting for me on the bench.
textes.Le soir, la brume monte du Bois Tors. La: In the evening, the mist rises from the Twisted Wood. The ball sees more clearly then. I see less.
textes.Le soir, la place danse. Je joue jusqu'à: In the evening, the square dances. I play until my fingers smoke. Literally: they smoke. We're demons.
textes.Le soir, la taverne est pleine. Pirates: In the evening, the tavern is full. Pirates on one side, fishermen on the other, and me in the middle with my cudgel.
textes.Le soir, le Cœur-Brasier ronronne. Je l': In the evening, the Ember Heart purrs. I listen to it, I talk to it, and sometimes it answers. Old keepers get a little odd. It's normal.
textes.Le soir, le Repu est plein : le Capitain: In the evening, the Diable Repu is packed: the Captain tells his storm, Kraxx sneezes, my Moloka laughs. It's the loveliest noise in the world.
textes.Le soir, le lac devient un miroir. Je re: In the evening, the lake becomes a mirror. I watch the moon settle on it. I haven't tired of it in sixty years.
textes.Le soir, le vent se couche. Moi aussi. O: In the evening, the wind goes to bed. So do I. We say good night to each other.
textes.Le soir, les crocodiles sortent. Je rent: In the evening the crocodiles come out. I bring in my boat, and my toes.
textes.Le soir, les histoires ont meilleur goût: Stories taste better in the evening. It's the shadows that give them their salt.
textes.Le soir, les hérons viennent voler mes p: In the evening, the herons come to steal my fish. I throw clods of mud at them. They think it's funny.
textes.Le soir, mon auberge est pleine de sorci: In the evening, my inn is full of tired wizards. They all tell of their great deeds. Half of it is true.
textes.Le soir, on boit le thé devant l'échoppe: In the evening, we drink tea in front of the workshop, without talking. Once, he talked. About his father's forge, in a port up north. With my ear, I heard half of it. The good half, I think. I never repeated it to anyone. And you didn't hear it either.
textes.Le soir, on fait un feu sur la plage, av: In the evening, we light a fire on the beach with the others. We grill what we caught, and we talk about what we didn't catch.
textes.Le soir, on pêche au bout du quai, elle: In the evening we fish at the end of the quay, she and I. She takes her hooks apart to see how they're made; I fish. At the end, I have six sardines and she has an improved hook. We share: she takes three sardines, I take the hook. That's fair.
textes.Le soir, quand Mélisse rince ses flacons: In the evening, when Mélisse rinses her bottles, I drop by to check the sugar at the bottom. It's serious work. There's always too much. I check every evening anyway, in case it changes. She's never noticed.
textes.Le soir, quand Nenetl joue de la flûte-c: In the evening, when Nenetl plays the hummingbird flute, Tlaco lifts his head and sings, ahoooooo! Not sad: happy! So I dance, and everyone claps. It's our act! Nenetl says we're the best performers in Aztlán. After her.
textes.Le soir, quand je descends de ma chaise,: In the evening, when I climb down from my chair, cooked like a prawn, Kiki has kept a bucket of ice for me. I put my feet in it and he serves me a “hero's punch”, fruit only. He says it's the official drink of lifeguards. I'm the only one who drinks it. He's very proud of it.
textes.Le soir, quand je ferme l'atelier, je mo: In the evening, when I close the workshop, I go up to my roof terrace and count the lights on the galleon. Seven, above the cannons. The brightest, Bertha's, is one of my eight-pointed stars. The hardest one I know how to pierce. She has good taste, that thief. Deep down, I like it that my lanterns go sailing.
textes.Le soir, quand les clients sont partis,: In the evening, when the customers have gone, I take a bath of my own. Just me, the bubbles and the stars. And sometimes Bobor, bobbing like a cork.
textes.Le soir, sous la treille, avec les lampi: In the evening, under the trellis, with the lanterns… It's my favourite moment.
textes.Le soir, sur mon banc de la Grand-Place,: In the evening, on my bench on the Great Square, Nox passes by with his lamplighter's pole. He lights the lantern above me, puts a little folded paper on the bench and leaves without a word. On the paper, there's a poem. I keep them all in a box. I've got a hundred and twelve. I read them to the pups.
textes.Le soir, tout Port-Azur finit ici : les: In the evening, all of Port-Azur ends up here: fishermen, tourists, the mayor. Even Anselme, sometimes, when he forgets his lighthouse.
textes.Le soir, à la fête, je prends l'oud de m: In the evening, at the party, I take my father's oud. People dance. Or they leave. Either suits me.
textes.Le soir… L'heure où j'allume le premier: Evening… The hour when I light the first street lamp. The gentlest hour. You've got good taste. It's the hour of poems.
textes.Le sol fait « blop ». Une gelée verte gr: The floor goes “blop”. A green jelly as big as a house rises before the throne, a tiny crown perched crookedly: THE JELLY KING! “Who dares walk on my clean tiles?” he gurgles.
textes.Le sol tremble ! La Marmite bouillonne d: The ground trembles! The Cooking Pot bubbles harder and harder… An eruption is coming!
textes.Le sol tremble. L'eau noire des douves b: The ground shakes. The black water of the moat bubbles, and a gigantic crocodile rises from it, covered in spines, with jaws at every joint: CIPACTLI, the Earth monster, from whom the gods made the world!
textes.Le sol tremble. Quelque part dehors, un: The ground shakes. Somewhere outside, a bird falls off its branch, offended.
textes.Le soleil qui se lève… La lanterne de to: The rising sun… Everyone's lantern. I've never managed to make one as beautiful. I still try. Every morning, I watch it, to learn.
textes.Le soleil s'est levé… mais il ne bouge p: The sun has risen… but it doesn't move. It burns, motionless, above the fire. The gods, long ago, had the same trouble.
textes.Le soleil se lève. Une journée toute neu: The sun's rising. A brand-new day, not a scratch on it yet.
textes.Le soleil, c'est une grosse bougie sans: The sun is a big candle with no pattern. But I don't hold it against it: without it, I'd have no night to fill.
textes.Le soleil, chez nous, a trois visages :: Here the sun has three faces: Khepri the scarab, who pushes it up in the morning, Ra who shines at noon, Atum the old man who sets in the evening. Remember that: the Sphinx loves that sort of thing.
textes.Le soleil, là-bas. Il est pour moi. Pous: The sun, over there. It's mine. Move over.
The sun, perhaps. My throat, no.
textes.Le sommet du Mont Fusain — toute l'île,: The summit of Mount Charcoal — the whole island, in black and white, like a drawing laid on the blue sea
textes.Le souk est couvert de roseaux, pour l'o: The souk is roofed with reeds, for the shade. At noon, the light comes through the stalks and paints stripes on everything. Even on people.
textes.Le souterrain du Grand Moaï (yeux rendus: The underground of the Great Moai (eyes restored, going down)
textes.Le souterrain du Grand Moaï — un escalie: The underground of the Great Moai — a staircase that winds down into the dark… and, at the very bottom, something singing
textes.Le style. C'est ce que disait Barnabé de: The style. That's what Barnabé said about his map.
textes.Le tableau des records, là, c'est moi qu: The record board, there — I paint it. Bondi's been at the top for three years. He's starting to get bored, all alone up there.
textes.Le tableau est couvert d'affiches : slim: The board is covered in posters: slimes, frogs, goblins, a feathered hat… A sign: “Contracts reserved for registered adventurers. See Églantine at the counter. (She doesn't bite.)”
The stool is there. Like yesterday.
textes.Le tajine de Lalla Zohra : dorade, olive: Lalla Zohra's tagine: sea bream, olives, preserved lemon and saffron, cooked for three hours over the embers. Restores four hearts.
textes.Le tajine du vendredi, c'est la recette: The Friday tajine is my mother's recipe. Sea bream, preserved lemon, olives, and Lalla Aïcha's saffron, from nowhere else. It cooks in Halima's big dish, the one with the fish engraved on the lid. They say it's famous as far as Carène. It's true. A sailor from Carène asked me for the recipe. I gave him half. The other half is my hands.
A tajine is both the dish and the pot. The pointed lid sends the steam back down into the meat. Or the fish, here. It's magic you can eat.
textes.Le tambour bat toujours, quelque part…: The drum is still beating, somewhere…
textes.Le tapis des étoiles ? Il n'est pas à ve: The carpet of the stars? It's not for sale. Fine. For you, I'll show it. Look: the city gate, down here. Then three stars, one after the other, walking northeast, toward the dunes. Those are the old caravan markers: at night they still light up all by themselves, who knows why. After the third, the crescent dune: the walking dune. And beneath the dune, a sun. On the border, three signs, always in the same order: the star, the dune, the sun. My grandmother used to say: “that's the key.” Me, I say: it's pretty.
textes.Le temps ? Vingt-deux ans que j'attends: Time? Twenty-two years I've been waiting for it to wipe things out, and nothing. It must be on strike. Or it's waiting to get paid too.
Time wipes everything out in the end.
textes.Le terminal clignote : « > REMONTER ? [O: The terminal blinks: “> GO BACK UP? [Y]”. You type “Y”. Beep! The glass doors open… and there you are again in broad daylight, in front of the Grey Factory gate.
textes.Le thé d'abord, Corentin. Les fins se mé: Tea first, Corentin. Endings must be earned.
textes.Le thé d'abord, mon frère. L'histoire en: Tea first, my brother. The story after. Twice, if you like.
textes.Le thé de bienvenue ! Assieds-toi ! (Ses: The welcome tea! Sit down! (His four arms flutter: a teapot, a cup, a saucer, a teaspoon, all at once.) Stellar tea, served midnight blue, with gold sparkles. Drink slowly: it tastes of mint, of rain, and of something else nobody can quite name. So? You can't find the name either? Welcome to our home!
textes.Le thé, ici, se sert trois fois. Le prem: Tea, here, is served three times. The first glass is bitter like life, the second sweet like love, the third light like death. The fourth, you have to pay for.
Tea is not to be rushed.
textes.Le tic-tac de vingt horloges remplit la: The ticking of twenty clocks fills the room. It sounds like a very steady rain.
Yours, always. It has a future.
textes.Le timbre, c'est un sou. La conversation: The stamp is a penny. The conversation is free.
textes.Le titre, c'est le nom de la leçon. Ça n: The title is just the name of the lesson. It doesn't count.
textes.Le tombeau de la Dune qui Marche. L'air: The tomb of the Walking Dune. The air is dry, still. Sandstone columns, sarcophagi, and at the very back, on a dais, in a ray of light fallen from who knows where… a golden disc.
textes.Le tour de la ville en monorail: A monorail tour of the city
The lot? Go on then: {prix} coins.
textes.Le tout premier vol d'essai, nous étions: The very first test flight, there were two of us in the gondola, Héloïse and me. Her with her plans, me at the stick. At a hundred metres, it started to smell of cabbage. Héloïse went white as a sheet. I asked: “Is that normal?” She said: “I think so.” We landed bang on the cross painted in the middle of the field. I've never landed so well since.
textes.Le traité cale un pied de mon grand alam: The treatise props up one leg of my big still, so what? That book is at the heart of my work! Théophraste saw it, last time. He went white as a sheet and walked out without finishing his syrup. It's the first time he hadn't finished his syrup. I felt a bit guilty. A bit.
textes.Le trident des rois de l'Atlantide, offe: The trident of the kings of Atlantis, a gift from Queen Néréa. Gold, mother-of-pearl and a glowing sea stone. Damage: 14, and the third hit of a combo strikes half again as hard. Underwater, it strikes from afar.
textes.Le trident te va bien. Mon arrière-grand: The trident suits you. My great-grandfather used it to talk to whales. I never managed it.
textes.Le troc… Oh, non. Tu parles comme mon on: Swaps… Oh, no. You sound like my uncle! You'll end up with a carpet that doesn't fly and three goats, you'll see.
textes.Le trois. Tu avais raison la première fo: The third. You were right the first time.
textes.Le troisième jour, j'ai voulu interviewe: On the third day, I tried to interview Achille. Through a megaphone, from the airfield bench. First question: “Are you hungry?” He shouted something. The wind carried it all away. Adèle took the megaphone out of my hands, very calmly, and said: “He said yes. As always.” I didn't dare ask the second question.
textes.Le troisième soir, pour me faire rire, l: On the third evening, to make me laugh, Doctor Roux told me about the jungle berry she'd tasted that morning. She'd spent the afternoon seeing everything in purple. “Even the seagulls, my dear. Purple!” I laughed so hard that a gardener came to check everything was all right.
textes.Le trophée du Tournoi des Cornes : une c: The trophy of the Tournament of Horns: a ram's horn of solid gold, engraved with the names of all the champions. Yours is at the very bottom, in letters that still shine.
textes.Le trésor de Barbe-Sanglante… raconte-mo: Barbe-Sanglante's treasure… tell me about it.
textes.Le trésor des Rois-Ciel ! Deux cents piè: The treasure of the Sky Kings! Two hundred coins, three gold coins, two rubies, the Crown of the Clouds, the Sword of the Clouds whose blade crackles with lightning… and a strange diving mask with crystal lenses. With it, you can breathe underwater! Far below, beneath the sea, south-west of the village, a light shines…
textes.Le trésor du Cœur du Chant !: The treasure of the Heart of the Song!
The throne is six hundred years old, Coralin.
textes.Le vainqueur de Nâga ! Approche, que je: The vanquisher of Nâga! Come closer, let me look at you. You're smaller than in Barnabé's song.
textes.Le vainqueur du Serpent des Abysses ! Le: The vanquisher of the Serpent of the Deep! The ravens told me everything. Come closer!
textes.Le vendredi, Hnia et Rabia font leurs co: On Fridays, Hnia and Rabia do their accounts together: my hammer blows, his glasses of tea. Hassan and I wait on the bench. He serves me from his very first teapot, the dented one. I say it has a dent. He says: “It's yours.” I know. It's a fine dent.
textes.Le vendredi, Lola entre à la poste en pa: On Fridays, Lola comes into the post office slipping behind the pillar, then behind the postcard stand, then she pops her letter into the yellow postbox, very fast, and runs out again. As if nobody could see her. With her blue apron and her red hair, the whole square sees her. I wave to her. She pretends not to notice.
textes.Le vendredi, Lucas rentre du quai « un p: On Fridays, Lucas comes home from the quay “a bit early, by chance”. He sits on his step on High Street and watches the end of the street. When I arrive, he pretends to retie his shoelace. He wears boots without laces. I hand him the envelope. He says thank you three times.
textes.Le vendredi, je rentre du quai un peu pl: On Fridays, I come home from the quay a bit early. By chance. I sit on my step on High Street to get some air. Nadine comes along with her satchel. She says: “Nothing for you… Oh wait, here.” Every week, the same joke. Every week, my heart drops and jumps back up.
textes.Le vent a dispersé les trois pages de la: The wind has scattered the three pages of Django's most beautiful song across the quay, the square and the beach.
textes.Le vent dans les cheveux, c'est le bonhe: Wind in your hair, pure happiness!
textes.Le vent de Carène est très demandé ! Il: Carène wind is in great demand! It's fresh!
textes.Le vent du désert, le chergui, souffle t: The desert wind, the chergui, blows for three days, then stops. On those days, we don't go out.
The wind weaves very nicely these days.
textes.Le vent tourbillonne trop fort au-dessus: The wind swirls too fiercely above the Citadel: Ventaile will wait for you at the Wind Perch. Whistle for her from the esplanade.
The wind swirls far too hard above the Citadel. Go to the Wind Field.
textes.Le vent tourne au nord. Ça sent la tempê: The wind's turning north. Smells like a storm, or an adventure. Either suits me.
textes.Le vent tourne, moussaillon. Le vent tou: The wind is turning, cabin boy. The wind is always turning.
textes.Le vent, je ne peux pas le gronder. Toi,: I can't scold the wind. You, I can.
The wind. It's windy this afternoon.
textes.Le vent… il a emporté ma partition. Troi: The wind… it carried off my score. Three pages. One went off to the beach, one to the square, one to the east end of the quay. Without them, I can't play “The Azure Waltz” any more. If you find them…
textes.Le vert ! Et le hibou ? Il n'a rien dit: The green! And the owl? He didn't say anything? He never says anything, that's what's scary. (She hugs the pot to her chest.) Thank you, thank you. Hurry and pour it into paint cup number two. I want to see my leaves wake up. Here: a packet of my seeds. Plant them wherever you like, they even grow in black and white.
textes.Le vert du Bois des Hachures: The green of the Hatching Wood
textes.Le vert. Le pot numéro deux. Sans lui, m: The green. Pot number two. Without it, my plants no longer know they're plants. I think it rolled all the way to the Hollow Stump, deep in the woods, to the west. But a big owl lives there. It looks at me sideways, with eyes as round as coins. It doesn't know you: it won't have time to look at you sideways.
textes.Le vestibule de la Pyramide de Rê. L'air: The vestibule of the Pyramid of Ra. The air is cool and still, and smells of stone and incense. On the walls, thousands of painted signs; on the left, the sun's barque sailing through the night.
Heights. Me too. Remember? Hm. We'll take the stairs, one day. Together.
textes.Le vieil appareil photo de Gérard Dupuis: Gérard Dupuis's old camera. Three hundred photos of sunsets inside.
textes.Le vieux Corentin connaît mille histoire: Old Corentin knows a thousand stories. He says I add dragons. Not true: I add sharks too. And his stories are better with them.
textes.Le vieux Corentin dit qu'il y a un tréso: Old Corentin says there's treasure in the flooded holds. He mostly says it after his third mug of hot honey.
textes.Le village ! Je vois parfois vos lantern: The village! Sometimes I see your lanterns at night. It keeps me company.
textes.Le village ! La cabane de l'ermite, la j: The village! The hermit's hut, the jungle, the great kapok tree… I drew it from Léon's descriptions. I'll put a little cross for you in the corner, there. That's you, the cross.
textes.Le village est bâti dans les maisons-cha: The village is built in mushroom houses: you hollow out the stalk, open a window, and there you go. It grows along with us.
textes.Le virus est parti ! Glitch t'attend (pr: The virus is gone! Glitch is waiting for you (near the Arcade Station, or in the arcade hall in the afternoon).
textes.Le voilà, Brindille ! Et ma nouvelle du: Here it is, Brindille! And my news of the day?
textes.Le voisin du village ! Dis-moi, ils mang: The neighbour from the village! Tell me, do they still eat their soup cold over there?
textes.Le voisin s'appelait Larbi. Il pêchait a: The neighbour was called Larbi. He fished at the end of the jetty, and he never beat me at knots, never, for all his efforts. At seventeen, he left as a cabin boy on a merchant ship, to see the world. I stayed on the quay, mending. With each knot I told myself: one more day. That's a lot of knots, a wait.
textes.Le volcan donne des rubis, quand il est: The volcano gives rubies, when it's in a good mood. The miners find them in the red rock.
textes.Le volcan nous donne tout : le fer, le f: The volcano gives us everything: iron, fire, and warmth for the winter. Sometimes it takes a roof or two. That's the price.
textes.Le voleur de croissants ? Hier soir, en: The croissant thief? Last night, as I was closing, I saw a little white shadow dash towards the quay, east side, with a croissant in its mouth. A dog, I'd say.
textes.Le vrai secret de l'apnée ? Ne pas paniq: The real secret of free-diving? Don't panic. And don't think about sharks.
textes.Lentille agite sa louche géante : « Tu a: Lentille waves her giant ladle: “You've already had your bowl today! Come back tomorrow, there'll be another soup. Well, the same one, with different vegetables.”
textes.Lentille remplit un bocal de soupe fuman: Lentille fills a jar with steaming soup. “Enjoy your meal!”
textes.Lequel ? Le tien, ou son amoureux ?: Which one? Yours, or its sweetheart?
textes.Les Aztèques adorent le cacao aussi. Ils: The Aztecs love cacao too. They call it xocolatl. Their nobles drink fifty cups a day, apparently. If I drank fifty, I'd never sleep again.
textes.Les Aztèques d'Aztlán sont venus du nord: The Aztecs of Aztlán came from the north, from a place also called Aztlán. Their god told them to stop where an eagle would eat a snake on a cactus. Here, the serpent has feathers, and nobody eats it.
textes.Les Aztèques font pousser du maïs sur le: The Aztecs grow maize on the lake. On the lake! I struggle enough on solid ground.
textes.Les Bureaux. Un open-space gris à perte: The Offices. A grey open-plan space as far as the eye can see: desks in rows, plastic plants, buzzing neon lights… and bailiff drones reading eviction notices out loud. At the far end, a turnstile. Near the entrance, a staff memo.
textes.Les Caves Gluantes. Des couloirs de pier: The Sticky Caves. Corridors of mossy stone that twist every which way, and everywhere, little puddles going “blop”. Slimes! The staircase down is somewhere to the southeast.
textes.Les Champs de Blé Dur — le blé des pâtes: The Durum Wheat Fields — pasta wheat rippling in the wind
textes.Les Clous Rouillés ! Avant, on s'appelai: The Rusty Nails! We used to be called The New Nails, but we got old.
textes.Les Falaises du Clan — les grottes du Cl: The Clan Cliffs — the Clan's caves are dug into the rock
textes.Les Furies ! Elles planent au-dessus de: The Furies! They hover above the gate of Dis, then swoop at you. Step aside when they dive, strike when they climb back up.
textes.Les Hauts — les grandes tours de bureaux: The Heights — the great office towers, their ribbons of light, and the cars zipping between them
textes.Les Huit Recommandations des Pâtes\n1. T:
The Eight Recommendations of Pasta
1. Thou shalt not overcook the pasta.
2. Thou shalt share thy sauce with thy neighbour.
3. Thou shalt not break spaghetti in two.
4. Thou shalt taste before salting.
5. Thou shalt not throw pasta at the wall to see if it sticks.
6. Thou shalt leave a place at the table for the stranger.
7. Thou shalt do the dishes (even the pot).
8. Thou shalt smile: it tastes better with a smile.
textes.Les Jardins de Cendre sont au sud de la: The Ash Gardens are south of the Lower Town, next to my son's Baths. Volcano ash is the best soil in the world. Everything grows in it: all it takes is a little hot water and a lot of patience.
textes.Les Jumeaux ont joué contre les Seigneur: The Twins played against the Lords of Xibalba. They won. I dream of playing against the Lords. But preferably while staying alive.
textes.Les Limbes, le Premier Cercle. Des ombre: Limbo, the First Circle. Shadows glide between the columns. A stone sage holds a golden light; three bronze mirrors, a dark crystal, and a closed door.
textes.Les Lisses… gens d'un autre monde. Tout: The Smooth Ones… people from other world. All round, all soft, not one square. They say they see things… how to say… in very, very tiny pixels. So tiny you not see them. Strange, no?
The Smooth Ones… legend speak true.
textes.Les Mayas de Yaxché et les Aztèques d'Az: The Mayas of Yaxché and the Aztecs of Aztlán have their own sun too. Three peoples, three suns. The ancients said that one day someone would bring them together on the altar of the highlands.
textes.Les Mayas de Yaxché font une boisson de: The Mayas of Yaxché make a cacao drink, frothy and bitter. I tasted it once. I added honey, and they cried sacrilege.
textes.Les Mayas de Yaxché vendent des plumes d: The Mayas of Yaxché sell macaw feathers. I buy them too. Then I sell them on, dearer. That's trade.
textes.Les Mayas tissent aussi, avec un métier: The Mayas weave too, on a loom they tie to their waist and to a tree. Ix Sak, their weaver, works wonders with colours. I only do white. But what a white!
textes.Les Perles, {surnom}. Il en manque encor: The Pearls, {surnom}. {manque} are still missing. The coral garden, the wreck, the jellyfish trench… Abyssos will tell you more.
textes.Les Prés Blancs — des milliers de fleurs: The White Meadows — thousands of flowers… all white, waiting for their colours
textes.Les Rois-Ciel ! Ils descendaient nous vo: The Sky Kings! They used to come down to see us wearing masks like yours, before the flood. Their castle flew above us; their waterfalls brought us fresh water. You defeated Lord Storm? Then sky and sea are friends again.
textes.Les Ruelles — de vieux immeubles serrés,: The Alleys — old buildings packed close, signs everywhere, steam rising from the ground
textes.Les Récifs de Feu, à l'ouest ! J'y suis: The Fire Reefs, to the west! I sailed by there when I was young. Well, near there. Smoke everywhere, black rocks spitting sparks… We turned back. A dwarf made a gesture at us from the beach. Not a friendly one.
textes.Les Résidences — des immeubles d'habitat: The Residences — apartment buildings, balconies, water tanks on the roofs
textes.Les Seigneurs t'attendront. Ils ont le t: The Lords will wait for you. They have time.
textes.Les Taupes Hurlantes. On répétait dans u: The Howling Moles. We used to rehearse in a cellar. The moles moved out.
textes.Les Thermes de Soufre et les Jardins de: The Sulphur Baths and the Ash Gardens are in the south of the Lower Town. The sulphur from the springs is excellent for the skin, the horns and the spirits. Technically. I've never measured the spirits.
textes.Les Thermes de Soufre, au sud de la Bass: The Sulphur Baths, south of the Lower Town: three pools, steam, and the best view of the volcano. Sulphur is good for the skin, the horns and the spirits. My sister says it's not proven for the spirits. Well, I've proven it: look at me!
textes.Les abeilles de l'Arbre-Mère sont de bon: The Mother Tree's bees are in a good mood.
textes.Les abeilles vivent tout en haut de l'Ar: The bees live right at the top of the Mother Tree. Thalion fetches the honey. He says it's training.
textes.Les abords mènent à la porte. Restez géo: The surroundings lead to the gate. Stay a geographer.
textes.Les accessoires du chantier : chacun s'i: The shipyard accessories: each one is installed once and for all.
textes.Les affaires marchent ! Un client de la: Business is booming! A customer from the surface is the best of signs.
textes.Les affaires vont bien. Les affaires von: Business is good. Business is always good here. People steal, people sell, people buy. Me, I count.
textes.Les algues de la baie soignent les plaie: Seaweed from the bay heals wounds. Meadow honey, coughs. And Gwenola's hot honey… nothing at all, but everyone feels better.
textes.Les araignées de cristal laissent des éc: The crystal spiders leave shards behind. Grommelot loves them. Shh, it's a secret.
textes.Les araignées de cristal ont envahi la g: The crystal spiders have invaded the western cave. They leave shards behind when you break them. Bring me {manque}. For my fireplace. Not because they're pretty. Hmph.
The trees hear everything, you know.
textes.Les arbres entendent tout, tu sais. Eux: Trees hear everything, you know. They love it too.
textes.Les arbres qui portent une entaille clai: The trees with a pale notch, I marked those myself: soft wood, easy to fell. Leave the others alone.
textes.Les arbres, hein ? Et l'elfe qui danse d: The trees, eh? And the elf dancing behind them, does she like it too?
textes.Les armures s'effondrent dans un fracas: The armour collapses with a crash of scrap metal. At the back of the armoury, a chest has appeared.
textes.Les astres sont bien alignés. Et mes pie: The stars are well aligned. And my feet are nice and cool. What more could I ask?
textes.Les avares, dit-on, poussent ces poids d: The misers, they say, have been pushing these weights forever. You, though, have a goal: the golden slabs.
textes.Les babouches de noce sont presque finie: The wedding slippers are almost done: a cloth of her own, embroidered with gold thread. So Rachid won't see them, I hide them in a basket of ordinary yellow slippers, right at the bottom. The other day, a caravan trader wanted to buy the whole basket. I had to say it was reserved. For a wedding. Rachid was three steps away.
textes.Les babouches jaunes sont pour les homme: The yellow babouches are for men, the red and embroidered ones for women. The black ones, for pirates. They don't wear them, they hang them from their mast.
textes.Les balayeurs ont déposé une réclamation: The sweepers filed an official complaint. Signed “BEEP”. I wasn't the one who typed it. Hm. She replied with a letter. A fat letter. Stuffed with confetti. I put it in the Works' sorting machine. The machine jammed for three days. Confetti still comes out of it. Pink, mostly.
textes.Les balayeurs ont fait une réclamation o: The sweepers have filed an official complaint against me. Signed “BEEP”.
textes.Les bananiers sont mes amis. Ils ne dise: The banana trees are my friends. They never say anything, but they're very good listeners.
textes.Les barques des bergers viennent parfois: The shepherds' boats come here sometimes, with wool. The Carène boats too, with cider. And the Petit Piston, my tugboat, hasn't moved in three years. He's very happy like that.
textes.Les bateaux de nacre que les enfants fon: The mother-of-pearl boats the children float on the canal? His. Light, fast, they never sink. Mine, carved from the solid block, sank by the third bridge. One day I had Ondine buy one in secret, to work out how he does it. I still don't understand.
textes.Les beaux rêves passent par le trou du m: Good dreams pass through the hole in the middle.
textes.Les bergers des hautes terres allument d: The highland shepherds light fires on the ridges on full-moon nights. I don't know what they're celebrating.
textes.Les bergers des hautes terres ont un mou: The highland shepherds have a windmill that's been turning for a hundred years. A hundred years! I'd love to see how it's made. They won't let me near it.
textes.Les bergers gardent un secret, dans une: The shepherds keep a secret, in a cave under the great ridge. A round stone, carved. My grandfather said it's a key. A key to a door that can't be opened.
textes.Les biches ne savent ni forger, ni pêche: Does can't forge, or fish, or trade. But when we dance, the whole village forgets how tired it is. That's a job too, I think.
textes.Les bleus pour la sardine, les orange po: Blue ones for sardines, orange ones for sea bream. I always mend Driss's first. Next to me, Lalla Fatima, whom I keep an eye on without her knowing. The pirates' parrot that repeats everything: careful what you say. And at home, the jar of shells that's overflowing, and that nobody is allowed to touch.
textes.Les bocaux de « vent de Carène » que je: The jars of “Carène wind” I sell to the caravan traders: Nolwenn sews their canvas lids. She pretends to hate it. But she embroiders a little boat on every lid, and I never asked her to. It's the boat that makes them sell. She knows it. She doesn't want me to say so.
textes.Les bons ! Tu as l'œil. Donne-moi tes ma: The right ones! You have a good eye. Give me your hands. They're warm, that's good. Think of someone you love, very hard, and put your hand on your heart. … Do you feel it? That's healing. Now, go and see the wounded owl, near Agathe's caravan, in the Twisted Wood. She lets no one come near her. You, perhaps.
textes.Les bouchons, c'est pas contre toi, Tcho: The earplugs aren't against you, Tchoum. They're for the ears.
textes.Les bougainvilliers sur les façades, c'e: The bougainvillea on the house fronts — I planted it twenty years ago. Now it's eating the houses.
textes.Les bras en l'air, c'est pour les morcea: Arms in the air are for the tracks that build up. I'll save one for you, you'll recognise it: your arms will be up before you know why.
textes.Les braseros, la fresque… Les Anciens ad: The braziers, the fresco… The Ancients loved riddles. Read carefully what's carved under the pictures: for them, night always comes first.
textes.Les bûches du Bois Tors brûlent longtemp: Logs from the Twisted Wood burn long and without smoke. Crooked wood has patience, and gives it back as heat.
Cacti don't say anything. They prickle.
textes.Les cailloux-qui-chantent, tu connais ?: Singing-stones, ever heard of them? When the wind blows through them, they whistle. I hang them under the bridges so I know when the wind picks up. For a singing-stone, I'd give my finest golden acorn!
textes.Les canons de la Skala sont en bronze. J: The Skala's cannons are bronze. I polish them once a year. They've never fired. I hope it stays that way.
textes.Les canons du Léviathan ne tirent plus d: The Léviathan's cannons haven't fired in two centuries. I turned one into a hearth, two anvils and a cooking pot. Better that way.
Cannons. Cannons calm me down. Boom. That calms me. Boom.
textes.Les caravaniers du désert viennent ici v: The desert caravaneers come here to sell their dates and their salt, and leave with our dried fish. Carène, to the west, buys our spices. Everything passes through Tazira.
textes.Les caravaniers du sud disent que le dés: The southern caravanners say the desert is advancing. The northern shepherds say the snow is coming down. If everyone's right, we'll all end up on the Léviathan. Oh, but we're already here.
textes.Les caravaniers du sud m'apportent du co: The southern caravanners bring me desert cotton. The northern shepherds, wool. The mist people… nothing. They don't trade. But once, one of them left me a silver thread that glows in the dark.
textes.Les caravaniers du sud ont la peau dure: The southern caravanners have skin as tough as leather. They say it's the sun. I think it's a cream. I want the recipe.
textes.Les caravaniers du sud viennent parfois: The southern caravanners sometimes come to sell their spices. Last time, they sold me red sand, swearing it was chilli.
textes.Les carpes changent de couleur toutes le: The carp change color every ten minutes. I timed it.
textes.Les cartes ne mentent jamais. Moi, parfo: The cards never lie. I sometimes do.
textes.Les cartes ont parlé de vous, cette nuit: The cards spoke of you last night, Madame Sylvie.
