textes.Les cartes sont blanches… Tu as aidé tou: The cards are blank… You've helped everyone. All that's left is to live happily. That's the hardest part.
textes.Les cartes t'écouteront. Elles écoutent: The cards will listen to you. They always listen very well.
textes.Les cercles rouges au sol : des ronces v: The red circles on the ground: brambles are about to burst out! Get out of the circle, quick!
textes.Les chambres du dessus ont des lits à re: The rooms upstairs have spring beds. One of Héloïse's inventions. You sleep very well in them, if you manage to stay in.
textes.Les chambres sont dans l'entrepont, sous: The rooms are on the lower deck, under the main deck. You sleep in hammocks, like sailors of old. It rocks you, even though the ship doesn't move any more.
The camels are waiting for you.
textes.Les champignons sauteurs, c'est nous qui: We were the ones who grew the bouncing mushrooms, to play on. One morning I went back in secret, despite the crystal spiders. I jumped too high, my wand slipped out of my hand, it landed on the ledge right at the top… and a spider sat down next to it. I ran away. Since then, I don't like mushrooms any more.
textes.Les champs ! Enfin quelqu'un de raisonna: The fields! At last, somebody sensible. The earth, at least, doesn't move. Except when a crocodile crosses it.
textes.Les champs de chanvre — de hautes tiges: The hemp fields — tall green stalks: they're made into ropes and canvas
textes.Les champs de coquelicots — un grand tap: The poppy fields — a great red carpet rippling in the wind
textes.Les champs de la rive sud, personne n'en: Nobody wanted the fields on the south bank: too close to the plateau of the dead. My father took them. The silt there is black and rich, the barley grows as tall as a man. He built the shadoof with his own hands. When he left to join Osiris, I kept the fields and the shadoof. The pole creaks. I don't fix it. It's his voice.
textes.Les chats de Ramure pêchent dans les mar: The cats of Ramure have always fished in the pools. Not with our paws: with rods. Paws were a long time ago. We've moved on.
textes.Les chats ne courent pas longtemps. Mais: Cats don't run for long. But fast. Very fast. The last bend, before the Watchtower: that's where I'll pass Bondi. One day.
textes.Les chats… Hm. Je ne dis rien. Je ne dis: Cats… Hm. I'm not saying anything. I'm not saying anything. … At least cats don't spit fire. Come and see my pups anyway: they'll change your mind.
textes.Les chats… Ne le dites pas trop fort. Bo: Cats… Don't say it too loudly. Boulon won't hold it against you. Much. He has bad memories of the cats of Tazira. So does his nose.
textes.Les chaussettes : avant ou après le pant: Socks: before or after the trousers?
textes.Les chauves-souris ronflent moins fort q: The bats snore quieter than you, my dove.
textes.Les chiens ! Évidemment ! Tu as un cœur: Dogs! Obviously! You've got a kennel for a heart, you have! Come and say hello to mine. Careful: they spit a bit of fire. Like all babies.
textes.Les chiens d'enfer sauvages du champ de: The wild hellhounds of the lava field, east of the volcano, aren't nasty: they're just badly brought up! They pounce, they breathe fire, and they're hungry. My brother says they must be driven back. I say they must be understood. Still, watch out: they bite hard.
textes.Les chiens du champ de lave ne s'approch: The lava field hounds don't come near our walls any more. My sister says they've understood. I say you were convincing. Nothing to report. Thank you.
textes.Les chiens sauvages ont reculé dans le c: The wild dogs have pulled back into the lava field. I'll still take them bones. A dog that backs off is a dog that's thinking. That's a start.
Hilda's goats graze on ash. I don't know how. Their cheese is the best in the world.
textes.Les chênes attirent la foudre. Je dis ça: Oaks attract lightning. I'm just saying… for no reason.
textes.Les cinq braseros de l'Aire des Duels fl: The five braziers of the Duelling Ground blaze! Pyra Flammèche applauds from afar.
textes.Les cinq pierres chantent ensemble ! Des: The five stones sing together! Thousands of fireflies burst out of the pool and swirl up to the ceiling… With a long creak, the roots blocking the staircase draw back.
textes.Les cloches vibrent ensemble, discordant: The bells ring out together, jangling, then fall silent… That was not the right order.
textes.Les clochettes de cristal, c'est moi qui: I tuned the crystal bells myself. You have to listen before you play. Always listen.
textes.Les clochettes de cristal, je les avais: I'd spent a year tuning the crystal bells. Pimprenelle wanted to make them play by themselves, with a flick of her wand. They played all night, faster and faster. Nobody slept. It took me a month to retune them. She calls it modern music.
textes.Les clous du chantier disparaissaient, u: Nails kept disappearing from the yard, a handful a day. I thought there was a thief. One evening, I followed Amine down to the beach: he was burying them in a crate, under a cross drawn in the sand. A treasure chest. Three hundred nails. I left them there. The day he digs them up, he'll know what treasure is: nails.
textes.Les clowns ? Ha ! Moi aussi ! Il y en av: Clowns? Ha! Me too! There was one, Bobo, who put his make-up on in the morning and never took it off. Not even to sleep. Brr.
textes.Les colis qui arrivent pour la douze son: The parcels that arrive for room twelve are worryingly varied. A crate that ticked. A basket that clucked. A copper tube labelled “Fragile, do not open before the full moon”. I sign. I take them up. I ask no questions. Pauline, on the other hand, asks plenty.
textes.Les complaintes… Ah. Toi, tu as un cœur: Laments… Ah. You've got a heart that listens. That's rare, around here. I'll play you one, some rainy evening. The whaler's one, the one Mama loves.
textes.Les coquillages ? … Vous sortez de chez: Shells? … You've just come from Victor's, admit it. Well. At least a real shell doesn't lie. As long as it isn't painted.
textes.Les corbeaux des cendres portent nos mes: The ash ravens carry our messages to the king, under the mountain. They drop feathers everywhere.
textes.Les couleurs… Ah. Ix Sak t'aurait sauté: Colours… Ah. Ix Sak would have hugged you. Here, we've always woven in white. But I understand. I… understand very well.
textes.Les coups qui enlèvent un cœur ou plus p: Blows that take a heart or more lose half a heart.
textes.Les courants apportent des choses d'en h: The currents bring things down from above: a bit of rope, a feather, an empty bottle that smells of apples. Every thing has its story, you just have to listen. One day I found a sandal. I got forty stories out of it. Abyssos says it's just a sandal. That's why he writes, and I tell.
The crabs have a whole beach, Zoé.
textes.Les cristaux s'allument et chantent tout: The crystals light up and sing softly… The crystal engine is in place. Look behind you as you sail: a wake of stars!
textes.Les crocodiles de l'embouchure de l'Iter: The crocodiles at the mouth of the Iterou keep stealing the nets of Khéty, the fisherman. He wants someone to bring him two of their teeth, so they get the message.
textes.Les crocodiles du marais ont les meilleu: The marsh crocodiles have the best teeth in the world. Hard as steel. With three teeth, I'll make you an iron fist: your punches will count double in a brawl. Well, a bit more.
textes.Les crocodiles viennent de l'embouchure,: The crocodiles come from the river mouth, to the east. There are three, maybe four. The biggest one we call Sobek, like the crocodile god. He doesn't deserve the name.
textes.Les daurades « d'hier » de Paulo ? C'éta: Paulo's sea bream “from yesterday”? They were mine. I'd kept them overnight in my bucket, I couldn't be bothered to go to the stall. Rosalie took them without a word, and when Paulo shouted, she swore they were from that morning. She fell out with him for my sake. Don't repeat that, youngster.
textes.Les dents ? Une à chaque victoire. Il ne: The teeth? One for every win. I haven't a single real one left. That tells you how often I win.
textes.Les derniers feux s'éteignent dans le ci: The last fireworks fade in the sky, the flying lanterns turn into stars. Lumina cries with joy in Bobor's arms. “The most beautiful Night of Lanterns in a thousand years!” (The party itself will go on until dawn.)
textes.Les dettes ne rouillent pas, sous la mer: Debts don't rust, under the sea.
textes.Les deux ! Comme Youssef. Il casse en so: Both! Like Youssef. He breaks things with a smile, then pays in sardines. So be careful when you turn around, all right? Especially if you're smiling.
textes.Les deux ! Comme le fer : solide, mais o: Both! Like iron: strong, but you can give it any shape if you heat it enough. You'd make a good metal, you would.
textes.Les deux ! Comme ma fille et moi. Elle f: Both! Like my daughter and me. She does the useful, I do the pretty, and between us we make a house that stands up. More or less up.
textes.Les deux ! Je les ai encore tous les deu: Both! I've still got both of them!
textes.Les deux ! Tic-tac, tic-tac, BOUM ! C'es: Both! Tick-tock, tick-tock, BOOM! That's exactly how Zigomar's rockets work. You've got a scientific mind. I hereby name you my assistant.
textes.Les deux ! Un cœur grand comme un chenil: Both! A heart as big as a kennel, with a cat flap! You've got room, you have. Want a pup? No? Think about it. You've got room.
textes.Les deux ! Une réponse de sage. Ou de ma: Both! A wise man's answer. Or a merchant's. So take a sardine, and a note on the house: SARDIIINES! There, you've got everything.
textes.Les deux ! Voilà. Tu as compris ce que j: Both! There you go. You've understood what took me eighty years to understand: the best stories are true and made up. They happened twice.
textes.Les deux ? Ha ! Tu es gourmand. C'est bi: Both? Ha! You're greedy. Good. Both does exist: it's called the Requin Borgne. And no, she's not for sale.
textes.Les deux ? Montre. … Hm. Celle-là travai: Both? Show me. … Hm. That one works. That one watches. Put the other one to work.
textes.Les deux ? Petit diplomate ! Tu ferais u: Both? Little diplomat! You'd make a good mayor. Not a good measurer, but a good mayor. Right, I'm sulking. Just a little, for form's sake.
textes.Les deux ? … Les deux. Mais oui ! Pourqu: Both? … Both. Of course! Why didn't we think of that?
textes.Les deux dalles d'Isis s'illuminent ! Co: Both of Isis's slabs light up! Against the back wall, a casket slowly rises from the floor.
textes.Les deux forges de la terrasse, c'est po: The two forges on the terrace are for heavy work. The Royal Forge, under the mountain, is for masterpieces.
textes.Les deux gardiens de bronze s'effondrent: The two bronze guardians collapse with one last clatter. The sheepfold goes quiet again… At the back of the niche, a small fresco.
textes.Les deux gardiens de pierre s'arrachent: The two stone guardians tear themselves free from their pedestals!
textes.Les deux gardiens sont tombés. Dans un c: Both guardians have fallen. With a rattle of chains, the grate rises!
textes.Les deux poids sont sur les dalles d'or: Both weights are on the golden slabs! A deep “clack” somewhere in the walls: the south door sinks into the floor.
textes.Les deux vieux de la pétanque, Raymond e: The two old boys at the pétanque pitch, Raymond and Marcel, have been squabbling for forty years. They're inseparable.
textes.Les deux villages ensemble, en direct de: Both villages together, live from the Main Stage. The crowd sings. It whistles, it crackles, it's magnificent.
textes.Les deux yeux de corail du Grand Moaï: The Great Moai's two coral eyes
textes.Les deux yeux de corail s'envolent de te: The two coral eyes fly out of your hands, rise high up and settle into the Great Moai's face. He blinks. Once. Slowly.
textes.Les deux. Comme moi, peut-être. Le blanc: Both. Like me, perhaps. White by day, colours… in my thoughts. You're wiser than you look.
textes.Les donjons ont une acoustique formidabl: Dungeons have wonderful acoustics for thunder.
textes.Les draps, monsieur ! Je fais les draps: The sheets, sir! I'm doing the sheets!
textes.Les dés ? Toujours ! Montre-moi la coule: Dice? Always! Show me the colour of your coins.
textes.Les dés m'aiment. Ils m'ont toujours aim: The dice love me. They always have.
textes.Les elfes n'oublient rien. Surtout pas l: Elves forget nothing. Least of all kind people.
textes.Les elfes ne quittent presque jamais le: Elves almost never leave Bois-Doré. The mist protects us… and shuts us in a little, too. I'm the first in a long time to speak to a human.
textes.Les enfants croient que je vole. Je les: The children think I fly. I let them. Really, I take the stairs. Very slowly.
textes.Les enfants disent qu'il y a un dragon s: The children say there's a dragon under the great pool. It's the King of the Pools. He gets a little bigger every time someone talks about him.
textes.Les enfants du port veulent tous apprend: The harbour kids all want to learn knots. Little Yasmine is gifted. She'll make a good pirate. Or worse: a good captain of the guard.
textes.Les enfants me réclament la pieuvre géan: The children beg me for the giant octopus every night. Thirty arms, then forty, then fifty. Triton came to ask me to stop, very polite, very straight, trident in hand. The children shouted “it's him!” and formed a guard of honour all the way to the Gate. He went bright red. He's never asked for anything since.
textes.Les engrenages du Colosse se bloquent !: The Colossus's gears jam! Its furnace opens: strike!
textes.Les engrenages grincent… et se mettent à: The gears creak… and start turning! The bronze gate lifts, the water of the big pond rushes into the old canal with a roar. The level drops, drops… In the middle of the pond a big round stone appears.
textes.Les enveloppes de Lola sentent le punch: Lola's envelopes smell of coconut punch. Every one of them. She must write them on the Perroquet's counter, between orders. When I sort them, the whole post office smells like holidays. Once, there was a little syrup stain in the corner. I put the stamp over it, to hide it. A stamp with a heart. By chance.
textes.Les femmes du désert tissent des tapis ;: The women of the desert weave carpets; we weave nets. Same hands, different thread.
textes.Les feuilles qui bougeaient se redressen: The moving leaves stand upright: carnivorous plants! And a bundle of brambles that walks…
textes.Les feux follets ? Des farceurs. Ils te: Will-o'-the-wisps? Pranksters. They charge at you for a laugh. Their laugh hurts.
textes.Les filets bleus sont pour les sardines,: The blue nets are for sardines, the orange ones for sea bream. The green one… the green one is the one the pirates tore with their anchor. I'll make them pay for it.
The nets are cast. Sing, Celebrë.
textes.Les flammes vacillent… puis toutes s'éte: The flames flicker… then all go out at once. That was not the right order.
textes.Les fleurs de braise poussent sur les pe: Ember flowers grow on the slopes of the volcano. My mother is always looking for some for her flowerbeds. They burn without burning up: a botanical mystery. If you pick some, hold them by the stem, and speak to them politely.
textes.Les fleurs de cempasúchil, orange comme: Cempasúchil flowers, orange like the sun, go on the altars to guide the souls of the dead. Their scent shows them the way.
textes.Les fleurs le matin, les fleurs l'après-: Flowers in the morning, flowers in the afternoon, and in the evening, my bench. There was Hugo and his refused rose, waiting in a vase. Léa, a real florist from the mainland, who I talked with for two hours. Kiki, my neighbour from the ferry terminal, who plays the ukulele under my window at midnight. And the elves' moonflower, which I've never seen, and which grows in my dreams.
textes.Les flocons de givre éternel tombent sur: Everlasting frost flakes fall on the northern cliffs, where the wind never stops. They don't melt. Not even in Pyra's hand. Especially not in Pyra's hand.
textes.Les fusées de Zigomar prêtes, revenir la: With Zigomar's rockets ready, come back at night (after 8 p.m.) to the Great Lantern Square for the party
textes.Les fusées sont prêtes, grâce à tes cris: The rockets are ready, thanks to your sulphur crystals! Now they're just waiting for the Night of Lanterns. And a bit of luck. A lot of luck.
textes.Les fèves de cacao, chez nous, servent a: Here, cacao beans are also used as money. A rabbit is worth ten beans. A turkey, a hundred. Me, I'd rather drink them.
Fairies? Glitter gnats. All of them. … Brindille is nice. Don't repeat that.
textes.Les fées de l'ouest ont des fleurs de lu: The fairies in the west have moon flowers. Here, we have moon mushrooms. The fairies say their flowers glow brighter. The fairies say a lot of things.
textes.Les fées des racines, sous l'Arbre-Mère: The root fairies, beneath the elves' Mother Tree, are our cousins. They dig; we fly.
textes.Les fées du Bois-Doré auraient des cloch: Apparently the fairies of the Bois-Doré have little bells that ring in rhythm. I'd so love to hear them.
textes.Les fées du village ont toutes un servic: The village fairies all have a favour to ask of you. In exchange, they give fairy dust!
textes.Les fées m'ont dit que la musique de Mis: The fairies told me Mistral's music rises all the way to their kingdom, when the wind blows the right way.
textes.Les galions ne volent pas, Silas. Mais r: Galleons don't fly, Silas. But go on.
textes.Les gardiens de corail… Des soldats chan: The coral guardians… Soldiers turned to stone. My sword cuts through them like stale bread. Especially the third hit.
textes.Les gargouilles des ruines, au nord-oues: The gargoyles from the ruins, to the north-west, come and steal my fish from the quay. They drop out of the sky like stones, grab a sea bream and off they go. One took a whole grouper from me. The grouper was bigger than she was.
textes.Les gargouilles ne plongeront plus sur v: The gargoyles won't dive onto your sails anymore.
The gargoyles crumble to dust. The courtyard is yours… To the east, the library; to the west, the armoury; to the north, the keep, sealed.
textes.Les gargouilles, voilà mon souci. Elles: The gargoyles, that's my worry. They nest in the Ruins of the Old Pandemonium, on the north-west cliffs, and they dive at my ships: sails torn, fish stolen. Stone skin, bat wings. My harpoons bounce right off them.
textes.Les genoux grincent, mais le cœur bat à: The knees creak, but the heart beats at a hundred and forty-five.
textes.Les gens d'Aztlán vivent sur un lac, dan: The people of Aztlán live on a lake, in white houses, and grow gardens that float. Gardens that float! Here, it's the garden that drowns, when the flood comes.
textes.Les gens d'ici ? J'en connais quelques-u: The folks around here? I know a few. Which one interests you?
The folks around here? I know a few. Which one interests you?
textes.Les gens d'ici croient que nous sommes v: The people here think we came to plunder. We came to search. It's not the same thing. … Well, a little.
textes.Les gens d'ici ont leurs habitudes : le: People here have their habits: at work in the morning, elsewhere in the evening. If you can't find someone, come back at another time.
textes.Les gens d'ici sont charmants mais ils o: The people here are charming, but they've all got a little problem. Talk to them, you'll see. I'll give a reward to whoever helps out the whole town.
textes.Les gens des brumes viennent parfois sur: The mist people sometimes come onto the beach at night, without a sound. They leave shells on Fañch's boat. Nobody knows why.
textes.Les gens des brumes, à l'est, jouent à u: The mist people, to the east, play a game with white and black stones. My automaton wanted to learn. It lost. I never talk about it.
textes.Les gens des brumes, à l'est, pêchent da: The mist people, in the east, fish in the pools with baskets. They say their fish glow at night.
textes.Les gens qui se connaissent parlent les: People who know each other talk about each other. Listen closely: that's often where you learn the most.
textes.Les gigues ! Ha ! Toi, tu as des pieds q: Jigs! Ha! You've got feet that want to live! Come tonight, I'm playing the whalers' jig. Watch out for flying chairs.
textes.Les glands d'or ? Pomme-de-Pin en trouve: Golden acorns? Pomme-de-Pin finds one now and then, at the top of the oldest oaks. Owls adore them. For a golden acorn, I'd give… a moon feather, there.
textes.Les golems des hauteurs ont été taillés: The golems of the heights were carved by our ancestors to guard the Heart of the Mountain. Someone — or something — woke them. They no longer recognise anyone.
textes.Les golems des hauteurs… ce sont les anc: The golems of the heights… they're the mountain's ancient guardians. They woke when the volcano rumbled. Nori says someone woke them.
textes.Les golems descendent plus bas chaque nu: The golems come further down every night. I don't like it.
textes.Les graines lumineuses de Photon se sont: Photon's glowing seeds have flown off to the Zero-Gravity Garden: over there nothing falls back down, and they're floating right at the top. Photon's knees are too old to jump that high. They must be caught (three seeds) and brought back to him so you can plant them together.
textes.Les grands arbres de la jungle font de b: The big jungle trees make good masts. But to cut them, you have to cross spider territory. Nobody wants to go. Me neither.
textes.Les grands, au lac ?: The big ones, at the lake?
textes.Les hautes terres, c'est chez moi : la b: The highlands are home: the heather, the wind, the sheep, the snow in winter. It's harsh, but it's beautiful. And nobody ever blows anything up.
textes.Les histoires de Corentin changent chaqu: Corentin's stories change every night: a mapmaker's nightmare. But at the bottom of each one, there's a little piece of truth. I hunt for it with a pencil.
textes.Les humains ont des oreilles rondes. C'e: Humans have round ears. It's cute.
textes.Les humains vivent si peu de temps… Dis-: Humans live such a short time… Tell me: if you had three hundred years ahead of you, what would you do with them?
Your thoughts settle back into place.
textes.Les ingénieurs de Cliquetis ont regardé: The engineers from Cliquetis looked at my bridges. They wanted to replace them with metal ones. I asked them if metal could dance. They went home.
textes.Les ingénieurs de Cliquetis ont une gran: The engineers of Cliquetis have a big telescope, I hear. An astronomer over there, Céleste, writes to me. She says our moon is an illusion. I told her to come and see.
textes.Les inventées ! Ah, un rêveur. Tu sais,: Made-up ones! Ah, a dreamer. You know, a made-up story always ends up happening somewhere. You just have to wait. And then, it's happened twice.
textes.Les inventées ? Écoute. Un conteur inven: Made-up ones? Listen. A storyteller made up a djinn in a sardine. The next day, a fisherman opened a sardine, found nothing… and searched his whole life. The story had come true. You see?
textes.Les jaguars du Mont Fumant: The jaguars of the Smoking Mountain
textes.Les jaguars du volcan ne tueront plus de: The volcano's jaguars will kill no more turkeys.
textes.Les jaguars du volcan… je viens avec toi: The volcano jaguars… I'm coming with you.
textes.Les jaguars, il faut leur jeter des os,: You have to throw bones to the jaguars, like the Twins. Then they gnaw and forget to eat you!
textes.Les jardins d'algues sont derrière les m: The seaweed gardens are behind the houses, at the edge of the dome. They drink the crystal's light.
Young Moai don't know anything anymore.
textes.Les jeunes disent que Nono danse comme u: The youngsters say Nono dances like a seal. In my photos, he dances like a wave. You just have to look at him long enough, that's all.
textes.Les jeunes disent que je danse comme un: The young ones say I dance like a seal. A very elegant seal, I hope.
textes.Les jeunes mariés de l'hôtel se sont dis: The newlyweds at the hotel had a row on the beach. She was crying. He must have lost something…
textes.Les jeunes mariés de la chambre sept ne: The newlyweds in room seven haven't spoken since yesterday. The young lady is crying on the balcony.
textes.Les jours d'après, j'ai refusé la rose q: In the days after, I refused the rose Hugo had bought at Rose's. Doctor Roux made me herbal tea in the hotel garden. The gentleman with the moustache had tea sent up to me. Madame Dupuis passed me chocolate over the railing. And Pauline told the whole town everything. The eleventh day, that's what I call the day after: the one when you start again. Everyone has the right to an eleventh day.
On crisis days, I forget to eat. Gwenola always knows, I don't know how. At noon on the dot, a full crêpe appears in front of me, and Gwenola stands there, arms crossed. I tried giving her an order, once. She laughed. Then she waited for me to eat.
textes.Les jours de gros souci, l'Amirale oubli: On days of big worries, the Admiral forgets to eat. So at noon, I save her the back table, put a full crêpe in front of her and stand there, arms crossed. She sighs: “Gwenola, I don't have time.” I don't move. She eats. Every time.
textes.Les jours de pluie, je vais au Bazar écr: On rainy days, I go to the Bazaar to write the labels. “Useless”, on the propeller umbrella. “Useless”, on the silent whistle. “Very useless”, on the compass that points south. Madame Bricolette says nobody writes the word “useless” as beautifully as I do. It's a gift, apparently. I didn't know I had one.
textes.Les jours de pluie, quand mon bras gratt: On rainy days, when my arm itches, I find a little pot outside my door. Graphite ointment, with a label: “For the arm. É.” She never signs any other way. And she never drops it off when I'm in.
textes.Les lanternes de lune, sur les ponts, ce: The moon lanterns on the bridges are pool mushrooms that glow at night. Every spring, I put new ones out. This year, my old paws won't carry me to the water's edge any more.
textes.Les lapins de Ramure se lèvent avant le: The rabbits of Ramure get up before the sun. We light the oven, we knead, we taste. We taste a lot.
textes.Les lianes, ne t'y pends pas trop. Celle: The vines: don't hang off them too much. The one on the right dropped me three times. We're not speaking any more.
textes.Les loups veillent sur Ramure depuis que: The wolves have watched over Ramure ever since Mère-Lune arrived. She was a she-wolf too, and a tracker. The wolves followed her. We still follow her.
textes.Les loups, c'est l'endurance. On court l: Wolves are all about stamina. We run for ages. The Great Race is too short for a wolf, that's the problem. It ought to go round the whole island.
textes.Les lucioles d'Yggdrasil sont mes cousin: Yggdrasil's fireflies are my cousins. They know all the Tree's secrets.
textes.Les lucioles sont en avance, cette année: The fireflies are early this year.
textes.Les lunettes de soleil, la nuit… je dis: Sunglasses at night… I say it's style. Truth is, without them I'm shy. If you look a clown in the eyes, you see he's scared of not being funny. With the glasses, nobody sees a thing. You can see, {surnom}. But quickly, okay? There. Putting them back on.
textes.Les mains d'ombre reculent devant la Lue: The shadow hands recoil before the Moonglow and sink back under the flagstones!
textes.Les mannequins de paille de l'Aire des D: The straw dummies on the Duelling Ground, I've burned every one of them at least once. Not on purpose. Pyra says it's a record.
textes.Les marches de lumière tintent sous tes: The steps of light chime under your feet, one by one… A thousand steps, but they climb all by themselves. And here you are in the ruined tower, in broad daylight, the Royal jelly heart in your bag.
textes.Les marches sentent la pomme verte. Ce n: The steps smell of green apple. That's not a good sign.
textes.Les marches tremblent un peu. Tout en ba: The steps tremble a little. Way down at the bottom, a huge engine goes “vroom”. Politely.
textes.Les mares de la forêt sont reliées sous: The forest pools are connected underground, says Mère-Lune. A fish that dives here comes up over there. That's why the King of the Pools is everywhere and nowhere.
textes.Les mariés de la sept ont perdu leur all: The newlyweds in seven lost their wedding ring on the beach. She won't see him until he's found it.
textes.Les matins d'hiver, quand son savon gèle: On winter mornings, when his soap freezes, I bring Basile gear cookies. We dunk them in our coffee while we wait for the boiler to thaw. He blows on them to cool them, and a little bubble comes out every time. He doesn't do it on purpose. He just can't help it.
textes.Les meilleurs rêveurs. Lulu est comme to: The best dreamers. Lulu is like you: she dreams with her eyes open, while dancing. Her dreams rise all the way up here. Perhaps yours do too.
textes.Les miens aussi. Mais eux, c'est la flem: Mine too. But mine are just lazy.
Mummies are wrapped in linen. Hundreds of metres of it. Sometimes I think I'm weaving for people who aren't dead yet. It gives me the shivers.
textes.Les mouettes me volent une sardine sur d: The seagulls steal one sardine in ten from me. I count it as a tax.
textes.Les mouettes n'ont aucune oreille musica: Seagulls have no ear for music whatsoever.
textes.Les mouettes sont plus nombreuses cette: There are more seagulls this year. Or else Mustapha is grilling more sardines. Both, no doubt.
textes.Les mouettes volent les frites, ici. Gar: The seagulls steal the fries here. Guard your snack.
textes.Les moustiques ne dorment jamais. Les pr: Mosquitoes never sleep. Nor do priestesses.
textes.Les murs de la rue Haute sont fins. Le s: The walls on the Rue Haute are thin. In the evenings, I hear Lola writing: the pen, paper being crumpled, starting over. I've never said a thing. To anyone. A musician listens, he doesn't repeat. I just play a little softer when Lucas walks into the Perroquet. She asks me to stop. I don't.
textes.Les mâts se lèvent… les voiles se déplie: The masts rise… the sails unfold… PERFECT! You have fairy fingers! Here, this one's for you.
textes.Les nains de la Montagne de Feu ont de g: The dwarves of Fire Mountain have great forges. I went there when I was young. They found me too hairy. I found them too chatty.
textes.Les nains forgent mieux que moi. Je ne l: The dwarves forge better than me. I'll only say that once.
textes.Les nains m'ont demandé si je pouvais jo: The dwarves asked if I could play louder. Louder! They're miles away!
textes.Les nains n'aiment ni la magie, ni les e: Dwarves like neither magic, nor elves, nor water. But they do like gold, fizzy drinks and good stories. Tell them about Nâga. Exaggerate a little.
textes.Les nains sont bourrus, mais ce sont les: The dwarves are gruff, but they're the best blacksmiths in the world. Grommelot says that's not true. Grommelot is jealous.
textes.Les navires ont un problème, capitaine ?: Are the ships in trouble, captain?
textes.Les neuf couleurs sont revenues ! Toute: All nine colours are back! All of Sketched Island regains its colours at once, like a watercolour spreading…
textes.Les nouilles de Hiro… ou de Gaston. Peu: Hiro's noodles… or Gaston's. Doesn't matter: they're perfect.
textes.Les nouvelles runes de garde brillent su: The new warding runes shine on the gates. Thanks to you, the city sleeps better.
textes.Les nuits claires, on voit un château da: On clear nights you can see a castle in the sky, far to the south, above the ocean. A king should worry about that. I worry about it. Royally.
textes.Les nuits de pluie, mon encre de seiche: On rainy nights, my cuttlefish ink thickens. So I go and set my ten little pots on the warm stone, next to his forge. In the morning, I take them back, and I leave a pearl on the anvil, for rent. He never says anything. One day, I saw a little jar on his shelf: he keeps them all. There are about thirty.
textes.Les nuits de pluie, son encre de seiche: On rainy nights, her cuttlefish ink thickens in her tent. She comes and sets her pots by my forge so it stays runny. Ten little pots lined up on the warm stone. In the morning, she takes them back. She always leaves a pearl on the anvil. I say nothing. I keep it. I have thirty.
textes.Les nuits de tempête, {surnom}, je ne do: On stormy nights, {surnom}, I don't sleep. Abdelkader is somewhere at sea, on his coaster, and I listen to the wind in the shutters. Do you know why my Friday tajine matters so much to me? So there's always a dish waiting for him on the fire. Even when he's not here. Especially when he's not here.
textes.Les nuits où la reine ne dort pas, je m': On the nights the queen doesn't sleep, I settle beneath her windows with a lamp and an empty scroll. Sometimes her lamp goes out. Then I write, very precisely: “The queen's lamp went out.” I don't write that she slept: I don't know that. But I hope so, very hard. And hope can't be archived.
textes.Les offrandes du Grand Temple: The offerings of the Great Temple
The bears of Ramure are strong and slow. We forge, we carry, we don't run. Leave the racing to the rabbits.
textes.Les ouvriers de la pyramide, autrefois,: Long ago, the pyramid workers were paid in bread and beer. My family fed them. Without us, no pyramid!
textes.Les paniers de légumes des Jardins Parta: The vegetable baskets from the Shared Gardens haven't arrived at the Pay-What-You-Can Canteen. No vegetables, no soup, and no soup means half of the Boucan will go hungry tonight. Three baskets must be fetched from the Shared Gardens.
textes.Les pattes de Ramure sont rapides… Une r: Ramure's paws are quick… A rematch?
textes.Les perles pour ta robe de fête: The pearls for your party dress
textes.Les perles pour ta robe de fête…: The pearls for your party dress…
textes.Les perles… Vous aimez ce qui se cache l: Pearls… You like what stays hidden for a long time and grows slowly, layer after layer. Nobody chooses pearls by chance. I'll look at you differently now.
textes.Les petites ! (Il les prend dans ses mai: The little ones! (He takes them in cupped hands. All the flowers in the Gardens blink twice. Twice means thank you.) Come, let's plant them together. A hole made with a finger, a seed, a little soil, a little water... and a kind word. That's the most important part, the kind word. Say something to it. ... There. Did you see? It blinked. It heard you. Tomorrow morning, at sunrise, they'll sing. Off-key, surely. But with a great deal of heart.
textes.Les petits Moaïs, beaux joueurs, te donn: The little Moai, good sports, give you their treasure.
textes.Les pierres ? Elles ont dit quoi, les pi: The stones? And what did the stones say?
textes.Les pierres disent qu'hier l'était aussi: The stones say yesterday was too.
textes.Les pierres du Cercle attirent les éclat: The stones of the Circle attract moon shards, and I gather some there for my lessons. The first time, Ysolde appeared behind me without a sound. I dropped the shard, my glasses and a bit of my dignity. Now I say thank you out loud to each stone before gathering. Nine thank-yous. She nods at the ninth.
textes.Les pierres s'éteignent toutes d'un coup: All the stones go dark at once… That wasn't the right order. (The firefly pool can show you the song again.)
textes.Les pierres s'éteignent une à une. Les f: The stones go out one by one. Perhaps the corridor frescos tell the story in the right order…
textes.Les pierres. Bien. Ceux qui aiment les p: Stones. Good. People who like stones want to be told the truth, even when it cuts. I'll remember that: with you, I won't mince my words.
textes.Les pirates ? Ils sont amarrés à notre q: The pirates? They've been moored at our quay for three weeks. They pay for their water, their bread and their rum. As long as they pay, they're customers. The day they stop paying…
textes.Les pirates m'ont cassé trois cruches en: The pirates broke three of my jugs in a week. I charge them double. They know it, and they break them anyway.
textes.Les pirates m'ont demandé de réparer leu: The pirates asked me to repair their galleon. I told them: “I build boats, not mountains.”
The pirates eat here every lunchtime. They pay in gold coins from a kingdom nobody's heard of. I keep them: they're pretty.
textes.Les pirates me paient en pièces d'or d'u: The pirates pay me in gold coins from a kingdom nobody knows. I showed them to the amin, who knows every port in the archipelago. He turned them over and over, bit them. He didn't recognise the king on them. He said: “Keep them. They're pretty.” I keep them in a box, under the grill.
textes.Les pirates ont demandé le chemin de l'o: The pirates asked the way to the oasis. I pointed them the wrong way. The desert will send them back.
textes.Les pirates ont des canons. Nous, on a d: The pirates have cannons. We have nets. It doesn't worry me: nets catch more things.
textes.Les pirates viennent écouter, le soir. I: The pirates come to listen in the evening. They pretend to be passing by chance. Pirates love stories more than anyone: they're living one.
textes.Les pitons de pierre, je les escaladais,: I used to climb the stone peaks. Now I have a ladder, and creaky knees.
textes.Les pièces de Grelot, je les ai accroché: I hung Grelot's coins under the west bridge, on strings. When the wind blows, they jingle, ding, ding, so pretty! Bedaine walked underneath. He heard coins jingling. Under a bridge! In Ramure! He threw a fit, he said it was the end of swapping. Grelot laughed so hard she nearly fell over.
textes.Les plantes retombent, fanées. La Salle: The plants wilt and fall. The Hall of Seasons grows calm again… The stele, near the staircase, is waiting to be read.
textes.Les platines étaient trop hautes pour mo: The decks were too high for me, I was mixing on tiptoe. Gaspard took a rope, measured my arms while I played, without a word, and the next day there was a stage. Exactly the right height. It creaks on the offbeat. He swears it's on purpose.
textes.Les plumes d'ara rouges, dans la nuit, o: Red macaw feathers look like embers in the dark. The Twins used them to fool the Lords of Xibalba in the Dark House: they had to keep the torches lit all night without burning them. They put feathers in place of the fire!
textes.Les plumes du vent ? Le vent en perd qua: Wind feathers? The wind loses them when it turns too fast. They land where it blows hardest: on the heights, at the edge of the cliffs.
textes.Les plus beaux couchers de soleil, c'est: The best sunsets are from the jetty. The lighthouse lights up, the sea turns pink. I wrote a song about it. Well, I had.
textes.Les plus belles du lac, Xóchitl ! Grâce: The most beautiful on the lake, Xóchitl! Thanks to you!
The most golden. Your seagulls are waiting.
The fish in the bay thank you.
The fish are asleep. As they should be.
textes.Les portes de verre se ferment. L'ascens: The glass doors close. The elevator shoots up to the sky: 50 floors, 100, 150… you can feel your ears pop. Ding!
textes.Les portes vitrées coulissent dans un «: The glass doors slide open with a polite “pshhh”. The air of Port-Boucan smells of sea, soup and fresh paint. It feels good.
textes.Les potions de magie de Gustave, elles s: Gustave's magic potions are really good. When you've no strength left for your spells, one sip, and off you go again.
textes.Les pouvoirs des sceaux se rechargent 30: Seal powers recharge 30% faster. (You need at least one seal.)
textes.Les pâtes de Mamma… La sauce de la Marmi: Mamma's pasta… The sauce from the Cooking Pot… and the Golden Grater! It still shines! (The Reverend cooks the tagliatelle in the fountain on the square, coats them in sauce, grates a snow of parmesan over them, then sets it all on a big golden dish.) There. The Dish of the Great Reconciliation. It's not for me to offer it to him, my child: you're the one who gathered everything. Go and place it on the altar, next to the eternal plate. And smile. He likes it when people smile.
textes.Les pêcheurs et les pirates boivent sous: Fishermen and pirates drink under the same roof. They argue, then they sing together. That's how we make peace around here.
textes.Les pêcheurs m'apprennent à pêcher. C'es: The fishermen are teaching me to fish. Can you believe it, on the Murène nobody knows how. We eat biscuits as hard as wood.
textes.Les quarante couplets, Barnabé. Le héros: All forty verses, Barnabé. In it, the hero is ten feet tall.
textes.Les quatre cloches chantent ensemble ! L: All four bells sing together! The Song of the Sky Kings rolls across the whole island… At the centre of the belfry, a slab opens and a chest rises up.
textes.Les quatre cristaux brillent ensemble !: All four crystals shine together! The Heart seal spins on itself with a long rumble, and a column of red light rises from the floor where it was sealed. (E, in the centre: descend into the Hall of the Heart)
textes.Les quatre flammes rugissent ensemble !: All four flames roar together! With a rumble, the stone door sinks into the floor.
textes.Les quatre fleurs s'ouvrent ensemble : l: The four flowers open together: spring in the east, summer in the south, autumn in the west, winter in the north. A scent of every season at once fills the hall… The roots of the last staircase draw back. At the very top, the Crown.
textes.Les quatre livres envolés de Théophraste: Théophraste's four flown-away books: I know where they are. But I don't know how to get them down. You need telekinesis. I'm not there yet.
textes.Les quatre passerelles de corde, toutes: All four rope bridges crossed! They creak a little, but they hold fast.
textes.Les quatre runes sont brisées ! Le Gardi: All four runes are shattered! The Guardian falls to his knees… his chest opens: the fire heart is exposed. Strike it!
textes.Les quatre sceaux ? Tu veux… vraiment ?: The four seals? You want to… really? Ha! I knew you were one of those who finish their maps! Listen: nobody here knows where they are. But Old Corentin knows all the old stories of Carène. Go and see him: on the bridge by the bell during the day, at La Dernière Bordée in the evening. Me, I'm keeping a nice clean corner of the map for Stoneheart.
textes.Les quatre sceaux s'allument ensemble. L: The four seals light up together. The great circle blazes… The mountain rumbles, far away, very deep, like a heart waking up. Then, in a crash of stone, the Gate of the Four Seals sinks into the ground.
textes.Les quatre sceaux… Assieds-toi, petit. I: The four seals… Sit down, lad. Two hundred years ago the mountain woke up: the Stoneheart beat so hard that the sea trembled all the way here. The four peoples went down beneath the mountain and put to sleep whatever was beating down there. Then they shut the door, and each one went home with a seal. Ours, the Seal of Sea Spray, was hidden somewhere aboard by the Leviathan's last captain. Where? He wrote it in his logbook… which my grandfather sold, one winter of famine, to a storyteller from Tazira. Ba Sidi, he was called. He must be very old by now, if he's still alive.
textes.Les quatre serpents fixent l'autel. Leur: The four serpents stare at the altar. Their eyes blaze… and the lid slides open with a rumble!
textes.Les quatre temps de silence ? Ce soir, p: The four beats of silence? Tonight, I promise, my friend.
textes.Les racines ne bougent pas. Les quatre f: The roots don't move. The four stone flowers are not yet in the order the stele asks for.
textes.Les renards ont le meilleur nez de Ramur: Foxes have the best noses in Ramure. Mine can tell three hundred herbs apart. And every one of Trèfle's pies, from a hundred paces.
textes.Les robots ! Ha ! Alors vous préférez Bo: Robots! Ha! So you prefer Boulon. That's the right answer, and he knows it: look, he's sitting up and begging. He only does that for good people.
textes.Les robots de la cour de l'usine: The robots of the factory yard
textes.Les robots déménageurs de Monsieur Lisse: Mr Lisse's mover robots stole the Bilge Rats' gear just before the Great Boucan, the biggest concert of the year: Germaine the Terrible (Clou's guitar), the tube amp and the drumsticks. You need to find everything, give the guitar and the amp back to Rouille, then come to the Great Boucan, in the evening, at the Howling Hall.
textes.Les robots repartent vers l'Usine Grise,: The robots head back to the Grey Factory in single file, apologising as they go. The Boucan applauds! The furniture stays right where it was.
textes.Les ronces au nord du jardin… c'est le d: The brambles to the north of the garden… that's the domain of the Bramble Queen. We'll need five pinches of fairy dust to get through.
textes.Les ronces s'effondrent… Le bois de la C: The brambles collapse… The wood of the Crown trembles. In the middle, something enormous pushes through the bark!
textes.Les ronces se fanent, les roses refleuri: The brambles wither, the roses bloom again. Before you floats an immense fairy, gentle and luminous: Églantine, the true Fairy Queen. Speak to her.
textes.Les ronces se referment derrière toi. Su: The brambles close behind you. On the throne, a figure rises… THE BRAMBLE QUEEN spreads her black wings!
textes.Les rondes ! On voit toute la cité, on c: The rounds! You see the whole city, you know every cobblestone, and you come home with sore feet. It's the best post. I always keep it for myself.
textes.Les roses de lumière brûlent la Reine !: The roses of light burn the Queen! Her shield shatters, she falls: STRIKE!
textes.Les rouleaux disent oui. Demande quand m: The scrolls say yes. Ask the traveller anyway.
textes.Les runes de garde de la cité s'effacent: The city's warding runes are fading. I need obsidian to carve new ones: {manque} shards. You'll find it near the crater, where the lava cooled into black glass. Watch out for the elementals.
textes.Les runes du Cercle s'allument une à une: The runes of the Circle light up one by one… The nine Moonstones sing. You are a wizard of Arcanelle!
The runes don't tell everything, {surnom}. You… do you believe the future is already written?
textes.Les runes parlent d'un grand venu de la: The runes speak of a tall one from the sea, who will defeat fire with fire. I'm not saying it's you. I'm not saying it isn't.
textes.Les runes t'attendaient, le grand…: The runes were expecting you, big one…
textes.Les récifs et la cendre nous cachent. Ce: The reefs and the ash hide us. Those without the map go round in circles and leave. That's how we like it.
textes.Les réponses, alors. La porte dit : « Vo: The answers, then. The gate says: “You who enter here, keep hope (and bring a coat)”. The ferryman of the Acheron is called Charon, and he asks for an obol. Limbo is lit by the light of the sages, bounced between the mirrors. And there are nine circles. Got all that?
textes.Les salamandres de feu dorment sur les p: The fire salamanders sleep on the hot stones. Don't touch them: they don't bite, but they burn.
textes.Les scorpions ne bougent plus. Le tombea: The scorpions stop moving. The tomb falls silent again… On the back wall, a great fresco.
textes.Les seaux sont près de la porte. Place-l: The buckets are by the door. Place them under the three drips.
textes.Les sept Grandes Lanternes brillent sur: The seven Great Lanterns shine over the city… but Lumina shakes her head: “No Night of Lanterns without Zigomar's rockets! I think he's missing his sulphur crystals.”
textes.Les soirs de brouillard, je garde la lan: On foggy evenings, I keep the lantern lit until Fañch's boat is home. He knows. He's never said thank you. Once, he left a lobster outside my door, without a word. I pretended to believe the sea had brought it.
textes.Les soirs de brume, je fais un plus gros: On misty evenings, I build a bigger fire, so my smoke can be seen clearly from his kapok tree. Why? So he knows I'm still here. It must annoy him tremendously. That's reason enough.
textes.Les soirs de pluie, Silas s'installe dan: On rainy evenings, Silas settles into the corner of the Shark's Tooth and tells how the ghosts of a crew still play here at night, and always lose. The gamblers shiver and bet smaller. It costs me money. But when I close, at four, I always leave three dice on the table. Just in case.
textes.Les soirs où je dors pas, Anouk me donne: On nights I can't sleep, Anouk gives me the captains' hot honey, in a mug. It's the best hot honey in the world, it smells of honey and a little bit of moon. Lucie says it's just herbal tea. Lucie talks nonsense sometimes.
textes.Les soirs où le Zéphyr arrive plein, Sal: On evenings when the Zéphyr comes in full, Salomé rents out seaweed sacks in the hold, “for a cool night's sleep”. She's stealing my customers. With seaweed. That's a declaration of war.
textes.Les spaghettis qui restent ne sont pas e: The spaghetti that's left isn't dry yet. It takes patience (and sunshine).
textes.Les spectres se défont en lambeaux de br: The specters fall apart into shreds of mist. The big pond grows calm again… The old sluice gate closes gently: the water rises back.
textes.Les squelettes du cimetière sortent quan: The skeletons in the graveyard come out when the moon rises. Don't hang about there after sunset.
textes.Les squelettes du fort ? Les hommes de B: The skeletons in the fort? Barbe-Sanglante's men. They still guard the fort, as they were ordered a hundred years ago. Loyal soldiers. And very skinny.
textes.Les surprises en couleur, alors ! Celles: Colourful surprises, then! The ones that come down gently. The other kind, the scary surprises, we can leave to the professor.
textes.Les tanukis troquent depuis toujours. Mo: Tanukis have always swapped. My grandfather swapped a leaf for a house. He made everyone believe the leaf was magic. It wasn't. The house was, though: it's still standing.
textes.Les tapis viennent des femmes du désert,: The carpets come from the women of the desert, from the oasis tribes. They weave the dunes, the stars, the caravan routes. Some say an ancient carpet shows the way to the lost seal.
textes.Les toilettes ? Au fond à gauche. … NON: The bathroom? At the back on the left. … NO! Not at all! OUT!
textes.Les touristes achètent des colliers de c: Tourists buy shell necklaces. Locals buy wedding rings. I sell memories to some and promises to others.
textes.Les trois ! (Philémon les étale, les tou: All three! (Philémon spreads them out, turns them, flips them, and sews them back together with silk thread.) Look: the Peak, the Balafre… and there, at the end, a skull, and a red cross. Skull Rock! But read the margin: “My second keeps watch.” Captain Fleshless… Beware, young man.
textes.Les trois ! Et pas une seule cornée. (El: All three! And not a single dog-ear. (She gives you a little curtsy, with just one wing.) If you ever want a job, the post office is hiring. Even without wings.
textes.Les trois ! Respect, champion. Je les re: All three! Respect, champ. I'll put them back in the water, they're better off down there. And you, your lungs have grown, I can tell.
textes.Les trois Perles s'élèvent toutes seules: The three Pearls rise by themselves toward the tower… and the Great Crystal blazes! A blue light floods the city, the dome begins to sing. Atlantis is saved!
textes.Les trois Perles… Les trois âges de la m: The three Pearls… The three ages of the sea, together again! Look at the Great Crystal, {surnom}, look! … Take this trident: the trident of the kings of Atlantis. And these three gold coins, struck before the flood.
textes.Les trois affiches ont voyagé, Agrafe !: The three posters have travelled, Agrafe!
textes.Les trois autres sont de sortie, je te d: The other three are out, I'm telling you.
textes.Les trois fragments de jade, soudés auto: The three jade fragments, joined around a green eye. Underground, it lights up the darkness around you. It hums near the seal of the Abyss.
textes.Les trois morceaux recousus au fil de so: The three pieces sewn back together with silk thread by Philémon Lunette: One-Eye Peak, the Balafre, and at the end of the ravine a skull marked with a red cross. In the margin, in shaky handwriting: "My first mate keeps watch."
textes.Les trois pains sont livrés, Honorine !: All three loaves are delivered, Honorine!
textes.Les trois rayons frappent Nâga ! Sa tête: The three beams strike Nâga! His head crashes onto the platform: STRIKE!
textes.Les trois runes ! « Fiat lux » : « que l: The three runes! “Fiat lux”: “let there be light.” It's the motto of the Academy, and from now on it's a little bit yours. Keep these coins. And come back and watch the stars with me one night: it's even more beautiful with someone who can make light.
textes.Les trois runes de la crypte brillent !: The three runes in the crypt are shining!
textes.Les trois runes de la crypte brillent d': The three runes of the crypt shine gold: “Fiat lux”. Aurélien Lumen will want to know.
textes.Les trois soleils se lèvent ensemble ! R: The three suns rise together! Ra, Kinich Ahau and Tonatiuh greet you: you are the Child of the Three Suns.
textes.Les tuyaux qui s'allument en bleu sont d: The pipes lit up in blue are already connected to the battery. Start from the battery, on the left, and go one tile at a time.
textes.Les témoins, dans l'affaire des croissan: The witnesses in the croissant case: the baker, her daughter Nina, and Bruno the ice-cream man, who closes late. Question them for me.
textes.Les têtes de la Carrière regardent l'hor: The Quarry heads look at the horizon, or at their feet… All of them? No: a little lower down, one of them has its nose in the air, watching the clouds go by.
The waves… They play better than I do. Always in rhythm, never tired. Wait: a minor chord, very soft. That's the sea.
textes.Les vieilles blagues, c'est comme le lev: Old jokes are like sourdough: they keep!
textes.Les vieilles bottes, je les rachète. Pou: Old boots, I buy them back. Why? For nothing. That's the house rule.
textes.Les vols sont gratuits : les ingénieurs: Flights are free: the engineers pay for everyone. Since this spring, there's a stop at Ramure, on the landing ground north of the village, with Plumette's mail. I had to turn Achille down. Adèle waits on my bench, Rosette lies in wait for my mailbags. And I still go aboard, by day, as a passenger. With a cushion. Don't laugh.
textes.Les voyageurs du Zéphyr me rapportent qu: Travellers on the Zéphyr tell me he tells the wreck of the Léviathan swaying, like a ship. I tried it one evening, on my stone. I got seasick, and so did the front row. He has a thousand, I have a thousand and one. But that one, I'll leave to him.
textes.Les vraies ! Bon choix. Mais attention :: True ones! Good choice. But careful: a true story is a story that happened once. The best ones happened twice.
textes.Les vraies ? Écoute. Un pêcheur jurait n: True ones? Listen. A fisherman swore he only liked true ones. One evening, he really did catch a talking sardine. Nobody believed him. So he said he'd made it up, and everybody believed him. You see?
textes.Les vrais Seigneurs ont crié, et les aut: The real Lords cried out, and the others called them by name! Two of them didn't flinch: wooden dummies.
textes.Les xolos guident les morts dans le Mict: Xolos guide the dead into Mictlan, the world below. Tlaco will guide me, later on. But not now: he can't even find the way home.
textes.Les yeux de pierre brillent. « Tiens. Je: The stone eyes shine. “Here. I found it in my dream. It's for you.”
textes.Les yeux de tes amis, m'avais-tu dit. J': Your friends' eyes, you told me. I've thought about it. Ulfa's eyes shine when she's robbing me. It's a start.
textes.Les yeux fermés ? Montre ! … Hé ! Pas ma: With your eyes closed? Show me! … Hey! Not bad. The rabbit comes out of the hole, goes round the tree, goes back down the hole. My father would be pleased.
textes.Les éclats de cristal… Quand le feu pass: Crystal shards… When the fire shines through them, they make colours. Red, blue, gold. Like the northern gardens, before the brambles. In the evening I sit in front of them and watch. I've never said this. They're pretty. There. I've said it. If you repeat it, I'll say you're lying. Hmph.
textes.Les éclats de lune ? Des morceaux de lum: Moon shards? Bits of light that fall on the island on clear nights. They stay where they fall, and glow softly.
textes.Les éclats de lune tombent souvent près: Moon shards often fall near the Circle. The stones attract them. Or the shards like the stones. Nobody knows who started it.
textes.Les écouter ?! Oh, toi, tu as tout compr: Listen to them?! Oh, you've understood everything. It's the sea talking inside. My father used to say that. Nobody here believes me. Except you, now.
textes.Les élèves m'appellent l'hippopotame. Il: The pupils call me the hippopotamus. They think I don't know. I slipped into a lesson the story of Taweret, the hippopotamus goddess who protects children. The next day, I heard Nebet whisper: “Now we say Taweret.” Taweret is a lady. But she's a goddess. I pretended not to hear a thing.
textes.Les épices ! Ah, un nez, enfin ! Un vrai: The spices! Ah, a nose, at last! A real one! Come, smell this one and tell me. … Cinnamon? Bravo! You'll be back, you will, I can smell it.
textes.Les épices de Lalla Aïcha… Ho ho. Si un: Lalla Aïcha's spices… Ho ho. If I ever retire, it'll be here. A little eatery on the quay, and all the cumin I want.
textes.Les étoiles : on les compte ou on les re: The stars: do you count them or watch them?
textes.Les étoiles ? Je ne les ai pas encore ga: The stars? I haven't won those yet.
textes.Les étoiles… Celles-là, personne ne les: The stars… Nobody pierced those. I've been looking at them for sixty years, and I can't find the hole the light comes through.
textes.Les étoiles… Les lanternes de quelqu'un: The stars… Someone else's lanterns, very far away. One day, I'll make lanterns that rise so high people will mistake them for stars.
textes.Lestrange ? Un bon marin, un mauvais per: Lestrange? A good sailor, a bad loser and a very bad payer. His brig is fast. Mine is faster. It makes him sick, and it makes me feel better.
textes.Lettres, colis, télégrammes, et beaucoup: Letters, parcels, telegrams, and a lot of chatter. Victor crying unfair competition while buying a stamp from me. Professor Moreau trembling in front of his university letters. Lola's letters “To L.”, which I slip into Lucas's letterbox, whistling. And my cards for Barnabé, Lyra, Ulfa and the queen under the sea. If she exists.
textes.Lever les yeux vers le Grand Spaghetti V: Look up at the Great Flying Spaghetti
textes.Levée à quatre heures, comme tous les jo: Up at four, same as every day. But when people smile biting into my bread, I go back to bed happy.
textes.Levée à quatre heures. Fanny, mon appren: Up at four. Fanny, my apprentice, comes straight from the beach party with sand in her hair and kneads while dancing. Raymond delivers the bread, at the moment with a sprained ankle. Paulo tells everyone I steal his croissants. The Lord takes six. Croissants went missing in the night, and the sergeant investigated, a croissant in his hand. And in the dough, a drop of elven honey. Shh.
textes.Le… le poisson-lune doré ? Pour moi ? Je: The… the golden sunfish? For me? I… I don't know what to say. Neither does Gaston. That's a first.
textes.Le… le poisson-lune doré. Ma parole. {pr: The… the golden sunfish. Well I never. {prix} coins, and that's a bargain for you. Clou, close your mouth.
textes.Lhoucine dort le jour. Rien ne le réveil: Lhoucine sleeps by day. Nothing wakes him: not the auction, not the gulls, not Saïd. Nothing, except me. I knock on his door, in rhythm: boom, ta-ka, boom. On the third boom, he opens. He says his body gets up on its own so as not to miss the beat. For one minute, he hates me.
textes.Lhoucine joue bien. Trop bien. Une nuit,: Lhoucine plays well. Too well. One night, he played until sunrise, and the fleet came home empty. Since then, the music stops at midnight. He obeys. More or less.
textes.Lhoucine joue derrière moi, le matin. Qu: Lhoucine plays behind me, in the morning. When the tale reaches the desert, he strikes a low note, and the whole circle gets thirsty. The music takes the pauses for me. All I have to do is breathe.
textes.Lhoucine m'a composé un air, rien que po: Lhoucine composed a tune just for me: the whale dance. Nobody had ever given me a gift like that. Not even a captain.
textes.Lhoucine tient la basse, et il tient la: Lhoucine holds the bass line, and he holds the party together. He says I sing too loud. I say he plays too softly. We're both right.
textes.Lhoucine, c'est la vague, et moi le pas: Lhoucine is the wave, and I'm the camel's step. We've played together since we could hold a spoon. By day, he sleeps. By night, he lives. Me, I do both.
textes.Lila ! Je t'ai rapporté un bâton lumineu: Lila! I brought you back a glow stick. Just the one.
textes.Lila a photographié ma danse, l'appareil: Lila photographed my dancing, with the shutter open for a whole track. In the photo, my orange beanie makes a big curve, like a rolling wave. I folded it in four and I keep it in my beanie. When some youngster tells me I dance like a seal, I take it out. He goes quiet.
textes.Lila attrape la lumière avec sa boîte ma: Lila catches light with her magic box. In her photos, you can see what you can't see with the naked eye. She photographed my fairy pollen. Bastien says it's a fault. Bastien says a lot of things.
textes.Lila est la seule à voir que je danse co: Lila's the only one who sees that I dance like a wave. The others see a seal. She has an artist's eyes and a grandmother's patience. At her age!
textes.Lila fait des photos magiques. Sur toute: Lila takes magical photos. In every one of mine, I'm a pink ghost with sunglasses. She says it's my fault. I say it's my style.
textes.Lila m'a demandé de rester immobile une: Lila asked me to stay still for just one second for a photo. I made an enormous effort, held my breath, closed my eyes behind my sunglasses… and sneezed. She sighed so hard the photo moved too. I had it framed. It's my favourite portrait.
textes.Lila m'a prêté toutes ses photos de la t: Lila lent me all her party photos for the mural. I spread them out on the sand for a whole night, by the light of a mushroom. There was Grandpa as a wave, Titou as a ghost, Yaya as a moon. It was so beautiful I was afraid of spoiling it by painting it. In the morning, I gave her photos back, neatly sorted.
textes.Lila, c'est ma sœur, ma voisine depuis t: Lila is my sister, my next-door neighbour forever and my only audience when I was ten. She even proved that the cat dances. She's always right, it's annoying.
textes.Lila, ma belle, tu veux ma vague, ce soi: Lila, my dear, want my wave tonight?
textes.Lila, ta photo du chat, je l'ai encore r: Lila, I looked at your photo of the cat again last night.
textes.Lila, tu as photographié la lune, ce soi: Lila, did you photograph the moon tonight?
textes.Lilas danse comme une feuille qui aurait: Lilas dances like a leaf that's decided never to fall. She comes to me for advice. I tell her nonsense, and then one real piece of advice, at the end. She always waits for the end.
textes.Lilas danse comme une plume qui tombe. E: Lilas dances like a falling feather. Every evening she asks me to play softer. I promise, and then the moon rises out of the pond, and… boom. She's very patient with me.
textes.Lilas danse la louve qui a sauvé la lune: Lilas dances the she-wolf who saved the moon better than the she-wolf herself, I'm sure of it. When she dances, I'm eighteen again. It doesn't last, but it's good.
textes.Lilas, c'est ma meilleure amie et la plu: Lilas is my best friend and the most beautiful dancer in the forest. She blushes at the slightest thing. Especially at a certain “hrmm”. Just saying.
textes.Lilas. Hrmm. Elle danse. Je tape. C'est: Lilas. Hrmm. She dances. I drum. That's all. … She dances well. Very well. Hrmm. That's all.
textes.Lili Pinceau, la fille de Basile (neuf a: Lili Pinceau, Basile's daughter (nine and a half), saw the pot of yellow (no. 4) roll along the beach to the big sandcastle at the far end of the shore, to the west. But the tide has covered everything, and she can't remember where the castle door is.
textes.Lili, j'ai trouvé le jaune ! Il était au: Lili, I found the yellow! It was at the foot of the tower.
textes.Lin ! T'es toujours là ? Pas dans le liv: Lin! You're still here? Not inside the book?
textes.Lin lit plus vite que moi. Je l'ai chron: Lin reads faster than I do. I timed her. I haven't told anyone. Except you. Don't repeat it.
textes.Lin lit tellement qu'un jour, elle va re: Lin reads so much that one day she'll walk into a book and we'll never see her again. I told her. She smiled.
textes.Lin lit tout le temps, même en marchant,: Lin reads all the time, even while walking, even while eating her soup. I keep an eye on her, in case a book swallows her. She's my best friend, even if she doesn't talk much. She listens really well.
textes.Lin vient lire au pied des pierres. Elle: Lin comes to read at the foot of the stones. She reads them stories in a low voice. I think the stones like it.
textes.Lin écoute avant de parler, et elle parl: Lin listens before she speaks, and she speaks softly. That's rare in the young. The stones like her. So do I. I'm teaching her their names, one by one.
Lin. Nacre was waiting for you.
textes.Lirael ! Une planche gémit, vers l'est ?: Lirael! Is a plank moaning, over to the east?
textes.Lirael veille la nuit, je pêche à l'aube: Lirael keeps watch at night, I fish at dawn. We pass each other at daybreak: she goes to bed, I go to work. Three centuries of saying good morning and good night at the same time.
textes.Lirael veille les lanternes pendant que: Lirael watches over the lanterns while I watch over a window. At that hour, we're the only two awake in the Bois-Doré. She dims the light when I play. She's a friend.
Lirael lives on the platform next door. She hangs her lanterns on my railings and warns me when a plank moans in the dark. The best neighbour in the sky.
textes.Lirael. Tu baisses la lanterne bleue, ce: Lirael. Will you dim the blue lantern tonight?
textes.Lire la dernière rune, tout au fond, prè: To read the last rune, at the very bottom, near the Heart of the Mountain. Nobody has read it for a thousand years. I'll have to go down there before my fingers forget.
textes.Lire les pages blanches du journal de bo: Read the blank pages of the logbook by Moonglow (key 4 then X; in VR, B), with the logbook in your bag
textes.Lire mes romans d'amour en terrasse, au: To read my romance novels on a café terrace, in the sun, with no newspaper in front. Let everyone see the cover. And let me finish the chapter.
Read every book in the library. All three thousand. Even the ones that flew away. Especially those, maybe.
Read. Not summon. Not make things fly.
textes.Lis-moi la rune du nord, Ori. Pour t'ent: Read me the north rune, Ori. For practice.
Lise left us one winter, from a fever. Margot was two. For a year, I didn't blow a single bubble. And then one morning, Margot, aged three, found my old straw in a drawer. She blew into the dishwater, and she laughed. I started the machine that very day. For her. So that there would always be bubbles in this house.
textes.Lisez votre journal. Il le dit tous les: Read your paper. It says it every morning.
textes.Lisse & Fils vous remercie de votre coop: Lisse & Fils thanks you for your cooperation.
textes.Livraison pour… erreur. Livraison pour p: Delivery for… error. Delivery for nobody. Bzz.
textes.Livrer enfin ma lettre à Nessa. Peut-êtr: To finally deliver my letter to Nessa. Maybe at the next Dawn festival, between two dances. And not to tread on her feet this time. Or not more than ten times, anyway.
textes.Livrer le pain à Edmond (Grand Hôtel): Deliver the bread to Edmond (Grand Hotel)
textes.Livrer le pain à Gisèle (Café de la Plac: Deliver the bread to Gisèle (the Square Café)
textes.Livrer le pain à Paulo (Chez Paulo, sur: Deliver the bread to Paulo (Chez Paulo, on the quay)
Logical. I'll start with the east.
textes.Logique. Les chiffres, on ne les perd pa: Logical. You don't lose numbers. Letters, you do: Rosette's press misses one in a hundred. You can help me count Dad's bubbles one day.
textes.Loin, loin ? Plus loin que les nains ? I: Far far? Further than the dwarves? Are there seeds there? Will you bring me one next time? Just one! Two!
textes.Lola, c'est ma serveuse, et presque ma n: Lola is my waitress, and almost my niece. She carries four glasses in each hand and writes the chalkboard better than a poet. She has a soft spot for a docker. I'm not saying anything. Well, maybe a little.
textes.Lola, c'est ma voisine, ma serveuse préf: Lola is my neighbour, my favourite waitress and my glass of water between songs. She deserves to have waltzes played for her.
textes.Lola, du Perroquet, envoie une lettre ch: Lola, from the Perroquet, sends a letter every week to a certain “L.”. It's none of my business. But it's Lucas, isn't it?
textes.Lola, la serveuse du Perroquet. Elle pos: Lola, the Perroquet's waitress. She posts a letter every Friday, hiding behind the pillar. I know nothing. I'm a tomb. A smiling tomb.
textes.Lola, la serveuse du Perroquet… elle est: Lola, the waitress at the Perroquet… she's nice, isn't she? … Nothing. Forget it.
textes.Lola, la table du fond. Et le grand du q: Lola, the table at the back. And look, the big fellow from the quay just came in.
textes.Lola, ma petite passagère. Elle est mont: Lola, my little passenger. She came aboard for the day, five years ago. The day isn't over yet. I'm keeping her return ticket, just in case.
Lola… She writes the menu on the slate. She has lovely handwriting. She's nice, isn't she? … Nothing. I'm not saying anything.
textes.Long-Cou ? Long-Cou gentil ! Long-Cou ma: Long-Neck? Long-Neck nice! Long-Neck eat trees. Long-Neck never mean. But watch his feet: very big feet.
textes.Longue-vue : clic droit (ou stick droit): Spyglass: right click (or right stick) to look around; L to put it away.
textes.Longues comme le canal, Thalassa ! Et un: Long as the canal, Thalassa! And a cracker with it?
textes.Lord Pemberton paierait cher une vraie c: Lord Pemberton would pay a lot for a real curiosity: a feather from the giant eagle, a naga scale, or a shark tooth.
textes.Lord Pemberton, chambre douze. Le client: Lord Pemberton, room twelve. The nicest guest in the hotel, and the most cluttered. Before you can touch the bed, you have to dust a dragon's tooth, eleven snow globes and a porcelain egg.
textes.Lord Pemberton, mon client le plus fidèl: Lord Pemberton, my most faithful and most distinguished customer. He owns four thousand objects, and his favourite comes from my shop. From mine! I can't get over it. I don't want to get over it.
textes.Lourde et bien équilibrée. Elle abat les: Heavy and well balanced. It fells young trees (a pale notch on the trunk) and coconut palms: logs, coconuts, honey… Damage: 5.
textes.Lucas ! Chut, pour Brioche. Il dort dans: Lucas! Shh, for Brioche. He's sleeping in the crate.
textes.Lucas ? Un docker. Grand. Il joue aux ca: Lucas? A docker. Tall. He plays cards, he loses. That's it. That's all I have to say. … He's nice, isn't he?
textes.Lucas a encore perdu aux cartes. Il est: Lucas lost at cards again. He's cute when he loses.
textes.Lucas est le plus honnête docker que j'a: Lucas is the most honest docker I've ever seen. He steals nothing, he breaks almost nothing, and he talks to crates. I pretend not to know. It makes him happy.
textes.Lucas, c'est mon adversaire aux cartes,: Lucas is my card opponent, every evening. I always win. Not because I'm good: because he looks at the waitress instead of his cards. I'm not going to complain.
textes.Lucas, il est grand comme une porte et i: Lucas is as tall as a door and he talks to crates. He keeps all my secrets. And he's the only one who believes in my dolphin, because he saw it too.
textes.Lucas, le docker, parle aux caisses quan: Lucas, the docker, talks to the crates when he thinks nobody can hear.
textes.Lucas, le grand docker. Solide comme une: Lucas, the big tall docker. Solid as a crate, and red as a tomato the moment he sees my satchel. It's very sweet. I say nothing. Almost nothing.
textes.Lucie ! Aujourd'hui, je compte avec des: Lucie! Today I'm counting with pebbles, one at a time!
textes.Lucie ! J'ai fait tomber ma pipe au bout: Lucie! I dropped my tin whistle off the end of the pontoon.
textes.Lucie ! J'ai une théorie sur tes cercles: Lucie! I've got a theory about your circles, they could be…
textes.Lucie ! Une perle aujourd'hui ? Je te fa: Lucie! A pearl today? I'll give you a good price.
textes.Lucie a trouvé des pierres taillées au f: Lucie found carved stones at the bottom of the bay. Carved! Someone lived here before us.
textes.Lucie et moi, on se connaît depuis qu'on: Lucie and I have known each other since we could walk. Well, her, since she could swim. She doesn't talk much. With her, I don't need to talk either.
textes.Lucie fait le tour de la coque par en de: Lucie goes round the hull from underneath and tells me where it's seeping. She's never wrong, and she never talks for nothing. If all of Carène were like her, I'd have fewer headaches.
textes.Lucie m'a apporté une perle presque rose: Lucie brought me an almost pink pearl, with a little spot. I paid her the price of a spotted pearl. That evening I sold it for triple to a caravan trader, as a “pearl of the Figurehead Lady”. The next day, Lucie walked past the stall, read the label, and just said: “Have a nice day, Salomé.” I didn't sleep a wink.
textes.Lucie m'a appris à faire la planche dans: Lucie taught me to float on my back in the basin. She told me: “Look at the sky and forget you have a back.” I forgot my back, I floated, and then a seagull gave me a funny look. I burst out laughing and sank. Lucie laughed too. Lucie laughing is rare. It was worth the mouthful of salt water.
textes.Lucie me rapporte les meilleures algues: Lucie brings me the best seaweed in the bay, from the bottom, the kind you never find at low tide. She doesn't talk much and she listens well. Around here, both are rare.
textes.Lucie me rapporte les plus belles perles: Lucie brings me the finest pearls on the island and never haggles. She looks at me with her big calm eyes, and I get the feeling I'm the one being swindled. It's very unpleasant.
textes.Lucie peut rester sous l'eau plus longte: Lucie can stay underwater longer than a seal. I timed her. Well, I counted. Up to a hundred, then I got mixed up.
textes.Lucie plonge sous la coque. Elle dit qu': Lucie dives under the hull. She says there are things carved on the keel, underneath. Things nobody wrote.
textes.Lucie voit sous l'eau ce que personne ne: Lucie sees things underwater that nobody else sees: carved stones! She talks little, and when she does, I forget what I was going to say. For me, that's very rare.
textes.Lucie, c'est la meilleure plongeuse de l: Lucie is the best diver on the island. She stays underwater longer than a seal, I counted. She doesn't talk much, but when she does, it's to say incredible stuff.
textes.Lucie, je l'ai connue grosse comme une s: I've known Lucie since she was the size of a sardine, clinging to her mother's neck in the bay. She fishes out everything I drop. And I drop everything.
textes.Lucie. Alors, ça suinte où, aujourd'hui: Lucie. So, where's it seeping today?
textes.Lucie. Tu as cinq minutes ?: Lucie. Have you got five minutes?
textes.Lui, il a de l'humour !: Now he's got a sense of humor!
textes.Lulu ! Il souffle d'où, le vent, ce soir: Lulu! Where's the wind blowing from tonight?
textes.Lulu ? La seule humaine dont j'entende l: Lulu? The only human whose dreams I can hear from up here. They go boom-boom. I entrusted her with our glowing mushrooms: she knows who deserves to come up.
textes.Lulu a des champignons qui emmènent au p: Lulu has mushrooms that take you to fairyland. I ask her every day, nicely, very nicely. She always answers: “Soon.” Soon takes a long time.
textes.Lulu a promis de peindre le mur de son i: Lulu promised to paint the wall of sound two years ago. The wall is still white, and it's my favourite mural. She sees things I can't hear.
textes.Lulu dit que les enceintes ont des senti: Lulu says the speakers have feelings. Everyone laughs. Not me. One evening she pressed her ear against Jojo: “He's sad, he's all alone down there.” I moved him up next to Raoul. He sounds better. … Don't tell her it was for her.
Lulu sleeps against Germaine in the afternoons. Germaine doesn't like it. … Neither do I. But Lulu says Germaine purrs. It's true. She purrs.
textes.Lulu dort contre les enceintes, l'après-: Lulu sleeps against the speakers in the afternoon. She says it's like a massage.
textes.Lulu m'a fait asseoir sur la balançoire: Lulu sat me on Gaspard's swing, “just to see”. She said: “Up there, the world spins a bit, at first.” By the third swing, I was all green. She said softly: “We'll wait until your tummy is ready.” I think she's worried for me. That's kind. It's also a long wait.
textes.Lulu m'a tendu un de ses champignons qui: Lulu handed me one of her glowing mushrooms, in front of everyone. “One bite and you fly.” I put it in my pocket to be nice. The next day, it was still glowing in my hook box. I threw it into the sea. The fish came and swam round it, all lit up. I haven't told anyone.
textes.Lulu voit des couleurs qui n'existent pa: Lulu sees colours that don't exist yet. I catch them, she puts them on the sails. We're made to work together. If she ever decides to start the mural.
textes.Lulu voulait peindre les fées sur une vo: Lulu wanted to paint the fairies on a sail, but when she wakes up she always forgets our colours. So I have Zéphyr bring her a petal every month, one colour at a time. Her mural isn't finished. She says she has time. I think she's right.
textes.Lulu, avec ses champignons et ses fées…: Lulu, with her mushrooms and her fairies… Me, I believe what I see, and what I see is a purple octopus on my sail scaring off the fish. She's sweet. She talks nonsense.
textes.Lulu, c'est ma petite-fille, mon soleil: Lulu is my granddaughter, my sunshine and my second chance. She sees fairies. Me, I saw dwarves dance in a mine. In our family, we see things.
textes.Lulu, c'est vrai, ton histoire de royaum: Lulu, is it true, your story about the fairy kingdom?
textes.Lulu, ce soir tu brilles. Je peux ?: Lulu, you're glowing tonight. May I?
textes.Lulu, je te le demande très gentiment, a: Lulu, I'm asking you very nicely today.
textes.Lumen vient me demander si les étoiles b: Lumen comes and asks me whether the stars will move tomorrow. I tell him yes. He's always reassured.
textes.Lumi ! Tu me prêtes Cacahuète, ce soir ?: Lumi! Can I borrow Peanut tonight?
textes.Lumi croit que ses lucioles l'aiment. El: Lumi thinks her fireflies love her. Mostly they love the honey she gives them.
Lumi thinks her fireflies love her. Mostly they love the honey she gives them. She talks nonstop, she shows off with her drawings in the sky. Fine. She draws well.
textes.Lumi parle fort, rit fort, vole fort. Ma: Lumi talks loud, laughs loud, flies loud. But every morning, before dawn, her fireflies light up my flowers. Without her, I'd be setting down my drops by feel.
textes.Lumi t'a guidé jusqu'ici ? C'est la plus: Lumi guided you here? She's the youngest of us. And the bravest.
textes.Lumi voulait une goutte à son nom. Chaqu: Lumi wanted a drop with her name. Every drop already has its own. So I set one under a firefly, on a flower by the pond. It was glowing. I said: “This one is called Lumi.” She shrieked with joy so loudly that the drop fell off. I set down another one. Gently.
