In the evening we go down to the party together, she holds my arm all the way to the dance floor, and there I let go. The youngsters say I dance like a seal. Lila has the photo: it's a wave.
textes.Maintenant, j'ai mon étal sur la place,: Now I've got my stall on the square, in the afternoons: botched potions, cheap, every one unique. Zéphyrine is my best customer. In the evening, I put my vials away under my bed, in the dormitory, between Lin who reads and Pip who talks in his sleep. Gustave lends me his cellar. Well, I take it, and he says yes afterwards. It's almost the same.
textes.Maintenant, j'enseigne au pied de la tou: Now I teach at the foot of the tower, since it leans. I have lunch on the bench in Mother Sage's garden, in the afternoon I go and listen to the wind on the cliffs, and in the evening I chat at the fountain. I keep an eye on Pip and his bedsheets. I argue with Borée. I visit Aurélien on his roof. And the wind follows me everywhere, like a mad dog.
textes.Maintenant, je construis des cabanes pou: These days I build huts for whoever wants one. Marley's, above his banana trees. Mistral's stage. My little test hut near the beach, the one that leans, where Zoé is sleeping at the moment. In the evenings, I nod my head next to Tchoum. We don't talk. We're good. Right.
textes.Maintenant, je dors dans la cabane d'ess: Now I sleep in Gaspard's test hut, the leaning one, with three crabs. In the afternoons I go to Yaya's class. I swim with Sofia, I help Momo drill his shells. I dance till sunrise, and every morning I suggest a name for Mistral's track. The village has adopted me, I think. And I've adopted it too.
textes.Maintenant, je grimpe aux passerelles, j: Now I climb the footbridges, I listen to Faelar's stories, I eat Sylwen's bread and I ask loads of questions. Aëlwen patches up my knees. Lyra told me about the sea and the shells. And then you turned up with your round ears! It's the best year of my whole life. Well, of all forty-two.
textes.Maintenant, je me lève à quatre heures,: These days, I get up at four, knead till noon, sleep a little, and in the evening I take the boat with Margaux's leftovers. I dance, I catch the last Swallow back, I sleep three hours. I knead in rhythm, at a hundred and forty-five. Margaux says my croissants have swing. I think that's a compliment.
textes.Maintenant, je peins les voiles des pêch: Now I paint the fishermen's sails: an octopus for Bastien, stars for others. In the afternoon, I nap against Germaine, the speaker that purrs. At night, I pick the fairies' mushrooms in the ring, behind the dune. And the mural on the wall of sound… it's coming along. In my head. It's very beautiful, in my head.
textes.Maintenant, les mouettes connaissent l'h: Now the seagulls know the time. From half past six, there are a dozen of them lined up on the bakery roof. Waiting for the Lord. When he comes out with his bag, they all take off together behind him, like an escort. Nina says it's his royal guard.
textes.Maintenant, mes genoux ne veulent plus g: These days, my knees won't climb any more. I keep watch from the bow, with the spyglass, and it's my grandson Ewen who goes up to light the lantern. I still count the ships. This year: three. Including you. I wrote you in the journal. In ink, not pencil.
textes.Maintenant, quand je vois arriver sa gro: Now, when I see his big moustache coming at the end of the terrace, I hide the salt cellar in my belt. He comes back every day for another glass “to check”, his little bag of salt in hand. I watch him like a guard of the Skala. He's never managed to salt a single glass. Not yet.
There is now. I added it.
textes.Maintenant, à la fin de la criée, Jacquo: Now, at the end of the auction, Jacquot buys up everything that's left: scorpionfish, sunfish, spiky things nobody can name. One day, I followed him to the galleon to see what he did with them. At the foot of the gangway, I caught the smell: cinnamon, herring, and something else. I came back down. There are mysteries a crier must respect.
textes.Maintiens pour mouliner, relâche si ça t: Hold to reel, release if it pulls too hard
textes.Mais Kick et Basse vont s'ennuyer, Gaspa: But Kick and Bass will get bored, Gaspard!
textes.Mais Peek' veut apprendre les traces, Ba: But Peek' wants to learn tracks, Balam!
textes.Mais Rê doit m'entendre, Néferet ! Il es: But Rê has to hear me, Néferet! He's far away!
textes.Mais elle te ressemble ! Elle ne sourit: But she looks like you! She never smiles.
textes.Mais je l'écris, mon journal !: But I'm the one who writes it!
textes.Mais l'autre main, elle tient la fusée !: But my other hand's holding the rocket!
textes.Mais le Sceau d'Airain cliquette dans ta: But the Bronze Seal clicks in your pocket… The Cogwheel (key 3, then X)?
textes.Mais moi si, si on traîne !: But I will, if we dawdle!
No they're not, come now. … Oh, they are. Thanks, little one.
textes.Mais vous ne savez même pas ce que c'est: But you don't even know what it is!
textes.Mais à Ramure, il n'y a jamais de nuit s: But in Ramure, there's never a moonless night. Maybe that's why we're so rarely afraid here. I keep looking all the same. A nose never sleeps.
textes.Mais… QU'EST-CE QUE TU FICHES CHEZ MOI ?: But… WHAT ON EARTH ARE YOU DOING IN MY HOUSE?!
textes.Mais… comment ça tient ?: But… how does it stay up?
textes.Mais… je suis déjà là, juste derrière to: But… I'm already here, right behind you! I have been all along!
textes.Majesté ! C'est vous ! Vous êtes revenue: Majesty! It's you! You've come back!
textes.Majesté ! Ce soir, je te dessine une cou: Your Majesty! Tonight, I'm drawing you a crown!
textes.Majesté ! Je vous ai apporté des fleurs: Your Majesty! I've brought you moonflowers.
textes.Majesté ! Le brin de ta couronne a une t: Your Majesty! Has the sprout in your crown got a third leaf?
textes.Majesté ! Le soleil, il fait du bruit ?: Majesty! Does the sun make a noise?
textes.Majesté ! Toutes les lettres livrées ! U: Your Majesty! All letters delivered! A record!
textes.Majesté ! Vous avez vu le nez du roi Atl: Majesty! Have you seen King Atlas's nose? I polished it this morning.
textes.Majesté ! Vous êtes descendue ! Pif ! Pa: Your Majesty! You've come down! Pop! Bang! Welcome!
Majesty, your decree is four pages long.
textes.Majesté. Les runes ont parlé, cette nuit: Majesty. The runes spoke last night.
Your Majesty. Your crows are tired.
textes.Majesté. Votre couronne brille, aujourd': Majesty. Your crown is shining today.
textes.Mal. Clou a caché mon marteau. Et il ne: Bad. Clou hid my hammer. And he won't say where.
Badly. I think about too many things.
textes.Mal. Les golems des hauteurs se sont rév: Bad. The golems of the heights have woken up. They come down at night. The stones rumble.
textes.Mal. Très mal. Mais tu n'y es pour rien…: Bad. Very bad. But it's not your fault… well, hardly your fault.
textes.Malachar dit que c'est moi qui ai mis le: Malachar says I'm the one who set fire to the Academy tower, when we were pupils. It was him. Well… it was us. But it was his idea.
textes.Malachar était le premier de la classe,: Malachar was top of the class, and I was bottom in flames. He became headmaster, I became a sweeper, and we both found our place. He refuses to admit that burning down the tower was his idea.
Malachar, the tower was your idea.
textes.Malaterre a des dents en or et des dés e: Malaterre has gold teeth and loaded dice. I can't prove it. He won my compass from me. I can't prove how, either. But I know.
textes.Malaterre sourit en or massif et triche: Malaterre smiles in solid gold and cheats with everything else. Nobody's ever proved it. Me, I only play with him using my own dice.
textes.Malaterre. Ma boussole indique toujours: Malaterre. Does my compass still point north?
textes.Malaterre. Toujours tes dés dans la manc: Malaterre. Still got dice up your sleeve?
textes.Malebolge, le Huitième Cercle : trois fo: Malebolge, the Eighth Circle: three ditches of fire, three turning iron bridges. And little imps, the Malebranches, sniggering as they wait for you.
textes.Malheureuse. Mon mari a perdu son allian: Miserable. My husband lost his wedding ring after ten days. Ten days!
textes.Malin. Les gens en savent plus que les c: Clever. People know more than maps. But watch out: in Carène, if you ask Corentin for directions, you end up in a story, not at your destination.
textes.Mal… Je m'en doutais : tu as les yeux ce: Badly… I thought so: you've got rings round your eyes like a tanuki. Prescription: a mist tea every evening, and no Trèfle tart after midnight.
textes.Mama ! Qui a mis de la cannelle dans mon: Mama! Who put cinnamon in my stew?
textes.Mama ! Une soupe pour le musicien ?: Mama! A soup for the musician?
textes.Mama Grog est la conseillère la plus pré: Mama Grog is the most precious adviser in my government. She doesn't know it. Between us, citizen, she has more authority than I do. Don't repeat that. Especially not to her.
textes.Mama Grog est la seule personne de la Ba: Mama Grog is the only person on the Balafre I'm afraid of. Between us, there's a matter of forty coins and a lukewarm grog. She has her opinion. I have mine.
textes.Mama Grog fait le meilleur grog de l'île: Mama Grog makes the best grog on the island, I'll grant her that. But cinnamon in a stew! She says it's her grandmother's recipe. Her grandmother packed a punch, fine. But she had no taste.
textes.Mama Grog garde un tonneau de cidre de C: Mama Grog keeps a barrel of Carène cider just for me. Nobody else touches it. On this island, that's the closest thing to tenderness. The rest is rum.
textes.Mama Grog m'a donné une soupe et une scè: Mama Grog gave me a soup and a stage the evening I arrived with nothing. I've played for her ever since. She pays me in grog and stew. I'm the best-paid man on Balafre.
textes.Mama Grog me cherche. Je l'évite. C'est: Mama Grog is looking for me. I'm avoiding her. Avoiding Mama Grog is an art. She's everywhere.
Mama Grog is demanding her forty coins.
textes.Mama Grog tient le Crâne Fendu et le por: Mama Grog runs the Crâne Fendu and the port with the same hand. We signed a treaty, years ago, on a napkin. We both respect it. It's the only treaty in the archipelago that's respected.
textes.Mama Grog, c'est la meilleure femme de l: Mama Grog is the best woman on Balafre. Her grog is the best in the world, nice and hot, nice and gentle. I pay my tab every Saturday, down to the last penny. Hic! I'm the only one.
textes.Mama Grog, une holo-photo pour un touris: Mama Grog, a holo-photo for a space tourist?
textes.Mama Lou ? Il paraît qu'elle a coulé tro: Mama Lou? They say she sank three ships. I like her a lot. And I drink everything she serves me. Well… almost everything.
textes.Mama Lou achète toutes ses cruches chez: Mama Lou buys all her jugs from me, and her pirates break them. Three a week. I charge double, she pays without arguing. She calls me “girlie”. I let her.
textes.Mama Lou dit que c'est le rhum qui fait: Mama Lou says it's rum that keeps the peace in Tazira. It's tea. She may have sunk three ships, but peace isn't something you sink: it's something you serve.
textes.Mama Lou, autrefois Lou la Terrible. Ell: Mama Lou, once Lou the Terrible. She threw me into the sea when I was twenty; today, she serves me rum. That's what you call a career. She knows more than she lets on.
textes.Mama Lou, la patronne de la taverne des: Mama Lou, the landlady of the pirates' tavern, used to be a pirate herself. They say she sank three ships. Me, I never tell her her rum is too strong.
textes.Mama Lou, à la taverne, a été pirate. La: Mama Lou, at the tavern, used to be a pirate. The most terrible of them all. She retired because she got seasick. A seasick pirate!
textes.Maman ! J'ai trouvé un scarabée vivant !: Mum! I found a live scarab!
textes.Maman ! J'ai vu une tortue ! La quarante: Mum! I saw a turtle! The forty-fourth!
textes.Maman ! J'ai été très sage, aujourd'hui: Mummy! I was really good today!
textes.Maman ! Je peux aller au Bois de Cendre: Mum! Can I go to the Ash Wood?
textes.Maman ! Je peux aller jouer ?: Mum! Can I go and play?
textes.Maman ! Je peux emprunter ta grosse pinc: Mum! Can I borrow your big tongs?
textes.Maman ! Ma prochaine fusée, elle fera de: Mum! My next rocket's going to make green smoke!
textes.Maman ! Ton bain est prêt ! Moitié prix: Mum! Your bath is ready! Half price!
textes.Maman chante quand elle pétrit. Elle cha: Mum sings when she kneads. She sings out of tune, out of tune, out of tune! Even the dough pulls a face. I sing with her, and then we laugh so much she has to start the dough again. Fanny says we're the worst singers on the island. It's true. At least we're champions at something.
textes.Maman cueille les fleurs de tout le vill: Mummy picks the flowers for the whole village. She always smells of violets, and she always knows when I've been naughty. Even when I haven't done it yet.
textes.Maman dit qu'on n'a pas le droit d'y tre: Mum says we're not allowed to dip our bread in it. But she says nothing about fingers.
Mum says I ask too many questions. Why does she say that?
textes.Maman dit que je suis née un matin de pl: Mummy says I was born on a rainy morning, and that I yelled so loud the frogs in the fountain went quiet. Daddy says I opened my eyes and straight away looked up, at the footbridges. I don't remember, I was too little. But I believe Daddy.
textes.Maman dit que l'Arbre-Mère veille sur no: Mummy says the Mother Tree watches over us at night. Once I asked her: “And who watches over the Mother Tree?” She thought for a really long time. Then she said: “You will, when you're grown up.” Ever since, I say goodnight to the Tree every evening. And to Mummy too.
textes.Maman fait pousser des fleurs sur l'eau: Mum grows flowers on the water! And maize, and chillies, and squash. She laughs all the time, except when I come home late. Then she laughs afterwards.
textes.Maman m'a donné des graines de maïs à pl: Mum gave me some maize seeds to plant. I put them in with the tip pointing up, so they could see the sun. They all grew crooked. Mum looked at the maize and smiled really big, with wet eyes. She said Dad used to grow maize like that. Dancing maize.
textes.Maman m'a interdit de grimper au premier: Mum told me I'm not allowed to climb to the first platform without the stairs. So I take the stairs! Running, four steps at a time, shouting “I'm obeying!”. Mum goes “Mrrr” with her eyes closed. That means she's got nothing to say back. I won.
textes.Maman m'a offert un petit marteau avec m: Mum gave me a little hammer with my name engraved on it. I improved it with gears and a whistle: now it sings when you shake it. Mum said: “Ortie, a hammer is for hitting.” I answered: “Mum, a hammer can sing too.” She didn't say anything. She shook the hammer. Twice.
textes.Maman m'a tissé une robe avec des algues: Mum wove me a dress out of seaweed in every colour of the canal. She put in a golden thread, a tiny one, hidden in the hem. She says it's a ray of sunshine, so I have one on me until I see the real thing. I check every night that it's still there.
textes.Maman tisse les algues : les robes, les: Mum weaves seaweed: dresses, curtains, blankets. She says I'm the only thread she can't keep straight. It's a compliment, I think.
textes.Maman voudrait que je devienne forgeronn: Mum would like me to become a blacksmith. But forging is hitting a thing until it has the right shape. Inventing is hitting things until they do something new. It's not the same.
textes.Maman, c'est la meilleure marchande d'ép: Mum is the best spice seller on the whole island. She smells of cinnamon and pepper. She worries about me all the time. She says that's a mum's job.
textes.Maman, c'est la meilleure tisserande du: Mum is the best weaver on the river! Her linen is so fine you can see the sun through it. She says I run around too much. That's because I have lots of places to go!
textes.Maman, c'est la plus forte de toute la c: Mum is the strongest in the whole city. She hammers iron all day long and laughs so loud the bells ring. She'd like me to be a blacksmith. I love her, but I'm going to be an inventor.
textes.Maman, elle crie fort, elle sent le pois: Mum shouts loud, she smells of fish and she dances like crazy at parties. She's the best mum in the world. But don't tell her, or she'll shout even louder.
textes.Maman, elle fait le meilleur pain et ell: Mum makes the best bread and she gets up while it's still dark. She says I ask too many questions. But she answers anyway. One time in three.
textes.Maman, elle me met de la crème solaire p: Mummy puts sun cream all over me. On my nose, on my ears, behind my knees. I'm all white, I look like a ghost. The ladies on the beach laugh. Even Kevin the lifeguard said “Hi, little ghost.” Mummy says it doesn't matter, ghosts don't get sunburnt.
textes.Maman, pourquoi le pain il gonfle ?: Mum, why does bread puff up?
textes.Maman, tu me racontes la fin de l'histoi: Mummy, will you tell me the end of the story?
textes.Maman. Il me faut de la menthe de cendre: Mum. I need some ash mint. Three bunches.
textes.Mamie Barricade, une holo-photo pour un: Mamie Barricade, a holo-photo for a space tourist?
Mamie Kiku sent you a message! (No. But click anyway.)
textes.Mamie Tournesol et Mère Averse ont fait: Granny Sunflower and Mother Downpour have made peace: the Larsen Festival can come back! Jack, the head roadie, has been repairing the Main Stage for years. He's missing Galet's ropes, Lune's canvas… and someone to tell Mégaphone to finally press his third button.
textes.Mamie Tournesol, Mère Averse vous a fait: Granny Sunflower, Mother Downpour made you this umbrella.
textes.Mamie Tournesol, la doyenne du Camp des: Granny Sunflower, the eldest of the Flower Camp, and Mother Downpour, the eldest of Rainville, were the best friends in the world. Fifty years ago, they fell out over the weather (sun or rain for the festival?), and since then nobody has dared to step onto the Main Stage. Granny Sunflower would like to make peace… but she doesn't dare.
textes.Mamie Tournesol, pourquoi regardez-vous: Granny Sunflower, why are you looking at Rainville like that?
textes.Mamie, comment arrêter Lisse pour de bon: Mamie, how do we stop Lisse for good?
textes.Mamie, que se passe-t-il quand la sirène: Mamie, what happens when the siren wails?
textes.Mamma Lasagna a encore fait trop de pâte: Mamma Lasagna has made too much pasta again. Like every day. Luckily.
textes.Mamma Lasagna, le Révérend a besoin de v: Mamma Lasagna, the Reverend needs your pasta for the sacred Dish.
textes.Manette : croix ou stick pour viser: Controller: d-pad or stick to aim
textes.Mange d'abord, Odette. Il ne va pas s'en: Eat first, Odette. Your sailboat isn't going to fly away.
textes.Mange d'abord. Les voiliers ne partiront: Eat first. The boats won't sail off.
textes.Mange-Clous ! Il refte de ta femoule ?: Mange-Clous! Ith there any themolina left?
textes.Mange-Clous ! J'ai épluché tous les oign: Mange-Clous! I've peeled all the onions!
textes.Mange-Clous dit que j'ai un trou dans l': Mange-Clous says I've got a hole in my stomach. I say he's got a hole in his recipe. We're both right. But his stew, I always finish it.
textes.Mange-Clous est un bon cuisinier qui a e: Mange-Clous is a good cook who had a very bad day. Thirty sick sailors in one night. Since then, he brings me soup every lunchtime to make amends. My geranium thanks him.
textes.Mange-Clous fait le meilleur ragoût du m: Mange-Clous makes the best stew in the world, except when he puts in too much chilli. He's teaching me to peel onions. It makes you cry, but they're grown-up onions.
Mange-Clous talks too much. He cooks well. He swallowed one of my nails. He's still alive. It was a good nail.
textes.Mange-Clous vient m'aider à la cheminée: Mange-Clous comes to help me at the fireplace every lunchtime. He cooks well, he sings loud, and he puts chilli in everything. Everything! Even in my cinnamon. I like him. Don't tell him.
textes.Mange-Clous, c'est un artifte. Il me fai: Mange-Clous ith an artitht. He maketh me mathed thtew, with tender little bitth, and the betht themolina in the archipelago. Without him, I'd have been hungry for thirty yearth.
textes.Mange-Clous, je viens vous débarrasser d: Mange-Clous, I've come to rid you of the rat.
textes.Mange-Clous. Ta soupe du jour ?: Mange-Clous. Your soup of the day?
textes.Marcel ! Trois fois l'archipel, tu dis ?: Marcel! Three times round the archipelago, you say?
textes.Marcel ? Un bavard qui jure trop. Trente: Marcel? A chatterbox who swears too much. Thirty years he brought me my letters, and on days with no letters he came anyway. About the lavender, he denies it. He denies it very badly.
textes.Marcel ? Un tricheur, un menteur et un f: Marcel? A cheat, a liar and a postman. Forty years he's been measuring crooked. He's my best friend, but if he asks you, I never said so.
textes.Marcel a porté le courrier pendant trent: Marcel carried the post for thirty years, and he carried my one-centimetre victory. A precise man. Sometimes too precise.
textes.Marcel, c'est le facteur le plus marcheu: Marcel is the walkingest postman in history. He says his round is worth my marathons. We argued, we did the maths: he might be right.
textes.Marcel, mon ancien chef de tournée. Il m: Marcel, my old round boss. He taught me everything, and he still keeps an eye on me from his pétanque pitch. I pretend to be annoyed. I'm touched.
textes.Marchander ? Ha ! Enfin quelqu'un qui co: Haggle? Ha! At last someone who knows the custom. … But no. Not today.
textes.Marchander ? J'ai calculé le prix au cen: Haggle? I worked out the price to the last cent with my calculating machine. It's never wrong. Well, almost never.
textes.Marchander ? Le prix est juste, comme la: Haggle? The price is fair, like Maât's feather. One does not argue with Maât.
textes.Marchander ? Mes prix sont déjà plus dou: Haggle? My prices are already gentler than the morning lava. No.
textes.Marchander ? Mon prix a été calculé à la: Haggle? My price was calculated by moonlight. You don't argue with the moon.
textes.Marchander ? Sur un bateau, les prix son: Haggle? On a ship, prices are nailed to the mast.
textes.Marchander ? Va voir Bedaine, au Grand T: Haggle? Go and see Bedaine, at the Great Swap. My prices are round as the moon.
Haggle with a dwarf? Ho ho! No.
textes.Marchander avec un pirate ? T'es courage: Haggle with a pirate? Either you're brave, or you're daft.
textes.Marcher ?! Hop hop… Bon. Chacun son truc: Walk?! Hop hop… Fine. Each to their own. Walking is running with patience. Lots and lots of patience.
textes.Marcher jusqu'au bout de la brume, là où: To walk to the very end of the mist, where it stops, and see what lies beyond. Not to leave. Just so I can make my report: “Report: the world is big.”
textes.Marché conclu ! Tope là, de la patte. Qu: Deal! Shake on it, paw to hand. What shall we swap next?
textes.Marché conclu. {objet}, pour {prix} pièc: Deal. {objet}, for {prix} coins. You won't regret it.
textes.Margaux m'a appris le pain, la patience: Margaux taught me bread, patience and getting up at four. She grumbles when I dance in the bakehouse, but she's the first to start humming.
textes.Margaux me donne ses invendus du soir po: Margaux gives me her evening leftovers for the party, so they don't go to waste, she says. One evening there were twelve croissants in the basket, still piping hot, with a note: “Leftovers.” We never bake a batch in the evening. Margaux can't lie to save her life. I didn't say a thing. I just hugged her really tight.
textes.Margaux n'a personne pour livrer le pain: Margaux has no one to deliver the bread to Chez Paulo, the Square Café and the Grand Hotel.
textes.Margaux vole mes croissants à moi. Non,: Margaux steals my croissants. No, I'm joking, I'm the one who steals hers. No, I'm joking again.
textes.Margaux, c'est la meilleure boulangère d: Margaux is the best baker in Port-Azur. The only one, too, but that changes nothing. Her bread is my soup's best friend. She laughs at my jokes. Almost always.
textes.Margaux, c'est la petite qui a repris ma: Margaux is the girl who took over my bakery. She puts too much honey in her bread. I eat it twice a day, to check. Always too much honey.
textes.Margaux, ma belle ! Tes croissants, ils: Margaux, bella! Your croissants are at my place, I stole them!
textes.Margot a fait les comptes de l'année. El: Margot did the year's accounts. She showed me a column: “Papa, thirty-one per cent of your bubbles, you blow for yourself. Not for the customers.” I asked how she knew. She said: “They're the ones you watch fly away.” I said it was an investment. She wrote “no”.
textes.Margot a refait de tête les calculs de d: Margot redid in her head the distance calculations for a double star. She found a mistake in the Academy's tables. A real one. I took the correction to the director myself, with Margot's notebook open at page twelve, her crossings-out and her drawings of Bidule in the margin. He had to accept it. Margot said: “Logical.”
textes.Margot a refait tous les calculs de ma p: Margot redid all the sums for my first rocket. Three pages. She says it would have taken off with three kilos less smoke. Three kilos! I told her smoke is the best bit. She sighed, like a grown-up. Then she wrote at the bottom of the page: “Smoke: keep.” She's nice, really.
textes.Margot calcule mieux que l'Académie et r: Margot calculates better than the Academy and observes better than I do. I give her ten minutes at the telescope every evening. It's not much. It's all I dare give her.
textes.Margot est trop sérieuse pour son âge. E: Margot is too serious for her age. She looks at me with calculating eyes. I'm sure she knows something. About my engine. Or about me.
textes.Margot, c'est ma fille, mon comptable et: Margot is my daughter, my accountant and my alarm clock. She's eight and a half and she looks after me better than I do. I make the bubbles; she does everything else.
textes.Margot, c'est mon associée. Elle fait le: Margot is my partner. She does the sums, I do everything else. She's a bit bossy. Very bossy. But when I clown around, she laughs, even if she pretends she isn't.
textes.Marley ! Combien de régimes, cette semai: Marley! How many bunches this week?
textes.Marley ? Il cultive ses bananes dans mon: Marley? He grows his bananas in my corner and pays me in bunches. The best tenant in the world. He only makes noise for the banana trees.
textes.Marley fait écouter de la musique à mes: Marley plays music to my banana trees, on a little box that goes boom. I sing them sea shanties. We ended up making a deal: him on even days, me on odd days. The bunches have never been so big. Gaston leans towards the boom.
textes.Marley jure qu'il n'écoute jamais ce que: Marley swears he never listens to what I confide in my banana trees. But last week, he asked me, all casual: “And Mireille, is she any better?” By Neptune's beard! I've switched banana trees.
textes.Marley m'a demandé un collier en peau de: Marley asked me for a banana-peel necklace. I said it wouldn't hold. He insisted, so I made it. He wore it proudly a whole evening. Two days later it was all black and the flies followed him across the dance floor. He said: “That's nature, my brother.” I fell off the stall laughing.
textes.Marley n'a jamais pris le bateau. Jamais: Marley has never taken the boat. Never. So he gives me messages for Port-Azur: “Say hello to the harbour for me.” “Tell the lighthouse it blinks nicely.” I say them out loud, on deck. Captain Léon gives me funny looks. But I say them. That much I can't refuse him.
textes.Marley veut tellement aller chez les fée: Marley wants so badly to go to the fairies. He asks nicely, very nicely, every day. But his tummy already spins on a swing. I don't want him to be scared, up there.
textes.Marley, aujourd'hui, on vend. On ne donn: Marley, today we sell. We don't give anything away. Deal?
textes.Marley, c'est mon associé au stand du ma: Marley's my partner at the market stall. I sell the necklaces; he gives away the bananas. He says everyone is family. And family never pays.
textes.Marley, c'est mon voisin et mon meilleur: Marley's my neighbour and my best mate. He pays for my huts in bananas and says everyone is family. With him, it's true.
textes.Marley, j'ai vu une banane qui brillait,: Marley, I saw a glowing banana, in the ring.
textes.Marley, je l'aime bien, hein. Mais il ve: I like Marley, really. But he wants to put banana in everything I make. In croissants, in brioche, in baguettes. In baguettes, {surnom}!
Marley, no. I know what you're going to say. No.
textes.Marley, tu as bu de l'eau ?: Marley, have you drunk some water?
textes.Marée ? La meilleure commerçante du dôme: Marée? The best trader in the dome. We nearly got married, four hundred years ago. We got stuck on the price of the ring. Three coins apart.
textes.Marée coupe mes algues. Une sur trois, e: Marée cuts my seaweed. One in three, she says. She counts the way she talks: very fast, and not always right.
textes.Marée m'a proposé de vendre des « galett: Marée suggested selling “royal crackers”, with my portrait on them, at twice the price. I refused. The next day she was selling “almost royal crackers”, with a lady who looked a great deal like me, except for the nose. I walked by and bought one. I paid for it.
textes.Marée me paie en galettes. En galettes !: Marée pays me in crackers. In crackers! I've got thirty under my bed. But when I dance in front of her stall, she's the one who claps loudest. So, well.
textes.Marée me vend les plus longues laminaire: Marée sells me the longest kelp under the dome. She talks as much as she sells, which is to say a lot. She has a good heart, under all the coins.
textes.Marée parle plus vite que le courant et: Marée talks faster than the current and counts faster still. Her crackers, I really do love them. I think I'm the only one.
Marée won't let me archive her recipes. “Secrets don't get written down.” Everything gets written down. Except, apparently, the seaweed cracker.
textes.Marée vend des galettes d'algues. Elles: Marée sells seaweed cakes. They're… nourishing. That's the kind word.
textes.Marée, la galette de ce matin était parf: Marée, this morning's cracker was perfect.
textes.Marée, si tu me paies en galettes, je da: Marée, if you pay me in crackers, I'll dance at a walk.
textes.Marée. Juste le sel. Dis-moi juste combi: Marée. Just the salt. Just tell me how much salt.
textes.Marée. Un sac de galettes, comme d'habit: Marée. A bag of crackers, as usual.
textes.Matelot ! Au rapport ! T'as fait ton nœu: Sailor! Report! Have you done your bowline today?
Mathurin! Your slice is under the tea towel.
Mathurin! Your thyme is coming along nicely.
textes.Mathurin dit que je lui ai prédit une gr: Mathurin says I predicted a big catch for him and he caught a boot. It was a very big boot. I was right.
textes.Mathurin et moi, nous sommes deux vieux: Mathurin and I are two old men by the water. Him, the sea; me, the lake. He talks too much, he drinks a little. But he understands water. That's rare.
textes.Mathurin le passeur a vu un serpent de m: Mathurin the ferryman saw a sea serpent near the coast. After three glasses of honey drink. He sees serpents every evening.
textes.Mathurin m'a amené dans sa barque, l'an: Mathurin brought me in his rowing boat, last year. There was mist everywhere, and I wasn't scared. OK, a bit. And all of a sudden, the tower came out of the fog, standing tall, with the Great Crystal shining on top. I shouted “Wow!” so loud that Mathurin dropped an oar. We had to fish it out with my hat.
textes.Mathurin me boude pour une histoire de b: Mathurin is sulking with me over a boot. I stand by my prediction. He grumbles, he grouches, and he comes back to sit at my table every month. Deep down, he loves having things predicted for him.
textes.Mathurin rame comme personne et raconte: Mathurin rows like nobody else and tells stories like nobody else. Especially his sea serpents, which always come out after the mead. He pinches my rum. We like each other. We don't say so.
textes.Mathurin, ça fait trente ans qu'il « rep: Mathurin has been “leaving tomorrow” for thirty years. He tells his sea serpent stories, he brings me the first fish of the day, and he always finishes the pie. A good man. The best.
Mathurin. Thank you for the wood.
textes.Matthias ! Cette année, on y va, à la gr: Matthias! This year, are we going to the great gate?
textes.Matthias ! Note bien : ce soir, la balei: Matthias! Write this down: tonight, the whale has six trees.
textes.Matthias ! Toujours pas de clé ? Je t'ai: Matthias! Still no key? I'll give you a good price.
textes.Matthias ! Tu es repassé voir ma prairie: Matthias! Did you go and check on my meadow?
textes.Matthias a un carnet rien que pour mes h: Matthias has a journal just for my stories, his thirteenth. He notes the date, the place, and the number of hot honeys. One evening he told me: “Yesterday your whale had three trees on its back. Today it has five.” I answered: “It grew.” He wrote that down.
textes.Matthias est le seul à prendre mon auber: Matthias is the only one who takes my inn seriously. He drew me the plot, the plans, even the sign. He talks a lot, but it's always to say kind things.
textes.Matthias est venu à la proue avec un com: Matthias came to the bow with a compass and a protractor, to measure the angle of my blue light. I showed him the spot. He calculated all afternoon. That evening, on his map, there was a little blue dot, and next to it: “according to Grégoire (?)”. It took me three weeks to speak to him again.
textes.Matthias et moi, on doit aller voir ense: Matthias and I are supposed to go and see the hinges of the great gate together. We decide it every year, at the tavern, on the third round of sparkling apple. We've never gone.
textes.Matthias m'a dessiné les plans de mon au: Matthias drew the plans for my inn: twelve rooms. In one corner, I pencilled in a little room for my aunt, with a stove. A few days later, it had been gone over in ink, with an extra window. He didn't say anything. Neither did I. He's a true friend.
textes.Matthias m'envoie : que savez-vous des q: Matthias sent me: what do you know about the four seals?
textes.Matthias me pose cent questions et n'éco: Matthias asks me a hundred questions and doesn't listen to a single answer. He put my blue light on his map with a question mark. A question mark. Next to my name.
textes.Matthias parle trop. Il voudrait que je: Matthias talks too much. He wants me to draw underwater, with a pencil. But he's the only one who didn't think I was mad about my stones. That counts.
textes.Matthias raconte à qui veut l'entendre q: Matthias tells anyone who'll listen that he'll open the Gate of the Four Seals. I offered to sell him a key. He didn't laugh.
textes.Matthias rêve d'ouvrir la Porte aux Quat: Matthias dreams of opening the Gate of the Four Seals. The four seals must be found, one for each people of the great island: the sea spray of Carène, the sands of Tazira, the bronze of the northern shepherds, the mists of Ramure. Each seal leads to the next.
textes.Matthias veut ouvrir une porte que perso: Matthias wants to open a door nobody has opened in two hundred years. I offered him a key. He didn't laugh. Dreamers never laugh at their dreams. It's touching.
textes.Matthias écrit mes histoires dans un car: Matthias writes my stories down in a journal to check them. As if you could check a story! But he's the only one who listens to me with a pencil. It's flattering.
textes.Matthias, le cartographe de Carène, rêve: Matthias, the mapmaker of Carène, dreams of drawing the heart of the island. He'd like to know what the great sealed gate at the foot of Stoneheart looks like.
textes.Matthias. Tu as toujours ton point d'int: Matthias. Still got your question mark?
textes.Mauvaise réponse. Pour un garde. Pour un: Wrong answer. For a guard. For a tracker, right answer. Go and see Brume. She'll like you. Me, I'll keep an eye on you.
textes.Mauvaise. Comme d'habitude. Ma jambe me: Bad. As usual. My leg itches. It's made of wood, and it itches. Explain that to me.
textes.Mauvaise. Comme d'habitude. Merci de dem: Bad. As usual. Thanks for asking. Hmph.
textes.Maître ! J'ai encore écrit mon nom avec: Master! I wrote my name with the leg again!
textes.Maître Faelar ! Vous connaissez vraiment: Master Faelar! Do you really know my song?
textes.Maître Filandre m'aime pas trop. Depuis: Master Filandre doesn't like me much. Since the bookshelf business, he watches me like a book that might fly off. But he lets me come back every day. So maybe a little.
textes.Maître Hugues, la fontaine fait des bull: Master Hugues, the fountain is making green bubbles
Master Hugues, the fountain is making green bubbles…
textes.Maître Lumen enseigne la lumière avec le: Master Lumen teaches light with his hands and his eyes closed. I do it with books. It's not the same. It works both ways. He talks a lot. In the middle, he says beautiful things.
textes.Maître Rivet a construit mon majordome,: Master Rivet built my butler, the slowest and most loyal of waiters. He never smiles, he says “Hm”, and he comes to check on his robot every lunchtime. A real father, really.
textes.Maître Rivet dit que Boulon est inutile: Master Rivet says Boulon is pointless: “a robot that wags its tail”. But the other day, I saw him at the corner of stand 4, crouching, scratching him under the chin. Boulon was wagging so hard the spring was singing. When Master Rivet saw me, he stood up and said: “Hm. His tail's got some play in it.”
textes.Maître Rivet glisse sous ma porte des pl: Master Rivet slips robot-boat plans under my door. Very beautiful, in blue ink, with arrows everywhere. I send them back annotated in red: “No.” Sometimes “No, thank you”. Once: “No, but nice rudder.” He never replies. But the next plan had an even nicer rudder.
textes.Maître Rivet m'a tout appris, et il m'a: Master Rivet taught me everything, and he helped me make myself a new arm. He says Boulon is useless. He says it while petting him, when he thinks I'm not looking.
textes.Maître Rivet m'a tout appris, sauf à par: Master Rivet taught me everything except how to talk. He hasn't said a word to me in six years. I don't think he knows how to start again. Neither do I.
textes.Maître Rivet ne m'aime pas beaucoup, à c: Master Rivet doesn't like me much, because of his sweepers. I understand. But he never smiles, and honestly, it makes you want to confetti him.
textes.Maître Rivet voudrait des robots partout: Master Rivet would like robots everywhere, even on the water. Me, I want to keep my harbour. But I have to admit one thing: nobody tightens a nut like him. Nobody.
textes.Maître Rivet voudrait que je lui constru: Master Rivet wants me to build him a robot boat. A boat that steers itself. I said: and what am I supposed to do, then?
textes.Maître. Vous avez bien dormi, cette nuit: Master. Did you sleep well last night?
textes.Maîtresse ! Ciel parfait cette nuit, ven: Mistress! Perfect sky tonight, come and see!
textes.Maîtresse ! Tlaco a appris quoi, aujourd: Miss! What did Tlaco learn today?
textes.Maîtresse Pyra ! J'ai pas brûlé Bertrand: Mistress Pyra! I didn't burn Bertrand today!
textes.Maîtresse Zéphyrine ! Je peux refaire vo: Mistress Zéphyrine! Can I make your chair fly again?
textes.Mbarek ! Mon ami ! Du miel des brumes co: Mbarek! My friend! Mist honey for your dates?
Mbarek has lodged with me for fifteen years. Always the same room, window to the east. He says he's leaving tomorrow. He's been saying it for fifteen years. He's my best customer.
textes.Mbarek ne dit rien, et il gagne toujours: Mbarek says nothing, and he always wins. I don't understand how. I talk better than him, longer than him, louder than him. And I pay his price.
textes.Mbarek, l'homme bleu de Tazira ! Il parl: Mbarek, the blue man of Tazira! He talks little and never laughs at my jokes. Never. I count that as friendship, my friend: you have to be very close to dare not to laugh.
textes.Mbarek, le caravanier, loge chez moi. Il: Mbarek, the caravaneer, is staying with me. He never sleeps before midnight. He watches the stars. He says they move.
textes.Mbarek, le frère d'Itto. Il ne parle pas: Mbarek, Itto's brother. He doesn't talk, he watches. It took him two seasons to give me his sister. I think he likes me now. He's never said so. That's a good sign.
textes.Me marier un jour sans date et sans heur: To get married one day with no date and no time, without telling anyone. A Tuesday, perhaps, or a Thursday that thinks it's a Tuesday. And on that day, for every watch in the Bazaar to ring at once. Even the ones that run backwards. Especially those.
textes.Me rendre ma canne ? Jamais de la vie !: Give me back my rod? Not on your life! It's yours now. Go fishing, {surnom}.
Giving me back my own work? Keep it. What's sold is sold.
textes.Me reposer ? À mon poste ? Majesté, quel: Rest? At my post? Majesty, what an idea!
textes.Meilleure fournisseuse de l'île : du mie: Best supplier on the island: treetop honey, and not one complaint, even with a stung nose. She can't count coins, but she knows how to make them sing.
textes.Mener la lumière de la sève jusqu'au cœu: Guide the light of the sap to the heartwood
textes.Merci ! Et un client content, un !: Thanks! And that's one happy customer!
textes.Merci ! Je fermerai les yeux pour le tra: Thanks! I'll close my eyes to get through it.
textes.Merci ! Je vais le démonter pour voir co: Thank you! I'll take it apart to see how it works.
textes.Merci ! Lune a tissé la toile, Galet a f: Thanks! Lune wove the canvas, Galet made the ropes, and I painted the door. Here, take this for the road.
textes.Merci ! Merci ! Deuxième, c'est battre t: Thanks! Thanks! Second means beating everyone but one. That's almost everyone, right! I'm going to tell Pépin. And Bondi. Especially Bondi.
textes.Merci ! Ne le dis pas trop fort : sinon: Thank you! Don't say it too loud, or we'll have to repaint the kitchen too.
textes.Merci ! Reviens quand tu veux, la porte: Thanks! Come back whenever you like, the door is always open.
textes.Merci ! Reviens quand tu veux. Même pour: Thanks! Come back whenever you like. Even for nothing. Especially for nothing: I'm a bit bored.
textes.Merci ! Tiens, prends donc ça pour la ro: Thank you! Here, take this for the road. Nobody leaves my house on an empty stomach!
textes.Merci ! Tu es mon plus grand fan. Mon se: Thank you! You're my biggest fan. My only fan, but the biggest.
Thanks! You hide well, you know.
textes.Merci bien. Ça trouvera sa place dans la: Thanks kindly. It'll find a place in the hold.
textes.Merci d'avoir ramené les esprits-luciole: Thank you for bringing the firefly spirits back. The Mother Tree has been singing ever since you came.
textes.Merci de ne pas me mentir. La peur, je l: Thank you for not lying to me. Fear I know well: you don't chase it away, you learn to walk beside it. So it will be up to us to be gentle, when the day comes.
textes.Merci de patienter : votre déménagement: Please wait: your move is in progress.
Thank you again, from the bottom of my heart.
textes.Merci encore, {surnom}. Grâce à toi, je: Thank you again, {surnom}. Thanks to you, I can go home. And you can come too: the compass knows the way.
Thank you for the lavender, Marcel.
textes.Merci, Bastien ! T'es le meilleur porteu: Thanks, Bastien! You're the best carrier on the island, you are.
textes.Merci, Belle-Humeur. Je l'avais pas dema: Thanks, Belle-Humeur. Didn't ask for it.
textes.Merci, Bobor. Il était une fois un boula: Thank you, Bobor. Once upon a time, there was a round little baker…
textes.Merci, Brutus ! Et ton enclume, elle te: Thanks, Brutus! And your anvil, do you still like it?
Thank you, Bulle… I'll get in gently.
textes.Merci, Grumbald ! Tu connais la nouvelle: Thanks, Grumbald! Have you heard the news? … No, I can't tell!
textes.Merci, Grumbald. Ce soir, je raconte la: Thank you, Grumbald. Tonight, I'm telling the ash storm!
Thank you, Gwenola. Sorry. I mean, thank you.
Thank you, Isaac. The fish are waiting.
textes.Merci, Khéty. Pas de lotus, cette fois ?: Thank you, Khéty. No lotus this time?
textes.Merci, Madame Hurla… vous pouvez le chuc: Thank you, Madam Hurla… could you whisper it too?
textes.Merci, Mama ! Ce soir, je joue la gigue: Thanks, Mama! Tonight, I'm playing the whalers' jig!
textes.Merci, Mama. Et ton comptoir, il tient ?: Thanks, Mama. And your counter, is it holding?
textes.Merci, Mange-Clous. Mon géranium… pardon: Thank you, Mange-Clous. My geranium… sorry, my stomach thanks you.
textes.Merci, Marée. Elle a le goût de ta grand: Thank you, Marée. It tastes of your grandmother.
textes.Merci, Moloka ! Les chiots te disent mer: Thank you, Moloka! The puppies say thank you too!
textes.Merci, Moloka. Une dorade ! Superbe !: Thank you, Moloka. A sea bream! Superb!
Thank you, Nox. It's shining nicely tonight.
textes.Merci, Oscar. Pourquoi est-elle bleue ?: Thank you, Oscar. Why is it blue?
textes.Merci, Perlée. Et toi, qui t'arrose ?: Thank you, Perlée. And you, who waters you?
Thank you, Sage. I'll let it cool and reflect.
textes.Merci, Triton. Repose-toi un peu, veux-t: Thank you, Triton. Do rest a little, won't you?
textes.Merci, Xóchitl. Encore une page à peindr: Thank you, Xóchitl. Another page to paint.
textes.Merci, Yum Kab ! Xan aussi peut goûter ?: Thank you, Yum Kab! Can Xan have a taste too?
textes.Merci, Yum Kab. Et tes abeilles restent: Thank you, Yum Kab. And your bees stay at home.
textes.Merci, cher Bulle. Mes cornes ont besoin: Thank you, dear Bulle. My horns need to breathe.
textes.Merci, chère Mama ! Au nom de la cité !: Thank you, dear Mama! In the name of the city!
textes.Merci, merci ! Tenez, des croissants tou: Thank you, thank you! Here, some piping hot croissants. And from now on, at my place, you'll always get a little discount.
textes.Merci, mon ami ! Personne n'entre sans s: Thank you, my friend! Nobody comes in without saying hello!
textes.Merci, mon gars. Tiens, quelques pièces,: Thank you, lad. Here, a few coins, and a bag of seeds. Plant them wherever you like. But if one day they run away… it won't be my fault. It'll be the soil of Montjoie.
textes.Merci, mon garçon. On ira demain, doucem: Thank you, my boy. We'll go tomorrow, slowly.
textes.Merci, mon gros ! Tu as goûté mon mérou: Thanks, big guy! Did you taste my grouper?
textes.Merci, mon jaguar. Tu danses, ce soir ?: Thank you, my jaguar. Are you dancing tonight?
textes.Merci, parrain ! Et mon île, tu t'en sou: Thanks, godfather! And my island, do you remember it?
textes.Merci, petit. Ton père me la gardait aus: Thank you, lad. Your father kept it for me too.
textes.Merci, petite pousse. Tiens, une fleur d: Thank you, little sprout. Here, a nebula flower from my garden: it opens when you're happy. And two moon biscuits: Gloubi makes them with flour from my flowers. Don't tell him, he thinks it's a secret.
textes.Merci, {surnom}. Chez nous, un cadeau ré: Thank you, {surnom}. Here, a gift warms you twice: when you receive it, and when you think of it again.
Thank you. Have a good day. … Good night.
textes.Merci. C'est… curieux. Je lui trouverai: Thank you. It's… curious. I'll find a place for it.
Thank you. That one's very beautiful.
textes.Merci. Je me demande bien qui les a posé: Thank you. I do wonder who put them there.
textes.Merci. Je vais lui trouver une place dan: Thank you. I'll find a place for it among my things.
textes.Merci. Note-le aussi. Ça fait combien ?: Thank you. Write that down too. How many is that?
textes.Merci. Tu as bien mis les étiquettes ?: Thank you. Did you put the labels on properly?
textes.Merci. Vous ne pouvez pas savoir ce que: Thank you. You can't imagine what that feels like. The whole Academy laughs, and one single person says yes. That's the one you hear.
textes.Merci. À Tazira, on dit merci avec un ve: Thank you. In Tazira, we say thank you with a glass of tea. I owe you one.
Thank you. … And for the candle. Thank you.
Thank you. … The stones are calm.
textes.Merci… Je ne sais pas à quoi ça sert, ma: Thank you… I don't know what it's for, but it's pretty when it floats.
textes.Merci… c'est gentil. Je vais bien lui tr: Thanks… that's kind. I'm sure I'll find a spot for it.
textes.Merfi, Mange-Clous ! Et ta femoule, il e: Thankth, Mange-Clouth! And your themolina, ith there any left?
textes.Merveilleuse ! J'ai vendu trois boîtes à: Marvellous! I sold three boxes of nothing this morning. People love having nothing.
textes.Merveilleuse ! J'ai vendu un tapis volan: Marvellous! I sold a flying carpet this morning. It doesn't fly, but it sold.
textes.Merveilleuse ! J'ai vendu une boule à ne: Marvellous! I sold a snow globe to a penguin. No, to a tourist. But he looked like a penguin.
textes.Merveilleusement ! Le cristal chante de: Wonderfully! The crystal is singing again!
textes.Merveilleusement bien ! Le pain a levé,: Wonderfully well! The bread has risen, the bees are singing, and nobody has spilled my flour today.
textes.Merveilleux ! Mes oiseaux chantent, le s: Marvellous! My birds are singing, the sun is shining, and nobody's had a fight near my stall yet today!
textes.Merveilleux. Tu viens goûter la tisane,: Wonderful. Coming to taste the tea this evening?
So were my bees. For a thousand years.
My wings are too small to fly. As a child, I used to jump off the roof flapping my wings with all my might. I always landed in Mother Brasille's cabbages. She'd give me a herbal tea and send me home.

My wings are too small to fly. As a child, I'd jump off the roof flapping my wings as hard as I could. I always landed in Mother Brasille's cabbages. She'd give me a herbal tea and send me home. After ten times, she put a cushion under the roof. I never knew if it was for me or for her cabbages.
My friends are my other halves.
textes.Mes amoureux ! Une table pour deux ?: My lovebirds! A table for two?
textes.Mes bougainvilliers ont envahi le toit d: My bougainvilleas invaded Kiki's roof, then his chimney. He's never complained. He brings me empty coconuts, cut clean with a single stroke of the machete, and I turn them into pots. I've got thirty-two now. My customers love them. I've never thanked him. If I thank him, he'll play me one more song.
textes.Mes bras sont fatigués : j'ai moulu du m: My arms are tired: I've been grinding maize all day.
textes.Mes bâtons ? Je ne t'ai rien demandé. Pa: My sticks? I haven't asked you for anything. Not yet.
textes.Mes bâtons, tu y penses ? Il m'en faut {: My sticks, remember? I need {manque}. Without a handle, a shovel is just a flat rock.
textes.Mes cent théières renversées sortaient t: My hundred spilled teapots all came from his shop. The very first one, I kept: a bent spout, a dent in the side, a lid that doesn't sit right. I don't serve anyone from it. Except him. When he comes to the terrace, I bring out the dented one. He looks at it, grumbles, and says it's still beautiful. It's true.
textes.Mes chèvres grimpent partout : sur les r: My goats climb everywhere: on rocks, on roofs, on Bramm. Their milk makes the best cheese on the mountain.
textes.Mes confettis vont se loger dans les eng: My confetti gets lodged in Firmin's gears; that's the wind, not me! To make it up to him, I made him a confetti filter, out of fine wire mesh, with a ribbon. He turned it down: his engine needs nothing, apparently. That very evening, I saw him picking confetti out of his cogs with tweezers. Two hours.
textes.Mes coquillages ? Quels coquillages ? Ah: My shells? What shells? Ah… I haven't asked you for anything yet, I believe.
textes.Mes coquillages chantent ! Enfin, ils fo: My shells sing! Well, they go “whoooosh”. It's the sea singing, Faelar says.
textes.Mes coquillages nacrés, tu y penses ? Il: My pearly shells, have you remembered? I need {manque}. My collection is trembling with impatience.
textes.Mes coquillages « authentiques » ? Je le: My “authentic” shells? I pick them up myself, I paint them myself. They're authentically mine.
textes.Mes cornes sont polies chaque lundi par: My horns are polished every Monday by Monsieur Tiburce. The sheen of a horn, you see, is the reputation of a household. One dull horn, and the whole palace looks as if it has just got out of bed.
textes.Mes cornes vous remercient. Elles respir: My horns thank you. They're breathing better already.
textes.Mes couleurs ! Tu as volé mes couleurs !: My colours! You stole my colours!
textes.Mes dents ? Perdues dans une bagarre ave: My teeth? Lotht in a brawl with Belle-Humeur. Thirty yearth ago. He wath already grumpy. He'th never thmiled thinthe. Me neither, but for other reathonth.
textes.Mes deux bobines font un million de volt: My two coils make a million volts. The lab catches fire now and then, nothing serious. On stormy nights, I climb the tower to fly my kite, with a key at the end of the string; Héloïse disapproves. Three years ago, I lost the lighting contest to Professor Boum. Well, we both lost. And with Céleste, I'm studying the blue glow.
textes.Mes deux doigts ? Ah ! Un requin, en ple: My two fingers? Ah! A shark, on the open sea, that wanted to taste my soup. No: a giant lobster, in the hold of a warship. Or else the soup itself, a very lively soup… I keep changing the story, I know. The only truth, {surnom}: it was in a kitchen, and the soup was very good. Ho ho!
textes.Mes doigts ? Ils comptent les pièces plu: My fingers? They count coins faster than the eye can see. I don't cheat: I'm quick. That's not the same thing. Well, not exactly.
textes.Mes doigts sont plus précis. C'est prouv: My fingers are more precise. It's been proven.
textes.Mes dés pipés ? Ils roulent un peu… mieu: My loaded dice? They roll a bit… better. But at the Shark's Tooth, Sylvain spots them by the sound. Use them with amateurs. Or not at all. I just sell them, that's all.
textes.Mes filles comptent leurs brassées, elle: My girls count their armfuls too.
textes.Mes filles ont travaillé toute la semain: My girls worked all week for you.
My girls can hear you, Aëlwen.
textes.Mes fils te rattraperont. Comme d'habitu: My threads will catch you. As usual.
textes.Mes fleurs n'ont jamais été aussi belles: My flowers have never been so beautiful. You're a very kind human.
textes.Mes fleurs, Tochtli. Je le sais. Tu me d: My flowers, Tochtli. I know. You owe me half.
textes.Mes flèches de ton bois volent droit. Je: My arrows made from your wood fly true. I don't forget.
textes.Mes fruits ! Tout par terre !: My fruit! All over the ground!
textes.Mes gouttes ! Toutes ! Tiens, de la pous: My drops! All of them! Here, fairy dust, two pinches. And twenty coins. And… thank you. Really.
textes.Mes héros, c'est le professeur Boum, qui: My heroes are Professor Boum, who gave me his flying goggles. And Achille, the flying man: in the evening I wait for him with Adèle on the airfield bench. And the Colossus, who waved at me. Once I went for a ride in the Zéphyr and spat out of the window. The commander saw me. From the ground! With her binoculars! She sees everything, she does.
textes.Mes journées ? J'aide Mélisse à remplir: My days? I help Mélisse fill her bottles, I tell Brindille stories so she doesn't cry, and I invent spells in a notebook. There are three hundred and four! Number one is the frog spell for Grommelot. It has forty-two variations. Grommelot has tried them all. Not willingly.
textes.Mes lanternes s'éteignent tout le temps,: My lanterns keep going out down there. I'd need {manque} magma hearts: they glow for a hundred years. The magma elementals near the crater have one in their bellies… You see what I mean.
textes.Mes livres… Quatre. Pendant la grande te: My books… Four of them. During the great storm, they flew out the window. One is on the library roof. Another on the tallest of the Moonstones. The third on the ledge of a window in the Leaning Tower. The last in a big twisted oak in the Twisted Wood. Nobody can climb up there. But we can call them. I'll teach you.
My fireflies saw you going round in circles.
textes.Mes moteurs ne sont pas faits pour ça. J: My motors aren't made for this. I keep going anyway.
textes.Mes onze prototypes sont dans la vitrine: My eleven prototypes are in the Bazaar's window, lined up like sleeping soldiers, under a sign: “Almost Perpetual”. The first time I saw it, I wanted to buy them all back. The second time, I noticed she dusted them every morning. Now, I walk past with my head down. But I walk past every day.
textes.Mes os craquent comme du bois sec, mais: My bones creak like dry wood, but my heart is green. I'm fine.
textes.Mes pages ! (Elle les recoud dans le gri: My pages! (She sews them back into the grimoire with a needle that sews by itself… almost.) Let's see… “How to turn a bubble into a butterfly.” “How to find your glasses.” “Nettle soup.” Oh! The soup! I've been looking for it for years!
textes.Mes pages ! Les trois ! … Ce soir, au Pe: My pages! All three! … Tonight, at the Perroquet, I'll play “The Azure Waltz” for you. And that song… it will give you breath, you'll see.
textes.Mes palmes te vont ? Tu nages comme un v: Do my flippers fit? You swim like a real Atlantean now. Almost.
textes.Mes parents avaient une savonnerie, et n: My parents had a soap works, and we lived above it. You could smell lavender even in the soup. Me, I blew bubbles through a straw in the dishwater. One day, a bubble lasted a whole minute! I followed it down the street, then across the square, all the way to the railing on the cliff. It went off over the sea. I waved it goodbye.
textes.Mes parents cherchaient une île que pers: My parents were looking for an island no one had ever drawn. One morning, off the north-west, I saw a light in the mist, just one, spinning on itself. They couldn't see anything. I took the little rowboat and rowed towards it. It was the Great Crystal. That was forty years ago, and I've never made the journey back.
textes.Mes parents croient que je rentre la sem: My parents think I'm coming home next week, {surnom}. I've been writing that to them for eight weeks. “Next week.” Eight letters. I don't dare tell them I want to stay. To be a painter, not a notary. Every time I pick up my pen, I hear my father sigh from across the sea.
textes.Mes parents fabriquaient des violons. Su: My parents made violins. On the mainland. In the workshop, nobody talked: we listened to the wood. A violin that sounded off, my father heard it at the fifth plank. Me, at the first. He told me: “You've got the ear.” That's all he said to me. It was a lot.
textes.Mes parents sont artificiers. Ils vont d: My parents are fireworks makers. They go from island to island on their boat, the Rocket, setting off fireworks at festivals. I grew up between barrels of powder and rolls of coloured paper. I could make a red bouquet before I could tie my shoelaces. Actually, I still can't really tie my shoelaces. But the red bouquet, yes.
textes.Mes parents voulaient que je sois notair: My parents wanted me to be a notary. I paint notaries, sometimes. They pose well, they don't move.
textes.Mes parents étaient boulangers. On vivai: My parents were bakers. We lived at night, them and me. While the bread was rising, I'd climb onto a sack of flour and watch the sky through the bakehouse skylight. At six, I knew more stars than neighbours. The stars, at least, didn't ask me why I had flour in my hair.
textes.Mes parents étaient maraîchers, sur le c: My parents were market gardeners, on the mainland, among the leeks and cabbages. I was such a shy child I blushed when people asked me the time. So I never wore a watch. That way, I could say “I don't know” without lying. And blush anyway.
textes.Mes petits pieds préférés ! Trente-six e: My favourite little feet! Thirty-six and a half, I haven't forgotten. You haven't grown, at least?
textes.Mes pieds vont très bien. C'est le tambo: My feet are just fine. It's the drum that's running.
textes.Mes plus beaux champs de fleurs étaient: My finest flower fields were in the north, all the way to the sea. The winter the brambles came, a hundred years ago, I lost them in a single night. By morning there was nothing left but black thorns and a smell of burnt sugar. Since then my flowers grow in three pots outside my door. So yes, my nectar is expensive. So are flowers.
textes.Mes plus belles unes ? « Le maire de Por: My finest front pages? “Mayor of Port-Azur stuck in the sky”, with his whole poem, rhymes included. “Lighting contest: jury covered in soot”. “Professor Boum's ninth roof lands on the Bielle”. And “Achille Plumevent still in flight”, eight days running. Tomorrow, nine. I never tire of it. Neither do the readers. Adèle does.
textes.Mes pots sont prêts à rester sur l'étagè: My pots are ready to stay on the shelf, Nenetl.
textes.Mes premiers flacons étaient tout tordus: My first bottles were all crooked: I melted the crystal shards too close to the waterfall, and they ran like honey. At the Cousins' Festival, when the sky fairies came down to visit us, I sold the lot anyway. My first buyer was Zéphyr. He drank the bottle in one gulp and said “more”.
My prices are as steady as the dome.
textes.Mes prix sont justes. Les elfes ne mente: My prices are fair. Elves never lie about prices.
textes.Mes robots sont simples, solides, et ils: My robots are simple, sturdy, and they don't argue. Unlike engineers.
textes.Mes ruches sont des troncs creux, couché: My hives are hollow logs, lying under a roof of palm leaves. We open them at the end, take a little honey, never all of it. The bees trust us.
textes.Mes sujets m'ont tout dit : tu as aidé m: My subjects told me everything: you helped my guard, my forge, my kitchens, my mines. A king rewards. Here: three gold coins from the Royal Forge. And the title of friend of Forgefer. The title is free. The gold isn't.
textes.Mes tuyaux ! Ne touche pas à mes tuyaux: My pipes! Don't touch my pipes!
textes.Mes yeux ne voient plus loin. Alors Gasp: My eyes can't see far any more. So Gaspard shows me. He points: a sail, a dolphin, the smoke of Carène. One day he drew on his slate the whole coast he can see from his lookout, with the caves and the reefs. I told him the name of every rock. He wrote them underneath, very small.
textes.Mes yeux vont très bien, {surnom}. Une n: My eyes are perfectly fine, {surnom}. One night, above Stoneheart, every compass on the Zéphyr started spinning. All at the same time. Three hours lost in the fog, and beneath the gondola, a blue glow. Since then, I'm afraid to fly. I lied to everyone. I hate compasses that lie. People who lie, I understand a little better.
textes.Mes {manque} bâtons ? Une flèche tordue,: My {manque} sticks? A crooked arrow is a lost arrow.
textes.Mes {manque} champignons de braise, {sur: My {manque} ember mushrooms, {surnom}! Look for the little red glows in the ash, near the fumaroles.
textes.Mes {manque} minerais, {surnom} ? Les pi: My {manque} ores, {surnom}? The rust-veined stones, on the mountainside.
textes.Mes {manque} perles… La fête approche. E: My {manque} pearls… The festival is getting close. Well, in ten years. But still.
textes.Mes {manque} plumes, {surnom} ? Regarde: My {manque} feathers, {surnom}? Look under the rocks where the ravens land.
textes.Mes {manque} rayons de miel, tu y penses: My {manque} honeycombs, have you thought about them? My oven brings it up every day.
textes.Mes {manque} rayons de miel, {surnom} ?: My {manque} honeycombs, {surnom}? On your island, in the hollow trees.
textes.Mes {manque} éclats. J'attends. J'ai l'h: My {manque} shards. I'm waiting. I'm used to waiting.
textes.Mes éclats de cristal ? Je les fais fond: My crystal shards? I melt them in the waterfall light to make bottles. I'll buy them from you if you find any.
textes.Mes élèves n'arrivaient pas à retenir l': My pupils couldn't remember the order of the suns. Nenetl made up a song, on her slit drum: “Jaguar! Wind! Rain of fire! Water!” Tok, tak, tok, tak. The next day, the whole class was singing it. Even Pilli, in his sleep. The high priest heard it. He frowned. Then he tapped his foot. Once.
textes.Mes épices viennent par les caravanes du: My spices come with the desert caravans, who buy them from other caravans, who buy them from people nobody's ever seen. That saffron has travelled more than you have.
textes.Mesdames et messieurs ! Port-Azur reconn: Ladies and gentlemen! Port-Azur today honours one of its own! Here is the key to the town. From now on, all our shopkeepers will give you a discount, and you'll always have a seat on our terraces. And in our hearts. Django, music!
textes.Messager du Soleil et de la Pluie: Messenger of the Sun and the Rain
textes.Mets des gants, cette fois. Et appuie mo: Wear gloves this time. And press less.
textes.Mets-le au frais. Et toi, assieds-toi et: Put it somewhere cool. And you, sit down and eat.
textes.Mets-toi bien en face du bloc pour le po: Stand squarely in front of the block to push it.
textes.Mettre au tapis les trois champions du p: Knock down the three harbour champions, with fists and no blades: Gros-Louis (Requin Borgne), the Silent One (Veuve Écarlate), Belle-Humeur (Morue Enragée) — you can offer them a fair duel
textes.Miaou. Miaou ? Miaaaou. Cette maison app: Meow. Meow? Meeeow. This house obviously belongs to the cats.
textes.Midi ! Le soleil est tout en haut. L'omb: Noon! The sun is right at the top. The shadows are tiny.
textes.Mieux. Encore un « hop » de moins, et je: Better. One less “hop” and I'll give you a hug.
textes.Mieux. Mais ton pain, toujours trop de m: Better. But your bread, still too much honey.
A thousand! Really? You've got good stamina. Or a good imagination. Both make astronomers. Come back and see me, I have tables to copy.
textes.Mille ans que je n'avais pas parlé !: A thousand years since I last spoke!
One thousand two hundred and twelve teaspoons. This one tasted the king's soup. This one stirred a dragon's tea. Well, that's what I was told.
textes.Mille douze ! Il y en a une nouvelle !: One thousand and twelve! There's a new one!
textes.Mille et une histoires, et un cercle qui: A thousand and one stories, and a circle that changes every evening. Lalla Fatima, in the front row, correcting me. Lhoucine and his guembri, taking the pauses for me. Nourredine's lantern, casting stars on the faces. Little Tibo, my keeper of the djinn. And the pirates, at the back, who just happen to be passing. Every evening, just happening. Chance is very faithful, in Tazira.
textes.Mille histoires, Corentin ? Moi, mille e: A thousand stories, Corentin? I have a thousand and one.
textes.Mille sabords… Un jour, je viendrai véri: Blistering barnacles… One day, I'll come and check.
textes.Milord ! J'aurai peut-être une plume de: Milord! I might have a flying-fish feather for you.
Milord, I still don't have change.
Milord. My moustache stays where it is.
textes.Mince ! Il est maigre comme un balai, mo: Drat! He's thin as a rake, my poor grimoire! I opened the window to let out a little draught spell, and it left with three pages! The most important ones! Well, I think so: I can't remember what was on them. That's why they're important. They flew off over the town. Find them for me, dearie. They glow a little. They're surely magic.
textes.Minos enroule sa queue autour de lui, un: Minos coils his tail around himself, once, twice, three times… “WRONG! Go back to the start of the hall, and think.” (Ombreline, the librarian, knows all the answers.)
textes.Mio, pourquoi Zéro ne fait-il que « bip: Mio, why does Zéro only ever say "beep"?
textes.Miou aime bien aller sur le plateau, che: Miou likes going up to the plateau, where the dead are, near the square tombs. He says it's quiet. Well, he doesn't say anything, he's a cat.
textes.Miou ronronne dans tes bras. Ramène-le à: Miou purrs in your arms. Take him back to Nebet, in Per-Hâpy!
textes.Miou, le chat roux à l'oreille tordue de: Miou, little Nebet's ginger cat with the crooked ear, has been missing for three days. Khéty says cats love the coolness of the tombs, up on the plateau of Ra.
textes.Mirabelle ! Elle fait quoi, la rose ?: Mirabelle! What does the pink one do?
textes.Mirabelle ! Ma cave sent la framboise br: Mirabelle! My cellar smells of burnt raspberry.
textes.Mirabelle ! Une potion ratée, la plus lé: Mirabelle! A botched potion, the lightest one!
textes.Mirabelle a plus de talent dans le petit: Mirabelle has more talent in her little finger than I had in both hands at her age. She botches her potions, yes. She botches them in colour. And she's turned my cellar into a battlefield.
textes.Mirabelle dit que je vais entrer dans un: Mirabelle says I'll walk into a book and disappear. That would be nice, if it's a good book.
textes.Mirabelle dit que ses potions ratées son: Mirabelle says her failed potions are art potions. Once, I drank one. My ears were green for a whole day.
textes.Mirabelle fait bouillir des choses sous: Mirabelle boils things under her bed. It smells of raspberry, or of socks. She talks for two, which suits me. She's my friend. I think I'm hers.
textes.Mirabelle rate ses potions avec un talen: Mirabelle botches her potions with crazy talent. She has a sparkle in her eye and fingers stained every colour. I buy a botched potion from her every week. To encourage the arts!
Mirabelle sells potions on the square. Failed potions. She says it's art. I won't say no.
textes.Mirabelle, elle m'a donné des oreilles v: Mirabelle gave me green ears! OK, she didn't give them to me, I drank them. But still. She's funny. I'm never tasting her potions again. Except the blackberry juice one.
textes.Miriel cueille les fleurs de mes abeille: Miriel picks my bees' flowers before they've finished foraging them. She says flowers belong to no one. They belong to whoever feeds on them.
textes.Miriel m'a apporté un jour une fleur de: Once, Miriel brought me a moonflower picked at high noon. “It was open, I swear!” A moonflower picked in the sun cures nothing. We argued about the price for an hour. Then we put it in a glass of water and had tea beside it.
textes.Miriel me cueille les fleurs de lune. El: Miriel picks moonflowers for me. She sells them dear, I pay a fair price. We never agree on the difference. She's a good mother, and a tough trader.
textes.Miriel sait où pousse chaque fleur de l': Miriel knows where every flower on the island grows. I know where every path goes. Between the two of us, we never get lost. Well, I do. But she always finds me.
Miriel, I'm going for a little stroll.
textes.Miriel. Tu as cueilli le pré de lavande: Miriel. Did you pick the lavender meadow?
textes.Miser %d pièces… avec tes dés pipés: Bet %d coins… with your loaded dice
textes.Mistral ! Ma barque te salue. Elle a enc: Mistral! My boat says hello. Her back still aches.
textes.Mistral ? Le seul client de l'île qui pa: Mistral? The only customer on the island who pays cash without haggling. Shame he makes so much noise with what he buys from me.
textes.Mistral ? Le seul homme de l'île qui fas: Mistral? The only man on the island who makes more noise than I do. I admire him, and I sleep with cotton wool in my ears.
textes.Mistral a promis une teuf sous l'eau, à: Mistral promised an underwater party, in Atlantis. I don't know how he's going to manage the speakers.
textes.Mistral est merveilleux, mais il parle d: Mistral is wonderful, but he talks about Atlantis like it's the next beach over. “Going this week?” He doesn't know what's down there. I know a little.
textes.Mistral fait trembler la baie toutes les: Mistral makes the bay shake every night. I ought to complain. But his beats sound like those of the Mother Tree, when you press your ear to the bark.
textes.Mistral joue pour nous, pour la mer et p: Mistral plays for us, for the sea and for the fairies, even if he didn't know it at first. He's been waiting for my mural for two years without ever rushing me. He's the most patient of winds.
textes.Mistral mixait sur la pointe des pieds,: Mistral used to mix on tiptoe — his decks were too high for him. My calves hurt just watching him. I took a rope, measured his arms while he played, and the next day he had a stage. It creaks a bit on the offbeat. I tell him it's on purpose. It almost is.
textes.Mistral, c'est la raison pour laquelle j: Mistral is the reason I'm still here. One single track, at sunrise, and I missed my boat. I'll never forgive him. I adore him.
textes.Mistral, c'est le cœur de la teuf. Il ou: Mistral is the heart of the party. He forgets to drink, he forgets to sleep, he even forgot his decks were too high. Me, I don't forget. That's why I'm here.
textes.Mistral, comme le vent. J'ai monté ce mu: Mistral, like the wind. I built this sound wall piece by piece, with Barnabé lending me his rowing boat to carry it all.
textes.Mistral, le vent tourne vers les nuages,: Mistral, the wind's turning towards the clouds tonight.
textes.Mistral, ton chant de baleine… c'est pre: Mistral, your whale song… it's almost right.
textes.Mistral. … Le meilleur. Il compose, je r: Mistral. … The best. He composes, I tune. He talks, I nod. It's worked like that for six years. It'll keep working.
textes.Mistral… Ce soir, tu pourrais jouer un p: Mistral… Tonight, could you play a little less loudly?
textes.Misère. Elle a appris ça où, cette petit: Good grief. Where did she learn that, this girl?
textes.Misère… Elle était bonne, au moins ?: Oh, misery… Was it good, at least?
textes.Mixtli ! Encore en train d'attendre le b: Mixtli! Still waiting for the right day?
textes.Mixtli ! Je peux porter ton bouclier ?: Mixtli! Can I carry your shield?
textes.Mixtli dit que je lui ai vendu une fauss: Mixtli says I sold him a fake quetzal feather. It was a test. I had to check he could recognise a real one.
textes.Mixtli est brave, fort et rapide. Il est: Mixtli is brave, strong and fast. He's also as proud as a turkey on a feast day. I told him about Tecciztécatl, the proud god. He found the story very beautiful. He didn't understand it.
textes.Mixtli est guerrier-jaguar : fort, fier,: Mixtli is a jaguar warrior: strong, proud, and very serious. Even when he dances. Especially when he dances. He has two left feet. I adore him. The way you adore a show, of course.
textes.Mixtli est mon cousin. Il est fort, fier: Mixtli is my cousin. He's strong, proud, and he can't haggle. He captured me in training, in front of everyone. I sold him a fake feather. We're even. Almost.
textes.Mixtli m'a promis de chasser les jaguars: Mixtli promised me he'd hunt the jaguars that took one of my animals. That's kind. He's as proud as a turkey and he falls into the canals. But he has a good heart. He hides it under his jaguar skin.
textes.Mixtli m'a prêté son bouclier. Il était: Mixtli lent me his shield. It was so big I couldn't see anything! I shouted: “I'm invincible!” and stepped forward. I fell into a basket of chillies, at the market. The chillies stung my eyes. Mixtli said a warrior cries too, sometimes. Especially because of chillies.
textes.Mixtli porte une peau de jaguar et veut: Mixtli wears a jaguar skin and wants to hunt the real ones, on the Smoking Mountain. You don't hunt the jaguar to make a name for yourself. I told him. He didn't listen.
textes.Mixtli, c'est le guerrier-jaguar ! Il a: Mixtli is the jaguar warrior! He has a real jaguar skin, a shield and a weapon made of black stone. Tlaco barks at him. Me, I want to be like him. With a dog as well.
textes.Mixtli, notre guerrier-jaguar, dit qu'il: Mixtli, our jaguar warrior, says he has seen real jaguars on the slopes of the Smoking Mountain. He wants to go and face them. A jaguar warrior against jaguars… The gods do love a joke.
textes.Mixtli. Guerrier-jaguar d'Aztlán. Je por: Mixtli. Jaguar warrior of Aztlán. I wear the jaguar's skin because I fight like it: fast, and in the shadows. You look like you can fight. We'll see.
textes.Mixtli. L'orgueil est un mauvais bouclie: Mixtli. Pride is a poor shield.
textes.Mixtli. Les jaguars sont chez eux, là-ha: Mixtli. The jaguars are at home, up there.
textes.Mmh ? Pardon, je bronzais. Sylvie, la fe: Mmh? Sorry, I was sunbathing. Sylvie, Gérard's wife. Are you local?
textes.Mmh… pas maintenant… je suis occupé… à d: Mmh… not now… I'm busy… sleeping…
textes.Mmmh… une tarte… grande comme la maison…: Mmmh… a pie… as big as the house…
textes.Moaïs : la doyenne et la légende: Moai: the elder and the legend
textes.Moaïs : le petit qui n'a jamais vu la me: Moai: the little one who has never seen the sea
textes.Mochi ! Tu as de la farine jusqu'aux ore: Mochi! You've got flour up to your ears.
textes.Mochi dit que c'est un dragon-poisson, s: Mochi says it's a dragon-fish under the pool. Gland says it's a dragon. I say it's the King of the Pools, and he's got a crown.
textes.Mochi m'a demandé si son papa était dans: Mochi asked me if her papa was among the stars. I said I hadn't finished counting. That same evening, she wanted to name star four thousand two hundred and thirteen. She called it “Cerfeuil”. I wrote it down like that in my journal, in ink, not pencil. Since then, when I reach thirteen, I say good evening.
textes.Mochi monte l'escalier avec moi au crépu: Mochi climbs the stairs with me at dusk, very slowly, asking a thousand questions. A thousand and twenty-three, yesterday. She always has cake somewhere on her.
textes.Mochi, c'est ma copine, même si nos mama: Mochi's my friend, even though our mums are cross with each other over some sardine-and-carrot business. She talks nonsense about the dragon-fish. But she gives me her sardines.
textes.Mochi, c'est une pipelette. Elle parle p: Mochi's a chatterbox. She talks almost as much as me, it's very annoying. She says “dragon-fish”. She tells on me. But she helps me look for my hazelnuts. And she eats them.
textes.Mode PC classique — F11 plein écran • F6: Classic PC mode — F11 full screen • F6 ultra sharpness (GPU) • no headset needed.
textes.Mode testeur : ce lieu n'existe pas dans: Tester mode: this place doesn't exist in this version.
textes.Mode testeur : l'Île Pixelithique n'est: Tester mode: Pixelithic Island isn't here.
textes.Mode testeur : l'Île aux Moaïs n'est pas: Tester mode: Moai Island isn't here.
textes.Mode testeur : pas de maison à visiter i: Tester mode: no house to visit here.
textes.Moi ? Charpentier et forgeron de la Moue: Me? Carpenter and blacksmith of the Stubborn Seagull, the finest three-master in the kingdom. Until the rock.
textes.Moi ? Comme un coquillage à marée haute: Me? Like a shell at high tide: full of water and delighted about it!
textes.Moi ? Euh… Un verre pour un collègue, al: Me? Er… A drink for a colleague, then?
textes.Moi ? J'ai trois cent douze ans. C'est j: Me? I'm three hundred and twelve years old. That's young, where I come from. My mother says I'm “still very green”.
textes.Moi ? Jamais de la vie. Qu'est-ce que tu: Me? Never in my life. What did you find?
textes.Moi ? Jamais. Je réfléchissais très fort: Me? Never. I was thinking very hard.
Me? Never. Back to your carpets.
Me? I haven't the faintest idea.
textes.Moi ? Je ne tapote pas. (Tap-tap-tap, bo: Me? I don't tap. (Tap-tap-tap, boom-tchak.) ... Well. All right. I tap. I always have. On everything. You know, every evening, I listen to the Bilge Rats from behind the Hall's door. I know all the songs. All the drum parts. And every night, the stand-in drummer gets it wrong, and in my head, I play it right. But I don't have any sticks. Dad would never have allowed it. And besides... I'm a Lisse. They'll never want a Lisse on their stage. (He looks at your hands.) You... you have drumsticks, don't you? The ones from the Great Boucan?
textes.Moi ? Je ne vois rien d'ici. À peine tou: Me? I can't see a thing from up here. Barely the whole square.
