textes.Montre tes mains. … Tu as déjà construit: Show me your hands. … Have you ever built anything, with those hands?
textes.Montre-la à Ilyria, elle en fera une bro: Show it to Ilyria, she'll make an embroidery from it.
textes.Montre-moi ta lame. Tiens-la en main, qu: Show me your blade. Hold it in your hand, so I can see how you hold it.
textes.Montrer la fresque du tombeau à Céleste: Show the tomb's fresco to Céleste Lunette, the astronomer of Cliquetis (at her observatory)
textes.Montrer le pot d'orange à Achille (au pi: Show the pot of orange to Achille (at the foot of the waterfall in the daytime, near the Palette in the evening), then pour it into the Palette
textes.Montrer le pot de bleu à Basile (au bord: Show the pot of blue to Basile (by the pond in the daytime, on the Brush Oak terrace at noon), then pour it into the Palette
textes.Montrer le pot de jaune à Lili (sur la p: Show the pot of yellow to Lili (on the beach in the daytime, at the swing in the evening), then pour it into the Palette
textes.Montrer le pot de rouge à Capucine (aux: Show the pot of red to Capucine (in the White Meadows in the daytime, on the Blotter Oak terrace at noon and in the evening), then pour it into the Palette
textes.Montrer le pot de vert à Rosalie (à la l: Show the pot of green to Rosalie (at the edge of the wood in the daytime, on the Eraser Oak terrace at noon), then pour it into the Palette
textes.Montrer le pot de violet à Gaspard (au B: Show the pot of purple to Gaspard (at the Lookout in the daytime), then pour it into the Palette
textes.Montrer les cinq champignons à Mère Mori: Show the five mushrooms to Mère Morille (at her caravan, in the middle of the Spore Cathedral)
textes.Montrer les trois sceaux à la Dame de Pr: Show the three seals to the Lady of the Prow, the Léviathan's figurehead (right at the front of the deck, near the telescope)
textes.Montrer les étoiles de mer à Kevin, au p: Show the starfish to Kevin, at the lifeguard post
textes.Montrez voir, milord… Ah ! Ça, c'est le: Let's have a look, milord… Ah! That there is a mermaid's thimble.
textes.Morgane, je l'ai fait sauter sur mes gen: Morgane, I bounced her on my knees, and now she frowns at me. An admiral without a fleet, with the heart of a whole fleet. I laugh at her title, never at her.
textes.Mouillée. Comme toujours. C'est le métie: Wet. As always. Comes with the job.
textes.Moulay Brahim fixe le prix de la sardine: Moulay Brahim sets the price of sardines, I sing it. A great man. Too serious. He's never understood that a price has to ring.
textes.Moulay Brahim règle les disputes de tout: Moulay Brahim settles the disputes of the whole port. On my terrace, he cheats at draughts. I've let him for twenty years. An amin has the right to win somewhere.
textes.Moulay Brahim se méfie des pirates. Moi,: Moulay Brahim doesn't trust the pirates. Me, I don't trust their cook. He tasted my tea and said: “Not salty enough.”
textes.Moulay Brahim, l'amin. Il fixe le prix d: Moulay Brahim, the amin. He sets the price of sardines. I set the gull tax. He says he's the one who sets taxes. We don't agree, but we eat together.
textes.Moulay Brahim. Bon amin. Il écoute. Avan: Moulay Brahim. Good amin. He listens. We used to fish side by side. Twenty years. He talked, I fished. It worked.
textes.Mousse ! Ton lapin, il trouve son terrie: Cabin boy! Is your rabbit finding its hole?
Cabin boy at thirteen, gunner at twenty. I served one month under Lou the Terrible, the most fearsome pirate of the day. I gave her some cheek, very good cheek, and she threw me overboard. I swam back. At thirty-five, I bought an old galleon and named her the Murène Noire, in memory of my grandfather's Murène. Blistering barnacles, what a day.
textes.Mousse, c'est déjà bien. Je sais sonner,: Cabin boy's already good. I can ring, scrub and tie knots. Mostly scrub. I'm the best scrubber on the whole island, ask anyone.
textes.Mousse, puis pêcheur, puis charpentier :: Cabin boy, then fisherman, then carpenter: I tried everything, and I was average at all of it. The evening my grandfather died, the tavern stayed silent. Gwenola's mother put a mug in my hand and said: “You tell it.” I told the shipwreck. I've never stopped.
textes.Mousse. Qu'est-ce que tu vois, à l'horiz: Cabin boy. What do you see on the horizon?
textes.Moustache attend que le monde écrive, mo: Moustache waits for the world to write, I read what it has written. A fisherman and a tracker, it's the same trade. I don't believe in his King. But I love his patience.
textes.Moustache dit qu'il a vu un poisson d'or: Moustache says he saw a golden fish in the great pool. Big as a rabbit. He calls it “the King of the Pools”. He's never caught it. Maybe he's never seen it.
textes.Moustache m'a appris un nœud de pêcheur,: Moustache taught me a fisherman's knot, with the string from his rod. A real one! It tightens all by itself when you pull. Now I tie it everywhere: on my hazelnut bags, on Mochi's ribbon, on Pomme-de-Pin's laces. Moustache says I learn too well. That's a compliment, right?
textes.Moustache, c'est le pêcheur du ponton. I: Moustache is the fisherman on the jetty. He says that under the big pond lives the Pond King, and that he grows every time you talk about him. So I talk about him all the time, to see!
textes.Mrrr ! Toi. Tu sens le poisson. C'est un: Mrrr! You. You smell of fish. That's a compliment.
textes.Mrrr. Aujourd'hui, j'élève Myrtille, gri: Mrrr. These days, I'm raising Myrtille, grey like her father, who climbs everywhere except by the stairs. I keep an eye on Dad, who catches more colds than kings. I spoil my little sister Éclair. And I don't speak to Trèfle, the baker, any more. Well, I say hello: our daughters make us. It's tiring, being cross. Almost as tiring as making up.
textes.Mrrr. J'ai grandi sur le ponton de mon p: Mrrr. I grew up on my father's jetty, among the rods and buckets. He'd say “watch the float”, so I'd watch the float, and doze off in the sun. As a kitten, I believed in the Pond King, even stronger than Dad did. I'd save sardines for him. At twelve, I stopped believing. And started eating them myself. You grow up.
textes.Mrrr. Le rhume aussi est là, papa. Rentr: Mrrr. So is your cold, Dad. Come home.
Mrrr. Myrtille, come down from there.
Mrrr. Your skewer. The biggest one.
textes.Mrrr. Tant mieux pour toi. Tu me raconte: Mrrr. Good for you. Then you'll tell me what it's like. Slowly. With details. And without the waves.
Mrrr. You've got your letter-day face on.
textes.Mrrrou ! Course jusqu'au premier planche: Mrrrou! Race you to the first platform?
textes.Mrrrou ! J'ai sept ans. J'habite à la pê: Mrrrow! I'm seven. I live at the fishery with Mummy Caramel and Grandpa Moustache. My papa is Ardoise. He fishes in the sea, at Tazira, on a blue boat, and he sends letters that smell of salt. I'm grey like him, look! Mummy says I've got his eyes. Grandpa says I've got his tail. I say it's MY tail.
textes.Mrrrou ! T'as vu le Roi des mares ? Non: Mrrrow! Have you seen the King of the Pools? No? I nearly did.
textes.Mrrrou ! Toi qui viens de la mer… tu sai: Mrrrow! You come from the sea… can you swim?
textes.Mrrrou ! Trop fort ! Alors si le Roi des: Mrrrow! So cool! So if the Pond King comes by, you're the one who dives. I'll watch. I watch super well.
textes.Mrrrou ! Tu sens bizarre. Pas mauvais. B: Mrrrow! You smell funny. Not bad. Funny. I'm Myrtille. My grandpa is Moustache. He's looking for the King of the Pools. So am I, but I look better.
textes.Mrrr… Bonjour. Caramel, poissonnière. Po: Mrrr… Hello. Caramel, fishmonger. Pool fish in the morning, grilled skewers in the afternoon. And no, I don't taste the goods. Not much.
textes.Mrrr… Toi qui viens de la mer : la mer,: Mrrr… You come from the sea: doesn't it scare you, the sea?
textes.Mrrr… Tout le monde croit que je suis re: Mrrr… Everyone thinks I stayed for Dad. Or for Myrtille. No, {surnom}. I'm scared of the sea. I've never seen it, and I'm scared of it anyway. All that blue, with no edge. I'm ashamed. So when I write back to Ardoise, I send fish recipes. Seven recipes per letter. He must think all I think about is food.
textes.Mustapha grille des sardines. Quelle hor: Mustapha grills sardines. What a horror, the smell! But he puts my cumin on them, and it's the only well-used cumin in Tazira. So I forgive him. Half-way.
textes.Mustapha me fait toujours des sardines s: Mustapha always makes me special sardines, just for me. He puts them on the left corner of the grill: the captains' corner. Amine says they're the same as the others. Amine talks nonsense. Mine are better, they have to be, 'cause they're in the captains' corner.
textes.Mustapha me paie en sardines pour taper: Mustapha pays me in sardines to drum on his table. The best contract in Tazira. He says that with my rhythm, the customers eat faster. Me, I eat more slowly, on purpose.
textes.Mustapha nourrit tout le port, et les mo: Mustapha feeds the whole port, and the seagulls too. He calls it the seagull tax. I remind him that I'm the one who sets the taxes. He grills me a sardine, and I forget.
textes.Mustapha retourne les sardines sans rega: Mustapha turns the sardines without looking, in rhythm: boom, he turns, ta-ka, he salts. One day I sped up to catch him out. He kept up. Faster still. He kept up. By the end, the sardines were flying over the grill. He caught them all. Except one, which left with a gull. “The tax,” he said.
textes.Mustapha, c'est mon frère de quai. Mes c: Mustapha is my quay brother. My shouting brings him customers, his smell gives me my voice. Good business: nobody pays, and everybody eats.
textes.Mustapha, il fait les meilleurs oiseaux: Mustapha makes the best seabirds in the world. They're not fish, they're birds that fly underwater. I pretend to believe him. He pretends I believe him.
textes.Mustapha, un grand du grill ! Il m'a don: Mustapha, a master of the grill! He gave me his recipe, just like that, cook to cook. I follow it to the letter. My sardines aren't like his yet, but they're getting there.
textes.My dear Edmond ! Avez-vous réfléchi ?: My dear Edmond! Have you thought it over?
textes.My dear Fernand ! Et ce dragon, il morda: My dear Fernand! And that dragon, did it bite?
textes.My dear friend ! Quelles merveilles aujo: My dear friend! What marvels have you got today?
textes.Myrtille grimpe presque aussi bien qu'un: Myrtille climbs almost as well as a squirrel! It's brilliant, and I tell her all the time. She gets cross. I don't get why. And she believes in a king with a crown. Total nonsense.
textes.Myrtille, c'est ma copine. Elle croit au: Myrtille's my friend. She believes in the Pond King, with a crown. It's almost true. Our mummies are cross with each other, but we don't care. I give her my sardines, yuck, and she eats my cake.
Mâchefer? A big bear who says “hm”. He's respected me since I threw him out by the ear. Me, I'm wary. A first mate counting the days wants a ship.
Mâchefer? A pirate who used to be a blacksmith. He watches me hammer every day, like a cat watches a fish. He says nothing. He doesn't touch anything any more. It's better that way.
textes.Mâchefer, mon second. Il a vu mourir tro: Mâchefer, my first mate. He's seen three captains die, and he looks at me as if he were taking my measurements for the fourth coffin. An excellent first mate. I sleep with my sabre.
textes.Mâchefer, parce que j'ai été forgeron av: Mâchefer, “Clinker”, because I was a blacksmith before I was a pirate. I bend iron bars. And noses.
textes.Mère Averse, Mamie Tournesol vous envoie: Mother Downpour, Granny Sunflower sends you these sunflowers.
textes.Mère Brasille ! Vous n'auriez pas vu Sui: Mother Brasille! You haven't seen Suie, have you?
textes.Mère Brasille dit qu'elle déteste mes ch: Mother Brasille says she hates my pups. She made me move out with her broom. But I know one of my pups sleeps in her watering can every afternoon. She has a garden's heart: prickly outside, tender inside.

Mother Brasille says she hates my puppies. And yet Suie sleeps in her watering can every afternoon, and she never chases him out. I saw her sing him a lullaby. She denied it. She blushed. On ash-coloured skin, it really shows.
textes.Mère Brasille m'a ramassé cent fois dans: Mother Brasille picked me up out of her cabbages a hundred times when I was little and thought I could fly. Now, at dawn, she gives me mint to help me sleep. She's a bit like my morning grandmother.
textes.Mère Brasille, la jardinière des Jardins: Mère Brasille, the gardener of the Ash Gardens, would like five ember flowers for her flowerbeds. They only grow on the slopes of the Great Blaze.
textes.Mère Gwenola est la seule personne de Ca: Mother Gwenola is the only person in Carène who still calls me by my first name. She makes me eat by force. If she were gone, Carène would go out along with her stove.
textes.Mère Gwenola s'était fait vendre par des: Mother Gwenola had been sold red sand by some caravan traders, passed off as chilli. I took the sack to Aïcha. She tasted it, spat it out, swore in three languages, and gave me a real sack of chilli, free, “for the honour of spices”. Gwenola put some in the soup. Fañch is still crying.
textes.Mère Gwenola, c'est la seule personne de: Mother Gwenola is the only person in Carène I'm scared of. She let me touch her stove, once. It's the greatest honour of my life as a smith.
textes.Mère Morille, la sage de la Cathédrale d: Mother Morille, the wise woman of the Spore Cathedral, wants to teach you about the five fairy mushrooms that grow in the old gasholder: the Spring-Bolete, the Moonling, the Chatterbox, the Rainbow and the Little-Giant. They must be picked and shown to her. These are storybook mushrooms: in real life, you never eat a mushroom you don't know.
textes.Mère Morille, quels sont ces champignons: Mère Morille, what are these glowing mushrooms?
textes.Mère Sauge ! Vous avez de la mélisse pou: Mère Sauge! Do you have some lemon balm for me?
textes.Mère Sauge dit que je sale trop ma soupe: Mother Sage says I put too much salt in my soup. She always has two extra helpings. I didn't say a word. I just smile.
textes.Mère Sauge m'a soigné plus de bosses que: Mother Sage has treated more of my bumps than I have hairs. She never says “you again?”. She says “Show me.” She's the kindest person on the island. With Pip. And Gérard.
textes.Mère Sauge m'apprendra le sort de soin s: Mère Sauge will teach me the healing spell if I bring her three mushrooms from the Twisted Wood. Then I'll have to heal the injured owl that lives near Agathe's caravan.
textes.Mère Sauge me vend ses herbes, mais elle: Mère Sauge sells me her herbs, but she sorts them first: what heals on one side, what goes boom on the other. I'm only allowed the second pile. It's vexing, and rather fair.
textes.Mère Sauge soigne mes brûlures depuis qu: Mother Sage has been treating my burns since I was eight. She never lectures me. She looks at me. That's worse. And her honey ointment smells nice, I admit.
textes.Mère-Lune ? Ma plus vieille amie, et la: Mother Moon? My oldest friend, and the most beautiful thing that ever happened to Ramure. She's been falling asleep during my stories for seventy years. I take it as a compliment.
textes.Mère-Lune dit que la lune parle aux pist: Mère-Lune says the moon speaks to trackers. That it spoke to her, at the edge of the world. I've been listening to it since I was eight, {surnom}. Every night. It's never said anything to me. Not a word. I read tracks, but I can't hear the moon. One day, someone will have to come after Mère-Lune. I'm not sure it's me. Don't tell her.
textes.Mère-Lune est la seule encore là à avoir: Mother Moon is the only one still here who tasted my grandmother's cake. Every evening, I take her a slice and hold my breath. Every evening, she says “almost”.
textes.Mère-Lune m'a appris à pister. Elle disa: Mother Moon taught me to track. She used to say: one track is a sentence. Several tracks are a story. Lots and lots of tracks is Bedaine doing his shopping.
textes.Mère-Lune m'a tout appris. À lire une tr: Mère-Lune taught me everything. How to read a track, how to wait, how to keep quiet. She listens to everything I report and says nothing. I think she knows something. I don't ask.
textes.Mère-Lune sait des choses que les autres: Mère-Lune knows things the others don't. About the seal. About the great pool. She'll only tell them to someone who loves Ramure. Make Ramure love you.
textes.Mère-Lune était l'amie de ma grand-mère,: Mother Moon was my grandmother's friend, and she's my most disobedient patient. In the evening, while she drinks her tea, she tells me about Garance. I could listen to her all night.
textes.Mère-Lune, c'est la lune de Ramure, mon: Mère-Lune is Ramure's moon, my friend: always full, always there. I revere her. And I swapped away her cloak. I've never forgiven myself. She has, I think. Almost.
Mother Moon is who I dance for. Well, for the moon. But she's the one I look at when I raise my arms. I often wonder… No, nothing.
textes.Mère-Lune, la doyenne de Ramure, change: Mère-Lune, the eldest of Ramure, changes the moon lanterns on the bridges every spring. Her old paws can no longer reach the edge of the ponds, where the glowing mushrooms grow.
textes.Mère-Lune. Les loups l'ont suivie jusqu': Mère-Lune. The wolves followed her here. We still follow her. She teases me to make me smile. I do my best. It doesn't show. But I do my best.
textes.Mégaphone pousse les boutons de la régie: Mégaphone is pushing the buttons on the sound desk. The red one, the blue one… and the one in the middle, all the way up.
textes.Mélisse ! Ton nectar est parfait, aujour: Mélisse! Your nectar's perfect today! Perfect!
textes.Mélisse ! Toujours pas trouvé ma réponse: Mélisse! Still haven't found my answer?
textes.Mélisse ! Trois flacons, vite, je suis p: Mélisse! Three bottles, quick, I'm in a hurry!
textes.Mélisse ? Moucheron à paillettes. Elle s: Mélisse? Glitter-gnat. She smells of sugar, she talks too much and she melts crystal shards to make bottles. Bottles. Hmph.
textes.Mélisse est la meilleure marchande du mo: Mélisse is the best merchant in the world, and she puts far too much sugar in her nectar. But shh: if she finds out, she'll throw petals at me.
textes.Mélisse fait le meilleur nectar de l'arc: Mélisse makes the best nectar in the archipelago. And she's the stingiest merchant in the world. I pay her in Ventaile feathers, which are very rare, and she grumbles. I don't get it.
textes.Mélisse met trop de sucre dans son necta: Mélisse puts too much sugar in her nectar. Don't tell her, she'd throw petals at me.
textes.Mélisse rit de moi quand je perds mes go: Mélisse laughs at me when I lose my drops. She says it's never-ending. But she always has a bottle for me, and I think deep down she isn't such a tease.
textes.Mélisse vend son nectar trop cher, et il: Mélisse sells her nectar too dear, and it's delicious. Both are true: that's her own riddle. I'm fond of her. She's been demanding three bottles from me for ten years.
textes.Mélisse vend son nectar trop cher. Mais: Mélisse charges too much for her nectar. But it's delicious. Both are true: that's a riddle.
textes.Mérit ! Une bière, contre une perche bie: Mérit! One beer, for one very dead perch.
Mérit! A beer, and a cat bread.
textes.Mérit dit que j'ai refusé trois prétenda: Mérit says I turned down three suitors. That's not true. I turned down four.
textes.Mérit dit que son four est le meilleur d: Mérit says her oven is the best in the village. I built it. So she's right. But she says it as if it were thanks to her.
Mérit says her oven is the best in the village. I built my oven with my own hands. Hers too, as it happens. I'm the one who built it.
textes.Mérit est mon amie depuis toujours. Elle: Mérit has been my friend forever. She counts my suitors better than her loaves, and she tells the whole village about them. But when things go wrong, she turns up with a warm flatbread. Always.
textes.Mérit et Ptahmosé se disputent pour savo: Mérit and Ptahmosé argue about who has the finest oven. They're ovens. They all look alike.
textes.Mérit et lui se disputent pour savoir qu: He and Mérit argue about whose oven makes the best bread. One evening, at the brewery, I secretly swapped their two loaves. Ptahmosé tasted, and said: “Mine, obviously.” It was Mérit's. I told them. He didn't speak to me for a month. Best month of my life: I could finally finish my sentences.
textes.Mérit fait du bon pain et de la bonne bi: Mérit makes good bread and good beer with my barley. She talks too much. But she listens too, when she has to. And she counts the onions well. Too well.
textes.Mérit fait du bon pain et vend de bonnes: Mérit makes good bread and sells good dates, I admit it. But she put honey in my cacao, in front of the whole fair. You don't put honey in cacao. You do NOT.
textes.Mérit fait la meilleure bière du fleuve: Mérit makes the best beer on the river and the best bread on both banks. She also knows everything about everybody. She'd have made an excellent scribe. Too excellent: nothing would have stayed secret.
Mérit makes the best beer on the river. Don't tell her I said so: she'd put her prices up.
textes.Mérit, c'est la bière, le pain et les no: Mérit is beer, bread and the village news. I give her fish, she gives me beer, and everyone knows what I've caught before I'm even home.
textes.Mérit. Combien de prétendants, ce mois-c: Mérit. How many suitors this month?
Mérit. You've got your beans, I've got my dates.
Mérit. A beer. Here are seven onions.
textes.Même les jaguars finissent par avoir fai: Even jaguars get hungry in the end. Patience.
textes.Même pas une demie en plus ?: Not even half a drop extra?
textes.Même pas une pièce ? Bon. Je te chante l: Not even one coin? Fine. I'll sing you the chorus for free, but I sing off-key on purpose.
textes.Même si, aujourd'hui, le cœur n'y est pa: Even if my heart isn't in it today.
textes.Même texte. Et mettez-y une faute, ça ma: Same text. And put a mistake in it, it works better.
textes.Même trois marches ? Deux ? Une ?: Not even three steps? Two? One?
textes.N'a rien, Caelan. Comme mardi. Comme il: …is fine, Caelan. Like on Tuesday. Like a hundred years ago.
textes.N'est-ce pas ? Je me demande bien pourqu: Aren't they? I really do wonder why.
textes.N'est-ce pas ? Pleines de couleurs. Je m: Aren't they? Full of colours. I really do wonder why.
Right? {Il}'s just like that, {nom}. I'll pass it on, it'll make {son} day.
textes.N'importe où ? Un vrai voyageur. Alors a: Anywhere? A true traveller. Then above the camels: it's warm, it smells strong, and you sleep like a baby. Ask the mute pirate.
textes.N'installe jamais un programme qui vient: Never install a program that comes from a stranger, even if it's cheap. And never click on big shiny buttons: close windows with the little cross!
textes.NOTE DE SERVICE\nn° 4 512-B\n\nPour desc:

(Do not ask why. It is the procedure.)
— Management
textes.NOTE DE SERVICE n° 4 512-B. « Pour desce: STAFF MEMO No. 4 512-B. “To go down, stamp the forms in the regulation order: THE SKY before THE SUN, THE SUN before COTTON CANDY. (Do not ask why. It is the procedure.) — Management.” Three offices have a coloured form: a blue one, a yellow one, a pink one.
textes.Nadine ? Ma meilleure élève, et ma seule: Nadine? My best pupil, and my only one. She does the round better than me, but I'll never say so. She cut ten minutes off it. Ten!
textes.Nadine est adorable, et elle a une langu: Nadine is a sweetheart, and a terrible chatterbox. She guessed about my letters. She promised to keep quiet. She keeps half quiet.
textes.Nadine m'a demandé de lui écrire une car: Nadine asked me to write her a postcard from Atlantis once I've found it. “With a stamp from there, if possible.” I promised her, solemnly. I've even started the draft: “Dear Nadine, I am writing to you from…” I'm still missing the street name.
textes.Nadine voudrait que des cartes postales: Nadine would like postcards from Port-Azur to reach the four corners of the archipelago.
textes.Nadine, la postière. Elle vend des carte: Nadine, the postmistress. She sells postcards, like me — unfair competition. But she has the loveliest smile in Port-Azur. So I buy a stamp from her every day, to keep an eye on her.
textes.Nadine, la postière. Une jeune femme cha: Nadine, the postwoman. A charming young woman who brings me envelopes I have no wish to open. And a caramel. The caramel helps.
textes.Nager ! Alors là, c'est encore plus fou: Swim! Now that's even crazier than boats. Me, I keep my feet in the sand. Sand doesn't sink.
textes.Nager jusqu'au nénuphar géant, au milieu: Swim to the giant water lily in the middle of the Rubbed-Out Pond and take the pot of blue
textes.Nager un jour, devant tout le monde, de: To swim one day, in front of everyone, from the beach to Yannick's jetty. In a regulation swimsuit. For Rosalie to see it, and have nothing to say. For once.
textes.Nature ! Toi, tu as compris. Une bonne b: Plain! You've understood. Good embers, a fresh sardine, and nothing to hide it. Like good people: no need for sauce.
textes.Naturellement, je me souviens de vous. J: Naturally, I remember you. I remember everyone. It's my job.
textes.Naturellement. Je vous en signe une bell: Naturally. I'll sign you a fine one.
textes.Nausicaa chante la marée haute sur les m: Nausicaa sings the high tide on the steps of the Gate every evening. It's the best moment of my watch. Don't tell her. I'm on duty.
textes.Nausicaa chante les marées pour la cité,: Nausicaa sings the tides for the city, and for me on the nights I can't sleep. Her voice makes the crystal tremble, in the good way.
textes.Nausicaa chante mes histoires mieux que: Nausicaa sings my stories better than I tell them. She complains that I change the words. But a song is like the sea: never the same twice.
textes.Nausicaa chante, moi je danse. Elle dit: Nausicaa sings, I dance. She says people listen to her. I say they watch me. Truth is, everyone does both.
textes.Ne bouge pas, je te soigne ! Voilà, comm: Hold still, I'll heal you! There, good as new. Almost.
textes.Ne bouge pas, petit pigeon. Je ne fais q: Don't move, little pigeon. I'm only… looking.
textes.Ne bouge pas, {surnom}. … Dis-moi : tu c: Don't move, {surnom}. … Tell me: do you choose your clothes to look good, or to feel good?
textes.Ne bouge pas. … Voilà. Tu as des épaules: Don't move. … There. You have a traveller's shoulders, and terrible posture. Hello. Grisette, seamstress. I dress the Archduchess, the champion of the Arena, the violinist on the square, and anyone who wants to stop looking like a sack of coal.
textes.Ne bouge plus… plus… Voilà ! Ta main a l: Don't move… stay still… There! Your hand left a blue trail — it looks like a wing. You're very photogenic, at night.
textes.Ne bougez plus, je fais une photo avec l: Don't move, I'm taking a photo with the glow sticks!
textes.Ne dites pas ça, je vais devoir augmente: Don't say that, I'll have to raise the price.
textes.Ne frappe jamais personne. Ici, tout le: Never hit anyone. Around here, everyone has a long memory.
textes.Ne le dites pas à Adèle. Elle croirait q: Don't tell Adèle. She'd think I was making fun. I'm not. I'm waiting, like her. With ink.
textes.Ne le répète pas, {surnom}. Je ne dors j: Don't repeat this, {surnom}. I never sleep in a hammock. It makes me seasick. A hammock innkeeper, on a beached ship, who gets seasick! I sleep on the floor, under the counter, on a blanket. Only Anouk knows, with her ginger teas. That's why I want an inn on dry land.
textes.Ne les casse pas ! Recommandation numéro: Don't break them! Recommendation number three!
textes.Ne m'appelez pas comme ça. Et le gilet,: Don't call me that. And the life jacket, does he have it?
textes.Ne m'appelez pas « Yo ». Et vos clients,: Don't call me “Yo”. And do your customers have life jackets?
textes.Ne m'appelle pas « ma petite » devant to: Don't call me “little one” in front of everyone.
textes.Ne mange jamais les baies bleues du sous: Never eat the blue berries in the undergrowth. Unless you want to see talking fireflies. For two days.
textes.Ne mange jamais un champignon blanc de l: Never eat a white mushroom from the mountain. The red ones, yes. The white ones, you see dragons for a week.
textes.Ne me gronde pas, Perlée… Tu m'as manqué: Don't scold me, Perlée… I missed you.
textes.Ne me parle pas. Je suis de très mauvais: Don't talk to me. I'm in a very bad mood. Buy something or go away.
textes.Ne me présente personne aujourd'hui, kha: Don't introduce me to anyone today, khalti.
Don't go up to the crater without a weapon. The golems and the elementals don't like visitors.
textes.Ne pas toucher les hélices. Elles morden: Do not touch the propellers. They bite.
textes.Ne plus avoir peur… C'est une belle poti: Not being scared any more… That's a lovely potion. I don't know how to make it. I don't think anybody does. But if I find it, you'll be the first to taste it.
textes.Ne sors pas sans ton masque, hein. Dehor: Don't go out without your mask, eh. Outside, it's the sea. Everywhere.
textes.Ne te presse pas. Une île, ça se découvr: Don't rush. An island is something you discover slowly.
Don't touch, look with your eyes.
textes.Nebet ! Mon moustique est toujours le me: Nebet! My mosquito is still the best!
textes.Nebet ! Ton panier est toujours un pot ?: Nebet! Is your basket still a pot?
textes.Nebet est triste, depuis que son chat a: Nebet has been sad since her cat disappeared. Me too, a little. He was a good mouser.
textes.Nebet et Kinich m'ont demandé de choisir: Nebet and Kinich asked me to choose the best story: the mosquito who bites the Lords, or the great cat who cuts up the serpent. I said: Tlaco's. They said Tlaco didn't have a story. Yes he does! One day, he'll guide the dead across the river of Mictlan. That's the best one. It hasn't even happened yet!
textes.Nebet me suit partout avec un sistre et: Nebet follows me everywhere with a sistrum and a thousand questions. She wants to be a priestess, or a fisherwoman, or a cat. The temple would be lucky. So would the cats.
textes.Nebet parle trop, court trop, et touche: Nebet talks too much, runs too much, and touches everything in my workshop. She has good hands. She'd make a good potter. Don't tell her, she'd want to start tomorrow.
textes.Nebet pose plus de questions que tous me: Nebet asks more questions than all my pupils put together. She runs, she sings, she writes her name with one leg too many. She'll be a great scribe. Or a cat. We'll see.
textes.Nebet veut être pêcheuse, ou prêtresse,: Nebet wants to be a fisherwoman, or a priestess, or a cat. For fishing, she has everything: patience, a good flick of the wrist. She just lacks the heart to keep the fish.
textes.Nebet, c'est ma copine de Per-Hâpy ! Ell: Nebet is my friend from Per-Hâpy! She talks almost as much as I do. She has a ginger cat with a crooked ear. She says her cat story is better than my mosquito. It's not true.
textes.Nebet, c'est ma fille, mon soleil et ma: Nebet is my daughter, my sun and my storm. She runs everywhere, she asks a thousand questions, and she has her father's laugh. I wouldn't change a thing. Except perhaps her knees, always scraped.
textes.Nectar de fée, quatre cœurs ! Et je rach: Fairy nectar, four hearts! And I buy crystal shards. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Nenetl ! Doucement, ce soir. Mes pots so: Nenetl! Gently tonight. My pots are fragile.
textes.Nenetl ! La chanson des soleils, ce soir: Nenetl! The song of the suns, tonight?
textes.Nenetl ! Tu joues ce soir ? Gratuitement: Nenetl! Are you playing tonight? For free, again?
textes.Nenetl joue du tambour comme d'autres re: Nenetl plays the drum the way others breathe. She helps me make the lessons sing. What the children don't learn by heart, they learn with their feet, dancing.
textes.Nenetl joue du tambour comme le tonnerre: Nenetl plays the drum like thunder and the flute like a hummingbird. She laughs at everything. She says I dance with two left feet. Not true. I have one left foot and one jaguar foot.
textes.Nenetl joue du tambour si fort que mes p: Nenetl plays the drum so loudly that my pots shake on the shelves. She says they're dancing. Maybe. But when they dance too much, they fall. And she plays the flute I made her. That, I don't complain about.
Nenetl plays the drum so loud my pots shake on their shelves. One day they'll jump into the lake all by themselves.
textes.Nenetl joue du tambour, de la flûte, et: Nenetl plays the drum, the flute, and a shell that squeaks! When she plays the hummingbird flute, Tlaco sings. She says he's a musical dog. Me, I'm her dancer.
textes.Nenetl joue tous les soirs et ne fait ja: Nenetl plays every evening and never charges. It's a serious business mistake. I tell her so often. She laughs. She laughs at everything. Even at my advice, which is excellent, mind you.
textes.Nenetl m'a soulevé jusqu'au grand tambou: Nenetl lifted me up to the big drum, and I hit it with all my might. BOOM! The dancers jumped, Tlaco ran under a bench, and I made thunder! Like Tlaloc! Now I ask her every evening. Once. She always says yes. Once.
textes.Nerveux. Il y a une voile au large depui: Nervous. There's been a sail out at sea since this morning. It doesn't move. A sail that doesn't move is waiting for something.
textes.Nessa ! Tu as encore emmêlé ton ruban ?: Nessa! Have you tangled your ribbon again?
textes.Nessa ! Un message pour toi. Enfin… pres: Nessa! A message for you. Well… almost.
textes.Nessa danse comme le vent dans les feuil: Nessa dances like the wind in the golden leaves. I was her partner at the last Dawn festival. I trod on her feet seventeen times. She still smiles at me.
textes.Nessa danse si vite qu'elle use un ruban: Nessa dances so fast she wears out one ribbon a season. I weave her new ones, longer every time. The last one is thirty paces long. She's already tangled it in a footbridge.
textes.Nessa danse sur tout ce que je chante. M: Nessa dances to everything I sing. Even the sad songs. Especially the sad songs: she says it's to cheer them up.
textes.Nessa vient danser sous mon métier à tis: Nessa comes and dances under my loom when she's inventing a step. She says the sound of the shuttle gives her the rhythm: clack, swish, clack. Her loveliest dance is called “The Loom”. I pretend to be flattered. I am.
textes.Neuf ! Comme les vies d'un chat. C'est p: Nine! Like a cat's lives. It's handy, that makes one cat per life.
textes.Neuf heures, Ewen. J'ai compté dix coups: Nine o'clock, Ewen. I counted ten strokes.
textes.Neuf minutes cinquante. Je garde dix sec: Nine minutes fifty. I'm keeping ten seconds for tomorrow.
textes.Neuf, Amirale ! Plus un pour l'écho !: Nine, Admiral! Plus one for the echo!
Nine. And that was the last one.
textes.Neuf. Il en avait neuf. Le neuvième, c'e: Nine. It had nine. The ninth one's a secret.
textes.Ni l'un ni l'autre ? … Je calcule. Si ce: Neither? … I'm calculating. If it's not numbers or letters, that leaves drawings. What do you draw? I draw stars, with their distances next to them.
textes.Nimiel ! Qu'est-ce que tu caches dans to: Nimiel! What are you hiding behind your back?
textes.Nimiel ! Viens ici. Montre-moi tes poche: Nimiel! Come here. Show me your pockets.
textes.Nimiel ? Quarante-deux ans, et déjà plus: Nimiel? Forty-two years old, and already more bandages than Faelar in nine centuries. She climbs, she falls, she laughs. I scold her, and I always keep her favourite moss aside.
textes.Nimiel ? Trop petite, trop rapide, trop: Nimiel? Too small, too fast, too many questions. She has a good eye, though. I won't teach her archery. Not yet. Don't tell her I said “not yet”.
textes.Nimiel a caché une grenouille dans mon p: Nimiel hid a frog in my kneading trough. I won't tell her mother. This time.
textes.Nimiel a emprunté mon vieil arc, sans de: Nimiel borrowed my old bow without asking. Three arrows in Sylwen's door. I told her off. Then I went to look at the door up close. Three arrows in a circle the size of an apple. At her age. I said nothing. To anyone.
textes.Nimiel a encore fait une bêtise. Je ne s: Nimiel's been up to mischief again. I don't know what, but I'm sure of it.
textes.Nimiel est mon meilleur public : une que: Nimiel is my best audience: a question every three sentences, and she remembers everything. In nine hundred years, she'll be the one telling the stories. I'm leaving her mine.
textes.Nimiel m'a cassé une porte, caché une gr: Nimiel has broken one of my doors, hidden a frog in my dough trough and pinched three brioches. She's the most adorable of disasters. I never tell her mother anything. Hardly ever.
textes.Nimiel m'a demandé un jour ce qu'il y av: Nimiel once asked me what's at the bottom of singing shells. I said: “The sea, remembering it was once a great story.” She thought about it, then said: “So it's you, as a shell.” I've never had a finer compliment in nine centuries.
textes.Nimiel m'a offert un jour un pissenlit t: One day, Nimiel gave me a very crumpled dandelion, picked “specially for you, Mama”. She'd spent the night outside looking for a moonflower, and fallen asleep in a bush. I scolded her for three minutes. The dandelion I'll keep for a hundred years.
textes.Nimiel s'est présentée un matin avec une: Nimiel turned up one morning with a bump on her forehead, round as a plum. “I fell off the third walkway. But with no hands!” It took me three days to realise she was proud of it. I patched her up, and I said nothing to Miriel. Nothing serious.
textes.Nimiel te suit partout, hein ? Elle veut: Nimiel follows you everywhere, doesn't she? She wants to know everything about humans. Everything.
textes.Nimiel veut devenir archère. Elle a tiré: Nimiel wants to be an archer. She shot at Sylwen's door. The door didn't survive.
Nimiel wants to know everything about humans. Everything. She's like me, three centuries ago. Only much noisier.
textes.Nimiel, pourquoi y a-t-il une grenouille: Nimiel, why is there a frog in my pocket?
Nimiel. Get down off that railing.
textes.Nina ! T'as cassé mon fossé hier !: Nina! You broke my moat yesterday!
textes.Nina ? Ma future capitaine. Elle pose pl: Nina? My future captain. She asks more questions than the sea has waves. She'll make a very good captain. A bit chatty at the helm.
textes.Nina dit que la fontaine exauce les vœux: Nina says the fountain grants wishes. I asked for my kite. It's not working yet.
textes.Nina est née ici, il y a sept ans et dem: Nina was born here, seven and a half years ago. The first few months, I kneaded dough with her asleep in a big bread basket, under a clean tea towel, warm by the oven. She smelled of brioche. Raymond came to see the baby every morning; that's how he became Grandpa Raymond. I'm raising her on my own. And don't ask me about the father.
textes.Nina sera la meilleure glacière de l'arc: Nina will be the best ice-cream maker in the archipelago. Or a captain. Or both. She's already invented a flavour; at her age, I was licking spoons.
textes.Nina veut connaître le nom de toutes les: Nina wants to know the name of every crate. Every single one. She turns up with a notebook and asks: “And that one?” “Bérénice.” “And that one?” “Marcelin.” She writes it down. Her notebook is full. She's the only one who doesn't think I'm weird. She says giving names is normal. That it's everybody else who's weird.
textes.Nina, c'est la grande. Elle a sept ans e: Nina's the big girl. She's seven and a half and she bosses everyone. She knows loads of things, like about the fountain. But she calls me baby. And she can't make a moat.
textes.Nina, c'est ma petite-fille de cœur. Je: Nina is my granddaughter at heart. I saw her in her bread basket, no bigger than a loaf. She tells everyone I'm the champion. She's the only honest person in this town.
textes.Nina, elle a dit que la fontaine, elle e: Nina said the fountain grants wishes. You have to close your eyes, turn round three times and throw a coin. I turned six times, to be sure, and I asked for my kite. Really hard, in my head. Nina says wishes are like cakes, you have to wait for them to bake. But she doesn't know how long a wish takes to bake.
textes.Nina, elle commande à la fontaine. Mais: Nina's the boss at the fountain. But at the beach, I'm the boss. One day she wanted to dig my castle's moat. She dug it straight towards the sea, and the sea came in and broke everything. A moat has to go round! Everybody knows that. She said she did it on purpose. She didn't do it on purpose.
textes.Nina, ma fille. Sept ans et demi, trois: Nina, my daughter. Seven and a half, three hundred questions a day. I answer one in three. The rest I save for when I've had some sleep.
textes.Nina. La petite de la boulangère. On a u: Nina. The baker's little girl. We've got a secret, she and I. She talks a lot, but that secret she keeps.
textes.Noisette ! Pépin, Gland et Cacahuète son: Noisette! Pip, Acorn and Peanut are ready!
textes.Noisette ! Une graine des elfes, toute f: Noisette! An elf seed, fresh as can be!
textes.Noisette est née dans une noisette que l: Noisette was born in a hazelnut the wind had carried all the way up to me. Ever since, she's been looking for her tree and sowing seeds everywhere. Even in my crown.
textes.Noisette garde un trésor de graines dans: Noisette keeps a treasure of seeds in her pocket. She thinks nobody knows.
textes.Noisette pose plus de questions que je n: Noisette asks more questions than I have drops. She thinks nobody knows about the treasure of seeds she keeps in her pocket. Everybody knows. Nobody says a word.
textes.Noisette s'endort souvent près de l'étan: Noisette often falls asleep by the pond, her hand on her pocket. One night, a seed rolled out, all the way to the water's edge. I put it back in her pocket without a sound. The next day, she recounted: one thousand one hundred and eleven. She was relieved. She never found out why that one seed was wet.
textes.Noisette, c'est ma meilleure amie ! Elle: Noisette is my best friend! She's got seeds everywhere, she asks a thousand questions, and she laughs as loud as I do. Together, we make enough noise for four.
textes.Noisette, c'est un peu ma faute : c'est: Noisette is a bit my fault: I'm the one who carried her hazelnut up here. I'd picked it up on an island. Which one? An island. With trees. She asks me every week.
textes.Noisette, qu'as-tu encore dans les poche: Noisette, what have you got in your pockets this time?
textes.Noisette. Ton cactus a bu sa goutte du m: Noisette. Your cactus has had its drop for the month.
textes.Noisette. Une fée des nuages qui descend: Noisette. A cloud fairy who comes down to dig in MY roots with a little shovel. For a seed. A thief with wings. Hmph hmph.
textes.Nolwenn ! Il me faut vingt couvercles po: Nolwenn! I need twenty lids for tomorrow's Zéphyr!
textes.Nolwenn ! Ton aiguille courbe, elle tien: Nolwenn! Your curved needle, holding up?
textes.Nolwenn coud comme une fée et vend comme: Nolwenn sews like a fairy and sells like an oyster. I help her canvas offcuts find a buyer, and she looks at me as if I were stealing them. Artists are so touchy.
textes.Nolwenn coud des voiles depuis toujours: Nolwenn has sewn sails all her life and had never seen one fill with wind. So I'm teaching her to steer, at dawn, while Carène sleeps. She's got the sea in her hand, that girl.
textes.Nolwenn et moi, on a grandi ensemble, el: Nolwenn and I grew up together, her on the canvas, me in the water. She always looks at the horizon. I look underneath. Between the two of us, we see everything.
textes.Nolwenn m'a cousu mon sac de plongée dan: Nolwenn sewed me my diving bag from a scrap of old sail, with a seam that lets nothing out, not even an angry crab. That was ten years ago. The bag's still here. So is the crab, I think, somewhere at the bottom. I don't look any more.
textes.Nolwenn, c'est la seule qui entre dans m: Nolwenn's the only one who comes into my forge without jumping when I strike. I make her needles. She has the patience I don't have, and the hard head I do.
Nolwenn. A pearl, for the ribbon.
textes.Non ! C'est le Grand Chat du soleil !: No! It's the Great Cat of the sun!
textes.Non ! C'est le canal qui m'a mouillée, m: No! The canal got me wet, Mum!
textes.Non ! C'était un trou. Mais je te donner: No! It was a hole. But I'll give you a little something anyway. Ask.
No! Well, yes. Well… run slowly.
textes.Non ! Enfin… comme tu veux. Je suis de g: No! I mean… as you like. I'm on guard.
textes.Non ! Il est vieux, mais pas à ce point-: No! He's old, but not that old!
textes.Non ! Pas le gros bouton qui brille ! C': No! Not the big shiny button! It's always a trap: it makes more windows appear. Only the little cross ✕.
textes.Non ? Alors assieds-toi là, à côté de mo: No? Then sit here, next to me. To learn. Hold the line. Don't move. … See? Nothing's biting. That's the first lesson.
textes.Non ? Alors t'es l'ennemi des sept mers: No? Then you're the enemy of the seven seas! And of Lantern Square! … Just kidding, huh. You can still change your mind. Until tonight.
textes.Non ? Bon… Tu as peut-être raison. Une f: No? OK… Maybe you're right. Once, he bit Mixtli. Well, his jaguar skin. He thought it was a real one.
textes.Non ? Hm. Bien. Très bien. Le moteur vou: No? Hm. Fine. Very well. The engine will prove you wrong. Come back in a hundred years, it'll still be turning. And you won't be around to apologise. Too bad for you.
textes.Non ? Hm. Je respecte. J'ai passé quaran: No? Hm. I respect that. I spent forty years surrounded by people who said no. You're in plentiful company. But you'll see. You'll see.
textes.Non ? Oh. Vous avez de la chance. Je vou: No? Oh. You're lucky. I envy you a little, politely. Take the red car, then, and look out of the window for me. Well, for everyone.
textes.Non ? … Ah. Bon. C'est normal, hein. C'e: No? … Oh. Right. That's normal, huh. I'm the weird one. Forget it. Step aside, the crate's heavy. It's called… nothing. It's called nothing.
textes.Non ? … C'est vrai ? Ouf ! Enfin, je veu: No? … Really? Phew! I mean: that's all right! You can learn! You just need somebody very big to hold your belt.
No thanks, I'm not hungry anymore.
No thanks, I'm just passing through.
textes.Non, Bastien. Mais regarde ton banc, à m: No, Bastien. But check your bench at noon.
textes.Non, Borin. Aujourd'hui, c'est ton enclu: No, Borin. Today, it's your anvil that's leaning.
textes.Non, Doc ! Un amoureux ! Il ne mange plu: No, Doc! One in love! He's stopped eating!
textes.Non, Majesté. Et votre trésor ne m'a tou: No, Majesty. And your treasury still hasn't paid me for the throne.
textes.Non, Maîtresse Zéphyrine. Juste un mouch: No, Mistress Zéphyrine. Just a handkerchief.
No, it's a loop. Ask Fañch.
textes.Non, j'adore quand ça flotte !: No, I love it when things float!
No, I'm afraid I'll break everything.
No, I love travelling too much.
No, I can't hear a thing.
No, I've never thought about it.
No, the world is my home.
textes.Non, mais j'ai trouvé une deuxième botte: No, but I found a second boot! Your monster's got two of them!
textes.Non, mais j'en ai trouvé une autre ! Ell: No, but I found another one! Whose is it?
textes.Non, mais tu rougis. Ça se voit depuis l: No, but you're blushing. You can see it from the door.
textes.Non, maman, c'est pas moi qui ai mangé l: No, Mom, I'm not the one who ate the cake…
textes.Non, non ! Une fois ! La dernière fois,: No, no! Once! Last time you said once!
textes.Non, non, j'ai vraiment éternué !: No, no, I really did sneeze!
textes.Non, on les REGARDE ! Si tu les comptes,: No, you WATCH them! If you count them, you lose them!
textes.Non, pas tout. Vous avez sans doute rais: No, not everything. You're probably right. But a ring in the sand can be forgiven, can't it? Say yes. … Thank you.
textes.Non, petit. La fois où je t'ai porté. Tu: No, lad. The time I carried you. You weighed a barrel.
textes.Non, petite étoile. Il chauffe en silenc: No, little star. It warms in silence.
textes.Non, un nœud de lacet ! Mais il est très: No, a shoelace knot! But it's really pretty!
No. The tea was getting cold.
No. Make a beautiful one, that's all.
textes.Non. Je ne l'ai dit qu'une fois. Profite: No. I only said it once. Make the most of it.
No. I just wanted to see him dance.
textes.Non. Ma boutique est fermée. Pour toi, e: No. My shop is closed. To you, anyway. Come back when I've cooled down.
No. But he plugs the hole a bit.
No. Not even for four hundred and eleven.
No. We write it as we walk.
No. Not today. Not for you.
textes.Non. Pas cette fois. … Attends, attends,: No. Not this time. … Wait, wait, give it back!
textes.Non. Pas du tout. Il n'est pas dans mon: No. Not at all. He's not in my watering can.
textes.Non. Quelqu'un tapait au-dessus de ma tê: No. Somebody was banging above my head.
No. You're getting warm, but no.
No. You hold the tongs. Full stop.
No. Go sell your syrup somewhere else.
textes.Nono m'a demandé un slow, un soir. « Un: Nono asked me for a slow dance one night. “A real one, like on my father's boat.” I made him a slow dance at a hundred and forty-five beats per minute. He said it was a disgrace to humanity, danced it to the very end, and asks for it again every Saturday. In protest, he says.
textes.Nono m'a donné mon nom quand j'avais six: Nono gave me my name when I was six. He grumbles that my music is too fast, then dances till morning. A real mystery, with creaky knees.
textes.Nono m'a porté jusqu'à la source le jour: Nono carried me to the spring the day I got sunstroke. I owe him everything. But if he tells me about the party in the mine one more time, I'll keel over again. On purpose.
textes.Nono m'a raconté la fête dans la mine de: Nono has told me about the party in the dwarves' mine at least forty times. In the first version, there was an echo. In the tenth, a dragon. In the latest, the dwarves carried him in triumph. I told him we knew it by heart. He answered: “And yet you stay till the end.” It's true. I stay.
textes.Nono raconte qu'il a dansé dans une mine: Nono says he danced in a dwarf mine. Nobody knows if it's true, but the story changes every time.
Nono, drink a little, it's hot.
textes.Nono, c'est la mémoire de toutes les fêt: Nono is the memory of every party in the archipelago. His stories change every time, and that's why they're good. I collect them, like juggling balls.
textes.Nono, raconte la mine ! La version avec: Nono, tell us about the mine! The version with the dragon!
textes.Nono, refais ta vague, j'ai raté le débu: Nono, do your wave again, I missed the start!
textes.Non… mais j'ai trouvé des miettes jusqu': No… but I found crumbs all the way to the door, and little marks in the flour. Marks… from paws?
textes.Nord-est. Il tourne toujours autour de n: North-east. He keeps circling around us.
textes.Nori ! La montagne a fait boum, cette nu: Nori! The mountain went boom last night.
textes.Nori boit de l'eau. De l'EAU. Dans ma ta: Nori drinks water. WATER. In my tavern. He says it's moon water. I tasted it: it's water. But he listens well when you talk to him. That makes up for it.
textes.Nori boit de l'eau. De l'EAU. Dans une t: Nori drinks water. WATER. In a tavern. I say nothing. I think plenty.
textes.Nori est le seul client qui ne me racont: Nori is the only customer who never tells me anything. So I'm the one who tells him everything, all the gossip in Forgefer, for a hundred years now. The other day, he corrected me: “No, Ulfa. Sixty years ago, you told it differently.” He remembers everything I say. EVERYTHING. It's terrifying. And a bit flattering.
textes.Nori lit l'avenir dans les pierres et me: Nori reads the future in the stones and tells it to me crooked. But he has never lied to me. For a king, that's rarer than rubies.
textes.Nori lit les runes et il écoute la monta: Nori reads runes and listens to the mountain. I listen to the mountain too, but all I understand are the cave-ins. He understands the rest. He scares me a little, and does me a lot of good.
textes.Nori lit les runes. Il dit que la montag: Nori reads the runes. He says the mountain is afraid. A frightened mountain… Hmm.
textes.Nori sait tout, il a toujours raison, et: Nori knows everything, he's always right, and he says it under his breath so everyone can hear. Unbearable. But when he carves a rune on my steel, the steel stands up straight.
textes.Normal. Elle est en bon acier, pas en pl: Of course. It's made of good steel, not feathers.
textes.Nos auvents ont fait la guerre. Le sien: Our awnings went to war. Hers cast a shadow on my swords, mine on her saffron. We raised them, and raised them, and raised them. After a week, they were higher than the rooftops. Pyrus came along, looked up for a minute, and said: “No.” We lowered them. Same day. Same height.
textes.Nos filles, Mochi et Myrtille, sont insé: Our daughters, Mochi and Myrtille, are inseparable. Mochi gives her sardines to Myrtille, and Myrtille eats all of Mochi's cakes. So every evening, Trèfle and I have to say hello on the way out of the Circle. She says “Caramel”. I say “Trèfle”. That's all. That's already far too much.
textes.Note aussi que je t'ai vu racler le plat: Also note that I saw you scrape the dish clean.
Write it down. We'll call it Peek'.
Write it down: the sea, before sixty.
textes.Notification : votre coiffure n'est pas: Notification: your hairstyle does not comply with regulations.
textes.Notre bon docteur Roux. Une femme de sci: Our good Doctor Roux. A woman of science. She saved my leg the summer of the jellyfish, and she saves my back every week. Discreetly, as is proper.
textes.Notre calendrier sacré, le Tzolk'in, com: Our sacred calendar, the Tzolk'in, counts two hundred and sixty days: thirteen numbers and twenty day names turning together, like two wheels. A day comes back every two hundred and sixty days. Like an old acquaintance.
textes.Notre champion ! Tout en haut du tableau: Our champion! Top of the board for three years. I saw him run before he could walk. I'm as proud of him as of a little brother. Don't tell him: his ears are big-headed enough already.
textes.Notre cité a sept quartiers et un canal: Our city has seven quarters and a circular canal. The children say the canal goes round the world. It's almost true.
textes.Notre maire. Un brave homme qui parle lo: Our mayor. A good man who talks long. He owes me his sash, and he knows it. I know it too. We smile at each other.
textes.Notre mariage a été fixé sept fois. La p: Our wedding has been set seven times. The first time, a clock to repair. The second, a storm. The seventh, the great clock running a second fast. One second! Tic was so sorry. I told him it didn't matter, that we had all the time in the world. He made a funny face when I said “all the time”.
textes.Notre numéro au Crâne Fendu : je joue de: Our act at the Crâne Fendu: I play faster and faster, and she throws a knife on every note, at a painted board. At the end, my last note and her last knife land together. One evening, I finished too early. She threw in the silence. The whole room shivered. Since then, I always finish too early. On purpose.
textes.Notre partie de dames dure depuis le pri: Our game of draughts has been going on since spring. It never ends: every time I'm about to lose, a piece appears. I don't know where from. Hassan looks at my sleeve, then at the sea, then at my sleeve. He says nothing, he pours more tea. He's very polite, or he has bad eyesight. For a friend, it's the same thing.
textes.Notre partie tient toujours, entre humai: Our game still stands, human to human. I've written it down. I'm still thinking about my first move.
textes.Notre premier marchandage a duré trois h: Our first haggle lasted three hours and four teapots. She wanted my apple juice, I wanted her saffron, and neither of us would give in. In the end, we swapped a jar of saffron for a barrel of apple juice and a sea shanty, sung by me, in Breton, in front of the whole souk. She says it was the song that tipped the scales.
textes.Notre premier marché, à Tazira : mon mie: Our first deal, in Tazira: my honey for his dates. It should have taken a minute. It took a whole day and three teapots. He'd name a price, drink a glass, go quiet; I'd talk, drink, talk. At sunset, we shook on it. Ever since, every year, I go down to see him: on foot along the coast in the old days, by Zéphyr now, when my paws complain.
textes.Notre île flotte au-dessus des nuages, l: Our island floats above the clouds, far from the archipelago. No one comes here… except those who dream hard enough. Or eat the right mushroom.
textes.Nourredine fait des trous dans mon cuivr: Nourredine pokes holes in my copper and calls them stars. For forty years now. Without him, my lanterns light up nothing. Don't tell him I said that.
textes.Nourredine fait les plus belles lanterne: Nourredine makes the most beautiful lanterns on the island. I've got seven above my cannons. I… borrowed them. He knows and says nothing. He's a good man.
textes.Nourredine perce la nuit avec des millie: Nourredine pierces the night with thousands of little holes. He thinks he's making lanterns. He's making paintings. I spend my nights copying them.
Nourredine pierces the night with holes. His big lantern lights my circle every evening, and my stories are better for it. He never hears them to the end: he's working.
textes.Nourredine perce les lanternes, moi je l: Nourredine pierces the lanterns, I shape them. We've been arguing for forty years about who has the finer trade. It's me.
textes.Nourrissantes ! Vous avez parlé à Corali: Filling! You've been talking to Coralin, you have. That's his word. He's been saying it for four hundred years, and he buys a bag from me every week. Beware of people who say “filling”.
textes.Nous avons comparé nos calendriers, pour: We compared our calendars, to celebrate the Serpent on the same day. The dates didn't fall the same way. Their astronomer, Ah Kin Pech, counted on his fingers all afternoon, then declared that both our dates were right. Ix Kanul and I found that answer unacceptable. At last we agreed on something.
textes.Nous avons signé notre traité sur une se: We signed our treaty on a Crâne Fendu napkin: at hers, you play small and eat well; at mine, you play big and don't eat. I signed with my name. She signed with a cross, pressed very hard. I asked no questions. A cross drawn by Mama Grog is worth all the signatures in the world.
textes.Nous cacher ? Non. Nous attendons. La me: Hide? No. We're waiting. The sea has its reasons; one day it will give us back our island. Meanwhile, the dome is our sky.
textes.Nous commerçons avec les trois autres pe: We trade with the island's three other peoples. Not always gladly, but we trade. Matthias, our cartographer, will tell you all that better than I can.
textes.Nous habitions la maison 7. Papa et mama: We lived at number 7. Papa and Mama were roofers, and in the evening, Mama sewed umbrellas “for those who are between two roofs”. Achille, four years younger than me, jumped off the workshop roof with them. I held the spare umbrella and counted the bumps: seventeen before I turned ten. I still have the list, with the dates.
textes.Nous jouons aux dames de basalte chaque: We play basalt draughts every week. When I'm thinking about a move, Ébène starts telling a story. I listen, and I lose. On his birthday, I let him win on purpose. He thinks it's thanks to the story. Maybe that's a little bit true: his stories are very good.
textes.Nous nous disputions les vieilles bottes: We used to fight over the old boots that fell off the cliff. So we signed a truce: every first Monday of the month, at the foot of the crane, I swap a left boot for a right boot, and we each make up our pairs. It's very official. We don't talk, we swap. Like spies, but with boots.
textes.Nous nous disputons depuis des années po: For years we've argued over whether Skull Rock faces north or east. He says east, because Barbe-Sanglante loved the rising sun. Me, I measured: north-north-east. He said: “You see? It's looking a bit east.” We celebrated at the Crâne Fendu. He paid. The first time in thirty years.
textes.Nous nous disputons depuis dix ans l'inv: For ten years we've been arguing over who invented fire-cinnamon tea. She put in the cinnamon; I put in the hot water and wrote down the recipe. My mother says it was her, because she grew the cinnamon. We drink it together every winter, arguing. It's the best herbal tea in the city.
textes.Nous nous disputons depuis dix ans pour: For ten years we've been arguing over who invented fire-cinnamon tea. I say it was me: I put in the cinnamon. She says it was her: she put in the hot water. Mother Brasille, her mother, says it was herself, because she grew the cinnamon. We can't agree. We drink it together.
textes.Nous nous sommes disputés tout un dîner: We argued through a whole dinner about the wild dogs of the lava field. He wanted to drive them away, I wanted to understand them. The next day, I brought him a list of names for the wild dogs, in case we ever tamed them. He laughed. But he folded the list and put it in his pocket. I saw him.
textes.Nous nous sommes disputés une heure, à l: We argued for an hour at the fair: Kukulkan or Quetzalcóatl, who saw the Feathered Serpent first? Néferet listened without a word. At the end, she sighed: “Where I come from, the serpent is the enemy of the sun.” Ix Kanul and I fell silent. Then we drank a cacao together. In silence.
textes.Nous nous sommes mariés il y a dix jours: We got married ten days ago. Léa wanted to see the sea. I wanted to see Léa seeing the sea.
textes.Nous sommes arrivés le même automne, il: We arrived the same autumn, forty years ago. He's addressed me formally since day one. I've been on first-name terms with him since day one. Neither of us has ever given in.
textes.Nous verrons cela, Monsieur Bobor. Ma rè: We shall see about that, Monsieur Bobor. My ruler, if you please.
textes.Nous vivons sous le Cinquième Soleil. Qu: We live under the Fifth Sun. Four worlds came before it, and all were destroyed. This one will end too, one day, in earthquakes. But not today.
textes.Nous écrivons les nombres avec des point: We write numbers with dots and bars: a dot is worth one, a bar is worth five. Thirteen is two bars and three dots. Simple, isn't it?
textes.Nous étions une seule goutte, ma sœur Br: We were a single drop, my sister Brindille and I, on a leaf of the highest branch of Yggdrasil. One morning, a gust of wind split us in two. I stayed on the leaf. She rolled, and fell down through the clouds. I watched her fall until she was nothing but a dot. Then nothing at all.
textes.Nova, vous cherchez quelque chose ?: Nova, are you looking for something?
textes.Nox allume les réverbères de la cité. Il: Nox lights the city's street lamps. He talks little, blushes a lot, and knows every lantern by name. I think he writes poems. I even think I know who for.
textes.Nox allume les réverbères la nuit, et il: Nox lights the street lamps at night, and goes home to bed when I leave for the garden. As a boy, he used to fall into my cabbages thinking he could fly. Today, I give him mint to help him sleep. He's a nice boy. Too shy.
textes.Nox allume les réverbères pendant que je: Nox lights the street lamps while I play. He never applauds, he never says a thing, but he lights the lanterns in rhythm. One flame per note. It's the most beautiful applause I get.
textes.Nox emprunte des poèmes par la fenêtre,: Nox borrows poems through the window, at night, and brings them back before dawn. He signs with a single word: “Thank you”. We've never said more than twenty words to each other. All in writing.
textes.Nox écrit des poèmes comme on allume des: Nox writes poems the way you light lanterns: gently, one by one, so the night is less dark. He's teaching me poetry. He's very patient. I'm very slow. We get on well.
textes.Nox… j'ai trouvé une rime à « braise » !: Nox… I've found a rhyme for “ember”!
textes.Nuit calme. Il a chanté, vers trois heur: Quiet night. He sang, around three o'clock.
Nowhere, Pyrus. I'm taking a stroll.
textes.NÂGA ! Vaincu ! Par toi ! Gaston, sors l: NÂGA! Defeated! By you! Gaston, bring out the ceremonial barrel… Ah, it's coconut juice. Gaston, bring out the ceremonial coconut juice!

textes.Nâga plonge dans les abysses : tu ne peu: Nâga dives into the depths: you can't reach him anymore! The three Stone Eyes awaken… wake them with the amulet (E).
textes.Nâga pousse un dernier sifflement… et s': Nâga lets out one last hiss… and slowly sinks into the abyss. The Serpent is defeated!
textes.Nâga siffle de rage ! Il va cracher son: Nâga hisses with rage! He's about to spit his venom: don't stand in the green puddles.
textes.Nâga, le Serpent des Abysses: Nâga, the Serpent of the Abyss
textes.Nâga… Le Serpent des Abysses. Sur ma car: Nâga… The Serpent of the Abyss. On my map, there's just a big black drawing and the word “NO” written three times. I'll make you some soup. For afterwards. If there is an afterwards.
textes.Né dans une forge. Ma mère soufflait le: Born in a forge. My mother worked the bellows. My father hammered the iron. Me, I slept in a basket, next to the anvil. The sound of the hammer was my lullaby. Even today, I sleep badly when it's quiet. My first word was “hot”. The second, “more”. My father was proud. My mother, a bit less.
textes.Néferet ! Je peux sonner le sistre demai: Néferet! Can I shake the sistrum tomorrow?
textes.Néferet ! La meilleure élève que j'aie j: Néferet! The best pupil I ever had. She writes better than me, she sings better than me, and she corrects me in public. That last point, I forgive her for. Slowly.
textes.Néferet ! Ton chat dort toujours dans la: Néferet! Your cat is still asleep in the margin.
Néferet is the calmest of us all. She wears my robes, she blesses my looms, and she listens without judging. When Sennefer left, she came every evening. I haven't forgotten.
textes.Néferet sert Rê, le soleil des Égyptiens: Néferet serves Ra, the sun of the Egyptians, who travels by night in a boat. She is as calm as the water of a cenote. We see each other every year, at the fair of the longest day. I look forward to it.
textes.Néferet sert le soleil des Égyptiens. El: Néferet serves the sun of the Egyptians. She says it is reborn by itself, every morning, without the help of men. I disagree. But she says it so calmly that I sometimes doubt. Rarely.
textes.Néferet, c'est la prêtresse de Rê ! Elle: Néferet is the priestess of Rê! She greets the sun every morning, and she lets me shake the sistrum. She knows everything about the gods. And she never gets cross. Well, almost never.
textes.Néferet, c'est la prêtresse de Rê. Je la: Néferet is the priestess of Rê. I ferry her across to the other bank every day. She looks like she's asleep in my boat. She never sleeps. She hears everything. Watch out.
textes.Néferet. Moins de copal, cette année. Pr: Néferet. Less copal this year. I promise.
textes.Néferet. Ton soleil a bien traversé sa n: Néferet. Did your sun make it through the night?
textes.Néopolis — la ville qui ne dort jamais :: Neopolis — the city that never sleeps: glass towers, neon lights, flying cars…
textes.Néopolis, au sud de l'archipel: Neopolis, in the south of the archipelago
textes.Néopolis, la ville qui ne dort jamais: Neopolis, the city that never sleeps
