textes.Parler à Gédéon après le concert (à la H: Talk to Gédéon after the concert (at the Howling Hall, or the next day in town)
textes.Parler à Hector, l'armurier (rue du Phar: Talk to Hector, the armourer (Lighthouse Street)
textes.Parler à Jack après le concert (près de: Talk to Jack after the concert (near the stage, or the next day)
textes.Parler à Mange-Clous, le cuisinier du Re: Talk to Mange-Clous, the cook of the Requin Borgne (on the deck of the Requin Borgne in the morning, by the fireplace of the Crâne Fendu around noon, at the nets on the quay in the afternoon)
textes.Parler à Pauline, la femme de chambre (a: Talk to Pauline, the chambermaid (at the Grand Hotel: in the corridors in the morning and afternoon, in the hotel garden at noon)
textes.Parler à Rouille après le concert (à la: Talk to Rouille after the concert (at the Howling Hall, or the next day at the Cannery)
Tell me about the Wisteria Cottage.
textes.Parrain Pépin, il vient tous les matins: Godfather Pépin comes every morning to bring the flour, at a run. He lets me bang his drum. And he tells me about my papa. He's the best godfather in all of Ramure. In the whole world, even.
textes.Parrain a un chronomètre qui fait tic-ta: Godfather has a stopwatch that goes tick-tock, it comes from Cliquetis. One day he timed me eating a mooncake. Two minutes! He said: “Two minutes for a cake, Mochi, new record!” He told everyone. Mummy didn't think it was funny. Me, I wanted to beat the record. Mummy hid the cakes.
textes.Parrain me raconte papa. Il dit que papa: Godfather tells me about Papa. He says Papa burned every loaf, that he laughed so loud the birds flew out of the Mother Oak, and that one day he made a loaf so black they used it to prop open the bakery door. The loaf's still there. I've seen it. It's really black.
textes.Partez ! Jusqu'à la porte du phare !: Go! All the way to the lighthouse door!
textes.Partir dans la forêt des brumes avec un: To set off into the misty forest with an empty basket, and come back with the plant that brings a fever down in one night. I'll come back. I promised myself. And I'm taking seaweed for the road.
All over your beach hut, for instance.
Everywhere. Leave it. It suits you.
textes.Paré ! Pourquoi on dit « larguer » ?: Ready! Why do we say “cast off”?
textes.Paré à larguer, capitaine Nina ?: Ready to cast off, Captain Nina?
textes.Pas assez de pièces, {surnom}. Va pêcher: Not enough coins, {surnom}. Go fishing and bring me some fish, I'll buy it from you.
textes.Pas assez de place ici pour qu'un aigle: Not enough room here for a giant eagle to land. Go to an open area.
textes.Pas assez de place pour déplier l'Alouet: Not enough room to unfold the propeller Alouette here (it needs clear ground).
textes.Pas aujourd'hui, Coquille ! Un récif dan: Not today, Coquille! A reef in your way?
textes.Pas aujourd'hui. Il y a des choses qu'on: Not today. Some things you don't tell to just anybody.
textes.Pas aujourd'hui. Je ne suis pas d'humeur: Not today. I'm not in the mood to sell. Or to talk. Or anything.
Not today… Fine. Here, have a crust.
textes.Pas avant que vous ayez corrigé le retar: Not until you've corrected yesterday's delay.
textes.Pas beaucoup… Chut, je ne juge pas. Chaq: Not much… Shh, I'm not judging. Every reader starts with a first book. Sit here, I'll pick you a very small one. With pictures.
textes.Pas besoin d'oser : approche doucement,: No need to dare: come closer gently, talk to them kindly. They love being told hello. Like everyone, really.
textes.Pas ce soir, ma chère. J'ai vu ton tourn: Not tonight, my dear. I saw your screwdriver.
Not against Germaine. She runs hot.
textes.Pas d'animal ? Pas même un petit scarabé: No pet? Not even a little scarab? Oh… Come with me to the temple, there are soft cats sleeping in the sun. They belong a bit to everyone.
There's no deep enough water in front of you.
textes.Pas d'un pouce ? Même avec le vent ?: Not an inch? Not even with the wind?
Not an inch. It's waiting for you.
textes.Pas d'un pouce… Et les chênes ?: Not an inch… And the oaks?
textes.Pas d'épée ? Et tu traverses la mer comm: No sword? And you cross the sea like that? Hm. Come back. I'll give you a price. An armourer's price, not a friend's price.
textes.Pas dans la Citadelle : le vent y est tr: Not in the Citadel: the wind is too violent there. Land on the Wind Perch, south of the island.
Not in my workshop, this time.
textes.Pas de blagues pendant la fête, cette fo: No jokes during the festival, this time.
textes.Pas de caillou ?! Dans une MONTAGNE ?! V: No pebble?! In a MOUNTAIN?! Go pick one up outside, big fella. They're everywhere. That's sort of the whole point of a mountain.
textes.Pas de canon à confettis à bord… Le chan: No confetti cannon on board… The Port-Azur shipyard installs a very pretty one.
textes.Pas de chanson ? Tu me demandes de ne pa: No song? You're asking me not to breathe!
textes.Pas de chichis ! Tiens. Tu me remerciera: No fuss! Here. You'll thank me later.
textes.Pas de honte, champion. Il y a des gens: No shame in that, champ. Plenty of fine people can't swim. If you like, I'll give you lessons, early in the morning, when nobody's around. Nobody. It stays between us.
textes.Pas de longue-vue à bord… Le chantier na: No spyglass on board… The Port-Azur shipyard installs one.
textes.Pas de photo ? Quelle misère… Bon. Je re: No photos? What a disaster… All right. I respect that. Sylvie would say you're right: you see better without. She's often right. It's exhausting.
No photos of my canvas, Gérard.
textes.Pas de pieds, pas de danfe. C'est logiqu: No feet, no danthe. It maketh thenthe.
textes.Pas de point de talent : gagne un niveau: No talent points: gain a level.
textes.Pas de poisson ? Ici ? À Tazira ? Ho ho…: No fish? Here? In Tazira? Ho ho… I have a plan. I'll make you love fish. With honey! You won't even know it's fish. Well, you will: it'll smell a bit.
textes.Pas de poisson. Juste le tajine. Deux fo: No fish. Just the tajine. Twice.
textes.Pas de porte… Un voyageur sans maison. C: No door… A traveller with no home. Very romantic, and very bad for the rugs. Here, you will always have an open door. And a doormat.
textes.Pas de queue du tout ?! Mais comment tu: No tail at all?! But how do you show you're happy? With your eyebrows? Show me! … Ha ha ha! That's so weird!
textes.Pas de souci ! La porte est toujours ouv: No worries! The door is always open. Like my muscles. Uh… well, you know what I mean.
textes.Pas de terre ferme sous Ventaile : survo: No solid ground beneath Ventaile: fly over an island to land.
textes.Pas de vertige, toi. Hrmm. Penche-toi. R: No fear of heights, you. Hrmm. Lean out. Look at the sea.
textes.Pas demain non plus. Merci pour les noix: Not tomorrow either. Thanks for the coconuts.
Not from the rowboat: dock first.
textes.Pas devant les mouettes, monsieur le mai: Not in front of the seagulls, Mr Mayor.
Not in front of the seagulls.
textes.Pas devant mon étal !: Not in front of my stall!
textes.Pas du tout ! C'est le chat !: Not at all! It was the cat!
textes.Pas du tout ? Alors tu n'en as jamais vu: Not at all? Then you've never had one look at you. I have. It didn't even smile at me, and I still dropped my net.
textes.Pas du tout ? Dans une cité de démons ?: Not at all? In a city of demons? Oh, poor little flame. Well. You've still got Grumbald's frozen lava. And my friendship, which never stings.
textes.Pas du tout ? Hm. Tu as peut-être raison: Not at all? Hm. Maybe you're right. But tell me: have you ever seen the eyes of Skull Rock light up? No? Then wait a little before deciding.
textes.Pas du tout ? Tout le monde sait danser: Not at all? Everyone can dance! Can you walk? Then you can dance. You just have to walk in rhythm. Tum, tum, tum. There. You're dancing.
textes.Pas du tout ? Tu as traversé la mer et t: Not at all? You crossed the sea and you can't tie a knot? Fatima, come and see this! … She's laughing. She's laughing, {surnom}. Sit down, we'll start from the beginning.
textes.Pas du tout ? Ça doit être reposant. Moi: Not at all? That must be restful. If a seagull gives me a funny look, I wonder what I've done. I'd like to be like you. One day. Maybe.
textes.Pas du tout ? … Ah. Bon. Il y a plus de: Not at all? … Ah. Well. There are more people than you'd think, you know. Many more. People just don't say so, that's all.
textes.Pas du tout ?! Devant une poissonnière ?: Not at all?! To a fishwife?! … Fine. I forgive you, because you've got a nice face. But don't say it too loud at the port. The mackerel have ears.
textes.Pas du tout ?! Mais on t'a jamais rien a: Not at all?! Did nobody ever teach you anything? Come here. Shiny eye, nice red gills, gleaming skin. And if the fishmonger's singing, you can buy.
Not at all. I can see your feet.
Not in the middle of the sea! Dock first.
textes.Pas encore ! Alors vous êtes le seul êtr: Not yet! Then you're the only being in the world with no opinion. Enjoy it, it's a very restful state. And it costs six coins to leave it.
textes.Pas encore ! J'adore. Alors on s'y met q: Not yet! I love it. So when do we start? Tomorrow? I make the rocket, Margot does the sums, and you do… the courage. You need lots of it, afterwards. For explaining.
textes.Pas encore ! Laissez-lui le temps de gra: Not yet! Give him time to grow.
textes.Pas encore ! Voilà une réponse de coureu: Not yet! Now that's a runner's answer. “Not yet” is almost “soon”. I timed you while you said it: one second. Fast!
textes.Pas encore ? Mais c'est gratuit ! Montez: Not yet? But it's free! Hop on when it's landed, I'll give you a wave. Take the left-hand seat, on the Stoneheart side. The view… you'll see the view.
textes.Pas encore de bague ? Patience. L'amour: No ring yet? Patience. Love has waited a hundred years, after all.
textes.Pas encore ma baguette ? Tout en haut de: Still no wand? Right at the top of the cave, on the ledge, to the west!
textes.Pas encore, Mixtli. Mais ne tombe plus d: Not yet, Mixtli. But don't fall into my canals again!
Not yet, Dad. A seam to finish.
textes.Pas encore, professeur. Pas avec vous de: Not yet, Professor. Not with you inside.
textes.Pas encore. Il a toussé ce matin, le Pet: Not yet. The Petit Piston coughed this morning!
Not yet. He's waiting. Like a jaguar.
textes.Pas encore. Il le garde pour l'hiver, je: Not yet. He's saving it for winter, I think.
Not yet. I've got two more calculations.
Not yet. I've got a seam to finish.
textes.Pas encore. Mais il a l'air de réfléchir: Not yet. But it looks like it's thinking.
Not yet. Not with you inside.
textes.Pas encore… C'est un beau mot, « encore: Not yet… “Yet” is a lovely word. Then Ramure will wait for you, little one. We know how to wait, here: the moon has been full for so long.
textes.Pas grave ! Tu n'as qu'à me demander : j: Never mind! Just ask me: I'll look for you. I do that for everyone here. For free. Well, for a pearl.
textes.Pas grave, matelot ! Tout le monde comme: No worries, sailor! Everyone starts somewhere. I'll give you a free lesson: tiller to the left, boat to the right. Or the other way round. Well, we'll see on the water.
textes.Pas la Morue ! Ici, c'est le Sans-Pitié: Not the Cod! Here, it's the Merciless!
textes.Pas le temps ! Comme moi, alors. Ce n'es: No time! Like me, then. That's not a compliment, {surnom}. Sit down. There. Three breaths. You see, that didn't take long.
textes.Pas maintenant, Pépin ! Je calcule un tr: Not now, Pépin! I'm calculating something!
textes.Pas mal ! Trois pompes ! Bon, deux et de: Not bad! Three push-ups! Well, two and a half. It's a start!
Not bad, Zoé. Not bad at all.
textes.Pas mal, pas mal. Un peu de vague à l'âm: Not bad, not bad. Feeling a little at sea. But then, the sea is where I'm most at home, isn't it?
textes.Pas mal. Je le mets de côté avec les vin: Not bad. I'll put it aside with the other twenty.
Not bad… for a big one.
textes.Pas même un mouton, capitaine. J'ai bien: Not even a sheep, captain. I looked carefully.
textes.Pas pendant le trajet ! Attends d'être a: Not during the trip! Wait until you've arrived.
textes.Pas pendant que je parle à mes fées, s'i: Not while I'm speaking to my fairies, if you please.
textes.Pas pendant une éruption ! La Marmite cr: Not during an eruption! The Cooking Pot spits, step back a little…
textes.Pas pour un tajine célèbre jusqu'à Carèn: Not for a tagine famous all the way to Carène.
textes.Pas question ! Tlaloc garde son tonnerre: No way! Tlaloc keeps his thunder at home!
textes.Pas si vite ! Je suis maîtresse, pas dan: Not so fast! I'm a teacher, not a dancer.
textes.Pas si vite, Nenetl. Pas si vite !: Not so fast, Nenetl. Not so fast!
textes.Pas sur le quai, l'Amiral ! Tu vas faire: Not on the quay, Admiral! You'll scare the fishermen.
textes.Pas terrible. Grommelot m'a encore trait: Not great. Grommelot called me a “glitter gnat” again.
Not every one. Every other one.
textes.Pas trop ? Tiens, ma gourde. Bois. Encor: Not much? Here, my water bottle. Drink. A bit more. There. Now you can dance. Not before, {surnom}.
textes.Pas trop bas, Barnabé. Les fougères s'en: Not too deeply, Barnabé. The ferns still remember.
textes.Pas trop haut. Il faut redescendre, aprè: Not too high. You have to come back down afterwards.
textes.Pas trop sucré, tu es sûre ?: Not too sweet, are you sure?
textes.Pas trop vite. Mes chaises sont fatiguée: Not too fast. My chairs are tired.
textes.Pas trop. Je tiens à garder mes auditeur: Not too slow. I'd like to keep my listeners.
textes.Pas trop… C'est honnête. Mange trois car: Not very… That's honest. Eat three carrots, not one more, and shoot off like an arrow. You'll still be “not very”, but with style.
Not a word. That's an order.
textes.Pas une clé ! Une serrure ! Pour aller a: Not a key! A lock! To go with your gate.
textes.Pas une seule paire ! Rien que des chaus: Not a single pair! Only lone socks. Every one has a story. That one went around the whole archipelago inside a fisherman's boot.
textes.Pas une seule pièce ? Bon… pour toi, c'e: Not a single coin? Well… for you, it's free! A welcome gift.
Not one single row. One single candle.
textes.Pas vraiment ? Ce n'est rien, ça s'appre: Not really? That's nothing, you can learn! A map is a story seen from above. North at the top, the sea in blue, and the monsters in the corners.
textes.Pas vraiment ? Hm. Je note : « Citoyen e: Not really? Hm. I'm noting: “Demanding citizen.” Being demanding is very good. Write a complaint. I won't read it, but do write it.
textes.Pas à bord de L'Hirondelle ! Attends d'ê: Not aboard L'Hirondelle! Wait until you're on the dock.
Not to me, Thalion. To them.
textes.Passe demain. J'ai de l'huile de lin tou: Come by tomorrow. I've got fresh linseed oil.
textes.Passe-moi le parmesan, s'il te plaît. Me: Pass me the parmesan, please. Thank you. Ramen.
textes.Passer Bondi. Au virage des racines, ava: Pass Bondi. At the root bend, before the Lookout. Once. … Just once.
textes.Passer au Borgo des Coquillettes, le ham: Stop by the Borgo of the Macaroni, the followers' hamlet
textes.Passer l'épreuve du contrat avec Ombreli: Take the contract test with Ombreline, the librarian (at the Library of Souls)
textes.Passer une nuit entière à la fête de la: Spend a whole night at the beach party, in front of the great wall of sound, without hiding behind a kapok tree. Dance until the sun comes up. My people would talk about it for a thousand years.
textes.Patatras ! Tu tombes dans le bac des piè: Crash! You fall into the spare parts bin. A sorting robot picks you up, stamps you “MISCELLANEOUS” and politely sets you back at the start of the line.
textes.Patronne ! J'ai fini le pétrin, je peux: Boss! I've finished the dough, can I dash off to the boat?
textes.Pauline fait d'excellents lits et d'épou: Pauline makes excellent beds and appalling gossip. I taught her hospital corners. I did not manage to teach her silence.
textes.Pauline fait très bien les lits et très: Pauline makes beds very well and keeps secrets very badly. The whole town knew I was sulking at my husband before my husband did.
textes.Pauline, Rosalie dit que Brioche aime vo: Pauline, Rosalie says Brioche likes your wool…
textes.Pauline, ma voisine, mon amie, ma petite: Pauline, my neighbour, my friend, my little chambermaid. She talks a lot, and I listen very well. We're made for each other, like the cup and the saucer.
textes.Pauline, my dear ! Une histoire pour mon: Pauline, my dear! A story for my new object?
textes.Paulo ! La même, avec un pantalon plus g: Paulo! Same again, with bigger trousers.
textes.Paulo ? Mon meilleur client et mon pire: Paulo? My best customer and my worst prankster. He tells everyone I steal his croissants. I'm the one who makes his croissants!
textes.Paulo ? Un grand cuisinier, une grande b: Paulo? A great cook, a big mouth and a great ingrate. He says my voice puts heart into his soup, and then he calls my sea bream old. I have dinner at his place every evening. To make him feel ashamed.
textes.Paulo a dit que mes daurades n'étaient p: Paulo said my sea bream wasn't fresh enough anymore, and Lola repeated it to the whole quay. At Rosalie's! I swore it was caught that morning. Well. Between us: it was Fernand who'd kept them overnight in his bucket, the old rascal. I found out afterwards. If Paulo knew, he'd never buy another scale from him. So I took the blame for him.
textes.Paulo cherche des poissons pour sa bouil: Paulo's looking for fish for his bouillabaisse. He says Rosalie's sea bream aren't fresh enough any more. Don't repeat that.
textes.Paulo est un génie, un ténor et un dange: Paulo is a genius, a tenor and a danger to my belt. His bouillabaisse is the best in the archipelago. The others are just soups, he's right.
textes.Paulo fait la meilleure bouillabaisse de: Paulo makes the best bouillabaisse in the archipelago, with my fish. Still, something's missing. I don't know what. I'm working on it.
textes.Paulo nous nourrit tous les soirs, même: Paulo feeds us every evening, even when we're not speaking. Especially when we're not speaking. He sings very loudly, but always at the right moment.
textes.Paulo veut des poissons pêchés du jour :: Paulo wants fish caught today: two sea bream and two mackerel.
textes.Paulo vient avec une marmite ? Ulric ave: Paulo's coming with a cooking pot? Ulric with frogs? And a fiddler pirate? (He jots it all down in his notebook, full of ink.) Stop the presses! That's the front page of the next Boucanier: “THE ISLANDS MEET AT THE BOUCAN!” And underneath, in small print: “thanks to a heroic poster courier.” That's you. Here, for your tired feet, and a zine still warm from the press.
Paulo. Not in front of the customers.

textes.Pavillon rangé dans le coffre. Discret,: Flag put away in the chest. Discreet, the captain…
textes.Payer dix pièces à Églantine et poser la: Pay Églantine ten coins and lay your hand on the crystal ball (at the Adventurers' Guild counter, on the Great Square in the Middle Town)
textes.Payer trois cents pièces à Monsieur Pros: Pay three hundred coins to Mr Prosper (at his agency in the Upper Town, or in the garden of the Wisteria Cottage at noon)
textes.Peek' a creusé sous la vieille ruche de: Peek' dug under Yum Kab's old hive looking for a bone, and he made a tunnel. Now the bees go in through Peek's tunnel! Yum Kab says it's their back door. Peek' built a house for the bees! He's the most useful dog in Yaxché.
textes.Peek' a enterré un os dans la table de s: Peek' buried a bone in Ah Kin Pech's sand table, the one where he draws Venus. I was really scared he'd get angry. But when he dug up the bone, he found a mistake in his calculation, right underneath! Now Peek' is allowed into the observatory. He's the only astronomer dog in the world.
textes.Peindre Grosse-Dent, facile. Peindre toi: Paint Grosse-Dent, easy. Paint you, very hard.
textes.Peindre trois graffitis avec les bombes: Paint three graffiti with the spray paint cans (on the Expression Wall, west of the town, or on another paintable wall in Port-Boucan)
textes.Pelle, hache, épée. Rien de superflu. Et: Shovel, axe, sword. Nothing superfluous. And I buy back fish, shells and mushrooms.
textes.Penchez-vous. … C'est bien ce que je pen: Bend over. … Just as I thought.
textes.Pendant des années, j'ai crié sur mes fl: For years, I shouted at my flames to make them obey. They burned everything. One day, Brother Cendrin saw me at it and said: “You don't command a flame: you invite it.” I tried. The flame came and settled in my hand like a kitten. Ever since, I've taught the politeness of flames.
textes.Pendant des années, j'ai trouvé un pain: For years I found an extra loaf at the foot of my tower, every week, on the same day. I thought it was a mistake. The day Lyra came home, the extra loaf stopped. I understood. I didn't tell Sylwen. It was good, that loaf waiting for someone else.
textes.Pendant des années, je l'ai observé sans: For years, I watched him without his knowing. Every morning, before lighting his forge, he lays his big hand on the bark of his kapok tree and tells it: “Hang in there, old girl.” Then he grumbles very loudly, so nobody thinks he's kind.
textes.Pendant deux siècles, j'ai traversé la b: For two centuries, I crossed the mist every spring to watch over the Sacred Tree, without ever showing myself to the humans. Then one morning, I found a grey leaf at its roots. Then ten. Then a hundred. I told my mother I wouldn't come home until it could breathe again. She gave me her cloak and said nothing. Where I come from, that's like crying.
textes.Pendant l'affaire des croissants, Bruno: During the croissant case, Bruno was a witness, since he closes late. So I decided to keep the ice-cream man under surveillance. Three evenings in front of his kiosk, standing, eyes sharp, a cone in my hand so as not to attract attention. Three cones per evening. The surveillance was a success: Bruno stole nothing.
textes.Pendant l'affaire des croissants, le bri: During the croissant affair, the sergeant staked out the bakery. All night, on the bench, in uniform. At four, opening up the bakehouse, I found him asleep, his kepi over his nose. Six croissants were missing. I put the seventh in his hand. He woke with a start and said: “Exhibit A.”
textes.Pendant l'heure où j'ai chanté seule à l: During the hour I sang alone at the Dawn festival, Nessa never stopped dancing in front of the stage, so nobody would look at my trembling hands. A whole hour, to words I was making up as I went along. She didn't miss a single step. I still don't know how.
textes.Pendant l'hiver gris, Faelar nous racont: During the grey winter, Faelar told us about banquets to make us forget we were hungry. Tarts, roasts, brioches as big as houses. I put my hand up and said: “That makes it worse.” He laughed: “Then you make some.” I took him at his word. He's never got over it.
textes.Pendant l'hiver gris, il y a trois cent: During the grey winter, three hundred and fifty years ago, there was almost nothing left to eat. I told the children about feasts to comfort them. Little Sylwen raised her hand: “That makes it worse, Faelar. Now I'm even hungrier.” The next day, her hands were in her mother's flour. She's never taken them out.
textes.Pendant l'inspection de ma chaudière, j': During the inspection of my boiler, I blew a tiny bubble around Héloïse's monocle. She kept it for four seconds, without moving, without blinking. Then she said: “Regulation.” And she went on with her inspection. I think it's the nicest thing a chief engineer has ever said to me.
textes.Pendant la Grande Course, j'ai passé la: During the Great Race, I got through the first arch all by myself! And then Godfather Pépin caught me, hop, under the arms. He said: “Not yet, little arrow.” I kicked him, but nice kicks. Afterwards he carried me on his shoulders to the finish, to see Uncle win. You could see everything from up there.

During the Great Race, I got through the first arch, and Uncle Bondi turned round, right in the middle of the race, to wave at me! With both paws! Everyone shouted. Grisou nearly overtook him. Afterwards Uncle said he did it on purpose, to make it funnier. He won anyway. He always wins.
textes.Pendant la dernière tempête, l'antenne d: During the last storm, the Radio Boucan antenna blew off the mast of the Rusty Whale and landed on top of the painted water tower. Without it, Sergeant Fréquence is talking to nobody.
textes.Pendant la grande tempête, il y a deux a: During the great storm, two years ago, the fresh water barrel split. Without water, we were lost. Tonneau repaired it in the middle of the night, in the rolling hold, with iron hoops and a song. By morning, not a drop was leaking, and he was perfectly sober. It's the only time I've seen him like that. He scared me a bit.
textes.Pendant la grande tempête, la barrique d: During the great storm, the fresh-water cask split. The captain came down into the hold and said to me: “Tonneau, this is your trade.” So I did my trade, all night, with my hoops and my mallet. In the morning, he shook my hand. Only once in ten years. I didn't wash that hand for a week.
textes.Pendant la leçon des jours, je dormais u: During the lesson on the days, I was having a little sleep. Citlali said “Itzcuintli”, the day of the dog, and Tlaco barked. At just the right moment! Everyone laughed, and I woke up. I asked if it was playtime. It wasn't playtime. Now Tlaco sits in the front row. Me, still at the back.
textes.Pendant la leçon sur les jours du calend: During the lesson on the days of the calendar, Pilli was asleep. Tlaco, meanwhile, was sitting up straight. When I said “Itzcuintli”, the day of the dog, Tlaco barked. Once. Right on cue. The whole class laughed. Pilli woke up and asked if it was break time. Since then, Tlaco has had a seat in the front row.
textes.Pendant la prière du matin, il a ouvert: During the morning prayer, he opened his gourd. The mosquito stung me on the nose. I cried out. Kinich said, delighted: “You're a real one! The wooden mannequins don't cry out!” He wanted to check, like the Twins in Xibalba. I finished the prayer with a red nose. He had learned the story well.
textes.Pendant la prière, j'ai ouvert ma caleba: During the prayer, I opened my gourd to check whether Ix Kanul was a real person, like in the story of the wooden dolls. Xan bit her on the nose! She shouted “Ouch!”. So I knew she was real. She wasn't happy. But at the end, she told me: “Good method. Bad timing.”
textes.Pendant la roulade (Ctrl), les coups pas: During the roll (Ctrl), blows pass right through you. It goes further and costs less stamina. In VR: click the left stick to dodge.
textes.Pendant le dîner des ambassadeurs, ma fu: During the ambassadors' dinner, my test rocket took an unexpected turn and dived into the palace soup tureen. Asmodin didn't flinch: he put out the curtains with one hand, served the flambéed soup with the other and announced the “house speciality”. The finest composure I've ever seen. I wanted to shake his hand. He banned me from the palace.
textes.Pendant le dîner des ambassadeurs, une f: During the ambassadors' dinner, one of Monsieur Zigomar's rockets came in through the window and dived into the soup tureen. I put out the curtains, served the flambéed soup and announced: “House speciality.” People still ask for it. I have never forgiven Monsieur Zigomar. I kept the recipe.

During the ambassadors' dinner, one of Monsieur Zigomar's rockets came in through the open window and dived into the soup tureen. I put out the curtains with one hand, served with the other, and announced: “Flambéed soup, house speciality.” The ambassador of the northern isles had seconds twice. I have never told Monsieur Zigomar.
textes.Pendant les orages, je monte sur la tour: During storms, I climb the tower with a kite and a key. Héloïse says it's dangerous. Héloïse is right. But it's magnificent.
textes.Pendant les trois jours de pluie, ses ha: During the three days of rain, her beans floated away, in a line, like a procession for Tlaloc. I came to help her, in the rain, with a little net. We fished them out one by one. She was laughing and throwing wet beans at me. She said: “Your next jar, make it a little less beautiful.” I couldn't. I just can't help it.
textes.Pendant longtemps, je n'ai pas su où ma: For a long time, I didn't know where my other half had fallen. One day, Zéphyr came back from the elves' island with a soaking wet letter. It said: “I think I'm your other half. I always lose everything.” I knew straight away it was Brindille. Nobody else writes with tears.
textes.Pendant ma semaine au lit chez elle, apr: During my week in bed at her house, after the bedsheet, Mother Sage taught me to knit so I'd keep still. I made a scarf. It had more holes than wool. She wears it anyway, every winter. She says the holes let the skin breathe. I think she says it for my sake.
textes.Pendant mon apprentissage, il me faisait: During my apprenticeship, he made me redo every weld. Every one. I'd weld it again, he'd run his thumb over it, say “Hm”, and I'd start again. After eight months, he ran his thumb over it, said nothing, and set his own lamp down next to mine. It's the finest compliment I've ever received.
textes.Pendant qu'elle me tatouait, j'avais le: While she was tattooing me, I had hiccups. At every hiccup, Coralie said “Don't move!” and I answered “Hic!”. It lasted three hours. At the end, she was all red and I was very proud. She told me I could go and show off my octopus. I ran off to show off my horse. We've never agreed.
textes.Pendant quarante ans, Sigrun a lavé mes: For forty years, Sigrun washed my barrels, hauled my barley and tasted my batches. She wanted to touch the big vat. I'd say: “Next year.” One morning, she left without saying goodbye. She'd left the big vat clean as a mirror. I cried into it. Made a salty batch.
textes.Pendant quarante ans, j'ai livré les bag: For forty years, I delivered the baguettes to the Café de la Place. To Gisèle's mother first, a woman who counted the baguettes twice and the crumbs once. Little Gisèle used to wait for me at the door to get the crusty end. When I deliver for Margaux, I still give her the crusty end. She still eats it.
textes.Pendant que Lyra veillait son arbre, je: While Lyra was watching over her tree, every week I set a little loaf aside for her, in case she came home. She didn't come, so I gave it to Thalion. He never knew why he got an extra loaf. The day she came back, I gave her the whole batch.
textes.Pendant que je danse, Mère-Lune garde sa: While I dance, Mother Moon keeps her blanket over her knees. But underneath, her paws move. In rhythm. Exactly my steps, even the ones she never taught me. The children say she's the dancing she-wolf of the legend. I don't dare ask her. Oh… what if it were true?
textes.Pendant six ans, j'ai balayé la suie de: For six years, I swept the soot in the workshop. The professor would walk behind me saying: “Leave a bit, Capucine, soot is memory!” So I made little heaps, one per experiment, with a label. The day I left, there were a hundred and four. He kept them. All of them.
textes.Pendant son vol, il a posé une question: During his flight, he asked a question about the gas every five minutes. Gustave reported every one of them to me. “Does it smell of cabbage because it's cabbage?” “What if we light a match?” Gustave answered “I don't know” and “absolutely not”. Léonce wrote it all down in a notebook. I'm keeping an eye on that notebook.
textes.Pendant trente ans, Marcel a frappé à ma: For thirty years, Marcel knocked on my door every day, letter or not. On days without, he'd lift his cap: “Nothing today, Hortense.” On the day he retired, he knocked one last time and said: “Nothing today, Hortense. Nor tomorrow.” I laughed. That doesn't happen often.
textes.Pendant trente ans, je suis passé chez H: For thirty years, I stopped at Hortense's every day. On days with no letter, I'd tip my cap: “Nothing today, Hortense.” She'd say: “Thank you, Marcel.” As if I'd brought her something. I think I did bring her something. Sometimes nothing is better than nothing at all.
textes.Pendant un an, Hugo m'a acheté un bouque: For a year, Hugo bought a bouquet from me every morning “for his mother”. The day his mother came into the shop and sneezed eleven times in front of the hyacinths, I understood: hay fever, her whole life! I didn't say anything to Hugo. I just started making him pollen-free bouquets. In case they were for me.
textes.Pendant un an, chaque soir, au coucher d: For a whole year, every evening at sunset, I sat on the jetty writing a song to the sea. The Azur Waltz. Three pages. The day I wrote the last note, a gust of wind snatched them off my knees. Three pages, three directions. I ran. The wind runs faster.
textes.Pendant un an, j'ai acheté un bouquet ch: For a year, I bought a bouquet every morning “for my mother”. One day, Mum came into the shop to see where all those flowers were coming from. She sneezed eleven times in front of the hyacinths. Hay fever. Léa understood everything. She didn't say a word: she went on selling me bouquets, with a little less pollen.
textes.Pendant un exercice, Ortie devait allume: During an exercise, Ortie was supposed to light a single candle, from ten paces. She lit all thirty candles in the courtyard at once, with a single snap of her fingers. The class applauded. Then she lit my shoes. I gave her twenty out of twenty for precision, and zero for discretion.
textes.Pendant un match, j'ai ouvert ma calebas: During a match, I opened my gourd so Xan could watch Chak play. Xan bit Chak on the hip! Right at the big shot! The ball went really close to the ring. Really close! Chak says it was almost in. I say Xan helped him. Without Xan, the ball would have gone way wide.
textes.Pendant un mois, Pyrus est venu vérifier: For a month, Pyrus came to check his armour every day. It had been finished for three weeks. On the last day, he stood rooted in front of the anvil, bright red, without a word. I put down my hammer and said: “Yes.” He asked: “Yes what?” I answered: “Ask your question, and you'll see.”
textes.Pendant une Grande Alerte des Navets (qu: During a Great Turnip Alert (when Mélusine rings her bell, in the daytime), run to the Southern Fields (south of town, through the South Gate), catch five runaway turnips with a little tap, then bring them to Père Gaubert (in his fields, near the farm)
textes.Pendant une cérémonie, il s'entraînait c: During a ceremony, he was practising against the temple wall. The ball bounced, and went down the ninety-one steps, one by one, bonk, bonk, bonk, in front of the whole village at prayer. Kinich was counting out loud. Chak said it was an offering. I replied that the gods prefer silence.
textes.Pendant une cérémonie, je m'entraînais c: During a ceremony, I was practising against the temple wall. Just a little. The ball bounced and went down the whole staircase, ninety-one steps, in front of everyone. Kinich counted out loud. At the last one, he shouted: “Ninety-one!” Everyone looked at Ix Kanul. Me, I looked at my feet.
textes.Pendant une interrogation d'histoire, Pé: During a history test, Pépin handed in a blank paper, with just a drawing in one corner: me, as a big bat, yawning. The drawing was remarkably accurate. I gave him zero in history and eighteen in drawing. I kept it. It's pinned above my desk.
textes.Pendant une offrande au Cénote, une de m: During an offering at the Cenote, one of my bees landed on her nose. She didn't dare move. I whispered: “She thinks you're in bloom, priestess.” She laughed. Out loud. In front of the whole village. The next day, she told me: “Never again during a ceremony.” But she was still smiling.
textes.Pendant vingt ans, j'ai enseigné la lumi: For twenty years, I taught light. Then old Gaudence, the archmage back then, led me to the Circle and held out his staff to me. Aube Lunevoile sang the song that wakes the stones. Her daughter Ysolde held the lantern, sixteen years old, without blinking. I cried like an apprentice. The next day, I handed my light class over to Aurélien.
textes.Pense très fort à un lieu que tu as déjà: Think hard about a place you have already seen… and you'll be there. Choose your destination:
Think of those who are waiting for you, {surnom}. Their lantern is still burning. Send them a word through Plumette.
textes.Pensive. J'ai trouvé une énigme sans rép: Pensive. I've found a riddle with no answer. Unless the answer is “Grommelot”.
textes.Percer une lanterne si grande qu'elle po: To pierce a lantern so big it would lay the whole desert sky over the square, with the walking stars, like the caravans' lanterns. Abdellah would do the shape, of course. He'd grumble from the first hammer blow to the last.
textes.Perdu. Au moins, vous êtes honnête. Le p: Lost. At least you're honest. The lighthouse is to the east, the beach to the west, the square behind you. And if you don't know where to go any more, the harbour office is open until seven in the evening.
textes.Perlée ! Il a bu, mon cactus ?: Perlée! Has my cactus had a drink?
textes.Perlée ! Mes lucioles t'ont attendue, ce: Perlée! My fireflies waited for you this morning!
textes.Perlée est le calme du royaume. Elle con: Perlée is the calm of the kingdom. She knows every flower by name and every drop by its first name. When I'm worried, I go and sit at the edge of her pond.
textes.Perlée met une heure par fleur. Une heur: Perlée takes an hour per flower. An hour! In an hour, I can fly round the whole archipelago. She blames me for her drops. Drops are the wind's doing. Not mine. Well, a bit mine.
textes.Perlée parle à ses gouttes de rosée. Ell: Perlée talks to her dewdrops. They don't answer. Well, I don't think so.
Perlée talks to her dewdrops. They don't answer. Well, I don't think so. She's ever so calm, and she waters my pots without ever getting it wrong.
textes.Perlée se lève avant tout le monde pour: Perlée gets up before everyone else to set down her drops. She speaks ever so softly. I try to speak softly with her. I almost never manage.
textes.Perlée, c'est mon autre moitié. Elle n'a: Perlée is my other half. She's never lost a drop in her life. I love her with all my heart. But it's hard, being the half that loses things.
textes.Perroquet-Joe dit que ses perroquets son: Perroquet-Joe says his parrots are polite. They called me a “landlubber”. Is that polite?
textes.Personne ! Je suis un vrai fantôme ! Un: Nobody! I'm a real ghost! A ghost who has to be home before dinner, but a real one!
textes.Personne ? Hou… Écris-moi, alors. Je te: No one? Hoo… Then write to me. I'll write back. A real letter, with a stamp and a feather. That's a promise.
textes.Personne ? Ma doue. Eh bien maintenant,: Nobody? Ma doue. Well, now somebody is. Here, at the Bordée, there'll always be a crêpe for you and a chair by the stove. Don't argue.
textes.Personne ? Oh… Bon, je te prête Pomme-de: Nobody? Oh… Okay, I'll lend you Pomme-de-Pin! One day. Not for long, eh, she's mine. But one day, promise.
textes.Personne ? … Alors tu as beaucoup de ret: Nobody? … Then you're very far behind, {surnom}. Sit down. I'll start at the beginning, and we'll see where we've got to in a hundred years.
textes.Personne ? … Alors viens t'asseoir près: Nobody? … Then come and sit by me, now and then. I'll wait for you. I already know your step.
textes.Personne ici… pour l'instant. Allez salu: Nobody here… for now. Go and say hello to the locals!
textes.Personne n'a autant de chance. Personne: Nobody's that lucky. Nobody! You're cheating! Your turn to play… with my fists!
textes.Personne n'a jamais pris Tazira par la m: No one has ever taken Tazira from the sea. By trickery, once. Sixty years ago, a pirate turned up at the channel disguised as a salt merchant: Captain Sel. The caïd who let him in was my grandfather, Allal. That story isn't told on the Skala. I'm telling you once. Don't repeat it.
textes.Personne n'est blessé ? Parfait, on reco: Is anyone hurt? Good, let's go again.
textes.Personne n'habite plus ici depuis longte: Nobody has lived here for a long time. It smells of dust and old wood.
textes.Personne ne le sait, {surnom}. Il y a vi: Nobody knows this, {surnom}. Twenty years ago, I was the one carrying the golden seed, the only one the Mother Tree had made in three centuries. From my boat, I saw a human on a beach dancing with a parrot. I laughed, I leaned over… and the seed fell into the water. Barnabé picked up my mistake without knowing it. I've never dared tell him.
textes.Personne ne le sait. La nuit de l'orage,: Nobody knows this. On the night of the storm, I saw lights streaking towards the forest. I thought they were intruders. I shot. I didn't hit anything, I think. But they never came back, and the door closed. Since then, I don't shoot at what I don't understand. And I hardly sleep any more. … Don't repeat this, {surnom}.
textes.Personne ne m'a couronnée. L'Arbre m'a s: Nobody crowned me. The Tree simply let me listen to it. Then the fairies came, one by one: drops, seeds, breaths of wind. They asked me what to do, and I repeated what the Tree said. One day someone called me “Your Majesty”. I looked behind me. There was nobody there.
textes.Personne ne m'a nommé gardien. J'ai vu u: Nobody appointed me guardian. I saw a split root, I plugged it with clay. Then another. Then I chased off a mole. That was four hundred years ago. I know every root by its creak. The east one squeaks when it's going to rain. The south one, when Pimprenelle's coming.
textes.Personne ne me croyait pour le chat. Lil: Nobody believed me about the cat. Lila hid behind the fountain for a whole class and photographed him mid crab step, one paw raised. I hung the photo above my bed. When I have doubts, I look at it. The cat never has doubts.
textes.Personne ne répond. Ça sent l'encens à l: Nobody answers. It smells of lavender incense and apple pie.
textes.Personne ne sait, ma petite. Tout le mon: Nobody knows, my dear. Everybody's pretending.
textes.Personne à la maison. Une horloge fait t: Nobody home. A clock ticks. You whisper without knowing why.
textes.Personne. Juste le craquement du parquet: Nobody. Just the creak of the floorboards and the silence of a peaceful house.
Nobody. Just a little caravan driver.
textes.Personne. Mais quelqu'un a laissé un pet: Nobody. But someone left a little note: “Not here! Hee hee!”
textes.Personne. On entend juste un carillon qu: Nobody. You can only hear a chime tinkling inside, all by itself.
textes.Personne. Sur la porte, au feutre : « Pa: Nobody. On the door, in marker: “Gone to the garage. Or the café. Or elsewhere. Anyway, not here.”
textes.Personne. Une guitare débranchée est pos: Nobody. An unplugged guitar leans against the door, next to a holey umbrella.
textes.Personne. Une théière. Une théière qui t: Nobody. A teapot. A teapot that's looking at you. Teapots don't usually look.
textes.Personne… Alors chaque fleur que tu croi: Nobody… Then every flower you pass can be a little bit your other half. That's what I used to tell myself, before I found Brindille. It helps. A little.
textes.Petit ! Toujours tes trois dés pour les: Lad! Still leaving your three dice for the ghosts?
textes.Petit Malachar ! Tu as encore corrigé me: Little Malachar! Have you been correcting my dates again?
textes.Petit Malachar, dans mon histoire, c'éta: Little Malachar, in my story, it was a thousand years ago.
textes.Petit poisson argenté des côtes. Rend un: A small silvery fish from the coast. Restores half a heart.
textes.Petit, Bondi voulait « aider » à la boul: As a little one, Bondi wanted to “help” at the bakery. He ran round the oven, again, again, again, and every lap he knocked over a sack of flour. One morning, he came out all white, like a little ghost with ears. Grandma Luzerne said: “That one won't be a baker. He'll be fast.” She was right.
textes.Petit, Lhoucine venait dans mon cercle a: As a boy, Lhoucine used to come to my circle with his knees for a drum. He kept time during the tales, tap, tap, and he sped up when the djinn arrived. I told him: “One day, you'll play behind me.” He said: “No. You'll talk in front of me.” He was seven. He was right.
textes.Petit, au village, je grimpais partout :: As a kid, in the village, I climbed everything: the palm trees, the roof of the wash-house, once the mast of a boat that was leaving. They brought me down out at sea. My mum said I should have been born a monkey. I took it as a compliment. What she didn't know was that I climbed with my eyes shut. Easy.
textes.Petit, j'ai démonté le réveil de mon pèr: As a boy, I took apart my father's alarm clock to see where he hid the time. I didn't find it. So I put the clock back together, with three parts left over. Ever since, it rings every seven minutes. My father says it's my best invention: he's never been late again. Nor has he ever slept more than seven minutes.

As a boy, I took my father's alarm clock apart to see where time was hidden. I didn't find it. I put the clock back together: it rang every seven minutes. My father says it's my best invention. He was never late again.
textes.Petit, j'étais apprenti chez le vieux po: As a lad, I was apprenticed to the old polisher in the Upper Town. My first customer was Asmodin. He watched me work for an hour without a word, then said: “Acceptable.” I wept for joy. He still comes, every Monday. He still says “acceptable”.
textes.Petit, je buvais déjà de l'eau quand ta: Young man, I was drinking water when your spring was just a puddle!
textes.Petit, je dessinais les flaques d'eau. T: As a boy, I drew puddles. Every puddle in the yard, with their coasts, their bays, their gravel islands. My mother thought I was a little cracked. My father, who was a notary, thought I was very cracked. One day, I gave him a map of the yard, to scale, with the dog kennel as the “northern continent”. He framed it. He never said a word about it.
textes.Petit, je lui ai demandé ce que disait u: As a boy, I asked him what a very old rune at the back of his alcove said. He answered: “It says: ask me when you're grown up.” I thought he was making fun of me. Last year, I deciphered it on my own. That really is what it said. I've never dared ask him again.
textes.Petit, je m'endormais dans le cercle de: As a little boy, I'd fall asleep in Ba Sidi's circle, in the middle of the tales. At the end, I'd wake up and ask: “How much for the story?” The whole circle laughed. Ba Sidi answered: “Whatever you like.” I gave him a pebble. He took it, very serious. He says he still has them all. I hope he's lying.
textes.Petit, je me suis perdu dans les jardins: As a boy, I got lost in our mother's gardens, among the ash peppers. Vespérine found me and hung a label round my neck: “Bulle, do not lose”. I kept it. It's in my drawer. When I'm sad, I read it again. She'd put the date on it. Of course.
textes.Petit, je ne parlais à personne. Aux cor: As a boy, I talked to nobody. To the corals, yes. They don't answer, but they grow better when you talk to them. One finger's width a century, for the red. My father already tended the gardens. He said I was born with my hands in a basin. Hmm. It's almost true.
textes.Petit, je soufflais des bulles avec une: As a boy, I blew bubbles through a straw. Now it's a copper boiler, a steam bellows and two litres of soap a minute. You don't change, you grow.
textes.Petit, je suis tombé dans l'eau glacée d: As a boy, I fell into the icy water of a mountain spring, during a walk. I couldn't feel my horns. My mother carried me home on her back, and rubbed me by the fire for an hour, singing the peppers' lullaby. That was the day I decided always to have hot water.
textes.Petit, je vivais sous la table de ma non: As a boy, I lived under my nonna's table. From there, I watched her feet dance and heard everything. She sang as she put into the pot ten fish, a handful of saffron, and then… “a secret”. She'd say it with a wink, and the kitchen smelled like paradise. Me, I ate the crumbs. The crumbs of paradise, my friend!
textes.Petit, je voulais aider à la boulangerie: When I was little, I wanted to help at the bakery. So I ran round the oven. Fast. Very fast. Every lap, hop, a sack of flour on the floor. One morning, I knocked over six. Trèfle put me outside, all white, and said: “Go and run somewhere else.” So I did. All my life. Thanks, Trèfle.
As a boy, I wanted to see an eagle up close. I climbed onto the roof of the old temple, where an eagle had its nest. I got all the way to the top… and I couldn't get back down. A whole day, clinging on, under the eagle's eyes. In the evening, the priests got me down with a rope. The next day, they called me Cuauhtli: the Eagle. Priests have a sense of humour.
textes.Petit-Pierre ! Les graines t'attendent !: Petit-Pierre! The seeds are waiting for you!
textes.Petit-Pierre ! Les oignons t'attendent !: Petit-Pierre! The onions are waiting for you!
textes.Petit-Pierre ! Tu as vu mes lunettes ?: Petit-Pierre! Have you seen my glasses?
textes.Petit-Pierre ? C'est mon ombre. Une peti: Petit-Pierre? He's my shadow. A little shadow that talks all the time. I teach him stuff. He teaches me stuff too, but don't tell anyone.
textes.Petit-Pierre me rappelle quelqu'un. Moi,: Petit-Pierre reminds me of someone. Me, a very long time ago. He believes all my stories. Almost all. He's afraid of the dark, and he says so. That's braver than anything I've seen at sea.
textes.Petit-Pierre monte au mât plus vite que: Petit-Pierre climbs the mast faster than me, and he asks more questions than there are stars. He always finds my glasses. I don't know how he does it.
textes.Petit-Pierre pose plus de questions qu'i: Petit-Pierre asks more questions than there are waves in the sea. The cabin boy doesn't fight: that's my rule. So he counts the blows. He counts well.
textes.Petit-Pierre vient donner des graines à: Petit-Pierre comes to feed seeds to my parrots every evening. He asks a thousand questions. My parrots repeat them. My stall has turned into a school. A very noisy school!
textes.Petit-Pierre épluche mes oignons, goûte: Petit-Pierre peels my onions, tastes my sauces and tells me about his day without taking a breath. One day, he'll be a great cook. Or a great chatterbox. Or both, like me.
textes.Petit-Pierre, Biscotte est sur mon épaul: Petit-Pierre, Biscotte is on my shoulder!
textes.Petit-Pierre, pourquoi tu caches du pain: Petit-Pierre, why are you hiding bread in your pocket?
textes.Petite ! Je le savais ! Trente-sept. Non: Small! I knew it! Thirty-seven. No, thirty-six and a half. I can tell from the way you walk on tiptoe, like a cat on a roof. I have a yellow pair waiting for you.
Lass! Your keel is straight this morning.
textes.Petite peintre… Elles brillent presque a: Little painter… They glow almost as much as you do.
textes.Petite question avant le prochain tir :: Quick question before the next shot: do you like surprises?
textes.Petite question de métier : quand vous a: A little professional question: when you get a scrape, do you patch yourself up, or run to the doctor?
textes.Petite, Caramel gardait une sardine de s: As a little one, Caramel used to save a sardine from her plate for the King. Every evening she'd put it at the end of the jetty, on a leaf. In the morning, no more sardine: she was sure it was him. … It was the heron. I never told her. She stopped at twelve. Some evenings, I still put one out. To see.
textes.Petite, Flammèche a caché un crabe de la: When she was little, Flammèche hid a lava crab in my helmet. I put it on the next day for Guard school. The crab pinched my ear during the salute. I held the salute to the end. So did the crab. We kept it for ten years. His name was Mister Pincer.
textes.Petite, Lumina s'endormait toujours avan: When she was little, Lumina always fell asleep before the end of my stories. So I'd tell her the ending the next day, at breakfast. Once, I'd forgotten the ending. I made one up with toast in it, because that's what we were eating. She believed it. She grew up thinking all stories end with toast. Maybe she's right.
textes.Petite, Nolwenn a trempé sa tresse dans: When she was little, Nolwenn dipped her plait in my tar pot. I spent the evening cleaning it out with butter, strand by strand. Her mother was laughing. I couldn't: I'd been too frightened the tar was hot. It wasn't. Since then, there's a lid on every one of my pots. Twenty years of lids.
textes.Petite, au village, je passais mes journ: As a little girl, in the village, I spent my days on the beach watching the crabs. They walk sideways, raise a claw, stop, set off again. I copied them for hours. My grandmother used to say: “That child has a crab in her legs.” The crab step, I invented it at six. Really, I did.
textes.Petite, elle m'a supplié de changer la f: When she was little, she begged me to change the ending of the story of the princess who wanted to see snow, because she cried at the end. I refused: sad endings, we keep, and it's we who change. Twenty years later, she came to tell me she'd understood. I'd forgotten I'd said it. I pretended to remember.
textes.Petite, j'ai caché un crabe de lave dans: When I was little, I hid a lava crab in Pyrus's helmet. He put it on for his first salute at the Guard school, and the crab pinched his ear for the whole salute. He didn't flinch. That evening, he came home with the crab in his hand and said to me: “His name is Mister Pincer. We're keeping him.” I adored him forever after.
textes.Petite, je gardais une sardine pour le R: As a kitten, I'd save a sardine for the King. Every evening, I'd put it at the end of the jetty, on a lily pad. In the morning, no sardine. I was sure it was him. At twelve, I saw the heron fly off with it. I didn't tell Dad. He looked so happy when I told him the King had eaten.
textes.Petite, je lui avais demandé de changer: As a little girl, I asked him to change the ending of the story of the princess who wanted to see snow, because it made me sad. He refused. He told me: “Sad endings, we keep; we're the ones who change.” I only understood at twenty. I went to tell him. He'd forgotten.
textes.Petite, je m'endormais toujours avant la: As a little girl, I always fell asleep before the end of his stories. So he'd tell me the ending the next morning, at breakfast, his mouth full of toast. For years I thought all stories ended with “… and they ate toast.” I still believe it a little.
textes.Petite, je me cachais dans le grand lust: As a little girl, I used to hide in the great chandelier of the throne room. Asmodin always found me by the smell of singed lace. I never admitted to him that what I liked most was him looking for me.
textes.Petite, je me suis échappée de mon panie: When I was little, I escaped from my basket one night. The whole Circle searched for me. Séraphine found me asleep on the altar, arms spread wide. My mother said the stones had chosen me. Séraphine tells everyone that. I say my feet were cold. The altar is warm at night. That's a fact.
textes.Petite, je sautais du grenier avec un pa: When I was little, I used to jump from the attic with an umbrella. My mother screamed. So did the umbrella. One day, I stayed up in the air. My mother stopped screaming.
textes.Petite, mon père me laissait tenir le po: When I was little, my father let me hold the tar pot. Once, I dipped my plait in it. He spent the evening cleaning it with butter, without a word, very gently. My mother laughed. He didn't. That night, I understood my father was someone who's afraid of people getting hurt.
textes.Petite, pendant ses histoires, je tapais: As a cub, during his stories, I banged on pots. Bing for the dragon, bang for the storm. My mother wanted to stop me. He slowed his story down to follow my beats. That night, we told it together. Next day, he gave me a little hammer. He says he already knew.
textes.Petite, une nuit, je me suis perdue dans: When I was little, one night, I got lost in the alleys while Papa was lighting the other end of town. An hour in the dark. Since then, I've been afraid of the dark, {surnom}. I sleep with a bulb on. If I want to light up the whole city, it's so that no child is ever afraid again. Léonce doesn't know. Don't tell him. A mother isn't afraid.
textes.Petite, Éclair ne tenait pas en place su: As a kitten, Éclair couldn't keep still on the jetty. Dad would say “watch the float”, she'd watch it for two seconds, then run from one end to the other, and every fish in the pond would dash off and hide. Dad would sigh. I'd take her on my lap so she'd keep still. She kept still. For four seconds.
textes.Petites baies sucrées des buissons. Rend: Small sweet berries from the bushes. Restores half a heart.
textes.Petites, je montais des spectacles dans: When we were little, I put on shows in the street with bedsheets, and Lila ran the till. Our first fee was a fish, given by a passing fisherman. One fish for two. We grilled it on the beach like a feast for queens. I think it was Bastien's father. I'll have to ask him.
textes.Petites, on se cachait dans la pirogue d: When we were little, we used to hide in her father's canoe, under a mat, to get out of work. One day, the canoe came loose. We drifted to the middle of the lake, with no paddle. Xóchitl paddled with a bunch of flowers. It was no use at all, but it was very pretty. A fisherman brought us back at sunset.
textes.Petites, on se cachait sous une natte da: As little girls, we used to hide under a mat in my father's canoe. One day, the canoe came loose and we drifted into the middle of the lake. No oar. I paddled with my bouquet. Citlali told me, very calmly: “It won't work, but keep going, it's pretty.” A fisherman brought us back in the evening. I didn't have a single flower left.
textes.Petits, sous les arcades, elle me faisai: When we were little, under the arcades, she'd make me judge the fishes' eyes, like grandmother. “This one?” I'd say: “Fresh!” She'd say: “Three days old! You've got no eye!” She was nine and already scolding like an old fishwife. Today she scolds just the same, but with earrings.
Doesn't matter, as long as there are some.
textes.Peut-être. Tu danserais sur une chanson: Maybe. Would you dance to a song of my own?
textes.Pff. J'arrive avec le goudron. Garde le: Pff. I'll be over with the tar. Keep the mackerel cool.
textes.Pff. Si on avait fait ça, il n'y aurait: Pff. If we'd done that, there'd be no Carène left. Just a beach. Oh well. Each to their trade. Mine is throwing nothing away.
Pff. If you're here at seven.
textes.Pfff. Tu as de la chance, je suis de bon: Pfff. You're lucky, I'm in a generous mood. Fifteen percent, today only.
textes.Pfffft ! Un petit nuage sort de vos chev: Pfffft! A little cloud comes out of your ankles. Your toes thank you.
textes.Pff… Passe-moi l'étoupe, futur capitaine: Pff… Pass me the oakum, future captain.
textes.Pff… Tout le monde m'aime bien, ici. C'e: Pff… Everybody likes me round here. It's exhausting.
Pff… You've been saying that for a hundred years.
textes.Philibert ! Le tourne-pages a fait toute: Philibert! The page-turner got through the whole sonata without a hitch.
textes.Philibert ! Tu ne vas pas me le ressorti: Philibert! You're not going to bring that up every evening, are you?
textes.Philibert croit qu'il n'a jamais rien in: Philibert thinks he's never invented anything. My piano turns its pages thanks to him every day. He's much more of an inventor than he thinks.
textes.Philibert est le meilleur voisin de banc: Philibert is the best bench neighbour in the world, and he invents with a heart this big. His boxes of nothing, on the other hand… No. I won't say a thing. I've said too much already.
textes.Philibert est le passager le plus étrang: Philibert is the strangest passenger at my airfield: he wants to go where there are no ideas. A charming man, as sad as a windsock with no wind.
textes.Philibert est un vrai inventeur, quoi qu: Philibert is a real inventor, whatever the Academy says. His box of nothing never breaks down. It's the only thing in my Bazaar that's never let me down.
textes.Philibert invente tout, toujours un peu: Philibert invents everything, always a little after everyone else. I turn down his patents one by one. And I read every one of them, to the very last line. He doesn't know that.
textes.Philémon ! Les trois squelettes sont ren: Philémon! Have the three skeletons come home?
textes.Philémon ! Une crique, au nord-ouest. To: Philémon! A cove, to the northwest. Brand new.
textes.Philémon ! Une vieille carte, toute fraî: Philémon! An old map, fresh today!
textes.Philémon Lunette reconnaît une fausse ca: Philémon Lunette can spot a fake map by the smell of the ink. He ruined a whole season for me. Since then, I pay him to check my maps before I sell them. He's become my partner without knowing it.
textes.Philémon dessine ce que je vois. Je lui: Philémon draws what I see. I tell him “a cove to the west”, and he turns it into a marvel with curly waves. He lends me his spyglass. I give it back. Nearly always in one piece.
textes.Philémon me dessine les roses des vents: Philémon draws the compass roses I tattoo. He's jealous of my copies. He chases after crow feathers, and he chases slowly. He's a charming old gentleman. And a rival.
textes.Philémon écrit mes histoires dans les ma: Philémon writes my stories in the margins of his maps. He says they're half false. He writes them anyway. That's a true friend: someone who keeps your lies.
textes.Photon, vos plantes clignotent bizarreme: Photon, your plants are blinking strangely
Photon, your plants are blinking strangely…
textes.Pierre et feu ! Ton acier fond très bien: Stone and fire! Your steel melts very nicely, tall one. That's a compliment.
textes.Pierrick ! Le Zéphyr arrive plein ce soi: Pierrick! The Zéphyr's coming in full tonight. May the best one win!
textes.Pierrick ! Ta prairie n'a pas bougé, je: Pierrick! Your meadow hasn't moved, I went to check on it.
textes.Pierrick ! Tes hamacs sont bien attachés: Pierrick! Are your hammocks tied on properly today?
textes.Pierrick ? C'est mon neveu. Il croit qu': Pierrick? He's my nephew. He thinks he runs the inn. I let him think so, it makes him happy.
textes.Pierrick croit que je lui vole ses clien: Pierrick thinks I steal his customers with my seaweed sacks. It's true. But somebody has to make him fight, or he'd spend his days asleep in his hammocks.
textes.Pierrick est gentil, mais il me dénonce: Pierrick is nice, but he always tells on me to the Admiral. And he can't laugh when you tie knots in his hammocks.
textes.Pierrick est persuadé de tenir l'auberge: Pierrick is convinced he runs the inn. I let him believe it. He's clumsy, touchy, and gentle as a lamb. His mother would be proud. Me, I am, in secret.
textes.Pierrick m'a demandé un jour, très série: Pierrick once asked me, very seriously, where the stillest place on the island was. No wind, no slope, no sea. I searched for three weeks. I drew him a little meadow above the bay, between two oaks, behind the north point. He asked: “Does the meadow move?” I said no. He smiled like a child.
textes.Pierrick recompte les hamacs chaque soir: Pierrick recounts the hammocks every evening, out loud. Thirty-two. Always thirty-two. Once, for a laugh, I took one down. He counted thirty-one, went white as a sheet, and searched the lower deck until midnight. I hung it back up in secret. I never did it again.
textes.Pierrick rêve d'une auberge sur la terre: Pierrick dreams of an inn on dry land, with beds. I drew him the best plots on the island. He keeps my map in his apron, and looks at it when his aunt's back is turned.
textes.Pierrick vient me voir chaque semaine av: Pierrick comes to see me every week with a new illness. I listen to him, I give him a ginger tea, and he leaves cured. It's my greatest success.
textes.Pierrick, tu as rempli les cruches ?: Pierrick, have you filled the jugs?
textes.Pigment, la graffeuse, trouve que tu as: Pigment, the graffiti artist, thinks you "look like someone who makes beautiful walls". She gives you three spray paint cans: three graffiti must be painted on the paintable walls of Port-Boucan.
textes.Pika a trouvé un œuf ! … C'était un cail: Pika found egg! … It was rock.
textes.Pile ? Comme un cadran solaire ? Ça doit: Right on time? Like a sundial? Must be restful, being you. Me, I'm either early or late. Never in the middle.
Pilli! Wake up, it's the lesson.
textes.Pilli ! Tlaco n'a toujours pas de poils: Pilli! Tlaco still doesn't have any hair?
textes.Pilli ! Ton chien chante, ce soir ?: Pilli! Is your dog singing tonight?
textes.Pilli ! Tu as arrosé le maïs ?: Pilli! Did you water the maize?
textes.Pilli danse avec son chien. Le chien dan: Pilli dances with his dog. The dog dances better than half the warriors of Aztlán. Pilli, a bit less well. But with more joy than anyone. That's what dancing is.
textes.Pilli dort en classe. Avec son chien. Le: Pilli sleeps in class. With his dog. The dog learns better.
Pilli sleeps in class. With his dog. The dog, meanwhile, listens and learns better. Pilli is as clever as a monkey, when he's awake. The problem is the “when”.
textes.Pilli n'a pas le droit de monter l'escal: Pilli isn't allowed to climb the stairs of the Great Temple. He knows it. He tries anyway. He's stubborn, curious, and accompanied by a dog that barks at the stone serpents. I was like him. Without the dog.
textes.Pilli veut toucher mon bouclier, ma peau: Pilli wants to touch my shield, my jaguar skin and my weapon. He asks a hundred questions. His dog has been barking at me since the first day. Maybe the dog is right to be wary of jaguars.
textes.Pilli vient m'aider à remplir les jarres: Pilli comes to help me fill the jars at the lake. He spills half. The other half, his dog drinks. But he asks good questions about Tlaloc. He'll make a good potter. Or a good swimmer.
textes.Pilli, c'est mon copain d'Aztlán ! On se: Pilli is my buddy from Aztlán! We see each other at the fair of the longest day. He has a hairless dog, Tlaco, who's all warm. Peek' has hair. We don't agree on which is the best dog.
textes.Pilli, c'est mon fils. Il court partout: Pilli is my son. He runs everywhere with his dog, he asks a thousand questions, and he has his father's laugh. He never helps me in the garden. He helps me smile. That's already a lot.
Pilli. Your dog is still barking.
textes.Pimprenelle ! Tu allumes toujours les la: Pimprenelle! Do you still light the lanterns with a snap of your fingers?
textes.Pimprenelle ! Tu ne trouves pas mon nect: Pimprenelle! You don't find my nectar too sweet, do you?
textes.Pimprenelle ? Une tornade avec des ailes: Pimprenelle? A tornado with wings. She bad-mouths my sugar behind my back, but she's the only one who helps me fill my bottles without asking for anything.
textes.Pimprenelle ? Une étincelle de fée, en b: Pimprenelle? A spark of a fairy, down below, in the roots. I gave her a branch of Yggdrasil a hundred years ago. She deserves it. She doesn't know it yet.
textes.Pimprenelle a perdu sa baguette dans la: Pimprenelle lost her wand in the Cave of Jumping Mushrooms. Don't tell her I told you.
textes.Pimprenelle m'a encore changé en grenoui: Pimprenelle turned me into a frog again. My paws hurt. My legs. Hmph.
textes.Pimprenelle parle tout le temps, très fo: Pimprenelle talks all the time, very loud, very fast. Next to her, I feel like a tiny little silence. But she holds my hand when I'm scared.
textes.Pimprenelle raconte à tout le village qu: Pimprenelle tells the whole village I put too much sugar in my nectar. She thinks I don't know. But every evening she drops by “by chance” when I'm rinsing my bottles, and licks the bottoms. I've seen her. I'm saving my petals for the right moment.
textes.Pimprenelle répond à mes énigmes avant q: Pimprenelle answers my riddles before I've finished asking them. Always wrong, always with admirable enthusiasm. It's a gift, in its way.
textes.Pimprenelle, une énigme : qu'est-ce qui…: Pimprenelle, a riddle: what is it that…
textes.Pimprenelle. Une étincelle qui parle. El: Pimprenelle. A spark that talks. She turns me into a frog when I grumble. I grumble all the time. Do the maths. Hmph.
textes.Pimprenelle… tu n'aurais pas un sort pou: Pimprenelle… you wouldn't have a spell for my drops, would you?
textes.Pinceau sec : trempe-le dans la Palette: Dry brush: dip it in the Palette
Pip! That sheet is for sleeping.
textes.Pip ! Tes oreilles sont redevenues norma: Pip! Are your ears back to normal?
textes.Pip a bu une de mes potions. Il a eu les: Pip drank one of my potions. His ears went green. He says it's my fault. It's partly his: the label said “not for Pip”.
textes.Pip a peur de moi. C'est bien : il ne to: Pip is afraid of me. That's good: he doesn't touch the stones anymore. He brought me his blanket, for the smallest one. I didn't know what to say. I laid it on her. It's still there.
textes.Pip essaie de léviter en sautant du dort: Pip is trying to levitate by jumping off the dormitory with a bedsheet. I'll have to have a word with him before he has a word with the ground.
textes.Pip est le plus jeune de mes apprentis e: Pip is the youngest of my apprentices and the chattiest on the island, Zéphyrine included. He asks a hundred questions a day. I've granted him the right to one.
textes.Pip veut léviter en sautant avec un drap: Pip wants to levitate by jumping with a bedsheet. I did that last year. Mother Sage had to look after me for a week.
Pip wants to jump off the dormitory with a bedsheet. I showed him the scar on my knee, to scare him. He said: “So cool!” That wasn't the idea at all. Since then, I keep an eye on bedsheets. He's got one with stars, he hides it under his pillow. I know it. He knows I know it.
textes.Pip, c'est le petit du dortoir. Il me su: Pip's the little one in the dormitory. He follows me everywhere and asks questions non-stop. He thinks I'm amazing. He's the only one. So I'm careful not to let him down too much.
textes.Pip, c'est un courant d'air avec des jam: Pip is a draught with legs. He decided to fly before he could levitate, with a bedsheet. It frightens the life out of me. I adore him, and I'd like him to keep his feet on the ground a little longer.
textes.Pip, il touche à tout. Il lit pas les ét: Pip touches everything. He doesn't read the labels, or he only reads half of them. But he's funny, and he believes in my potions. Well, he did before the green ears.
textes.Pivoine ! Pile à l'heure, comme toujours: Pivoine! Right on time, as always.
textes.Pivoine ! Ton cueilleur préféré est là !: Pivoine! Your favourite picker is here!
textes.Pivoine ? Le meilleur nez de Ramure et l: Pivoine? The best nose in Ramure and the sharpest tongue. We learned herbs together at her grandmother's. She learned the herbs. I learned Pivoine.
textes.Pivoine a goûté mon gâteau de lune longt: Pivoine tasted my mooncake for a long time, eyes closed, nose forward. Then she said: “It's missing a herb.” I went cold all over. “Which one?” “I don't know.” Since then, she keeps trying: mint, sage, meadowsweet. I chased her out with the bread peel. Her mushrooms, for their part, have always been banned in my shop.
textes.Pivoine dit que je dors sous les arbres: Pivoine says I sleep under trees instead of gathering. Not true. I gather while I sleep. It's a fox technique.
textes.Pivoine essaie toujours de me tirer les: Pivoine is always trying to wheedle the post's secrets out of me. “What does this envelope smell of? And that parcel there?” I answer: “A postmistress says nothing.” So she sniffs my counter. I think she guesses half of it anyway. With a nose like that, it's not fair.
textes.Pivoine me donne des tisanes de brume po: Pivoine gives me mist teas so I can sleep in the daytime, I give her moon feathers for her vials. She's as nosy as a fox. Makes sense, she is one.
textes.Pivoine, c'est mon amie. Elle m'a rendu: Pivoine is my friend. She gave me back my sleep when I'd lost it. In return, she gets my warm bread for life, and the right to tell me my cake is missing a herb. She takes full advantage.
textes.Pixel et son petit frère Quark jouent à: Pixel and her little brother Quark are playing hide-and-seek, and Quark always cheats. Pixel invites the hero to play: the two children will hide somewhere in Astralys, and both of them must be found.
textes.Pixel, tu veux jouer à quelque chose ?: Pixel, do you want to play something?
textes.Place ! Place au chevalier de Tournevent: Make way! Make way for the knight of Tournevent!
textes.Plante verte (en plastique).\nNe pas arr:
Houseplant (plastic).
Do not water. Do not love.
textes.Plateaux, théières, lanternes. Les cent: Trays, teapots, lanterns. The hundred teapots my brother-in-law Hassan knocked over, I'm the one who made them: he's been feeding my workshop for ten years. Once a year, I polish the seven cannons of the Skala. A pirate, Mâchefer, comes to watch me hammer every day. And little Omar steals my tac-tac for his festival. Tac. Everybody helps themselves at my place.
textes.Plein ?! Comme des noisettes ? Et tu sai: Loads?! Like hazelnuts? And do you always know where they all are? Lucky you. Me, I lose my hazelnuts.
textes.Plein d'espoir. Aujourd'hui, j'invente q: Full of hope. Today, I'm going to invent something new. I can feel it.
textes.Plein de monde ! Hou ! Ma sacoche t'ador: Loads of people! Hoo! My satchel loves you already. Write small, then: it's not that big.
textes.Pleine d'espoir. Tu es là-dedans pour no: Full of hope. You're in there for us, I can feel it.
textes.Pleine, décroissante, nouvelle, croissan: Full, waning, new, waxing: the four dials line up, a chime of crystal… and the slate door slides away upward.
textes.Plic… plic… plonc ! Les trois gouttes to: Drip… drip… plunk! The three drops fall into the three buckets, and it almost makes a melody. “Brilliant! Thank you! I'll call it: Concerto for a Leaky Roof.” He gives you a few coins.
textes.Plic… ploc… Il pleut dans la yourte. Tro: Drip… drop… It's raining inside the yurt. Three drops fall from the roof onto the rug, and someone watches them with resignation.
textes.Ploc ! Moi Ploc ! (Il te pique avec un b: Ploc! Me Ploc! (He pokes you with a stick.) Poke! … You not say “ouch”? You not even drop pixels when poked? You too strong!
textes.Ploc veut voir Grosse-Dent ! … Non. Ploc: Ploc want see Grosse-Dent! … No. Ploc not want.
textes.Plonger au pied de la pointe du phare, c: Dive at the foot of the lighthouse point, on the open-sea side, and find the lens shard
textes.Plouf ! L'Achéron est glacé… Charon te r: Splash! The Acheron is freezing… Charon fishes you out with his oar, sighing: “One obol, I said. Not a swim.”
textes.Plouf ! L'eau du lac est froide comme un: Splash! The lake water is as cold as a winter morning. You climb back onto the shore, shivering; the frogs are laughing (well, croaking). Hop from stone to stone!
textes.Plouf ! L'eau noire du bassin amortit ta: Splash! The black water of the pool cushions your fall.
textes.Plouf ! Tu nages dans l'eau froide jusqu: Splash! You swim through the cold water to the entrance ledge and haul yourself up, soaked.
textes.Plouf ! Tu remontes, trempé, sur le rebo: Splash! You climb back out, soaked, onto the entrance ledge. The basin is too deep to swim in.
textes.Plouf ! Tu te poses dans l'eau. L'Alouet: Splash! You land in the water. The Alouette, soaked, folds back into your bag. Time to swim!
textes.Plume-de-Nuage file sous la grande verri: Plume-de-Nuage darts under the great glass roof of the Greenhouse, does three happy loops among the other creatures of the sky, and comes back to brush your cheek. She's home! Go and tell Nova.
textes.Plume-de-Nuage s'est arrêtée : tu vas tr: Plume-de-Nuage has stopped: you're going too fast, she's afraid of getting lost. Go back for her!
textes.Plume-de-Nuage, la plus jeune méduse de: Cloudfeather, Nova's youngest sky jellyfish, has escaped from the Greenhouse of Species. She's floating somewhere around the island and can't find her way home on her own. Sextant, who draws the island from the lookouts, may have seen her go by.
textes.Plumette ! Mécaniquement parlant, vous a: Plumette! Mechanically speaking, you have feathers on your head.
textes.Plumette m'apporte les cartes de tante S: Plumette brings me Aunt Sésame's cards. She knows all of Ramure's secrets and tells none of them: a postwoman says nothing. Good thing. Neither do I, sometimes.
textes.Plumette m'apporte les lettres d'Ardoise: Plumette brings me Ardoise's letters. It's not her fault. I hold it against her a little anyway. It's easier to be cross with the postwoman than with the sea.
textes.Plumette me donne les plumes de lune pou: Plumette gives me moon feathers for my vials; I give her teas to help her sleep during the day. She knows all of Ramure's secrets. She doesn't tell a single one. It's infuriating.
textes.Plumette ne dit jamais rien de ce qu'il: Plumette never says anything about what's in the letters. Even when the envelope's all crinkled from rereading. “A postwoman says nothing.” She puts the letter down, waits for the reply, and off she goes. I gave her a skewer once, with my reply. So it would fly faster.
textes.Plumette, c'est notre postière ! Elle rê: Plumette is our postmistress! She dreams of a golden acorn for her counter. I've got one, my most beautiful one, I'm saving it for a big occasion. Meanwhile, I show it to her from a distance. Tee hee.
textes.Plumette, la postière de Ramure, c'est m: Plumette, the postmistress of Ramure, is my pen pal. We write to each other on the mail dockets. She's the only aviator in the archipelago who flies without an engine. I envy her a little.
textes.Plus au sud, cette fois. J'ai refait mes: Further south, this time. I've redone my calculations.
textes.Plus bas, la salle des Avares, pleine de: Further down, the hall of the Misers, full of heavy bronze weights you must push into place; the Styx, where only the flagstones that don't bubble will hold you; the city of Dis and its three Furies. Then Geryon, who has the face of an honest man and the tail of a scorpion: he carries travellers all the way down, gliding like a leaf.
textes.Plus calme… (Il regarde le lac longtemps: Calmer… (He looks at the lake for a long time.) It's true. You can hear the ducks. I hadn't heard the ducks in years. Here, my friend: frog legs for Ulric, he'll cook them for you. And my eternal gratitude. It's very big, my gratitude. Like my fears.
textes.Plus de galette pour l'instant ! Revenir: No more flatbread for now! Come back later, empty belly.
textes.Plus de toit, plus de porte, plus de sou: No more roof, no more door, no more eyebrows! My fifteenth roof, I want to make it out of iron. Thick iron. I need three blocks of iron ore. The shepherds of the north sell it, so do the dwarves of Fire Mountain, and you can find some by digging in the rocks. Bring me three, and I'll give you… something. Something pretty. That doesn't explode.
textes.Plus faim ? À ton âge ? Allons donc ! Ti: Not hungry? At your age? Nonsense! Here.
textes.Plus fort ? Je vais réveiller les squele: Louder? I'll wake the skeletons in the graveyard!
textes.Plus gros que celui de la gargouille, ma: Bigger than the gargoyle's one, dear?
textes.Plus jamais de potion le lundi !: No more potions on Mondays, ever!
textes.Plus juste que toi en rentrant, mon chou: More in tune than you on your way home, sweetie.
textes.Plus lentement ? Tes deux pieds gauches: Slower? Are your two left feet struggling?
textes.Plus maintenant ! Ça veut dire qu'avant,: Not any more! That means that before, you were. And that we changed your mind. That's the loveliest thing anyone can say to an Archduchess.
textes.Plus maintenant. Mais quelle carrière !: Not any more. But what a career!
