The first for the legs, the second for the breath, the third for courage, the fourth for the end. We sang it every day for six years. I still sing it, all alone, when nobody can hear me.
textes.Quand ça gronde, tu as peur, m'as-tu dit: When it rumbles, you're scared, you told me. It's rumbling more and more, {surnom}. Keep that to yourself.
When they bite, reel in with little turns. If the tension goes red, ease off a bit. The fish tires before you do. Normally.
textes.Quand ça vous arrange ! C'est très malin: When it suits you! That's very clever. I'll do the same: the good signs, I'll believe; the bad ones, I'll leave at the bottom of the sea.
textes.Quarante ans boulanger. Lever à trois he: Forty years a baker. Up at three, kneading trough, oven, and in the afternoon, pétanque. On the first day, Marcel, the postman, put his satchel down at the edge of the pitch and said: “You point like a baker.” I answered: “And you shoot like a postman.” We argued the whole game. That was forty years ago. We've never finished.
textes.Quarante ans d'université. Des cours, de: Forty years at the university. Lectures, papers, conferences. And always, at the back of the hall, someone whispering the same phrase with a smile. In the end it became my name: in the corridors, they no longer said “Professor Moreau”, they said “Moreau and his Atlantis”. Very well. A name is a promise. I kept searching.
textes.Quarante ans dans la grande hune. Mainte: Forty years in the main top. Now my knees won't climb any more, so I keep watch from the bow. Ewen goes up to light the lantern for me.
Forty years in your cellar, Ulfa.
textes.Quarante ans de pêche, pas un jour de na: Forty years of fishing, not one day of shipwreck. The secret: I come home when the seagulls come home.
textes.Quarante ans derrière ce comptoir. J'ai: Forty years behind this counter. I sold apples to the mayor when he was knee-high.
textes.Quarante ans là-haut, par tous les temps: Forty years up there, in all weathers. I've seen whales go by, two waterspouts, and a boat from Port-Azur lost in the night, which I guided home with the lantern. It's all written in my journal, with the time. Ships, I counted them. Hardly any ever came by. That's no reason to stop counting.
textes.Quarante ans là-haut. Trois cent vingt m: Forty years up there. Three hundred and twenty steps, twice a day. I've got the calves of a young man and the heart of an old one.
textes.Quarante ans que je joue avec Marcel. Qu: Forty years I've been playing with Marcel. Forty years we've been arguing. He's my best friend, but don't tell him.
Forty years I've been fishing off this jetty. I've caught sardines, perch, an old boot and a cold. The King of the Pools, never. One day.
Forty years I've run this tavern. It was my mother's, and her mother's before. The fireplace is an old stove from the Léviathan's galley. It's never gone cold.
textes.Quarante ans à l'université. On s'est mo: Forty years at the university. They mocked me at every conference: “Moreau and his Atlantis”. I never gave up.
Forty minutes of rain on a tent. Nothing else. “It's my favorite record to fall asleep to,” says the owner.
textes.Quarante tasses à la minute, et un coup: Forty cups a minute, and a toot of the whistle when it's ready. Upstairs, Héloïse's spring beds. Waiting tables, Master Rivet's butler. At the counter, Professor Boum and his iron powder; on the terrace, his ninth roof as an awning. Every morning I make Achille's sandwich. And the coffee comes from the Tazira caravaners, by the Zéphyr.
textes.Quarante épices, et je les connais toute: Forty spices, and I know every one of them by its first name. Zohra and her Friday saffron, Mustapha and his cumin, Samira who wastes my saffron dyeing rags. Salomé, in Carène, who buys everything from me and calls me a thief. And a big pirate cook who brings me parsley as if it were roses. Parsley! Smell, smell… All of Tazira passes under my nose.
textes.Quarante-deux ans d'horlogerie. Je dors: Forty-two years of clockmaking. I sleep with three alarm clocks. They all ring at the same second. It's the most beautiful sound in the world.
Forty-two. And a half. For dancing.
textes.Quatorze promesses. Je les ai toutes not: Fourteen promises. I've written them all down.
textes.Quatre ! J'ai une grosse idée !: Four! I've got a big idea!
textes.Quatre cent douze, Zigomar ! Et ta chaus: Four hundred and twelve, Zigomar! And your shoe!
Four hundred? I'll count them, mind.
textes.Quatre chemins partent du carrefour : un: Four paths leave the crossroads: a red one, a black one, a white one, a yellow one. On the stele, these words: “Here, the Twins hesitated. But Xan, the mosquito, went on ahead of them.”
textes.Quatre creux ronds… vides. Et un cercle: Four round hollows… empty. And a circle that glows! So Corentin was telling the truth: four seals, one for each people of the island. Here, that's for your trouble, and my map of the island, copied out for you. One day, you'll have to go and see the shepherds of the north, the mist people and the caravaneers of the south. And find our own seal.
textes.Quatre de mes livres se sont envolés pen: Four of my books flew away during the storm. I can still see them, stuck where nobody can climb. They pretend they can't hear me.
textes.Quatre petits Moaïs, immobiles au fond d: Four little Moai, motionless at the back of the room. Very motionless. Too motionless.
textes.Quatre peuples sur cette île, quatre sce: Four peoples on this island, four seals on the great gate. Ours, the Seal of Mists… It sleeps at the bottom of the biggest pool. Only the moon knows where, and the moon speaks only to the elders. Not to you. Not yet.
textes.Quatre pièces. Le fil n'est pas gratuit,: Four coins. Thread isn't free, and neither is the disinfectant. Especially the disinfectant.
textes.Quatre régions, quatre peuples. Nous, à: Four regions, four peoples. Us, in the west, on the coast. In the north, the highland shepherds: tough folk who don't say much. In the east, the people of the misty forest: you hardly ever see them. In the south, the desert caravanners: they sell everything, and at a steep price.
textes.Quatre sceaux pour la dernière porte. Le: Four seals for the last gate. The desert keeps its own under a dune that walks. To find it, they say, you must follow the stars that walk. … The caravan lanterns, perhaps. Or something else.
textes.Quatre serpents qui tournent deux par de: Four serpents turning two by two? Ah, the Ancients and their pranks… Start with the one that's already in the right place, and see which one it drags along.
textes.Quatre statues de pierre, chacune avec s: Four stone statues, each with its medallion: a sailor (the wave), a caravan woman (the sun), a shepherd (the cogwheel), a fox woman (the moon). On the fresco above the staircase, the four peoples hold hands before the great gate; above them, a red stone heart, linked by four rays to four crystals.
textes.Quatre symboles gravés, dans l'ordre : I: Four symbols engraved, in order: I, II, III, IIII. And beneath: “When the night lifts the sea, the day rises, and the guardian awakes.”
textes.Quatre, cinq… Ne parle pas en comptant,: Four, five… Don't talk while you count, you lose your air.
textes.Quatre-vingts ans. J'ai ramendé les file: Eighty years old. I've mended the nets of three generations of fishermen. Moulay Brahim, I knew him when he was tiny. He used to cry when he saw a crab.
textes.Quatre-vingts ans. Mes yeux ne voient pl: Eighty years old. My eyes don't see far any more, but my hands tie two thousand knots a day. Khadija, my pupil, ties a thousand, and she threads my needles. Larbi lights his green lighthouse: I know it by the smell of the wick. Little Brahim is amin. Ba Sidi gets the beard wrong every evening. Lou has come back. And Sel's grandson asks me questions. Everything comes back, my child.
Four. And I keep my secrets.
Four. I've got a big idea.
That Caelan dares before the Dawn Festival. There are ten years left. For an elf, that's tomorrow. For Caelan, it's cutting it a bit fine.
textes.Que Gaspard voie le Crâne Fendu un soir: For Gaspard to see the Crâne Fendu on a party night: Tom on the fiddle, the whole port singing, and not a single broken chair. Well, one. Just one, for the atmosphere.
textes.Que Myrtille voie le Roi des mares. Une: That Myrtille sees the Pond King. Once, with her own eyes. Not catch him. See him. That he looks at her, and laughs.
textes.Que cache l'Arbre-Mère ?: What does the Mother Tree hide?
textes.Que cherchez-vous sur cette carte ?: What are you looking for on that map?
textes.Que cherchez-vous, milord ?: What are you looking for, milord?
textes.Que de livres ! Tous bien rangés… sauf u: So many books! All neatly arranged… except one, a red one, that isn't quite in its place.
textes.Que demande Charon pour passer l'Achéron: What does Charon ask for to cross the Acheron?
textes.Que dit un arbre à un autre arbre ? « Tu: What does one tree say to another? “You seem very grounded today.” … Tree jokes are slow.
textes.Que dit un caillou à un autre caillou ?: What does one pebble say to another pebble?
textes.Que dit un oignon quand il se cogne ?: What does an onion say when it bumps itself?
textes.Que dit une huître à une autre huître ?: What does one oyster say to another oyster? Nothing. They keep their mouths shut. … It's a very old joke.
textes.Que dit une imprimante dans l'eau ?: What does a printer say when it's sinking?
textes.Que fait une fraise sur un cheval ?: What does a strawberry do on a horse?
textes.Que faut-il faire, au sommet du Grand Te: What must be done at the top of the Great Temple?
textes.Que faut-il pour soigner l'arbre ?: What does the tree need to heal?
textes.Que la Chope Ardente serve ma bière, ave: For the Blazing Mug to serve my fizz, with my name on the barrel. In big letters. And for Ulfa to read it out loud, in front of everyone.
textes.Que la cloche sonne midi juste, devant t: For the bell to strike noon on the dot, in front of the whole square. Twelve strokes, not one fewer. And for one passer-by, just one, to look up and wonder who it's ringing for.
textes.Que la fête de Tazira s'entende jusqu'à: For Tazira's festival to be heard all the way to Carène. For one evening, over there, a fisherman to stop eating his flatbread and start tapping his foot without knowing why. Boom.
textes.Que la porte reste fermée encore mille a: May the gate stay shut another thousand years. And may Kalda guard it after me. She'll be better than me. Don't tell her.
textes.Que le Fondouk vive encore trois cents a: May the Fondouk live another three hundred years. May its walls hear languages nobody knows yet. And may the girl who replaces me know how to say “you pay in advance” in twenty languages.
textes.Que le courrier de Ramure fasse le tour: For Ramure's post to go all the way round the island! Every tree, every port, every hut. Hoo, just thinking about it wakes me up.
textes.Que le cristal brille assez pour que le: For the crystal to shine bright enough that the red coral grows two fingers a century instead of one. Hmm. Doesn't sound like much. For a coral, it's huge.
textes.Que les canons de la Skala ne tirent jam: That the Skala's cannons never fire. Never. That Abdellah polishes them until the end of time, for nothing.
textes.Que les pierres choisissent elles-mêmes: That the stones choose for themselves who will keep them, after me. I have no daughter. I hope they have an idea. I think they do. She reads a lot.
textes.Que les siennes sont mieux. Hé oui. Il d: That his are better. Oh yes. He says that about everything.
textes.Que les étoiles éclairent ta route, {sur: May the stars light your way, {surnom}!
textes.Que mon faisceau porte un jour jusqu'à l: That my beam might one day reach the blue glow, to the west. Once. To know what it is. Not for the professor. For me.
textes.Que mon mari rentre pour de bon. Qu'il s: For my husband to come home for good. For him to sit at my table one Friday, and then the next, and then all the others. For him to complain about the salt. I'll let him complain.
textes.Que puis-je faire pour Port-Azur ?: What can I do for Port-Azur?
textes.Que quelqu'un m'emmène un jour jusqu'à l: For someone to take me one day all the way to the floating island. By Zéphyr, by bubble, on steam wings, I don't mind. Just to see up close what nobody believes.
textes.Que se passe-t-il, avec l'horloge ?: What's going on with the clock?
textes.Que sont ces lanternes bleues, sur les p: What are those blue lanterns on the bridges?
textes.Que ta forge ne s'éteigne jamais, {surno: May your forge never go cold, {surnom}.
textes.Que toute la Balafre chante ma chanson,: For all of Balafre to sing my song, one evening, all at once: the three crews, Mama, the Governor, and even the skeletons in the graveyard, clacking their bones. The finest concert in history. And the loudest.
That you're less grumpy in the mornings.
That you owed me a pot of honey.
textes.Que tu tombais ? C'est normal, ça ! C'es: Falling? That's normal! That's the beginning. You fall and fall, and one night you forget to touch the ground. It happened to me when I was nine.
textes.Quel accident ! Je m'en occupe !: What an accident! I'll take care of it!
textes.Quel beau jour pour la sardine !: What a fine day for sardines!
textes.Quel est le métier préféré des petits Mo: What's the favorite job of little Moai?
What knee? I haven't got a knee.
What a waste. Here. It's more expensive.
textes.Quel gâchis. … Il est beau, hein ?: What a waste. … It is lovely, isn't it?
textes.Quel hasard, Bobor ! Il y a eu un accide: What a coincidence, Bobor! Has there been an accident?
textes.Quel pavillon hisser ? La Mouette rieuse: Which flag to hoist? The Laughing Seagull, the Sailor's Star, the Grinning Skull, the Brave Heart, the Golden Anchor or the Moonfish.
textes.Quel pot, Bobor ? Je ne vois pas de quoi: What jar, Bobor? I don't know what you're talking about.
textes.Quel âge ?! On ne demande pas son âge à: How old?! You don't ask a stone lady her age! … One thousand two hundred and forty years. And a half. But I look a thousand, don't I?
textes.Quelle barque ? Il n'y a jamais eu de ba: What boat? There never was a boat.
What a lovely day for sailing.
textes.Quelle blessure ? Je ne me blesse jamais: What injury? I never get hurt.
textes.Quelle brume dans ma tête…: Such a fog in my head…
textes.Quelle chanson joue le juke-box ?: Which song does the jukebox play?
textes.Quelle chute ? Celle-là ? Elle était par: What offcut? This one? It was on the floor, so it's nobody's!
What nutshell? Never heard of it. Hmph.
textes.Quelle couleur pour la coque ? (On peut: Which colour for the hull? (You can change it for free, I've got pots all over the workshop.)
textes.Quelle heure il est ? … Oh, c'est encore: What time is it? … Oh, it's still very early. Or very late. Good night!
textes.Quelle louve ? Ah… Il était deux fois, u: What she-wolf? Ah… Twice upon a time, there was a she-wolf…
textes.Quelle mousse ! Tu es doué ! Un peu en a: What foam! You're gifted! A little splashed onto the ceiling, but that's the sign of a good cacao. Here, taste!
textes.Quelle soupe, mon chou ? Je ne vois pas: What soup, sweetie? I don't know what you're talking about.
textes.Quelle surprise ! Haute comme le phare,: What a surprise! As tall as the lighthouse, the wave?
textes.Quelle tristesse ! Une bière pour oublie: How sad! A fizz to help you forget?
textes.Quelle île ! L'hôtel est parfait, la pla: What an island! The hotel's perfect, so is the beach, and the bouillabaisse… I'll have to buy bigger trousers.
textes.Quelles dettes ?! Ha ! Tu parles comme u: What debts?! Ha! You sound like a certain captain with a wooden leg! Careful, sweetie: sooner or later, everybody runs into Mama Grog.
textes.Quelqu'un ! Plume-de-Nuage, ma plus jeun: Someone! Plume-de-Nuage, my youngest sky jellyfish! She's as big as an umbrella, transparent, with little pink glints, and she sings very softly, like a rubbed wine glass. This morning, I opened the Greenhouse roof to air it out... and poof. She's gone. She has a jellyfish's sense of direction: none. She must be floating somewhere around the island. Sextant spends his days sketching from the lookouts: ask him if he's seen her. And if you find her, approach gently. She follows light, and kindness.
textes.Quelqu'un ? TOUT LE MONDE me doit de l'a: Someone? EVERYBODY owes me money, dearie. But only one has owed me forty coins for three moons: Gontran Lestrange, Jambe-de-Bois, captain of the Veuve Écarlate. Go and demand my purse from him. Politely, first. And if he plays the smart aleck… here, we settle things fair and square, with fists. But don't break him too badly: he's one of my best customers.
textes.Quelqu'un a vu Lyra danser derrière les: Someone saw Lyra dancing behind the trees. Elves love the beat, even if they won't admit it.
textes.Quelqu'un gratte une guitare, assis sur: Someone strums a guitar, sitting on a purple pouf. A young woman hums along with him.
textes.Quelqu'un laisse des poèmes dans mes boî: Someone leaves poems in my lantern boxes. Poems about the night, about flames. Never signed. I think it's Nox. He blushes as soon as anyone says the word “poem”. And he's already completely blue.
Someone who measures better than you.
Someone is practicing a piece of music. Well… it sounds like a piece of music.
textes.Quelqu'un tire sur une citrouille, la nu: Someone shoots at a pumpkin at night, behind the fountain. One arrow in three, bullseye. I do my rounds further away, so as not to disturb. The elbow's still too high. I don't know who it is. Officially.
textes.Quelqu'un vole des croissants à la boula: Someone's been stealing croissants from the bakery at night. The sergeant's investigating. I'm saying nothing, but I saw a snout.
textes.Quelqu'un vole les croissants de Margaux: Someone steals Margaux's croissants every night. Officer Lefort wants witness statements.
textes.Quels dés, ma chère ? Je n'ai que des ma: What dice, my dear? I've only got sleeves.
textes.Question d'examen, {surnom} ! Quand tu n: Exam question, {surnom}! When you don't know an answer, what do you do?
textes.Question d'ingénieur : vous croyez, vous: Engineer's question: do you believe something can last forever?
textes.Question d'ingénieure, {surnom} : si vou: An engineer's question, {surnom}: if you could invent just one thing, just one, what would it be?
textes.Question de la maison, {surnom} : café,: House question, {surnom}: coffee, tea or hot chocolate?
textes.Question de laboratoire : vous préférez: Laboratory question: do you prefer storms or fine weather?
textes.Question de métier : quel est l'objet qu: A question of the trade: what's the one thing you'd never sell?
textes.Question de routine. Vous avez déjà enfr: Routine question. Have you ever broken the law? Even a tiny bit?
textes.Question importante : tu préfères les co: Important question: do you prefer round shells or pointy ones?
textes.Question importante, mon ami : tu es plu: Important question, my friend: are you more of a punch, coconut water or cool water person?
textes.Question pour mes rouleaux, {surnom} : l: A question for my scrolls, {surnom}: up there, does anyone still remember us?
textes.Question scientifique ! Vous avez déjà f: Scientific question! Have you ever blown something up?
textes.Question scientifique, {surnom} ! Si tu: Scientific question, {surnom}! If you could invent anything at all, what would it be?
textes.Question scientifique, {surnom} : tu pré: Scientific question, {surnom}: do you prefer things that go boom, or things that go tick-tock?
textes.Question sérieuse, la plus importante de: Serious question, the most important of the day: are you more of a croissant or a pain au chocolat person?
textes.Question sérieuse, très sérieuse : ton p: Serious question, very serious: your favourite flavour, vanilla, strawberry or coconut?
textes.Question sérieuse, {surnom} ! Vous préfé: Serious question, {surnom}! Do you prefer useful things or pretty things?
textes.Question sérieuse, {surnom}. Quand tu es: Serious question, {surnom}. When you're ill, do you take a potion, or wait for it to pass?
Quetzalcóatl greets you too, Ix Kanul.
textes.Queue-Massue : dos tout dur, comme pierr: Club-Tail: back all hard, like stone. Hit on back, no use. His tail spin, spin… and BAM. Hit on head, or when he tired.
textes.Qui est là ? … Ha ! Je le savais. C'est: Who's there? … Ha! I knew it. It's always you.
textes.Qui est là ? … Un visiteur ! Désolé, je: Who's there? … A visitor! Sorry, I can't open up: I'm made of stone, it takes a while to get up. Come back in a hundred years!
textes.Qui monte à mon échelle sans prévenir ?: Who's climbing my ladder without warning? … A customer, maybe. Octave Taillefer, blacksmith. Here we sell, we buy, we don't chit-chat. Well, not much.
textes.Qui sait ? Quelqu'un a peut-être déjà ré: Who knows? Maybe someone already has.
textes.Qui va là ? Un client ou un voleur ?: Who goes there? A customer or a thief?
textes.Qui va là ? … Un terrien. Bon. Tu as dev: Who goes there? … A landlubber. Fine. Before you stands Captain Croc-de-Sel, master of the Murène Noire, terror of the seven seas, and regular customer of the tavern across the way. What do you want?
textes.Quinze pièces. L'encre de seiche, ça ne: Fifteen coins. Cuttlefish ink doesn't fish itself. Come back when you've got enough.
textes.Quoi ? Ah, les meubles ? C'est le reste: What? Oh, the furniture? It's the rest of the world that's upside down. I'm perfectly fine like this.
textes.Quoi ? Bon… oui. Elle s'appelle « Gertru: What? Fine… yes. She's called “Gertrude”. Like crate number twelve. Don't look at me like that.
textes.Quoi ? Jamais ? Comme le pirate ! Assied: What? Never? Like the pirate! Sit down, you've gone all pale. No, I'm the one who's pale. Water! Brother, I have to teach you. It's urgent.
RAINVILLE
It rains here. All the time.
We've got used to it.
textes.RHUBARBE ! (L'oiseau saute sur son épaul: RHUBARB! (The bird jumps onto her shoulder and nibbles her ear: “Shiver me timbers!”) … Well. You saw nothing. A captain doesn't cry. Here, some coins, and one of his feathers: he lost that one biting me the day I found him. You're a friend of the Requin Borgne now.
textes.RIEN ?! COMMENT ÇA, RIEN ?! … Tu te moqu: NOTHING?! WHAT DO YOU MEAN, NOTHING?! … Are you making fun of me? … No? Then you're lucky. Very lucky. It annoys me.
textes.RIEN ?! Par les racines de l'Arbre-Mère: NOTHING?! By the roots of the Mother Tree! Sit down. Right now. In the Bois-Doré, nobody leaves on an empty stomach. Here. And here. And this one too.
textes.RRRIIIIIII ! Le larsen siffle dans toute: EEEEEE! The feedback whistles through the whole yurt! The two musicians burst out laughing: “That's the sound of Rainville!”
textes.Rachid ? Le petit-fils de Lalla Mennana,: Rachid? The grandson of Lalla Mennana, the greatest weaver of the oasis. He inherited her carpets, not her silence. He talks prices the way I talk djinns.
Rachid and I are getting married in the spring. He wants a carpet for the wedding. I told him he'd get babouches.
textes.Rachid m'a demandée en mariage comme on: Rachid proposed to me the way you sell a carpet. Hand on heart: “One husband, very handsome, very chatty, special fiancée price.” I said: “Too expensive.” He lowered it. “Still too expensive.” He lowered it. At the third price, I said yes. He looked so surprised that I nearly started haggling again. We're getting married in the spring.
textes.Rachid ne se tait jamais. Jamais ! Sauf: Rachid never stops talking. Never! Except in front of me: then he searches for words, and it's the most beautiful silence in the souk. That's why I'm marrying him.
textes.Rachid, c'est mon frère de souk. Il parl: Rachid is my souk brother. He talks, I laugh, we sell. The only man in Tazira who chatters more than I do. And he suspects nothing about his wedding. NOTHING.
textes.Rachid, petit, s'endormait dans mon cerc: As a boy, Rachid used to fall asleep in my circle, his head on a sack of dates. At the end of the story, he'd wake with a start and ask: “How much, the story?” Eight years old! I'd tell him: “Whatever you like.” He'd answer: “Then it's too expensive.” I knew that day he'd sell carpets.
textes.Rachid. Il parle. Je me tais. Il perd. I: Rachid. He talks. I keep quiet. He loses. He doesn't understand why. That's why he loses.
textes.Raconte ! Tout ! Même la chèvre !: Tell me! Everything! Even the goat!
textes.Raconte-moi d'abord d'où vient la menthe: First tell me where the mint comes from, Aëlwen.
Tell me about your life again.
textes.Raconter la fresque de la Bergerie à Mèr: Tell Mother Moon, the elder of Ramure, about the Sheepfold fresco
textes.Raconter tout au Vieux Silas (près des f: Tell Old Silas everything (near the fires on the shore in the morning, at the Crâne Fendu in the evening)
textes.Raconter une dernière histoire, la plus: To tell one last story, the finest, in front of the whole Crâne Fendu. And at the end, for nobody to ask if it's true. For them to just be quiet, that's all. Like the Silent One.
textes.Raconter à Matthias ce que j'ai vu (capi: Tell Matthias what I saw (Carène harbour master's office, on the poop deck)
textes.Raconter à Nadine le voyage de ses carte: Tell Nadine about her postcards' journey
textes.Racontez-moi, Pauline ! Je prends ma plu: Tell me, Pauline! I'm taking up my pen!
Stingy, my little soap bubble. Like your father.
textes.Ragoût aux champignons de braise et bièr: Ember mushroom stew and Forgefer fizz! And I buy anything edible. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Rainville — des yourtes sombres, des gar: Rainville — dark yurts, garages, amps… and a little cloud that never leaves
textes.Rallumer le cristal de l'Aile de la Lune: Rekindle the crystal of the Moon Wing (to the east)
textes.Rallumer le cristal de l'Aile des Marées: Rekindle the crystal of the Tide Wing (to the west)
textes.Rallumer le cristal de l'Aile des Rouage: Rekindle the crystal of the Cog Wing (to the north)
textes.Rallumer le cristal de l'Aile des Sables: Rekindle the crystal of the Sand Wing (to the south)
textes.Ramasser les trois éclats de lune : près: Pick up the three moon shards: near the altar of the Circle of Moonstones (west of the Academy), in the Twisted Wood (to the south-west) and on the western shore
textes.Ramasser trois bûches de bois tordu dans: Pick up three logs of twisted wood in the Twisted Wood (south-west of the island)
textes.Ramasser trois cristaux de soufre au bor: Pick up three sulphur crystals at the edge of the hot springs (at the foot of the Great Blaze)
textes.Ramasser trois flocons de givre éternel: Pick up three everlasting frost flakes on the northern cliffs of the island
textes.Ramasser trois fragments de météorite to: Gather three meteorite fragments that fell during the last shooting-star shower (one on the Agora of Stars, one in the Hanging Gardens, one at the Spaceport)
textes.Ramasser trois paniers de légumes dans l: Gather three baskets of vegetables in the Shared Gardens (east of the town, near the container village of the Boxes)
textes.Ramasser trois plumes du vent : sur la c: Pick up three wind feathers: on the western hill, at the edge of the northern cliffs, and on the eastern cliff
Pick up items on the island with E.
textes.Ramender un dernier filet, le plus grand: To mend one last net, the biggest in Tazira, with Khadija. So big it would take the whole fleet to haul it. And to give it to the whole fleet.
textes.Ramener Miou à Nebet, à Per-Hâpy: Bring Miou back to Nebet, in Per-Hâpy
textes.Ramener Rhubarbe à la capitaine Anne-Ros: Bring Rhubarbe back to Captain Anne-Rose Corbeau (at the helm of the Requin Borgne by day; at the Crâne Fendu at noon)
textes.Ramener Sardine à Tornade (au Bassin à s: Bring Sardine back to Tornade (at the Dry Dock, the skatepark, in the north-east of the town)
textes.Ramure : la théière qui remue la queue: Ramure: the teapot that wags its tail
textes.Ramure est née dans les arbres parce que: Ramure was born in the trees because the forest was full of mist, and the mist full of wolves. Real wolves, not Croc-Gris. We built our houses up high. Then the wolves left, and we stayed: it was too lovely.
textes.Ramure, le village des oreilles — les ar: Ramure, the village of the ears — the giant trees, the Swap Market, the Moon Circle
Hard feelings too. Use the door.
textes.Range cette épée dans le village. Ici, c: Put that sword away in the village. Here, I'm the one who keeps watch.
textes.Range ton doigt. Pas de grenouille aujou: Put that finger away. No frog today.
textes.Range ça, ou je te le fais avaler !: Put that away, or I'll make you eat it!
textes.Rangez ce papyrus, Amenemhat. Je vous en: Put that papyrus away, Amenemhat. I beg you.
textes.Raoul grésillait. Mistral disait « la me: Raoul was crackling. Mistral said “the sea”. I'd been searching for an hour. Bastien walked by, listened for two seconds: “It's a crab.” I opened it up. A crab. Two seconds. … I haven't forgiven him yet. It'll come. Not right away.
textes.Raoul, le gros caisson, grésillait. Mist: Raoul, the big speaker, was crackling. Mistral said it was the sea, Tchoum had been searching for an hour. I was passing by and said: “It's a crab.” A fisherman knows the sound of a crab in a box. Tchoum opened it up: a crab. Since then, he doesn't look at me quite the same way. A bit sideways.
textes.Rapport : né il y a trois siècles, au bo: Report: born three centuries ago, at the edge of the forest. First memory: a deer track in the mud. Second memory: my mother looking for me, because I'd followed the track. I always found the track. Nobody ever found me. I came back on my own.
textes.Rapport, oncle Bramm. Les golems sont de: Reporting, Uncle Bramm. The golems have come further down.
textes.Rapporte-les à la reine Néréa !: Bring them back to Queen Néréa!
textes.Rapporter 4 bûches à Tobias (une hache e: Bring 4 logs to Tobias (an axe and a tree will do), on the Léviathan's lower deck
textes.Rapporter au Révérend Père Farfalle (au: Bring Reverend Father Farfalle (at the Colander Temple) Mamma Lasagna's pasta, a jar of volcano sauce and the Golden Grater
textes.Rapporter deux cuisses de grenouille (co: Bring back two frog legs (an order for the inn)
textes.Rapporter deux dents de crocodile à Khét: Bring two crocodile teeth to Khéty (the crocodiles lie at the mouth of the Iterou, east of Per-Hâpy)
textes.Rapporter deux navets dorés (Père Gauber: Bring back two golden turnips (Father Gaubert wants them stuffed)
textes.Rapporter huit pots de gelée (Madame Olg: Bring back eight jars of jelly (Madame Olga is preparing a bath)
textes.Rapporter l'alliance à Léa: Bring the wedding ring back to Léa
textes.Rapporter l'antenne à Sergent Fréquence: Bring the antenna back to Sergeant Fréquence (at the Radio Boucan studio, in the wheelhouse of the stranded cargo ship in the north-west)
textes.Rapporter l'engrenage à Firmin Cogne, à: Bring the gear back to Firmin Cogne, at his stand at the Fair
textes.Rapporter l'holo-photo à Glorb (il se pr: Bring the holo-photo back to Glorb (he wanders all over Astralys: Museum, Agora, Nebula Café, lookouts, Bazaar…)
textes.Rapporter l'éclat de lentille à Anselme,: Bring the lens shard back to Anselme, at the lighthouse
textes.Rapporter l'Œil d'Horus de la Pyramide d: Bring back the Eye of Horus from the Pyramid of Ra
textes.Rapporter la Plume de Quetzalcóatl des C: Bring back Quetzalcóatl's Feather from the Five Suns
textes.Rapporter la bannière à Sire Tancrède (à: Bring the banner back to Sir Tancrède (at the Guild, in the castle courtyard in the morning, or on the ramparts in the afternoon)
textes.Rapporter la carte au Capitaine Croc-de-: Bring the map back to Captain Croc-de-Sel (on the deck of the Murène Noire by day, at La Murène Ivre in the evening)
textes.Rapporter la clochette d'argent à Bedain: Bring the silver bell back to Bedaine, at the Swap Market (at the foot of the Mother Oak)
textes.Rapporter la graine à la reine Oriane, d: Bring the seed back to Queen Oriane, in the fairy clearing
textes.Rapporter la partition à Django: Bring the sheet music back to Django
textes.Rapporter la puce à Kenji, à son atelier: Bring the chip back to Kenji, at his workshop in the Alleys
textes.Rapporter le Cœur de gelée royale à Maît: Bring the Royal jelly heart back to Master Hugues (in his office, at the back of the Guild, or at a tavern table in the evening)
textes.Rapporter le Masque de Jade de Xibalba: Bring back the Jade Mask from Xibalba
textes.Rapporter le chapeau au Baron Barthélemy: Bring the hat back to Baron Barthélemy (at the castle, at the top of the Hill: throne room in the morning, garden or rampart in the afternoon)
textes.Rapporter le panier vide à Margaux: Bring the empty basket back to Margaux
textes.Rapporter le parapluie à Mamie Tournesol: Bring the umbrella back to Granny Sunflower, in the Flower Camp
textes.Rapporter les champignons à Mère-Lune (d: Bring the mushrooms back to Mother Moon (in front of her house, halfway up the Mother Oak, or at the Moon Circle at night)
textes.Rapporter les noms à Odette, à la capita: Bring the names back to Odette at the harbour master's office
textes.Rapporter les plans du Lisse-Center à Ma: Bring the Lisse-Center plans back to Mamie Barricade (at the Cannery, in the assembly room on the roof)
textes.Rapporter les quatre livres à Théophrast: Bring the four books back to Théophraste Filandre
textes.Rapporter les trois graines à Photon et: Bring the three seeds back to Photon and plant them with him (in the Hanging Gardens, west of the Agora)
textes.Rapporter les trois pages à Madame Olga: Bring the three pages back to Madame Olga (at her magic shop, on the Great Square)
textes.Rapporter trois crocs de gobelin (pour l: Bring back three goblin fangs (for Master Hugues's necklace)
textes.Rapporter trois dents de crocodile à Bru: Bring three crocodile teeth to Brutus, at the forge (you get them from the crocodiles of the Drowned Marsh, west of the island)
textes.Rapporter trois pots de gelée de slime (: Bring back three jars of slime jelly (for the apothecary)
textes.Rapporter une bouture du bougainvillier: To take home a cutting of Rose's bougainvillea and have it climb up my shop, back there. So that people on the mainland walk past and wonder where that colour comes from. From Port-Azur, I'll tell them.
textes.Rapporter à Orbe un coquillage (sur les: Bring Orbe a seashell (from the beaches of Port-Azur or Village Island), a parrot feather (Balafre Island), a scarab (Island of the Three Suns), a Bilge Rats patch (Boucan Island) and a golden turnip (Montjoie Island, in the Southern Fields) — Orbe is at the Museum of Worlds, west of the Agora
textes.Raptor : petit, rapide, toujours en band: Raptor: small, fast, always in pack. Raptor circle around, then jump. When raptor crouch and hiss: you move! After jump, raptor all dizzy: hit!
textes.Rater ? Moi ? (Un couteau se plante dans: Miss? Me? (A knife thunks into the post, an inch from your ear.) Oops. See? I did NOT miss. I was aiming at the post.
textes.Rattraper trois graines lumineuses qui f: Catch three glowing seeds floating high up in the Zero-Gravity Garden (at the end of the bridge of light, past the Hanging Gardens: you jump three times higher there)
textes.Raté ! C'était un secret. Mais tu as ess: Wrong! It was a secret. But you tried, that's good.
textes.Raté ! Le virus ricane… On revoit la séq: Missed! The virus sniggers… Let's see the sequence again.
textes.Raté… le poisson a filé avec l'appât. Il: Missed… the fish got away with the bait. Another one will come.
textes.Ravi ! J'ai déjà pris trois cents photos: Delighted! I've already taken three hundred photos. Two of them in focus.
Delighted! I planted the seed myself. Well, the queen let me hold the spade.
textes.Raymond ! Tu pointes ou tu boudes ?: Raymond! Are you pointing or pouting?
textes.Raymond ? Un menteur, un mauvais perdant: Raymond? A liar, a sore loser, a good-for-nothing shooter. Forty years I've put up with him. If he doesn't come to play one morning, I go knock on his door. To check he's still cheating.
textes.Raymond ?! Il t'a payé combien ? Une bag: Raymond?! How much did he pay you? A baguette? Two? … Fine. I don't hold it against you. Well, a little. Go on, you'll come to your senses.
textes.Raymond dit qu'on lui a volé la mairie,: Raymond says the town hall was stolen from him, and he votes for me at every election. I don't understand the man, but I like him.
textes.Raymond et Marcel jouent à la pétanque d: Raymond and Marcel have been playing pétanque for forty years. They lost the jack yesterday, and they've been sulking ever since.
textes.Raymond et Marcel ont perdu leur cochonn: Raymond and Marcel have lost their jack, somewhere near the fountain.
textes.Raymond m'a livré le pain pendant quaran: Raymond delivered my bread for forty years. When he loses at pétanque, he comes to sulk at my place. He's the finest sulker on the square.
textes.Raymond m'a vendu la boulangerie, mais i: Raymond sold me the bakery, but he never really left. He comes up behind me at the oven and says: “Too hot.” “Too much honey.” “You knead like a seamstress.” Twelve years he's been giving me advice. I followed one piece. The bread is better. I've never told him which one.
textes.Raymond s'est fait une entorse à la péta: Raymond sprained his ankle playing pétanque. On Monday, he told me he'd tripped while pointing. On Tuesday, that a dog ran between his legs. On Wednesday, that Marcel had shoved him. On Thursday, Marcel came to tell me Raymond had tripped all by himself over his own ball. I believe them both. It suits me.
textes.Raymond t'a dit qu'il était champion ? I: Raymond told you he was champion? He's lying. It's me. Marcel, pleased to meet you.
textes.Raymond, c'est mon livreur, mon critique: Raymond is my delivery man, my critic and Nina's grandpa. He thinks there's too much honey in my bread. He eats it twice a day. I adore him.
textes.Rayon quatre. Les chiots sont rares en p: Shelf four. Puppies are rare in poetry.
textes.Rayé de bleu, vif et nerveux. Rend un cœ: Striped with blue, quick and lively. Restores one heart.
textes.Re-bienvenue, {surnom} ! Ta chambre sur: Welcome back, {surnom}! Your room on the terrace is free.
textes.Re-bonjour ! J'ai raté une nouvelle poti: Hello again! I've botched a new potion. It's even more botched than the others. I'm very proud.
textes.Re-bonjour ! Le piano a appris un nouvea: Hello again! The piano has learned a new piece. Well, it thinks it has.
textes.Re-bonjour ! Tes pommes d'hier étaient b: Hello again! Were yesterday's apples good? Today's are better.
textes.Re-bonjour ! Toujours rien de cassé ? Br: Hello again! Still nothing broken? Well done.
textes.Re-bonjour ! Tu as oublié quelque chose: Hello again! Did you forget something?
textes.Re-bonjour ! Tu veux voir le tapis du ca: Hello again! Want to see the captain's carpet? It's coming along.
textes.Re-bonjour ! Ça mord, aujourd'hui. Ou al: Hello again! They're biting today. Or maybe I'm the one biting. We'll see.
textes.Re-bonjour. Regarde, celle-ci est nouvel: Hello again. Look, this one's new: an eight-pointed star.
textes.Re-salam, {surnom}. La pêche était bonne: Salam again, {surnom}. The fishing was good.
textes.Re-salut ! Je t'ai rouvert le système. L: Hi again! I reopened the system for you. The virus hasn't moved: it's sulking in its corner. Let's pick up where you left off!
textes.Recevoir ! Ah, le bruit de l'enveloppe q: Receive! Ah, the sound of an envelope being torn open! It's the best job in the world, bringing that sound to people's homes. I'll bring you one, one day. Promise.
textes.Recevoir la graine de l'esprit de l'arbr: Receive the seed from the tree spirit
textes.Recommence, et c'est mon marteau qui te: Do that again, and my hammer will answer you.
textes.Recompte vite. Le match est à l'aube !: Count fast. The match is at dawn!
textes.Reculez ! Non, avancez ! Non, reculez !: Step back! No, step forward! No, step back!
textes.Redanser avec le dauphin. Mais en vrai,: Dance with the dolphin again. But for real this time: it looks at me, it does a step, and everyone sees it. Especially Bastien.
textes.Redémarrage impossible : ferme l'applica: Cannot restart: close the app and launch the EXE again after Quest Link.
textes.Regarde ! Elles poussent ! Tu as une jol: Look! They're growing! You have a lovely voice… for a human.
textes.Regarde ! Pif ! Paf ! Des étincelles ! M: Look! Zip! Zap! Sparkles! My wand works wonderfully!
textes.Regarde ce que j'ai. Tu as {pieces} pièc: Look at what I have. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Regarde comme l'eau est claire !: Look how clear the water is!
textes.Regarde d'en bas. C'est plus sûr. Pour t: Look from the bottom. It's safer. For everyone.
Look up there. It moved a noodle. It did, I swear.
textes.Regarde partout, même en l'air et sous l: Look everywhere, even up high and under stones. Islands love hiding things.
textes.Regarde toutes ces belles fenêtres !: Look at all these lovely windows!
textes.Regarde toutes ces étoiles. On ne s'en l: Look at all those stars. You never tire of them.
textes.Regarde, choisis, et ne te brûle pas les: Look, choose, and don't burn your fingers. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Regarde, choisis. Tout est fait ici, sou: Look, choose. Everything is made here, under the sun. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Regarde, il arrive ! Ah non, c'est une m: Look, it's coming! Oh no, it's just a seagull.
textes.Regarde, je fais un bateau avec ma purée: Look, I'm making a boat out of my mashed potatoes!
textes.Regarde, mais ne touche pas avec les doi: Look, but don't touch with greasy fingers. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Regarde, renifle, choisis ! Tu as {piece: Look, sniff, choose! You have {pieces} coins. We take coins here too, even if we'd rather swap.
textes.Regarde, touche, sens, goûte. Ici, on pr: Look, touch, smell, taste. Here, we take our time. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Regarde, voyageur. Tu as {pieces} pièces: Take a look, traveller. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Regarde-les se bousculer ! Le gros orang: Look at them jostle! The big orange one is Admiral: he always eats first. Thank you! Here, a pearl from my garden.
textes.Regarde-le… l'Albatros ! Il flotte, il r: Look at it… the Albatros! It floats, it purrs, it's magnificent. I think I'm going to cry. No. Yes. A little. Call it wherever you like: it will come and land next to you.
Look. But hands behind your back.
textes.Regarder dans la longue-vue du Belvédère: Look through the telescope at the Lookout of Colours (E, at the edge of the platform, at the very top of the Great Oak)
textes.Regarder la Palette de pierre et ses neu: Look at the Stone Palette and its nine empty paint pots
textes.Regarder une fois dans la grande lunette: To look just once through Céleste's great telescope, in Cliquetis. A real one, with glass. And see whether, from there, our moon is still full.
textes.Regardez ! Trois mille bulles par minute: Look! Three thousand bubbles a minute! And that one… that one is heart-shaped. I don't know how I do it. Tell the jury people smile thirty-four per cent more near my machine.
textes.Regardez ce livre, sur l'étagère. Ne ten: Look at that book, on the shelf. Don't reach out your arm: reach out your wish. Want it. Gently. … It's coming! It's coming! Catch it! Perfect. Aim, and call: the book will fly to you. Now, go and fetch me the four runaways.
textes.Regardez ce que j'ai trouvé dans le cerc: Look what I found in the fairy circle, behind the dune…
textes.Regardez sa queue ! Boulon a compris. Il: Look at his tail! Boulon understood. He's wagging so hard the spring is singing. You've just made a friend for life. A robot dog's life is a long one.
Look at it, instead. It doesn't move.
textes.Regardez-les briller dans vos mains… Mai: Watch them shine in your hands… Now, close your eyes. Think of the morning, of the first glow on the sea. Open your hand. … There! A little light, all yours. It will follow you. Go and try it in the Crypt of Runes: the three runes at the back show themselves only to it.
textes.Rejoindre l'île des elfes en bateau: Sail to the island of the elves
textes.Remettre le Petit Piston en marche et l': Get the Little Piston running again and take it all the way to Carène, along the coast. With Gonzague on board, if he wants. Especially if he wants.
textes.Remettre une roue à ma roulotte, un jour: Put a wheel back on my caravan one day, and go round the archipelago again. One last time. And come back here, of course. The ball says I'll come back. For once, I believe it.
textes.Remonter le temps… Il y a un matin, il y: Going back in time… There's a morning, six years ago, when I could have used that. … Sorry. It's nothing. It's a lovely idea, {surnom}. A lovely idea.
textes.Remonter les trois étoiles de mer du fon: Bring up the three starfish from the bottom of the bay, in front of the beach
textes.Remplir un pot de sauce à la Louche Sacr: Fill a jar with sauce at the Sacred Ladle (at the edge of the Cooking Pot), then ask Captain Rigatoni for the Golden Grater (his Houseboat, east of the Parmesan Beach)
textes.Rencontrer Lyra, l'elfe, au cœur de l'îl: Meet Lyra the elf in the heart of Village Island
textes.Rendre l'appareil photo à Gérard: Give the camera back to Gérard
textes.Rendre la Flamme Éternelle au Cœur-Brasi: Return the Eternal Flame to the Ember Heart (in the middle of the nave of the Forge Cathedral)
textes.Rendre la guitare et l'ampli à Rouille (: Give the guitar and the amp back to Rouille (at the Cannery in the morning, on the square in the afternoon, at the Howling Hall in the evening)
textes.Rendre le cerf-volant à Théo: Give the kite back to Théo
textes.Rendre le cochonnet à Raymond: Give the boules jack back to Raymond
textes.Rendre sa lumière au Cœur de la Flèche: Restore the light of the Spire's Heart
textes.Rendre visite au Capitaine Rigatoni, dan: Visit Captain Rigatoni in his Houseboat
textes.Rendre à l'Île Crayonnée toutes ses coul: Give Sketched Island back all its colours
textes.Rentre ce soir, ou c'est moi qui descend: Come home tonight, or I'm coming down.
Come home tonight. I'll make soup.
textes.Rentrer un jour sur mon île, avec Bertha: To go home to my island one day, with Bertha all shiny. Fire a blank in front of the harbour to salute my father. He'll come out swearing like a carter. And then I'll come ashore.
textes.Repassé en biais ! C'est la nouveauté !: Ironed on the bias! It's the latest thing!
textes.Repassé en biais, chère Grisette ! La no: Ironed on the bias, dear Grisette! The latest thing!
textes.Reprendre le ciseau d'argent à ce requin: To get the silver chisel back from that shark. I don't wish it any harm. Well, a little. One teeny red-coral bite, for honour's sake.
textes.Reprendre les commandes un jour. De jour: To take the controls again one day. By day, in fine weather, without a single cloud. All the way to Ramure. And there, above the six great trees, wave to Plumette. In flight. Her with her wings, me with my Zéphyr.
textes.Repu ! Comme ma taverne. J'ai goûté ma n: Stuffed! Like my tavern. I tasted my new sauce all morning. It's ready. So am I. For a nap.
textes.Repêcher le gros mérou. Pas pour le mang: Catch the big grouper again. Not to eat him, eh! So he repeats his answer in front of witnesses. I'll carry him to the tavern in a bucket, and Gwenola won't be able to say I dreamed it.
textes.Rester à Tazira pour toujours. Avoir une: To stay in Tazira forever. Have a blue boat with Ahmed, with an eye on the prow, and catch real sardines. In the evening, sit in Ba Sidi's circle. And one day, I'll be the one telling the stories.
textes.Rester. Juste ça. Et un jour, perdre mon: To stay. Just that. And one day lose my return ticket by accident, and not even look for it.
textes.Retiens ton souffle ! Sans masque, tu ne: Hold your breath! Without a mask, you can only last a few seconds underwater. Come up for air (Space).
textes.Retourner une fois dans le pays blanc. P: To go back to the white country once. Not to stay: to see if the ice remembers me. I think it does. Ice has a very good memory.
textes.Retourner voir Coyotl, le potier (à son: Go back to Coyotl, the potter (at his workshop, or at the market at noon)
textes.Retourner voir Grand-Mère Aquarelle: Go back to see Grand-Mère Aquarelle
textes.Retourner voir Grand-Mère Aquarelle (dev: Go back to see Grand-Mère Aquarelle (in front of the Palette in the daytime, on the Council terrace at noon and in the evening)
textes.Retourner voir Nova (à la Serre des Espè: Go back to see Nova (at the Greenhouse of Species, in the north-east, past the Academy)
textes.Retourner voir Petit-Pierre (sur le quai: Go back to see Petit-Pierre (on the quay, by the crates, in the morning; at the fishing jetty in the afternoon; on the square in the evening)
textes.Retourner voir Pixel pour la fin de la p: Go back to see Pixel for the end of the game
textes.Retourner voir Père Gaubert (aux Champs: Go back to see Père Gaubert (in the Southern Fields, in front of his farm; in the yard at noon)
textes.Retourner voir Rosalie (à la poissonneri: Go back to see Rosalie (at the fishmonger's, on the harbour, in the morning; on a café terrace or the promenade in the afternoon)
textes.Retourner voir Rouille (à la Conserverie: Go back to see Rouille (at the Cannery in the morning, on the square or the quays in the afternoon, at the Howling Hall in the evening)
textes.Retourner voir l'archimage, dans la cour: Go back to the archmage, in the courtyard of the Great Crystal
textes.Retourner voir la Doyenne Astrée (à la S: Go back to see Elder Astrée (at the Council Hall, at the foot of the Spire; on her bench in the Agora during the auroras)
textes.Retourner voir le Révérend Père Farfalle: Go back to see Reverend Father Farfalle
textes.Retourner voir le maire, devant la mairi: Go back to the mayor, in front of the town hall
textes.Retourner à Tortuga un soir de bal, avec: To go back to Tortuga on a ball night, with the Widow decked out in red. To pass under a certain window. And this time, stay standing, even if the pot falls.
textes.Retourner à la pointe dorée, descendre j: To go back to the golden point, dive down to the rooftops, and this time not come up too fast. Listen to the song right to the end. And maybe sing along.
textes.Retraité, voisin de villa de Raymond, ce: Retired, and Raymond's next-door neighbour, which is a punishment. Pétanque in the morning, pétanque in the afternoon, on pitch two. The day the jack rolled off towards the fountain, we played with a pebble, sulking. Bernard runs circles round us going hup hup. And Hortense is convinced I'm the one leaving lavender on her bench. It's not me!
textes.Retrouver Ba Sidi, le conteur de Tazira: Find Ba Sidi, the storyteller of Tazira (on Lantern Square), who has the logbook of the Léviathan
textes.Retrouver Comète (au Spatioport, ou l'ap: Find Comète (at the Spaceport, or in the afternoon at the Zero-Gravity Garden)
textes.Retrouver Germaine-la-Terrible, la guita: Find Germaine the Terrible, Clou's guitar (at the robots' lair, in front of the gate of the Grey Factory, in the south-east, behind the Spore Wood)
textes.Retrouver Mamie Barricade (à la Conserve: Find Mamie Barricade (at the Cannery, in the assembly room on the roof, or in front of the entrance in the afternoon)
textes.Retrouver Pixel et Quark, cachés quelque: Find Pixel and Quark, hiding somewhere in Astralys (in a street corner, behind a giant plant, on a floating bench… Quark hums when he hides)
textes.Retrouver Plume-de-Nuage (une petite méd: Find Plume-de-Nuage (a little pink sky jellyfish, over by the Zero-Gravity Garden, to the west) and gently lead her back to the Greenhouse of Species: she follows you if you stay close to her
textes.Retrouver Rhubarbe au vieux camp abandon: Find Rhubarbe at the old abandoned camp (to the north-west, along the camp path), and call him at the foot of his perch with the seeds (E)
textes.Retrouver Sardine, le chien au bandana r: Find Sardine, the dog with the red bandana (at the Scrapyard, in the south-east of the island, among the car wrecks: listen carefully, he barks at the robots)
textes.Retrouver Truffe dans les bosquets au bo: Find Truffe in the thickets at the edge of the Southern Fields and ring his little bell: he'll come
textes.Retrouver Zénith (à l'Observatoire, au t: Find Zénith (at the Observatory, at the telescope, at night)
textes.Retrouver l'ampli à lampes (à la Casse,: Find the tube amp (at the Scrapyard, in the south-east, among the scrap heaps, near the Scrap dragon)
textes.Retrouver la carte volée par le chat rou: Find the map stolen by the ginger cat: he climbs onto the roofs of Tazira using crates, near the houses on the quay, east of the square
textes.Retrouver la clochette de Truffe (tombée: Find Truffe's little bell (it fell in the grass near Clovis's windmill, in the Southern Fields)
textes.Retrouver la pelote de laine rouge tombé: Find the ball of red wool that fell out of Pauline's basket (in the Grand Hotel garden)
textes.Retrouver la puce holographique envolée: Find the hologram chip that flew off during the explosion in Professor Quasar's laboratory (at the Academy of Sciences, east of the Agora)
textes.Retrouver le cerf-volant de Théo sur les: Find Théo's kite on the hills, west of the town
textes.Retrouver le chapeau à plume du Baron (l: Find the Baron's plumed hat (the wind blew it south: look on top of Clovis's windmill, in the Southern Fields)
textes.Retrouver le cochonnet, près de la fonta: Find the boules jack, near the fountain on the square
textes.Retrouver le quatrième cœur de la potion: To find the fourth heart of Grandmother's potion. I taste a new root every spring. One day it'll be the right one.
textes.Retrouver les baguettes de batterie (au: Find the drumsticks (at the Dry Dock, the skatepark, in the north-east of the town, next to the harbour)
textes.Retrouver les huit autres pots de couleu: Find the eight other paint pots and pour them into the Palette: the families know where six of them fell (Basile at the pond, Rosalie in the wood, Capucine in the meadows, Lili on the beach, Gaspard at the Lookout, Achille at the waterfall); as for the turquoise and the pink, Grandpa Augustin has a little idea
textes.Retrouver les trois fromages affinés cac: Find the three aged cheeses Biscotte has hidden around Port-Coutelas (between the crates on the quay, under the fishing jetty, near the well): follow your nose
textes.Retrouver les trois pages de la partitio: Find the three pages of sheet music (the beach, the square, the quay to the east)
textes.Retrouver les trois éclats du Cœur de la: Find the three shards of the Spire's Heart (one near the Observatory, to the north; one in the Greenhouse of Species, to the north-east; one high up in the Zero-Gravity Garden, to the west): they beat softly and sing a single note
textes.Retrouver ma minute bleue ! Une seule !: Find my blue minute again! Just one! And this time, I write everything down. Even the colour of my socks.
textes.Retrouver trois pages de grimoire envolé: Find three spellbook pages that blew away around Montjoie (they glow a little: on the Great Square, in the Upper Town, in the Lower Town…)
textes.Revanche ? Ah non, vous n'avez jamais jo: A rematch? Ah no, you've never played. Not yet.
textes.Revenir chaque année à Port-Azur, chambr: To come back to Port-Azur every year, room seven, on the same day. And one day, with a child who'll ask why daddy always checks his finger. I'll say it's an old habit. He won't believe me, I hope.
textes.Revenir voir Agrafe (à l'imprimerie de l: Go back to see Agrafe (at the Spinning Mill print shop, or in the evening at the Expression Wall)
textes.Revenir voir Brindille (à la poste du po: Go back to Brindille (at the port post office)
textes.Revenir voir Honorine (à la boulangerie,: Go back to see Honorine (at the bakery, in the Middle Town)
textes.Revenir voir Ionie au Spatioport: Go back to see Ionie at the Spaceport
textes.Reviens avec ton petit ballon, Pied-Lour: Come back with your little balloon, Heavy-Foot! I only transform things that already fly.
textes.Reviens quand tu veux, j'adore ton argen: Come back any time, I love your money.
textes.Reviens vite. Et garde ton masque bien s: Come back soon. And keep your mask on tight.
textes.Reviens voir les gens souvent : à force: Come back and see people often: the more you chat, the more they'll tell you things they tell no one else.
textes.Reviens à six heures, on verra pour le r: Come back at six, we'll see about the record.
textes.Revoir le jaguar du Mont Fumant. Une foi: To see the jaguar of the Smoking Mountain again. Once. From afar. To say thank you.
textes.Rhubarbe ? Ha ! Il ne descend pour perso: Rhubarbe? Ha! He won't come down for anyone. Except for this. (He hands you a little pouch.) Sunflower seeds roasted with salt. Show them to him, and don't look him in the eye: he hates that. And if he calls you a jellyfish head, it means he likes you.
textes.Rhubarbe en dit dix. Question d'éducatio: Rhubarbe says ten. It's all in the upbringing.
textes.Rhubarbe est parti. Mon perroquet. Ce ma: Rhubarbe is gone. My parrot. That cursed bird flew off towards the jungle. I can't sleep anymore.
textes.Rhubarbe te regarde de haut, ébouriffé :: Rhubarbe looks down at you, ruffled: “Jellyfish head!” He won't come down for nothing… Perroquet-Joe surely has something to lure him.
textes.Rhubarbe, le perroquet de la capitaine,: Rhubarbe, the captain's parrot, used to land on my shoulder and shout swear words in my ear. I wanted to teach him to say “Petit-Pierre”. He learned “Petit-Pirate”. The captain laughed so hard she had to sit down on a barrel. It's the only time I've seen her laugh that much. I was really proud.
textes.Rhubarbe, le perroquet rouge de la capit: Rhubarbe, the red parrot of Captain Anne-Rose Corbeau, has flown off towards the old abandoned camp in the north-west of the island. Perroquet-Joe will know how to lure him back.
textes.Rhum ambré, eau chaude, miel et citron,: Hot water, honey and lemon, served steaming in a pewter mug. Corentin swears it cures everything. Restores one and a half hearts.
textes.Rien ! Aïe, aïe, aïe. Tu me brises le cœ: Nothing! Ouch, ouch, ouch. You're breaking my heart. Well. You're honest. That's rare in a customer, and useless in a merchant.
textes.Rien ! Enfin, une petite fusée. Toute pe: Nothing! Well, a little rocket. A tiny one. Harmless!
textes.Rien ! Juré, craché, sardiné !: Nothing! Cross my heart, spit, and sardine!
textes.Rien ! Juste un ver de terre, qui te reg: Nothing! Just an earthworm, looking at you in surprise.
textes.Rien ! Rien du tout ! … Pourquoi tu sors: Nothing! Nothing at all! … Why are you getting your quill out?
textes.Rien ! Rien du tout. Je vais le chercher: Nothing! Nothing at all. I'll get it myself.
textes.Rien ? Alors tiens, prends ce maillet. T: Nothing? Then here, take this mallet. Hit this peg. There. Now you've built a little piece of the Merciless. That counts.
textes.Rien ? Attends. Tac ! TAC ! … Toujours r: Nothing? Wait. Tac! TAC! … Still nothing? Then we're two half-deaf people. I'll hit harder when you come by.
textes.Rien ? Oh, my dear… Mais vous êtes libre: Nothing? Oh, my dear… But you're as free as a seagull! I envy you. A little. I'd offer you an object, but it would spoil everything.
textes.Rien ? … Je comprends. Plus que tu ne cr: Nothing? … I understand. More than you think. A skin without ink is a blank page. Keep it for something that's worth it.
textes.Rien ?! Viens ici. Sens. Plus fort. Safr: Nothing?! Come here. Smell. Harder. Saffron! Can you smell it now? A nose can be trained! Yours, I'll take care of.
textes.Rien du tout ? Mon pauvre ! Tenez, je vo: Nothing at all? You poor thing! Here, I'm giving you a box of nothing. In spirit, for now. That way, you'll at least have something that's good for nothing.
textes.Rien du tout ? Pas même un mouton ?: Nothing at all? Not even a sheep?
textes.Rien du tout. C'est un secret, monsieur: Nothing at all. It's a secret, Monsieur Cogne.
textes.Rien du tout. Le pirate grogne dans son: Nothing at all. The pirate grumbles in his sleep.
textes.Rien en vue pour l'instant. Explorez, re: Nothing in sight for now. Explore, meet people!
Nothing here. The treasure must be nearby.
Nothing for you, Lucas… Oh wait, here.
textes.Rien qu'avec moi ? C'est un compliment o: Only with me? Is that a compliment or a threat? Both, I hope. I love both.
textes.Rien que des cailloux. Ronds, plats, gri: Nothing but pebbles. Round, flat, grey, a little less grey… That one looks like my aunt. That one too, actually.
textes.Rien sous la tête… mais tu as l'impressi: Nothing under the head… but you get the feeling it snickered when you leaned over.
textes.Rien sur la mer. Le Cœur-de-Pierre, roug: Nothing at sea. Stoneheart, red, like yesterday.
textes.Rien à signaler. Et ne me demande pas de: Nothing to report. And don't ask me for details.
textes.Rien, Mademoiselle ! Juste un scarabée d: Nothing, Miss! Just an ember beetle!
textes.Rien, Majesté ! Absolument rien ! Comme: Nothing, Majesty! Absolutely nothing! As usual!
textes.Rien, Majesté ! Enfin… des graines. Un p: Nothing, Your Majesty! Well… seeds. A few. Lots.
textes.Rien, mon ami. Elle est parfaite. Comme: Nothing, my friend. It's perfect. Like you.
textes.Rien. Absolument rien. C'est très reposa: Nothing. Absolutely nothing. It's very restful.
textes.Rien. C'est déjà beaucoup. En surface, i: Nothing. That's already a lot. Up top, there's never nothing. There's always someone talking.
Nothing. It's none of my business.
textes.Rien. Cette tête-là regarde l'horizon, d: Nothing. This head looks at the horizon, straight ahead; not at the clouds.
textes.Rien. Hm. Les gens qui ne font rien, c'e: Nothing. Hm. People who do nothing are the ones pirates count on. I'll remember that.
textes.Rien. Ils sont de pierre, ils parlent av: Nothing. They're made of stone, they talk with their… rocks. Er. Their relations. Anyway.
Nothing. I'm not hungry in the morning.
textes.Rien. Juste l'écho de ta propre main sur: Nothing. Just the echo of your own hand on the stone. In the beginning, there was…
textes.Rien. Mais le Cœur-de-Pierre était rouge: Nothing. But Stoneheart was red tonight. Redder than yesterday.
Nothing. No Chak in the forest.
textes.Rien. Sauf peut-être… une petite vanille: Nothing. Except perhaps… a small vanilla.
textes.Rien. Tu peux vérifier. Je sais que tu v: Nothing. You can check. I know you're going to check.
textes.Rien… à part une vieille chaussette de p: Nothing… except an old pirate sock. Yuck.
textes.Rita m'a annoncé, l'œil mystérieux, que: Rita announced, with a mysterious look, that Gérard would find his camera thanks to “someone who walks a lot”. It's pretty, I'll admit. But the day before, she was on the promenade when Gérard came down from the lookout, empty-handed and looking like a lost dog. I saw her watching him. Just saying. Or not saying.
textes.Rita m'a dit que l'horloge sonnerait de: Rita told me the clock would chime again thanks to a stranger. I don't believe that nonsense. But I'm watching you, all the same.
textes.Rita me prédit un grand amour tous les a: Rita foretells a great love for me every year. She's wrong every year. I pay every year. Don't try to understand.
textes.Rita prédit à Colette un grand amour tou: Every year Rita foretells a great love for Colette, at the same price. For me, she foretold a stranger who'd make my clock ring. I told her: “Nonsense.” She replied: “You'll see.” Since then, that's how we greet each other, from one door to the other. “Nonsense.” “You'll see.”
textes.Rita, la voyante, m'a prédit un grand am: Rita, the fortune-teller, predicted a great love for me. She predicts it every year. I still pay.
textes.Roadie d'honneur du Festival du Larsen: Honorary roadie of the Larsen Festival
Round and happy! Like my belly.
textes.Ronds comme la lune, ami ! Ronds comme l: Round as the moon, friend! Round as the moon!
textes.Ronflements. Sur le canapé, quelqu'un do: Snoring. On the sofa, someone sleeps under three plaid blankets. A black cat sleeps on top of him. Nobody moves.
textes.Ronron. Le chat se roule sur le dos. C'e: Purr. The cat rolls onto its back. It's a trap, everybody knows that.
textes.Rosa a seize canons. J'en ai sept. Elle: Rosa has sixteen cannons. I have seven. She reminds me every day. Hers fire. Mine keep watch. It's not the same.
textes.Rosa m'a appris le nœud de chaise. Alors: Rosa taught me the bowline. So to practise, I tied Amine to the fountain. A perfect knot! Nobody could undo it, not even the slipper man. They had to go and get Rosa. She undid the knot, and afterwards, very quietly, she said: “Well done, little cabin girl.” Amine's still sulking.
textes.Rosa m'emprunte une lanterne à chaque fê: Rosa borrows a lantern from me at every festival. I know it, she knows I know it, and we don't talk about it. A thief who brings back what she damages: that only exists in Tazira.
textes.Rosa, c'est la plus forte pirate du mond: Rosa is the strongest pirate in the world. She's got hair as red as fire, sixteen cannons, and she knows every knot. When I grow up, I'll be like her. But a captain. And not a pirate.
textes.Rosa, la pirate, m'a montré comment on f: Rosa, the pirate, showed me how to tie a bowline. I can do it with my eyes closed. Well, almost.
textes.Rosa. La rouquine des pirates. Fille de: Rosa. The pirates' redhead. A fisherman's daughter. She rows well. She doesn't talk at sea. That's rare. I take her along.
textes.Rosalie Gomme, la jardinière, croit que: Rosalie Gomme, the gardener, thinks the pot of green (no. 2) rolled all the way to the Hollow Stump, the oldest stump on the island, deep in the Hatching Wood. She doesn't dare go there: a big owl lives there, and it gives her funny looks.
Rosalie has some lovely sea bream this morning.
textes.Rosalie chante en vidant le poisson, tou: Rosalie sings while she guts the fish, every morning, at her stall. One day, she lost her voice. My bouillabaisse was… fine. Fine! Mine! I ran to bring her honey and lemon. The next day she was singing, and so was my soup. Don't ask me to explain. Cooking isn't a science.
textes.Rosalie divise par deux toutes mes taill: Rosalie halves the size of all my fish. She's right, the rascal. I owe her a big one, and she knows it.
textes.Rosalie est à la lisière du Bois des Hac: Rosalie is at the edge of the Hatching Wood, Grandpa Augustin near the Palette.
textes.Rosalie vend le meilleur poisson du port: Rosalie sells the best fish in the harbour and repeats everything she sees. The fish, I buy. The rest, I leave to her.
textes.Rosalie, Brioche vient avec moi !: Rosalie, Brioche is coming with me!
textes.Rosalie, c'est ma poissonnière, ma chant: Rosalie is my fishmonger, my singer, and the biggest sulker in Port-Azur. Her voice puts heart into my soup. Her day-old sea bream, a lot less.
textes.Rosalie, c'est à qui, ce chat roux sur l: Rosalie, whose is that ginger cat on the roof?
textes.Rosalie, la poissonnière. Poisson excell: Rosalie, the fishmonger. Excellent fish, regrettable tongue. She undermines authority every day, out loud, in front of the whole harbour.
textes.Rosalie, ma belle ! Ce soir, la bouillab: Rosalie, my beauty! Tonight, the bouillabaisse is in your honour!
textes.Rosalie, voilà le pot de vert ! Le hibou: Rosalie, here's the pot of green! The owl didn't say a thing.
textes.Rosalie, vous cherchez quelque chose dan: Rosalie, are you looking for something in the wood?
textes.Rose a mis ma rose dans un vase, « en at: Rose put my rose in a vase, “in the meantime”. I like a florist waiting with me. She believes in happy endings, like Léa.
textes.Rose est une gentille fille, qui vend sa: Rose is a sweet girl, who sells her lavender to everyone. Which is exactly what complicates my investigation.
textes.Rose est une vraie fleuriste. Elle parle: Rose is a real florist. She talks to her bougainvillea, and it doesn't listen to her. Mine doesn't either. We understood each other straight away.
textes.Rose, c'est mon amie, ma jardinière et m: Rose is my friend, my gardener and my best supplier. Without her lavender, my herbal teas would be nothing but hot water.
textes.Rose, ma voisine. Ses bougainvilliers on: Rose, my neighbour. Her bougainvillea has invaded my roof, my ukulele invades her nights. We're even. Well, she says we're not.
textes.Rosette ! Gardez-moi la une !: Rosette! Save me the front page!
textes.Rosette a fait de mes toits une rubrique: Rosette made my roofs into a regular column! “Roof of the Week.” She understands science, she does. Well, she understands headlines. It's almost the same thing.
textes.Rosette a voulu faire son interview à cô: Rosette wanted to do her interview next to the big coil. A million volts. In the middle of her second question, her pencil melted, and her hair stood straight up. It stayed like that for three days. She wrote the article anyway, with a spare pencil. Since then, rubber boots are compulsory in the lab.
textes.Rosette a voulu interviewer Achille au p: Rosette tried to interview Achille through a megaphone, from the airfield roof. Eight days he's been circling up there, alone, with a boiler on his back, and her first question was: “Are you hungry?” He said yes. It made the front page. I could have told her he was hungry.
textes.Rosette achète ses plumes de corbeau che: Rosette buys her crow feathers from me, a dozen a month. She says they write faster than the others. I pick them out for her one by one, the blackest ones, and I sell them to her at cost. Business is tenderness with a cash register.
textes.Rosette est curieuse comme un courant d': Rosette is as curious as a draught, and just as hard to stop. She drops by the lab every afternoon. I like her, with her boots.
textes.Rosette est la meilleure gazetière de l': Rosette is the best gazette-writer on the island, and my advert appears in every issue. She writes with my crow feathers. Between you and me, she's practically family.
textes.Rosette fait de mon frère la plaisanteri: Rosette has made my brother the morning joke. “Still in flight”, the way you'd say “cloudy”. I read it anyway. To check.
textes.Rosette guette mes sacs de courrier comm: Rosette lies in wait for my mailbags like a seagull lies in wait for a trawler. And she prints my delays on the front page. She drives me up the wall. I read her Gazette every morning.
Rosette. The bag hasn't landed yet.
textes.Rou ? Rou. Rouuu. (C'est très profond, e: Coo? Coo. Cooo. (It's very deep, in pigeon.)
textes.Rou-rou. Je crois qu'il veut redevenir c: Coo-coo. I think he wants to be a hat again.
Red! Ah, the hardest one to paint. An adventurous red, afraid of nothing. For you, I'll have to outdo myself.
textes.Rouge, jaune, bleu et vert, avec une lon: Red, yellow, blue and green, with a long knotted tail. It belongs to little Théo.
textes.Rouille ? Alors c'est la maison qui offr: Rouille? Then it's on the house. (She sets a lemonade in front of you with a rat-shaped straw.) Sirène's lemonade, lemon, mint and bubbles. Nothing that goes to your head: just enough to dance until midnight. There's a concert in the evening. Come. And bring your ears, Larsen takes care of the rest.
textes.Rouille m'envoie te dire bonjour !: Rouille sent me to say hello!
textes.Rouille t'envoie ? Alors tu fais partie: Rouille sent you? Then you're part of the family! Here, have a taste. (He holds out his giant ladle, full of soup.) No, not the whole ladle. Just a sip. … There. Now you know the taste of Boucan. Come back whenever you like: here, you pay what you can. Even zero. Especially if you're hungry.
textes.Rouille, la chanteuse des Rats de Cale,: Rouille, the singer of the Bilge Rats, wants you to get to know Port-Boucan. To start with: say hello to Lentille at the Pay-What-You-Can Canteen, to Rustine at the bike workshop and to Sirène at the Howling Hall bar.
textes.Rouille, pourquoi tout le monde fait cet: Rouille, why the long faces everywhere?
textes.Rouille, tu peux me présenter un peu la: Rouille, could you show me around town a bit?
textes.Rouleau quatre cent douze, Coralin. On a: Scroll four hundred and twelve, Coralin. We're nearing the end.
textes.Rouvrir la ligne des hautes terres. Un s: To reopen the highlands line. Just one Sunday, no more. With the coffee machine at the head of the train, the Bielle puffing out steam, and a steaming cup at every window. The shepherds on the platforms. And me pulling the whistle as we pull into the station. For real, this time.
textes.Roux ? Un grand dadais de renard qui cue: Roux? A great lump of a fox who picks herbs in his sleep, apparently. He's made me laugh since we were five. It's exhausting. It's irreplaceable. Don't repeat the second word to him.
textes.Roux ? Un renard qui vend contre des piè: Roux? A fox who sells for coins on MY market! An insult to tradition. But a rival worthy of me, my friend: foxes and tanukis, it's the oldest quarrel in the forest.
textes.Roux dit que mon étoile tombée était une: Roux says my fallen star was a firefly who'd had too much tea. It's not funny. He plays the flute like nobody else. That's true. I won't tell him.
textes.Roux est encore rentré avec des feuilles: Roux came home with leaves in his tail again. He says he was gathering. I say he was sleeping under a tree.
textes.Roux joue de la flûte pendant que je dan: Roux plays the flute while I dance. He's the only one who can make me laugh in the middle of a step, and the only one I ask for advice. He answers with a joke, then with good advice.
textes.Roux raconte à tout le village que mon é: Roux tells the whole village that my star that fell into the big pond was “a firefly who'd had too much moon tea”. The children laugh. Fireflies don't fall, Roux. They don't drink tea either. I wrote him a poem to explain. He set it to music. That's worse.
textes.Roux, c'est le renard qui m'a appris les: Roux is the fox who taught me the rhythms of Tazira. Boom, boom-boom! Without him, I'd still be going boom, boom, boom. Like Bourru, but faster.
textes.Royalement bien. La bière est fraîche, l: Royally well. The fizz is cold, the forges are burning, the golems… hmm. Almost well.
textes.Royaume des fées : chez une fée: Fairy kingdom: at a fairy's home
textes.Rrriiiii ! Le larsen siffle encore. Les: Eeeeeee! The feedback squeals again. The Rainville crows fly off, offended.
Rrrrrr… pffff… (He's asleep. Deeply. There's moss on his shoulder.)
textes.Rrrr… non, pas les cailloux… rrrr…: Rrrr… no, not the pebbles… rrrr…
textes.Rubis sur l'ongle ! Ha ! Toi, tu peux t': Right on the nail! Ha! You can sit wherever you like, sweetie. Your seat is warm. And if you meet a captain with a limp, set him an example.
textes.Rubis, pièces d'or… et j'achète tout ce: Rubies, gold coins… and I buy anything that sparkles. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Rustine n'a plus de pièces de vélo : les: Rustine has run out of bike parts: Lisse's robots searched the Scrapyard to build themselves arms. There are three batches of parts left, hidden in the Scrapyard, to the south-east.
textes.RÈGLEMENT DU DONJON\nDES MILLE MARCHES\n:
RULES OF THE DUNGEON
OF A THOUSAND STEPS

1. Do not feed the slimes (they grow).
2. Do not pet the frogs (they swallow).
3. A chest that smiles is not a chest.
4. The blue crystals bring you back up here. The falls do not.

— Odon, keeper and step counter
textes.Réclamer la dette à Gontran Lestrange, d: Claim the debt from Gontran Lestrange, known as Jambe-de-Bois (on the Veuve Écarlate by day; at the Shark's Tooth in the evening)
textes.Récolter deux rayons de miel aux ruches: Gather two honeycombs from the fire bees' hives, in the Ash Wood (south-east of the city)
textes.Réconcilier Mamie Tournesol et Mère Aver: Make peace between Granny Sunflower and Mother Downpour
textes.Réconcilier le Grand Spaghetti Volant av: Reconcile the Great Flying Spaghetti with its followers
textes.Récupérer l'antenne de Radio Boucan (tou: Get back the Radio Boucan antenna (at the very top of the painted water tower, east of the town)
textes.Récupérer l'appareil photo de Gérard au: Get Gérard's camera back from the lookout (at the top of the hill path)
textes.Réparer le Léviathan, le remettre à l'ea: Fix the Léviathan, put her back in the water, and set sail with everyone on board. Everyone! Fañch and his boat on the deck, Gwenola and her stove, and my grandad right at the top of the crow's nest, like before. I'll carry him, if I have to.
textes.Répondre aux trois questions du Sphinx (: Answer the Sphinx's three questions (on the plateau of Ra, across the river, south of Per-Hâpy)
textes.Réponds-moi sérieusement, {surnom} : cro: Answer me seriously, {surnom}: do you believe the sun will rise tomorrow?
textes.Réponse de fée ! Prudente, maligne, et q: A fairy's answer! Cautious, clever, and says nothing at all. I'll write it in my big book, with your name beside it.
textes.Répète ça, et on n'est plus amis. Enfin,: Say that again, and we're not friends anymore. Well, we weren't, but we'll be even less so.
textes.Répète-le plus fort, qu'on l'entende jus: Say it louder, so they can hear it all the way to Octave's kapok tree.
textes.Résoudre l'énigme des serpents: Solve the riddle of the snakes
textes.Réunir une dernière fois les trois conte: To bring together the three storytellers of the big island one last time, Ba Sidi, Corentin and me, at the Moon Circle. Now that the Zéphyr links the towns, no more excuses! A whole night of stories…
textes.Réussir le rose. Le rose du port, le soi: To get the pink right. The pink of the port in the evening, when the lighthouse comes on. Just once. After that, I could paint notaries for the rest of my life, no problem.
textes.Réveiller les esprits de la forêt et ouv: Wake the forest spirits and open the root gate
textes.Réveiller les trois runes de la Crypte a: Wake the three runes of the Rune Crypt with the light spell (key 5 then V; in VR, left trigger): the crypt is above the garden, on the path to the Twisted Wood
textes.Révérend ! Il danse ! Il m'a touché l'ép: Reverend! He's dancing! He touched my shoulder!
textes.Révérend, pourquoi le Grand Spaghetti a-: Reverend, why does the Great Spaghetti look so sad?
textes.Révérend, voici les pâtes, la sauce et l: Reverend, here are the pasta, the sauce and the Golden Grater.
textes.Rêveuse. La mer était couleur de saphir: Dreamy. The sea was sapphire-coloured this morning.
textes.Rêveuse. Le jour, je suis rêveuse. La nu: Dreamy. By day, I'm dreamy. By night, I'm wide awake.
textes.Rúmil ! Tu es en retard. Mes lanternes o: Rúmil! You're late. My lanterns are hungry.
textes.Rúmil dit que la lumière vient mieux qua: Rúmil says light comes more easily when someone sings. So every morning at dawn, I sing for his nets. He never says thank you. He leaves me the first ray.
textes.Rúmil est né trois minutes avant moi, et: Rúmil was born three minutes before me, and he reminds me every morning. He fishes the light, I keep it. Without him, my lanterns would be empty. Without me, he'd be asleep.
textes.Rúmil pêche la lumière à l'aube, comme s: Rúmil fishes for light at dawn, like his grandfather, like I saw it done nine centuries ago. It's a dying trade. He doesn't let it die: he listens.
textes.Rúmil vient au cercle des contes avec se: Rúmil comes to the storytelling circle with his nets to mend. He never looks up, he never asks a question, and he remembers everything, word for word. One day I got a name wrong in a six-hundred-year-old story. He just coughed. I corrected myself.
S to go down, W to go back up.
textes.S'il dort ? Ha ! Il dort tout le temps à: If he's asleep? Ha! He sleeps all the time at school! With me. Come to the calmecac, you can pet us both.
If he leaves the clouds alone.
textes.S'il vous plaît, Berthe ! Il est midi, c: Yes please, Berthe! It's noon, it's time.
