textes.Survolté ! J'ai bu le jus de quatre noix: Supercharged! I drank the juice of four coconuts. I can see sounds. They're green.
textes.Sylvain ! Le stock est prêt, pour vous…: Sylvain! The stock is ready, for y— for you.
textes.Sylvain ! Une petite partie, entre gens: Sylvain! A little game, between honest folk?
textes.Sylvain a des doigts d'argent et un cœur: Sylvain has silver fingers and a heart of stone. He claims he can spot loaded dice by the sound. I have no idea what he's talking about. But I never play at his table with… my lucky dice.
textes.Sylvain est le fils de Firmin, le vieux: Sylvain is the son of Firmin, the old croupier, and he has the same fingers. They say he keeps a scrap of parchment up his sleeve. I've watched him play for twenty years. He never shows it. Like father, like son.
textes.Sylvain est le seul homme calme de la De: Sylvain is the only calm man in the Shark's Tooth. He doesn't like questions. Neither do I. We get on without talking. He asks me to keep my hook under the table.
textes.Sylvain garde un bout de parchemin dans: Sylvain keeps a scrap of parchment up his sleeve at the big table. A piece of a map, they say. He only bets it against a player who beats him three times in a row. Nobody's ever managed it.
textes.Sylvain me rachète tous mes dés trafiqué: Sylvain buys back all my loaded dice every month, and throws them into the bay. He's a man of honour, or a madman. Both pay well. I've never managed to fool him.
textes.Sylvain, c'est la Dent du Requin ; moi,: Sylvain is the Shark's Tooth; I'm the Crâne Fendu. We share the customers, the dice and the gossip. He's polite, cold and honest. All three at once. That's rare, around here.
textes.Sylvie dit que je photographie plus que: Sylvie says I take more pictures than I look. She's right. But photos, at least, don't go away.
textes.Sylvie jure qu'elle ne croit pas aux car: Sylvie swears she doesn't believe in the cards. And yet she's come back three times, always “just passing by”. Last time, I announced: “If you would come tomorrow, you would have a surprise.” She corrected me at once: “If you came, Madame Rita. No ‘would’ after ‘if’.” I let her. Even destiny needs a schoolteacher.
textes.Sylvie, c'est ma femme, la maman de Théo: Sylvie is my wife, Théo's mum, and the person who's always right. She says I photograph more than I look. It's exhausting, someone who's always right.
textes.Sylvie, la femme du photographe. Une ins: Sylvie, the photographer's wife. A schoolteacher: she believes in nothing, she corrects everything, and she still comes back to sit at my table. Sceptics make the best clients.
textes.Sylwen ! J'ai un nouveau couplet sur ta: Sylwen! I have a new verse about your brioche.
textes.Sylwen ! Le miel du jour. Tilleul et trè: Sylwen! Today's honey. Lime and clover.
textes.Sylwen ! Ton four a l'air de bonne humeu: Sylwen! Your oven seems in a good mood.
textes.Sylwen ! Ton pain de miel a traversé la: Sylwen! Your honey loaf crossed the mist, you know.
textes.Sylwen ! Ça sent le pain au miel jusqu'à: Sylwen! You can smell the honey bread all the way to the fountain!
textes.Sylwen a goûté ma chanson sur le pain. E: Sylwen heard my song about bread. She said “nice”. Coming from her, that's a triumph.
textes.Sylwen a raté son pain ce matin. Elle di: Sylwen ruined her bread this morning. She says it's the oven. It's always the oven.
textes.Sylwen dit bonjour à mes abeilles, maint: Sylwen says hello to my bees now. From a distance, but she says it. They like her. Her bread tastes of their work: that's the finest thank-you there is.
textes.Sylwen est le meilleur public du Bois-Do: Sylwen is the best audience in the Bois-Doré. She listens while kneading, she laughs at the right moment, and when she says “pretty”, it's a triumph. Her bread, now, that's a song.
textes.Sylwen fait le meilleur pain du monde, e: Sylwen makes the best bread in the world, and she never tells Mummy anything. Well, hardly ever. She forgave me for the door and the frog. I love her loads.
textes.Sylwen jure que je me suis endormie au d: Sylwen swears I fell asleep at the twelfth verse of the song he sang me last summer. I wasn't asleep. I'd closed my eyes to listen better. But if I admit it, he'll write forty more.
textes.Sylwen me garde la croûte du premier pai: Sylwen saves me the crust of the first loaf of every batch. In exchange, I tell her oven a story while it bakes: according to her, it rises better when you talk to it. It's already heard two thousand of my stories. It's my warmest listener.
textes.Sylwen me laisse façonner un petit pain,: Sylwen lets me shape a little bread roll on Saturdays. Mine always comes out a funny shape. Once it looked like Button. Sylwen baked it anyway and put it on the stall with a label: “Frog-bread, not for sale.” Everyone came to see it!
textes.Sylwen nourrit le Bois-Doré depuis deux: Sylwen has been feeding the Bois-Doré for two centuries. When she was little, I told the children about banquets so they'd forget they were hungry. She preferred to make bread. She was right.
textes.Sylwen nourrit tout le Bois-Doré et se v: Sylwen feeds the whole of Bois-Doré and takes offence if you don't have seconds. I always have seconds. It's a matter of diplomacy.
textes.Sylwen raconte à tout le monde que ma pl: Sylwen tells everyone my plank creaked on the day of the forty loaves. She doesn't even hold it against me: she laughs about it. That's worse. I wish she'd hold it against me a little.
textes.Sylwen. Elle me laisse un pain tous les: Sylwen. She leaves me bread every morning at the foot of my tower. I never see her put it there. Me, who sees everything. I don't ask her anything. I eat it.
textes.Sylwen. J'ai refait toutes les planches: Sylwen. I've redone all the planks on the north side.
Séraphine! Don't talk to me about Borée.
textes.Séraphine est une bonne archimage. Elle: Séraphine is a good archmage. She laughs when she falls; that's rare. But she's set on making me forgive. Forgiveness is like frost: it can't be ordered.
textes.Séraphine et moi sommes arrivés le même: Séraphine and I arrived the same autumn, forty years ago. She has been on first-name terms with me since the first day; I have addressed her formally since the first day. It's a matter of principle. She laughs at my principles. She is wrong to.
textes.Séraphine m'a amenée à l'Académie par l': Séraphine brought me to the Academy by the ear, and she still pulls it now and then. She's the wisest of us all. But she needs to stop trying to make me friends with that icicle.
textes.Séraphine m'a tout appris, sauf à dormir: Séraphine taught me everything, except how to sleep at night. She's the greatest witch I know, and the gentlest. I still call her “Mistress”. She pretends it annoys her.
textes.Séraphine était l'amie de ma mère. Elle: Séraphine was my mother's friend. She comes up to the Circle every evening. She thinks it's to listen to the stones. It's to watch over me: my mother asked her to. I pretend not to know.
Séraphine. Don't talk to me about Pyra.
textes.Séraphine. Pas d'échelle cette année, je: Séraphine. No ladder this year, I beg you.
textes.Sérieusement ? {dernier_cadeau} ? Tu te: Seriously? {dernier_cadeau}? Are you making fun of me, {surnom}?
textes.Sûr comme la dernière fois, Ah Kin ?: As certain as last time, Ah Kin?
textes.Sœur Pétronille, la prêtresse du Temple: Sister Pétronille, the priestess of the Temple of Dawn, was praying by the Frog Lake when the biggest giant frog in the lake swallowed her sun rosary. Without it, she doesn't dare go adventuring any more.
textes.Sœur Pétronille, vous voulez que je vous: Sister Pétronille, would you like me to read you something?
textes.T'as de la sauce sur le nez !: You've got sauce on your nose!
textes.T'as essayé, le château ? Si ça a cassé,: Did you try the castle? If it broke, it's ruins. Ruins are good too.
textes.T'as pas d'oreilles ! Enfin si, mais ell: You haven't got any ears! Well, you have, but they're teeny, on the sides! That's funny! I'm Mochi. My mum makes the bread.
textes.T'as renversé mon verre, là. Tu vas me l: You knocked over my glass, there. You're going to pay for it.
textes.T'as toujours pas vu de dauphin ? Viens: Still haven't seen a dolphin? Come to the end of the quay tomorrow morning. I'll save you a spot.
textes.T'as une queue d'écureuil, c'est de la t: You've got a squirrel tail, that's cheating.
textes.T'as vu mon château ? Il a quatre tours: Seen my castle? It's got four towers and a moat. The sea made the moat.
textes.T'as écrit le « pas » en gros, cette foi: Did you write the “not” big this time?
textes.T'es le meilleur ! Punch ce soir, c'est: You're the best! Punch tonight, it's on me!
textes.T'es qui ? T'es un pirate ? Non ? Dommag: Who are you? Are you a pirate? No? Shame. I'm Amine. When I grow up, I'll be a pirate. Or a fisherman. Or both: a treasure fisherman!
textes.T'es un inventeur ? Moi oui ! Léonce, ap: Are you an inventor? I am! Léonce, apprentice! I invented a rocket. It didn't take off. But it made loads of smoke!
textes.TE PRÉSENTER ? Avec plaisir ! Bon, je ne: INTRODUCE YOU? With pleasure! Well, I can't introduce you to everyone, there are too many of us and Tapage would talk for three days. So start with the three pillars of Boucan: Lentille, who feeds everyone at the Canteen, on the ground floor of the Cannery; Rustine, who keeps everything with wheels rolling, at the bike workshop in the Spinning Mill; and Sirène, who quenches everyone's thirst, at the bar of the Howling Hall. Tell them Rouille sent you. They'll give you a… noisy welcome.
textes.TING ! … Dans le berceau : « HIHIHI ! EN: DING! … In the cradle: “HEEHEEHEE! AGAIN! AGAIN! DING!”
textes.TOI ! Celui que rien n'énerve ! … Ça m'é: YOU! The one nothing annoys! … It still annoys me. But a bit less.
textes.TOI ! LE SEL EST À CÔTÉ DE TON ASSIETTE: YOU! THE SALT IS NEXT TO YOUR PLATE!
textes.TOI ! TU ME REGARDES ?!: YOU! ARE YOU LOOKING AT ME?!
textes.TOI AS CHASSÉ GROSSE-DENT ! (Ougha lève: YOU HUNTED GROSSE-DENT! (Ougha raises his arms. The whole Clan cheers.) Tonight, big feast! Ocre paint this on wall. You… you now of the Clan. Clan of Squares… and one Smooth!
textes.TOI QUI AIMES QUAND ÇA CRIE ! … Ta place: YOU WHO LOVE IT WHEN THERE'S SHOUTING! … Your front-row seat at the Arena is waiting for you. I reserved it by shouting.
textes.TOUCHÉ ! Hi hi hi ! On a gagné ! On reco: TAGGED! Hee hee hee! We won! We can go again whenever you like.
textes.TOUS LES TROIS ?! (Tom saute sur la tabl: ALL THREE?! (Tom jumps on the table and plays until his strings nearly snap.) ♪ And then came a stranger, with fists as hard as bronze, he put all three on the mat: long live the King, the king of fists! ♪ … Here, the King's belt: it belonged to the last champion, forty years ago. No one has worn it since.
textes.TROISIÈME FOIS DANS L'ANNEAU ! Les Seign: THIRD TIME IN THE RING! The Lords of Xibalba are defeated at the ball game, just as the Twins once beat them. “Go then… to the House of Bats.” The door at the back opens.
textes.TROP vite ! Ils vont se décrocher la mâc: TOO fast! They'll dislocate their jaws!
textes.TU AS GAGNÉ ! Devant Bondi ! Bondi a les: YOU WON! Ahead of Bondi! Bondi's ears are all flat, look at him! I'll paint your name at the very top of the board, in lantern letters. Here, the Great Race cup: it's made of Mother Oak wood, and it hasn't left Bondi's side in three years. It'll have a lot of fun with you.
textes.TU AS PÊCHÉ LE POISSON-LUNE DORÉ ?! Gast: YOU CAUGHT THE GOLDEN SUNFISH?! Gaston, fall off your perch, now's the time! You're a legend, {surnom}!
textes.Ta Chanson du Roi de la Bagarre… il lui: Your Song of the Brawl King… is it missing a verse?
textes.Ta barbe pousse encore de travers, Griml: Your beard's still growing crooked, Grimli.
textes.Ta barque peut s'amarrer au petit ponton: Your boat can moor at the little wooden jetty, next to mine. It's free. Well, for you.
textes.Ta barque va bien ? Gertrude te dit bonj: How's your rowboat? Gertrude says hello. Well… I say hello for her.
textes.Ta bière fume, Ulfa. Les runes n'aiment: Your fizz is fuming, Ulfa. The runes don't like it.
textes.Ta chambre côté mer est prête. J'ai chan: Your sea-side room is ready. I changed the sheets. There's hardly any blue left.
Your goat's on my shoulder again.
textes.Ta fleur à nectar a bien poussé, dis don: Your nectar flower's really come along, hasn't it.
textes.Ta grand-mère, elle, se taisait en tissa: Your grandmother, now, kept quiet while she wove.
textes.Ta hache sent la sève fraîche. Combien d: Your axe smells of fresh sap. How many trees was it again? {nb_arbres}? Leave me one for the shade.
textes.Ta halle tient debout sans toi ?: Is your hall still standing without you?
textes.Ta lanterne m'a volé la vedette, ce soir: Your lantern stole the show tonight.
textes.Ta lavande est coupée, Amélie. Trois bot: Your lavender's cut, Amélie. Three bunches.
textes.Ta mer, ton premier souvenir : c'est ell: Your sea, your first memory: it chose the way here. The stones say it was meant to be.
textes.Ta mère a raison. Prends-en un troisième: Your mother's right. Have a third.
textes.Ta pelle heurte de la pierre… Une trappe: Your shovel strikes stone… A trapdoor engraved with a serpent, with a bronze ring!
Your octopus scares off my sardines, Lulu.
Your pickaxe is on my goat.
textes.Ta porte aussi, Bramm. Elle ne bouge pas: So is your gate, Bramm. It doesn't move on its own, you know.
textes.Ta première fête, c'était ici. Tu la rac: Your first party was here. How do you tell it now? Polished up a bit already? Good. That's how it's done.
textes.Ta queue cachée, elle va bien ? Chut, j': How's your hidden tail? Shh, I didn't tell anyone! … Well, just Myrtille. And Gland. And Uncle.
Your railing, under my threads, Taeron.
textes.Ta réponse est dans mon grand livre : «: Your answer is in my big book: “Depends on the mystery.” Page one hundred and twelve. Between two “hmphs”.
textes.Ta tisane, Mère-Lune. Et pas de mares ce: Your tea, Mother Moon. And no ponds tonight.
textes.Ta tisane, mon vieux glaçon. Chaude, com: Your tea, my old icicle. Hot, as always.
textes.Ta épaule, c'est le meilleur poste de vi: Your shoulder is the best lookout post in the archipelago!
textes.Ta-ka ! Et un morceau de pain !: Ta-ka! And a piece of bread!
textes.Tac, tac, tac. Pardon. Abdellah, dinandi: Tap, tap, tap. Sorry. Abdellah, coppersmith. I hammer copper: trays, teapots, lanterns. Tap. Tap. Hear that? It's the music of the souk.
textes.Tac. Dis-moi, toi. Tu l'entends chanter,: Tac. Tell me, you. Do you hear the copper sing?
textes.Tac. Mon père était dinandier, et son pè: Tac. My father was a coppersmith, and his father before him. At six, I got my first hammer, the size of a finger. My father used to say: “Don't listen to your hand, listen to the copper. When it's ready, it sings clearer.” I heard nothing. For months, nothing. Then one morning, I heard it. Tac. Just like that.
Tac. Your teapot has a dent.
textes.Tac. Tac. Tac. Un nain creuse dans le mu: Tap. Tap. Tap. A dwarf is digging through the wall of his own living room.
textes.Tac. Tu écoutes, cette fois ? Tu m'avais: Tac. Listening this time? You told me you never paid attention. I haven't forgotten.
textes.Tacquet est mon plus vieil ami et mon pl: Tacquet is my oldest friend and my most faithful executioner. Forty years he's been beating me. Not at chess: on the clock. He plays fast. He's right to play fast.
textes.Tacquet tient le score dans un petit car: Tacquet has kept the score in a little black notebook for forty years. I've never dared look at the total. One evening, he left it open on table 2. I closed my eyes and shut it. There are numbers a man doesn't need to know.
textes.Tacquet vient déjeuner à midi pile, mont: Tacquet comes to lunch at noon sharp, watch in hand, to check that my machine whistles on time. It does. With him, it has no choice.
textes.Tad-kozh ! La lanterne est allumée, bien: Tad-kozh! The lantern's lit, nice and straight!
textes.Taeron ! Ta passerelle du nord est solid: Taeron! Is your north footbridge sturdy, at least?
textes.Taeron ! Ta planche du milieu soupire, c: Taeron! Your middle plank is sighing tonight.
textes.Taeron construit les passerelles et répa: Taeron builds the footbridges and mends everything, even my door. But he swears the plank didn't crack on the day of the forty loaves. It cracked. I was there. So was he.
textes.Taeron entend ses planches comme j'enten: Taeron hears his planks the way I hear my flames. Up there, we each watch over our own things. He made me hooks for my lanterns. He doesn't make them for anyone else.
textes.Taeron pose les planches, je tisse les v: Taeron lays the planks, I weave the sails. He says his planks hold up the footbridge. I say my threads hold up his planks. We're both right, except him.
textes.Tailler la pierre parfaite. Sans un défa: To cut the perfect stone. Not a flaw, not a bubble. Just one, in my whole life. And show it to nobody. Except you, maybe. For a small fee.
textes.Taillées par Coralin dans du corail et d: Carved by Coralin from coral and shark teeth, ribbed with mother-of-pearl. As long as they're in your bag, you swim one and a half times faster.
textes.Tam tam ! Dis-moi, {surnom}, tu sais dan: Tum tum! Tell me, {surnom}, can you dance?
textes.Tant mieux pour toi. Ça rend méfiant. On: Good for you. It makes you wary. You start watching the night more than the day. Keep your eyes at peace.
textes.Tant mieux. Ici, on aime les gens qui s': All the better. Around here, we like people who get along.
textes.Tant mieux. J'ai une corbeille de pétale: Good. I've got a basket of petals, just in case.
textes.Tant mieux. J'ai une pleine corbeille de: Good. I've got a whole basket of petals, just in case.
textes.Tant mieux. Le rebord de ma fenêtre auss: Good. So is my windowsill, sweetie.
textes.Tant pis pour eux ! Tam, tam, tam !: Too bad for them! Tum, tum, tum!
textes.Tant pis pour toi ! Enfin… tant mieux po: Too bad for you! Well… lucky for you, maybe. Hehe. The offer still stands!
textes.Tant pis. Gardez-moi celui de la semaine: Never mind. Save me next week's.
textes.Tant pis. Mais tu rates quelque chose !: Too bad. But you're missing out! Well… the neighbors say not, but you are.
Oh well. It can be glued back together… maybe.
textes.Tant que l'Usine Grise de Lisse & Fils f: As long as the Lisse & Sons Grey Factory keeps building robots, the raids will go on. Mamie Barricade knows that the plans for the Lisse-Center are kept at the very bottom of the factory, underground, guarded by Mr Lisse's favourite machine: the Great Digger. You need to go down the five floors, defeat the machine and bring back the plans.
textes.Tata ! Je t'ai vue courir cette nuit !: Auntie! I saw you running last night!
textes.Tata m'apprend à courir. Elle dit qu'il: Auntie's teaching me to run. She says you have to “wait for the bend”: start gently, wait, wait, and at the bend, hop, give it everything. I said: “Like Grandpa with the float?” She gave me a funny look, for a long time, and said: “… Yes.” I think I said something clever.
textes.Tatouer une baleine entière sur le dos d: Tattoo a whole whale on the Mute's back. From the nape of his neck to the small of his back, with the waves and the seagulls. He'd agree. He always agrees. He's a wonderful customer.
textes.Tazira est le port du sud. Derrière les: Tazira is the port of the south. Behind the ramparts lies the desert: the dunes, the caravans, the oases. In front, the sea, the richest in fish on the island. We are between the two, and we live off both.
textes.Tazira me rappelle chez moi. Les barques: Tazira reminds me of home. The boats, the nets, the smell of sardines. Only hotter.
textes.Tazira, le pont de la Murène Noire: Tazira, the deck of the Murène Noire
textes.Tazira, le port des sables — la criée, l: Tazira, the port of sands — the fish auction, the souk, and the Murène Noire at the quay
textes.Tchoum ! Tu m'as dit bonjour en premier: Tchoum! You said hello first! I'm writing that down!
textes.Tchoum avait un coup de soleil sur le cr: Tchoum had sunburn on his scalp, bright red. He didn't complain, he never complains. I had a green beanie knitted in Port-Azur and put it on his head. He said: “Yeah.” He's worn it every day since. Even when it's hot. Especially when it's hot.
textes.Tchoum connaît toutes les enceintes par: Tchoum knows all the speakers by their first names, and he knows they have feelings. He pretends not to believe it. Germaine told me everything, though.
textes.Tchoum et moi, on hoche la tête côte à c: Tchoum and I have been nodding our heads side by side for five years. We hardly talk. We don't need to. He's my calmest friend, and my most loyal.
textes.Tchoum ne parle presque pas, mais il con: Tchoum hardly talks, but he knows every speaker by its first name. He does, really.
textes.Tchoum ne parle presque pas, mais quand: Tchoum hardly talks, but when he does, everyone goes quiet to listen. He knows every speaker by its name. Except one, which he refuses to tell me.
textes.Tchoum, Germaine ronronne fort, aujourd': Tchoum, Germaine is purring loudly today.
textes.Tchoum, c'est la moitié de ce mur. Il di: Tchoum is half of this wall. He says three words a day and all three are right. Without him, the party would be noise with sand in it.
Tchoum is a mystery with a beard. He can hear a crab in a speaker before the crab knows it's there. Well… almost. That one time, I was the one who heard it.
textes.Tchoum, il ne grésille pas, c'est la mer: Tchoum, it's not crackling, that's the sea.
textes.Te perdre ?! Mais… Bon. C'est vrai que l: Get lost?! But… Well. It's true the finest discoveries often come from people who are lost. Don't tell anyone. It would ruin my profession.
Stitch you up? There's nothing to stitch. Come back after your next brawl. It shouldn't be long.
You're back! Come closer, I don't bite. I just burn a little, that's all.
You're back! The mist let you through. It likes you.
textes.Te revoilà ! Le village parle de toi, tu: You're back! The village talks about you, you know.
textes.Te revoilà ! Où en étais-je ? Ah oui. La: You're back! Where was I? Ah yes. The night the Léviathan struck land…
You're back! The whole city is talking about you.
textes.Te revoilà ! Tu as aimé notre cuisine, h: You're back! You liked our cooking, huh? Come back whenever you like!
Back in the fairy kingdom again.
textes.Te revoilà parmi nous. Yggdrasil murmure: You are among us again. Yggdrasil whispers your name, you know.
textes.Te revoilà, mon petit ! Montre-moi tes m: You're back, little one! Show me your hands… More scratches. Young ones, always running everywhere.
textes.Te revoilà, {surnom} ! J'ai du nectar to: You're back, {surnom}! I have fresh nectar, picked at dawn. Well, fairy dawn: when the waterfall lights up.
textes.Te revoilà, {surnom} ! Le vent est bon,: You're back, {surnom}! The wind is good, the sea is like glass. We cast off whenever you like.
textes.Te revoilà, {surnom} ! Le vent m'avait p: You're back, {surnom}! The wind warned me. It's a chatterbox, the wind.
textes.Te revoilà, {surnom}. La brume m'avait d: You're back, {surnom}. The mist told me you would return.
textes.Te revoilà, {surnom}. Le dôme frissonne: You're back, {surnom}. The dome shivers when you pass through the Tide Gate. It likes you.
textes.Te revoilà, {surnom}. Les feuilles t'ont: Here you are again, {surnom}. The leaves announced you before your footsteps did.
textes.Te revoilà, {surnom}. Tu as la tête de q: You again, {surnom}. You've got the look of someone looking for work. Or trouble. Often it's the same thing.
textes.Te revoilà, {surnom}. Un rhum ? Ou tu pr: Back again, {surnom}. A rum? Or would you rather live?
textes.Te revoilà. Tu ne grandis pas, au moins: You're back. You're not getting any taller, at least?
textes.Te voilà revenu dans le cercle. Où en ét: So you're back in the circle. Where were we? Ah. The sultan, the sardine and the djinn…
textes.Te voilà, l'ami des poissons ! {nb_poiss: There you are, friend of the fishes! {nb_poissons} catches, according to Gaston. He counts everything, that bird.
textes.Te voilà, {surnom} ! Assieds-toi, j'ai u: There you are, {surnom}! Sit down, I've got a crêpe on the griddle.
textes.Te voilà, {surnom} ! Django va bientôt j: There you are, {surnom}! Django's about to play.
textes.Te voilà. Montre-moi ces égratignures… H: There you are. Show me those scratches… Hmm. You'll live.
textes.Te voilà. Tu vois, Ramure t'attendait. M: There you are. You see, Ramure was waiting for you. So was I, a little.
textes.Temple-Passoire\nEntrez, la porte est ou:
Colander Temple
Come in, the door is open (everything is open: it's a colander).
Quiet, please, we're draining.
textes.Tenez, Gédéon. Ces baguettes vous attend: Here, Gédéon. These sticks were waiting for you.
textes.Tes amis… Ah. C'est le feu le plus solid: Your friends… Ah. That's the sturdiest fire there is: it doesn't go out when you walk away from it. Keep them close, and let them keep you.
textes.Tes bottes ! Ah, une âme soignée ! Une b: Your boots! Ah, a well-groomed soul! A shiny boot is a horn that walks. I'll lend you my oil. It works wonders on leather.
textes.Tes bâtons ont fait de belles flèches. T: Your sticks made fine arrows. You have an eye for wood. For a human.
textes.Tes champignons de braise ont fait le ra: Your ember mushrooms made the stew of the century.
textes.Tes champignons ont soigné la toux de to: Your mushrooms cured the whole village's cough.
textes.Tes coups le traversent ! Il faudrait un: Your blows go right through it! You'd need a light to reveal what's hiding… (the Moonglow)
textes.Tes coups rebondissent sur le bronze ! S: Your blows bounce off the bronze! If only its gears would jam…
Your magma hearts light up my tunnel. It doesn't get lost anymore.
textes.Tes genoux, Nono, ils ont battu la mesur: Your knees, Nono, kept the beat the whole track.
You make up your stories, admit it.
Your pearls shine on my party dress. Everyone asks me where they come from.
textes.Tes perroquets, ils disent que des gros: Your parrots only say rude words.
textes.Tes pieds deviennent légers, légers… Ici: Your feet grow light, so light… Here, gravity is taking a nap. Jump!
textes.Tes rayons de miel ont fait le meilleur: Your honeycombs made the best bread of the year.
textes.Tes roses sont sur le chemin de mes abei: Your roses are in my bees' way, Miriel.
textes.Tes rêves aussi font boum-boum. On les e: Your dreams go boom-boom too. We can hear them from up above.
textes.Tes sabres, ils se cassent au premier co: Your sabres break on the first blow, don't they?
textes.Tes sels de bain. Tu les as encore mélan: Your bath salts. You've mixed them up again.
textes.Thalassa ! Les laminaires sont arrivées,: Thalassa! The kelp's in, long as the canal!
textes.Thalassa m'a tissé un tablier pour l'éta: Thalassa wove me an apron for the stall, with my name embroidered on it. I wanted to pay her, she refused, twice. So I slip a cracker into her basket every morning. I don't think she eats them. Ondine makes boats out of them for the canal. Apparently they float very well. I don't know if I should be proud.
textes.Thalassa me prend toutes les longues lam: Thalassa takes all my long kelp for her weaving. She pays on the nail, never haggles. It's almost insulting.
textes.Thalassa. Des laminaires, à côté du méti: Thalassa. Some kelp, beside the loom.
textes.Thalassa. Elle tisse ce que je fais pous: Thalassa. She weaves what I grow. We understand each other without talking. Especially me.
textes.Thalion ! Aujourd'hui, tu m'apprends l'a: Thalion! Are you teaching me archery today?
textes.Thalion ! Tu as mangé ton pain ?: Thalion! Did you eat your bread?
textes.Thalion ! Tu es encore monté sans dire b: Thalion! You went up again without saying hello.
textes.Thalion ? Il garde une porte fermée depu: Thalion? He's been guarding a closed door for three centuries, and he thinks it's my harp that makes noise. A little music wouldn't hurt him. And he sings out of tune, which doesn't help.
textes.Thalion a peur des grenouilles. C'est vr: Thalion is scared of frogs. It's true! I saw it!
textes.Thalion dit que ma harpe l'empêche de mo: Thalion says my harp stops him keeping watch. He only says that because he sings out of tune.
textes.Thalion grimpe chez les abeilles d'en ha: Thalion climbs up to the top bees like a bear, without saying hello, and comes back down with their honey. He calls it training. My bees call it something else.
textes.Thalion m'a surprise une fois à viser un: Once Thalion caught me aiming at an apple with a stick and a bit of string. I thought he was going to tell me off. He looked at me for ages, then he said: “Your elbow's too high.” And he left. I didn't get it at first. It was a lesson! A real one!
textes.Thalion m'a tout appris. Deux siècles pl: Thalion taught me everything. Two centuries later, he still checks my arrows one by one. I respect him more than anyone. He exasperates me more than anyone, too.
textes.Thalion me demande où je vais dix fois p: Thalion asks me where I'm going ten times a day. I'm a messenger: I go everywhere. He knows that. He asks anyway. One day I'll tell him the truth, just to see his face.
textes.Thalion surveille la place d'en bas, moi: Thalion watches the square from below, I watch it from above. He thinks he's the only one who sees everything. He doesn't see half of what I see. And he never misses an apple, alas.
textes.Thalion surveille tout le monde et oubli: Thalion keeps an eye on everyone and forgets to eat. So I keep an eye on him. Every morning, a honey loaf at the foot of his tower. He pretends not to know where it comes from.
textes.Thalion t'a encore demandé où tu allais: Did Thalion ask you where you were going again?
textes.Thalion t'a à l'œil. Ne lui en veux pas: Thalion has his eye on you. Don't hold it against him: he has his eye on everyone.
textes.Thalion va me chercher le miel sauvage t: Thalion fetches me the wild honey from the very top of the Mother Tree, where the bees are the most golden. For him it's an exercise, like archery. He comes down covered in stings, jaw clenched, and hands me the comb without a word. I give him the first loaf. He eats it with his back to me.
textes.Thalion, c'est le meilleur archer du mon: Thalion's the best archer in the world! But he won't teach me. He says “later”, “never” or “ask Sylwen's door”. And he's scared of frogs. He is, he is!
textes.Thorgal chante faux, danse mal et perd s: Thorgal sings off-key, dances badly and loses his crown while it's on his head. He's the best king we've ever had. And he can't tell I water down his fizz. Well… I think.
textes.Thorgal est un bon roi, mais il croit qu: Thorgal is a good king, but he thinks my crows exist to bring him cheese at midnight. My crows aren't kitchen boys. Neither am I.
textes.Thorgal porte la plus belle couronne du: Thorgal wears the most beautiful crown in the world. I should know: I made it. He still owes me half of it. Ninety years of half a debt weighs heavy on a crown.
textes.Thorgal vient me demander l'avenir comme: Thorgal comes to ask me about the future the way you'd ask the time. He doesn't want to know: he wants to be reassured. I do my best not to lie to him.
textes.Thot, le dieu à tête d'ibis, a inventé l: Thoth, the ibis-headed god, invented writing. He is the one who records the weighing of the heart on judgement day. A scribe is a little Thoth with ink-stained hands.
textes.Théo cherche son cerf-volant. Il l'a vu: Théo's looking for his kite. He saw it fly off towards the hills, to the west. I haven't got the legs to climb up there.
textes.Théo est mon meilleur critique. Il regar: Théo is my best critic. He watches, he asks questions, and he says “you don't paint fast”. He's right.
textes.Théo est né il y a six ans, un mardi, pe: Théo was born six years ago, on a Tuesday, during a storm. Gérard took forty photos of the window and none of the baby. Since then, I've been watching over two children: Théo, who wants to touch everything, and Gérard, who wants to photograph everything. The first is growing up very fast. The second, I'm not so sure.
textes.Théo, c'est mon fils, six ans, construct: Théo is my son, six years old, builder of sandcastles. The best subject in the world. He never stops moving, so all my photos of him are blurry.
textes.Théo, c'est mon petit architecte. Six an: Théo is my little architect. Six years old, and already building castles with four towers and a moat. One day, he'll build a town. And I'll run the beach hut in it.
textes.Théo, c'est un bébé. Il a six ans et il: Théo is a baby. He's six and he cried for days and days over his kite. But he makes really, really good sandcastles. I have to say that.
textes.Théo, le garçon de l'hôtel, il a perdu s: Théo, the boy at the hotel, lost his kite. He cries all the time. He's a baby.
textes.Théo, mon fils. Six ans, une imagination: Théo, my son. Six years old, the imagination of a sixty-year-old, and a kite that flew away and broke his heart. He builds castles bigger than himself. I can't wait to see what he'll build later on.
textes.Théophraste ! J'ai rapporté un livre !: Théophraste! I've brought a book back!
textes.Théophraste Filandre m'apprend la téléki: Théophraste Filandre is teaching me telekinesis. Four of his books flew away during the great storm and are stuck where no one can climb: I have to bring them back down.
textes.Théophraste aime les livres plus que les: Théophraste loves books more than people. So do I, a little. We understand each other without talking. His library is the best place on the island. And that's thanks to him.
textes.Théophraste dit qu'un de ses livres s'es: Théophraste says one of his books flew all the way up onto the library roof. Théophraste's books have imagination.
textes.Théophraste est un trésor caché sous une: Théophraste is a treasure hidden under a moustache. He scolds me for being late, rightly so. I always bring his books back. Always! A little later than planned, that's all.
Théophraste times me when I read. He thinks I don't notice. I pretend to read more slowly, to please him.
textes.Théophraste me réclame son livre depuis: Théophraste has been asking for his book back for six years. He's grumpy, fussy, he looks at me like an ink stain. And he's loyal: once a month, without fail. You don't have that many loyal friends.
textes.Théophraste réclame son traité des mélan: Théophraste wants his treatise on explosive mixtures back. I'm reading it, I'm reading it! It's a book you have to read slowly. To avoid accidents.
textes.Tibo m'a appris à jurer comme un pirate,: Tibo taught me to swear like a pirate, but without rude words, 'cause mum's listening. “Blistering barnacles!” “Thundering typhoons!” I taught him knucklebones. He loses all the time. He says “blistering barnacles” every time. That's a lot of barnacles.
textes.Tibo m'a payé ses babouches jaunes en de: Tibo paid for his yellow slippers in two goes. The first with his cabin-boy savings. The second with a gold coin gone all green, found at the bottom of the hold. A coin from a kingdom nobody knows. I kept it. I look at it when I'm bored and I imagine the king: he surely had big feet.
textes.Tibo, c'est mon meilleur copain, et c'es: Tibo's my best pal, and he's a real pirate! He scrubs the deck and peels potatoes, but he's still a pirate. He's got a bandana. A red one.
textes.Tibo, le mousse de la Murène. Il est ven: Tibo, the Murène's cabin boy. He came to ask me how to fish. A pirate! He talks all the time and scares off the sardines, but he learns fast.
textes.Tibo, le mousse de la Murène. Premier ra: Tibo, the Murène's cabin boy. Front row, every evening, eyes like lanterns. I've named him keeper of the djinn. One day, he'll tell stories. I can feel it.
textes.Tibo, le mousse des pirates, m'a acheté: Tibo, the pirates' cabin boy, bought babouches from me in secret. He doesn't want the captain to know. Pirates aren't allowed warm feet.
textes.Tibo, mon client le plus secret. Un pira: Tibo, my most secret customer. A pirate with cosy feet! He's scared his captain will find out. With me, his secret is safe. I've only told you. And Rachid. And…
textes.Tibo, mon commis ! Le meilleur éplucheur: Tibo, my kitchen boy! The best potato peeler on the seven seas. He says my cooking is inedible, and he always clears his plate. That's real criticism.
textes.Tibo, mon mousse. Il récure mal, il éplu: Tibo, my cabin boy. He scrubs badly, peels badly, talks too much, and spends his evenings at the storyteller's. He reminds me of someone. Me. Only worse. Well, only better. Don't tell him.
textes.Tiburce ! Jeudi ! Ta vapeur est prête !: Tiburce! Thursday! Your steam is ready!
textes.Tiburce passe dix fois par jour devant m: Tiburce walks past my workshop ten times a day to show me his collar, the same one for three centuries. One morning, I stopped and said: “Oh, that one's new.” He beamed all day. It was the same one, ironed on the bias. I'd seen that perfectly well. I just wanted him to have a nice day. Don't tell him.
textes.Tiburce polit des cornes à côté de mon a: Tiburce polishes horns next door to my workshop. He's worn the same collar for three centuries and he dares to criticise my capes. We won a prize together. I've never forgiven him for being right about the horns.
textes.Tiburce vend une huile à cornes qui « gu: Tiburce sells a horn oil that “cures everything”. I analysed it. It cures nothing. It smells nice, that's all. He sells perfume while claiming to sell remedies. I can't stand him. Well, almost can't.
textes.Tiburce vend une « huile à cornes » qui: Tiburce sells a “horn oil” that supposedly cures everything. I analysed it: nine tenths perfume, one tenth vanity. It cures nothing, but it smells very nice. That's something.
textes.Tiburce vient chaque jeudi faire « respi: Tiburce comes every Thursday to let his horns “breathe” in my steam. Horns don't breathe. He says his do. He pays well, he smells nice, and he tells me the gossip from the Upper Town.
textes.Tiburce vient m'écouter tous les soirs,: Tiburce comes to listen to me every evening, in the front row, eyes closed. He sighs off the beat. His horns shine brighter than his conversation. I tease him a lot. Maybe a little too much.
Tiburce comes to listen to me every evening. He sits in the front row, closes his eyes and sighs. Loudly. Off the beat. I think he's in love. With my music, I hope. Well… we'll see.
textes.Tiburce vient « faire respirer ses corne: Tiburce comes to “let his horns breathe” in my steam, every Thursday. I told him horns don't breathe. He said his do. I don't argue with a paying customer.
textes.Tiburce, tu as encore soupiré à contrete: Tiburce, you sighed off the beat again.
textes.Tiburce, tu soupires encore à contretemp: Tiburce, you're sighing off the beat again.
textes.Tiburce. Ton huile guérit toujours tout: Tiburce. Does your oil still cure everything?
textes.Tic est le meilleur horloger de l'île et: Tic is the best clockmaker on the island and the most patient fiancé in the world. Thirty-one years engaged. Apparently it's a record. I'm in no hurry.
textes.Tic me laisse tirer du haut de sa tour a: Tic lets me fire from the top of his tower at New Year. He pulls a face, but he lets me. He's the sweetest of the punctual grumps.
textes.Tic-tac… Hm. Les horlogers sont patients: Tick-tock… Hm. Clockmakers are patient. I'm not. But you're right: at least a machine that goes tick-tock doesn't go boom.
textes.Tic. Tac. Tic. Tac. Des horloges partout: Tick. Tock. Tick. Tock. Clocks everywhere… and not one shows the same time.
textes.Tic… tac… Bonjour ! Tacquet. Horloger. C: Tick… tock… Hello! Tacquet. Clockmaker. That great clock up there, I wind it every morning. It has never been a second late. A second early, once. I gave it a telling-off.
textes.Tic… tac… Je suis né à midi pile, {surno: Tick… tock… I was born at noon sharp, {surnom}. My mother checked it herself, on the great clock, through the window, between two screams. So they called me Tic. With a surname like Tacquet, the rest followed on its own. I never got to choose my trade. But I've never had a second of regret.
textes.Tic… tac… Une question sérieuse : vous ê: Tick… tock… A serious question: are you more often early, or late?
textes.Tiens : une pour maintenant, une pour la: Here: one for now, one for the road. And remember: herbal tea is meant to be sipped slowly, while looking at something beautiful.
textes.Tiens bon, on tangue un peu !: Hold on tight, we're rocking a bit!
textes.Tiens, Barbe-de-Fer. Toujours à refondre: Well, well, Barbe-de-Fer. Still melting down other people's work?
textes.Tiens, Lestrange. Ta jambe tient le coup: Well, Lestrange. Is your leg holding up?
textes.Tiens, Pépin ! Quatre heures ! Quel hasa: Well, Pépin! Four o'clock! What a coincidence!
textes.Tiens, des pièces, et deux jarres de la: Here, some coins, and two jars of Mérit's date juice. And if one day you want to fish, my boat is yours.
textes.Tiens, des pièces, et du copal pour le t: Here, some coins, and copal for the temple: they say the gods love the smell of flowers and copal together.
textes.Tiens, des pièces. Des vraies, des ronde: Here, some coins. Real ones, round ones. And a patch, just in case. You never know when you'll get a flat. A tyre, I mean.
Here, some tamales. For your patience.
Here, keep this one as a souvenir.
textes.Tiens, goûte. … Alors ? Je le savais. Le: Here, taste. … Well? I knew it. The saffron comes from Aïcha's, the preserved lemon from my mother's, and the sea bream… from yours. Take one for the road, and these few coins. And come back on Friday.
textes.Tiens, le fuyard ! Tu cours toujours aus: Well, if it isn't the runaway! Still running as fast?
textes.Tiens, le passager ! Toujours en bateau: Well, the passenger! Still going by boat? Do me a favour: the steps of the quay, at a run. Hop!
textes.Tiens, le supporter de Raymond. Tu viens: Well, if it isn't Raymond's supporter. Come to see a real champion, or did you get the wrong pitch again?
textes.Tiens, mon amateur de vanille ! Ta boule: Well, my vanilla fan! Your scoop is waiting for you. In my mind, still. But for real too, if you drop by.
textes.Tiens, mon chou : deux potions de mana,: Here, dearie: two mana potions, for your trouble. They're surely magic. These ones, I'm almost sure.
textes.Tiens, mon retardataire. À l'heure, aujo: Well, if it isn't my latecomer. On time, today? No? I only said it to encourage you.
textes.Tiens, quelques pièces, et deux bols de: Here, a few coins, and two bowls of soup to take away. They're in jars, with a lid. Copeau made the lids. Out of pallets, of course.
textes.Tiens, revoilà la jeunesse. Tu viens m'a: Well, look who's back, young blood. Come to help me untangle, or just to listen to my stories?
textes.Tiens, te revoilà, {surnom} ! Ça fait {a: Well, look who's back, {surnom}! It's been {absence}. Gaston thought the crabs had eaten you.
Here, hold the pot. … (You hold the pot. He gets paint everywhere. Mostly on you.) … Perfect! Here, for the helping hand.
textes.Tiens, tiens… Toi qui réfléchis : tu pré: Well, well… You're a thinker: would you rather know the answer, or keep the mystery?
textes.Tiens, tiens… Un humain. Je suis Cardamo: Well, well… A human. I'm Cardamome. I love riddles, secrets and people who think. Do you think?
textes.Tiens, tiens… Venez donc m'expliquer, vo: Well, well… Come and explain yourself, you.
textes.Tiens, tiens… Viens donc m'expliquer, to: Well, well… Come and explain yourself, you.
textes.Tiens, toi. L'eau est bonne, aujourd'hui: Oh, it's you. The water's lovely today. Coming in?
textes.Tiens, un gâteau de miel de Bobor, que j: Here, a Bobor honey cake that I was saving for myself. I'm giving it to you: you did the hardest part, I only did the planting.
textes.Tiens, un nouveau visage ! Rosa. On m'ap: Well, a new face! Rosa. They call me the Red, for my hair, not for blood. Well, not only. I look after the Moray's cannons. Sixteen cannons, all my babies.
textes.Tiens, un nouveau. Scarlett. On m'appell: Well, a new one. Scarlett. They call me la Rouquine — the Redhead — guess why. I throw knives. Not at people. Well… not at polite people.
textes.Tiens, une bulle. Avec du rien dedans. E: Here, a bubble. With nothing inside. And no wood.
Here, a corn cake from Ix Chab.
textes.Tiens, une petite carte de ton portrait,: Here, a little card of your portrait, as a souvenir!
textes.Tiens, une petite fusée de remerciement…: Here, a little thank-you rocket… no, some coins, rather. Rockets are for the party.
textes.Tiens, une petite inconnue à capuche…: Well, well, a little stranger in a hood…
textes.Tiens, {dernier_cadeau}. Hmm. Merci, je: Well, {dernier_cadeau}. Hmm. Thanks, I suppose. I'm sure I'll find a use for it.
textes.Tiens, {surnom} ! Monte, j'ai du neuf. E: Well, {surnom}! Come on up, I've got new stock. Well, the same stock.
textes.Tiens, {surnom}. Je t'ai vu venir depuis: Well, {surnom}. I saw you coming from the jetty.
Here. Hang it above your bed. And if you ever have a nightmare, come tell me: I'll strengthen the net.
textes.Tiens. Des pièces, et trois flacons de m: Here. Some coins, and three flasks of my tonic: honey, fever grass, syrup and a secret. One sip, and you get back up from any brawl. Well, almost any.
textes.Tiens… on se connaît ?: Well now… do we know each other?
textes.Tilleul ! Et alors, cette louve, elle l': Tilleul! So, that she-wolf, did she fish the moon out?
textes.Tilleul ! Tu as reçu mon histoire ?: Tilleul! Did you get my story?
textes.Tilleul ? Le premier qui m'ait raconté u: Tilleul? The first one who told me a story in Ramure, and the only one who's never told me the end of one. My oldest friend. His paws creak as much as mine.
textes.Tilleul, le conteur de Ramure. Un ours q: Tilleul, the storyteller of Ramure. A bear who tells stories the way you take a nap: slowly, and you wake up happy. He taught me that a story can happen twice.
textes.Tilleul, le conteur de Ramure. Un ours,: Tilleul, the storyteller of Ramure. A bear, a real one, with ears. He tells stories better than me, but he falls asleep before the end. In Carène, nobody believes me when I talk about him.
textes.Tisane de brume pour dormir, de lune pou: Mist tea for sleeping, moon tea for dreaming. Every evening I take Mother Moon hers, and I sew the fox ears she gives to travellers who help her. Roux comes home with leaves in his tail and swears he was picking herbs. And Trèfle's tarts, I can smell them a hundred paces off: I walk past just as they come out of the oven. How? The nose, of course.
textes.Tisser en secret le tapis de ma propre n: To secretly weave the carpet for my own wedding, at night, while Rachid sleeps, and unroll it in front of him on the wedding day. For once in his life, he'd be speechless.
textes.Tisser un huipil avec toutes les couleur: To weave a huipil with all the colours of the island: the blue of the Cenote, the green of the jungle, the yellow of the sun, the red of the macaws, and Tiyi's white. You'd see it from Aztlán!
textes.Tisser un lin si fin qu'il flotterait da: To weave a linen so fine it would float in the air like smoke. We'd let it go from the top of the temple, and it would take an hour to fall.
textes.Tisser à Ondine une robe couleur de sole: To weave Ondine a sun-coloured dress, for the day she goes up there. I'd need yellow thread. Under the sea, there's only the gold of the crown, and the queen is rather attached to it. Will you bring me some?
textes.Titou ! Ta pirouette, elle compte pas do: Titou! Your pirouette doesn't count double.
textes.Titou a inventé le crabe amoureux, je le: Titou invented the lovestruck crab, I admit it. But he danced it badly: too many arms, not enough hips. I fixed it, called it the “sentimental crab” and I teach it. He's demanding his name on my poster. I offered him a teeny little line at the bottom. He said: “Thank you, Miss.” I couldn't tell if that was mean.
textes.Titou compte les versions de mes histoir: Titou counts the versions of my stories and imitates my dancing on the square, in front of all the kids. “The elegant seal.” Cheeky. And he forgets the shoulder move, on top of it.
textes.Titou dit qu'il en est à dix-sept versio: Titou says he's up to seventeen versions of my party in the mine. He writes them down in a journal. One evening he read me version seven, the one with the dragon. I didn't remember telling it. It was very good. I served it up again to Gaspard the next day, polished a little.
textes.Titou dit qu'une pirouette compte double: Titou says a pirouette counts double. That's not in the rules! There aren't any rules, but it's not in the rules. Apart from that, he's my jumping brother.
textes.Titou est adorable, drôle, généreux… et: Titou is adorable, funny, generous… and I haven't got a single sharp photo of him in three years. Not one. And on top of that, he's the one who lost my last glow sticks.
textes.Titou fait le dauphin dans son spectacle: Titou plays the dolphin in his show on the square, to make fun of me. He jumps, he goes “kik-kik”, he ends up in a bucket of water. The kids scream with laughter. I went to watch, ready to grumble. I laughed so hard I gave every kid a necklace. His dolphin cost me fifteen necklaces.
textes.Titou me pique mes élèves, mes idées et: Titou steals my pupils, my ideas and my side of the fountain. He's funny, that's the worst part. His lovestruck crab, I kept it in my class, under a better name.
textes.Titou, l'épaule. On roule l'épaule, comm: Titou, the shoulder. You roll the shoulder, like this.
textes.Titou, ton pas de danse, là, c'est quoi: Titou, that dance step of yours, what is it?
textes.Titou, tu es encore de mon côté de la fo: Titou, you're on my side of the fountain again.
textes.Titou. Une photo. Tu ne bouges pas. D'ac: Titou. One photo. You don't move. OK?
textes.Titre de demain : « Achille Plumevent to: Tomorrow's headline: “Achille Plumevent still in flight”. Like yesterday. Like the day before.
textes.Titre de la Gazette, un mardi : « Le Zép: Gazette headline, one Tuesday: “The Zéphyr Is Three Minutes Late”. On the front page! Three minutes! There was a headwind over Carène. I wrote a right of reply. She printed it. With a typo: “The commander disputes the elay”. The whole city laughed. So did I. A little. The next day.
textes.Tiyi ! Le quatrième, c'est qui ? Juste l: Tiyi! Who's the fourth one? Just the first sign!
textes.Tiyi ! Tu as porté ma ceinture ?: Tiyi! Have you worn my belt?
textes.Tiyi ! Une perche, pour Nebet. Rien que: Tiyi! A perch, for Nebet. Just for Nebet.
textes.Tiyi tisse le lin le plus fin du monde,: Tiyi weaves the finest linen in the world, white as dawn. She speaks softly and laughs on the inside. She says she only likes white. I don't entirely believe her.
textes.Tiyi tisse mes robes et le lin des autel: Tiyi weaves my robes and the altar linen. She speaks little, laughs softly, and her white is the purest on the river. I'd trust her with my secrets. I already trust her with my wardrobe.
textes.Tiyi tisse mon lin. Elle choisit chaque: Tiyi weaves my flax. She picks each bunch the way you pick a friend: slowly, in silence. She's fair, she pays well, and she never laughs at my crocodiles. That's rare.
textes.Tiyi tisse un lin si fin qu'on voit le s: Tiyi weaves linen so fine you can see the sun through it. Me, when I see her, I can't see anything at all. Because of the sun, I mean. Obviously.
textes.Tiyi, c'est ma meilleure amie depuis l'e: Tiyi has been my best friend since childhood. She weaves the most beautiful linen on the river and she turned down three suitors this year. She says four. I don't know the fourth one. I'll find out.
textes.Tiyi, la tisserande, a refusé trois prét: Tiyi the weaver turned down three suitors this year. Three! She says she prefers her loom. I understand her: at least the loom doesn't snore.
Tiyi, your robe still shines at dawn.
Tiyi. The flax is fine this year.
textes.Tlaco a juste soif ! Tlaloc est d'accord: Tlaco's just thirsty! Tlaloc doesn't mind!
textes.Tlaco aboie après Mixtli depuis le premi: Tlaco has been barking at Mixtli since the first day. Because of the jaguar skin. I explained to Tlaco that he's a man. He doesn't agree. Mixtli says Tlaco is right to be wary of jaguars, even jaguars with a man inside. So now Tlaco barks, and Mixtli says thank you.
textes.Tlaco aboie après les serpents de pierre: Tlaco barks at the stone serpents at the bottom of the stairs. Every day. I tell him they're gods, he barks louder. One day, Cuauhtli walked by, looked at Tlaco, looked at the serpents… and I think he smiled. Just a tiny bit. Nobody believes me.
Tlaloc forgives him. So do I.
textes.Tlaloc va t'adorer ! La pluie, c'est le: Tlaloc is going to love you! Rain means maize, flowers, the lake. It's life. And a few colds, all right. But mostly life.
Tobias! My roof's leaking, on the north side.
textes.Tobias ! Ta galette, dans ta poche, comm: Tobias! Your crêpe, in your pocket, as usual.
textes.Tobias a cloué une casserole au plafond: Tobias nailed a saucepan to the ceiling of his workshop, right under my anvil. Every time I strike, it rings. He says it's so I hear what he hears. So I hung a saucepan under my anvil too, which rings at the same time. Now it makes music. He doesn't find it funny.
textes.Tobias bouche les trous du bateau depuis: Tobias has been plugging the holes in the ship for thirty years and never has time to eat. So every morning, I put a crêpe in his pocket. He says thank you the way other people say sorry.
textes.Tobias dit que je suis ses yeux sous la: Tobias says I'm his eyes under the hull. I tell him where it's seeping, where the wood's soft. He listens without sighing, which is rare for him. And his daughter is my friend.
textes.Tobias dit que la coque tiendra encore c: Tobias says the hull will hold for another hundred years. Tobias has been saying that for thirty years.
textes.Tobias me dit que la coque tiendra encor: Tobias tells me the hull will hold another hundred years. He's been telling me that for thirty years. I know what it means: he'll spend his life on it. No one is more faithful to this ship.
textes.Tobias recalfate ma barque-maison chaque: Tobias re-caulks my boat-house every autumn and won't let me pay him. He takes a mackerel, he sighs, he leaves. Gloomy as a windless day, but a good lad.
textes.Tobias se plaint de tout, et surtout de: Tobias complains about everything, and especially about me. He says one day I'll go straight through the deck. He's the grumpiest man in Carène, and I owe him more than he'll ever say.
textes.Tobias se plaint du bruit. Tobias se pla: Tobias complains about the noise. Tobias complains about everything.
textes.Tobias soupire chaque fois que je parle: Tobias sighs every time I talk about putting the Léviathan back in the water. He sighs when I don't talk about it too. But he's the one who knows how to plug the holes, so I keep coming back.
textes.Tobias, le calfat, doit reboucher une vo: Tobias, the caulker, has to patch a leak in the hull of the Léviathan. He needs good timber.
textes.Tobias. Tribord, sous la troisième membr: Tobias. Starboard, under the third frame, it's seeping.
textes.Toc toc ! … Ah non, c'est toi qui frappe: Knock knock! … Oh no, you're the one knocking. Shall we start over?
textes.Toc toc toc ? Hé, c'est MOI qui fais les: Knock knock knock? Hey, I'M the one who tells the jokes around here!
textes.Toc toc… (Une voix ensommeillée, derrièr: Knock knock… (A sleepy voice, behind the door.) “Who's there? … Ah, it's you. We're asleep, it's night! Come back tomorrow, we'll look for the colours together.”
textes.Toc toc… La Maison du Conseil est fermée: Knock knock… The Council House is closed. A poster: “Extraordinary meeting: WHERE HAVE OUR COLOURS GONE? Everyone is asked to search everywhere.”
textes.Toc toc… Personne : de jour, tout le mon: Knock knock… Nobody: by day, everyone is out looking for the colour pots.
textes.Toc toc… Personne. Sur la porte, un peti: Knock knock… Nobody. On the door, a little note: “Gone to find the blue of the sky. Back soon! — the Brush family”
textes.Toc toc… Personne. Un mot un peu taché :: Knock knock… Nobody. A slightly smudged note: “Gone to find the red of the poppies. Please water our flowers, thanks! — the Blotter family”
textes.Toc toc… Personne. Un petit mot : « Part: Knock knock… Nobody. A little note: “Gone to find the green of the leaves. Don't erase anything while we're away! — the Rubber family”
textes.Toc, toc, toc. Une petite voix, derrière: Knock, knock, knock. A little voice, behind the door: "
textes.Toc, toc. Le seul qui répond, c'est la p: Knock, knock. The only one answering is the rain on the roof: tic, tic, tic…
textes.Toc, toc. Rien… Un écriteau peint : « En: Knock, knock. Nothing… A painted sign: “Meditating. Come back in an hour, or in a lifetime.”
textes.Toc, toc… Personne. Sur la porte, un pet: Knock, knock… Nobody. On the door, a little note: “Gone to pick poppies. Come back whenever you like, the door of the heart is always open (this one, not so much).”
textes.Toc, toc… Rien. Puis, de très loin dans: Knock, knock… Nothing. Then, from deep inside the yurt, a sleepy voice: “… It's not time for rehearsal yet…”
textes.Tochtli ! Encore un escargot magique à m: Tochtli! Another magic snail to sell me?
textes.Tochtli ! Mes plumes sont bien arrivées: Tochtli! Did my feathers get to Aztlán safely?
textes.Tochtli ! Tu as vendu ma jarre à crocs ?: Tochtli! Did you sell my fanged jar?
textes.Tochtli a voulu me vendre une plume de q: Tochtli tried to sell me a quetzal feather. It was a parrot feather painted green. I gave him his feather back. On his head.
textes.Tochtli emporte mes jarres jusqu'à Per-H: Tochtli takes my jars all the way to Per-Hâpy and comes back with stories. He sells everything, even my cracked jars. Especially my cracked jars. I never know how much he makes. That's probably for the best.
textes.Tochtli est mon cousin. Il vend de tout,: Tochtli is my cousin. He sells everything, he talks non-stop, and he sold me a parrot feather painted green. I gave it back to him. On his head. He hasn't forgiven me for the training. We're even. Almost.
textes.Tochtli m'achète mes plumes d'ara et les: Tochtli buys my macaw feathers and sells them for three times the price in Aztlán. He calls it trade. I call it feathers that gain value by travelling.
textes.Tochtli vend son copal plus cher les jou: Tochtli sells his copal for more on feast days. The gods see it. He sells them copal anyway, through me. I don't know who he's robbing. Maybe everyone, a little.
Tochtli sells his copal dearer on feast days. The gods see it. Tochtli sees the gods too, for that matter: he sells them copal.
textes.Tochtli vend tout, même ce qu'il n'a pas: Tochtli sells everything, even what he doesn't have. He sells me my own seeds dearer on feast days. He's funny, he's clever, and you never know if he's lying. Neither does he, I think.
textes.Tochtli vendrait le vent s'il pouvait. I: Tochtli would sell the wind if he could. He has tried, actually. He says I should charge for my music. Music is like air: if you sell it, it suffocates.
textes.Tochtli. Mes fleurs, à ton étal ?: Tochtli. My flowers, on your stall?
textes.Tochtli. Ton copal coûte combien, aujour: Tochtli. How much is your copal today?
textes.Tochtli. Une plume de quetzal, une vraie: Tochtli. A quetzal feather, a real one?
textes.Toi ! Ne crois pas que je ne sais pas ce: You! Don't think I don't know what you did.
textes.Toi ! T'as un sacré crochet du gauche. M: You! You've got a cracking left hook. My jaw still remembers it. Respect.
textes.Toi ! Toi trop maigre ! Pas assez de car: You! You too skinny! Not enough squares! Eat, eat. Fern flatbread, Granny Silex recipe. Nice and crunchy.
textes.Toi ! Tu as l'air affamé. Entre donc !: You! You look starving. Come on in!
textes.Toi ! Tu as une tête à aimer les histoir: You! You look like someone who loves stories.
textes.Toi ! Tu sais manier la hache ?: You! Can you handle an axe?
textes.Toi ! Tu sais quel jour on est ?: You! Do you know what day it is?
textes.Toi ! Tu tombes bien ! Dis-lui, toi :: You! Just in time! Tell him, would you:
textes.Toi ! Tu veux voir du feu ?: You! Want to see some fire?
textes.Toi ! Viens voir, j'ai presque fini les: You! Come and see, I've almost finished the boats.
textes.Toi ? Dans les Neuf Cercles ? (Le vieux: You? Into the Nine Circles? (The old guardian looks at you for a long time, then unhooks a big black key from his belt.) The Key of the Ember. The door is at the back of the nave. Listen well: a coin for Charon, honey cakes for Cerberus, good answers for Minos. And take a coat, little one. Cocytus is no joke.
textes.Toi ? Dans une mine ? Je rentre !: You? In a mine? I'm coming home!
textes.Toi ? Peur de la mer ? Mais tu es venu j: You? Scared of the sea? But you came all the way here! … So you can be scared and go anyway? Oh. That changes everything.
textes.Toi ?! Sur MA scène ? … D'accord. Vas-y,: You?! On MY stage? … Fine. Go ahead, the audience is hot. Well, warm. Well, it's made of stone.
textes.Toi aussi tu veux rester, hein ? On a un: You wanna stay too, huh? We've got a secret together now. Shh.
textes.Toi aussi, tu as eu peur de la mer, et t: You were scared of the sea too, and you came anyway. I think about it every time I look up.
textes.Toi aussi, tu as peur de la mer. Je ne l: You're scared of the sea too. I won't forget. That makes us two pond cats.
You heard it too, the song. There are two of us. It does me good to know that.
textes.Toi aussi, tu perds le compte. On devrai: You lose count too. We should start a club. There'd be four thousand two hundred and twelve of us. Or thirteen.
textes.Toi aussi, tu pleures, quelquefois. Je l: You cry sometimes too. I kept it to myself. If it ever happens to you here, come and find me. I know the good spots.
You too. I mean… have a nice evening.
textes.Toi aussi. À ton enclume. Et aux pierres: You too. With your anvil. And with stones.
You no move! Ocre look at you.
textes.Toi chez qui tout meurt : j'ai écrit une: You whose plants all die: I've written a lullaby for plants, just for you. It starts with “sorry”.
textes.Toi du Clan. Toi toujours bienvenu au fe: You of the Clan. You always welcome at fire.
textes.Toi encore. Bien. Tant que tu respectes: You again. Good. As long as you respect the ship, you're welcome.
textes.Toi encore. Tu n'aurais pas croisé un ch: You again. You wouldn't have come across a ginger cat, by any chance? A filthy beast. A demon with whiskers.
textes.Toi et ta fête de village… j'y repensais: You and your village party… I was thinking about it. There was an old fellow in a beanie dancing, wasn't there? No? Pity.
textes.Toi et ta harpe… Caelan a joué jusqu'à q: You and your harp… Caelan played until four. I thought of you. I looked behind me.
textes.Toi et tes lettres de chez toi : j'ai es: You and your letters from back home: I tried to invent two. They look like ducks.
textes.Toi et ton mal de mer ! Tu as repris des: You and your seasickness! You've got your colour back since. Arcanelle suits you better than the waves.
textes.Toi et ton poisson grillé… j'ai essayé u: You and your grilled fish… I tried a sardine with ember mushroom. It sneezed. So did I.
textes.Toi grandir. Toi devenir carré comme nou: You grow. You become square like us!
textes.Toi l'amateur de mystères, je t'ai gardé: You lover of mysteries, I've saved you a riddle with no answer. Don't solve it too fast.
textes.Toi le bateau : ta pirogue est dans mon: You, the boat: your canoe is in my codex. I gave it waves. Lots of waves.
textes.Toi le bâtisseur de cabane : elle tient: You, the hut builder: is it still standing? If it lets water in, come and see me. I've got tar.
textes.Toi le champion ! Un jour, toi et moi, s: You, the champion! One day, you and me, on the court. I'll let you score once. Maybe.
textes.Toi le chanteur ! Le roi demande si tu r: Hey, singer! The king's asking if you're coming back tonight. He says he needs someone to drown out his voice.
textes.Toi le difficile, je cherche toujours to: You, the fussy one, I'm still looking for your dish. I tried biscuit tagine. Tibo says no.
textes.Toi le dormeur : je t'ai gardé une datte: You, sleepyhead: I've saved you a date. For the day you want to see the dawn.
textes.Toi le ramasseur de coquillages : la Pla: You the shell collector: Bone Beach has some magnificent ones. Hurry, the crabs like them too.
textes.Toi non plus, tu n'as jamais vu la balei: You've never seen the whale either. Shall we start a club? Two members already makes a watch.
textes.Toi que le feu réchauffe, n'oublie pas :: You who are warmed by fire, don't forget: the Ember Heart belongs to everyone. Come and sit by it whenever you like.
textes.Toi que les bons repas réchauffent, je t: You who are warmed by a good meal, I'd saved you a slice of brioche. Well, I ate it. But I thought of you.
textes.Toi que les bêtes escaladent, je t'ai mi: You whom the animals climb all over, I've put aside a thick old cloak for you. Hooves leave marks.
textes.Toi qui adores danser : ce soir, je joue: You who love dancing: tonight, I'm playing for you. Fast. Very fast. Get your feet ready.
textes.Toi qui adores le bateau… tu me raconter: You love boats… will you tell me about Port-Azur? With details. I want to know everything, without going.
textes.Toi qui aimes ce qui dure, regarde ma gr: You who love things that last, look at my grate in the Heart: forty years, and not one crack. Like my marriage. Well, almost.
textes.Toi qui aimes danser… il y a un bal, par: You who like dancing… there's a ball, sometimes, at the Crâne Fendu. Dance. For those who can't any more.
textes.Toi qui aimes la cuisine douce, j'ai mis: For you who likes it mild, I put less rouille in your portion. My pot hasn't spoken to me since.
textes.Toi qui aimes la mer : si tu croises Sob: You who like the sea: if you run into Sobek out there, tell him to stay there. With his friends.
textes.Toi qui aimes la nuit… Gustave, le réver: You who love the night… Gustave, the market street lamp, flickered when you walked past yesterday. He likes you.
textes.Toi qui aimes la pluie : j'ai fait une j: You who like rain: I made a jar thinking of you. Get ready to be soaked.
textes.Toi qui aimes la pluie la nuit : la proc: You who like rain at night: next time it falls on your roof, listen carefully. It's Tlaloc singing for you.
textes.Toi qui aimes la soupe de poisson, j'en: You who love fish soup, I made some yesterday. With thirteen fish. I beat Port-Azur by three fish.
textes.Toi qui aimes la ville : tu as vu Aztlán: You who like the town: have you seen Aztlán? They farm on the water. You'd like that sort of madness.
textes.Toi qui aimes le blanc : regarde ma toil: You who love white: look at my cloth against the light. You'll see what I mean.
textes.Toi qui aimes le blanc : tu as vu le lin: You who love white: have you seen Tiyi's linen, in Per-Hâpy? Go and look at it. Against the sun.
textes.Toi qui aimes le blanc et les couleurs :: You who love white and colours: we're alike, you and me. Don't tell anyone.
textes.Toi qui aimes le bleu : regarde mes doig: You who like blue: look at my fingers. Still a little blue. We're alike.
textes.Toi qui aimes le bruit. Le souk t'attend: You who like noise. The souk awaits you. Go. Salam.
textes.Toi qui aimes le calme, tu remarques que: You who love peace and quiet, have you noticed I talk more softly with you? It's a huge effort. HUGE.
textes.Toi qui aimes le cirque : un de ces soir: You, who love the circus: one of these evenings, I'm doing an act at the Crâne Fendu. Hold your breath for me.
textes.Toi qui aimes le jour : tu me racontes l: You who love the day: will you tell me about the colours? I imagine them. Red, especially. Like someone's cheeks.
textes.Toi qui aimes le jus de coco : il y en a: You, who like coconut juice: there's some at Mama's bar. I've seen it. I haven't touched it. Hardly.
textes.Toi qui aimes le piment : je t'ai gardé: You who like chilli: I've saved my strongest recipe for you. Get your tears ready.
textes.Toi qui aimes le poisson grillé : Grumba: You who love grilled fish: Grumbald has put “fish à la Moloka” on his slate. He says it's in your honour. He's lying, but it's sweet.
textes.Toi qui aimes le rouge : j'ai trouvé une: You who like red: I found a perfect macaw feather. I'm keeping it for you.
textes.Toi qui aimes le silence : écoute bien m: You, who love silence: listen closely to my song tonight. There are four beats of silence in the middle. They're for people like you.
textes.Toi qui aimes le silence, ce soir je fer: You who love silence, tonight I'll leave a pause between two songs. A long one. You'll know why.
textes.Toi qui aimes le silence. Assieds-toi. O: You who like silence. Sit down. We'll say nothing. Together.
textes.Toi qui aimes le soir, j'ai allumé le pr: You who love the evening, I lit the first street lamp thinking of you. It made a shy little flame. Like me.
textes.Toi qui aimes les bains très chauds : le: You who love very hot baths: the second pool has been singing louder since you came by. It likes you.
textes.Toi qui aimes les belles histoires, j'en: You, who love beautiful stories, I've got a brand-new one. It isn't true at all. It's magnificent.
textes.Toi qui aimes les champs : viens tirer l: You who like the fields: come and work the shadoof one morning. It builds your back. And your character.
textes.Toi qui aimes les chiens et les chats :: You who love dogs and cats: a cat has moved into the kennel. The pups adore him. He tolerates them.
textes.Toi qui aimes les complaintes : un soir: You, who love laments: some rainy evening, sit near the stage. I'll play for you. Softly.
textes.Toi qui aimes les couleurs : va voir Ix: You who love colours: go and see Ix Sak, in Yaxché, and tell her Tiyi sent you. She'll understand.
textes.Toi qui aimes les deux… Il était deux fo: You who like both… Twice upon a time, {surnom}. See? You're smiling already.
textes.Toi qui aimes les feux de camp : Grand-p: You who love campfires: Grandpa's telling stories on the square tonight. There'll be a flame-shaped lantern. For you.
textes.Toi qui aimes les fins, je t'en garde un: You who love endings, I'm saving one for you. But not just yet. An ending has to be earned. Come back and see me.
textes.Toi qui aimes les gigues : ce soir, la p: You, who love jigs: tonight, the fastest one in my repertoire. If you last to the end, I'll buy you a grog.
textes.Toi qui aimes les histoires vraies : cel: You who like true stories: this one really happened. Twice, in fact. Sit down.
textes.Toi qui aimes les lames légères… j'ai pe: You who like light blades… I thought of you this morning while thinning an edge. By a hair. A dwarf's hair, mind, which is already a lot.
textes.Toi qui aimes les levers de soleil : j'a: You who love sunrises: I've made an orange and pink lantern. It's not as beautiful. But it rises whenever you like.
textes.Toi qui aimes les tic-tac et les boums,: You who love tick-tocks and booms, you're my official assistant. I've written your name on my cupboard door.
textes.Toi qui aimes les tic-tac, j'ai pensé à: You who love tick-tocks, I thought of you: I put a clock in my machine. Now it goes tick-tock before it goes boom.
textes.Toi qui aimes les étoiles : à la prochai: You who love the stars: at the next festival, look carefully at the sky. One of the stars will be one of my lanterns. Will you know which?
textes.Toi qui aimes quand ça pique un tout pet: You, who like things just a tiny bit spicy: I've kept some fire cinnamon for you. The mildest. Hardly any smoke.
textes.Toi qui aimes quand ça pique, j'ai un no: You, who like things spicy: I have a new chili. Stronger. Grumbald tasted it. He hasn't spoken since yesterday. He's fine.
textes.Toi qui aimes recevoir des lettres, je n: You who love receiving letters: I don't have one for you yet. But I look in my bag every morning. You never know.
textes.Toi qui aimes te perdre : si tu trouves: You, who like getting lost: if you find a cove that's on no map, come and tell me. I'll name it after you.
textes.Toi qui aimes à la fois ce qui dure et c: You who love both what lasts and what changes, you're like good iron. I told Pyrus. He nodded. Coming from him, that's a compliment.
textes.Toi qui aimes écouter : j'ai trois histo: You who love to listen: I've got three brand-new stories for you. One of them's about Orsik. Shh!
textes.Toi qui aimes écrire des lettres, tu m'e: You who love writing letters: will you give me one to deliver? No? I'll wait. My bag always has room.
textes.Toi qui arrives toujours en avance… tu n: You who always arrive early… couldn't you lend me your secret? For one letter. Just one.
textes.Toi qui as abandonné de compter les étoi: You who gave up counting the stars: so did I, last night. Three hundred and twelve. Always the same.
textes.Toi qui as caressé Tlaco : il se souvien: You who petted Tlaco: he remembers you! He's wagging his tail. Or maybe he saw a heron.
textes.Toi qui as compté jusqu'à mille : j'ai v: You who counted up to a thousand: I checked, there are more. Sorry. But well done.
textes.Toi qui as compté les étoiles : ce soir,: You who've counted the stars: tonight, count again with me. Two of us will make fewer mistakes. Or twice as many.
textes.Toi qui as construit un radeau : je t'ai: You who built a raft: I've kept you a plank from the Merciless. For your next one. Or for a stool.
textes.Toi qui as construit une barque, dis-moi: You who've built a boat, tell me: you wouldn't have a bit of wood, would you? People in the trade always do.
textes.Toi qui as des amis pour moitiés… combie: You who have friends for halves… how many do you have now? I count. It's my job.
textes.Toi qui as déjà mangé un truc horrible :: You who've eaten something horrible: I've saved you a portion of stew. To make peace with cooking.
textes.Toi qui as eu le mal de mer une fois : j: You who were seasick once: I haven't told anyone. Except Zébuline. She laughed. She understands you.
textes.Toi qui as eu peur en voyant Arcanelle :: You who were afraid when you saw Arcanelle: are you still afraid of her? She, at any rate, has got used to you. I can see it.
textes.Toi qui as gagné une fois : tu l'as raco: You who won once: have you told the story today? You must. Every day.
textes.Toi qui as jamais peur du noir, tu me ra: You who are never scared of the dark, will you tell me how you do it? Slowly. With some fireflies around, though.
textes.Toi qui as la main verte : il reste un c: You with the green thumb: there's still a free corner on my chinampa. For your willow.
textes.Toi qui as la main verte : mes poivriers: You with your green fingers: my peppers were asking for you yesterday. Well, they leaned your way. Same thing.
textes.Toi qui as le monde pour maison : n'oubl: You who have the world for a home: don't forget you also have a room here, under the roof. With the skylight.
textes.Toi qui as le rythme dans les pieds… tu: You with the rhythm in your feet… would you teach me? No, nothing. I didn't say anything. Boom.
textes.Toi qui as le rythme, viens taper avec m: You who've got rhythm, come and drum with me at the grill. Mustapha will pay you in sardines. Me, in applause.
textes.Toi qui as oublié ta première fête… je t: You, who forgot your first party… I made one up for you. There were dwarves. You danced a lot.
textes.Toi qui as pas de queue, t'as fait des s: You with no tail, did you do happy eyebrows today? Show me!
textes.Toi qui as peur de l'eau. … Bien. Regard: You who are afraid of water. … Good. Always watch the water. Not the sky.
textes.Toi qui as peur des clowns : rassure-toi: You, who are scared of clowns: don't worry, there aren't any on Balafre. Apart from the Governor.
textes.Toi qui as peur du noir : la forge reste: You who are scared of the dark: the forge stays red till midnight. Drop by.
textes.Toi qui as plusieurs maisons… Ramure en: You who have several homes… Is Ramure one of them now? Don't answer. I'll feel it.
textes.Toi qui as reconnu mon poisson, viens vo: You recognised my fish, so come and see the next one. I think it's a fish too. Maybe.
textes.Toi qui as toutes tes dents : fais-y att: You, who've got all your teeth: take care of them. And never take Belle-Humeur for a jokethter.
textes.Toi qui as trouvé un vrai trésor ! Tu m': You found a real treasure! Will you take me next time? I'll carry the shovel!
textes.Toi qui as très peur des crocodiles : je: You who are very scared of crocodiles: I count my toes, do you? Ten? Good. Me too.
textes.Toi qui as un chat ! Tu lui as dit bonjo: You who have a cat! Did you say hello to it from Miou? You have to, it's polite.
textes.Toi qui as un chien : est-ce qu'il aime: You who have a dog: does it like cats? Miou likes Peek'. Peek' isn't so sure.
textes.Toi qui as un peu peur de la mer : moi a: You who are a little scared of the sea: me too, a little. All right. A lot. But that stays between us.
textes.Toi qui as un peu peur des crocodiles :: You who are a little scared of crocodiles: we make a fine pair. We'll fish upstream, you and me.
textes.Toi qui as un peu peur du fond, comme mo: You, who are a bit scared of the deep, like me: breathe slower than the fear. It works for dancing too.
textes.Toi qui as un peu peur du noir… j'ai dem: You who are a bit scared of the dark… I asked a firefly to follow you tonight. If you see a little light, that's her.
textes.Toi qui as vu des dauphins, tu crois que: You've seen dolphins, so do you think mine was a real one? Say yes.
textes.Toi qui as vu du pays, dis-moi francheme: You've seen the world, so tell me honestly: can a map be wrong?
textes.Toi qui as vu tant d'îles… Si tu aimais: You who've seen so many islands… If you'd loved someone for a hundred years, how would you tell them?
textes.Toi qui as vu un serpent de mer : j'en a: You who've seen a sea serpent: I saw another one last night. Three humps. I've saved you a spot on the jetty.
textes.Toi qui as vu une baleine ! Raconte enco: You who've seen a whale! Tell me again. Nobody believes me, so I listen to you twice.
textes.Toi qui as vu une lumière que personne n: You who saw a light nobody else saw: if it comes back, come and get me. I'll believe you.
textes.Toi qui as été piqué : mes abeilles te p: You who've been stung: my bees apologise for the others. With a buzz.
textes.Toi qui attends que ça passe : tu as l'a: You, who wait for it to pass: you look well. This time. I'm keeping a potion aside anyway. With your name on it.
textes.Toi qui attises les feux de camp, je sur: You, who stoke campfires: I'm keeping an eye on your eyebrows. Still there? Good. Keep it up.
textes.Toi qui avais mangé « tout à l'heure » :: You who'd eaten “a while ago”: is it still a while ago, now? Ha!
textes.Toi qui avais un peu peur la première fo: You were a bit scared the first time: would you come with me on the Swallow? One day. Not today.
textes.Toi qui bois de l'eau… Hic ! Tu as peut-: You, who drink water… Hic! Maybe you're right. Mama Grog says the same. Don't tell her I said so.
textes.Toi qui bois des litres, je te fais conf: You drink gallons, I trust you. But drink anyway. Just to make me happy.
textes.Toi qui bois du lait chaud… j'ai repensé: You, who drink hot milk… I thought about Papa again, because of you. It did me good. Hic.
textes.Toi qui caches des choses vraies dans te: You who hide true things in your jokes… made one this morning? I'm suspicious now.
textes.Toi qui caresses les chiens qui dorment: You who pet sleeping dogs: come back during Tlaco's nap. He takes lots of them. Like me.
textes.Toi qui casses et qui répares : tu as fa: You who break and mend: were you careful turning around today?
