I've never thanked her. She's never confessed. One morning I left a cup of tea beside it, with a note: “For the wind.” The cup was empty by noon.
textes.Tous les quatre ! Le traité des nuages,: All four! The treatise on clouds, the herbal of shadows, the grammar of ravens and… “Berthe's Recipes, Volume Two.” I'd forgotten that one. Thank you. Truly. Here, some coins. And you may borrow any book you like, whenever you like. Without dog-earing it.
textes.Tous les samedis, je pose mes pièces sur: Every Saturday, I put my coins on the counter, and Mama wipes my tab off the slate with her tea towel. She says I'm the most honest customer in the port. Once, I was one coin short. She said: “Next week.” The following week, I gave her two. She cried a little. Hic! Or maybe it was the onions.
textes.Tous les samedis, on fait un bras de fer: Every Saturday, we arm-wrestle on a barrel at the end of the quay. It takes a long time. A very long time. The barrel gave way before we did, three times. Tonneau, the real one, took it badly: he thought we were making fun of him. The score is nil-nil. The Silent One says with his hands that he's winning. I don't understand hands.
textes.Tous les soirs après la garde, je monte: Every evening after my watch, I go up to the terrace to buy a mug of golden fizz from Sigrun. I drink it very slowly, so I can stay. Yesterday, she said: “Gunnar, you've been drinking the same mug for three years.” She's right: I top it up with water so it lasts. She laughed. I blushed.
textes.Tous les soirs, Barnabé agite son chapea: Every evening, Barnabé waves his hat towards our mist from his beach. Thalion says we don't answer humans. One evening I took a lantern and flashed it three times from the top of the highest platform. Barnabé jumped on the spot and danced. His parrot must have told him it was a firefly. Don't tell Thalion.
textes.Tous les soirs, Kiki rentre de la paillo: Every night, Kiki comes back from the beach hut at midnight on the dot and plays three songs under my window. He thinks I like it. So at midnight on the dot, I close my shutter. Clack. He takes it for applause. The next day he asks me: “Did you hear the new one?” I heard. All the new ones.
textes.Tous les soirs, Ori compte mes rubis ave: Every evening, Ori counts my rubies with me and writes them one by one in the big ledger. Every evening, one is missing. Ori writes: “one ruby, out”. Not “stolen”. “Out.” I asked him why. He said: “Because it comes back.” That lad is wiser than his great-uncle.
textes.Tous les soirs, au ponton, Bastien m'att: Every evening, at the jetty, Bastien waits to carry my baskets. He says he's checking the tides. At seven in the evening. Every evening. Empty-handed. One day I gave him the most golden croissant of the batch. He held it like treasure. He didn't eat it in front of me. Funny boy.
textes.Tous les soirs, j'agite mon chapeau vers: Every evening, I wave my hat towards the mist. Nobody ever answers. Except once: a lantern blinked three times, high up in the trees. Gaston says it was a firefly. Me, I'm sure it was Faelar. Old folks understand each other.
textes.Tous les soirs, j'écoute grand-père Till: Every evening I listen to Grandpa Tilleul at the Circle. The other little ones fall asleep before the end. Not me! Never! I ask “And then?”, and he starts another story. He's got loads. Under the big pond there's a dragon, I'm sure of it, and one day he'll tell me its very own story. Mochi says a dragon-fish. Myrtille says a king. Both total nonsense.
textes.Tous les soirs, je monte au Cercle avec: Every evening, I go up to the Circle with two cups of mint tea. Ysolde drinks hers without a word. Aube hated mint. I sometimes wonder if her daughter does too, and drinks it to please me. I don't dare ask. We drink, we listen to the stones. That's our way of talking about Aube.
textes.Tous les soirs, je monte sur ma plus hau: Every evening, I climb onto my highest branch and look across to the other side of the island. I check that the smoke from his hut is rising. If it is, I climb back down. I don't know why I do it. Neither does Clou.
textes.Tous les soirs, mademoiselle ! Un jour,: Every evening, miss! One day, someone will answer.
textes.Tous les soirs, maman me raconte une his: Every night, Mummy tells me a story she makes up. They're the best in the world. Yesterday it was Captain, my bear, who went off on a boat to find my kite. He found it on an island made of clouds. I fell asleep before the end. This morning I asked for the end. Mummy said it's a secret. Mummies have loads of secrets.
textes.Tous les soirs, quand L'Hirondelle accos: Every evening, when the Swallow docks, I'm at the jetty to carry Fanny's baskets to the dance floor. One evening she gave me the most golden croissant of the batch. I didn't eat it right away. I looked at it for a long time, sitting in my boat. It was all squashed the next day. Silly, isn't it.
textes.Tous les soirs, une lanterne de nacre ar: Every evening, a mother-of-pearl lantern drifts down the canal, right in front of my bridge. I pretend to believe it's the current. But the current flows the other way, {surnom}. I know perfectly well who blows those lanterns. I'm waiting for him to tell me himself. It's been thirty years. I'm patient. Well, less and less.
textes.Tous les trois ! Et chauds encore, je pa: All three! And still warm, I bet. You're a darling, my little one. Here, some coins, and a nice warm honey bread. That one, you're allowed to eat on the way.
textes.Tous les vendredis, quelqu'un paie ma pu: Every Friday, thomeone payth Mange-Clous for my mathed thtew. Mange-Clous won't thay who. But one Friday, I thaw Belle-Humeur put two coinths on the counter and walk off grumbling, without looking at me. He doethn't know I thaw. I'll never tell him. He'd mithhear it anyway.
textes.Tous trouvés ! Tu es le champion du cach: All found! You're the hide-and-seek champion!
All of it? Very well: {prix} coins for the lot.
textes.Tout ? D'accord : {prix} pièces pour le: Everything? All right: {prix} coins for the lot.
textes.Tout ? Ha ! Personne ne veut tout. Bon :: Everything? Ha! Nobody wants everything. Fine: you're going to eat, sleep, walk, and meet some amazing people. See? I'm never wrong.
textes.Tout ? {prix} pièces le lot. Et je suis: All of it? {prix} coins for the lot. And I'm being generous.
textes.Tout Arcanelle passe par mon auberge. Le: All of Arcanelle passes through my inn. The masters, the apprentices, the ferryman, the seer. If you want to know something about someone, ask Berthe. But not too loudly.
textes.Tout au fond des Neuf Cercles, il y a le: At the very bottom of the Nine Circles lies the Cocytus, a frozen lake. They say a Frost Titan sleeps there, and that the Eternal Flame, which feeds our Ember Heart, burns right next to him. If you go down, wrap up warm. Really.
Very softly, then. Close your eyes.
textes.Tout ce que tu vends est volé, non ?: Everything you sell is stolen, isn't it?
textes.Tout ce qui arrive sur l'île passe par m: Everything that arrives on the island goes through my arms. Margaux's bread, Toni's bottles, the jewellery shop's dresses.
textes.Tout ce qui est ici a été honnêtement… t: Everything here was honestly… found. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Tout de suite ! Voilà. C'est pour toi qu: Right away! There you go. That's who we play for. Dancing feet are half the orchestra. Tonight, stand at the front, near Omar.
textes.Tout de suite ? Alors tu es plus sage qu: Straight away? Then you're wiser than all the gamblers on this island put together. Be wary of that wisdom. It doesn't always last.
textes.Tout de suite, chef ! Combien, aujourd'h: Right away, boss! How many today?
textes.Tout de suite, milord. Mais je n'ai touj: Right away, milord. But I still don't have change.
textes.Tout droit ? La dernière fois, c'était u: Straight ahead? Last time, it was a reef!
textes.Tout en haut de la grotte ! Les gros cha: Right at the top of the cave! The big mushrooms bounce: climb on, and boing!
textes.Tout en haut du tableau, champion. Il s': Right at the top of the board, champ. It's getting a bit bored.
textes.Tout est beau ici. Même quand on est tri: Everything is beautiful here. Even when you're sad.
textes.Tout est cher à Port-Azur, parce que tou: Everything's expensive in Port-Azur, because everything comes by boat. But my prices are fair. Well, nearly.
textes.Tout est prêt, Sylvain ! Vingt dés, frai: All ready, Sylvain! Twenty dice, fresh today!
Everything's too close to you, lad. Hmph. Again.
Everything is for sale! … Well, almost.
textes.Tout flotte ! La table, les chaises, les: Everything floats! The table, the chairs, the books… even the houseplant, which looks delighted.
textes.Tout l'hiver, il m'a appelée « la grande: All winter, he called me “the big hairy one”. “Big hairy one, sweep! Big hairy one, stand back!” I swept. I watched. He refused to teach me the runes. I didn't ask twice. Tempering, I learned by watching him. He knows, I think. He grumbled, the day I left. A good grumble.
textes.Tout le lot ? Allez : {prix} pièces, et: The whole lot? Go on: {prix} coins, and a scorching handshake thrown in!
textes.Tout le monde a le rythme. Ton cœur bat,: Everybody has rhythm. Your heart beats, doesn't it? Tap on the table… There. Boom. Boom. See? You had it, you were hiding it.
textes.Tout le monde croit que Grimli dort dans: Everyone thinks Grimli sleeps in the mine because I snore. I snore, fine. But that's not why. He forgets things, {surnom}. Real things. He's afraid I'll see it. So I embroidered both our names inside his cap. He hasn't noticed yet.
textes.Tout le monde croit que je parle aux cro: Everyone thinks I talk to crocodiles to calm them down. I'll tell you the truth, {surnom}. I talk to them because I'm scared. When I talk, my legs stop shaking. So I tell them about my day, the barley, the beer, the onions. They listen. They don't come closer. Maybe they're bored. That suits me.
textes.Tout le monde me demande ce que dit le M: Everyone asks me what the Silent One is saying. So I translate. He points at the sea: “He says the weather's fine.” He points at Tonneau: “He says Tonneau's thirsty again.” Sometimes I make things up, for a laugh: “He says Belle-Humeur is in love.” The Silent One shakes his head, very slowly. Belle-Humeur didn't hear a thing. Luckily.
textes.Tout le monde parle de ce que tu as fait: Everyone's talking about what you did for {qn}.
textes.Tout le monde parle de ce que vous avez: Everyone's talking about what you did for {qn}.
Everyone knows I'm scared of heights. What nobody knows is why I'm cross with Thalion. Not because he shakes the bees up there. Because he can climb up and see them, and I can't. I hear them singing on windy days. I've never seen them. Not once.
textes.Tout le monde sait que tu as offert {obj: Everyone knows you gave {objet} to {qn}. Around here, news travels faster than the wind.
textes.Tout le monde sait que vous avez offert: Everyone knows you gave {objet} to {qn}. Around here, news travels faster than the wind.
textes.Tout le reste. Mais on a des amis partou: All the rest. But we've got friends everywhere now.
textes.Tout le temps ! Ha ha ! Tu es un renard: All the time! Ha ha! You're a fox in disguise, admit it! … All the time, eh. It gets tiring, in the long run. I know.
textes.Tout là-haut, au sommet du Mont Fusain,: Way up, at the summit of Mount Charcoal, beside the cairn: a little glint. Purple. A pot!
Everything looks lovely to me today.
textes.Tout meurt ? Ha ! Même les cactus ? Il f: Everything dies? Ha! Even cacti? You have to talk to plants, come on. And water them. Above all, water them. The talking is just for fun.
textes.Tout meurt chez toi ? Ce n'est pas ta fa: Everything dies on you? It's not your fault, little one. You just didn't sing them a song, that's all. Plants need a lullaby. Like children.
Everything grows! Then Tlaloc likes you. Come and plant a willow on my chinampa: it'll bear your name. Well, it won't say it. Willows are shy.
textes.Tout près, hein. Pour qu'il la voie bien: Really close, eh. So he can see it properly. He'd say “Hm.” But a proud “Hm”. I know those, I've heard two.
textes.Tout se vend ? Ha ! Toi, tu ferais un ex: Everything's for sale? Ha! You'd make an excellent fence! Or a very bad friend. Both, maybe. Come back and see me, we'll talk business.
textes.Tout simplement… Tu dis ça comme si c'ét: Simple as that… You say it as if it were simple. For humans, maybe: you live fast, you talk fast. I should take lessons.
textes.Tout tourne… Tu ferais mieux de t'arrête: Everything's spinning… you'd better stop there!
textes.Tout à l'heure ? Mais tout à l'heure, c': A while ago? But a while ago is ages! I ate a while ago too. And look: I'm hungry anyway. That's the job sinking in.
textes.Tout ça ? D'accord. {prix} pièces le lot: All that? Alright. {prix} coins for the lot. You're getting a good deal, and I'm getting a better one.
textes.Toute l'huile, cette fois, Monsieur Tibu: All the oil this time, Monsieur Tiburce. For both horns.
textes.Toute l'huile, cette fois. Pour les deux: All the oil, this time. For both horns.
textes.Toute l'huile, très cher. Je vous le jur: All the oil, my dear sir. I swear it.
textes.Toute la caverne chante, d'une seule voi: The whole cavern sings, with one low, soft voice. The veins of the rock light up all the way to the ceiling… At the back of the room, the great slab sinks into the floor. “The Heart of the Song is yours, friend of the Moai.”
textes.Toute la forge se tait. Borin et Nori le: The whole forge falls silent. Borin and Nori the Runecarver engrave the armour for an entire night. By morning, the runes beat softly, like a heart. “The finest I've ever made.”
textes.Toute la forêt, tonton ! Surtout la part: The whole forest, Uncle! Especially the part with the arches.
textes.Toute la journée, Chak ! Avec les hanche: All day, Chak! With the hips!
textes.Toute la place a entendu. Le trente-sixi: The whole square heard. The thirty-sixth verse was pretty.
textes.Toute légère ! Les fleurs boivent, les f: Light as air! The flowers are drinking, the fairies are singing.
textes.Toute ma vie, j'ai cherché la cité englo: All my life, I've searched for the sunken city. The texts speak of a great crystal that gave air and light. If one day you find that city, if you see that crystal shining… come back and tell me about it. I beg you.
textes.Toute petite ourse, pendant mes histoire: When she was a tiny bear cub, during my stories, she'd bang on the pots with a spoon. Bing! when the dragon came. Bang! when the storm broke. Her mother wanted to hush her. Me, I understood that night she'd be a blacksmith. Old Charbon took her on as an apprentice at ten. He said she struck true.
textes.Toute petite, Lumi passait ses journées: When she was tiny, Lumi spent her days trying to light herself up, like the fireflies who saw her born. One evening, she came and cried on my lap. I told her: “You don't need to glow, Lumi. You make the others glow.” The next day, I put her in charge of the fireflies.
textes.Toutes ? Ah… Tu es un bon public, mousse: All of them? Ah… You're a good audience, cabin boy. The best. Sit down, I'll tell you a true one. Well, almost true.
textes.Toutes ? Alors profite ! Croque des pomm: All of them? Then make the motht of it! Bite into appleth, nutth, thhip'th bithcuitth! And above all, never athk Belle-Humeur to path the thalt.
textes.Toutes ? Et combien de détours ?: All of them? And how many detours?
textes.Toutes ? Il en faudrait peut-être quatre: Every one? There may be four hundred… But I like your answer. You have human feet and the heart of a migrating bird.
textes.Toutes ? Même celle qui ne craquait pas: All of them? Even the one that didn't creak?
textes.Toutes ? Même… la reine ? Oh ! J'ai les: All of them? Even… the queen? Oh! I have tears in my eyes. You carried a little of my heart to the end of the world. Take a little of mine: it's big, I have too much.
textes.Toutes droites, monsieur Asmodin ! Comme: All straight, Monsieur Asmodin! As usual!
textes.Toutes les couleurs de l'île: All the colours of the island
textes.Toutes les heures, Gaspard pose une gour: Every hour, Gaspard puts a bottle of spring water on my table. If I don't drink, he stays there, looking at me, nodding. Once, I held out for four minutes. I drank it in one go, laughing, and improvised a track for him. I called it “Water Bottle”. He's never found it funny. He dances to it anyway.
textes.Toutes les journées sont belles, au Bois: Every day is lovely, in Bois-Doré.
textes.Toutes les nuits ! Oh, je le savais ! Tu: Every night! Oh, I knew it! You've got a cloud head, that's a compliment. People who fly in their dreams levitate faster, everyone knows that. Well, I say so.
textes.Toutes les semaines, le mousse m'apporte: Every week, the cabin boy brings me a bill. The green net. Three weeks of work. Plus interest. I read it. I fold it in four. I put it in my pocket. I've got three. I don't pay. I don't throw them away either. Hm. Don't know why.
textes.Toutes les yourtes sont vides… Où sont d: All the yurts are empty… Where have the people of Larsen Island gone? It looks like they're preparing something.
textes.Toutes mes passerelles sont solides, Syl: All my footbridges are sturdy, Sylwen. All of them.
textes.Toutes mes versions sont vraies, ma puce: All my versions are true, sweetheart. Especially the best ones.
textes.Toutes, Majesté ! Un record ! Fffiou !: Every one, Your Majesty! A record! Fffwoosh!
All of them, Philibert. Thanks to you.
textes.Toutes… Toutes les couleurs. (Elle regar: All… All the colours. (She looks at the clearing, the giants, the houses, the sky in the pond, for a long time, saying nothing.) The Council met this morning. Well, Gaspard, Augustin and I, on the terrace. We voted. From now on, you will be the Colourist of Sketched Island. Keep the Brush: it's yours now. And if one day it rains too hard, you'll know what to do. Here, also: a honey cake from Rosalie, and a little from the Council's fund. It was only used for buying paint.
textes.Tout… Vous avez un grand cœur. Ou beauco: Everything… You have a big heart. Or a lot of practice. A ring in the sand should be easy to forgive, shouldn't it? So why is it so hard?
textes.Tranquille, Barnabé. Plancher, murs, toi: Chill, Barnabé. Floor, walls, roof. And a bottle of water.
textes.Tranquille. Le cuivre se travaille lente: Calm. Copper is worked slowly. So is light.
textes.Tranquille. Le fil ne casse pas, la nave: Peaceful. The thread doesn't break, the shuttle sings.
textes.Tranquille. Le son est bon, l'eau est fr: Chilled. The sound is good, the water is cool.
Peaceful. The books are all in order. Almost all.
textes.Tranquille. Tu veux de l'eau ? J'ai touj: Chill. Want some water? I've always got water.
textes.Traverser le Lac Miroir sur un chemin de: Cross Mirror Lake on a path of ice (frost spell, key 7 then V, facing the islet; in VR, left trigger) and touch the Frost Crystal (E)
Thirteen! I could hear it from here.
textes.Trente ans de mer. Le premier capitaine,: Thirty years at sea. The first captain, a storm took him. The second, a fever, in three days. The third died old, in his hammock, snoring. Good death. The fourth is Croc. He's alive. I keep an eye on him. A captain who's scared of a cat needs watching.
textes.Trente ans de mer. Quatre capitaines. Tr: Thirty years at sea. Four captains. Three are dead. The fourth, I'm keeping an eye on.
textes.Trente ans de réception. J'ai accueilli: Thirty years at reception. I've welcomed princes, pirates and a performing bear. The bear was the most polite.
textes.Trente ans en haut du Guet. Par tous les: Thirty years at the top of the Lookout. In all weathers. The zip line, I strung it up to get down fast in an alarm. The children use it. And Grisou. From up there, I see the forest, and the forest knows I see it. That's the job. Being seen seeing. So nobody gets up to mischief. Almost nobody.
textes.Trente ans facteur à Port-Azur. Je conna: Thirty years as Port-Azur's postman. I knew every letterbox, every dog, every creaky step. At Hortense's I'd stop by even with no letter. For my last year, they gave me an apprentice, Nadine. I taught her everything. She remembered everything. Except the route: she made it shorter. That one still sticks in my throat.
textes.Trente ans plus tard, je suis retourné à: Thirty years later, I went back to Tazira on a boat loaded with sparkling apple. That evening, in the square, we held a storytelling duel: each of us told the other's story. He told my shipwreck better than me, and I told his sultan and his sardine better than him. People threw coins at both of us. We drank the whole lot together.
textes.Trente ans que je nourris des pirates !: Thirty years I've been feeding pirates! Four ships, four galleys, and the Murène Noire for the last ten years. Nobody has ever died of my cooking, I say it with pride. My ship's biscuit is as hard as wood: we wedge the tables with it, and once we plugged a leak with it. For a whole hour! That's proof it's solid.
textes.Trente ans que je nourris des pirates. P: Thirty years I've been feeding pirates. Nobody's ever died of my cooking. Well, nobody who complained about it.
textes.Trente mètres de haut : il se cache derr: Thirty meters tall: what's he going to hide behind?
textes.Trente secondes ! Personne ne t'a touché: Thirty seconds! Nobody touched you! … You've got eyes in the back of your head, haven't you?
textes.Trente-deux directions, cette fois ! Ess: Thirty-two points this time! Try copying that!
textes.Tribord, la troisième membrure. Et un cr: Starboard, third rib. And a crab has moved in.
textes.Triste ? Je suis… aveugle, presque. (Il: Sad? I'm... practically blind. (He points to the big telescope.) The last meteor shower. A little meteorite fragment, the size of a hazelnut, fell right into the tube. Three cracked lenses. I see the stars in three pieces. The Big Dipper looks like three little angry bears. I'd need three meteorite fragments to melt down new lenses. They fell everywhere that night: on the Agora, in the Hanging Gardens, at the Spaceport... Would you look for them? They're black, heavy, and they still glow a little.
textes.Triste. L'horloge s'est arrêtée. Une pla: Sad. The clock has stopped. A square without a clock is a heart without a beat.
textes.Triste. Miou est parti depuis trois jour: Sad. Miou's been gone for three days. Mum says he'll come back. Cats always come back, she says.
textes.Triste. Sans cerf-volant, la plage c'est: Sad. Without a kite, the beach is just sand.
textes.Triton ! Il mord toujours, ton trident ?: Triton! Does your trident still bite?
textes.Triton ! Le seul client qui ne s'est jam: Triton! The only customer who's never complained about my work. Three hundred years with the same trident, not one complaint. A saint.
textes.Triton ! On compte ? Un, deux…: Triton! Shall we count? One, two…
textes.Triton ! Ta pieuvre a soixante bras, ce: Triton! Your octopus has sixty arms tonight.
textes.Triton ?! … Attends. Recule. … Par les m: Triton?! … Wait. Step back. … By the tides, it's true. The eyebrows. Don't tell him, he'd want me to put it up at the Gate.
textes.Triton est le héros de mes plus belles h: Triton is the hero of my finest stories. He hates it. Which is exactly what makes him such a good hero.
textes.Triton est le plus fidèle de mes sujets: Triton is the most loyal of my subjects and the worst storyteller. He tells the children I'm a thousand years old. I'm a little more.
textes.Triton est le seul qui m'écoute chanter: Triton is the only one who listens to me sing without moving an inch. He says it's discipline. I think it's something else.
textes.Triton garde la Porte depuis trois cents: Triton has guarded the Gate for three hundred years, and he says he's never bored. I think he's a bit bored. That's why I go and see him every day.
textes.Triton m'apporte un rapport chaque soir: Triton has brought me a report every evening for three hundred years. Always the same: “Nothing to report.” It's the most reassuring scroll in all my archives.
textes.Triton m'apprend à retenir mon souffle,: Triton is teaching me to hold my breath, so I can go out one day. We sit in front of the Gate and count together. I can get to forty. He says he can last till three hundred. But around a hundred he goes all blue and pretends to cough because of the sand.
textes.Triton monte la garde à la Porte depuis: Triton has been guarding the Gate for three hundred years. He'd never seen anyone come in. You made him very happy.
textes.Trocante pose ton objet sur la table, bi: Trocante puts your item on the table, nice and visible: “Thank you! Somebody is going to be so happy.”
textes.Trois ! Ils sont encore tièdes… (Il les: Three! They're still warm... (He melts them in a little light furnace, blows on them, polishes them with his cape.) Three new lenses. (He presses his eye to the telescope.) Oh... Oh! The Big Dipper is a single bear again! She looks relieved. Come back tonight, during the auroras. I want to show you something.
textes.Trois Grandes Courses, trois fois deuxiè: Three Great Races, three times second behind Bondi. Second! That's almost first, you know. The problem is the race is too short: a wolf starts slow and then never stops. If it went round the whole island, I'd have been first ages ago. Well… I think. My paws think so too.
textes.Trois amis à table, pliés de rire. Perso: Three friends at the table, doubled over with laughter. Nobody has noticed you.
textes.Trois ans plus tard, on s'est croisés da: Three years later, we crossed paths in the fog off the south point, him in his longboat, me in a rowing boat. We argued over right of way for an hour, at the top of our voices. Then he held out a bottle of grog… er, juice on the end of a boathook, and I a mug of sparkling apple. Each of us said the other's drink was revolting. We drank the lot.
textes.Trois ans à porter le charbon. Pas un mo: Three years carrying coal. Not a word from him. One morning, he set a hammer on the anvil, handle turned towards me. He said: “One blow.” I struck. One single blow. He looked at the iron, for a long time. He grunted. The next day, he let me strike two.
Three years is a lot of time.
textes.Trois cafés le matin chez Gisèle, sans d: Three coffees in the morning at Gisèle's, without a word: I'm thinking. The hotel lounge in the afternoon, my charts spread out on the rug. The bench at the lookout at sunset, watching the west. Pauline found my drawing under the pillow: the whole town knows. Nadine brings me the letters from the university. And I can't swim. A mere detail.
textes.Trois caisses de poivre des îles, ma fil: Three crates of island pepper, my girl. And a parrot.
textes.Trois carottes avant la course, pas une: Three carrots before the race, not one more. The fourth weighs you down.
textes.Trois carottes, pas une de plus. Départ: Three carrots, not one more. Off like an arrow. Grisou says “this time” every time. Éclair trains at night, in secret; I've seen her by lantern light. My niece Mochi wants to be like me, she jumps the hop. Grelot makes fun of my carrots. And me, I train. Morning, noon, evening. All the time.
You've been telling me that for three hundred years.
textes.Trois cents ans sans réclamation. Tu es: Three hundred years without a complaint. You're my favourite customer.
textes.Trois cents ans à frapper le fer. J'ai f: Three hundred years hammering iron. I forged the king's axe, the city gates, and Dagna's spoon. She says it's my masterpiece. Hmph.
textes.Trois cents noix de coco par semaine, mo: Three hundred coconuts a week, my friend! Kevin next door, saving people who aren't drowning. Théo in front, building castles. Hugo, who dug with my ladle until midnight. My neighbour Rose, whose bougainvillea ate my roof. And in the evening, when I close, I go for a drink at Toni's. Somebody has to serve me one, after all.
textes.Trois cents photos en dix jours. Deux ne: Three hundred photos in ten days. Two in focus: I know them by heart. And then one evening, I left it at the lookout, photographing the sunset. The painter saw it and left it there. What a disaster! And Théo lost his kite on the hill, and I haven't got the legs to climb up there. What a week, oh my.
textes.Trois colliers. Et toi, tu as donné comb: Three necklaces. And you, how many bananas did you give away?
textes.Trois compagnons, c'est déjà une petite: Three companions is already quite a crowd! You'll have to send one to rest at the Guild first.
textes.Trois contrats à la fois, pas plus : c'e: Three contracts at a time, no more: that's the rule (and Églantine knows it by heart).
textes.Trois coudées, ma lumière. Comme annoncé: Three cubits, my light. As advertised.
textes.Trois cristaux, deux fragments, quatre e: Three crystals, two fragments, four gears, two rolls of sailcloth! (She disappears into the hangar. Sounds of wrenches, glowing welding, a “clack”, an “oops”, another “clack”.) It's coming along! The hull is done, the engine is purring. Now I need the navigation: the Professor's hologram chip, and a star chart from Sextant.
textes.Trois dents de requin ! Bien pointues… A: Three shark teeth! Nice and sharp… Wait. … There! Atlantean flippers, ribbed with mother-of-pearl. Put them on and zoom off like a dolphin!
textes.Trois dés chacun. Le plus gros total gag: Three dice each. Highest total wins, and three of a kind beats everything. How much are you betting?
textes.Trois dés d'os qui roulent un peu… mieux: Three bone dice that roll a little… better than the others, sold on the sly by Isaac Cinq-Doigts. You can play dice with them. But if the pirate across from you notices (one time in three), it's a brawl.
textes.Trois flammes rouges qui ne brûlent pas: Three red flames that don't burn! A dry voice in the dark: “Our torches are… whole?” The Lords are furious, but the door opens.
textes.Trois flammes. Le sol vibre très légèrem: Three flames. The floor trembles ever so slightly.
textes.Trois fois depuis ce matin, ma voix d'or: Three times since this morning, my golden voice!
textes.Trois fois l'archipel, Bernard !: Three times round the archipelago, Bernard!
textes.Trois fois. Elle ne bouge pas, elle. Pas: Three times. She doesn't move. Not like Titou.
Three times. I wasn't going anywhere.
textes.Trois fois. La reine m'a dit que l'arbre: Three times. The queen told me the tree was sick. I hope someone will help it…
textes.Trois galettes de maïs encore chaudes, c: Three corn cakes still warm, cooked on Ix Chab's clay griddle, folded around a few beans and some chilli. Restores two hearts.
textes.Trois graffitis ! Pigment va être fière: Three graffitis! Pigment is going to be proud of you.
textes.Trois graffitis sur les murs du Boucan: Three graffiti on the walls of Boucan
textes.Trois grands tournesols du jardin de Mam: Three tall sunflowers from Granny Sunflower's garden, tied with a yellow ribbon. They turn their heads towards you, as if towards the sun.
textes.Trois grognements, trois paires d'yeux d: Three growls, three pairs of glowing eyes… CERBÈRE, the three-headed dog, rises from his straw! (They say he loves honey cakes. One per head.)
textes.Trois gâteaux pour trois têtes, retiens: Three cakes for three heads, remember that. If you only give two, the third head sulks, and a sulking head, on a dog that size… Ébène says it ends badly. I say it ends in a fight. Same thing, with fewer cakes.
Three hours with the comb, every morning.
textes.Trois heures pour tatouer son poulpe, av: Three hours to tattoo his octopus, with a hiccup every ten seconds. Every tentacle has a little bump where a hiccup was. At the end, an octopus with eight wavy arms, very nice work. Scarlett looked and said: “A magnificent horse!” Tonneau believed her. I shouted “IT'S AN OCTOPUS!” Nobody listened to me. I'll never forgive Scarlett.
textes.Trois heures, c'est bien ça ?: Three hours, that's right, isn't it?
textes.Trois jours d'anneaux, un par un. Ursule: Three days of rings, one by one. Ursule hands you the chain mail: heavy, supple, cold. “Put it on. Stand straight. Good.”
textes.Trois lampes, trois « clac » : la porte: Three lamps, three “clacks”: the south door sinks into the floor with a rumble. The stairs lead down to the Underground Lake.
textes.Trois lettres, Capitaine ! Et un bonjour: Three letters, Captain! And a hello from the lighthouse!
textes.Trois mille nuits à vérifier que notre l: Three thousand nights checking that our moon stays full. It does. Four thousand two hundred and twelve stars. Or thirteen. I write to Céleste Lunette, the astronomer in Cliquetis: she says our moon is an illusion. Forty nights ago I saw a star fall into the big pond. And the Night of the False Alarm… the monster was me. Hoo. Sorry again.
textes.Trois minutes, Lirael. Comme à notre nai: Three minutes, Lirael. Like when we were born.
textes.Trois minutes, c'est un fait ! On ne cor: Three minutes is a fact! You don't correct facts.
textes.Trois mouettes, un nuage en forme de cha: Three seagulls, a cloud shaped like a sock, and no ships.
textes.Trois noix de coco contre un seau de gla: Three coconuts for a bucket of ice cubes?
textes.Trois noix de coco, et mon punch revit !: Three coconuts, and my punch lives again! The jungle boat hasn't come by. You can find some at Colette's, or under the coconut palms in the jungle.
textes.Trois paniers ! Des poireaux, des courge: Three baskets! Leeks, squashes, potatoes, and... (He pulls out a bitten carrot.) A carrot. Just one. I told you I'd be counting! Ha ha! (He pours everything into the pot.) Tonight, everybody's soup! Because it's made by everybody, and for everybody. And a little bit by you.
textes.Trois perles parfaites ! Tu as l'œil, {s: Three perfect pearls! You have a good eye, {surnom}. Here's thirty-five coins. And if you ever want a cloak, I'll weave you one.
textes.Trois personnes sont assises en silence: Three people sit in silence on colored mats. A soft voice murmurs: “Breathe…”
textes.Trois petits Moaïs, alignés, très concen: Three little Moai, lined up, concentrating hard, make a grimace. Well… they try.
Three coins for the temple offering. The gods are not stingy, but the temple has lamps to fill.
textes.Trois pièces, mon cœur. La brume de la b: Three coins, my dear. The mist in the ball doesn't clear for nothing.
Three coins. It's got a spot.
textes.Trois pour toi, deux pour moi, un pour G: Three for you, two for me, one for Gaston. That's family!
textes.Trois prix, Héloïse ? Pour une seule mac: Three prizes, Héloïse? For a single unbeatable machine?
Three rays, Faelar. And a reflection.
textes.Trois rochers. Et j'ai une pierre pour t: Three boulders. And I've got a stone for you.
textes.Trois semaines à quai. La nuit, mes homm: Three weeks at the quay. At night, my men search the caves with lanterns. Mâchefer counts the days until the end of summer, grinding his teeth. In the evening, Mama Lou's rum. By day, the weaver, who's weaving me a carpet… a very special one. Old Fatima, who answers me in riddles. And the caïd, up there, keeping watch on me. By the captain's beard, I'm very well surrounded.
Three centuries behind. On the bias.
Three centuries and three minutes. I know.
textes.Trois siècles, et toujours pas réveillés: Three centuries, and still never awake at the same time.
textes.Trois tapis de l'oasis. J'ai parlé quatr: Three carpets from the oasis. I talked for four hours, my brother: the wool, the tribes, my grandmother, the wedding, the rain that never comes. Mbarek drank his tea. At the end, I named my price. He said: “No.” One word! I paid his and collapsed onto the carpets. He let me rest on them. That was kind of him, all the same.
Three glasses of tea! You feel refreshed.
textes.Trois verres, c'est la tradition ! Le qu: Three glasses, that's the tradition! The fourth is for the greedy ones… Come back tomorrow, I'll make a new pot.
textes.Trois victoires d'affilée à ma table, et: Three wins in a row at my table, and I'll give you my most precious possession. Nobody's ever done it. Nobody.
textes.Trois voiliers ce matin. Dont un mal ama: Three sailboats this morning. One of them badly moored.
textes.Trois étoiles de mer orange, au fond de: Three orange starfish, at the bottom of the bay, in front of the beach. Bring all three back up and I'll recognise you as a true diver. No mask needed, just breath. Go on, champ!
textes.Trois, Ambroise. Votre automate saura pa: Three, Ambroise. Your automaton will learn to share.
textes.Trois, Tiyi ! Et tu n'en as gardé aucun: Three, Tiyi! And you didn't keep a single one!
Three, then. Go on, put it down there, you old fibber.
textes.Trois, et la meilleure parle de toi, Aby: Three, and the best one is about you, Abyssos.
textes.Trois, un, deux… Un déclic, puis un long: Three, one, two… A click, then a long clatter: the round door starts turning on itself, like a gear… and rolls aside!
textes.Trois. Et les jumelles, demain matin, co: Three. And the binoculars, tomorrow morning, as usual.
textes.Trois… quatre… cinq moutons… six… un mou: Three… four… five sheep… six… a sheep riding a bike…
textes.Trompé de porte… C'est vrai qu'elles se: Wrong door… It's true they all look alike on this street. Go on, off you go. And close it properly behind you!
textes.Trop bas pour t'envoler : l'Alouette ne: Too low to take off: the Alouette only launches from a high point. You need twelve metres of empty space beneath you: a cliff edge, a tower, the launch pad of the Wing Workshop… or jump first, and unfold it mid-fall!
textes.Trop bien ! Et il cache des noisettes ?: So cool! And does he hide hazelnuts? Or she? You've got to teach them, hazelnuts are super important!
textes.Trop bien ! J'ai les jambes en compote m: So good! My legs are jelly but I'm not stopping.
textes.Trop calme ? Peuchère ! Mais c'est notre: Too quiet? Good heavens! But quiet is our pride and joy! Well. I hear you. I'll think about a second harbour festival. With paper lanterns. I'm making a note.
textes.Trop chaud ? Ah, ça… je ne peux pas fair: Too hot? Ah, well… I can't put rain to the vote, I've tried. But I can decree shade! One more plane tree in the square. Promise. Before the end of the year.
textes.Trop loin du rivage : approchez un ponto: Too far from shore: get close to a jetty or a beach.
textes.Trop long… La Grande Course est finie sa: Too slow… The Great Race is over without you. Come back to the Games Clearing for a rematch.
textes.Trop sucré ? Moi ? Jamais ! Il est parfa: Too sweet? Me? Never! It's perfect! Perfect!
textes.Trop tard ! Il est dans ma poche !: Too late! It's in my pocket!
textes.Trop tard ! Les anneaux s'éteignent un i: Too late! The rings go dark for a moment, then light up again. We start over from the first.
textes.Trop tard, Théophraste. Elle a déjà son: Too late, Théophraste. It already has its ribbon.
Too fast? I'll slow down, madame.
textes.Trop à faire ! Les jeunes croient toujou: Too busy! Young people always think that. The world can wait an hour, little one. It's used to it. A cup of lime-blossom tea tonight, and off to bed.
textes.Troquer la fiole de brume avec Ursule, l: Swap the vial of mist with Ursule, the blacksmith (the bears' forge, south-east of the village)
textes.Troquer la plume de lune avec Pivoine, l: Swap the moon feather with Pivoine, the herbalist, at the Herb Stall (halfway up the Mother Oak)
textes.Troquer le caillou-qui-chante avec Pomme: Swap the singing-stone with Pomme-de-Pin, the bridge carpenter (on the western tree in the morning, near the big pond in the afternoon)
textes.Troquer le gland d'or avec Plumette, à l: Swap the golden acorn with Plumette, at the Post Office, right at the top of the Mother Oak
textes.Trouve d'abord. Tu verras qui doit quoi: Find it first. Then you'll see who owes what to whom.
textes.Trouver Brioche, la chatte rousse et bla: Find Brioche, the ginger-and-white cat, on the harbour rooftops (near the fishmonger's and the harbour master's office), show her the ball of wool and let her come to you: she's the one who chooses
textes.Trouver Monsieur Paille, l'épouvantail,: Find Mr Paille, the scarecrow, in the middle of the White Meadows (east of the village), and take the pot of red at his feet
textes.Trouver deux morceaux de la carte : dans: Find two pieces of the map: in the keep of the Cursed Fort (on the eastern point) and in the graveyard mausoleum (on the western hill) — watch out for skeletons, especially at night
textes.Trouver enfin ce qui manque au gâteau de: To finally find what the mooncake is missing, and see Mother Moon finish her slice without saying “almost”. Just “mm”. A single “mm”, and I'll close the bakery for a day to celebrate!
textes.Trouver enfin la réponse de Faelar. Et p: To finally find Faelar's answer. And then, that very same day, set him a riddle he'll spend three hundred years working out. By the roots, it'll be delicious.
textes.Trouver l'Atlantide et rallumer son Gran: Find Atlantis and rekindle its Great Crystal
textes.Trouver l'entrée du temple sous le villa: Find the entrance to the temple under the village (a hidden trapdoor)
textes.Trouver l'herbe qui guérit la peur. On d: To find the herb that cures fear. They say it grows at the edge of the ponds, on moonless nights.
textes.Trouver l'objet. Celui qui manque à ma c: To find the object. The one missing from my collection, the one after which I'd never want to buy another thing. I've been looking for it for four thousand objects, my dear. I'll know it's the one when the manor falls silent.
textes.Trouver la Bergerie du Vent, au pied du: Find the Wind Sheepfold, at the foot of Stoneheart south-east of Cliquetis, burn its brambles with the Flame (key 2 then X; in VR, B), and take the Bronze Seal
textes.Trouver la Souche Creuse, au fond du Boi: Find the Hollow Stump, deep in the Hatching Wood (to the west, at the end of the woodland path), and take the pot of green from it
textes.Trouver la fin de la chanson de mon père: To find the end of my father's song. And sing it once on the square, so loud that the fishermen of Carène look up from their nets.
textes.Trouver la rose d'aube, la fleur des vie: To find the dawn rose, the flower from the old songs. The elders say it doesn't exist. I'll find it anyway, and I'll put it in Nimiel's hair on festival day.
textes.Trouver le calme au Jardin Zen: Find peace in the Zen Garden
textes.Trouver le grand château de sable de l'A: Find the big Averse sandcastle, at the far end of the White Strand (to the west), and take the pot of yellow at the foot of its tower
textes.Trouver trois lots de pièces de vélo cac: Find three batches of bike parts hidden in the Scrapyard (in the south-east of the island, under the scrap heaps)
textes.Trouver une première Perle de Lumière: Find a first Pearl of Light
textes.Trouvé ! Zut ! T'es trop fort. Tiens, po: Found! Darn! You're too good. Here, for the winner!
textes.Truffe ? Ce petit diable ? (Elle soupire: Truffe? That little devil? (She sighs, but she's smiling.) This morning I saw him go past Clovis's mill at a full gallop, snout in the grass. His little bell must have come off over there: I heard it jingle, then nothing. Find it. Truffe knows its jingle: when he hears it, he comes running. It's the snack-time bell. I used to shake it to call him when he was tiny. He's still tiny, mind you. Except for his appetite.
textes.Truffe a le groin d'or : une truffe tout: Truffle has a golden snout: a fresh truffle just for you!
textes.Truffe accourt en couinant de joie, la q: Truffle rushes over squealing with joy, tail in a corkscrew.
textes.Truffe frétille de la queue au groin, fa: Truffle wiggles from tail to snout, does a little hop for joy and presses his nose against your hand. Oink!
textes.Truffe monte dans la barque (elle tangue: Truffle climbs into the boat (it rocks a little) and sits at the front, snout in the wind.
textes.Truffe renifle, renifle… et creuse comme: Truffle sniffs and sniffs… and digs like mad! He brings you a black truffle that smells of the forest.
textes.Truffe rentre à la maison en grognant do: Truffle goes home grunting softly. There must be apples there.
textes.Truffe, le plus petit des cochons de la: Truffe, the smallest of the pigs on Old Man Gaubert's farm, pink and black, runs away every day to root around in the woods at the edge of the Southern Fields. He digs up truffles… and the turnips. Old Man Gaubert, with his knees, can't catch him any more, and his little bell has fallen off. He's looking for someone who likes walking to take him along.
textes.Trèfle a les oreilles de sa grand-mère L: Trèfle has her grandmother Luzerne's ears, plus the flour. Every evening she brings me her mooncake, and every evening she looks at me the way you look at the sky before rain.
textes.Trèfle, c'est la femme de mon meilleur a: Trèfle is my best friend's wife. His widow, people say. I don't like that word. Let's say: my old friend, who makes the best bread on the island and still laughs. That's what matters most.
Trèfle is my friend and my baker. She smells of flour and honey, and when she's sad, she smells a little of salt. I pass by every day just as the oven opens. The nose, always the nose.
textes.Trèfle. Pain de carotte, gâteau de carot: Trèfle. Carrot bread, carrot cake, carrot with carrot. At the last Great Swap, she turned down my sardine. All right, I'd turned down her bread first. That's not the point.
Very! … If I can remember it.
textes.Très bien ! Alors, cette bulle, Basile ?: Very well! So, this bubble, Basile?
textes.Très bien ! J'ai trouvé ce matin un cail: Very well! This morning I found a pebble that looks exactly like my Aunt Ursule. Except for the hat.
textes.Très bien ! La pêche était bonne. J'ai p: Very good! Fithing wath good. I caught a fith and a boot. The boot wath frether.
textes.Très bien ! Le feu tire bien, l'acier ch: Very well! The fire draws well, the steel sings. What more could you ask? A fizzy drink. There.
Very well! The wind smells of honey.
textes.Très bien ! Les champignons de lune ont: Very well! The moon mushrooms came up last night. I heard them.
textes.Très bien ! Ulfa a mis un nouveau tonnea: Very well! Ulfa has tapped a new barrel.
textes.Très bien, Citlali. Et je me suis réveil: Very well, Citlali. And I woke up at midnight.
textes.Très bien. J'ai inventé une machine à ra: Very well. I invented a bolt-collecting machine. It ate Zigomar's broom. But it works.
Very well. Don't say a word.
textes.Très bien. Prête pour la revanche ?: Very well. Ready for a rematch?
textes.Très chaud ! Ho ho ! Une vraie petite fl: Very hot! Ho ho! A real little flame! The second pool, the one that sings when you get in. You'll come out red as a demon.
textes.Très cher ! Voilà un vrai client ! Le qu: A fortune! Now there's a real customer! The quetzal is the bird of the gods, its feather is worth gold. I have one. Almost real. No, I'm joking. Real. Almost.
textes.Très faim, très faim… Un jour, ta faim,: Very hungry, very hungry… One day, I'll see that hunger of yours walk by.
Very off-key. Ulfa would be jealous.
textes.Très haut ! Et tes pieds, ils reviennent: Very high! And your feet, do they come back down?
textes.Très loin ? Combien, très loin ? Une lie: Very far? How far is very far? One league? Two? … Right, we'll have a contest, from the top of the mast. The loser scrubs the deck. I've already got the bucket.
textes.Très mal ? Ha. Ça s'apprend. Moi, j'ai a: Very badly? Ha. It can be learned. I learned on a quay, with barrels for partners. They never complained.
textes.Très mystérieux, voisine. Très, très mys: Very mysterious, neighbour. Very, very mysterious.
textes.Très satisfait ! Ah, citoyen ! Je le not: Very satisfied! Ah, citizen! I'm noting it in my register. It's the first favourable answer of the year. I'll have you decorated. As soon as I have a medal.
textes.Très stable, oui. Et il tourne bien, sur: Very stable, yes. And above all, it turns really well.
textes.Très vite ? Ha ! On verra ça sous les ar: Very fast? Ha! We'll see about that under the arches. Pépin has a stopwatch, it never lies. Neither do I, by the way. I'm just faster.
textes.Tu VOLES sur l'aigle du cratère ?! Mes c: You FLY on the crater eagle?! My goats watch you go by with their mouths open. So do I.
textes.Tu agites la plume. « MILLE SABORDS ! »: You wave the feather. “BLISTERING BARNACLES!” cries a voice in the distance. Or was it you who said it?
textes.Tu agites ton mouchoir rouge vers le cie: You wave your red handkerchief at the sky… A purr of propellers answers, far away. The Albatros is coming!
textes.Tu agrippes la chaîne et te hisses, mail: You grab the chain and haul yourself up, link after link…
textes.Tu aimais les dragons. J'ai retrouvé cel: You loved dragons. I've remembered the one about the dragon who collected spoons. It's a long one. Sit down.
textes.Tu allumes la torche… elle flambe, se co: You light the torch… it blazes, burns down, and falls to ashes. A laugh in the dark: “Give us back our torch WHOLE, tomorrow morning!” (It would have to shine without burning. The Twins had used red feathers.)
textes.Tu archives quoi, aujourd'hui ? Mes erre: What are you archiving today? My mistakes?
textes.Tu arrives de l'ouest. Tes bottes senten: You've come from the west. Your boots smell of moorland and salt. Brume, tracker of Ramure. I read tracks the way others read books.
textes.Tu as PERDU ma canne ?! Sapristi… Bon. J: You LOST my rod?! Blimey… Right. I've got another one, cut from the same bamboo. Don't tell anyone: the other one was the real one.
textes.Tu as abattu des golems. Pour un grand,: You brought down golems. For a tall one, that's… decent. Very decent. Hmph.
textes.Tu as abattu le Crabe-Roi ?! … Tu me rev: You took down the King Crab?! … Will you sell me its shell? No? Shame. I'd have made shields out of it.
textes.Tu as aidé mes sujets dehors. Bramm, Bor: You helped my subjects outside. Bramm, Borin, Dagna… A king does not forget.
textes.Tu as aidé {qn} ! {Il} me l'a raconté. J: You helped {qn}! {Il} told me all about it. I won't forget it, {surnom}.
textes.Tu as aimé ? J'ai fait une chanson sur t: Did you like it? I wrote a song about your bougainvilleas!
textes.Tu as appris à te taire ?: Have you learnt to keep quiet?
textes.Tu as assez de cristaux de soufre, cette: Do you have enough sulphur crystals this time?
textes.Tu as dit « promis » avec des petits poi: You said “promise” with little dots after it.
textes.Tu as dit « rien » trois fois. C'est sus: You said “nothing” three times. That's suspicious.
textes.Tu as du fromage ? Même un petit bout ?: Got any cheese? Even a little bit? Even a whiff of cheese?
textes.Tu as déjà creusé ici. Essaie un peu plu: You've already dug here. Try a bit further away.
textes.Tu as déjà fait ta part ! Et tu as encor: You've already done your share! And you still have paint in your hair.
textes.Tu as déjà pris L'Hirondelle ? Le capita: Ever taken L'Hirondelle? Captain Léon toots the horn in rhythm if you ask him nicely.
textes.Tu as déjà pris trois tomates. Il faut e: You've already taken three tomatoes. You have to leave some for the sauce (and for the others).
textes.Tu as déjà pris un objet aujourd'hui. De: You've already taken an item today. Tomorrow, the table will have changed!
textes.Tu as déjà ta thermos, petit gourmand !: You already have your thermos, little glutton! Come back tomorrow, I'll make more.
textes.Tu as déjà vu de l'eau, ou seulement du: Have you ever seen water, or only rum?
textes.Tu as déterré le coffre de la Mouette !: You dug up the Seagull's chest! I always said so: the map was right. That rock was in the wrong place, that's all.
textes.Tu as déterré le coffre de la Mouette. J: You dug up the Seagull's chest. I… I've got nothing to say. Actually I do: sixty percent. No? Fine.
textes.Tu as encore offert le quatrième ?: Did you give away the fourth again?
You've forgotten the ending again, Tilleul.
textes.Tu as encore parlé à ta barque ?: Have you been talking to your boat again?
textes.Tu as entendu ta voix, ce matin ?: Did you hear your voice this morning?
textes.Tu as eu l'occasion de lui parler, depui: Have you had a chance to talk to them since?
textes.Tu as fait la connaissance de {qn}, il p: You've met {qn}, I hear. What do you think?
textes.Tu as fini de la rater, oui. Hmpf. Montr: Finished botching it, you mean. Hmpf. Show me.
textes.Tu as fini tes calculs, petite ?: Have you finished your calculations, little one?
textes.Tu as frappé {qn} ? Ça ne se fait pas. T: You hit {qn}? That's just not done. Everyone's talking about it.
textes.Tu as frappé {qn} ?! On m'a tout raconté: You hit {qn}?! I've heard everything. You've got some nerve coming to talk to me.
textes.Tu as frappé {qn}, à ce qu'on dit. Je ne: You hit {qn}, so they say. I'm not saying it was deserved. I'm not saying it wasn't.
textes.Tu as gagné un poney en chocolat. Il fon: You won a chocolate pony. It melts fast: hurry!
textes.Tu as gardé la lavande sous ton oreiller: Did you keep the lavender under your pillow? And the bad dreams? Come and sit on the bench, if you want to talk about them.
textes.Tu as goûté le thé de Mamie Kiku ? Il ré: Have you tried Mamie Kiku's tea? It warms you down to your toes.
textes.Tu as gâté {qn}, à ce qu'on raconte. Ceu: Word is you spoiled {qn}. Anyone who's kind to my folks is welcome at my place.
textes.Tu as jugé, le grand. Un nain n'oublie j: You've passed judgement, tall one. A dwarf never forgets a judgement. Nor the person who gave it. … Come back anyway, go on.
textes.Tu as l'air soucieuse, ce soir, mon enfa: You look worried this evening, my child.
textes.Tu as l'air épuisé, {surnom}. Assieds-to: You look exhausted, {surnom}. Sit down under the leaves. Here, nothing can reach you.
textes.Tu as l'impression que les petits Moaïs: You feel like the little Moai at the back have moved. But no. … Did they?
You have your head on upside down.
textes.Tu as le nez fin ! Pas de soupe ! Les pa: You've got a good nose! No soup! The vegetable baskets from the Shared Gardens haven't arrived. Radis prepared them this morning, but he had to leave them in the plots: he was interrogating his carrots. My pot is empty, and an empty pot echoes. Go to the Shared Gardens, east of town, near the Boxes, and bring me three baskets. Don't eat them on the way! Well... one carrot. Just one. I'll be counting.
textes.Tu as les deux yeux de corail ! Il ne re: You have both coral eyes! All that's left is to give them back to the Great Moai, in the middle of the Elders' Plateau.
textes.Tu as mangé, ma petite Écrou ?: Have you eaten, my little Écrou?
You measured like a postman, Marcel.
textes.Tu as mis le pied sur l'île des nains ?!: You set foot on the dwarves' island?! Me, in sixty years at sea, never. Bring me back a pebble from their volcano so I can show it to Octave.
textes.Tu as mis tes gants ?: Have you got your gloves on?
textes.Tu as mis tes gants, au moins ?: Did you at least put your gloves on?
You wrote it down. Of course.
textes.Tu as offert {objet} à {qn} ? Tout le mo: You gave {objet} to {qn}? Everyone knows {il} can't stand that. I'm still laughing.
textes.Tu as pensé à une plume avant de dormir: Did you think of a feather before you slept? No? Try tonight! Just one. Feathers are patient.
textes.Tu as peur du noir, {surnom} ? Là-dessou: Are you scared of the dark, {surnom}? Down there, it's very, very dark.
textes.Tu as plongé jusqu'à la ville engloutie: You dived all the way down to the sunken city?! My grandfather was right! I have to redraw all my maps. All of them!
textes.Tu as pris la fuite… Ils s'en souviendro: You ran away… They'll remember that.
textes.Tu as pris le temps de t'asseoir au Cerc: Did you take the time to sit at the Circle? Is your first memory still sleeping? Leave it be. It will wake when it wants to.
textes.Tu as pris ta tisane de tilleul ? Tu as: Did you have your lime-blossom tea? You've still got owl eyes. The world can wait, I told you.
textes.Tu as quitté la Grande Course… Les coure: You left the Great Race… The runners head back to the Games Clearing.
You're right not to judge too quickly.
textes.Tu as raison, mon fils, je disais justem: You're right, son, I was just saying…
textes.Tu as rapporté deux runes de golem. La p: You brought back two golem runes. The gate of Forgefer opened for you.
textes.Tu as regardé dans les branches hautes ?: Did you look in the high branches?
textes.Tu as relu un de tes préférés, depuis ?: Have you reread one of your favourites since? I reread chapter twelve. Again. It's still good.
textes.Tu as remarqué. (Elle pose sa main sur l: You noticed. (She places her hand on yours; it's light as a leaf.) The bridges are flickering, the fountain can't choose between two planets, and the Spire beats more weakly. The Heart is fading, my little star. It's very old: it came from Ondelune with us. Last night, three shards broke off and fell onto the island. Without them, it beats like a tired heart. And if the Heart stops… (She smiles.) We won't fly away. We'll fall. Gently, I hope. I don't like big falls at my age. Go see Volt, at the foot of the Spire. He pretends everything is fine. He knows everything. Help him.
textes.Tu as remonté une vieille botte ? Montre: You reeled in an old boot? Show me! … It's mine! I've been looking for it since the shipwreck. Bring it to me, please.
textes.Tu as rencontré Aëlwen ? Elle m'a soigné: Have you met Aëlwen? She healed me when I was little. Her potions are bitter, but they work.
textes.Tu as répondu bien vite, toi…: That was a very quick answer, you…
textes.Tu as réussi ! Mais attention… la Reine: You did it! But careful… the Bramble Queen is waiting for us at the end of this corridor. I'll stay close to you.
textes.Tu as senti la mèche, Fatima ?: Did you smell the wick, Fatima?
What you mostly are is three times my price.
textes.Tu as surtout une tisane à boire, Faelar: What you mostly have is a tea to drink, Faelar.
You shot like a klutz, Marcel.
textes.Tu as tout ce qu'il faut. On le fait ?: You have everything you need. Shall we do it?
textes.Tu as traversé le Lac Noir ! Derrière to: You crossed the Black Lake! Behind you, the false slabs sink for good: the path of the Ancients stays marked out.
textes.Tu as traversé le gouffre ! Sous tes pie: You crossed the chasm! Under your feet, a flagstone sinks a notch: the grate at the back creaks open.
textes.Tu as trouvé Pixel et Quark ! Va dire à: You found Pixel and Quark! Go and tell Pixel the game is over.
textes.Tu as un cœur d'elfe, {surnom}. Je garde: You have an elf's heart, {surnom}. I'll keep {dernier_cadeau} close to me.
textes.Tu as un péché mignon ?: Do you have a guilty pleasure?
textes.Tu as une histoire à me raconter ?: Do you have a story to tell me?
textes.Tu as une mine affreuse, {surnom}. Tu t': You look dreadful, {surnom}. Did you pick a fight with a rock spire? Eat something, for goodness' sake.
textes.Tu as une tête de déterré, {surnom}. Ass: You look like something dug up from a grave, {surnom}. Sit down. And eat something before you fall off my ladder.
You look like someone who eats honey bread. That's my way of saying hello.
textes.Tu as une épée ! Je peux la toucher ? No: You've got a sword! Can I touch it? No? Just a little bit? Fine.
textes.Tu as vaincu le Serpent des Abysses ?! L: You defeated the Serpent of the Abyss?! The elders of my people will talk about it for a hundred years. Well… a hundred years isn't that long.
textes.Tu as vaincu le Serpent des Abysses… Bar: You defeated the Abyssal Serpent… Barnabé will make a forty-verse song out of it. Me, I'll just say: well done, {surnom}.
textes.Tu as vaincu un grand serpent, là-haut ?: You defeated a great serpent, up there? Hmph. Serpents are easy. Try brambles.
textes.Tu as vu ? Au milieu des aurores, à trav: You saw? In the middle of the auroras, through my new lenses... (He lets you look.) There. A tiny little star, at the edge of the sky. Ondelune's sun. You can only see it on aurora nights, when the sky is washed clean. I wanted someone from down below to see it too. Now there are two of us. Here: an astral crystal, and a star elixir. The crystal is for your machines. The elixir is for the evenings when you feel far from home.
textes.Tu as vu ? Tu as VU ? J'ai regardé le co: Did you see? Did you SEE? I watched the whole concert. Sitting in the grass. Without carrying a single crate. (He laughs, a real laugh.) Twenty years of touring, and it's on a little island that I got my first concert back. Thank you. Here: a share of the roadies' fund, two Spleen chocolates, and a title. Not an official one. We voted for it, by show of hands, last night. Unanimous, minus Grésil, who was asleep.
textes.Tu as vu Nimiel ? Elle est encore montée: Did you see Nimiel? She climbed onto the footbridge with no hands again.
textes.Tu as vu l'obélisque devant la Porte ? I: Have you seen the obelisk in front of the Gate? It goes all the way up to the surface! They say its tip touches the sky. Is that true?
textes.Tu as vu la Fontaine de lune ? La nuit,: Have you seen the Moon Fountain? At night, its crystal lights up all by itself.
textes.Tu as vu la baleine, aujourd'hui ?: Did you see the whale today?
textes.Tu as vu la grande porte, au pied du Cœu: Have you seen the great gate, at the foot of Stoneheart? I've been there! Well, nearly. As far as the first rock. Then I got hungry.
textes.Tu as vu la lumière, ce matin ? L'Arbre-: Did you see the light this morning? The Mother Tree was all golden.
textes.Tu as vu la plage ? Sable fin, eau turqu: Seen the beach? Fine sand, turquoise water, and a lifeguard with arms like hams. Long live Port-Azur!
textes.Tu as vu la tête de pierre à moitié ente: Have you seen the stone head half-buried west of the gorge? Clou won't go near it. He says it echoes, right next to it. Take a shovel… and a sword.
textes.Tu as vu le Grand Moaï, au milieu ? Il a: Have you seen the Great Moai, in the middle? He has a staircase in his belly!
textes.Tu as vu le canal ? Les enfants y font f: Have you seen the canal? The children float little mother-of-pearl boats on it.
textes.Tu as vu les passerelles ? Moi, je n'y m: Have you seen the walkways? I never go up there with a tray of loaves. Once, just once…
textes.Tu as vu ma queue ? Elle fait des tire-b: Did you see my tail? It makes corkscrews when I'm happy.
textes.Tu as vu mes champignons qui brillent ?: Have you seen my glowing mushrooms? The fairies make them grow. They take you up there, above the clouds… Ask me, if you want to travel.
textes.Tu as vu quelque chose, d'en haut, ou tu: Did you see anything from up there, or were you still asleep?
textes.Tu as vu ta baleine, ce matin ?: Did you see your whale this morning?
See that, Théo? I've nearly finished.
textes.Tu attends qu'on t'ouvre, toi. Moi, j'at: You wait for someone to open. I wait for someone to knock. We'd make a good door, the two of us.
textes.Tu attends que ça passe. Hm. Ça passe so: You wait for it to pass. Hm. It often does, true. But not always. Promise me you'll come and see me when it doesn't.
textes.Tu aurais encore un champignon des fées: Would you happen to have another fairy mushroom?
textes.Tu aurais une graine dorée ?: Would you have a golden seed?
textes.Tu avais raison : il chante encore. J'ai: You were right: he's still singing. I've been thinking about what you said. I'm considering helping him. A little.
textes.Tu bascules la louche géante dans la Mar: You tip the giant ladle into the Cooking Pot, blow for a long time, and taste… Mmm! A perfect tomato sauce: garlic, basil, a hint of sugar. You fill a little jar.
textes.Tu boucles la ceinture et tu bombes le t: You buckle the belt and puff out your chest. Somewhere, Tom the Fiddler launches into the last verse of his song.
textes.Tu boucles les sangles de la selle naine: You buckle the straps of the dwarven saddle. Ventaile rises, proud, and offers you a golden feather. She is yours, and you are hers.
You move: the line goes back up.
textes.Tu branches la vieille guitare et tu t'a: You plug in the old guitar and step up to the amp… EEEEEEEEEEEEE! A terrible squeal: it's the Larsen effect! (That's where the island's name comes from.)
textes.Tu chanteras la marée, ce soir, Nausicaa: Will you sing the tide tonight, Nausicaa?
You sing too slowly, big sister.
textes.Tu cherches de vrais pirates ? Va au nor: Looking for real pirates? Go north, far north of Port-Azur: Balafre Island. Port-Coutelas. Over there, one wrong word and it's a brawl. I left two teeth and a reputation there. I'm not going back.
textes.Tu chevauches Ventaile ! Mon arrière-gra: You ride Ventaile! My great-grandfather used to say the Sky Kings came down on eagles to drink our fizz. I didn't believe him. … Bring me back a feather from their castle.
textes.Tu connais du monde, ici ?: Do you know many people here?
textes.Tu connais l'histoire de Fanny qui a ren: You know the story of Fanny knocking over two glasses and a Bastien? The Bastien is me. Her arm flew out, and I ended up sitting in the sea. She laughed, I laughed. Since that night, I carry her baskets of croissants from the jetty to the dance floor. I've never told her why. The Bastien never really got back up, {surnom}.
textes.Tu connais les champignons sauteurs ? On: Do you know about jumping mushrooms? We grew them for fun. Then the crystal spiders came, and we don't play anymore.
textes.Tu couds trop tard, Nolwenn. Je vois ta: You sew too late, Nolwenn. I see your lamp at night.
You sew too late. I can see your lamp.
textes.Tu crois aux fées, toi ? Pour de vrai, a: Do you believe in fairies? For real, with your heart?
textes.Tu crois qu'elle est grande, la mer ?: Do you think the sea is big?
textes.Tu crois qu'ils sont vrais, les champign: Do you think Lulu's mushrooms are real?
textes.Tu crois que je serai un grand sorcier,: You think I'll be a great wizard, you told me so! I think about it every time my spark goes off.
textes.Tu croques le champignon de Lulu… Il a u: You nibble Lulu's mushroom… It tastes of honey and rain. Everything starts to turn gently, the colours begin to sing, and the world dissolves into a golden light…
textes.Tu cueilles une tomate cœur-de-bœuf, lou: You pick an oxheart tomato, heavy and warm from the sun. It smells of green leaves and summer.
textes.Tu danses toujours aussi mal ? Entraîne-: Do you still dance as badly? Practise with a barrel. Don't tell anyone, but it works.
textes.Tu descends dans les Neuf Cercles ? Ébèn: Going down into the Nine Circles? Ébène says the hall of the Misers is full of weights to push. I weigh spices all day long: you push a weight with your legs, not your arms. And think before you push: you can't pull a weight back.
textes.Tu descends l'escalier de la Cathédrale-: You go down the stairs of the Forge Cathedral. The air grows cooler with every step… At the bottom, a door, and an inscription in letters of fire.
textes.Tu descends l'escalier de la vieille tou: You go down the stairs of the old tower. The steps sink into the dark, the air smells of moss and… jelly? Below, a hall, a set of rules, and a blue crystal.
You climb down the ladder… for a long time.
textes.Tu descends sous le Grand Temple. Sur le: You go down beneath the Great Temple. On the walls, Tlaloc and Huitzilopochtli watch you pass; somewhere below, a drum beats like a heart.
textes.Tu descends, longtemps, dans le ventre d: You descend, for a long time, into the belly of the Temple of Kukulkan. The air turns damp and cold. On the walls, the Feathered Serpent descends with you… and two young people, a blowgun in hand: the Twins.
textes.Tu dis presque depuis ce matin !: You've been saying almost since this morning!
You've been saying that for a hundred years, Grimli.
textes.Tu dis ça depuis cent cinquante ans. Man: You've been saying that for a hundred and fifty years. Eat.
textes.Tu dis ça depuis des mois, Tchoum !: You've been saying that for months, Tchoum!
textes.Tu dis ça tous les jours, Borin. Et tu r: You say that every day, Borin. And you go back for thirds.
textes.Tu disais que le temps efface tout. J'ai: You said time wipes everything out. I checked this morning: still nothing wiped. I'll keep you posted.
textes.Tu disais que tu dormirais trois cents a: You said you'd sleep for three hundred years… You look wide awake today. Faelar would be disappointed.
You said that about the ninetieth.
textes.Tu dormais dans la mine, Grimli. Comment: You were sleeping in the mine, Grimli. How would you know?
textes.Tu dors toujours par terre, toi ? Moi no: Still sleeping on the floor, are you? Me neither, eh. Obviously. Well… the boards under the counter are very nice. So they say.
textes.Tu dors un peu, maintenant ? Non ? J'ai: Sleeping a bit now? No? I've put a herbal tea aside for you, under the counter. For serious cases.
textes.Tu dors. Hm. Le sommeil aussi est un voy: You sleep. Hm. Sleep is a journey too: every night, the sun goes down to Xibalba, and it comes back. So do you. Sleep well, then.
textes.Tu débouches la fiole. Ça sent la vanill: You uncork the vial. It smells of vanilla and woodsmoke. You don't have horns… but you rub your temples a little, just to see.
textes.Tu décroches une botte de spaghettis bie: You take down a bundle of nicely dry spaghetti: hard as sticks, and smelling of wheat. (Recommendation no. 3: don't break them in two.)
textes.Tu dégages les gravats à la pelle, pierr: You clear the rubble with the shovel, stone after stone…
textes.Tu déplies l'Alouette, tu prends ton éla: You unfold the Alouette, take a run-up… three steps… and the void carries you. You're gliding!
textes.Tu déplies le Bail collectif. Trente et: You unfold the shared lease. Thirty-one signatures, a crested rat, a paw print (Sardine) and, right at the bottom, a tiny grey signature that trembles a little.
textes.Tu déroules le papyrus. Thot montre le c: You unroll the papyrus. Thoth points at the cartouche: the ibis, the eye of Horus, the sun. From top to bottom.
textes.Tu déroules ton diplôme. Le sceau de cir: You unroll your diploma. The wax seal is still smoking a little. You are a bachelor of flames, it says so.
textes.Tu effleures ta Clé d'étoile… Une lueur: You brush your Star Key… A glimmer streaks across the sky: the Star Glider is coming!
textes.Tu en as combien, de côté ?: How many have you got saved up?
textes.Tu en as déjà un ! Un seul suffit : les: You already have one! One is enough: bad dreams are afraid of dreamcatchers.
textes.Tu en as déjà un : il te reste à trouver: You already have one: you still need to find the other.
textes.Tu en as déjà un, non ?: You've already got one, haven't you?
textes.Tu en as déjà un, non ? Il ne faut pas ê: You already have one, don't you? Don't be greedy. Well, yes, a little, but not too much.
textes.Tu en as déjà un. Un seul suffit, s'il e: You already have one. One is enough, if it's dwarf-made.
textes.Tu en as déjà une. Une seule suffit : ce: You already have one. One is enough: what I forge doesn't break.
textes.Tu enfiles le poing de fer et tu frappes: You slip on the iron fist and punch your palm. Clang! That's going to hurt. Somebody.
textes.Tu enfiles un grand manteau de laine rou: You slip on a big, warm red wool coat. It smells a little of sulfur. (You never know: the inscription on the door insists.)
textes.Tu entends le violon ? Ça veut dire que: Can you hear the violin? That means dessert is coming.
You step into the mushroom circle. The glimmers spiral up around you…
textes.Tu es allé chez Octave ?! Il t'a dit que: You went to Octave's?! Did he tell you the shipwreck was my fault? It's not true. The map was right. It was the rock that was in the wrong place.
textes.Tu es allé chez les elfes ! Raconte ! Es: You went to the elves! Tell me everything! Do they have shells? No? What a strange people.
textes.Tu es blessé ! Assieds-toi. Non, ne disc: You're hurt! Sit down. No, don't argue. One sap potion, and you'll be good as new.
textes.Tu es descendu dans l'Arbre-Mère ?! Il y: You went down inside the Mother Tree?! Are there fairies? REAL ones? Take me next time! Please!
textes.Tu es déjà au royaume des fées. Garde ce: You're already in the fairy kingdom. Keep this mushroom for another time.
textes.Tu es déjà mon écuyer, mon brave ! Le pr: You're already my squire, brave one! A squire's first duty: come back to see me. You did. Well done.
You're the best neighbour in the sky.
textes.Tu es le 1 000 000e visiteur de ton prop: You are the 1,000,000th visitor of your very own journal!
You're the best stove on the island.
You're the most useful deaf man in Carène.
textes.Tu es loin de chez toi, voyageur. Je sui: You are far from home, traveller. I am Ix Kanul, high priestess of Kukulkan, the Feathered Serpent. At the equinoxes, his shadow comes down the temple stairs. Today, it is you who climb them. What do you seek?
textes.Tu es mon humain préféré. Enfin, après T: You're my favourite human. Well, after Tornade. And after the sausage seller.
textes.Tu es monté jusqu'ici ? Bienvenue sur ma: You climbed all the way up here? Welcome to my platform. Ilyria Fildaube. Mind the threads: they're everywhere, and they're mine.
textes.Tu es passé par la boulangerie, la mare,: You went by the bakery, the pond, and the market twice.
textes.Tu es passé par les mares du nord. Il y: You went past the northern ponds. There's mud on your left boot. Hello, {surnom}.
textes.Tu es pire qu'Amenemhat avec ses devinet: You're worse than Amenemhat with his riddles.
textes.Tu es toujours pressé. Et tu me dois deu: You're always in a hurry. And you owe me two feathers.
textes.Tu es tout pâle ! Mange. Non, pas de dis: You're so pale! Eat. No, no arguing: EAT.
textes.Tu es un vrai pirate, toi, ou juste un m: Are you a real pirate, or just a cabin boy?
You've come to see me %d times.
textes.Tu es vraiment médecin, ou tu as juste u: Are you really a doctor, or have you just got a saw?
textes.Tu essaies. C'est honnête. C'est déjà pl: You're trying. That's honest. That's already more than half my customers. Here, a rum, on the house. To keep you going. Easy, it bites.
textes.Tu fais quoi dans la vie, déjà ?: What is it you do again?
textes.Tu fais rouler les dés dans ta main. Six: You roll the dice in your hand. Six, six, six. Again. Six, six, five. Not bad. Nobody saw a thing.
textes.Tu fais siffler la plume dorée… Un cri d: You blow the golden feather like a whistle… An eagle's cry answers, far away. Ventaile is coming!
textes.Tu fais tinter la clochette : ding, ding: You ring the little bell: ding, ding! The bushes shake, and Truffe trots out, ears flopping, tail curled like a corkscrew. He presses his snout against your hand. Oink! He follows you now.
textes.Tu fais tourner l'attrape-rêves. Les per: You twirl the dreamcatcher. The beads tinkle softly. You yawn.
textes.Tu fais tourner la plume entre tes doigt: You twirl the feather between your fingers. Somewhere in the Twisted Wood, an owl hoots.
textes.Tu fais un nœud de marin, comme Galet. P: You tie a sailor's knot, like Galet. Then you undo it. Then you tie it again. It's strangely soothing.
textes.Tu fais, avant, l'île f'appelait l'Île V: You know, the ithland uthed to be called Green Ithland. Then Barbe-Thanglante came and dug the Balafre — the Thcar — to hide hith treathure. That'th what they thay. I thay it wath the rain.
textes.Tu ferais ça ? Bien. L'herbe à fièvre po: You'd do that? Good. Fever grass grows at the water's edge, in the Drowned Marsh: silvery tufts that glow a little when the sun is low. I need three. And watch the water, not the tufts: crocodiles come out of the water.
textes.Tu ferais ça ? Les cempasúchil poussent: You'd do that? The cempasúchil grow on the chinampas in the south, beside the canals: orange tufts, like little suns. I need five bunches. Don't step on the beans!
textes.Tu ferais ça ? Mon tajine du vendredi, c: You'd do that? My Friday tagine is a whole affair: I need two sea bream, nice ones, fresh ones. Not Saïd's: he shouts at them all morning, their flesh gets stressed. Catch them yourself, or find them, but bring me two. And you'll taste the best tagine on the whole island.
textes.Tu ferais ça ? … Rhubarbe. Rouge comme u: You'd do that? … Rhubarbe. Red as a sunset, ill-mannered as a cabin boy. He flew off three days ago toward the northern jungle. Joe heard him swearing near the old abandoned camp. Spiders have made their nest there, be careful. First go and see Joe, in the square: he talks to birds better than to men.
textes.Tu fermes les yeux quand je chante, tu s: You close your eyes when I sing, you know.
textes.Tu feuillettes « Le Boucanier ». Page 3: You leaf through “Le Boucanier”. Page 3: “A ROBOT FROM LISSE APOLOGISES FOR FORTY MINUTES.” Page 4: a crossword where all the answers are “BOUCAN”.
textes.Tu fouilles tes poches… pas assez de piè: You rummage through your pockets… not enough coins. Lentille laughs: “Then it's zero! Zero is a price too!”
textes.Tu frappes un nain ? Sur SA montagne ?!: You hit a dwarf? On HIS mountain?!
textes.Tu frottes le patch des Rats de Cale. Qu: You rub the Bilge Rats patch. Somewhere in the Boucan, a guitar goes “BRRRANG”. It's surely no coincidence.
You rub the scarab between your fingers. It's warm, like a summer morning.
textes.Tu frottes ton badge. Il fait « bip-bip: You rub your badge. It goes “beep-beep” and displays, in tiny letters: “Hello!”
textes.Tu gardes un secret ? Chaque pièce que j: Can you keep a secret? Every coin I earn goes into a jar under my bed. I never buy myself anything, not even a ribbon. When there's enough, I'll buy giant flower seeds and replant the north, flower by flower, all the way to the sea. People think I'm stingy. I'm only patient.
textes.Tu gardes ça pour toi, hein, {surnom}. J: Keep this to yourself, OK, {surnom}. I made a necklace for Zoé, with a heart-shaped shell. I'd been looking for that shell for four years. She said “Oh, a crab!” and laughed. I said yes, a crab. Now she wears it every day, and I don't know how to tell her it wasn't a crab.
textes.Tu gravis l'escalier de racines…: You climb the staircase of roots…
textes.Tu gravis les marches de la Tour des Tem: You climb the steps of the Tower of Storms… the wind howls louder and louder.
textes.Tu grimpes sur le dos de Géryon. « Accro: You climb onto Geryon's back. “Hold on tight,” he says in his kindly voice. He spreads his wings, dives into the chasm in wide circles… and sets you down, all the way at the bottom, at the edge of Malebolge.
textes.Tu inventes ! Ha ! Comme Grand-père Ébèn: You make it up! Ha! Like Grandpa Ébène. Very bad for exams, and very good for stories. You'd make a poor scholar, but a marvellous storyteller.
textes.Tu jettes ce qui est cassé, toi. Ne jett: You throw out what's broken, you do. At least don't throw out the Léviathan. It's got two or three good centuries left in it.
textes.Tu jettes l'or et le jade dans le feu… L: You throw the gold and jade into the fire… The flames hiss and shrink back, like Tecciztécatl, the rich one, who drew back four times before the blaze. Nothing happens. (On the fresco, it's the other god who jumps.)
You throw the bones into the middle of the room. The jaguars pounce on them growling… and lie down to gnaw. They're not interested in you at all anymore.
textes.Tu jettes les roseaux et les épines de N: You throw in the reeds and thorns of Nanahuatzin, the poor one, the brave one, who leapt without hesitating… The fire roars, rising to the vault! And from the blaze, slowly, a sun rises.
textes.Tu jures de rien dire ? Juré craché ? Le: Swear you won't tell? Cross your heart and spit? The ginger cat sleeps on a roof near the Fondouk, everybody almost knows that. But I climbed up to see him, {surnom}. He was sleeping on papers. Old pirate papers. I only told Tibo. 'Cause I'm scared of one thing: that those papers make the pirates leave again. And Tibo with them. So shh. Shh shh shh.
