textes.Tu l'as arrosé, papa ? Il a grandi ?: Did you water it, Dad? Has it grown?
textes.Tu l'as entendue chanter, la baleine. De: You heard the whale sing. Since then I listen better. Nausicaa says I make a funny face.
textes.Tu l'as fait exprès ?: Did you do that on purpose?
textes.Tu l'as mangée, cette fois, ou tu as bou: Did you eat it this time, or plug a leak with it?
textes.Tu l'as pensé. Ça fume derrière tes yeux: You thought it. There's smoke behind your eyes.
textes.Tu l'as toujours, ton coquillage-trésor: Do you still have your treasure-shell? Keep it safe. Pirates steal everything.
textes.Tu l'as vu aussi, gamin ? Le slime remon: You saw it too, kid? The slime is rising. In the wells, in the fountain, and this morning in Rissole's soup. She's furious. It comes from below, from the Dungeon of a Thousand Steps, at the foot of the Fangs. Five floors. Right at the bottom is the Jelly King, with his little crown. As long as he's there, the jelly will keep rising. You're rank D now: you're ready. Go down, defeat him, and bring me his Royal jelly heart. And when he splits into little pieces… whatever you do, don't panic. I know what I'm talking about.
textes.Tu l'as vue, ce matin ?: Did you see it this morning?
textes.Tu l'as… tu es remonté de Xibalba. (Ix K: You have it… you came back up from Xibalba. (Ix Kanul kneels.) The Twins tricked the Lords and became the Sun and the Moon. You, you became a story. Keep the mask: its place is on the Altar of the Three Suns, in the highlands. Here, some festival cacao.
textes.Tu l'espères. C'est la réponse d'un sage: You hope so. That's a wise man's answer. We hope so too, every night. That's why we keep watch.
You'll let it freeze, you mean.
textes.Tu lances les trois gâteaux de miel. Tro: You throw the three honey cakes. Three heads, three “gulps”. Cerbère licks his chops… yawns with all three mouths… and collapses, snoring. A three-voice snore. The south gate opens.
textes.Tu le diras à personne, {surnom}. Les le: Don't tell anyone, {surnom}. The letters are signed “The Seagull”. But the handwriting, I know it. It's the one on the Perroquet's slate. Lola's. I keep them all in a crate I called “Lola”. I've written forty replies. Never sent them. I don't know how you start a letter to a seagull.
textes.Tu le dis à personne, hein ? Mon grand-p: You won't tell anyone, right? My grandad always asks me what I can see on the horizon. He says it's to train me to be a captain. That's not true. His eyes are tired, he can't see the line between the sea and the sky any more. So I pretend I don't know, and I tell him everything. Even the seagulls. Especially the seagulls.
textes.Tu le disais déjà quand j'avais vingt-qu: You were already saying that when I was twenty-four.
You'd know, if you tasted it.
textes.Tu le vois, au sommet de la tour, au cen: Do you see it, at the top of the tower, in the centre of the city? It makes the air, the light and the dome. When it shines, the sea sings. When it fades… the sea falls silent.
textes.Tu lâches tout juste au-dessus de ta bar: You let go just above your rowboat… and land right in it! The Alouette folds back into your bag.
textes.Tu lèves les quatre sceaux vers la grand: You raise the four seals toward the great gate…
textes.Tu lèves les trois sceaux vers la Dame d: You raise the three seals toward the Figurehead Lady. They light up: gold, bronze, silver… The wood creaks. Slowly, between her hands, the shell opens.
textes.Tu lèves les yeux. Une table te regarde,: You look up. A table stares back at you, legs in the air. All the furniture is stuck to the ceiling!
textes.Tu m'apportes un arbre, la prochaine foi: Will you bring me a tree next time?
You've bought %d item from me, for %d coins.
textes.Tu m'as acheté %d objets, pour %d pièces: You've bought %d items from me, for %d coins.
textes.Tu m'as apporté des coquillages de la vr: You brought me shells from the real sea! I've kept every one.
textes.Tu m'as avoué que le noir te fait un peu: You admitted the dark scares you a little. Me too, when it goes boom… boom. But shh.
textes.Tu m'as avoué que tu caches tes blessure: You admitted you hide your injuries. So I watch how you walk. You walk fine. For now.
textes.Tu m'as battu, à l'Arène. Doucement, mêm: You beat me, at the Arena. Gently, even. I wrote you a poem. It rhymes with “champion”. Twice. I'll read it to you one evening, under the lantern.
textes.Tu m'as dit : un équipage fidèle. Je m'e: You told me: a loyal crew. I remember. If I'm ever a hand short, I'll know where to look.
textes.Tu m'as dit merci, une fois. Je l'ai not: You said thank you to me, once. I noted it. In my head. Don't do it too often, it feels funny.
textes.Tu m'as dit qu'Arcanelle t'avait mis en: You told me Arcanelle filled you with joy, coming out of the mist. Keep that joy close: it's the best of lanterns.
textes.Tu m'as dit qu'il faut dire au revoir av: You told me you have to say goodbye before leaving. I think about it often. I haven't found the words yet.
textes.Tu m'as dit qu'ils auraient peur de nous: You told me they would be afraid of us. So I'm practising being gentle. I'm starting with Coralin. It's a long job.
textes.Tu m'as dit qu'on nous accueillerait à b: You told me they would welcome us with open arms. I repeat it to myself on the nights the crystal falls silent.
textes.Tu m'as dit qu'on écrit l'avenir en marc: You told me we write the future as we walk. Then walk straight, {surnom}. The stones are taking notes.
textes.Tu m'as dit qu'une carte, ça peut se tro: You told me a map can be wrong. I thought about it all night. So did Gaston. He was snoring, but he was thinking about it.
textes.Tu m'as dit que j'aurais un peu peur et: You told me I'd be a bit scared and that's normal. So I'm practising: I'm a bit scared every day now.
You told me your friends keep you warm. I think of it when I see Ébène cheating at draughts. You were right.
textes.Tu m'as dit que toi aussi, tu étais part: You told me you'd left without saying goodbye too. Have you thought about it since? I think about it every morning, while I polish Bertha.
textes.Tu m'as dit que tu aimais les lames lour: You told me you like heavy blades. I've got my eye on you, {surnom}. You've got a dwarf's heart in a body that's too long.
textes.Tu m'as dit que tu n'avais pas le rythme: You told me you had no rhythm. Fibber. Your heart beats in time, I checked.
textes.Tu m'as dit que tu ne chantais jamais. L: You told me you never sing. The festival's not over yet, {surnom}. I promised.
textes.Tu m'as dit que tu ne pleurais jamais. J: You told me you never cry. I think about it often. So I cry a little for you. It doesn't cost me anything.
You told me you'd plant a forest. I kept a seed for you. Start with one tree: the forest will come later.
textes.Tu m'as dit que tu te perdais dans la br: You told me you get lost in the mist. If one evening you don't come home, I'll come. I already know the way you walk.
textes.Tu m'as dit que tu trouvais %s très symp: You told me you found %s very nice.
textes.Tu m'as dit que tu trouvais %s un peu bi: You told me you found %s a bit weird.
textes.Tu m'as dit que ça dépendait de qui donn: You told me it depended on who gives the order. I hope I'm the kind people follow.
You've given me %d gift, the last one: %s.
textes.Tu m'as fait %d cadeaux, le dernier : %s: You've given me %d gifts, the last one: %s.
textes.Tu m'as fait une de ces peurs ! J'ai cru: You gave me such a fright! I thought it was Monday.
textes.Tu m'as frappé ?! À moi ?! Viens là !: You hit me?! ME?! Come here!
textes.Tu m'as parlé de perles sous la mer. Je: You told me about pearls under the sea. I can't sleep for thinking of them. Did you bring any back? A little one? Half of one?
textes.Tu m'as raconté qu'il vit dans une caban: You told me he lives in a hut perched up a tree, and that he forges up there. A forge in a tree! With wood all around! I laughed for three days. On the fourth, I thought: that takes courage. Or no brains. I haven't decided yet.
You brought me crystal shards. My fireplace has never been so pretty. … I mean: so warm.
textes.Tu m'as rapporté mes cinq gouttes de ros: You brought back my five dewdrops. I won't lose them again. Promise. Almost.
textes.Tu m'as rendu ma baguette ! Depuis, je n: You gave me back my wand! I haven't let go of it since. Not even to sleep.
textes.Tu m'as trouvé la bague. Je… je ne l'ai: You found me the ring. I… I haven't given it to her yet. But soon!
textes.Tu m'avais conseillé d'attendre un signe: You advised me to wait for a sign. I've noted a hundred and seventeen since. Not one of them is clear.
textes.Tu m'avais dit les étoiles. J'y repense: You told me the stars. I think about it every evening when I close the workshop. I still haven't found the hole.
textes.Tu m'avais dit qu'on a un peu peur des d: You told me people are a little afraid of demons back home. Have you told them about us since?
textes.Tu m'avais dit qu'on peut être fort et d: You told me you can be strong and gentle. I wrote the poem. It's three lines long. It rhymes with “gentle”. Twice.
textes.Tu m'avais dit que c'était difficile, d': You told me it was hard, being strong and gentle. You were right. I broke another cup this morning. Gently.
textes.Tu m'avais dit que j'étais la preuve qu': You told me I was the proof that you can be strong and gentle. I think of it every time I step into the Arena. Thank you.
textes.Tu m'avais dit que ma place était ici. T: You told me my place was here. You're right. But one day, here is going to float. You'll see.
textes.Tu m'avais dit que personne ne t'attenda: You told me nobody was waiting for you. That's not true any more: I'm waiting for you. Sit down.
textes.Tu m'avais dit que tu aimais ce qui chan: You told me you liked things that change. Ortie would be delighted. Me, I'm worried. And a little proud.
textes.Tu m'avais dit que tu demandes quand tu: You told me you ask when you don't know. So ask me anything. I've got three centuries of answers in store.
textes.Tu m'avais dit que tu dormais mal. Tu as: You told me you sleep badly. Have you tried my moon tea? No? The leaves told me so: you're stubborn.
textes.Tu m'avais dit que tu ne lisais pas beau: You told me you don't read much. The little book with pictures, have you finished it? It doesn't matter. It's waiting for you.
textes.Tu m'avais dit que tu ne savais pas nage: You told me you couldn't swim. I haven't told anyone. We don't talk about it, people like us.
textes.Tu m'avais dit que tu ne savais plus d'o: You told me you didn't remember where you came from. I know: from the Smoking Cauldron. A little. Sit down.
textes.Tu m'avais dit que tu préférais le milie: You told me you preferred the middle of stories. Then you'll love your own: I think you're right in the thick of it.
textes.Tu m'avais dit que tu préférais les rond: You told me you preferred the rounds. If you want to come with me one day, wear good shoes. And don't go clang.
You told me it depends who against. I think of it every race. Against Bondi, it counts double, I've decided.
textes.Tu m'avais dit que ça dépend de ce qu'on: You told me it depends what you're waiting for. I thought about it again on the jetty. You were right. Shh.
You told me it depended on the day. So today, is it a quiet day or a noisy one? … Oh well, I'm shouting anyway.
You told me it depended on the dark. I think about it all the time. Tonight, it's a nice dark. I think.
textes.Tu m'avais dit « bientôt ». J'ai repassé: You told me “soon”. I ironed my dress. Twice. Still nothing. I'm a little cross with you.
textes.Tu m'avais dit « pas encore ». Alors ? C: You told me “not yet”. So? When's your naughty thing happening? I've kept some smoke powder specially.
textes.Tu m'emmènes encore au désert, mon oncle: Will you take me to the desert again, uncle?
textes.Tu m'offres un verre avec quoi ? Tes poc: Buy me a drink with what? Your pockets sound empty.
textes.Tu marchanderais la lune elle-même, Aëlw: You'd haggle over the moon itself, Aëlwen.
textes.Tu marchandes bien, pour un {surnom}. Al: You haggle well, for a {surnom}. Go on then: a small discount. Don't tell anyone.
textes.Tu marches ? Bon. Marcher, c'est courir: You walk? All right. Walking is running with patience. Marcel says it's worth forty marathons. He exaggerates. Not by that much.
textes.Tu me cherchais jusqu'à la Cathédrale-Fo: You came looking for me all the way to the Forge Cathedral? At this hour, I come to listen to the Ember Heart. It tells me how the city is doing. Better than Asmodin, and in fewer words.
textes.Tu me dois deux pièces, Tonneau !: You owe me two coins, Tonneau!
textes.Tu me ferais une jarre de pluie ?: Would you make me a rain jar?
You'll tell me at the second coffee.
textes.Tu me le dis tous les matins depuis quat: You've told me that every morning for eighty years.
textes.Tu me racontes la suite ?: Will you tell me what happened next?
textes.Tu mesures encore les gens, Coquillard ?: Still measuring people, Coquillard? Go and measure your words.
textes.Tu montes l'escalier en colimaçon du bef: You climb the spiral staircase of the belfry…
textes.Tu montes sur l'estrade. Ton cœur s'envo: You step onto the platform. Your heart flies out of your chest — you can see it! — and lands on the left pan. The jackal leans toward you.
textes.Tu montes vers la lumière… le vent souff: You climb toward the light… the wind is blowing up above.
textes.Tu montes, marche après marche, dans le: You climb, step after step, into the heart of the tree…
You don't have any seal power yet.
textes.Tu n'as encore rien attrapé ? Patience,: Haven't caught anything yet? Patience, {surnom}. It took me three years to catch my first fish. Mind you, my rod was made of seaweed.
textes.Tu n'as jamais voulu me dire d'où tu vie: You never would tell me where you come from. That, I remember.
textes.Tu n'as pas encore de machine volante. À: You don't have a flying machine yet. In Cliquetis, Philibert Vis, “the inventor without an invention”, dreams of building one…
textes.Tu n'as pas encore de pouvoir. Les quatr: You don't have a power yet. The four seals of the great eastern island each hide one…
textes.Tu n'as pas eu le temps de dire « bonjou: You didn't have time to say “hello.” The door shut by itself. Well, not by itself.
textes.Tu n'as pas oublié mes {manque} coquilla: You haven't forgotten my {manque} shells? I've already made room for them on the shelf!
textes.Tu n'as que {coquillages} bâtons. Il m'e: You've only got {coquillages} sticks. I need {manque}. The island's woods are full of them.
textes.Tu n'aurais pas vu mes noix de coco, toi: You haven't seen my coconuts, have you?
textes.Tu n'avais jamais compté les étoiles. Tu: You'd never counted the stars. Have you started? One is already one more than none.
textes.Tu n'avais pas voulu répondre, l'autre f: You didn't want to answer, the other day. I won't ask again. Neither will Bertha.
textes.Tu n'en as que {coquillages}. Il m'en fa: You've only got {coquillages}. I need {manque} in all. Look on the beach by your village, they sparkle in the sun.
textes.Tu n'entends pas le cuivre, alors je tap: You can't hear the copper, so I hit harder for you. TAC. There. No need to thank me.
textes.Tu n'y connais rien ? Alors commence par: You don't know anything about it? Then start with the best! Sit down: a hot sulphur punch, a frozen lava, and you'll know.
textes.Tu n'étais pas sûr, la dernière fois. C': You weren't sure, last time. That's good. A good lookout doubts. And then he writes it down.
textes.Tu nages ! Espace : remonter, Ctrl : plo: You're swimming! Space: surface, Ctrl: dive, Shift: swim fast. Facing a pier or a rock, press Space to haul yourself up.
textes.Tu nages ! Stick gauche : nager vers où: You're swimming! Left stick: swim where you're looking (look down to dive). A: surface, B: descend, left trigger: swim fast.
textes.Tu ne connais encore aucun sort. Les maî: You don't know any spell yet. The masters of Arcanelle, the wizards' island, teach six of them.
textes.Tu ne connais pas encore la magie de tél: You don't know teleportation magic yet. The fairies, maybe, someday…
textes.Tu ne le diras à personne, que c'était m: You won't tell anyone it was me, right? I'm working on an even scarier ghost. With chains. And a saucepan.
textes.Tu ne les as même pas, les quarante pièc: You haven't even got the forty coins! Ha! Come back when you're rich.
You don't trust them, I know. Neither do I. But greet them all the same. They pay.
textes.Tu ne marchandes qu'avec moi, hein ? Alo: You only haggle with me, eh? Then come on, I've been practising. You won't win.
textes.Tu ne me ferais pas un prix ?: Couldn't you give me a better price?
You never make me pay for it.
textes.Tu ne parles jamais ? Tu as perdu ta lan: Do you never talk? Cat got your tongue?
textes.Tu ne sais pas ? Moi je savais, à ton âg: You don't know? I knew, at your age. I knew all too well. Look, my child. Someone is always waiting, somewhere.
textes.Tu ne sais pas ? Ta propre pointure ? Ma: You don't know? Your own shoe size? But how do you walk? At random? Sit down, take your boots off, I'll measure. No, don't take them off here. Further away. Thank you.
textes.Tu ne sais pas compter au-delà de dix, Y: You can't count past ten, Yum Kab.
textes.Tu ne savais pas faire un nœud. Fatima e: You couldn't tie a knot. Fatima's still laughing about it. Sit down, back to the lesson.
textes.Tu ne t'inclines plus, toi. Je l'ai rema: You don't bow anymore. I've noticed. I said nothing. That's what being king is.
textes.Tu nous as trouvés ! Tous les DEUX ! Mêm: You found us! BOTH of us! Even Quark! Why are you so good? Do you have hidden antennae? Show me! … No? Fine. You're the first Heavyfoot hide-and-seek champion. Quark is sulking. He says you cheated. HE's the one who cheats! Here, our moon cookies from recess. We kept three. Well, four. Quark ate one while hiding. That's how you found him: the crumbs.
You tell us that one every time, Nono.
textes.Tu ouvres la calebasse. Xan file droit…: You open the gourd. Xan flies straight… down the BLACK path! He vanishes there, then comes back zigzagging, all pleased, and goes into his gourd.
textes.Tu ouvres la lanterne. Un à un, les espr: You open the lantern. One by one, the firefly spirits fly out and settle in the niches… The bark trembles, and the door of the Mother Tree opens!
textes.Tu ouvres le grimoire. L'encre violette: You open the spellbook. The violet ink quivers, and the spells you know glow for a moment on the page.
textes.Tu ouvres les cinq bourses et souffles l: You open the five pouches and blow the fairy dust over the brambles. It sparkles… and the black brambles wither, curl up, and fall to dust. The way to the Bramble Throne is open.
textes.Tu paies ? Alors t'es mon ami. Jusqu'au: You're paying? Then you're my friend. To the bottom of the glass, at least.
textes.Tu paies MA dette ? … T'es un drôle de n: You're paying MY debt? … You're a strange one, you are. Here, take my purse, give it to the big lady, and tell her to leave me in peace. (He stuffs your coins into his purse and hands it to you.)
textes.Tu parles comme l'archimage ! Bon. D'acc: You sound like the archmage! Fine. OK. I'll work hard. But not on Sundays.
textes.Tu passes le portail de l'Usine Grise. D: You step through the Grey Factory gate. Inside, it's clean, grey and silent, like a giant waiting room. A reception robot smiles at you with its screen. Somewhere beneath your feet, machines purr.
You may pet me. Once. Not twice.
You may pass. I allow it.
textes.Tu plaisantais ? Moi je ne plaisante jam: You were joking? I never joke.
textes.Tu plonges la fiole de cristal dans le b: You dip the crystal vial into the basin. The spring water sparkles inside, as if full of stars.
textes.Tu plonges le bras dans l'eau froide du: You plunge your arm into the cold water of the lake… and pull out a big round stone, white as coral, with a black pupil: an EYE! It looks at you. It seems delighted to be out of the water. (“The water that looks at the sky”: it was the crater lake!)
textes.Tu portes mon épée ! Elle te va bien. En: You're carrying my sword! It suits you. Well, you suit it.
textes.Tu portes une hache. S'il te plaît… pas: You're carrying an axe. Please… not here. Not near the Tree.
textes.Tu poses l'amulette sur la pierre. Les y: You place the amulet on the stone. The serpents' eyes light up one by one…
textes.Tu poses l'obole dans la main osseuse de: You place the obol in Charon's bony hand. He bites it, looks at it, pockets it. “Get in. And don't lean over: the Acheron is cold, and it doesn't give back hats.”
textes.Tu poses la main sur la lentille. Bzzzt: You place your hand on the lens. Bzzzt! The carp change color and swoop in a big loop above the square. Somewhere, someone applauds.
textes.Tu poses le Plat de la Grande Réconcilia: You place the Dish of the Great Reconciliation on the altar, next to the eternal plate. A smell of tomato, basil and parmesan rises to the top of the colander… Up there, something stirs.
textes.Tu poses le cuissot de cerf sur l'autel: You lay the venison haunch on the altar: “Blades, here is the flesh of the beasts. All the beasts of the forest shall be yours.” A creak… and the four blades slide into the walls and lie down.
textes.Tu poses le tricorne sur ta tête. Il est: You set the tricorn on your head. It's a bit big. You feel ready to face the whole ocean.
textes.Tu poses les deux cristaux dans le Sceau: You place the two crystals in the Seal of Winds: one glows red, the other turns blue… A breath of wind sweeps through the courtyard, and the great doors of the keep slowly open.
textes.Tu poses les quatre morceaux dans le sar: You place the four pieces in the sarcophagus… A green light, like growing wheat, rises from the basin: Osiris is whole again! A very gentle voice: “Thank you. Now go before Anubis: your heart will be weighed.”
textes.Tu poses les trois fragments dans les em: You place the three fragments in the imprints… They sink in by themselves.
textes.Tu poses un morceau de fromage affiné su: You put a piece of aged cheese on the planks, against the hull. A snout. Whiskers. Biscotte comes out of its hole, nibbles, looks at you… then climbs up your leg, your arm, and settles on your shoulder. You did it!
textes.Tu pousses de toutes tes forces… Le poid: You push with all your might… The weight doesn't budge: something is blocking it from the other side.
textes.Tu pousses les battants d'obsidienne. La: You push open the obsidian doors. The green barrier dies out with a crackle…
textes.Tu prends la Perle de la Fosse sur son a: You take the Pearl of the Trench from its altar. It's as cold as the depths… the age of the abyss.
textes.Tu prends le Sceau des Sables. Il est ch: You take the Seal of Sands. It's warm like a stone in the sun… and suddenly it burns without hurting: a flame awakens in the hollow of your hand! (Press 2 to choose the Flame, X to throw it; in VR: B.) The sand in the corners starts to move…
textes.Tu prends un ruban et tu fais le tour de: You take a ribbon and skip around the tree. The ribbons braid around the pole, yellow, red, green, blue… it's very pretty, and a little dizzying.
textes.Tu prends une obole dans la coupe de bro: You take an obol from the bronze bowl. A little label: “For Charon. One per traveler. He counts.”
textes.Tu préfères les coquillages… aucun, héla: You prefer shells that are… none, alas.
textes.Tu préfères ne pas savoir. Alors je ne t: You'd rather not know. So I won't tell you what this morning's rune said about you. You see? I listened.
textes.Tu préférais la surprise, alors je n'ai: You preferred the surprise, so I didn't look at anything. Well, hardly anything. One little corner of a card. Nothing serious.
textes.Tu rates souvent ta cible, avec tes cout: Do you often miss your target with those knives?
textes.Tu regardes au fond de la fleur. Une tou: You look into the heart of the flower. A tiny galaxy turns and turns… You feel a little dizzy. It smells of vanilla.
textes.Tu regardes jamais sur ta tête !: You never look on your head!
textes.Tu regardes ta carte d'aventurier. Ton p: You look at your adventurer's card. Your portrait looks back at you. The nose, honestly, is not right.
textes.Tu relis les livres, toi ? Ou tu les lis: Do you reread books? Or do you only read them once?
textes.Tu relis ton titre de propriété. Tu as u: You reread your property deed. You have a house! With a wisteria! And a bed!
textes.Tu remontes de la fosse, couvert de sabl: You climb back out of the pit, covered in sand, at the chapel entrance. Those slabs had nothing on them… The scarabs, though, know where to step.
You climb back out of the pit, covered in sand.
textes.Tu remontes les couvertures jusqu'aux me: You pull the blankets up to their chins. One of the children murmurs “Thank you, Granny Sunflower…” without waking. The mother slips you a few coins: “For your gentleness.”
textes.Tu remontes les marches… L'air sent l'he: You climb back up the steps… The air smells of grass and wind. Odon looks up from his ledger: “Already?”
textes.Tu remplis un petit pot de sauce du volc: You fill a little jar with volcano sauce. It's just as good as before.
textes.Tu repenses à la légende de Mamie Basalt: You remember Granny Basalte's legend: give the Great Moai back his two eyes. One in “the water that looks at the sky”, the other “under the heads that look at the clouds”.
textes.Tu replies l'Alouette dans ton sac. Clic: You fold the Alouette back into your bag. Click, clack.
textes.Tu respires drôlement fort près de ma pâ: You're breathing awfully hard near my dough.
textes.Tu ressors de l'Arbre-Mère, ébloui par l: You step out of the Mother Tree, dazzled by the golden light of Bois-Doré.
textes.Tu reviens après ce que tu m'as fait ? J: You come back after what you did to me? I haven't forgotten. Neither has Gaston.
textes.Tu reviens après m'avoir frappé ? Les pr: Back after hitting me? Prices have gone up. For you.
textes.Tu reviens après une longue absence… {ab: You're back after a long absence… {absence}, I believe. For an elf, that's the blink of an eye.
textes.Tu reviens au Cercle. Les pierres s'en s: You've come back to the Circle. The stones remember. They remember everything.
textes.Tu reviens de la forêt ? Tu sens la mous: Back from the forest? You smell of moss and mushroom. That's a compliment.
textes.Tu reviens jouer ?: Are you coming back to play?
textes.Tu reviens pour la musique ? Le soir. To: Back for the music? In the evening. Always in the evening.
You're back. I saw you coming from a long way off.
textes.Tu reviens… La boule me l'avait dit. Ell: You're back… The ball told me. It tells me everything, the old chatterbox.
textes.Tu reçois le Sifflet des compagnons ! Ut: You receive the Companions' Whistle! Use it to choose who comes with you.
textes.Tu récupères ce que tu n'avais pas pu po: You pick up what you couldn't carry:
textes.Tu réfléchis avec le nez, alors !: Then you think with your nose!
Still dreaming of whales? I am. At night, they all believe me.
textes.Tu sais ce que dit une corne à l'autre c: Do you know what one horn says to the other horn? “You and me, we've always been in the same head space!”
textes.Tu sais ce que ça veut dire, maintenant,: Do you know what pointing means now? No? Come to pitch one, at three o'clock. I'm adopting you.
textes.Tu sais ce qui est le plus beau, ici ? L: You know what's the most beautiful thing here? The sunset behind the masts. And the scariest: Skull Rock. I saw it once, from far away. Its eyes were glowing.
textes.Tu sais ce qui est plus vieux que les Mo: Do you know what's older than the Moai? … Pebbles. Hee hee! They never brag about it.
textes.Tu sais d'où tu viens, toi ? De quelle î: Do you know where you come from? Which island, which tree? I don't, so I ask everybody!
textes.Tu sais garder un secret ? Je voudrais o: Can you keep a secret? I'd like to give Ilyria a ring. A human ring, with a blue stone, like her eyes. Could you find one? They say the beaches of your islands hide a few.
textes.Tu sais garder un secret, {surnom} ? Mér: Can you keep a secret, {surnom}? Mérit says Tiyi turned down three suitors. Tiyi says four. The fourth one is me. I brought her a perch, the finest one, with a lotus flower in its mouth. She laughed, kindly, and said no. Since then, I bring her a perch every week. For Nebet, I say. No flower. Well, almost.
textes.Tu sais où est le coffre, Lou ?: Do you know where the chest is, Lou?
textes.Tu sais pas ? Peuchère… Bon. Assieds-toi: You don't know? Oh, bless you… Right. Sit down. Pointing is putting your ball right up close to the jack. Shooting is knocking the other fellow's ball away. And lying about the measurement, that's Marcel.
textes.Tu sais pourquoi je ris tout le temps, {: Do you know why I laugh all the time, {surnom}? So as not to say certain things. My sister Sésame left ten years ago, with the family bell, “in exchange for a trip round the world”. My finest chain. I'm afraid that one day, someone will come to the market to swap me that bell… without her. That day, I won't know what to give in return.
textes.Tu sais pourquoi le Léviathan ne coule j: Know why the Léviathan never sinks? Because it's already hit rock bottom! … That's Corentin's joke, he tells it every evening.
textes.Tu sais pourquoi les Moaïs ne jouent jam: Do you know why Moai never play hide-and-seek? … Because they're found right away! Hee hee hee!
textes.Tu sais pourquoi les mouettes volent au-: Do you know why seagulls fly over the sea? Because if they flew over the bay, they'd be bagels! … Okay, fine.
textes.Tu sais pêcher ?: Do you know how to fish?
textes.Tu sais qui vole les croissants ?: Do you know who's stealing the croissants?
textes.Tu sais quoi ? Une baleine passe au-dess: Guess what? Sometimes a whale swims over the city. It sings. Abyssos says it talks to the Great Crystal.
textes.Tu sais retrouver ton chemin dans le bro: Can you find your way in the fog? Here, mist rises from the ponds every night. Those who can't go round in circles.
textes.Tu sais te battre ? J'ai des crocodiles: Can you fight? I've got some crocodiles to introduce you to.
textes.Tu sais te servir de tes mains, au moins: Can you at least use your hands?
You know, I sing while I gut the fish. Paulo says that's why his bouillabaisse has heart.
textes.Tu sais, tous les Moaïs regardent l'inté: You know, all the Moai look toward the inside of the island. It's tradition. So I… I've never seen the sea. Never. Not once. They say it's big, and blue, and that it sings.
textes.Tu sauras tenir ta langue, {surnom} ? Le: Can you keep a secret, {surnom}? On election day, I measured wrong. On purpose. Raymond's ball was closer. Not by one centimetre: by two. I didn't do it to annoy him. I did it to keep him. As mayor, Raymond would never have had time to play. And who would I play against then? A pebble?
textes.Tu sautes avec la foule ! Boïng ! Boïng: You jump with the crowd! Boing! Boing!
textes.Tu secoues la bombe : clic-clic-clic ! L: You shake the can: click-click-click! The wall is waiting. What will you paint?
textes.Tu secoues le sachet. Quelque part, un p: You shake the pouch. Somewhere, a parrot turns its head.
textes.Tu sens comme le kick a monté ? Mistral: Do you feel how the kick has come up? Mistral is on form tonight.
textes.Tu sens la sciure, {surnom}. Tu abats de: You smell of sawdust, {surnom}. Are you chopping down trees? Spare my banana trees, they're my confidants.
textes.Tu sens le fer rouillé et le charbon. Tu: You smell of rusty iron and coal. You've come from Octave's, admit it.
You smell of rotten fish, sailor.
textes.Tu sens le saucisson. Je dis ça, je dis: You smell of sausage. Just saying. Not saying anything.
textes.Tu siffles doucement… Tout le monde est: You whistle softly… Everyone has gone home. You walk a while on your own.
textes.Tu sors la pelote de laine et tu la fais: You take out the ball of wool and roll it gently over the cobblestones. Up above, two ears prick up. Brioche hesitates… stretches… and jumps, light as a rag, down beside the ball. She nudges it with a paw, then comes to rub against your legs. She's the one who chose: it's you.
textes.Tu souffles dans la conque d'Ehécatl, de: You blow into Ehécatl's conch with all your might. An immense wind rises in the hall, bending the flames… and the fifth sun starts to move! It turns, it crosses the stone sky. To the south, the last door opens.
textes.Tu souffles dans le sifflet : fuiii-iii: You blow the whistle: tweeeet! Who's coming with me?
You blow the whistle: tweeeet! … Nobody comes. You don't have a companion yet.
textes.Tu soulèves la pierre plate, au pied de: You lift the flat stone, at the foot of the only head with its nose in the air, watching the clouds go by… Underneath, in a nest of moss: a coral eye, white, round, with its black pupil. It looks like it's blinking. (No: that's just emotion.)
textes.Tu soulèves le couvercle… Le coffre ouvr: You lift the lid… The chest opens an eye. Then a mouth. Full of teeth. Oops.
You were smiling in your sleep. I saw you.
textes.Tu t'approches du Cœur de la Flèche. Les: You approach the Spire's Heart. The three shards slip out of your bag, float up to the great crystal… and melt into it in a flash of blue. The Heart begins to beat again, strong, steady, joyful. Far below, the bridges of light stop flickering. Go back and see Elder Astrée!
textes.Tu t'assois sur le tapis jaune. Inspire…: You sit down on the yellow mat. Breathe in… breathe out… The wind makes the canvas sing, someone laughs softly, a fly passes. After a while, you feel light as a feather.
textes.Tu t'es posé : la course s'arrête. Comèt: You've landed: the race is over. Comète turns around laughing: “Rematch? I'll be waiting at the golden ring!”
You've moved away: the line reels in.
textes.Tu t'installes avec eux. C'est délicieux: You sit down with them. It's delicious (and everyone watches you eat). Your hearts are full! For the road:
textes.Tu t'élèves de cinq ou six mètres, tu pl: You rise five or six metres, hover a moment, and float gently back down.
textes.Tu t'évanouis… et te réveilles au pied d: You faint… and wake up at the foot of the ladder.
textes.Tu tapes trop fort, Borin. Les pierres s: You hit too hard, Borin. The stones are complaining.
textes.Tu te dis aventurier. Je te crois. À moi: You call yourself an adventurer. I believe you. Halfway.
textes.Tu te glisses dans la couchette. Les vag: You slip into the bunk. The waves rock you… Good night, sailor.
textes.Tu te laisses glisser le long de la chaî: You let yourself slide down the chain, all the way to the bottom of the well…
textes.Tu te moques de moi ? Remballe ça avant: Are you making fun of me? Pack that up before I make you eat it.
textes.Tu te perds ? Mais c'est merveilleux ! L: You get lost? But that's wonderful! The great explorers get lost all the time. I got lost for twenty-two years, and look at everything I found.
textes.Tu te rappelles le gros mérou, celui des: Remember the big grouper, the two-boat one? Fifty years ago, Gwenola said to me: “I'll marry you the day a fish tells you yes.” So I ask them all the question. That grouper opened its mouth, and I heard “yes”. I let it go. I never went and told Gwenola. At my age, you get scared of winning.
textes.Tu te retournes toujours, la nuit, hein: You always look behind you at night, eh? Good. Keep it up. So do I.
textes.Tu te réveilles près du feu du Clan. Mam: You wake up by the Clan's fire. Mamie Silex dabs your forehead with cold moss: “Grosse-Dent too strong? Eat first. After, go hit again.”
textes.Tu te réveilles sur le quai, la mâchoire: You wake up on the quay, your jaw in a mess. The seagulls are laughing.
textes.Tu te sens toujours perdu ? Non ? C'est: Do you still feel lost? No? That's thanks to me! I'm a very good guide. Mum says I'm mostly a very good chatterbox.
textes.Tu te souviens de ton premier copeau ? I: Remember your first wood shaving? It's still on the workbench. I haven't swept it up.
textes.Tu tends l'os à Sardine. Il le prend tou: You hold out the bone to Sardine. He takes it very gently, lies down at your feet and gnaws on it, growling with joy. His tail sweeps the floor: flap, flap, flap.
textes.Tu tends les graines. Rhubarbe penche la: You hold out the seeds. Rhubarbe tilts his head… comes down from his perch, pecks from your hand, and climbs onto your shoulder: “SHIVER ME TIMBERS!” Take him back to the captain.
textes.Tu tiens la botte bien droite, comme une: You hold the bundle perfectly straight, like a conductor's baton. (Recommendation no. 3: don't snap it in half.)
textes.Tu tires ou tu pointes ? … Ah, tu ne sai: Do you shoot or do you point? … Ah, you don't even know what that means. Raymond. Port-Azur champion. Marcel will tell you otherwise, he's lying.
textes.Tu tombes encore, en rêve ? Bientôt, tu: Are you still falling, in your dreams? Soon you'll forget the ground, I promise. I forget it every day.
textes.Tu tombes… Un robot-trieur te ramasse, t: You fall… A sorting robot picks you up, stamps you “RETURN TO SENDER” and sets you back at the start of the room.
textes.Tu tombes… et tu te retrouves, étourdi,: You fall… and find yourself, dazed, at the edge of the hall.
You fall… and find yourself, dazed, at the start of the room. (One more step for Odon's count.)
You fall… and find yourself, dazed, at the entrance of the hall.
textes.Tu tournes la grande roue : des vannes s: You turn the great wheel: sluice gates open somewhere, the water drains away with a roar… The basin empties, the rafts sink all the way down.
textes.Tu tournes la grande roue : l'eau monte: You turn the great wheel: the water rises to half height, and the rafts with it. The chest on the pillar, to the right, is now level with them…
textes.Tu tournes la grande roue : l'eau monte,: You turn the great wheel: the water rises, and rises, up to the brim! The rafts reach the level of the ledge.
textes.Tu tournes la manivelle du rouet : les f: You turn the crank of the spinning wheel: the hemp threads twist together, tight, tight… and there's a sturdy rope! That's what hemp is for here: ropes, canvas, twine. You can keep it.
textes.Tu triches, Doigts-d'Argent. Tout le mon: You cheat, Doigts-d'Argent. Everybody knows it.
textes.Tu trouveras. Moi, j'ai trouvé. Chut. C': You'll find it. I did. Shh. It's a cabin boy's secret.
textes.Tu trouves que c'est bizarre ? Moi je tr: You think it's strange? I think it's strange that you all put your furniture on the floor. That's where we walk!
textes.Tu vas au Styx ? Écoute un spécialiste d: Off to the Styx? Listen to a bubble expert: a slab that bubbles is a slab that's sinking. The bubbles are air escaping from underneath. Walk on the calm slabs. And the Cocytus… brr. I don't even want to talk about it. It gives me cold horns.
textes.Tu vas encore te tromper de barbe, Sidi: Going to get the beard wrong again, Sidi?
textes.Tu vas encore teindre mon safran ?: Going to dye my saffron again?
textes.Tu vas me rembourser, j'espère !: You're going to pay me back, I hope!
textes.Tu vas rire, {surnom}. Moi, la Voix, j'a: You'll laugh, {surnom}. Me, the Voice, I'm afraid of silence. At night, I sleep with the window open onto the harbour: the gulls, the rigging, the galleon's pump creaking. The day I lost my voice, I thought I was disappearing, as if someone had rubbed me out. Since then, I make noise. All the time. To be sure I'm still here.
textes.Tu verses l'eau de la jarre dans la coup: You pour the water from the jar into the chacmool's bowl. A rumble of thunder rolls in the distance, over the lake… Tlaloc is pleased.
textes.Tu veux courir ? Vraiment ? Formidable !: You want to race? Really? Wonderful! The rule is simple: you start from the arch, there, you go under the ten lantern arches, in order, all around the village, and you come back here. Bondi, Grisou and Éclair run with you. Come in first, and your name will go right at the top of the record board. Nobody has beaten Bondi in three years. Nobody has really tried, mind you.
textes.Tu veux entrer ? Prouve ta valeur. Les g: You want to come in? Prove your worth. The golems of the heights, up near the crater, have woken. Bring me {manque} of their runes, and the Great Gate will open for you.
textes.Tu veux la vérité, {surnom} ? Ma premièr: You want the truth, {surnom}? My first whale, I never saw it. I was sick, everyone was making fun of me, so I shouted “whale” to make them look at me differently. It worked. And then one morning, with Gaspard, I saw a real one. Enormous. And nobody believes me. That's my punishment, I think. I sort of deserved it.
textes.Tu veux m'aider ? Ramasse {manque} plume: Want to help me? Pick up {manque} raven feathers. The ravens circle the summit and land on the rocks; they're always shedding them. I'll pay you in cheese.
textes.Tu veux m'aider ? Rapporte-moi {manque}: Want to help me? Bring me {manque} mushrooms from your forest. Here, they only grow at full moon. I'll pay you in potions.
textes.Tu veux m'aider, {surnom} ? Il me faut {: Want to help me, {surnom}? I need {manque} ember mushrooms. They grow in the ash, near the fumaroles smoking on the slopes. I'll make you some stew!
textes.Tu veux pêcher ? Tu sais quoi… tu m'as r:
You want to fish? You know what… you completed my collection. Here, take my old rod. It once caught a grouper as big as Gaston. Gaston didn't appreciate that.

Equip it, go up to the water, hold {bouton} to wind up and release to cast. When the float dips: {bouton} again, quick!
textes.Tu veux que je l'enlève ?: Want me to take it off?
textes.Tu veux que je te parle de qui ?: Who do you want me to tell you about?
textes.Tu veux savoir pourquoi je n'ose pas, {s: You want to know why I don't dare, {surnom}? It's not the “no” that scares me. It's the “yes”. All my songs are songs of waiting. If she says yes, what will I play the next day? I never learned to write a happy song.
textes.Tu veux savoir pourquoi mes sculptures f: Want to know why my sculptures end up as fish, {surnom}? I always start with my father's face. And I never get it right. So, before anyone can tell, I add fins. At night I say good night to them. To him, really. Ondine overheard me one evening. She thinks I talk to fish. Let her think so.
textes.Tu veux te rendre utile, {surnom} ? Rapp: Want to make yourself useful, {surnom}? Bring me {manque} nice straight sticks. I need shovel handles. I'll pay, of course. Not much.
textes.Tu veux un sac ? Je n'ai pas de sac. Mai: You want a bag? I don't have bags. But it's kind of you to think of it.
textes.Tu veux un secret ? Borin croit qu'il me: Want a secret? Borin thinks he steals a ladleful of stew from me every day. I'm the one who rests it on the edge of the cauldron, at five to eleven, handle turned towards his forge. For a hundred years. The day he doesn't come, I'll know he's ill. Or that he's finally figured it out.
textes.Tu veux un secret de Mérit, {surnom} ? U: Want one of Mérit's secrets, {surnom}? A real one, not gossip? Ptahmosé spent the whole night building my oven. In the morning, his hands were burnt. I never said thank you. Because if I say thank you, we stop arguing. And if we stop arguing, he won't have a reason to come by every evening. There. Don't repeat it.
textes.Tu veux un secret, {surnom} ? La boule n: Want a secret, {surnom}? The ball shows me almost nothing. Mist. I read people, not glass. Except once. A month before you arrived, it showed me, very clearly, a figure coming out of the sea with mist on its shoulders. So when I told you “I was expecting you”… for once, it wasn't just a figure of speech.
textes.Tu veux un secret, {surnom} ? Mixtli cro: Want a secret, {surnom}? Mixtli thinks nobody can see he dances to be near my drum. Everyone sees it. Me first of all. I play slower when he dances, so he falls less. And I pretend not to notice anything. Because I love watching him try. Tum, tum. Shh.
You want a secret, {surnom}? … Just one. Since the marsh, I'm afraid of still water. Puddles, ponds, the bay when there's no wind. Everyone thinks I bear a grudge against Vieille-Dent for my hand. It's not the hand. It's the fear. Brutus's forge is the only place on the island without a drop of water. There. No more questions.
textes.Tu veux une vraie arme, {surnom} ? Rappo: Want a real weapon, {surnom}? Bring me {manque} iron ores. You'll find them on the volcano's slopes, where the rock is red. I'll forge you a dwarven sword. A REAL one.
textes.Tu veux une vraie confidence, {surnom} ?: Want a real secret, {surnom}? No joke. I've asked Pivoine to marry me three times. Once in a riddle. Once with a flower in a vial. Once with the moon song. Three times, she said no, laughing: she thought I was joking. I don't know how to be serious for the fourth. I never learned.
textes.Tu veux vraiment savoir ? J'avais une fi: You really want to know? I had a fiancée, Mireille. She ran off with a lighthouse. I don't want to talk about it.
textes.Tu viens de chez Barnabé ? Il me fait ri: Have you just come from Barnabé's? He makes me laugh. He asked me whether elves eat shells.
textes.Tu viens de chez Barnabé, toi. Ça se sen: You've come from Barnabé's place. I can tell: you smell of seashells and old stories.
textes.Tu viens de la mer ? Il paraît qu'il y a: You come from the sea? They say some shells sing when you hold them to your ear. Will you bring me {manque}? Please, please, please!
You come from the village across the water.
textes.Tu viens me dire que ma rune est à l'env: Come to tell me my rune's upside down?
textes.Tu viens toujours goûter. C'est le plat: You always come to taste. It's the dish that makes the flavour, eh?
textes.Tu viens voir mon mérou ? Quarante kilos: Coming to see my grouper? Forty kilos.
textes.Tu vois ? C'est que tu en bois en cachet: See? That means you drink it in secret.
You see? You just had to be patient.
See? All's well, on both sides.
textes.Tu vois ce poing ? Il a envie de faire t: See this fist? It wants to make your acquaintance.
textes.Tu vois ce poêle, {surnom} ? Tout Carène: See this stove, {surnom}? All of Carène believes it hasn't gone cold since the shipwreck. The night Soazig passed away, I stayed at the sickbay till morning. When I came back, it was cold. I relit it before anyone was up, crying into the embers. That was twenty-five years ago. You're the first to know.
textes.Tu vois cette pointe dorée qui dépasse d: See that golden spire poking out of the water, to the south-west, when the sea is calm? It lights up at night. My grandfather said there was a city beneath it. A whole city! Under the water! … He did love his tall tales, my grandfather.
textes.Tu vois les pitons de pierre ? Ce sont l: See the rock spires? They're the fingers of a sleeping giant. Don't tickle him.
textes.Tu vois les rochers rouges, sur les pent: See the red rocks on the slopes? That's iron ore. Borin always wants more.
textes.Tu vois quoi, là-haut ?: What do you see up there?
textes.Tu voles déjà sur le dos de Ventaile !: You're already flying on Ventaile's back!
textes.Tu voudrais passer nos examens ? Trois é: You'd like to sit our exams? Three tests: the flames, the contract, the sparks. The flames demand mastery, the contract demands attention, and the sparks demand quick reflexes. The diploma makes you a Bachelor of Flames. Very fashionable to wear.
textes.Tu voulais bien croire aux fées. Alors,: You wanted to believe in fairies. So, is your heart ready? The ring is glowing bright these nights.
textes.Tu y retournes ? Tiens, j'en ai cueilli: Going back there? Here, I picked another one this morning. Say hello to Queen Oriane for me!
textes.Tu évites ? … Hm. Balam, le chasseur de: You avoid it? … Hm. Balam, the hunter from Yaxché, would say the same thing. Maybe he's right. Don't tell him I said so.
textes.Turbo joue. Personne ne parle. C'est la: Turbo is playing. Nobody talks. That's the rule.
textes.Turbo-Aventure 3000 a été supprimé. Grig: Turbo-Adventure 3000 has been deleted. Grigri went to the trash, and the trash was emptied.
textes.Tu… tu l'as trouvé. Le trésor du capitai: You… you found it. The captain's treasure. (Old Silas cries and laughs at once.) A hundred years I've been talking about it, and nobody believed me. Here, take this: his tricorn hat. He left it to me, the day he went to sea never to return. It suits you better than me. Go, heir of Barbe-Sanglante. And tell it well, this story. It's all that's left, in the end: stories.
textes.Tu… tu t'en fiches ? Gaston, bouche-toi: You… you don't care? Gaston, cover your ears.
textes.Télécharge plus de mémoire pour ton carn: Download more memory for your journal. Free*!  *not free
textes.Tête de méduse ! Ha ! C'est toi, l'admir: Jellyfish-head! Ha! It's you, Bartholomé's admirer! He recognised you, he's flapping his wings!
textes.UN CHEVAL ?! C'est un poulpe ! Huit bras: A HORSE?! It's an octopus! Eight arms! Eight! … OK, he wriggles while I draw. He's a bad customer. But don't criticise my art, or I'll tattoo a sardine on your forehead.
textes.UN CONCURRENT ! (Elle hurle tellement qu: A CONTENDER! (She yells so loudly that three pigeons fall off the roof.) Four rounds! Imps, hellhounds, bronze automatons… and in the final, GORGOTH THE HORNED! Strike the gong at the edge of the sand to start each round. If you leave the sand, you forfeit. If you fall, we pick you up. SIGNED UP!
textes.UN TROU ! Trois sur trois… ou presque. D: A HOLE! Three out of three… or nearly. Ask me for your prize, you've earned it.
textes.UNE MINI-PELLETEUSE ! Quand son godet se: A MINI DIGGER! When its bucket rises, a red circle marks where it will come down: get out of the circle! And watch out for its sweeps.
textes.Ulfa ! Mon ragoût fait encore boire tes: Ulfa! Is my stew still making your customers thirsty?
Ulfa! A fizz. A REAL one.
textes.Ulfa croit que je bois de l'eau. C'est d: Ulfa thinks I drink water. It's moon water. She wouldn't know the difference.
textes.Ulfa croit que je ne vois pas qu'elle me: Ulfa thinks I don't notice her watering down my fizz. I notice. I pretend not to. That's what being king is.
textes.Ulfa m'a prise comme apprentie. Quarante: Ulfa took me on as an apprentice. Forty years washing her barrels, hauling her barley and tasting her batches. She never let me touch the big vat. One morning, I scrubbed it till it shone, and I left. Dagna gave me her old oven, up on the terrace. I've been making fizz there for twenty years.
textes.Ulfa m'a tout appris, sauf à toucher la: Ulfa taught me everything except how to touch the big vat. She tells everyone she doesn't know me. It makes me laugh. A bit. The rest of the time, it stings.
textes.Ulfa me vole un rubis par soir et me les: Ulfa steals one ruby from me every evening and gives them all back at the Forge Festival. She's a thief. She's also the only person in the city who makes me laugh. That's no easy thing.
textes.Ulfa me vole un rubis par soir. Je le sa: Ulfa steals a ruby from me every evening. I know. I pretend not to. She gives them back at the Forge festival.
textes.Ulfa met de l'eau dans ma bière depuis q: Ulfa has been watering down my fizz for ninety years. I see it. I pretend. She thinks I don't see a thing. It's the oldest friendship in my kingdom.
textes.Ulfa ne me connaît pas, Dagna. Elle le d: Ulfa doesn't know me, Dagna. She tells everyone so.
textes.Ulfa parle plus qu'une cascade et elle c: Ulfa talks more than a waterfall and she thinks I drink water. It's moon water. She wouldn't know the difference. But her tavern is warm, and so is her laugh.
textes.Ulfa parle trop, rit trop, sert trop. Ma: Ulfa talks too much, laughs too much, serves too much. But after my watch, her fizz is the only thing that makes my knees bend. That's good.
textes.Ulfa sert mon ragoût à la Chope Ardente: Ulfa serves my stew at the Blazing Mug and swears it's her fizz that washes it down. I say it's my stew that makes them drink her fizz. We're both right.
textes.Un CHAT ! Je fais semblant de ne pas l'a: A CAT! I'm pretending I didn't see it.
textes.Un HUMAIN ?! Un vrai ?! Tu as des oreill: A HUMAN?! A real one?! You've got round ears! I'm Nimiel! I'm forty-two, I'm still little. What about you?
textes.Un accident, Zébuline ! Le comptoir penc: An accident, Zébuline! The counter slopes!
textes.Un air pour la journée. Tu veux une chan: A tune for the day. Want a song?
textes.Un allongé, comme d'habitude ? Je m'en s: A long one, as usual? I remember. I remember everything, it's my failing.
textes.Un ami ! Ah, mon ami… Tu viens de dire l: A friend! Ah, my friend… You've just said the only thing that isn't on any of my lists. Keep that one safe.
textes.Un ami, ça ne se troque pas, tu m'as dit: A friend can't be swapped, you told me. So I won't swap you. Not even for two.
textes.Un ampli, une batterie, deux musiciens q: An amp, a drum kit, two musicians head-banging… and earplugs on the table, for guests.
textes.Un animal ! Très aztèque. Nos jours port: An animal! Very Aztec. Our days are named after animals: the rabbit, the deer, the eagle, the jaguar. Choose well: your animal will follow you all your life.
textes.Un ankylosaure (Queue-Massue) ! Son dos: An ankylosaur (Club-Tail)! Its back is hard as stone. When its tail rises, back off: it's going to spin. After its blow, it catches its breath: hit it on the head!
textes.Un anneau d'or fin avec un petit diamant: A fine gold ring with a small diamond, engraved on the inside: "H & L, forever".
textes.Un anneau de verre taillé de la grande l: A ring of cut glass from the lighthouse's great lens. It focuses light like a giant magnifying glass.
textes.Un appareil photo holographique, un peu: A holographic camera, a little sticky (Glorb is gelatinous). It takes photos in three dimensions, and sometimes in four.
textes.Un apprenti demande à l'archimage : « Ma: An apprentice asks the archmage: “Master, how does one become wise?” “By doing silly things.” “And how does one do silly things?” “Ask Oscar.”
textes.Un après-midi au grill, Omar a tapé un r: One afternoon at the grill, Omar beat a rhythm on the table so hard that my sardines jumped off the plate. Two in the dust, one in my tea. Omar didn't even slow down. He said: “They're dancing, that's a good sign.” Mustapha grilled me two more. The one in the tea, I left it to swim.
textes.Un après-midi au grill, on répétait pour: One afternoon at the grill, we were rehearsing for the festival. I hit a ta-ka a bit hard, and Hamid's sardines jumped off his plate: two on the ground, one in his tea. I didn't slow down. I said: “They're dancing, that's a good sign.” Hamid looked at the one in his tea and let it swim. It's been our refrain ever since.
textes.Un après-midi, Roux s'est allongé sous l: One afternoon, Roux lay down under the tree in the Games Clearing saying “five minutes”. I started the stopwatch. Three hours and twelve minutes, {surnom}! Village nap record. He often asks me to remind people. There, done.
textes.Un après-midi, Suie, mon chiot le plus p: One afternoon, Suie, my most timid pup, had disappeared. I searched everywhere. I found him in Mother Brasille's watering can, asleep, and her sitting beside him, singing him a lullaby very softly. She saw me. She denied it. She blushed. On ash-grey skin, that shows a lot. Since then, Suie goes back there every day.
textes.Un après-midi, Théo a planté un panneau: One afternoon, Théo put up a sign in front of his castle: “Entry: one shell.” The tourists paid! By evening, he had a whole bucket of shells. He gave me one, “for the sand rent”. I hung it above the till. It's my first business shell.
textes.Un après-midi, Youssef a sorti une dorad: One afternoon, Youssef pulled out a sea bream, a real one, as lovely as one of Halima's dishes. He looked at it, it looked at him, and he put it back in the water. He told me: “It looked like it wanted to live.” I laughed for an hour. An hour! The only fish of the week on this jetty, and he lets it go.
textes.Un après-midi, il me croyait endormie au: One afternoon, he thought I was asleep at the bottom of his boat. He whispered to a heron: “The flood is rain in the mountains, not the tears of Isis.” I answered without opening my eyes: “And the rain, Khéty, who sends it?” He dropped his oar. The heron left. Since then, Khéty confides in the fish, who don't repeat anything.
textes.Un après-midi, j'ai fait ma ronde des cr: One afternoon, I made my round of the battlements, as always: slow steps, hand on my sabre, a glance through every arrow slit. Behind me, the whole way, Yasmine did the same. Same steps, same hand, same glance. I only saw her at the end, when I turned round. The guards had been laughing for a quarter of an hour. I nearly laughed. Nearly.
textes.Un après-midi, j'ai réussi une bulle de: One afternoon, I managed a two-metre bubble. Professor Boum ran over and stuck his head inside, “to feel the pressure”. For a whole minute, he talked to us as if from inside a jar: “Fffformidable, Bbbasile!” When it burst, he had soap right into his moustache. He said it was the best minute of his week.
textes.Un après-midi, j'ai sorti une dorade, un: One afternoon, I pulled out a sea bream, a real one, all shiny. It looked at me with its round eye. It looked like it really wanted to live. So I put it back in the water. Si Larbi laughed for an hour. An hour! The only fish of the week. Don't tell Zohra: for her, releasing a sea bream is a crime.
textes.Un après-midi, j'entends « Au secours !: One afternoon, I hear “Help!” from the beach hut. I jump off my chair, sprint, vault over the counter… Kiki was standing on a stool, a crab hanging off his sandal. A little crab, the size of a coin. He said it was a rescue all the same. He counted it in the weekly total.
textes.Un après-midi, je lui montre le nœud de: One afternoon, I show her the bowline. An hour later, I find Amine tied to the fountain on the square, trussed like a roast, with a perfect knot. Nobody could undo it. They had to call me. Yasmine told me: “He wanted to be captain.” I undid the knot. Then I congratulated her. Don't tell Zohra.
textes.Un après-midi, je me croyais seule. Je l: One afternoon, I thought I was alone. I was reading “The Foam of Your Heart”, by Sylvia Delarive, behind the counter, at the best chapter. The bell rang. I slid the book under the peaches. It was the peach tourist. She took her peaches. And the book appeared. There was nothing I could do.
textes.Un après-midi, je me suis endormi au-des: One afternoon, I fell asleep over my charts, spread out on the lounge rug. When I woke up, they had been arranged by depth: the lightest on the left, the darkest on the right, lined up perfectly straight. Edmond, at the reception desk, was reading the paper. He said nothing. I understood I had an assistant.
textes.Un atelier en désordre. Des engrenages,: A messy workshop. Gears, wires, a machine smoking a little… and someone muttering calculations.
textes.Un autel de pierre, vide, taché de vieux: A stone altar, empty, stained with old blood. Carved on it: “The blades are hungry. The Twins promised them the flesh of all beasts… and the blades lay down.”
textes.Un autodidacte ! Laissez-moi deviner : d: Self-taught! Let me guess: seawater on everything, and a bandage made from whatever's lying around? Diagnosis: brave, a bit stubborn. I know the type.
textes.Un automate de bronze ! Il lève sa halle: A bronze automaton! It raises its halberd before striking: parry or roll. The Cog (key 3) freezes it for a good while.
textes.Un autre chemin. Comme Grimli. Par-desso: Another way. Like Grimli. Underneath, round the back, through the hole. Hmph. I'll be keeping an eye on you.
textes.Un aventurier ! Comme moi à ton âge. Sau: An adventurer! Like me at your age. Except I got stuck here. Don't do the same.
textes.Un badge en plastique gris, avec une pho: A grey plastic badge, with a photo of someone who isn't smiling and the words "ACCESS: EVERYTHING. SMILING: FORBIDDEN." It opens the doors on the lower floor of the Grey Factory.
textes.Un badge rond qui brille, avec ton nom é: A round, shiny badge, with your name written in Lumen letters (which look like little dancing stars): "VERY WELCOME VISITOR — HEAVY-FEET, BUT KIND".
textes.Un bar ? Les bars ne savent pas ce qu'il: A sea bass? Sea bass don't know what they're saying.
A sea bass told me “maybe”, Gwenola.
A boat. Fair enough. You came by sea. Here, a boat is a canoe, with someone paddling. I'll draw you paddling. Very fast.
textes.Un battement d'ailes énorme fait vacille: An enormous beating of wings makes the flames flicker. A shape drops from the vault: a man's body, a bat's head, huge wings… CAMAZOTZ!
textes.Un batteur pour les Rats de Cale: A drummer for the Bilge Rats
textes.Un beau centimètre, Marcel ! Un centimèt: A fine centimetre, Marcel! A historic centimetre!
textes.Un beau pavillon tout neuf ! J'ai hissé: A lovely brand-new flag! I've hoisted the Laughing Seagull; choose the design you like.
textes.Un biscuit en forme de croissant de lune: A crescent-moon biscuit, sprinkled with silver sugar. Crunchy on one side, soft on the other (the Lumens can't make up their minds). Restores one heart.
textes.Un bleu ! Pour le douzième !: A blue one! For number twelve!
textes.Un bleu, pour le capitaine. Le dernier g: A blue one, for the captain. The last free one. Until tomorrow.
textes.Un bocal de « soupe de tout le monde »,: A jar of steaming "everyone's soup", with a pallet-wood lid made by Copeau. You never know exactly what's in it, but it's always good. Restores two hearts.
textes.Un bol de cacao mousseux, chez Ix Chab: A bowl of frothy cocoa, at Ix Chab's
textes.Un bol de nouilles, s'il vous plaît ! Av: A bowl of noodles, please! With a smiley!
textes.Un bol fumant de ragoût aux champignons: A steaming bowl of ember mushroom stew. It burns your tongue and restores four hearts.
textes.Un bon feu. La réponse la plus simple, e: A good fire. The simplest answer, and the truest. Come and sit by the Heart whenever you like. It isn't mine: it belongs to everyone who's cold.
textes.Un bon livre. J'en suis au meilleur pass: A good book. I'm at the best part, so be quick.
A good tool is all in the handle.
textes.Un bon repas ! Hé hé. Bobor serait d'acc: A good meal! Heh heh. Bobor would agree with you. Full belly, warm heart: the old folks said so already. I'll save you a slice of brioche.
textes.Un bouclier d'épines entoure la Reine !: A shield of thorns surrounds the Queen! Your blows do nothing now… Awaken the three roses of light (E)!
textes.Un bras ! Gauche ou droit ? Ne dis rien,: An arm! Left or right? Don't say anything, I'll guess by watching you walk. … The left. No? Oh well. Medicine is not an exact science.
textes.Un bras qui sentirait la chaleur d'une m: An arm that could feel the warmth of a hand. Léonce's, when he tugs me along to show me a rocket. Brass is sturdy, but it can't feel a thing.
textes.Un brevet cette semaine, Philibert ? Mon: A patent this week, Philibert? Show me.
textes.Un bâtard au bandana rouge sort de sous: A mutt in a red bandana crawls out from under a car wreck, one ear up, one ear down. It sniffs you, sneezes, and starts wagging its tail so hard its whole behind wiggles. SARDINE! It follows you now: take it back to Tornade!
textes.Un cadeau ! Je pourrai le troquer… non,: A present! I could swap it… no, I'm keeping it. Thank you!
textes.Un cadeau ! Que ta main ne se vide jamai: A gift! May your hand never be empty.
textes.Un cadeau ? Formidable. Je vais lui ajou: A present? Splendid. I'll add an engine to it.
textes.Un cadeau ? Merci ! Je vais voir s'il es: A present? Thank you! Let me see if it's magic. … No. But it's sweet.
textes.Un cadeau ? Pour moi ? … Qu'est-ce que t: A gift? For me? … What do you want in return?
textes.Un cadeau ? À Carène, on dit merci avec: A present? In Carène, we say thank you with a bowl of sparkling apple. I owe you one.
textes.Un cadeau ? À Port-Azur, on dit merci av: A present? In Port-Azur, we say thanks with a coffee. I owe you one.
textes.Un cadeau d'un grand ! Je le mettrai sur: A gift from a tall one! I'll put it on the shelf.
textes.Un cadeau de la surface ! Les enfants vo: A gift from the surface! The children will want to see it.
textes.Un cadeau des humains ! Je le montrerai: A gift from the humans! I'll show it to the others.
textes.Un cadeau des humains… Je le montrerai a: A gift from the humans… I'll show it to my people. They'll be curious.
textes.Un cadeau qu'on aime, ça ouvre les cœurs: A gift people love opens hearts. A gift they don't love… closes them a little.
textes.Un café du Brasier, au bord des bains: A Brasier coffee, by the baths
textes.Un café noir comme la lave refroidie, to: A coffee as black as cooled lava, roasted on the Ember Heart itself, served piping hot at Au Diable Repu. Restores one heart, and wide-open eyes.
textes.Un café à vapeur au comptoir: A steam coffee at the counter
textes.Un café, Raymond ? Tu as perdu ?: A coffee, Raymond? Did you lose?
textes.Un café, {surnom} ? Il sort de la chaudi: A coffee, {surnom}? Fresh out of the boiler.
textes.Un café. Et je n'ai pas perdu, j'ai été: A coffee. And I didn't lose, I was robbed.
textes.Un café. Et un biscuit. Enfin, la moitié: A coffee. And a biscuit. Well, half of one.
textes.Un caillou ! Le roi des trésors ! Ça ne: A pebble! The king of treasures! It doesn't rust, it doesn't break down, it keeps your hand warm. You've got the soul of a rag-and-bone woman. That's a compliment.
textes.Un caillou ? … Une pièce. Et c'est bien: A pebble? … One coin. And that's well paid: I only do it because it's pretty. It's pretty, right?
textes.Un caillou lisse. Servira à fabriquer de: A smooth pebble. Good for making tools.
textes.Un caillou noir et lourd, encore un peu: A heavy black stone, still a little warm, that fell from the sky onto Astralys on a night of shooting stars. It has an iron sheen and smells like stormy rain.
textes.Un caillou-qui-chante ! Écoute-le siffle: A singing pebble! Listen to it whistle! I'll hang it under the west bridge this very evening. Here, my finest golden acorn, found at the top of the Mother Oak. Plumette, the postmistress, adores them.
textes.Un canard de laiton à remontoir. Il nage: A wind-up brass duck. It swims, it quacks, it doesn't lay eggs.
textes.Un candidat libre ! Hm. Trois épreuves,: A private candidate! Hm. Three trials, like everyone else. The flames: Miss Sulfura wants to see if you know where fire is born. The contract: our librarian, Ombreline, will have you sign… after reading, I hope. The sparks: in front of me, you'll crunch an infernal chili pepper without crying. Or almost without crying.
textes.Un canon à confettis : à bord, touche K: A confetti cannon: on board, press K (B on the controller, A in VR). To celebrate every arrival, every treasure, every Tuesday.
textes.Un canon. Le plus gros de l'archipel. Qu: A cannon. The biggest in the archipelago. For me to fire it once, just once, over the bay, on a festival night. BOOM. And for everyone to shut up. At last.
textes.Un caravanier a voulu m'acheter une toil: A caravan trader wanted to buy one of Selma's canvases from me, a boat at sunrise, hanging above the well. He offered a week's lodging for it. I said: “Not for sale. It's mine.” He doubled it. I said no. Selma was watching from the terrace. That evening, I made her a tajine. For nothing. For the boat.
textes.Un caravanier m'a montré un jour un de m: One day a caravanner showed me one of my corsair sabres, bought from Salomé. She'd told him it had belonged to a famous pirate, “Captain Floc'h”. He'd paid a fortune for it. I went to see her, furious. She gave me half the fortune. I left less furious.
textes.Un carnet couvert de poussière. Sur la d: A dust-covered notebook. On the last page:
textes.Un cartographe ne se perd jamais, Taille: A cartographer never gets lost, Taillefer. He explores.
textes.Un catalogue complet. Chaque livre de la: A complete catalogue. Every book in the library in its place, on its card, and not one missing. Three thousand. I repeat: three thousand.
textes.Un cercle de bois tressé d'un filet de c: A wooden hoop woven with a hemp net, with beads and feathers. The net catches bad dreams; the good ones slide down the feathers.
textes.Un champignard ! Une petite créature cha: A mushling! A mischievous little mushroom creature. Its spore cloud doesn't hurt… but it makes you sneeze. One little tap and it scurries off; two, and poof!
textes.Un champignon au chapeau violet, constel: A mushroom with a purple cap, dotted with spots that shine like stars. Lulu says it takes you to the fairy kingdom, above the clouds. "Bite" it to make the journey; up there, the mushroom ring will bring you back to the beach.
textes.Un champignon de braise ?! Ho ho ! Ça, c: An ember mushroom?! Ho ho! Now THAT is a dwarf soup! It stings the eyes AND the beard! Here, taste, and take some for the road.
textes.Un champignon féerique au chapeau orange: A fairy mushroom with an orange cap, on a spiral stalk that bounces all by itself. "Munch": you jump three times higher and float gently back down (for a while). A storybook mushroom: in a real forest, you must NEVER eat a mushroom you don't know.
textes.Un champignon féerique aux lamelles de t: A fairy mushroom with gills of every colour. "Munch": the world ripples with colours, you run faster, and you leave a rainbow trail. A storybook mushroom: in a real forest, you must NEVER eat a mushroom you don't know.
textes.Un champignon féerique pâle et argenté q: A pale, silvery fairy mushroom that glows like a little piece of the moon. "Munch": you can see the invisible (glowing hiding places appear all over the island). A storybook mushroom: in a real forest, you must NEVER eat a mushroom you don't know.
textes.Un champignon féerique violet aux lamell: A purple fairy mushroom with gills shaped like a little mouth, which goes "blah blah blah" when you hold it up to your ear. "Munch": you understand animals. A storybook mushroom: in a real forest, you must NEVER eat a mushroom you don't know.
textes.Un champignon rouge et tiède qui pousse: A red, warm mushroom that grows in the ash, near the steam vents. Dagna puts it in her stew. Restores one heart.
textes.Un chapelet de perles de bois clair, ave: A string of pale wooden beads, with a little gold sun at the end. Sister Pétronille's, swallowed by the Queen Frog of the lake. It smells a little of mud (and a lot of frog).
textes.Un chat ! Comme moi ! Il a les oreilles: A cat! Like me! Does it have straight ears? Miou has a crooked one. It's the prettiest. Cats are the best, there's even a cat goddess!
textes.Un chat roux a volé la carte au trésor d: A ginger cat has stolen the treasure map of Captain Croc-de-Sel, the pirate moored at Tazira. And cats climb
A ginger cat has stolen the treasure map of Captain Croc-de-Sel, the pirate moored at Tazira. And cats climb…
textes.Un chat roux te fixe. Puis un noir. Puis: A ginger cat stares at you. Then a black one. Then a white one. You're outnumbered.
textes.Un chaudron qui bouillonne, une odeur de: A bubbling cauldron, a smell of sulfur… and a frog in a wizard hat, sitting on a chair.
textes.Un chevalier ne se fatigue jamais. Il… s: A knight never tires. He… rests strategically.
textes.Un chien ! Je le savais. Enfin, je m'en: A dog! I knew it. Well, I suspected it. Well… Case closed! Margaux will leave him one croissant a day, and everyone will be happy. Excellent work, detective.
textes.Un chien ? Comme Abouti, le chien de Hap: A dog? Like Abouti, Hapou's dog! Or like Peek', Kinich's dog! Dogs are nice too. But they don't purr.
A dog of my own. Brioche, if he wants. He'd sleep at the foot of my bed and eat the croissants that go wrong. Mum says hers never go wrong. So I'll make some go wrong myself.
textes.Un chien. Je l'ignore avec une grande di: A dog. I ignore it with great dignity.
textes.Un chiffon rouge troué, cloué sur un bât: A red rag full of holes, nailed to a stick, with a big tooth painted on it (crookedly). The banner of the goblin chief of the Goblin Wood. Sir Tancrède wants to bring it back as proof of his first real feat.
textes.Un chocolat ! Je vais vous en préparer u: A hot chocolate! I'll make you a proper one, thick enough to stand a spoon up in. For rainy days. It'll be our secret: the machine isn't very fond of milk.
textes.Un château ! Mais le vrai, le grand, il: A castle! But the real one, the big one, is over there, at the very end of the beach, to the west. It's the Downpour castle: the sand piled up all by itself, with towers and everything. And the yellow pot, number four, rolled inside! I saw it! But the sea came in, and now I can't find the door. Would you look for it? You have longer arms than me.
textes.Un cidre brut des pommiers de la côte ou: A dry sparkling apple drink from the west coast orchards, fizzing like the sea on a windy day. Restores one heart.
textes.Un cidre de Montjoie à la Grenouille Rep: A Montjoie apple fizz at La Grenouille Repue
textes.Un client ! Enfin… un grand. Orsik Serti: A customer! Well… a tall one. Orsik Sertissor, jeweller. I only buy what sparkles. Do you sparkle? No. Your pockets, maybe.
textes.Un client ! Un GRAND client ! Bienvenue: A customer! A BIG customer! Welcome to Mélisse's, nectars and sweets. Please don't step on my flowers.
textes.Un client de Carène est revenu au Bazar,: A customer from Carène came back to the Bazaar, furious: there was something in his box of nothing! A spider. I refunded him, of course. Philibert was in despair: “Then it's not useless any more.” Since then, on rainy days, he comes to check the boxes one by one, and he writes the “useless” labels in his very best handwriting.
textes.Un client est revenu lui demander quel d: A customer came back to ask her which dragon his sword had cut. Ferronde came to my stall, furious. I told her: “A small one.” She laughed so hard Zébuline spilled her pepper. Since then, she delivers her blades with a label: “This one has cut nothing at all.” I take them off.
textes.Un codex se lit en images : un pied qui: A codex is read in pictures: a walking foot is a journey; a tongue in front of a mouth is speech; a little dot is a number. The world is a picture book, if you know how to look.
textes.Un coffre ! Pauvre ceinture. Elle doit s: A chest! Poor belt. It must be so bored.
textes.Un coffre laissé par les Seigneurs « pou: A chest left by the Lords “for their guests”: a haunch of venison, and a few coins.
textes.Un colosse de roche se dresse sous le cr: A colossus of rock rises beneath the crystal: THE HEART GUARDIAN! Four runes glow on it, in the colours of the four seals.
textes.Un colosse des eaux profondes, au bout d: A giant of the deep waters, at the end of the jetties. Restores three hearts.
textes.Un compagnon de grève ! Montre-moi tes p: A fellow beachcomber! Show me your best ones someday. I'll show you mine. There are two hundred and twelve: keep the afternoon free.
textes.Un concert ! Avec des rats ! (Il plisse: A concert! With rats! (He squints.) Musician rats, not kitchen rats? Well. I'll hang it above the counter, next to my napkin frog. They go well together. And I'll come! With my number nine frog in a crust: the one you can eat while jumping. It fits very nicely in the hand. It was designed for adventurers on the run.
textes.Un concert ? Des punks ? (Il regarde l'a: A concert? Punks? (He looks at the poster, the rat, the mohawk.) Mamma mia, what a rat! He's got my cousin Gino's mohawk! I'll put it in my window, next to the bouillabaisse. And you know what? I'll come! With a cooking pot! A fish soup for the whole pit! Punks eat, right? Everybody eats. Even while jumping.
textes.Un concert de punks ? (Il fait grincer s: A punk concert? (He makes his fiddle screech, delighted.) People who play loud and fast and jump all over the place? Why, they're pirates without a ship! I'll hang it above my stage. And I'll come! With my fiddle! I've always dreamed of playing a jig with an electric guitar. Tell your singer that Tom the Fiddler will be in the pit. Front row. Wearing a tricorn. She'll recognise me.
textes.Un conseil de tavernier pour les Neuf Ce: A tavern keeper's tip for the Nine Circles: down there, the deeper you go, the colder it gets. Drink something hot before you set off, and take something to perk you up. A hot sulphur punch warms you right to the tips of your horns. Even if you don't have any.
textes.Un conseil, tout bas : dans l'Arène, ne: A tip, very quietly: in the Arena, never stand still. The imps are quick, the hounds pounce, the automatons hit hard but turn slowly. And Gorgoth… Gorgoth doesn't turn at all. Make the most of it.
textes.Un conseil, voyageur : quand un requin f: A tip, traveller: when a shark charges at you, hit it at the last moment. And jellyfish: you don't brush against them. Ever.
textes.Un coquillage ? Je le prends. Pas pour m: A shell? I'll take it. Not for me, mind you: so Barnabé doesn't get it. Heh heh heh.
textes.Un coquillage ?! Tu me prends pour Barna: A shell?! Do I look like Barnabé to you? Take it ba… no, leave it. Clou will throw it away.
textes.Un coquillage qui chante, Momo. Colle to: A singing shell, Momo. Put your ear to it.
textes.Un coquillage, c'est un trésor quand mêm: A shell is still a treasure! Driss gives one to his wife every time he comes home, and she keeps them in a big jar. So it's a treasure. That's logical.
textes.Un coquillage. Je ne sais pas du tout d': A shell. I have absolutely no idea where it came from.
textes.Un corbeau a perdu une plume magnifique: A raven dropped a magnificent feather on the square, jet black with blue glints. We saw it at the same moment, she from her tent, I from my tower. I ran. So did she. She's younger. She won. The next day, I found the feather cut into a nib on my door, with a note: “For your maps.” I only use it for important islands.
textes.Un crabe ? Il paie un loyer ?: A crab? Is he paying rent?
textes.Un crabe de roche ! Quand il lève les pi: A rock crab! When it raises its pincers, back off or parry (F)… then strike it.
textes.Un crabe grand comme ma cabane, à l'est: A crab as big as my hut, east of the pillared hall? Its shell is steel. Wait until it sticks its claws into the rock… then hit it.
textes.Un crissement de pierre au-dessus de toi: A grinding of stone above you… The gargoyles on the ramparts open their eyes!
textes.Un cristal bleu, froid comme le soir, ga: A blue crystal, cold as the evening, guarded by the suits of armour in the armoury. It fits into the Seal of the Winds.
textes.Un cristal bleu-violet qui pousse sous l: A blue-violet crystal that grows beneath the floating island of Astralys and hums very softly, as if it were singing to itself. The Lumens make engines, lamps and music boxes out of it.
textes.Un cristal d'un jaune vif, en aiguilles,: A bright yellow crystal in needles, picked up at the edge of the hot springs. It smells of eggs and matches. Zigomar, the fireworks maker, makes his finest rockets with it.
textes.Un cristal des sources ! Bien. Le soufre: A spring crystal! Good. Sulfur, air, a spark: that's fire. (She snaps her fingers: the crystal bursts into a little blue flame.) Trial of the flames: passed!
textes.Un cristal doré, tiède comme le soleil d: A golden crystal, warm as the morning sun, won by ringing the Citadel's bell tower. It fits into the Seal of the Winds.
textes.Un cristal violet, cueilli au sommet des: A purple crystal, gathered at the top of the Fangs, where lightning strikes most often. A little yellow spark runs inside it; it crackles when you squeeze it. Violette needs it for her great spell.
textes.Un croc blanc, long comme un doigt, enco: A white fang, as long as a finger, still warm. Kraxx, the armourer, says it makes very good arrowheads (and very good toothpicks).
