textes.Un crocodile ! Quand il ouvre grand la g: A crocodile! When it opens its jaws wide and flattens itself, it's about to leap at you: step aside (or roll, Ctrl), then strike while it recovers.
textes.Un croissant doré du Pain Doré, encore t: A golden croissant from the Pain Doré, still warm, that leaves crumbs everywhere. Restores one and a half hearts.
textes.Un cuissot de cerf enveloppé dans une fe: A haunch of venison wrapped in a banana leaf, from Balam's hunt. Not for you: for an offering. The Twins of the Popol Vuh knew who to give it to.
textes.Un cœur qui consomme plus que toute la c: A heart that uses more than the whole city.
textes.Un de mes plus vieux livres parle d'une: One of my oldest books speaks of an island, far to the west, beyond the island of the dwarves: the Island of the Three Suns. Three peoples live there, each under its own sun, with pyramids, sphinxes, feathered serpents. I'd give my beard to see it. Well, part of my beard.
textes.Un dernier marathon, le grand : celui de: One last marathon, the big one: the archipelago marathon! From the village all the way to Port-Azur, with Kevin swimming beside me for the crossing. Finally, a winner!
textes.Un des huit rubis de ma couronne est fau: One of the eight rubies in my crown is fake. I knew it on coronation day: walking past the lava channels, seven rubies lit up and the eighth just sat there looking silly. I said nothing. Orsik sweats every time I touch my crown. It's my little revenge for the bills.
textes.Un des livres de la bibliothèque d'Arcan: One of the books from the library of Arcanelle, blown away during the great storm. Its pages still flap a little, like wings. Théophraste is waiting for them.
textes.Un diablotin demande à sa mère : « Maman: A little imp asks his mother: “Mum, can I go and play in the lava?” She answers: “Yes, but put your coat on, it's barely lukewarm today!”
textes.Un dimanche, sur le banc, je lui ai raco: One Sunday, on the bench, I told her about the day Marius tried to harpoon a jellyfish, thinking it was an octopus. She laughed. All of a sudden, loud, her hand over her mouth. It was the first time since Marius. I didn't say a thing. I looked at the sea. I was afraid it would stop.
textes.Un disque d'argent pâle où dort un crois: A pale silver disc where a crescent moon sleeps; a light mist always drifts from it. The seal of Ramure. It awakened the Moonglow in you.
textes.Un disque d'or rouge, chaud comme une pi: A disc of red gold, warm as a stone in the sun, engraved with a sun rising over a dune. The seal of the desert. It awakened the Flame in you.
textes.Un disque de bronze aux bords dentés, qu: A bronze disc with toothed edges, which spins by itself when laid flat. The seal of the highlands. It awakened the Cog in you.
textes.Un disque de nacre bleu-vert, frais comm: A blue-green mother-of-pearl disc, cool as a wave, engraved with a compass rose. The seal of Carène. It awakened the Gust in you.
textes.Un do, Django ! Rien qu'un do !: One C, Django! Just one C!
textes.Un doigt de chaque main, alors !: One finger on each hand, then!
textes.Un doigt de mousse, Chak. Comme d'habitu: One finger of froth, Chak. As usual.
textes.Un donjon ! J'en ai vaincu cent. Enfin,: A dungeon! I've conquered a hundred. Well, three. Well, I've seen one.
textes.Un dragon-poisson avec une couronne, alo: A dragon-fish with a crown, then!
textes.Un drame ! Il me faut du poisson frais d: A disaster! I need fresh fish of the day for my Sunday bouillabaisse. Two sea bream, two mackerel. Caught by you, I trust you.
textes.Un drone-huissier ! Il tourne au-dessus: A bailiff drone! It circles above you reading out its notices… then dives in for a shock. Dodge its dive: it stays low, out of breath, for a moment. That's your chance to strike!
textes.Un duel ? J'ai pas cogné quelqu'un depui: A duel? I haven't thumped anyone since… this morning. Come on, then!
textes.Un duel, un vrai, devant toute l'île : m: A duel, a real one, in front of the whole island: me against Borée. Fire against ice. And at the end, steam everywhere, and nobody would know who won. It would be perfect.
textes.Un dé est tombé de sa manche, un soir, s: One evening, a die fell out of his sleeve onto my baize. I picked it up and rolled it in my palm. It sounded a little too heavy on the six side. I handed it back to him, saying: “You've lost a tooth, sir.” The whole room laughed. He laughed too, louder than the others. He's a quality opponent. I'll grant him that.
textes.Un elfe entre dans une mine. … C'est tou: An elf walks into a mine. … That's it. He's still bumping his head. HO HO!
A child of the surface… under my dome. The first in a thousand years. Come closer. I am Néréa, queen of Atlantis. You wear the mask of the Sky Kings; they were our friends, long ago.
textes.Un engrenage de laiton aux dents bien ta: A brass gear with neatly cut teeth, from the workshops of Cliquetis. It turns all by itself if you blow on it (no, that's not true, but it's nice to say).
textes.Un engrenage de quatorze dents, en or ma: A fourteen-tooth gear of solid gold, engraved "F. Cogne". The Fair's perpetual motion engine is missing it.
textes.Un escalier de lumière, des marches qui: A staircase of light, steps warming up one by one… and there you are in the nave of the Forge Cathedral, the Eternal Flame in your hands.
textes.Un escalier de lumière… et te voilà au s: A staircase of light… and there you are at the top of the Great Temple, above Lake Aztlán.
textes.Un escalier de service, des marches de t: A service staircase, sheet-metal steps that echo. On the wall: “Step 1 of 64. Please count.”
textes.Un feu d'artifice de pétales, si grand q: A firework of petals, so big it would cover the whole city, from the clock tower down to the harbour. For Professor Boum to look up and be left speechless. And for once, without an explosion. Just colours falling gently.
textes.Un feu d'artifice éternel… Oh. Oh ! Une: An everlasting firework… Oh. Oh! A rocket that never falls back down, that shines all night long… But that's a star! You've invented the stars! Bravo!
textes.Un feu de camp ! Avec des amis autour et: A campfire! With friends around it and stories rising with the smoke. That's Grandpa's favourite light. Mine too, I think.
textes.Un feu follet ! Quand il se met à brille: A will-o'-the-wisp! When it starts glowing very brightly, it's going to dash straight at you: step aside, then strike.
A thread, Mérit. A tiny white thread.
textes.Un fil, une perle, une plume…: A thread, a bead, a feather…
textes.Un filet sans un seul trou. Un jour, rie: A net without a single hole. One day, just one. I'd sit beside it, hands on my knees, and do nothing. Fatima would say I was ill.
textes.Un filou au grand cœur, ou un grand cœur: A rascal with a big heart, or a big heart that's a rascal, I've never known which. He swapped my cape, little one. My cape! I pretend I'm still cross. It keeps him busy.
textes.Un flocon tombé sur les falaises du nord: A snowflake that fell on the northern cliffs of Arcanelle. It doesn't melt, even in the palm of your hand. Borée Givrelin makes it the key to the frost spell.
textes.Un foir, Filas a raconté qu'il avait dan: One evening, Thilas told how he'd danthed with a mermaid. The whole room went “Ohhh”. Me, I athked: “Did she danthe well?” He thaid: “Badly. She had no feet.” I don't know if he'th lying. But it'th the only thtory where the detail maketh thenthe. Tho I believe that one.
textes.Un foir, un feune matelot f'est moqué de: One evening, a young thailor made fun of my two teeth at the Crâne Fendu. Belle-Humeur didn't hear a thing, of courthe. But he thaw the youngthter laughing and pointing at me. He thtood up. The youngthter that back down all by himthelf, very quickly. Belle-Humeur yelled “WHAT?!”, and that back down too. We didn't thay a word. We're even.
textes.Un fondouk, c'est une auberge autour d'u: A fondouk is an inn built around a courtyard. This one is three hundred years old. My ancestors lodged merchants from every land here. The walls have heard every language.
textes.Un fou rire général. Quelqu'un pleure de: A general fit of giggles. Someone is crying with laughter into a napkin.
textes.Un fragment d'amulette avec un œil ? Sur: An amulet fragment with an eye? On my map, there are three eyes drawn. One under the village… one under the jungle… and one under the sea, in between. Good luck.
textes.Un frigo qui chante l'opéra, livré ce so: A fridge that sings opera, delivered tonight by drone!
textes.Un gagnant ! Je le savais, tu as des mol: A winner! I knew it, you've got winner's calves. Then come under the arches: Bondi's bored, all alone at the top of the board.
textes.Un galet percé de petits trous. Quand le: A pebble pierced with little holes. When the wind blows through it, it whistles a clear note. The start of Bedaine's Great Swap.
textes.Un gardien de corail se réveille ! Il lè: A coral guardian awakens! It raises its spear before striking: roll (Ctrl) or parry (F). Three sword blows in a row hurt.
textes.Un geyser ! L'eau jaillit du fond du bas: A geyser! Water bursts from the bottom of the basin and flings you up. Watch the bubbles: they give a warning.
textes.Un gland d'or contre une plume ?: A golden acorn for a feather?
textes.Un gland doré, tout brillant, trouvé à l: A golden acorn, all shiny, found at the top of the Mother Oak. The owls of Ramure love them.
textes.Un golem des hauteurs ! Quand il lève se: A highland golem! When it raises both fists above its head, it's going to smash the ground in front of it: back off or roll (Ctrl)… then strike. Your blows don't stop it.
textes.Un goéland entre dans la taverne. Gwenol: A seagull walks into the tavern. Gwenola tells it: “We don't serve birds.” It answers: “I'm not a bird, I'm a customer with feathers.” She served it. It didn't pay.
textes.Un grand ! Approche, approche, mais pas: A tall one! Come closer, come closer, but not too near the anvil. Borin Barbe-de-Fer, master blacksmith. The best on the mountain. Ask anyone. Well, ask me.
textes.Un grand ! Sur la terrasse ! Bonjour, bo: A tall one! On the terrace! Hello, hello.
textes.Un grand banquet : la terrasse et la cit: A great banquet: the terrace and the city at the same table, from the king down to the last coal carrier. Even Bramm. Especially Bramm. I want to see him laugh with his mouth full.
textes.Un grand coquillage rose et blanc, coupé: A big pink and white shell, cut in a spiral: the conch of the wind god, Ehécatl. When you blow into it, you hear the sea, and the wind rises.
textes.Un grand feutre violet, un galon d'or, e: A big purple felt hat, with gold braid and a white feather as long as an arm. Baron Barthélemy's favourite hat. It flies off at the slightest gust of wind, and the Baron searches the whole island for it.
textes.Un grand plat doré : les tagliatelles de: A big golden dish: Mamma Lasagna's tagliatelle, the sacred sauce from the Cooking Pot, three meatballs, and a snowfall of parmesan grated with the Golden Grater. To be placed on the altar of the Colander Temple, so the Great Spaghetti stops sulking.
textes.Un grand qui forge dans un arbre. Il tap: A big'un who forges in a tree. He hits too hard on the left, but his steel sings true. Don't tell him I said that. Only tell him the first half.
textes.Un grand rouleau de plans tout gris : qu: A big roll of all-grey plans: four hundred shops, two thousand parking spaces, a fountain that plays an anthem, and where the Howling Hall stands… a car park. To bring back to Mamie Barricade.
textes.Un grand tournoi de pétanque de l'archip: A grand archipelago pétanque tournament, right here on the square! Dwarves, elves, fishermen from the village, sea folk if there are any. Balls of every size. And in the final, in front of everyone: me against Marcel.
textes.Un grand verre de jus de pomme du verger: A tall glass of apple juice from the farm orchard, cloudy and sweet, pressed that very morning. Restores one heart.
textes.Un grand verre de sirop de menthe à l'ea: A tall glass of mint cordial, green like Pigment's crest, with a paper straw. Tornade's favourite drink (and the Sergeant's, secretly). Restores one heart.
textes.Un grelot de cuivre au bout d'un cordon: A copper bell on a red cord, which the tanukis hang from their belts. The sign of a true master of swapping.
textes.Un grill si grand qu'il nourrirait toute: A grill so big it would feed the whole festival at once! A grill from the fountain all the way to the Skala, and the whole square eating at the same time.
textes.Un grimoire ? … (Théophraste disparaît e: A spellbook? … (Théophraste disappears between two shelves and comes back with a big purple leather book.) There. The pages are blank: you're the one who will write them. Every spell you learn will appear in it all by itself. Don't dog-ear it.
textes.Un grog de soufre au Diable Repu: A sulphur cordial at the Diable Repu
textes.Un grog pour moi, un grog pour toi ! San: A grog for me, a grog for you! Cheers, and may the sea be gentle with you!
textes.Un grondement : les deux blocs glissent: A rumble: the two blocks slide back by themselves to their starting places.
textes.Un grondement monte des profondeurs. Der: A rumble rises from the depths. Behind the Abyss Gate, NÂGA, THE SERPENT OF THE ABYSS, opens her eyes… You take the amulet back. The barrier wavers: the gate can open.
textes.Un grondement profond monte de la terre…: A deep rumble rises from the earth… At the foot of Yggdrasil, runes light up in the bark, trace a great door… which slowly opens!
textes.Un gros boulon gris, tombé d'un robot dé: A big grey bolt that fell off one of Mr Lisse's removal robots. Rustine, Ferraille and Fusible buy them back to make things far more useful than robots.
textes.Un gros gâteau rond du Four Éternel de B: A big round cake from Bobor's Eternal Oven, glazed with fire honey that runs down the sides. They say Cerberus, the three-headed dog, loves them: one per head. Restores two hearts (if you don't keep it for the dog).
textes.Un gros livre de cuir violet, une étoile: A big book of purple leather, with a gold star on the cover. Its pages were blank: each spell learned from a master of Arcanelle has written itself there, in purple ink.
textes.Un gros nœud de bois sombre, lisse comme: A big knot of dark wood, smooth as a river stone, and cold. It looks like it's waiting for the light. The mirror-flowers, as they turn, send back the light of the spring…
textes.Un gros poisson… Tu dis comme maman. C'é: A big fish… You sound like Mum. Maybe your big fish was a dolphin! You just didn't look properly, that's all.
textes.Un gâteau rond à la châtaigne et au miel: A round chestnut and honey cake with a moon drawn on top. In Ramure, they eat it every feast night. Restores three hearts.
textes.Un hamac dans l'arrière-salle, pour la n: A hammock in the back room, for the night
textes.Un haut-de-forme équipé d'un petit venti: A top hat fitted with a little hand-cranked fan. To keep your ideas cool.
textes.Un hiver, Thalion n'est pas descendu de: One winter Thalion didn't come down from his tower for four days, because of a noise in the mist. I took the soup up to him myself, by the ladder. Me, on a ladder! He looked at the soup, he looked at me, and he said: “You came up.” It's the longest sentence he's ever said to me.
textes.Un hiver, elle a tordu la cuillère que j: One winter, she bent the spoon I'd forged her, stirring a stew that was too thick. She came to the forge all red, holding the spoon in her hands like a baby bird fallen from the nest. I straightened it in three blows. She kissed me on the forehead. I botched the next sword.
textes.Un hiver, la tempête a soufflé toute une: One winter, the storm blew all night long. The shutters banged, the sea came over the quay. The whole port came to shelter here: fishermen, children, dogs. I served three hundred coffees. At dawn, I decided the Square Café would never close for good. There will always be a light on here.
textes.Un hiver, le chergui a soufflé trois jou: One winter, the chergui blew for three days. Forty caravan traders stuck at my place, the courtyard full of camels snoring louder than the wind. Hassan came to help me. All night long, we served tea side by side, him pouring, me carrying. Not one quarrel, not even over the fourth glass. In the morning, I said thank you. Once. You mustn't let him get used to it.
textes.Un hiver, pendant un mois entier, le cou: One winter, for a whole month, the mail from the mainland didn't arrive: the sea was too rough. The old folk of the harbour came to the post office every morning and left empty-handed. So, in the evenings, I wrote cards. To all of them. Signed “a friend”. The next day, everyone had mail. Nobody recognised my handwriting. Or nobody said anything.
textes.Un hiver, une de mes chèvres s'est perdu: One winter, one of my goats got lost in Grimli's tunnels. Three days without her. We found her in the Great Hall, lying on the throne. Thorgal looked at her, said “She has good taste”, and summoned me. I thought I'd be punished. He put me in charge of the city's messenger crows.
textes.Un hiver, une de ses chèvres s'est perdu: One winter, one of her goats got lost in my tunnels. We searched for three days. We found her in the Great Hall, lying on the king's throne, chewing a cushion. The king arrived. He looked at the goat. The goat looked at him. He said: “She has good taste.”
textes.Un hiver, une voie d'eau s'est ouverte s: One winter, a leak opened up under the tavern in the middle of the night. Tobias turned up in his nightshirt, with his pot of tar and a lantern, and worked until morning, lying in the cold water. In the morning, he just said: “She'll hold.” I served him a hot honey. He drank it without sighing. It's the only day I've ever seen him not sigh.
textes.Un humain ! Bienvenue sous le dôme, voya: A human! Welcome under the dome, traveller.
textes.Un humain a demandé à Faelar son âge. Fa: A human asked Faelar how old he was. Faelar started counting. He's still counting.
textes.Un humain dans mon herboristerie ! Appro: A human in my herb shop! Come closer, come closer. Aëlwen Feuillargent, herbalist. Here, everything that grows heals… or nearly.
textes.Un humain m'a demandé mon âge. J'ai répo: A human asked me my age. I said “three hundred and twelve”. He said “well preserved”. I still don't know if that was nice.
textes.Un humain qui répond aux énigmes d'une f: A human who answers a fairy's riddles! Here's your prize: a pinch of fairy dust. Don't sneeze it away.
textes.Un humain… dans mon royaume ? Le champig: A human… in my kingdom? Lulu's mushroom, I'll wager. Welcome, traveller. Here grows Yggdrasil, the World Tree, whose roots drink from every island.
textes.Un jaguar ! Quand il se tapit, il va bon: A jaguar! When it crouches, it's about to pounce: step aside at the last moment, then strike while it recovers.
textes.Un jaguar entre au marché. Le marchand d: A jaguar walks into the market. The merchant asks: “Can I help you?” The jaguar replies: “No thanks, I'm just looking.” And he looks at the merchant.
textes.Un jardin si grand qu'il y pousserait un: A garden so big that a herb would grow in it for every sorrow. I'm still missing a few seeds. The hardest ones to find.
textes.Un jeudi, Tiburce s'est endormi dans la: One Thursday, Tiburce fell asleep in the steam. When he woke, his gilded horns were all fogged up, and he couldn't see his reflection in them. He cried: “I'm dull!” The whole room jumped. I wiped them with my finest towel. He gave me a bottle of horn oil. I have no horns to oil. I use it for the doors.
textes.Un jeudi, je me suis endormi dans la vap: One Thursday, I fell asleep in the steam. When I woke up, my horns were all fogged up: I couldn't see my reflection in them any more! I cried out: “I'm dull!” The whole room jumped. Bulle wiped them with his finest towel, laughing. I gave him a bottle of horn oil. He uses it to grease his doors. His doors shine.
textes.Un jour d'orage, une rafale a arraché la: One stormy day a gust tore off half the north footbridge. Taeron held the planks, I held the threads, and we argued through the whole repair. By dawn it was sturdier than before. We only work well when we're cross.
textes.Un jour de Foire, on a fait un concours: One Fair day, we had a contest: who could make the most children laugh in an hour. Margot kept count, with a pencil and a big sheet of paper. Two hundred and twelve each! I demanded extra time, so did Basile. Margot refused: not regulation. Ever since, we've been arguing over who would have made the two hundred and thirteenth laugh.

One Fair day, we had a contest: who could make the most children laugh in an hour. Me with my bubbles, her with her confetti. Margot kept count, with a pencil and a big sheet of paper. After an hour: two hundred and twelve each. Capucine demanded extra time. Margot refused: “It's not regulation.” A draw. We still talk about it.
textes.Un jour de chaleur, la petite Suie s'est: One hot day, little Suie fell asleep on his helmet. Bramm didn't move for his whole watch. Six hours. I asked him why he didn't shoo her off. He said: “I'm guarding. She's sleeping. All is well.” I laughed till evening. He didn't. But his beard twitched.
textes.Un jour de chaleur, une petite chèvre es: One hot day, a little goat climbed onto my helmet and fell asleep there. I didn't move for the whole watch. Six hours. Hilda came by and asked why I didn't shoo it away. I said: “I'm guarding. It's sleeping. All is well.” She laughed till evening.
textes.Un jour de fête, Pilli m'a vendu un bouq: One feast day, Pilli sold me a bouquet of cempasúchil for a cacao. A very fine bouquet. I put it on my stall. Xóchitl walked by. She recognised it at once: they were her flowers. I offered her a friend's price. She said we'd been friends for thirty years. I said: “Then thirty years' discount.” She paid. Half.
textes.Un jour de fête, j'ai vendu un bouquet d: One feast day, I sold a bunch of Mum's flowers to Tochtli for a cacao. It was really good, the cacao. But afterwards, Mum saw her flowers on Tochtli's stall, really expensive. She looked at me. I said: “It's trade.” She laughed. Then she made me water the whole chinampa.
textes.Un jour de fête, j'ai vu à son étal des: One feast day, I saw magnificent cempasúchil flowers on his stall. Very expensive. I went closer: they were mine, bought from my son that very morning, for a cacao. Tochtli offered to sell them back to me at a friend's price. I said: “I've been your friend for thirty years.” He said: “Exactly. Thirty years' discount.”
textes.Un jour de grand marché, j'ai voulu le s: One big market day, I tried to shake him off by slipping behind Kraxx's stall. Pyrus tried to follow me, and his cape caught on a halberd. Thirty swords fell with a terrible racket. I went back to help him pick them up. We've never spoken of that day again.
textes.Un jour de grand vent, la casquette de G: One very windy day, Gonzague's cap blew all the way up to the top station. I set it on the seat of the red car all by itself, and sent it back down, just for the cap. A forty-second journey for a cap. Gonzague was waiting on the platform. He saluted the car.
textes.Un jour de grand vent, le Capitaine Char: One very windy day, Captain Charbonnel took me to the end of the jetty. He said: “Take off your coat, open your wings to the wind, and let it carry you.” I was scared. I did it anyway. I took off all at once, over the Harbour. I shouted with joy. I've never worn a coat since.
textes.Un jour de grand vent, le Capitaine m'a: One very windy day, the Captain took me to the end of the jetty. He told me to take off my coat, open my wings to the wind, and let it carry me. I took off all at once, over the whole Harbour. I was shouting with joy. Down below, he was waving his cap. That evening, all he said was: “Now you know.”
textes.Un jour de grand vent, ma casquette s'es: One very windy day, my cap blew away. A gust off the sea carried it along the cliff, right to the top. Ten minutes later, the red car came back down. Empty. With my cap sitting on the seat, nice and straight. Ernest had sent it down just for the cap. He says it's the prettiest car, for the prettiest cap.
textes.Un jour de grand vent, mon pédalo préfér: One very windy day, my favourite pedalo snapped its mooring and headed out to sea, all by itself. The “Gérard”, of course. Kevin dived off the lifeguard station, swam out to it and pushed it back, like a dolphin pushing a ball. The tourists applauded. I bought him punch for a week.
textes.Un jour de grand vent, ses yeux sont tom: One day of great wind, his eyes fell out. One rolled into the water that looks at the sky. The other hid beneath the heads that look at the clouds. Ever since, his door has been shut. The day someone gives him back his eyes… he will open his belly of stone. There you go.
textes.Un jour de grand vent, son auvent s'est: One very windy day, her awning tore off, and her jars were about to blow away. I grabbed my big shield, the one Pyrus finds too heavy, and held it in front of her jars while she ran after her awning. She didn't say thank you. The next day, there was no more pepper on my side. For two days. Then it came back.
textes.Un jour j'aurai ma propre barque. Je l'a: One day I'll have my own boat. I'll call it the Whale. That way, when I say I've seen the whale, it'll be true.
textes.Un jour où elle attendait des nouvelles: One day when she was waiting for news from Tazira, Rosette jumped on the mailbag before it touched the ground. Jumped, I tell you. She rolled across the grass with it, like a ball. Gustave thought we were under attack. I banned her from the airfield for a week. She covered the news through binoculars, from the promenade.
textes.Un jour où j'attendais des nouvelles de: One day when I was waiting for news from Tazira, I jumped on the mailbag before it hit the ground. Actually jumped. The commander shouted: “Rosette! It's not a ball!” I rolled across the grass with the bag. I had my front page. She banned me from the airfield for a week. I covered the news through binoculars, from the promenade.
textes.Un jour où j'étais parti livrer, Rachid: One day when I'd gone out on a delivery, Rachid minded my stall for an hour. When I got back, I'd sold three pairs, at triple the price. He'd told people they were the babouches of a desert sultan. He kept the difference “for the wedding”. I laughed so hard Abdellah missed his hammer stroke.
textes.Un jour, Abdellah m'a apporté un plateau: One day, Abdellah brought me a copper tray. Shaped like a slipper. Pointed at the front, round at the back, with engravings. He said: “For your feet.” I still don't know if it was a joke. Abdellah doesn't make jokes. The tray is on my stall, and I set the slippers on it. They look like queens.
textes.Un jour, Bedaine m'a proposé de troquer: One day, Bedaine offered to swap my flute for “two flutes”. Two for one! I was about to shake on it. Then, fox technique, I blew into the second one. Nothing. Not a sound. A silent whistle! I gave it back: “Keep it, Bedaine. It's just like you: lots of air, not a sound.” He laughed. He always laughs when he loses. It's infuriating.
textes.Un jour, Bedaine m'a proposé un troc : «: One day, Bedaine offered me a swap: “One bridge for two bridges!” I asked which ones. He said: “You make me a bridge, and I say thank you twice.” I laughed so hard I nearly fell off the branch. He said that meant yes. It was no! Well… I made him a little bridge for his balcony. He said thank you three times.
textes.Un jour, Brindille s'est posée trop vite: One day, Brindille landed too fast on my terrace and ended up in the soup pot. Luckily, it was lukewarm. She came out covered in vegetables, with a carrot on one horn. The sailors applauded. Since then, my soup has been called “the postwoman's soup”. It's the most ordered dish.
textes.Un jour, Bruno m'a dit : « Invente un pa: One day, Bruno said to me: “Invent a flavour, boss.” I took strawberry and a pinch of sea salt, for the dolphin. It's called strawberry-dolphin. Bruno tasted it, made a funny face, and then he said “Not bad at all”. Now it's written on his kiosk. With my name!
textes.Un jour, Bulle a voulu faire des bulles: One day, Bulle wanted to blow bubbles with one of my sap potions. The potion bubbled. So did Bulle: for two days, a bubble came out with every word. He thought it was wonderful. He opened the Baths anyway and talked to the customers in bubbles. They loved it. I took notes.
textes.Un jour, Cardamome m'a acheté trois flac: One day Cardamome bought three bottles and paid me with a riddle. “It's worth double,” she said. I've been looking for the answer for ten years. Until I find it, as far as I'm concerned she owes me three bottles. As far as she's concerned, I owe her gratitude.
textes.Un jour, Grisou a copié mes trois carott: One day, Grisou copied my three carrots, to see if that was the secret. He scoffed them all at once, just before the start. At the third bend, he was all green, bent double. He still came second, clutching his tummy. The secret isn't the carrots, Grisou. It's me.
textes.Un jour, Haldir est revenu d'une course: One day, Haldir came back from a delivery saying: “She smiled.” I found out later he hadn't delivered anything at all. He just wanted to make me happy. I forgave him: I imagined that smile all week, and it was a very good week.
textes.Un jour, Halima m'a fait une cruche inca: One day Halima made me an unbreakable jug. So thick you can't lift it any more. It takes two pirates to fill it, and nobody can drink from it. It props the tavern door open now. Halima says it's the best jug she's ever made. She's right: it's never broken.
textes.Un jour, Hapou a apporté du lin à Maman,: One day, Hapou brought some flax to Mum, and in the last bundle, there was a kitten! Ginger! With a crooked ear! Hapou said he wasn't his. I named him Miou, because he went “miou”. And Amenemhat told me that in the old language, cat is “miou”! For real! My cat speaks the old language!
textes.Un jour, Hapou m'a livré mes bottes de l: One day, Hapou delivered my bundles of flax, and out of the last one fell a ginger kitten with a crooked ear. Hapou said straight away: “He's not mine.” Nebet hugged him tight and named him Miou. I didn't ask anything more. The kitten came from his field, he knows it, I know it. He'll never admit it.
textes.Un jour, Hurla était enrhumée, et elle m: One day, Hurla had a cold, and she asked me to fill in for her at the Arena. I announced the fighters the way I sell my fish: “IN THE LEFT CORNER… A LOVELY SEA BREAM!” The crowd loved it. Gorgoth laughed for the first time in the Arena. Since then, whenever Hurla has a cold, it's me. I find she recovers slowly.
One day, Isaac gave me a shell. For free! A purple murex, magnificent, found in a lot of old junk. Isaac giving something away! I turned it every which way looking for the catch. There wasn't one. It doesn't come from any beach I've landed on, so it isn't in my collection. It's in my pocket. Set apart.
textes.Un jour, Karim est parti livrer et m'a l: One day, Karim went off on a delivery and left me minding his stall for an hour. I sold three pairs of slippers at triple the price: slippers of a desert sultan, stitched by moonlight. The difference, I kept “for the wedding”. It's a gift from Karim, really. He laughed so hard that Abdellah missed his hammer stroke.
textes.Un jour, Kevin m'a prêté son sifflet de: One day, Kevin lent me his lifeguard's whistle while he went to fetch a pedalo. “You watch the beach, sergeant.” Ten minutes. I watched like never before. I whistled twice: a child too far out, a dog on the sand. When he came back, I returned the whistle holding it like a medal.
textes.Un jour, Lalla Aïcha m'a vendu un sachet: One day, Lalla Aïcha sold me a yellow sachet: “Saffron for fabric.” I rubbed a pinch between my fingers. Turmeric. I looked at her, she looked at me, and we both burst out laughing. She said: “For dyeing, it's good enough.” I dyed with it. It faded in the first sun. She was wrong, but it was funny.
textes.Un jour, Lucie est remontée avec une alg: One day Lucie came up with a red seaweed as long as my arm, one I'd never seen. She said: “It grows on carved stones, and nowhere else.” I hung it up to dry. It smells of rain, even dried. I still haven't worked out what it's for, but I'm keeping it.
textes.Un jour, Lumi a planté une luciole dans: One day, Lumi planted a firefly in a pot, to grow a firefly tree. She watered it every morning. I explained to her, very gently, that fireflies aren't seeds. She said: “Are you sure?” She kept the pot. I water it too, sometimes. You never know.
textes.Un jour, Mochi a trouvé une de mes noise: One day Mochi found one of my hazelnuts in one of her mum's mooncakes! I don't know how it got there. Well, okay, I sort of do. Mochi ate it with the cake, and then she said it didn't count as found, because it was in her tummy. So there are still two hundred and ninety-nine left.
textes.Un jour, Momo m'a offert un collier : tr: One day, Momo gave me a necklace: thirty shells threaded on a string. In the middle, I recognised Hortense, my tiger cowrie, carried off by a tide six years ago. Drilled! I bought her back for a bunch of bananas. She's fine. She just has a little hole.
textes.Un jour, Nadine est entrée dans ma bouti: One day, Nadine slipped into my shop and bought a postcard. One of mine! With the lighthouse. I thought she was going to write to me. I watched my letterbox for a week. She'd sent it to her aunt. But she bought it from me, not at the post office. That means something, doesn't it?
textes.Un jour, Nebet est entrée dans l'atelier: One day, Nebet came into the workshop with Miou in her arms. The cat jumped down and walked over all my fresh jars, one by one, leaving little paw prints everywhere. I shouted. Then I looked. It was pretty. I fired them just like that. The temple bought them: “the cat jars”. I've never sold anything so fast.
textes.Un jour, Octave est descendu de son éche: One day, Octave came down his ladder to look at my test hut. He walked round it, tapped a post, and said: “It leans.” Then he showed me a mortise-and-tenon joint, in two minutes, without another word. And he charged me two coins for the lesson. I paid. It was worth more. Don't tell him.
textes.Un jour, Omar a voulu jouer sur ma grill: One day Omar wanted to play on my grill. “This grill must have a sound!” He slapped it with his whole hand. It was hot. He went “Boom! Ouch! Ta-ka!” and leapt all the way to the fountain. He played all evening with his fingers wrapped in a tea towel. He says it was his best concert.
textes.Un jour, Ombreline m'a dit tout bas que: One day, Ombreline whispered to me that I was allowed to fly in the library, but only above the bird section. I was so happy I did three laps over the bird books. I forgot to give her her letter. I came back the next day. On foot. She was smiling. That's rare.
textes.Un jour, Ondine est venue m'acheter un b: One day, Ondine came to buy a mother-of-pearl boat from me, whispering: “It's for Coralin, it has to be the sturdiest one.” I gave her the most beautiful one, for nothing. He doesn't know I know. I don't know what he did with it. I hope he took it apart. That would be a compliment.
textes.Un jour, Ori m'a montré une ligne vide d: One day, Ori showed me an empty line in my ledger, on the eve of the king's coronation, ninety years ago. He asked me what went there. I said: “A smudge.” He looked at the page. There was no smudge. He closed the ledger without a word. I like that Ori. He scares me.
textes.Un jour, Pierrick est arrivé en se tenan: One day Pierrick turned up clutching his stomach: he'd read the name of a whale disease in Tréphine's journal and was sure he'd caught it. I had him drink some warm water and told him he was saved. He said: “Just in time?” I said yes. Just in time.
textes.Un jour, Pépin a chronométré ma sieste a: One day, Pépin timed my nap with his Cliquetis stopwatch. Three hours twelve! Village record. He announces it to anyone who'll listen, very proud, as if it were his. It's the only record nobody will ever take from me. Bondi tried once. He lasted four minutes.
textes.Un jour, Roux est revenu de Tazira avec: One day Roux came back from Tazira with sand in his tail and his paws full of steps. He showed me: it looked like a goat on a rock! I laughed, and I learned them anyway. Over there they dance too, under a moon that grows thin. That troubled me. Who do they dance for, on the nights when it's only a thread?
textes.Un jour, Roux m'a posé une devinette : «: One day, Roux asked me a riddle: “I'm red, I can smell tarts a hundred paces away, I pick herbs in my sleep, and I'd like to marry you. Who am I?” I answered: “No, you silly.” Laughing. He laughed too. The answer was “me”. Easy. Too easy, for a fox's riddle.
textes.Un jour, Si Larbi m'a raconté qu'en mous: One day, Si Larbi told me that when he was a cabin boy, he saw a whale as big as the Skala, which soaked him right up to his cap. As big as the Skala! Since then, whenever people laugh at me, I say: “Even Si Larbi said so!” Moulay Brahim went to ask him. Si Larbi said yes. Best day of my life.
textes.Un jour, Tibo m'a rapporté une sardine q: One day, Tibo brought me a sardine he'd caught himself, on the quay, with Ahmed. I cooked it as if for an admiral: honey, cinnamon, three hours of cooking, Mustapha's recipe. It came out black as a boot. Tibo ate it down to the bone. He had tears in his eyes. From emotion, I think.
textes.Un jour, Tiburce est venu me voir, très: One day, Tiburce came to see me, very embarrassed: one of his clients had peeling horns. He asked me for a real remedy. I gave him a balm. He paid me double, begging me not to tell anyone. I didn't tell anyone. Except you, now. You mustn't repeat it.
textes.Un jour, Tlaco a bu dans la jarre d'offr: One day, Tlaco drank from the offering jar, the one for the blue shrine. Pilli was devastated: “Tlaloc will be angry!” I reassured him: Tlaloc likes thirsty dogs. That very evening, it rained. A little rain. Pilli came to tell me: “You see, Tlaloc put the water back.” I couldn't have found a better explanation.
textes.Un jour, Tlaco a bu l'eau de la jarre po: One day, Tlaco drank the water from Tlaloc's jar! I was really scared Tlaloc would get angry. Coyotl said Tlaloc likes thirsty dogs. And that evening, it rained! A bit. So I understood: Tlaloc put the water back in the jar. He wasn't angry at all. He's nice to dogs, Tlaloc.
textes.Un jour, Toni m'a demandé mon secret pou: One day, Toni asked me my secret for opening a coconut with one stroke. I showed him: you look at the nut, you breathe, and crack. He looked, he breathed, he nicked his thumb. I put a plaster on it with a little paper umbrella stuck in it. He kept it on all evening. He says it brings luck.
textes.Un jour, Ulfa m'a demandé, en essuyant u: One day, Ulfa asked me, wiping a mug, all casual, whether Sigrun was eating well, up on the terrace. I said yes. She said: “Who? I don't know any Sigrun.” And she went down to the cellar. She asks me every year. And every year, she doesn't know her.
textes.Un jour, Yannick m'a emmené en pédalo. T: One day, Yannick took me out in a pedalo. Three metres from the jetty. Three! I was green as seaweed. That's my tragedy: a cartographer who's never left his island. So I draw the archipelago through other people's eyes: Léon, his passengers, travellers like you. You are my telescopes, {surnom}.
textes.Un jour, Zéphyr a voulu battre son recor: One day Zéphyr tried to beat his record by carrying six crates at once. Over the sea, a crate slipped. Apparently it rained nectar on a beach in the archipelago for a whole minute. The folk down there still talk about it. Me, I mostly talk about my crate.
One day, then. The boat's waiting for you.
textes.Un jour, au conseil des pêcheurs, deux f: One day, at the fishermen's council, two families were fighting over a spot in the channel. Three hours of shouting. I had a headache. In the end, I asked Driss what he thought. He said: “No.” Nobody knew what he was saying no to. But everybody went quiet, and the quarrel stopped. I've never dared ask him.
textes.Un jour, au dessert, elle a souri. Pas à: One day, at dessert, she smiled. Not at me, at the sea. The tiniest little smile. I pretended not to see it and gave her the coffee on the house. She didn't notice. I kept that smile to myself all day. Here, you keep what you can.
textes.Un jour, au pied du Chêne-Mère, il m'a d: One day, at the foot of the Mother Oak, he said to me: “Hrmm. The treetop. Sunset.” I said yes, it must be very pretty from up there. He nodded and went off. Ever since, I've wondered what it meant. Advice? A remark about the weather? Oh… with Bourru, you never know.
textes.Un jour, avec une craie, j'ai écrit LA T: One day, with chalk, I wrote THE TERROR on the Zahra, in big letters, next to the eye. Uncle saw and said nothing. He left it a whole week! The fishermen called her “the Terror”, and he answered to it. And then it rained. It was the rain that washed it off, not him. He swore to me.
textes.Un jour, dans le salon de l'hôtel, le pr: One day, in the hotel lounge, the professor asked me in a low voice whether I could “lose a little” of his university's letters. Just a little. I said no: a postwoman loses nothing, it's sacred. He looked so sad that the next day I attached a caramel to the envelope. Since then, every letter from there travels with a caramel.
textes.Un jour, des nains m'ont invité à une fê: One day, some dwarves invited me to a party at the bottom of a mine. Why me? I never found out. We danced between the rails by lantern light, and every step echoed back three times. An old dwarf told me: “You dance like a rockslide.” The best compliment of my life. That's the true version. Today's one.
textes.Un jour, des pirates ont abordé mon navi: One day, pirates boarded my ship. They took the chests, the stamp, and even my hat. Then they wanted to take me along. After two days of speeches, they changed their minds: they dropped me on the quay of Port-Coutelas, in the rain. A lady opened the door of a tavern for me and served me soup. Nobody governed here. I decided it would be me.
textes.Un jour, deux pêcheurs ne se parlaient p: One day, two fishermen had stopped speaking over a spot on the quay. The amin sent for me: “Hassan, tea. For three.” I served them from very high, without a word, and they had to be quiet to watch the foam. By the third glass, they were laughing. Moulay Brahim said it was his judgement. It was my tea.
textes.Un jour, devant tout le monde, elle m'a: One day, in front of everyone, she told me I saw three-masters in the clouds. I told her, in front of everyone, that she saw channels in the reefs. Gros-Louis shouted “Fight!”. We looked at each other, and burst out laughing. Since then, we say hello by teasing each other. She brings me shells. I point out reefs to her.
textes.Un jour, du haut du mât, j'ai vu une gro: One day, from the top of the mast, I saw a big black hump in the water, blowing. I shouted “Whale!” and the whole crew ran to the same side of the ship. It was a whale! A real one, with a water spout! Fil-de-Fer hugged me so hard he nearly fell. He told me it took him three years to see his first one.
textes.Un jour, elle est montée au belvédère et: One day, she came up to the lookout and named all the herbs around my easel: thyme, savory, everlasting, and a little yellow one you mustn't pick. I put them all over my canvas. She leaned in: “That's everlasting. You've painted it as savory.” She sees everything.
textes.Un jour, elle est redescendue avec une p: One day she came down with a sting right on the nose. Red, swollen like a crab apple. She took the honey she'd just brought down and dabbed a bit on it: “It heals!” It did heal. I sold that jar for two coins extra: “Honey that heals its own stings”. And it was true, too.
textes.Un jour, elle m'a apporté un dessin : le: One day she brought me a drawing: the Pond King, golden, big as a rabbit. With a crown on his head. I looked at that drawing for a long time. A very long time. She asked: “Isn't it good?” I said: “Shh. It's very good.” It's pinned above my bed.
textes.Un jour, elle m'a apporté un grand coqui: One day, she brought me a big shell from Bone Beach, all pink inside. I said to her: “WHAT'S THAT?!” She said: “For you.” I grunted. I took it. I didn't throw it away. It's in my hammock. I'm not saying what I do with it. NONE OF YOUR BUSINESS.
textes.Un jour, elle m'a servi sa tisane. J'ai: One day, she served me her tea. I drank. I said: “Hot water.” She hasn't forgotten. Five years. She brings it up with every vial. Hm. It was good, really. A bit. I won't say so.
textes.Un jour, elle m'a tendu sa flûte en terr: One day, she handed me her clay flute, the bird-shaped one. “Try it,” she said. I blew. The sound of a duck with a cold. She laughed till she cried. I gave her back the flute very quickly. I've never tried again. Not in front of her.
textes.Un jour, en entrant acheter des pêches,: One day, going in to buy peaches, I caught Colette behind her counter, buried in “The Foam of Your Heart” by Sylvia Delarive. She slipped it under the crate of peaches, bright red. Then she looked at me and said: “Do you read? Read this.” She recommended it with such passion… I turned bright red too. Two peonies.
textes.Un jour, en grimpant chercher le miel, u: One day, climbing up for the honey, a bee stung me right on the nose. It swelled up like an apple! Grelot put a bit of the honey itself on it, to heal it: “Honey mends what the bee has done.” It worked. She still made me pay for the honey. One coin. I hung it under the bridge.
textes.Un jour, il a fait une lanterne sans un: One day he made a lantern without a single hole, “to see”. He lit it in the middle of the souk: nothing, a candle in a pot. He said it was on purpose, to prove copper is enough. I said it was the most honest of his lanterns. He didn't speak to me all day. The next day he brought me a tea.
textes.Un jour, il a gagné un match et il m'a d: One day, he won a match and dedicated the victory to me, in front of the whole court: “For Ix Chab and her pots!” Everyone laughed. Me, I was as red as cochineal. The next day, I served him two fingers of froth instead of one. He cried miracle. He'd better not get used to it.
textes.Un jour, il a voulu chasser les mouettes: One day he tried to chase the gulls off my grill with his amin's staff. He made great windmill swings. A gull slipped under the staff and took his turban. The whole auction watched the white turban fly away over the Skala. I told him: “You see, the gull tax is for everyone.”
textes.Un jour, il a voulu me mettre à l'épreuv: One day, he wanted to put me to the test. He threw five dice behind a curtain, four honest and one loaded, and asked me which. I listened. I said: “The third.” He opened the curtain. It was the third. He closed the curtain again, very gently. Since then, he raises his hat to me. He didn't before.
textes.Un jour, il a voulu présenter Xan à mes: One day, he wanted to introduce Xan to my bees, “so they become friends”. He opened his gourd in front of the hive. The bees came out, they circled around the mosquito, very curious… and Xan went back into the gourd all by himself. Kinich said: “He's shy.” I think he'd understood who was in charge.
textes.Un jour, il est arrivé dans ma cuisine a: One day, he came into my kitchen with a tiny little fish in his hands. I got out the frying pan. He looked at me with eyes like saucers and said: “He's going to grow.” We went and released him together, at the pontoon. Since then, when he goes fishing, he says hello to him. He's sure it's always the same one.
textes.Un jour, il est arrivé de l'oasis avec u: One day, he arrived from the oasis with a whole palm trunk on his camel. Three days' walk. “For your boats.” Palm wood is soft, it frays, it won't make a hull. I couldn't tell him. I made a bench out of it in front of the house: Mbarek's bench. He sits on it every visit. He looks pleased.
textes.Un jour, il est passé devant l'étal, il: One day he walked past the stall, said hello, smiled, turned round to smile at me again… and three bowls fell. Three! He paid in sardines, a whole crate. I gave it to Mustapha. The next day, he came by again. He smiled. I told him: “Don't turn round.” He turned round.
textes.Un jour, il est venu m'annoncer un impôt: One day, he came to announce a tax on trade. I took out my scales and said: “Very well, Excellency. Then I'll charge you the tax on scales.” He thought about it for a long time. Then he abolished the tax. That same evening, he gave a speech on the freedom of trade. A very good speech. I applauded.
One day, he came to return a book. Not the right one: another, borrowed eighty years ago, that I thought was lost. I thanked him. He stood there, wings drooping a little, like a pupil waiting for his mark. I smiled at him. He left without a word. For him, that's quite a feat.
textes.Un jour, il m'a acheté trois tapis de l': One day he bought three oasis carpets from me. He talked for four hours. The tribes, the wool, the price of tea, his grandmother, the wedding, the rain. Four hours. I drank my tea. At the end he named his price. I said: “No.” He paid mine. He sat down on a carpet, exhausted. I let him rest.
textes.Un jour, il m'a apporté une sardine fait: One day he brought me a sardine made “according to my recipe”, on a plate with a flower. Three hours of cooking, honey, cinnamon. Black as a boot, sticky as tar. He looked at me with happy-puppy eyes. I ate it. All of it. Smiling. I said the smoke was making my eyes water. It wasn't the smoke.
textes.Un jour, il m'a pris le marteau des main: One day, he took the hammer out of my hands: “A real blacksmith's blow.” A real blow, all right. The tray split in two. I made him pay for it, full price. He paid without arguing. The split tray, I hung on the wall of the workshop. When he walks by, he looks at it. So do I. Worth more than a speech.
textes.Un jour, il m'a proposé des lunettes. À: One day, he offered me spectacles. Me. The guard of the Lookout. I said no. The next day, a pair was sitting on the watchtower railing. “By chance.” I put them away in the drawer. Without trying them on. They're still there. I haven't tried them on. I'm telling you so it's clear.
textes.Un jour, il m'a proposé quatre cents piè: One day, he offered me four hundred coins for my whole collection. Four hundred! I thought about it for a second. One tiny little second. Then I thought of my father's spiral shell, and I said no. Isaac sighed: “Everything's for sale, my girl.” I said: “Not this.” He gave a strange smile. I think he was glad I refused.
textes.Un jour, il m'a vendu une boule à neige,: One day, he sold me a snow globe, a lighthouse in the snow. “To cool down your kiosk.” I paid full price. It's on my counter, next to the till. When it's too hot, customers shake it. It doesn't cool anything down at all. But everyone smiles.
One day, a mooncake was missing. Mochi was there, looking innocent, ears flattened right down. Too flattened. I lifted an ear: the cake was underneath, stuck, half-eaten. She said: “It was cold.” Since then, before I count the cakes, I count the ears.
textes.Un jour, j'abattais un grand chêne au bo: One day, I was felling a big oak by the river. I shouted “Timber!”, but too late: it fell right on the king's boat, which was passing by. The king wasn't in it, luckily. His hat was. They told me: “Prison or the navy.” Me, I ran all the way to the port and took the first boat leaving. It had a black flag.
textes.Un jour, j'ai acheté un sabre superbe à: One day, I bought a superb sabre from a passing sailor, and put it in the window: “Toledo sabre, rare piece”. Brutus came in, picked it up, turned it over, and showed me a little mark on the guard: a hammer. His mark. He'd forged it himself, three years earlier. I offered him a friend's price. He bent an iron bar. I lowered the price.
One day, I brought Miou to the workshop. He jumped onto the fresh jars and walked across them, one by one, with his little paws! Ptahmosé shouted “Hm!” really loudly. And then he fired the jars just like that, paw prints and all. The temple bought every one! Miou is an artist.
textes.Un jour, j'ai apporté à Aëlwen une fleur: One day I brought Aëlwen a moonflower that had opened at high noon. She said it was worthless. I said it was worth double, since it was rare. We argued for an hour. Then we put it in a glass of water between us and drank a cup of tea.
textes.Un jour, j'ai caché un gâteau de lune da: One day I hid a mooncake in my ears. They're floppy, so it's a really good hiding place. But Mummy lifted my ear, and the cake was there. A bit eaten. I said it was cold. Mummy laughed. She doesn't laugh like that very often, so sometimes I do it again, on purpose.
textes.Un jour, j'ai caché une de ses haches da: One day, I hid one of her axes in a wasps' nest. So she couldn't cut down a living tree! She went to get it. She came back with the axe, three stings on her snout, and she didn't say anything. Nothing at all. She just put the axe down on the anvil. Ever since, I've wondered whether that was a win.
textes.Un jour, j'ai calculé que le soleil alla: One day, I calculated that the sun would go out at high noon, forty days later. Nobody believed me, except Ix Kanul's mother, the high priestess at the time. When the day came, at noon, the sky went black, the birds fell silent… and the sun came back. For once, I had counted right. To the hour! I still tremble with pride.
textes.Un jour, j'ai copié son secret : trois c: One day I copied his secret: three carrots before the race, not one more. Except carrots don't suit a wolf at all. I ran the whole loop with a wolf-sized tummy ache. Still second! Bondi asked if I wanted a fourth one next time. He's very funny, Bondi. Very.
textes.Un jour, j'ai crié « Lucas ! » depuis la: One day, I shouted “Lucas!” from the harbour office, about a simple timetable. He jumped and dropped a crate of lemons into the harbour. We fished them out together, with landing nets, for an hour. He apologised for every lemon. I was counting. Three were missing. I didn't note them in the register.
textes.Un jour, j'ai demandé à Doc combien de t: One day, I asked Doc how long a parrot lives. He said: “A hundred years, sometimes more.” I did the maths. I didn't say a word for at least a minute: that's a record. He lent me a book on birds. I dog-eared every page about memory. He didn't ask me anything. Doc knows when not to ask.
textes.Un jour, j'ai dit que ses daurades n'éta: One day, I said her sea bream wasn't fresh enough anymore. Day-old sea bream! I said it to Lola, just to Lola, a bit loudly maybe, and Lola repeated it to the whole quay. Since then, Rosalie has dinner here every evening, sitting bolt upright, and she eats while staring at me. So I really feel that she's cross. I feel it. She has seconds of dessert.
textes.Un jour, j'ai entendu dire qu'à Cliqueti: One day I heard that in Cliquetis they had spring shoes. Boing, boing, and hop, three arches in one go! I ran to beg Ursule to forge me some. She said “No.”, she told Pépin, and Pépin said “cheating”. I sulked for a week. Now, every evening, I just ask her for horseshoes that are a teeny bit lighter. Just in case.
textes.Un jour, j'ai essayé de lui troquer « un: One day, I tried to swap her “one bridge for two bridges”. The deal of the century! She asked which ones. I showed her two little string bridges, knotted by yours truly the night before. She laughed so hard she nearly fell off her beam. She said no. But she gave me a hazelnut for the idea.
textes.Un jour, j'ai eu la fièvre et je suis re: One day I had a fever and stayed in bed. Mustapha sold half as much: the customers ate without hurrying, and nobody else came. The next day he came to my house with six sardines wrapped in paper. He said: “Get well quick, my grill is falling asleep.” I got well. Sardines cure everything.
textes.Un jour, j'ai fait toute la ronde des cr: One day, I did the whole round of the battlements behind the caïd. I walked just like him, really slowly, hand on my wooden sabre, nose in the air. The guards were laughing, and he didn't understand why. He only saw me at the end, when he turned around. He made a funny face. I think he wanted to laugh.
textes.Un jour, j'ai jeté une noisette dans la: One day I threw a hazelnut in the big pond to bait the dragon. Plop! Moustache went “Shhhhh” for a really, really long time. I asked if the dragon had eaten it. He said yes! So the next day I threw in three. He said the dragon wasn't hungry any more. I think it's on a diet.
textes.Un jour, j'ai livré mes bottes de lin ch: One day, I delivered my bunches of flax to Tiyi's. In the last one, there was a ginger kitten, the size of a fist, with a crooked ear. I swear I hadn't put it there. Little Nebet picked it up and named it Miou. Tiyi looked at me. I said: “It's not mine.” She smiled. It came from my field. I know.
textes.Un jour, j'ai mis trois fois trop de la: One day, I put three times too much of Zébuline's fire cinnamon in my brioches. They were smoking as they came out of the oven! The customers loved them. Now, every Friday, it's the “smoking brioche”. I say it's our joint invention. Zébuline says it's mostly mine. We can't agree.
textes.Un jour, j'ai parié au souk que je devin: One day, I bet in the souk that I could guess everyone's shoe size, just by looking. A whole month. I was wrong only once: Mbarek, the caravan driver. I said forty-three. He took off his sandal. Caravan-driver feet, wide as dunes! I made him a made-to-measure pair. He keeps them for special occasions.
textes.Un jour, j'ai pleuré au-dessus de sa mar: One day I cried over her pot of moon tea. She didn't say a thing; she bottled it all, with a label: “Tea of Tears”. She sold it very dear. I didn't get a single coin. Just a sugared petal. She says that's the fair price of a tear.
textes.Un jour, j'ai posé Bouton sur le rebord: One day I put Button on the ledge of the watchtower. Button jumped into Thalion's soup bowl. Thalion yelled so loud the birds flew off. He says he wasn't scared, he was “surprised”. I saw him jump backwards. He was scared. A bit.
textes.Un jour, j'ai pris une dorade vivante su: One day, I took a live sea bream from mum's stall and put it in the fountain on the square. I called it Captain. Mum shouted so loud that all the gulls flew off. And then she left it there for three days. On the fourth morning, Captain was gone. Mum says it went back to the sea all by itself. But mum's apron was all wet.
textes.Un jour, j'ai rapporté à Jacquot une sar: One day, I brought Jacquot a sardine I'd caught myself. He cooked it like it was for an admiral: honey, cinnamon, three hours of cooking. It came out all black. I ate it right down to the bone, 'cause he was watching me. I had tears in my eyes. He thinks it was emotion.
textes.Un jour, j'ai suivi le fleuve jusqu'à la: One day, I followed the river to the sea, to see where all that water was going. I never went home. Cabin boy, topman, boatswain. Ignace found me on a quay, twelve years ago. “Can you handle a crew?” I said: “Yes.” “Do you ask questions?” I said: “No.” He hired me. Best conversation of my life.
textes.Un jour, j'ai touché son chèche, et aprè: One day, I touched his chèche, and afterwards my fingers were all blue! I showed them to the whole square: “Look, I'm a blue man!” I didn't wash my hands for three days. Mum caught me on the fourth.
textes.Un jour, j'ai trouvé des traces de jagua: One day, I found jaguar tracks! I shouted for Balam. He looked at the tracks, then told me to look behind me. It was Peek', sitting with one paw up! They were his tracks. So I said: “It's a dog jaguar.” We followed them anyway. They led to a bone.
textes.Un jour, j'ai vendu du « copal béni par: One day, I sold “copal blessed by the high priest”. He hadn't blessed it. He came to my stall, looking stern. I held out a piece: “Bless it, and it'll be true.” He blessed it. I don't know why. Neither does he. That day I doubled my prices, and in the evening I treated him to a cacao. He drank it. I think he likes me.
textes.Un jour, j'ai voulu chasser les mouettes: One day, I tried to chase the seagulls off the grill with my amin's staff. Big swirling sweeps, lots of authority. A seagull flew underneath, took my turban and carried it off over the Skala. The whole fish market watched my turban fly. Mustapha said: “The tax is for everyone.” I didn't set a single price that day.
textes.Un jour, j'ai voulu lui troquer sa flûte: One day, I tried to swap his flute for “two flutes”. Two for one, a golden deal! That fox blew into the second one before shaking on it. Not a sound: it was a silent whistle. He gave it back to me, saying: “Keep it, Bedaine. It's just like you: lots of air, not a sound.” Heh heh… nicely done. I'll get him back for that.
textes.Un jour, j'ai voulu photographier la gra: One day, I wanted to photograph the big pot on the stove. Paulo leapt forward, threw a tea towel over it and planted himself in front of it, arms spread: “Not the pot! Because of the secret!” I only photographed the tea towel. It's my most mysterious photo. And it's in focus, too.
textes.Un jour, j'ai voulu rendre le nectar de: One day I tried to make Mélisse's nectar fizzy, to help her. Her bottles had hiccups for a week: they blew bubbles and sang! She sold twice as much. And my share? A ribbon. ONE ribbon. I kept it anyway, it's pretty.
textes.Un jour, j'ai voulu verser le thé de hau: One day, I wanted to pour tea from up high, like him. It looked easy. I raised the teapot very high, and drenched the turban of Mbarek, sitting next to me. Mbarek said nothing. He wrung out his turban and held out his glass. Since then, I let Hassan pour. To each his trade.
textes.Un jour, j'aurai un voilier, et je l'app: One day I'll have a sailboat, and I'll call it “Further-Out”. I'll sail round the archipelago, island by island: the village, the jungle, the elves, the dwarves… and the flying island, if it's willing to come down a bit.
textes.Un jour, j'ouvrirai une vraie auberge, a: One day, I'll open a real inn, with beds. On dry land. That doesn't move.
textes.Un jour, j'éclairerai toute la cité sans: One day, I'll light up the whole city without a drop of oil. For now, I light up my laboratory very nicely. When it isn't catching fire.
textes.Un jour, je ferai le tour de toute l'île: One day, I'll run all the way round the island. Cliquetis, Tazira, Carène, and back. Faster than the Zéphyr! … OK, maybe not faster than the Zéphyr.
textes.Un jour, je l'ai entendu chuchoter « dou: One day, I heard him whisper “easy now, my lovely” to a crate of bottles he was unloading from a boat. He set it down like a newborn. It arrived in one piece. Since then, when a fragile cargo arrives, I hand it to Lucas. I haven't told him why.
textes.Un jour, je l'ai mis à l'épreuve : cinq: One day, I put him to the test: five dice behind a curtain, only one loaded. He listened to them roll, and he said: “The third one.” It was the third one. I closed the curtain. I thought of all the times I'd sworn to a customer that those dice were undetectable. Since then, I take my hat off when he passes. Talent deserves respect.
textes.Un jour, je l'ai suivi de loin dans la m: One day, I followed him at a distance into the mine, to finally find his famous seam. After an hour, I had no idea where I was. He's the one who found me, whistling, lantern in hand. He never asked me what I was doing there. That's almost worse.
textes.Un jour, je l'ai vu plisser les yeux ver: One day I saw him squinting towards the big pond, for a long, long time. I offered him glasses, just in passing. He took offence: “A guard sees.” So I left my second pair on the Lookout railing, by chance. It vanished the next day. I don't know where. I don't ask.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai demandé : « Je tombe: One day I asked her: “I fall without getting hurt, I shine without fire, and I cry without sorrow.” She happened to be crying. She said: “A drop… like me?” She was right! I wrote in my big book: “the only riddle solved by Brindille”. She cried again. For joy, this time, I think.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai dit : « Hrmm. La cime: One day, I said to her: “Hrmm. Treetop. Sunset.” My longest speech. She said: “Oh… yes, it must be very pretty from up there.” And she left. She didn't come. Hrmm. Maybe I wasn't clear.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai fait sentir une épice: One day, I had her smell a spice from faraway islands, a black bark I've kept in my apron pocket for twenty years. She sniffed, went quiet, and asked: “What is it?” Aïcha, who knows everything! She didn't know it. I kept the name to myself. I need a secret of my own, too.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai offert ma meilleure t: One day, I offered her my best moon tea, the one with pond elderflower. She drank, she thought for a long time, and she said: “Hot water.” Hot water! I bring it up with every vial. She doesn't apologise. But I can tell she comes back for a cup, in winter, when nobody's looking.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai pris le marteau. Pour: One day I took his hammer. To show him a real blow. A blacksmith's blow. The tray split. In two. He looked at me. He made me pay. Full price. I paid. He hung the split tray on the wall of his stall. He says it's to remember. Hm. I remember too.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai proposé de goûter, le: One day I offered her a blindfold tasting of “a spice mix on bread”. She agreed, for the spice. She chewed, and said: “Delicious. What cumin!” I took off the blindfold. It was a sardine. She got cross and left shouting. But she'd said delicious. In front of Saïd. The whole quay knows.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai prêté ma flûte-colibr: One day, I lent him my hummingbird flute. He blew. It made the sound of a sneezing duck. I laughed till I cried. He gave it back to me very quickly, bright red. But afterwards, I saw him looking at the flute out of the corner of his eye. For a long time. The way a jaguar looks at a bird.
textes.Un jour, je me suis dit : et si un piano: One day, I thought: what if a whole piano played by itself? Three years. Twelve thousand pins planted by hand, one by one. The page-turner was Philibert's idea, a plaque says so. On opening night, the piano played its waltz, turned its pages, and at the end, it took a bow. The whole hall applauded. I was in the wings.
textes.Un jour, je montrais le fil d'or à Karim: One day, I was showing the gold thread to Karim when Rachid walked by. Karim hid the thread in his turban, Rachid asked what we were doing, and Karim started laughing. He laughed and laughed, he couldn't speak, with a bit of gold thread dangling over his ear. I said he was thinking of a joke. Rachid still looks at us sideways.
textes.Un jour, je réussirai un sort parfait, d: One day, I'll cast a perfect spell, in front of everyone. And Pyra will clap. Pyra never claps. It'll be the best day of my life.
textes.Un jour, je serai capitaine. Je réparera: One day, I'll be captain. I'll repair the Léviathan, we'll put it back in the water, and we'll all set sail. Everyone laughs when I say that. Except Tobias. He sighs.
textes.Un jour, je suis descendue d'un battemen: One day, I popped down in the blink of an eye to the kingdom of roots, under the elves' island. I wanted a seed from the Mother Tree. I dug under an old root, just a teeny hole. Well, big enough for me. A bearded goblin came out with a broom shouting “Thief!”. I got my seed. And I bumped into three roots running away.
textes.Un jour, je suis monté sur le toit de la: One day I climbed onto the roof of the Bielle with an umbrella from her shop. I'd opened it, I was going to jump, like Achille when he was little. And whoops, a hand grabbed me by the collar. Adèle! She'd climbed all the way up the ladder. She told me about all seventeen of Achille's bumps. One by one. On the roof. It took ages.
textes.Un jour, je suis restée longtemps sous l: One day, I stayed a long time under the hull, looking at the signs. When I came up, I found Ewen white as a sheet at the end of the pontoon, with a rope and a life ring: he'd stopped counting at three hundred, and he was about to jump. He can't dive. Since then, I wave to him before going down for a long time.
textes.Un jour, je suivais Gaspard sur le quai: One day, I was following Gaspard along the quay to see the Admiral up close. The Admiral looked at me with one eye, then the other, and squawked: “GROUPER-HEAD!” A rude word! For me! I told everybody. Mum said it wasn't a rude word. I say it is. It's my nickname now.
One day I'll trip and fall.
One day, I'll sell the wind. You'll see.
textes.Un jour, je voudrais m'allumer, rien qu': Someday, I'd love to light up, just once! Just for one little second, like a real firefly. And for Zéphyr to see me and say “wow”. He'll never say “wow”. But a fairy can dream!
textes.Un jour, la drisse a cassé pendant qu'il: One day, the halyard snapped while he was climbing the mast. I caught him by the belt, one-handed, and set him back on the shrouds like you put a bottle on a shelf. He weighs nothing, Fil-de-Fer. Less than a sack of potatoes. He said thank you for a week. After that, he told me my hands were dirty.
textes.Un jour, la veille d'une course, Grelot: One day, the day before a race, Grelot sold me an apple pie. Very good. Next day, I find out: there was grated carrot in it! A pie with hidden carrot! The day before a race! I ran with four carrots in my tummy, maybe five. I still won. But since then, I sniff all her pies.
textes.Un jour, le majordome a servi par erreur: One day the butler served an iron-powder coffee by mistake to a lady from Port-Azur. She thought it was a local speciality. The next day Master Rivet adjusted his robot: now it asks every customer “Iron, or no iron?”. The tourists find it very authentic.
textes.Un jour, le professeur m'a laissé appuye: One day the professor let me push the lever for an explosion. A teeny tiny one, he said. He made me step back: “Further. Further.” Then: “Go!” I pushed. It went pff, with a blue cloud of smoke as big as a hat. He clapped! He said: “Smoke is the beginning of everything.” I wrote it on my bedroom wall.
textes.Un jour, le sifflet de midi a retenti av: One day, the noon whistle went off two seconds late. Two! I put my watch on the counter, asked for a size-eight spanner, and went to adjust the valve myself, on the old locomotive. Since then, noon on the dot. Gaston says it has never whistled so true.
textes.Un jour, ma jambe s'est coincée entre de: One day, my leg got stuck between two rotten planks of the pontoon. Impossible to get it out. The whole port was watching, Corbeau first of all. The Silent One came along, took me under the arms and pulled me out like a carrot. Then he looked at Corbeau, without a word. She stopped laughing. Hm. It's a gift.
textes.Un jour, mon piano a joué une musique qu: One day, my piano played a tune I'd never taught it. I never found out where it came from. Maybe it came from Stoneheart.
textes.Un jour, on a fait la course autour de l: One day, we raced around the Tree. He won, fine. But he flew right through my cloud of fireflies, and they stayed stuck in his hair for three days. He glowed all over! He was furious. I thought he looked much prettier that way.
textes.Un jour, on a voulu attraper le Roi des: One day we wanted to catch the Pond King with a mooncake. We put it right on the edge of the big pond, and hid behind a bush, not moving, not talking. For three minutes! And then a duck came along and ate it. The whole thing! Myrtille said it might have been the King in disguise. I think it was a duck.
textes.Un jour, pendant la leçon, il nous a rac: One day, during the lesson, he told us about Taouret, the hippo goddess who protects children. So I told everyone: from now on, we don't say the hippo, we say Taouret! It's nicer. Taouret is a lady, but she's a goddess. He doesn't know we call him that. Shh.
textes.Un jour, petit, je me suis perdu dans le: One day, as a boy, I got lost in my mother's gardens, among the ash peppers. I cried so loudly the sulphur roses closed up. It was my sister who found me. She hung a label round my neck: “Bulle, do not lose”. I wore it for a year. I still have it, in my drawer. Shh.
textes.Un jour, porter autre chose que du charb: One day, I'd like to carry something other than coal. Flowers, say. Flowers weigh nothing. Or a barrel of Sigrun's golden fizz: that weighs plenty, but it's worth it.
textes.Un jour, pour lui donner une leçon, je l: One day, to teach her a lesson, I weighed out turmeric and wrote on the packet: “saffron for fabric”. She opened it, looked, sniffed, and burst out laughing: “Nice turmeric, Lalla Aïcha.” A weaver who can recognise saffron! I didn't know whether to be offended or proud.
textes.Un jour, pour lui faire plaisir, je suis: Once, to cheer him up, I came back saying: “She smiled.” I hadn't delivered anything. He beamed all week. So did Ilyria, as it happens, without knowing why: he smiled so much that she ended up smiling back. So it wasn't quite a lie.
textes.Un jour, pour me faire pardonner, je lui: One day, to make amends, I brought her back a book. Not the right one: another, borrowed eighty years ago and completely forgotten. She opened it and said: “I thought this one was lost. Thank you.” She smiled. I'd never seen her smile. I was struck dumb. That's rare, for me.
textes.Un jour, pour voir, j'ai fait une lanter: One day, just to see, I made a lantern without a single hole. Nice and round, nice and smooth, my finest bumps. We lit the candle inside. Nothing. Not a star, not a glimmer: a hot cooking pot. Nourredine said nothing. He sat in front of it all evening, staring at the dark, looking very interested.
textes.Un jour, sa tisane était trop forte. Je: One day, her tea was too strong. I fell asleep at the counter, head on the envelopes. Three letters went out late. Three! Never in eight years. Pivoine said she'd measured it “for an owl”. I answered that an owl asleep at the counter is an owl who doesn't deliver.
textes.Un jour, sous le cadran arrêté, un touri: One day, under the stopped clock face, a tourist looked at the hands during my speech, then at his watch, and congratulated me: for once, the time was right. I thanked him. Hortense, in the front row, didn't laugh at all. Since then, I avoid looking up.
textes.Un jour, sur le port, j'ai vu un jeune g: One day, at the port, I saw a young giant carrying four crates at once and saying sorry to them. I planted myself in front of him and shouted: “YOU'RE GOING TO BE A CHAMPION!” He dropped everything. Ash eggs, everywhere. I paid for the eggs. It was Gorgoth. The best purchase of my life.
textes.Un jour, tout le village a voulu savoir: One day, the whole village wanted to know whose oven was best. We made the same dough, baked in his oven and in mine. Amenemhat tasted, blindfolded. The two loaves were exactly the same. Ptahmosé said: “My oven won.” I said: “Mine too.” We each went home, very pleased.
One day, you'll swim better. Sit down, kid.
textes.Un jour, un jeune capitaine est venu com: One day, a young captain came to order a suit of armour. He never laughed, but I laughed at everything he said. He came back every day for a month to “check the measurements”. The armour had been finished for three weeks. I said yes before he dared to ask. Pyrus has been going clang beside me for twenty years.
textes.Un jour, un marchand de passage m'a ache: One day, a passing merchant bought all my cacao, paid in beans, counted in front of me. That evening, while putting them away, a bean broke: inside, clay! He had emptied them and filled them with earth. A month of work, paid in mud. Since then, I test every bean with my teeth. And I count everything again. Even Ah Kin Pech's beans.
textes.Un jour, un paquet pour Ramure s'est mis: One day, a parcel for Ramure started ticking in the bag. Tick-tock, tick-tock. I thought it was one of Professor Boum's bombs and ran all the way to the water tank to throw it in. At the last moment, I read the label: “Tic Tacquet, for Pépin. Stopwatch. Fragile.” I wrote to Plumette: “Don't drown this one. I almost did.”
textes.Un jour, un pirate a éternué pendant la: One day, a pirate sneezed during the auction. He left with forty kilos of sardines. He had to eat them all week.
One day, a peccary scratched my leg. Yum Kab put honey on the scratch, and leaves on top. He said: “The honey of my bees heals everything, except foolishness.” In three days, it had closed. I don't know if I had been foolish. I didn't ask.
textes.Un jour, un touriste a loué un pédalo po: One day a tourist rented a pedalo on the first day of his holiday. Gérard Dupuis, super nice guy. He went round in circles for an hour, photographing the lighthouse on every lap. An hour! Kevin had to swim out to fetch him. Ever since, that pedalo's been called “Gérard”. It's painted on the hull, really small. Gérard doesn't know. Shh, OK?
textes.Un jour, un touriste s'était installé à: One day, a tourist had settled at my table, with a newspaper and a hat. Gisèle came over and put a little card in front of him: “Reserved for the harbour office.” He asked since when. She said: “Since forever.” He got up. The card didn't exist the day before. She'd written it just for him.
textes.Un jour, un vieux marin m'a vendu une pe: One day, an old sailor sold me a blue pearl “that shines all by itself, picked up under the sea”. I paid a lot for it. That evening, in the dark, it didn't shine. The next day, it was coming off on my fingers. Painted glass. Since then, I hate fakes. And I'm looking for the real one, the pearl of light people talk about. Stones don't lie. Sailors do.
textes.Un jour, une caisse est arrivée de Carèn: One day, a crate arrived from Carène, full of ropes and pots. I opened it: out came a crab, as big as my hand, furious. He clearly didn't agree to being sold. He pinched my finger and scuttled off under Karim's stall. Salomé had put him on the bill. I put him on mine, as damages.
textes.Un jour, à la fontaine, il m'a dit : « B: One day at the fountain he said to me: “Lovely day.” I said: “Very.” He ran off. I waited there an hour, in case he came back to finish his sentence. He came back the next day and said: “Lovely day.” We're making progress.
textes.Un jus de pomme au bar de la Guilde: An apple juice at the Guild bar
textes.Un lac noir, au fond du puits, avec des: A black lake at the bottom of the well, with carved slabs? The Ancients only had one song, {surnom}: the one on the fresco. Night, sea, day, serpent. Sing it as you walk.
textes.Un lingot d'or, pour payer les dieux: A gold ingot, to pay the gods
textes.Un livre d'aventures. Ça se voit : tu as: An adventure book. It shows: your boots are full of dust and your eyes are searching for the horizon. Shelf twelve, on the left. There are more. Quietly.
textes.Un livre, c'est un sorcier qui a gardé s: A book is a wizard who saved his voice for later. When you open it, it starts speaking again. It's the oldest magic in the world.
textes.Un livre, quelque part, en parle peut-êt: A book, somewhere, may speak of it.
textes.Un long boyau qui monte, des marches tai: A long tunnel climbing up, carved steps… and daylight, in front of the Great Moai.
textes.Un long couloir, une ornière bien droite: A long corridor, a perfectly straight rut down the middle… and, at the end, a lever. On the ceiling, a big round hole. Hmm.
