I put it on the counter, without a word, and went upstairs. The next day it was still on the counter. In the middle. It's still there. Zineb dusts it every morning.
textes.Un printemps, j'ai suivi la côte jusqu'à: One spring, I followed the coast all the way to Tazira. Three days' walk, sea spray all over my whiskers. Over there, on a square full of sand, drums all night, and people dancing like happy goats. I came home with sand in my tail for a month, rhythms for Pépin, and steps for Lilas. The sand, I kept for myself.
textes.Un printemps, je me suis cachée sous la: One spring I hid under Lyra's cloak, at the bottom of her boat, to go and see the humans. I sneezed right in the middle of the mist. Atchoo! Lyra turned back. I sulked for a whole day, that's my record. Next time I'll bring a hanky.
textes.Un prix ? C'est déjà un prix. Le fer coû: A discount? That IS the discount. Iron costs, charcoal costs, Clou costs. No.
textes.Un prix honnête, Jos ! Pour un sabre his: An honest price, Jos! For a historic sabre.
textes.Un problème ? Une catastrophe ! Marcel a: A problem? A catastrophe! Marcel played like a beginner and the jack shot off towards the fountain. No way to find it. No jack, no pétanque. No pétanque, no life.
textes.Un professeur ! Qui nous cherche ! Par l: A professor! Looking for us! By the tides… A colleague. An archivist from up there. I'll write to him. Tell me, how does one send a scroll upwards? Do you let go of it, and it floats?
textes.Un programme pour que mon frigo me dise: A program so my fridge says hello to me… Cheap… Hm.
textes.Un ptéranodon (Grand-Bec) ! Il tourne au: A pteranodon (Big-Beak)! It circles above you, screeches… then dives. Roll aside! It climbs back slowly, very low: that's your moment to strike.
textes.Un punch coco à la paillote: A coconut punch at the beach hut
textes.Un punch que tout l'archipel viendrait b: A punch the whole archipelago would come to drink at the Perroquet: the dwarves with their beards in the glass, the elves dipping their lips in it, the folk from under the sea, if there are any. A punch that everyone would agree on.
A punch. Without a ladle in it.
textes.Un pécari lui avait griffé la jambe. J'a: A peccary had clawed his leg. I put honey on it, and leaves. I told him my honey heals everything except foolishness. He thought for a long time, then asked if the scratch was foolishness. I told him no: chasing a peccary is courage. Getting clawed is bad luck.
textes.Un radeau ?! Et il flottait ? Ha ! Alors: A raft?! And it floated? Ha! Then you're already a shipwright. The hardest part is going from raft to three-master. There are a few planks in between.
textes.Un rayon de miel trouvé dans un arbre cr: A honeycomb found in a hollow tree. Restores two hearts.
A register in order for a whole season. Not one line crossed out, not one boat without a name. I don't believe it, but you asked me for a dream.
A shark? … The shark, I ate it. Cooked over a wood fire, with onions. Do you want me to cook you too?
textes.Un ressort tout brillant, tombé d'un rob: A shiny spring that fell off one of Lisse's robots. It goes "boing" when you let go of it. Ferraille puts them in her sculptures; Cradoc in his shoes.
textes.Un rhum de la Balafre au comptoir: A Balafre dark tonic at the counter
textes.Un robot ! Il fait une révérence, perd u: A robot! He bows, drops a bolt, picks it up, and bows again.
A robot! Shall I bite it? I'M BITING IT.
textes.Un robot déménageur de Lisse & Fils ! Tr: A Lisse & Fils mover robot! Very polite… and very heavy. When it raises its pincers, it's going to shove you: step aside, then strike. It falls apart into bolts and springs.
textes.Un robot entre dans un café. Le majordom: A robot walks into a café. The butler says: “We don't serve robots.” The robot replies: “That's fine, I'm a toaster.”
textes.Un robot soudeur ! Son arc bleu ne porte: A welder robot! Its blue arc doesn't reach far: stay out of range when the sparks fly, then strike while it cools down.
textes.Un rocher. Un vrai. Il a l'air un peu ve: A rock. A real one. It looks a little offended that someone lifted it.
textes.Un roi a beaucoup à dire, Ori !: A king has a lot to say, Ori!
textes.Un ronceux ! Ce paquet de ronces marche: A bramblekin! This bundle of brambles walks toward you and raises its thorny arms before striking: parry (F) or back off, then cut it to pieces.
textes.Un rouage ? Pour l'horloge ? … Bon. Appo: A cog? For the clock? … Fine. Bring me two logs to heat the forge, and three stones for the mould. I'll do the rest.
textes.Un rouage neuf forgé par Hector pour l'h: A new cogwheel forged by Hector for the town hall clock. It shines like a gold coin.
A cog has broken in the mechanism. Hector, the armourer, could forge a new one. But he always says he has no time. Would you mind talking to him?
textes.Un rouleau de toile épaisse, tissée serr: A roll of thick, tightly woven canvas that smells of salt and hemp. For ships' sails… and the wings of flying machines.
textes.Un rubis tout neuf, Orsik ! Combien ?: A brand-new ruby, Orsik! How much?
textes.Un rubis… Il brille comme ma forge un so: A ruby… It glows like my forge on a winter evening. {prix} coins, and I won't ask where it came from.
textes.Un rythme pour la braise, Omar ?: A rhythm for the embers, Omar?
textes.Un sablé en forme d'engrenage, au beurre: A gear-shaped shortbread, with butter and cinnamon. The teeth are crunchy. Restores two hearts.
textes.Un sac de facteur qui irait partout. Le: A postbag that could go anywhere. The village, the jungle, the elves, the dwarves, the flying island, and under the sea, with a waterproof satchel. I'd knock on every door in the archipelago.
textes.Un sac de toile plein de chaînes, de péd: A canvas bag full of chains, pedals, spokes, brake pads, and a bell shaped like a rat. Ferraille had hidden them for Rustine.
textes.Un sceau de pierre barré de chaînes de b: A stone seal barred with bronze chains. Behind it, an icy breath… You would need the key of the Ancients.
textes.Un second saut en plein vol (Espace, ou: A second jump in mid-air (Space, or A in VR, a second time in the air).
textes.Un secret ! Bravo. Plus on est nombreux: A secret! Well done. The more people keep it, the faster it flies away.
textes.Un secret ! Ooooh ! J'adore les secrets: A secret! Ooooh! I love secrets! I'll keep it, promise, cross my heart, on my mooncake. Nobody will know. Shh!
textes.Un secret ! Vous me torturez. Bon. J'écr: A secret! You're torturing me. All right. I'll write “terra incognita” in the corner. That's what the old cartographers wrote when they didn't know. It suits you very well.
textes.Un secret : le coffre de paie de la Moue: A secret: the Seagull's pay chest was made of ironwood, bound with copper. If your shovel hits metal, call me. We'll split it. Sixty-forty. My way.
textes.Un secret de cartographe : les jarres de: A cartographer's secret: the jars in your village put themselves back together. Nobody knows why. Me neither. But I pretend I do.
textes.Un secret de cartographe : sur ma carte,: A cartographer's secret: on my map, I'd marked the Seagull's pay chest. On the sea side, about twenty paces from Octave's great kapok tree, between three flat stones. He lives right next to it and has never found it. He doesn't read my maps. Take a shovel.
textes.Un secret, puisque tu as l'air de savoir: A secret, since you look like you can keep quiet. A hundred years ago, I carried Églantine's letter to the queen. On the way, I ran into Ventaile, and I wanted my rematch. Three days of racing. When the letter arrived, the brambles were already closing everything off. Since then, I fly fast. I'm catching up three days. I never manage.
textes.Un secret, {surnom}, et tu le gardes. Si: A secret, {surnom}, and you keep it. Sigrun, my little apprentice: I tell everyone I don't know her. Every spring, she sends me a barrel with no name. I taste it alone, door shut. It's better than mine. There. I'm so proud of her I could cry, and I don't know how to tell her.
textes.Un secret, {surnom}. Au fond du bassin,: A secret, {surnom}. At the bottom of the basin, there's an old boat everyone thinks is rotten. I've been caulking it at night for two years, plank by plank. For Nolwenn. I know she wants to leave, I've always known. The day she leaves, I want her to leave in a boat that doesn't take on water. That's all I know how to do.
textes.Un secret, {surnom}. La nuit, quand Bori: A secret, {surnom}. At night, while Borin sleeps, I light the little forge and make a spearhead for Kalda. It's a bit crooked. Very crooked, actually. I've redone it seven times. I've never given it to her. I'm scared she'll laugh. Or worse: that she'll use it.
textes.Un secret, {surnom}. Le jour où j'ai ouv: A secret, {surnom}. The day I opened Marie-Jeanne, she was still loaded. Two hundred years of powder, dry as sand. I was about to light my first fire in there. It was Tobias who sniffed, who stopped my hand, who drowned the lot in a bucket, and who never said a word about it. So when he complains about the noise, I hit softer. A bit.
textes.Un secret, {surnom}. Les corbeaux, je ne: A secret, {surnom}. I only half understand the crows. The other half, I make up. One day, to save a goat that had eaten the king's cloak, I translated a message from Croâ: “The king is the handsomest of dwarves.” Croâ had said nothing of the sort. Thorgal had it carved above the throne.
textes.Un secret, {surnom}. Les yeux de mon gra: A secret, {surnom}. My great-uncle's eyes are failing. He reads the runes with his fingertips when he thinks nobody's watching. So every evening, I read him the others out loud, “for practice”. I get the easiest ones wrong on purpose, so he can correct me. He must never know.
textes.Un secret. Un secret ! … Bien. Je range: A secret. A secret! … Very well. I'm putting my pencil away. There, it's away. I'm not looking at you with pleading eyes at all. Not at all.
textes.Un septième bleu ! Je l'ajoute à la lége: A seventh blue! I'll add it to the key.
textes.Un serre-tête avec deux oreilles de rena: A headband with two red felt fox ears with black tips. A gift from Mère-Lune: in Ramure, they take you for one of their own.
Just one? There are five missing, Titou.
textes.Un seul, matelot. Gaston, note l'heure !: Just one, sailor. Gaston, write down the time!
textes.Un seul. Et cinq minutes de conversation: Just one. And five minutes of conversation.
Just one. But it looks friendly.
textes.Un sifflet qui ne fait aucun bruit. L'in: A whistle that makes no sound at all. The inventor insists it's perfect for calling fish.
textes.Un signe ! Oui ! Mais lequel ? Elle a so: A sign! Yes! But which one? She smiled this morning. She sighed yesterday. She closed her window the day before. Those are all signs. But of what?
textes.Un slime ! Une petite gelée qui rebondit: A slime! A little jelly that bounces. When it squashes down flat, it's about to jump on you: step aside, then strike. The blue and pink ones are tougher.
textes.Un soir au Crâne Fendu, ce lourdaud se p: One evening at the Crâne Fendu, that lump leans over to me and says: “You're a dolt.” I thumped him. Obviously. He woke up under the counter. Afterwards, everybody explained to me that he wanted THE SALT. The salt! Who asks for salt by mumbling? Fine. Since then, I put the salt cellar next to him without him asking. It's my way of saying sorry.
textes.Un soir au Crâne Fendu, je lui ai demand: One night at the Crâne Fendu, I asked him to pass the salt. He heard “you're a dolt”. He hit me before I'd finished my sentence. I woke up under the counter, with Doc over me and the salt cellar beside me. Since then, I don't ask him for anything. I get up and fetch the salt myself.
textes.Un soir d'hiver, elle est descendue au C: One winter evening, she came down to the Heart in her nightgown, unable to sleep. I put my old coat over her shoulders and taught her to listen to an ember. We both fell asleep against the grate. Asmodin woke us at dawn, with two cups of coffee and a terrible look.
textes.Un soir d'hiver, je suis descendue au Cœ: One winter night, I went down to the Heart in my nightgown, because I couldn't sleep. Brother Cendrin didn't say a word. He put his old coat over my shoulders and showed me how to listen to an ember. We stayed until dawn. Asmodin found us both asleep against the grate.
textes.Un soir d'hiver, on est restées près du: One winter evening, we stayed by the fire, she and I, from nightfall till midnight. She said: “Cold.” I said: “Yes.” She said: “Good.” Three words in all. On her way to bed, she hugged me, very quickly, without looking at me. It's one of my loveliest evenings.
textes.Un soir d'hiver, un seul client au Perro: One winter evening, just one customer at the Perroquet, a sailor crying into his glass. Django played for him. Two hours, without stopping. The sailor left smiling. And Django always puts his hat at the edge of the stage, like his grandfather. I fill it on the sly, at closing time. He doesn't know. Well, I think he doesn't.
textes.Un soir d'hiver. Le feu. Brume et moi. D: A winter evening. The fire. Brume and me. From nightfall to midnight. … I said: “Cold.” She said: “Yes.” I said: “Good.” … Three words. It was a lovely evening. One of the best.
textes.Un soir d'orage, Héloïse est montée sur: One stormy evening, Héloïse climbed the tower to make me come down. In a long dress, in the rain, up the iron ladder, with lightning all around. She grabbed my kite string and said: “Électre. Now.” I came down. So did she, but more slowly: her dress had caught on a rung.
textes.Un soir d'orage, elle était encore sur l: One stormy evening she was still up on the tower with her kite and her key. I went up to fetch her. In a long dress, up the iron ladder, in the rain. When I reached the top, I said: “Come down.” She said: “Look first.” I looked. It was magnificent. Then we came down. Her first.
textes.Un soir d'orage, j'ai trouvé un chiot d': One stormy evening, I found an abandoned hellhound pup under a bridge, soaking wet, spitting little flames to warm itself up. I brought it home under my coat. It burned my coat. I called it Braise. The next day, I found a second one. Then a third. Pyrus said: “Never again.” There are twelve of them.
textes.Un soir de brouillard, je suis rentré à: One foggy night, I came home at three in the morning following his lantern. Grégoire was at the bow, all alone, stiff as a mast. I shouted to him: “How many ships have you counted?” He said: “One. Yours. It was late.” And he went to bed without saying goodnight.
textes.Un soir de brouille, Paulo a posé entre: One evening when we'd fallen out, Paulo set a single slice of tiramisu between Léa and me, with two spoons, and walked off whistling. We didn't touch it. The tiramisu looked at us all evening. At the end, Paulo took it away with a sigh: “Not even my tiramisu can do it.”
textes.Un soir de brume épaisse, on a gratté à: One evening of thick mist, something scratched at my door. A little she-wolf of eight, soaked to the ears: she had followed my tracks from the big pond, all alone. I gave her a blanket and a lesson: “A track is a sentence.” She fell asleep repeating it. The next day she was my pupil.
textes.Un soir de brume, en passant, Agathe m'a: One misty evening, in passing, Agathe said to me: “Your mother is proud of you.” I had never spoken to her about my mother. I don't know if it was the ball, or Séraphine, or nothing at all. I didn't ask her. I was afraid of the answer. I think about that sentence more often than I'd like.
textes.Un soir de brume, je lui ai dit que sa m: One misty evening, I told her that her mother was proud of her. That wasn't the ball. I knew Aube when I arrived: she used to come and drink my tea and talked of nothing but her daughter. Ysolde has never asked me how I knew. I won't tell her until she asks. You have to want to know.
textes.Un soir de brume, je suis rentré tard, s: One misty evening, I came home late, alone, with the hold full. I was so tired I fell asleep at the tiller. When I opened my eyes again, the Zahra was in the channel. All by herself. Green on the left, red on the right, right in the middle. Since then, I talk to the eye like a crewmate. I even save it a sardine.
textes.Un soir de fête, Lumina m'a demandé sept: One festival evening, Lumina asked me for seven wicks lit at the Heart, one for each of the city's seven Great Lanterns. She carried them one by one, from the Forge Cathedral to the port and beyond. Seven round trips. By morning, she was asleep on her feet, against the grate. I covered her with my coat. I often do that, with the young ones.
textes.Un soir de fête, Zigomar a glissé une pe: One festival night, Zigomar slipped a little rocket into one of my lanterns, “just to see”. The lantern flew up over the square, like a rising star. I was furious. Then the crowd applauded, and I cried because it was so beautiful. Ever since, at every festival, we send lanterns flying.
textes.Un soir de fête, Zigomar a voulu « améli: One festival night, Zigomar wanted to “improve” one of my lanterns. He slipped a little rocket into it. The lantern flew up over the square, all by itself, like a star. Everyone applauded. I was furious. Then I cried, because it was beautiful. Ever since, at every festival, we send lanterns flying.
textes.Un soir de fête, elle a frappé son grand: One festival night, she beat her big drum so hard that a jar fell off my shelf. I caught it in mid-air, just before the ground, with a dive. Nenetl shouted: “You see! It wanted to dance, and you made it dance!” I put the jar on the floor. It still trembles a little when Nenetl plays. I think it likes it.
textes.Un soir de fête, j'ai dansé trop près de: One feast night, I danced too close to her big drum. I tried to do a jaguar leap. My foot hit the drumskin. BOOM. Everyone thought it was on purpose. Nenetl kept the rhythm going without stopping, and shouted: “Again!” I did it again. Now it's a dance move. They call it “the jaguar stomp”.
textes.Un soir de fête, j'ai fait sept allers-r: One festival night, I made seven round trips between the Forge-Cathedral and the Great Lanterns, one wick at a time. On the seventh, I fell asleep standing up against the Heart's grate. I woke up under Brother Cendrin's old coat. He was sitting beside me. He was watching over the fire, and over me.
textes.Un soir de fête, j'ai glissé une petite: One festival evening, I slipped a little rocket into one of Lumina's lanterns, just to see. The lantern flew up over the square, like a rising star. Lumina was furious. Then she cried, because it was beautiful. Since then, at every festival, we send lanterns flying. She says it was her idea. I let her.
textes.Un soir de fête, l'Amiral s'est mis à si: One festival evening, the Admiral started whistling “boom ta-ka boom” right in time with me, from up on the galleon. I stopped playing to listen: it carried on all by itself, without missing a beat. The whole square applauded a bird. Gaspard took a bow for it, bright red. Me, I was jealous and delighted at the same time.
textes.Un soir de fête, la peau du bendir d'Oma: One festival evening, the skin of Omar's bendir split right in the middle of a tune. He didn't miss a beat: he grabbed one of Abdellah's copper trays from the next table and carried on with it. The square danced twice as hard. Abdellah spent the evening staring at his tray, gritting his teeth.
textes.Un soir de fête, un coup de vent du larg: One festival evening, a gust of wind off the sea blew out every candle on the square at once. Darkness. The musicians stopped, the children cried. I took my taper and relit the lanterns one by one, starting with the one in the middle. At the tenth, the drum started up again. At the thirtieth, people were dancing. Ba Sidi made a tale of it. I've never heard it to the end.
textes.Un soir de fête, une terrasse qui débord: A festival evening, the terrace spilling out all the way to the fountain. Django playing, the clock striking, and everyone ordering at once.
textes.Un soir de grand vent sur la place, mes: One very windy evening on the square, my sheet music blew away all at once. I shouted. Scarlett threw six knives, very fast, and pinned the sheets to the gallows post, one by one. Not one torn. I was speechless. Then I played the Song of the Brawl King in front of the post, just for her.
textes.Un soir de grand vent sur la place, ses: One very windy evening on the square, his sheet music blew away all at once, like seagulls. I threw six knives, fast, and pinned them one by one to the gallows post. Not one was missing. Tom played the Song of the Brawl King right there, in front of the post, to thank me.
textes.Un soir de grande fête, en plein milieu: One big festival night, right in the middle of a tune, crack: the skin of my bendir split. The whole square froze. I grabbed the first round thing I saw: one of Abdellah's copper trays, on the next table. Boom! It rang like a bell! The square danced twice as hard. Abdellah stared at his tray all evening, the way you look at a child who's hurting himself.
textes.Un soir de tempête, il y a longtemps, un: One stormy evening, long ago, an old man in a hood sat down at my father's table. He lost three times in a row. He laid a scrap of parchment on the baize and said: “Three times, that's the price.” Then he went out into the rain. My father kept the parchment and made me swear to give it up only to whoever beat me three times in a row. That's the rule.
textes.Un soir où Léa regardait la mer, Paulo s: One evening while Léa was looking at the sea, Paulo leaned over to me: “The day you take her hand with your ring on your finger, I sing. At your table. In Italian. Very loud.” He chose the song that night, one of his nonna's, and rehearsed it in the kitchen all week. The whole quay heard it. Léa pretended not to smile.
textes.Un soir où il dormait, j'avais besoin d': One evening while he was asleep, I needed a stake. I… borrowed his hook from the crate next to his hammock, and bet it. I won, obviously. But Crochet woke up before I brought it back. He didn't speak to me for a week. With Crochet, that doesn't change much. But I felt the difference.
textes.Un soir où le Zéphyr débarquait douze vo: One evening when the Zéphyr landed twelve travellers, Salomé planted herself at the breach with a sign: “Seaweed beds, two coins, no risk of falling”. She got eight, I got four. The next day, her eight came begging me for a hammock, covered in sea fleas. I charged them double. I'm not proud of it. Well, a bit.
textes.Un soir où mon four boudait, Lyra lui a: One evening when my oven was sulking, Lyra sang it a bark lullaby. The bread rose. Pure chance, obviously. But ever since, when the oven's in a mood, I go and fetch Lyra. Also by chance.
textes.Un soir où son four boudait, je lui ai c: One evening when her oven was sulking, I sang it a bark lullaby. The bread rose. Sylwen swears it was luck. And yet, ever since, she comes to fetch me every time her oven is in a mood.
textes.Un soir, Agathe est arrivée au Cercle av: One evening, Agathe arrived at the Circle with her crystal ball under her arm. She wanted to put it on the altar, “to see what happens”. I said no before she'd finished her sentence. She smiled: “The ball warned me you'd say no.” Then why come? She didn't answer. She left happy.
textes.Un soir, Ambroise a voulu arrêter la pen: One evening, Ambroise wanted to stop the clock “just to think”. Stop the clock! At table 2! I laid my hand on it as if it were a newborn baby. Gaston blew the machine's whistle. The whole Crankshaft turned round. We didn't speak for four minutes. The longest silence in forty years of friendship.
textes.Un soir, Amine m'a emmené près du Fondou: One evening, Amine took me near the Fondouk. We climbed up some crates, one, two, three, without a sound. And at the top, on the roof, there was the ginger cat. Sleeping curled up, like a loaf of bread. Purring. And under him… no. That, I'm not telling. Cross my heart, spit and sardine.
textes.Un soir, Ba Sidi a raconté l'histoire d': One evening, Ba Sidi told the story of a pirate who'd hidden a treasure in the caves, a very long time ago, and of his grandson who came back to find it. I didn't sleep all night. I kept looking at the door of the captain's cabin, thinking: it's him, the grandson. We're in a story, us. For real.
textes.Un soir, Bartholomé l'a regardé fixement: One evening, Bartholomé stared at him and said: “The skull, the skull.” The little one went white as a sheet. I told him Bartholomé says that to everybody. It's true. But not with that look. Not like that. The next day, Petit-Pierre came back anyway, with his seeds. He's brave, that little one.
textes.Un soir, Bertha a toussé un peu fort, et: One evening, Bertha coughed a bit loudly, and the lantern above her went all black. I left it outside Nourredine's workshop at dawn, with a note of apology. A few days later, it was back on the square, clean as a new pin. So… I borrowed it again. It had to go back to Bertha, after all.
textes.Un soir, Bourru était enrhumé ; il est r: One evening Bourru had a cold; he stayed home with honey and one of Pivoine's teas. Pépin drummed alone. And me… I couldn't find the step. Not once. I stumbled twice in front of the whole Circle. The next day his drum came back, and so did my feet. Grelot went “hrmm” for a week.
textes.Un soir, Caelan est entré dans la boutiq: One evening, Caelan came into the shop clutching his chest: “Aëlwen, I'm dying.” I examined him for an hour. Ilyria had said hello to him. Just hello. I gave him a camomile and the bill. He wanted to pay in song. I refused the song.
textes.Un soir, Calcine m'a joué une valse, dev: One evening, Calcine played me a waltz in front of my bench and asked me what I thought of it. I told her the hem of her third bar was a little loose. She looked at me without understanding. Then she played it again, tighter. It was much better. She told me: “You hear music like fabric.” It's true.
textes.Un soir, Fanny a fait un grand geste. Ya: One evening, Fanny made a big gesture. Yaya landed in my arms. Just like that. All of a sudden. I said: “… You okay?” She said yes. I didn't let go right away. Three seconds. Maybe four. The whole dance floor saw. Nobody talks about it. … Good.
textes.Un soir, Hugo et Léa ont dîné chez moi s: One evening, Hugo and Léa had dinner here without saying a word to each other. He was looking at his finger, she was looking at the sea. I served them a single slice of tiramisu with two spoons. They each ate their half, sitting very straight, without touching. Never seen such a sad tiramisu. There was a mystery, I could feel it.
textes.Un soir, Lola a écrit sur l'ardoise : «: One evening, Lola wrote on the chalkboard: “Sweethearts' Punch”. I didn't even know we had one. She'd doubled the recipe: twice the coconut, twice the sugar. Lucas drank three. He went home singing, the big shy lump. I didn't say a thing. I left the line on the board. It's still there.
textes.Un soir, Lucas a joué sa casquette. Il l: One evening, Lucas bet his cap. He lost it, of course: he had three aces in his hand and his eyes on Lola. I kept it for a week. Then I gave it back to him “on rental”: one coffee a week. He's still paying. To make it up to him, I slip him a painted shell now and then. We've never done the sums.
textes.Un soir, Lucas est entré pendant que je: One evening, Lucas came in just as I was bringing Django his punch. Django saw and slowed his waltz down. So much that I had to cross the Perroquet in slow motion, in time with the music, with my tray, like in a dream. The whole room was watching me. Lucas too. I've never walked so slowly in my life.
textes.Un soir, Lulu est revenue de chez ses fé: One night, Lulu came back from her fairies with golden pollen on her cheeks. She climbed onto the stage and whispered: “Softer, they're sleeping.” I played the calmest set of my life, all night. Tchoum fell asleep standing up. The next day, Lulu thanked me on behalf of the queen.
textes.Un soir, Marley a glissé une banane dans: One evening, Marley slipped a banana into my basket, “so your boss can taste it”. During the crossing, I sat on it without seeing it. The next day's batch had a faint taste of banana, who knows how. Margaux looked at me for a long time. I said it was an experiment. We sold them. I never confessed to Marley.
textes.Un soir, Pilli m'a demandé s'il pouvait: One evening, Pilli asked me if he could hit the huehuetl. Once. I lifted him up to the skin. He hit it with all his might. Boom! Tlaco ran off, the dancers jumped, and Pilli looked at me with huge eyes: “I made thunder!” Since then, he asks me every evening. Once. Always once.
textes.Un soir, Pépin a tapé si fort, au moment: One evening Pépin drummed so hard, just as the moon was lifted out of the pond, that the skin of his drum burst. Boom… pfft. Nothing more. I finished the dance to the big drum alone. Slowly. Oh… it was the loveliest evening of the year. Pépin doesn't understand why I said that. I won't explain.
textes.Un soir, Pépin est rentré avec des feuil: One evening, Pépin came home with ember leaves in his hair and forty mushroom names in his head. He recited them to me over dinner. The biggest one is called Gérard. I pretended to be cross that he'd gone to the Wood. In truth, I was proud. He remembers mushrooms better than his lessons.
textes.Un soir, Pépin était enroué. Plus de voi: One evening, Pépin was hoarse. No voice. No pep. He left his drum. I played alone. Slowly. The whole Circle danced in slow motion. Even Gland. Even Mère-Lune, under her blanket. Good. Very good. Pépin says: longest evening of the year. Hrmm. Same thing.
textes.Un soir, Roux est monté à la cime avec s: One evening, Roux came up to the treetop with his flute, “to help me count”. He played a slow tune, with the squirrel note in the middle, and I listened. I forgot to count. When he left, I didn't know if I was at twelve or thirteen. Since that evening, it's twelve or thirteen. It was very beautiful. That's exactly the problem.
textes.Un soir, Silas m'a demandé de lui montre: One evening, Silas asked me to show him my scrap of parchment. I gave him the answer I give everyone: “Three wins, sir.” He sat down and played. He lost the first round. He stood up, bowed, and said: “Your father would have answered the same.” It's the finest compliment I've ever been paid.
textes.Un soir, Sofia m'a demandé un collier qu: One evening Sofia asked me for a necklace we'd never sell. With a single pearl, found near the golden point, to the south-west. She wouldn't say why that pearl mattered. I asked her only one question: “Blue thread or gold thread?” Blue. I ask Sofia just one question a day. That's our rule.
textes.Un soir, Tchoum cherchait depuis une heu: One night, Tchoum had spent an hour trying to work out why Raoul was crackling. Me: “It's the sea.” Bastien, passing by: “It's a crab.” Tchoum opened the speaker: a crab, making itself at home. Tchoum still hasn't forgiven Bastien for being right before him. And me, ever since, I check. While pretending not to check.
textes.Un soir, Tiburce m'a offert un bloc de c: One evening, Tiburce gave me a block of rosin for my bow, carved like a horn and polished with ember oil. It was so perfumed that my violin smelled of roses for a month. The whole square asked me if I'd changed violins. I didn't thank him right away. I made him wait three days.
textes.Un soir, Tom m'a demandé d'amener Bartho: One evening, Tom asked me to bring Bartholomé on stage. He played the whalers' jig, and when the chorus came, Bartholomé shouted “Jellyfish-head!” right on the beat. The whole Crâne Fendu howled with laughter. Since then, it's part of the song. Tom even rewrote the chorus around it. Bartholomé gets one seed per performance.
textes.Un soir, Vespérine est venue me montrer: One evening, Vespérine came to show me her figures: my peppers grow faster when I sing them a song. A quarter faster. She was so proud of having measured it. I told her I already knew. She pouted. Then she smiled, just a tiny bit. I wrote down the date. Like she would.
textes.Un soir, absorbée par mon roman, j'ai te: One evening, absorbed in my novel, I held the newspaper upside down for an hour. Gisèle walked by, turned it the right way up without stopping, and said out loud: “The weather reads better the right way up, Colette.” Nobody understood. I did. I blushed behind the weather forecast.
textes.Un soir, au Cercle, il y avait un gâteau: One evening, at the Circle, there was a mooncake all alone on a bench. Nobody around. I tasted it. To check. Mrrr… It was… good. Very good, even. I finished it. If you tell Trèfle, {surnom}, I'll say you're lying. And I'll charge you double for your skewers.
textes.Un soir, au Diable Repu, Charbonnel raco: One evening, at the Diable Repu, Charbonnel was telling his ash-storm story for the thousandth time. He got to the part where the wave is the size of the volcano. I said: “Hm. Last week, it was the size of the lighthouse.” The whole tavern laughed. He looked at me, thought about it, and said: “It's grown.” He's a real storyteller.
textes.Un soir, au Diable Repu, je racontais ma: One evening, at the Diable Repu, I was telling my ash storm. Kraxx said: “Last week, the wave was as tall as the lighthouse.” The whole tavern laughed. I answered: “It's grown.” Since then, Kraxx comes every evening to check the size of the wave. He says nothing. He listens. He's my most attentive listener.
textes.Un soir, au moment exact où le djinn sor: One evening, at the exact moment the djinn came out of the sardine, the lantern's candle went out. Pitch black. Someone screamed. I carried on, in the dark, in a low voice. Nobody moved, nobody breathed. The best story of my life. The next day, I asked Nourredine to blow out the candle for me every evening. He refused.
textes.Un soir, avec Bernard, on a calculé. Tre: One evening, Bernard and I did the maths. Thirty years on the round, twenty kilometres a day, six days a week… We worked it out on the back of one of Gisèle's receipts. Result: I walked three times round the whole archipelago. Bernard checked twice. He said: “No stopwatch, doesn't count.” It counts.
textes.Un soir, c'est grand-père qui s'est endo: One evening Grandpa fell asleep before me! Right in the middle of the story, snore. So I finished it myself, for the other little ones. With a dragon in it. A huge one. They loved it. Grandpa woke up and asked “Where was I?”, and everyone shouted: “THE DRAGON!”
textes.Un soir, depuis la Skala, j'ai peint le: One evening, from the Skala, I painted the pirates' galleon at dusk, all black against the pink sky. The captain gave me three gold coins, and a promise to keep: never show it to anyone. Later, looking at it by candlelight, I saw what I'd painted without noticing: behind the galleon, in the cliff, tiny little lights. In the caves.
textes.Un soir, depuis la cime, dans le noir, j: One evening, from the treetop, in the dark, I saw Mochi way down at the Circle. I called out: “You've got cake on your snout!” She jumped so hard her ears shot up. She thinks I can see in the dark. I can a little, it's true. But mostly, Mochi always has cake on her snout.
textes.Un soir, des jeunes se moquaient de moi: One evening, some youngsters were making fun of me because I was talking to the street lamps. Gorgoth got up from his bench. He didn't say anything. He just stood next to me, at his full height. The youngsters left. Gorgoth sat back down and asked me: “What's this street lamp called?”
textes.Un soir, deux marins de passage ont sort: One evening, two passing sailors drew their knives at my table. I snapped my fingers, and my two friends stood up. Monsieur Crochet stood up too, without my asking, and laid his hook on the table, in plain view. The knives went back into pockets. I offered him a rum. He didn't say thank you. He didn't need to.
textes.Un soir, deux marins de passage ont voul: One evening, two passing sailors wanted to fight at his table, with knives. Sylvain snapped his fingers. His two big lads stood up. So did I. The Code says: fists, never blades. The sailors looked at my hook, then at the lads, then at the door. They chose the door. Sylvain bought me a rum. No questions.
textes.Un soir, devant toute la place, elle m'a: One evening, in front of the whole square, she told me my horns shone brighter than my conversation. Everyone laughed. I bowed and replied: “Then I shall be silent, and let you play.” I stayed until the last note without a word. At the end, she looked at me one second longer than usual. I counted.
textes.Un soir, elle a mordu dans mon gâteau, e: One evening, she bit into my cake, closed her eyes, and opened her mouth as if to say “that's it”. I dropped the plate. And… she coughed. A crumb went down the wrong way. I patted her back, gave her water, and when she could talk, she said: “Almost.” I nearly cried. Or laughed. Both, I think.
textes.Un soir, elle a regardé par ma fenêtre p: One evening she looked through my window while I was looking at my shards. Next day, the whole village knew I was “smiling”. I wasn't smiling. I had a cramp. In my mouth. It happens.
textes.Un soir, elle est arrivée avec un pot de: One evening, she turned up with a pot of honey “to sweeten your soup”. I'd prepared her a little bag of salt “to wake up your tea”. We made the swap in front of the whole inn. Mathurin applauded. Since then, the pot of honey sits in pride of place on my counter, full, and I know my salt is on her shelf. Full too.
textes.Un soir, elle m'a apporté sept gâteaux d: One evening she brought me seven different cakes. Seven! More honey, less honey, baked longer, a pinch of who-knows-what… I tasted all seven, very seriously, and said “almost” seven times. The next day I had a tummy ache, and she already had an eighth attempt.
textes.Un soir, elle m'a cherché dans toute la: One evening, she searched for me all over the Shark's Tooth, rolling pin in hand. I hid under Sylvain's big table, and he carried on dealing the dice without a word. She walked past three times. My leg was sticking out. She pretended not to see it. I think. Or else she was letting me stew.
textes.Un soir, elle m'a obligé à jouer avec se: One evening, she made me play with her own dice, carved from the bone of the whale on Bone Beach. I lost three games in a row. Me! Three! Those dice are cursed, my friend. Or honest. I don't know which is scarier. Since then, when she takes them out of her pocket, I suddenly remember urgent business elsewhere.
textes.Un soir, elle m'a regardé boire mon rhum: One evening she watched me drink my rum. A long time. Then she said my age. Right. And the name of my first captain. Right too. I'd told nobody here. She said: “I know sailors who drink like you.” Hm. I'm wary now. I drink the same way.
textes.Un soir, en cueillant mes herbes dans le: One evening, picking my herbs in the hotel garden, I heard sniffling behind the thyme. It was the young bride from room seven, sitting on the ground. She asked me if I had anything for husbands. I said I had lime blossom. It's a start.
textes.Un soir, en essuyant les verres derrière: One evening, drying glasses behind the bar, she started singing the chorus with me. Very softly. She sings well, she doesn't know it. Lucas looked up from his cards. She stopped dead and dropped a glass. I carried on with the chorus alone, louder, to cover for her. That's what neighbours are for.
textes.Un soir, en longeant la côte ouest, j'ai: One evening, sailing along the west coast, I wanted to “borrow” the Léviathan's bell. A souvenir, nothing more. I climbed onto their wreck without a sound. She was waiting for me on deck, with a lantern, standing straight. She said: “Good evening, captain.” That's all. I turned back. Out of politeness. Purely out of politeness.
textes.Un soir, en m'entraînant, ma balle est e: One evening, while I was training, my ball went into her house through the window and broke three threads on her loom. She made me retie the threads myself. With these fingers, made for the ball! It took me an hour. I sweated more than in a match. Since then, I respect weavers. And windows.
textes.Un soir, en passant devant le chantier,: One evening, walking past the boatyard, I looked through the window. On the workbench, there was a brand-new plank, with a name carved on it: THE WHALE. And in a corner, a little carved whale. He's started before I've paid! I acted like nothing happened. I always act like nothing happened. But I walk past every evening.
textes.Un soir, en plein morceau, elle a levé l: One evening, in the middle of a song, she raised her hand: “Play the low note again, please. For the colour.” For the colour! I played it again. She closed her eyes and said: “Violet.” The whole room turned to look at me. I played it again. Ten times. I don't know why I obeyed.
textes.Un soir, en pleine chanson, une corde de: One evening, mid-song, a string on his oud snapped. Twang. Anyone else would have stopped. Not Hamid: every time the missing note came round, he sang it, right in the middle of the tune, as if nothing had happened. By the end, the whole square was singing it with him. It became the song of the broken string.
textes.Un soir, en pleine danse de la baleine,: One evening, in the middle of the whale dance, Jacquot took one step back too many and trod on my guembri, lying beside me. Crack went the neck. He was so sorry he nearly cried. He ran aboard to fetch a bit of rope from the Murène, and I fixed it on my knees. My guembri has a pirate's knot now. It sounds better.
textes.Un soir, en pleine histoire, j'ai oublié: One evening, in the middle of a story, I forgot the ending. Completely. Calcine understood straight away: she held a single note, very long, very soft. The crowd thought it was a moment of suspense. The note lasted ten minutes. Then the ending came back to me. The whole square applauded. The note, mostly.
textes.Un soir, en rentrant du Crâne Fendu, j'a: One evening, on my way back from the Crâne Fendu, I wanted to say goodnight to the moon in the water. I leaned over. A lot. Splash. The water was cold and all… see-through. I don't like that. It was the Silent One who fished me out by the collar, like a cat, and carried me back to the Widow on his shoulder. The next day, he patted me on the head without a word. The Code is the Code.
textes.Un soir, en rentrant, je suis passé sous: One evening, on my way home, I passed under Prudence's window. Windows shut. And inside, a piano was playing. Not the mechanical one: this one made mistakes, stopped, started again. Then it played the waltz all the way through, perfectly. I stayed in the dark until the last note. I've never mentioned it to her. Some things you don't file a patent on.
textes.Un soir, en revenant de là-haut, j'ai de: One night, coming back from up there, I asked Mistral to play more softly, because the fairies were asleep. He didn't ask a single question. He played the gentlest set in the world, all night long. Tchoum fell asleep standing up. The fairies slept well — the queen told me. I'll never forget it.
textes.Un soir, il a déposé le filet devant la: One evening, he left the net at the lighthouse door. Folded nice and square, my brother's lead weights inside. I found it on my way down, at dawn. I carried it to his door, on the quay, and went back up. Without a word. He thought that was what I wanted. That's not how you give back a net.
textes.Un soir, il a frappé à la Tour pour savo: One evening, he knocked at the Tower to find out whether the Great Crystal slept. I took him to the bench in the courtyard to keep watch with him. After a quarter of an hour, Pip was asleep against my shoulder; the Crystal was still spinning. I carried him to the dormitory. The next day, I told him he'd won: at least he had slept.
textes.Un soir, il a joué un air avec de grands: One evening, he played a tune with big drumbeats, BOOM, BOOM, like my cannons. I heard it! All of it! I tapped my foot. Mama Grog says I almost smiled. That's not true. I clenched my teeth so as not to smile. IT'S NOT THE SAME. But I bought him a grog, the fiddler. For the drum.
textes.Un soir, il a oublié la fin de son histo: One evening, he forgot the end of his story right in the middle of a sentence. I saw it in his eyes. So I held a note, very long, very soft. The crowd thought it was a moment of suspense. The note lasted ten minutes. My arm was on fire. Then he remembered, and the whole square applauded. He bought me one of Bobor's brioches.
textes.Un soir, il a parlé de la grande mare, e: One evening he talked about the big pond, and I asked questions about the dragon. How many teeth, how many legs, does it like hazelnuts, can it swim upside down… Forty-seven questions! Pomme-de-Pin counted. Grandpa said: “Twice upon a time…” and started another story. I think he knows too much.
textes.Un soir, il a parlé si longtemps que le: One evening, he talked so long the forge fire went out. All by itself. He didn't notice. He was telling me about his race, bend by bend. Ten arches. Twice. I went to bed. He finished the story to the anvil.
textes.Un soir, il a voulu faire un saut de jag: One evening, he tried to do a jaguar leap while dancing, and his foot hit my huehuetl. BOOM! Everyone thought it was on purpose. I shouted: “Again!” He did it again, very proud. Now it's a dance move: “the jaguar stomp”. All the young people copy it. He makes out it was his idea. It was mine.
textes.Un soir, il est venu me trouver seul, au: One evening, he came to find me alone, at the end of the quay. No airs and graces. He wanted to know how I set Bertha's elevation. I explained everything: the screw, the wooden wedge, the eye. He took notes in a little notebook. I didn't laugh, {surnom}. Not once. Don't tell him I told you.
textes.Un soir, il est venu me voir, tout série: One evening, he came to see me, all serious: “Ahmed, for the Whale's eye, what do you recommend?” He doesn't even have the boat, just a quarter of the coins. I said: “An eye that isn't cross-eyed.” He said: “No. A cross-eyed one, like yours. It brings you back to port.” I didn't answer. He was right.
textes.Un soir, il faisait tout noir, et monsie: One evening it was all dark, and Mister Hulotte, way up at the treetop, said to me: “Mochi, you've got cake on your snout.” IN THE DARK! From way up there! I wiped it, but it was too late, Mummy had heard. Since then I wash my snout before I go under the Post Office. Just in case.
textes.Un soir, il m'a apporté une perche contr: One evening, he brought me a perch in exchange for a jar of beer. The perch leapt out of the basket, straight into my dough. It swam in it, I swear, like in the river! Khéty fell off the bench laughing. I baked the dough anyway: “perch bread”, a hit. I never made it again. You can't find perch that motivated any more.
textes.Un soir, il m'a avoué qu'il aimait quelq: One evening, he confessed to me that he loved someone. Of course, I told everyone. But I don't know WHO! I've tried everything. Tiyi? He laughed. Néferet? He went pale. Ix Chab, the merchant from Yaxché? He said: “Why not.” He's making fun of me. I'll find out. Mérit always finds out.
textes.Un soir, il m'a battu deux fois de suite: One evening, he beat me twice in a row. The whole room went silent. On the third game, I listened. Not to the dice: to him. His heart was beating so hard you could hear it at the bar. He threw: two, three, one. I told him what I'd heard. He bowed very low to me, without a word. It's the only time I've seen him lost for words.
One evening he imitated me in front of the crew. Arms crossed, brows knitted. “Hm. The deck. Hm. Do it again.” Everyone was laughing. I was on the stairs. Saw it all. Said nothing. Went back up. The next day I shouted a bit less loudly. A bit. Hm. It was a good likeness.
textes.Un soir, il me dit : « Aide-moi à recomp: One evening he says to me: “Help me recount my gold.” I hear: “Help me knock you out cold.” I flipped the table. Dice, coins, everything went flying. Afterwards, Coquille explained. I apologised. Loudly. Ignace said it was the best evening of the week. I don't understand that man.
textes.Un soir, il n'est pas rentré. J'ai couru: One evening, he didn't come home. I ran everywhere. I found him on the south canal, in a canoe, stuck in the reeds, with Tlaco barking at the herons. He told me: “I wanted to see where the lake goes.” I scolded him. Then I hugged him very tight. Then I scolded him again. The herons were laughing.
textes.Un soir, j'ai accéléré le rythme pour vo: One evening, I sped up the rhythm to see if she'd keep up. She did. I sped up again. She sang faster and faster, without a single mistake, eyes shining. The dancers dropped to the ground one after another. We finished out of breath, laughing. Just in time for her midnight song.
textes.Un soir, j'ai allumé les réverbères en r: One evening, I lit the street lamps in time with her waltz: one, two, three, flame. I thought no one could see. The next day, Calcine played a new waltz, with an exact silence between each bar, just long enough to light a street lamp. She looked up at me, at the top of my ladder. I nearly fell.
textes.Un soir, j'ai dansé si fort que j'ai mar: One evening, I danced so hard I stepped on his guembri, laid on the ground during a break. Crack, the neck. Lhoucine didn't shout. I ran aboard to fetch a bit of rope from the Murène, and he mended the neck on his knees. He played the whale dance until midnight. Since then, he says his guembri is a bit of a pirate.
textes.Un soir, j'ai décidé d'en finir : je lui: One evening, I decided to settle it once and for all: I brought her seven different cakes. More honey, less honey, baked longer, more chestnut, a pinch of salt… She tasted all seven, very seriously, and said “almost” seven times. Seven almosts! The next day, Pivoine took her up a tea for her tummy. I felt very guilty.
textes.Un soir, j'ai emprunté le grand filet de: One evening, I borrowed the big fishing net from the harbour, and we stretched it between the mooring mast and the flagpole. Landing plan number one. Adèle shouted: “Now!” Achille went by ten metres to the side, waving. The net caught a seagull. It was furious. So was Adèle.
textes.Un soir, j'ai frappé le grand tambour tr: One evening, I hit the big drum really hard, and a jar fell off his shelf. He caught it in mid-air with a magnificent dive. I shouted: “See! It wanted to dance!” He was furious. Then he looked at the jar in his arms and burst out laughing. Since then, when I play, he stands by the shelves. To dance with them.
textes.Un soir, j'ai fredonné à Mistral un chan: One evening I hummed Mistral a whale song I'd heard while diving, to make him happy. He spent three nights recreating it with his machines. When he played it for me, it was almost right. I said “almost”. He looked so disappointed I nearly said “exactly”. He's still working on it.
textes.Un soir, j'ai gagné deux fois de suite à: One evening, I won twice in a row at his big table. The whole Shark's Tooth held its breath: one more, and he'd have to stake his famous scrap of parchment. I rolled. Two, three, one. Sylvain didn't even smile. He said: “I heard your heart beating, Monsieur Malaterre.” I hate him. With great respect.
textes.Un soir, j'ai imité le second devant tou: One evening, I did an impression of the first mate in front of the whole crew. Arms crossed, eyebrows like this: “Hm. The deck. Hm. Again.” Everybody was laughing. Luckily, he wasn't there. The next day, he yelled at me a bit less loud. He must've had a sore throat.
textes.Un soir, j'ai joué toute la fête sur un: One evening I played the whole festival on a single rhythm: Abdellah's tap-tap-tap, the one he beats on his trays at the end of the morning. Between two tunes, I shouted to the whole square: “This rhythm belongs to Abdellah!” He was furious. The next day he came to the grill to ask, all casual, whether we'd be playing it again.
textes.Un soir, j'ai joué un air de marins avec: One evening, I played a sailors' tune with a drum, really whacking it: BOOM, BOOM. Belle-Humeur, in the corner by the fireplace, tapped his foot. His moustache twitched. Mama Grog swears he smiled. He swears he didn't. Afterwards, he bought me a grog without a word. For a man who shouts everything, that was a speech.
textes.Un soir, j'ai laissé Tibo raconter tout: One evening, I let Tibo tell a story all by himself, on my stone. He told of the pirates' biscuit, so hard it broke the anchor, then the deck, then the captain's tooth. The circle laughed till they cried. So did I. He had stage fright, he talked too fast. But he knew where the pauses were. That can't be taught.
textes.Un soir, j'ai laissé une couronne de feu: One evening, I left a crown of golden leaves on his big black speakers, to thank him. He wore it until dawn. He tells everyone he has a secret admirer. That's not untrue.
textes.Un soir, j'ai mis dans le Bain Gorgoth d: One evening, I put some of my sister's purple salts in the Gorgoth Bath, as a surprise after a fight. He came out purple. Purple for three days! At the Arena, the crowd called him “Gorgoth the Mauve”. He came to see me, worried. I told him it was on purpose. It wasn't on purpose. But it was very pretty.
textes.Un soir, j'ai mordu dans son gâteau, et: One evening I bit into her cake, and for a second I saw Luzerne's kitchen again. I opened my mouth to say “that's it”… and coughed instead. Trèfle patted my back, all pale. It wasn't quite it yet. It was already something else. I didn't know which of the two to tell her.
textes.Un soir, j'ai mélangé de la poudre bleue: One evening, I mixed blue powder, raspberry syrup and a seagull feather. It went pfff, and the Rocket's whole mainsail turned pink. Pink forever! Dad said it was magic, not chemistry. Mum said: “We're taking her to the archmage before she repaints the sea.” That's how I got here.
textes.Un soir, j'ai oublié de rentrer dîner. P: One evening, I forgot to come home for dinner. For the third time that week. The next day, Margot slipped an alarm clock into my pocket, set for seven o'clock. It rang while I was blowing a giant bubble: it burst, and the whole stand screamed. I got home on time. Margot had already laid the table.
textes.Un soir, j'ai oublié des coquilles au pi: One evening, I left some shells at the foot of the tower, in the crystal's warmth. By morning, they were soft as wax. I blew into them through a hollow reed, and a bubble of mother-of-pearl was born, round, perfect. I ran to show Coralin. He said: “That's cheating.” I left that very evening.
textes.Un soir, j'ai oublié le salut. J'avais l: One evening, I forgot the signal. I had my eye to the telescope, on the Murène. So Si Larbi covered his light, and left it covered. The green lighthouse, dark. The channel without a green light! One minute, two, five. I ran to cover the red one three times. The green came back on. He never mentioned it again. There was no need.
textes.Un soir, j'ai parlé de pêche à Tchoum pe: One evening I talked fishing with Tchoum for two hours. Tides, bait, the moon. He said three words, one of which was “Right.” At the end, he shook my hand. I think it was the best conversation of my life. As for him, I think he's still tired from it.
textes.Un soir, j'ai parlé du dragon de la gran: One evening, I mentioned the dragon of the big pond. One sentence, just one. Gland asked me forty-seven questions. How many teeth? Does it eat hazelnuts? Does it have a mummy? Where does it sleep in winter? After the forty-seventh, I had to make up a dragon story that answered the questions. He asked ten more.
textes.Un soir, j'ai plié le filet du père Vass: One evening, I folded old Vasseur's net, nice and square, with Marius's lead weights inside, and I left it outside the lighthouse door. I told myself: there, it's given back. The next morning, it was outside my own door. Folded exactly the same. Not a word. I didn't understand. I still don't.
textes.Un soir, j'ai pris une pirogue tout seul: One evening, I took a canoe all by myself to see where the lake goes. I paddled and paddled… and got stuck in the reeds. The herons were looking at me and laughing. Tlaco was barking at them. Mum arrived with a lamp. She scolded me, then hugged me, then scolded me again. I still don't know where the lake goes.
textes.Un soir, j'ai raté un croquis : sa guita: One evening, I botched a sketch: his guitar looked like a pear. A real pear, stalk and all. Toni found it so funny he pinned it up behind the bar. Django now plays every night under a pear. He hasn't forgiven me.
textes.Un soir, j'ai recompté les hamacs : tren: One evening, I recounted the hammocks: thirty-one. I searched the lower deck until midnight, questioned the guests, suspected Ewen. The next day, there were thirty-two again. My aunt said: “You must have miscounted.” I'd counted right. I know it was her. She knows I know. We don't talk about it.
textes.Un soir, j'ai regardé vers son banc pend: One evening, I glanced at his bench during a fast tune. The amin had his arms crossed, looking stern. But his feet… his feet were tapping under his djellaba. Not quite in time. I played him the same tune three times running. On the third, he pretended to shoo a gull away with his foot.
textes.Un soir, j'ai remarqué que les réverbère: One evening, I noticed that the street lamps on the square were lighting up exactly on the strong beats of my waltz. One, two, three… flame. One, two, three… flame. It was Nox, at the top of his ladder. The next day, I composed a waltz just for him, with just enough time between the bars to light a street lamp.
textes.Un soir, j'ai sorti mon chronomètre de C: One evening, I took out my Cliquetis stopwatch right in the middle of the party: “One boom every two seconds, Bourru! It's measured!” He looked at me. He played one boom. He waited. After four seconds, he said: “Hrmm.” I wrote it down: one hrmm every four seconds. That's a rhythm, at least.
textes.Un soir, j'ai trouvé l'Amirale seule à l: One evening, I found the Admiral alone in the harbour office, bent over my map, a candle in her hand. She was tracing the route of my crossing with her finger. She didn't hear me come in. She said very quietly: “He went everywhere, the idiot.” I slipped out without a sound. I think it was a compliment.
textes.Un soir, j'ai trouvé un nouveau nom sur: One evening, I found a new name on my boat, in chalk, over “Zahra”: “THE TERROR”. With a cross-eyed skull. I left it there a week. The whole fleet called me “Captain Terror”. Zohra's the one who rubbed it off, grumbling. But she kept the bit of chalk.
textes.Un soir, j'ai voulu danser avec elle, po: One evening, I wanted to dance with her, to see what it's like on the other side of the drum. I trod on her hooves. Twice. The second time was in rhythm, at least. She laughed, kindly. Since then, I stay behind my drum: it's better for everyone, especially her hooves.
textes.Un soir, j'ai voulu l'inviter à danser a: One evening, I wanted to ask her to dance with a mechanical flower that opens by itself. The spring suddenly let go, and the flower leapt into the fountain. I dived in to get it back. She held out her hand to help me out. We danced, me soaking wet, her laughing. At the end, the flower opened by itself in my pocket.
textes.Un soir, j'ai vu dans la baie un serpent: One evening, I saw a sea serpent in the bay with eyes like embers. Two red eyes, floating just above the water. Pyra claims it was her, in my boat, with fire in her hands. A boat, at midnight? She can't even row! … Fine. My boat was wet the next day. I prefer the serpent.
textes.Un soir, j'ai vu une silhouette sur le t: One evening, I saw a figure on the roof of the Bielle, with an open umbrella. One of my umbrellas! I climbed Gaston's ladder without thinking and grabbed him by the collar. I was still shaking on the way down. I confiscated the umbrella and told him about Achille's seventeen bumps, one by one. At the fifteenth, he asked if he could see them.
textes.Un soir, j'ai écrit : « Rien à signaler,: One evening I wrote: “Nothing to report, except one very large sunfish.” Abyssos turned up at the Gate at midnight, out of breath, with three blank scrolls. The sunfish had gone. He made me describe it for two hours. Since then I only write “Nothing to report”. It's more restful for everyone.
textes.Un soir, j'avais dessiné la cité telle q: One evening, I had drawn the city as I imagine it: a dome, towers, and in the middle the great crystal. I slipped it under my pillow, like a child. The next day, Pauline made my bed. The day after, on the café terrace, the mayor asked me if my crystal was “pretty in real life”. I thought I would die.
textes.Un soir, j'avais le mal du pays. Je n'ai: One evening, I was homesick. I didn't say anything, but Mama saw it. She put a buckwheat galette in front of me, like in Brittany, a bit burnt around the edges. She'd made it herself, in secret, with flour she'd had sent from Carène. It was a flop. It was the best galette of my life.
textes.Un soir, j'étais derrière les filets, à: One evening, I was behind the nets, tidying up. Driss was talking to the Mabrouka, as always. He told her: “This morning, Khadija wore the blue scarf. She was beautiful.” I didn't move. I'll never tell him I know, {surnom}. Never. Otherwise he'll stop. And since then, I wear the blue scarf more often.
One evening, I had a cold. Stuffed nose. Pépin drummed alone. Lilas danced. Badly. Couldn't find the step. Tripped twice. Next day, I came back. She danced like the moon. Hrmm. Pépin says it's a coincidence. Hrmm.
textes.Un soir, je l'ai entendu raconter toute: One evening, I heard him tell the Mabrouka about his whole day. The wind, the gulls, the sardines, a dolphin, Hassan's over-sweet tea. Everything! In detail! When I ask him about his day, he says “Hm”. I nearly came out from behind the nets to give him a piece of my mind. I stayed put. I listened to every word.
textes.Un soir, je l'ai obligé à jouer avec mes: One evening, I made him play with my own dice, carved from a rib of the whale on Bone Beach. He lost three gold coins in a row. He stared at the dice for a long time, and he said: “They're cursed.” I told him they were honest. He looked even more worried.
textes.Un soir, je l'ai surprise derrière la be: One evening, I caught her behind the sheepfold, deep in conversation with Croâ. She was saying: “No, not tonight.” He said: “Croak.” She answered: “I know, but no.” At midnight, the king sent for cheese. She'd refused in advance! I heard it, I'm telling you!
textes.Un soir, je l'ai trouvée cachée derrière: One evening I found her hiding behind my workbench. She'd heard me saying good night to the sculptures. I expected the whole city to laugh at me. The next day, there was a little piece of seaweed laid on every sculpture, like a blanket. I left them there.
textes.Un soir, je l'ai trouvée endormie sur le: One evening, I found her asleep on the treatise on light, her glasses askew. I didn't want to wake her. I brought a blanket from the storeroom, gently, by telekinesis, and slipped a ribbon into her page. She never asked where the blanket came from. She folded it and put it back in its place. In its exact place.
textes.Un soir, je l'ai vue devant ma porte, la: One evening, I saw her at my door, her hand on the handle. She stood there a long time, looking at my lamp. Then she said out loud, to herself: “What if it's him?” And off she stalked. I never found out who she meant. Well. I have a little idea.
textes.Un soir, je lisais tout haut l'histoire: One evening, I was reading the history of the surface out loud to the shelves, as usual: nobody else listens to me. At the end, someone sneezed behind the wheat scroll. It was Ondine, who'd been asleep there since the afternoon. She said: “Again.” Nobody had ever said “again” to me.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai demandé comment on fa: One evening, I asked her how you let someone know you like them, without saying it. She answered: “Like goats do. You climb all over them.” I tried a stone instead. It didn't work: he threw it in the fire. Hilda laughed all the way to the goat pen.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai demandé de m'aider à: One evening, I asked him to help me count my winnings. He heard “help me pound your chin in”. The table flew, the dice too, and the coins rolled all over the room. Sylvain gathered them up with his little rake, and kept the ones that had rolled to his side. Belle-Humeur apologised. At the top of his voice, but he apologised.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai demandé de me montrer: One evening, I asked him to show me his scrap of parchment. He replied, very politely: “Three wins, sir.” I played. I lost the first round. I stood up, bowed to him, and told him his father would have answered the same. He lowered his eyes. It's the only time I've seen him moved. He soon went back to being a croupier.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai fait mon rapport : «: One evening I gave him my report: “Forest quiet.” He said: “Too quiet?” I said: “No, just quiet.” He went to check for himself. He came back at dawn, covered in dew, and said: “Quiet.” Then he checked my arrows. All of them. Again.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai montré mon croquis de: One evening, I showed him my sketch of the village coast, drawn from three passengers' accounts. He put his big finger on the beach and slid it north: “Higher. And the hermit's hut, there.” Then he tapped a rock: “That one, I hit once.” I corrected it. I drew the rock bigger.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai montré où dort le cha: One evening, I showed him where the ginger cat sleeps. We climbed up the crates, near the Fondouk, really quietly. The cat was sleeping curled up, on… on a thing. I'm not saying what. Tibo opened his mouth, then shut it again. He swore not to tell. Not even his captain. He kept his word. He's a real pal.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai échangé une perche co: One evening, I traded her a perch for a jar of beer. The perch wasn't quite dead. It leapt out of the basket, straight into the bread dough. Mérit screamed, the perch swam in the dough, and I laughed until I fell off the bench. The next day, Mérit was selling “perch bread”. It sold out in an hour.
textes.Un soir, je me suis cachée derrière son: One evening I hid behind his workbench. I heard him say good night to all his sculptures, one by one, even the fish-urchin. His voice was all soft, not grumpy at all. The next day I put a little piece of seaweed on each one, like a blanket. He didn't say anything. He left them there.
textes.Un soir, je me suis endormi au milieu d': One evening, I fell asleep in the middle of a game, my hand raised above the board. I woke up an hour later. Cendrin hadn't moved: he was waiting. I set down my piece as if nothing had happened and said: “Your move.” He smiled. I won. He never told me he'd seen me sleeping.
textes.Un soir, je me suis endormie sur le trai: One evening, I fell asleep on the treatise on light. I woke up under a blanket that hadn't been there before, with a ribbon marking my page. The library was empty. I folded the blanket and put it back where it belonged, in the storeroom, third shelf. I know where it came from. We've never talked about it.
textes.Un soir, je me suis endormie sur mon trô: One evening, I fell asleep on my throne. Noisette took the chance to plant a seed in my crown, “just to see”. By morning, a little shoot was standing between two of its flowers. The fairies didn't dare tell me. I kept it: it has two leaves now. Noisette comes to water it in secret. Very badly in secret.
textes.Un soir, je revenais des falaises en bar: One evening, I was coming back from the cliffs by boat, with two flames in my hands to keep warm. I'd borrowed Mathurin's boat. The next day, he was telling the whole inn he'd seen a sea serpent with ember eyes in the bay. I told him it was me. He doesn't believe me. He prefers the serpent.
textes.Un soir, je suis allé frapper à la Tour: One evening, I went and knocked at the Tower to find out if the Crystal was asleep. She took me to the bench in the courtyard to watch it with me. I woke up in my bed. She told me I'd won, because at least I'd managed to fall asleep. The Crystal doesn't know how. Poor thing.
textes.Un soir, je suis allé la trouver, seul,: One evening, I went to find her, alone, at the end of the quay. I asked her how she sets Bertha's elevation. She explained everything: the screw, the wooden wedge, the eye. In detail. Without mocking. I wrote it all down in my journal. If you repeat it, {surnom}, I'll say you're lying.
textes.Un soir, je suis monté à la cime avec ma: One evening, I went up to the treetop with my flute, to help him count: “Music keeps the rhythm!” He was at four thousand two hundred and twelve. I played the squirrel note. He said “thirteen?”, then “twelve?”, then he shut his notebook. Since then, it's been twelve or thirteen. He's never asked me back. But he hasn't chased me off either.
textes.Un soir, la bonde d'une barrique de cidr: One evening, the bung of a cider barrel got stuck, and Tonneau was looking at me with puppy-dog eyes. I threw a knife from the back of the room: the bung popped out, straight into his glass. Tonneau clapped as if I'd saved the world, and fell off his stool. Mama Grog made me pay for the stool.

One evening, the bung of a cider cask was stuck. I tried with my fingers, with a spoon, with my teeth. Nothing. Scarlett threw a knife from the back of the room: pop! The bung flew out, straight into my glass. I clapped so hard I fell off my stool. It was the most beautiful thing I've ever seen. Hic!
textes.Un soir, la cave sentait la fumée. Léonc: One evening, the cellar smelled of smoke. Léonce had tested a rocket “just a teeny bit” between two soap barrels. I had to explain to Dad. I said: “It's a controlled combustion experiment.” Dad asked: “Controlled by whom?” I didn't have an answer. It's the first time in my life.
textes.Un soir, la reine a planté une fleur en: One evening, the queen secretly planted a flower, to see whether I'd notice. I found it before dawn. I went to tell her: “Four thousand three hundred and two, Your Majesty. Yesterday it was four thousand three hundred and one.” She laughed. I named the flower Oriane. It gets the first drop every morning.
textes.Un soir, la reine s'est endormie sur son: One evening, the queen fell asleep on her throne. I planted a seed in her crown, just to see. By morning, there was a little shoot between two of its flowers! Nobody dared tell her. She kept it. It has two leaves now. I'm the one who waters it, in secret.
textes.Un soir, le Capitaine a perdu le fil de: One evening, the Captain lost the thread of his storm, right at the big wave. I whispered from behind my counter: “As tall as the lighthouse.” He picked it up again in a booming voice: “As tall as the volcano!” Since then, I prompt him every evening. And every evening, he goes bigger than what I prompt.
textes.Un soir, le Gouverneur est venu à ma tab: One evening, the Governor came to my table “to inspect games of chance, in the name of the city”. He didn't have a coin. He bet himself for a week. He lost. He came aboard the Cod with his gold tricorn, polished my boots, ate all my honey, and gave three speeches a day. After three days, I gave him back to the city.
textes.Un soir, le Lord m'a demandé un verre d': One evening, the Lord asked me for a glass of water. A glass of water! And he put a gold coin on the counter, with the profile of a great-grandfather with a big nose. I said: “Milord, that's worth a hundred glasses of water.” He said: “Keep the rest.” So I opened a tab just for him. I owe him ninety-nine glasses of water. I don't know how you settle that.
textes.Un soir, le capitaine m'a envoyé sur le: One evening, the captain sent me up on the Fondouk roof to fetch the ginger cat. I didn't bring back the cat. But on a washing line, there was a nightcap. I took it so I wouldn't come back empty-handed. The captain looked at it for a long time. He said: “That's not a cat.” I said: “No, captain. But it's warm.”
textes.Un soir, le plancher de ma cuisine s'est: One evening, my kitchen floor lifted up and a head popped out, right under my table. I grabbed whatever was handy: a bellows. Bonk. It was Grimli. I patched him up and made him soup. A year later, we were married. We kept the hole. It's the cellar trapdoor.
textes.Un soir, on a fait le calcul sur une nap: One evening, we did the sums on a paper tablecloth at the Perroquet. Thirty years of rounds, the hill, the stairs, the dogs… with the mailbag. Result: Marcel has walked round the archipelago three times. Me, with my forty marathons, twice. He kept the tablecloth. He says he's going to frame it.
textes.Un soir, on s'est regardés, lui et moi,: One evening, we stared at each other, him and me, from one end of the Crâne Fendu to the other. Without blinking. An hour. Two hours. The lanterns went out one by one. Mama Grog threw us both out with her rolling pin. Outside, we stared a bit longer. Then he nodded at me. I did the same. A draw. I HATE DRAWS.
textes.Un soir, penchés sur ses cartes, il m'a: One evening, bent over his charts, he said to me: “I can't swim.” I said: “I get seasick.” We looked at each other. I burst out laughing: “The two greatest explorers in the archipelago… who've never left!” He laughed too. Then he pencilled a cross to the south-west of the village. We believe in it.
textes.Un soir, pendant qu'il lisait ses runes: One evening, while he was reading his runes by the fire, I tasted his famous moon water. Yuck! Cold pebbles and dust. He saw me. He said nothing. He just jotted something in his journal. Ever since, I've been wondering what he wrote. It's eating at me. It's eating at me a lot.
textes.Un soir, pendant un gros morceau de Mist: One night, during a big Mistral track, my test hut collapsed. The next day, Clou turned up with a bag of nails, from Octave. Eleven nails. The bag said twenty. I rebuilt it with them. It still leans, but it holds: that's where Zoé sleeps. I've never dared ask where the other nine went.
textes.Un soir, pour la taquiner, j'ai planté u: One evening, to tease her, I secretly planted one extra flower in the clearing. The next day, before the sun was even up, Perlée came to find me: “Four thousand three hundred and two, Your Majesty. Yesterday it was four thousand three hundred and one.” She named the flower “Oriane”. She still gives it the first drop.
textes.Un soir, pour voir, je lui ai servi un v: One evening, just to see, I served him a glass of water. Well water, in a rum glass. He downed it in one, pulled a face, and said: “Strong, but good!” I laughed so hard two pirates fell off their stools. I never told him. He thinks he's getting used to it.
textes.Un soir, près du feu de la grève, il m'a: One evening, by the fire on the shore, he told me about his first night as a cabin boy: he was so scared he cried in his hammock. And the next day, nobody made fun of him. I asked him if it was true. He said: “That one, yes.” After that, I wasn't ashamed any more of being scared during my first storm.
textes.Un soir, près du feu, il m'a demandé si: One evening, by the fire, he asked me if I'd ever been scared. I told him about my first night as a cabin boy, crying like a fountain in my hammock. He looked at me, very serious, and asked if it was true. I said: “That one, yes.” He took my hand. He didn't let go of it for the whole of the next story.
textes.Un soir, pêcheurs et pirates allaient se: One evening, fishermen and pirates were about to fight over a place at the counter. Mama Lou grabbed me by the collar, stood me on a table and said: “Sing.” I sang the song of the boats. By the second verse, the fists had opened. By the third, everyone was singing. Even the pirates. Out of tune, but singing.

One evening, fishermen and pirates were about to come to blows on the quay over a net. Hassan arrived with his teapot, me with my rum. He served on the left, I served on the right. An hour later, everyone was singing. He says it was his tea. Ha! I saw the pirates pour rum into his tea. So it was my rum.

One evening, fishermen and pirates were about to fight on the quay, over a net. Mama Lou came out with her rum, me with my tea. She served on one side, I served on the other. An hour later, everyone was singing. She says it was the rum. I say it was the tea. Both sides drank both. That proves nothing.
textes.Un soir, sur cette pierre, Sidi Belaïd r: One evening, on this very stone, Sidi Belaïd was telling the tale of the sultan, the sardine and the djinn. Just as the djinn came out of the sardine, he stopped. He leaned forward gently, as if to listen to the earth, and he didn't straighten up again. The circle waited. I was twenty-five. I stood up, and I finished the story. For sixty years, I haven't left this stone.
textes.Un soir, sur l'ardoise du Perroquet, il: One evening, on the Perroquet's slate, it said: “Dish of the day: for Lucas, on the house.” Toni said it was a mistake. Lola wiped it off really fast with her sleeve. But I'd read it. I ate the dish of the day. I paid anyway. I don't know why. I was all flustered.
textes.Un soir, sur la Grand-Place, Zigomar a v: One evening, on the Great Square, Zigomar tried to ask me to dance with a mechanical flower that opens by itself. The spring suddenly let go: the flower leapt off and landed in the fountain. He dived in to get it back. I helped him out. We danced, soaking wet.
textes.Un soir, sur la plage, elle m'a pris l'a: One evening, on the beach, she took the camera out of my hands and put it away in her bag. “Look.” The sun went down. My hands kept reaching for the shutter button on their own. Ten minutes of looking, doing nothing. She asked: “Well?” I said: “A bit overexposed.” She pinched my arm.
textes.Un soir, sur le banc, Basile m'a dit : «: One evening, on the bench, Basile said to me: “A bubble is nothing wrapped in something pretty. Your box of nothing is nothing wrapped in wood.” He meant it kindly, I think. I went home. I didn't come back to the bench for a week. He waited for me every evening with two biscuits. He ate one and kept the other.
textes.Un soir, sur le banc, j'ai dit à Philibe: One evening, on the bench, I said to Philibert: “A bubble is nothing wrapped in pretty. Your box of nothing is nothing wrapped in wood.” I thought it was funny. He raised his hat, very politely, and didn't speak to me for a week. Seven evenings sitting next to me, without a word. The longest week of my life.
textes.Un soir, sur le ponton, j'ai failli tout: One evening, on the pontoon, I nearly told Lucie everything, about the sail. I opened my mouth. She looked at me and said: “Not now. When you're sure.” Then she dived in. She always knows when someone's carrying a secret. She never asks which one.
textes.Un soir, sur le quai, j'ai posé la carte: One evening, on the quay, I put the map down on a barrel. One second! Just long enough to light my pipe. A ginger cat leapt up, took the map in its mouth, and hop: a crate, another crate, a roof. And me down below, howling. Why didn't I climb up? … A captain doesn't climb onto roofs. That's why. Don't look at me like that, {surnom}.
textes.Un soir, une de mes lanternes a dérivé j: One evening, one of my lanterns drifted right up to her feet while she was dancing. She picked it up, raised it towards the crystal, and danced with it until the tide turned. I was hiding behind a column. I forgot to breathe. For a glassblower, that's serious.
