textes.Victor. Mon partenaire de cartes. Il gag: Victor. My card partner. He wins all the time. He says it's talent. It's because I'm looking somewhere else.
textes.Vide. Gâchette près d'un objet pour le r: Empty. Trigger near an item to pick it up.
textes.Vieille-Dent dort au fond du marais, sou: Vieille-Dent sleeps at the bottom of the marsh, under the dead mangroves. Whoever kills him will have my gratitude. My gratitude is rare.
textes.Vieille-Dent ne bougera plus. Le marais: Vieille-Dent will never move again. The marsh holds its breath… Crochet will be pleased.
Vieille-Dent will eat no one ever again.
textes.Vieille-Dent, le crocodile géant du Mara: Vieille-Dent, the giant crocodile of the Drowned Marsh, took Crochet's hand years ago. Crochet wants someone to settle the score.
textes.Vieille-Dent… tu veux qu'on t'en débarra: Vieille-Dent… want us to get rid of him for you?
textes.Viens plonger. Tu me la raconteras en bu: Come diving. You can tell me in bubbles.
textes.Viens pêcher ce soir. Je te fais griller: Come fishing tonight. I'll grill you the other half.
textes.Viens, je te retourne vers la fenêtre !: Come, I'll turn you toward the window!
textes.Viens, {surnom}, mais tu ne dis rien. Au: Come, {surnom}, but don't say a word. At the back of my shed, under a tarp, there's a sailboat. I've been building it for six years, plank by plank, in the evenings, to sail round the archipelago. It's almost finished. Almost. Thing is, I've never gone past the harbour wall on my own. I'm scared to finish it, really. Because after that, I'll have to leave.
textes.Vieux Flint se souvient… Quand Vieux Fli: Old Flint remember… When Old Flint was little square, Old Flint's grandfather tell: one day come a SMOOTH thing, from other side of big water. It chase away big roar of north. And Clan will dance. Hmm. Old Flint think it you.
textes.Vieux. Mais content. Tant qu'il y a du r: Old. But happy. As long as there's rum and someone to listen, Silas is happy.
textes.Vigilant. Avec un galion pirate au quai,: Vigilant. With a pirate galleon at the quay, you sleep with one eye open.
textes.Vigilant. Toujours vigilant. Même quand: Vigilant. Always vigilant. Even when nothing is happening. Especially when nothing is happening.
textes.Vingt ? Tu vends vraiment autant de vent: Twenty? Do you really sell that much wind?
textes.Vingt ans de piraterie. On m'appelait Lo: Twenty years of piracy. They called me Lou the Terrible. I retired to Tazira, because nobody knew me here. Now everybody knows me. So much for that.
textes.Vingt ans que je dis à Berthe qu'elle sa: Twenty years I've been telling Berthe she uses too much salt. Twenty years she hasn't listened. Her heart is on her sleeve and her hand is on the salt cellar. We argue every day. I couldn't do without it.
textes.Vingt ans que je tiens ce port. Je conna: Twenty years I've run this harbour. I know every hull, every knot, every lie about the size of a fish.
textes.Vingt ans, cette graine dorée a dormi da: For twenty years, that golden seed slept in my treasure box, between a shark's tooth and a mother-of-pearl button. On sad evenings, I held it in the hollow of my hand: it was warm, like a little sun. I didn't know I was keeping it for someone.
textes.Vingt-deux ans de service. Trois arresta: Twenty-two years of service. Three arrests: a chicken thief, a chicken thief, and the same chicken thief.
textes.Vingt-deux ans, et toujours pas d'excuse: Twenty-two years, and still no apology.
Twenty-thousand and a broken one. Noted.
textes.Violette ? Ortie, qu'est-ce que tu as mi: Purple? Ortie, what did you put in it?
textes.Violette, la jeune mage de la Guilde, ne: Violette, the Guild's young mage, can only cast lightning bolts, and they often hit her instead. According to an old book, three storm crystals, which grow at the top of the Fangs, would channel her lightning "forwards".
textes.Violette, si tu pouvais éviter de me fou: Violette, if you could avoid zapping me today, I'd appreciate it.
textes.Violette, vos cheveux… ils se dressent t: Violette, your hair… it's standing up all by itself.
Aim well away from me too.
textes.Visez avec la main droite, gâchette pour: Aim with your right hand, trigger to click, stick to scroll
textes.Visez un objet et appuyez sur la gâchett: Aim at an item and press the trigger, then “Use” or “Drop”
textes.Vite et bien, c'est mon métier !: Fast and well, that's my job!
textes.Vite, vite ! Derrière le canapé ! … Bon,: Quick, quick! Behind the sofa! … Well, he may not come before tonight. Would you like a slice of cake in the meantime?
textes.Voici Germaine et l'ampli ! Et j'ai auss: Here are Germaine and the amp! And I've got the drumsticks too.
textes.Voici cinq navets dorés, Père Gaubert. D: Here are five golden turnips, Father Gaubert. Gently, I promise.
textes.Voici cinq objets des îles d'en bas, Orb: Here are five objects from the islands below, Orbe!
textes.Voici la bannière du chef gobelin, Sire: Here is the goblin chief's banner, Sir Tancrède.
Here is the seed of Yggdrasil, Your Majesty.
textes.Voici la puce holographique et la carte: Here are the hologram chip and the star chart!
Here is the Royal jelly heart, Master.
Here are the logs and the stones.
textes.Voici les cinq champignons féeriques, Mè: Here are the five fairy mushrooms, Mother Morel.
textes.Voici les matériaux pour le Glisseur, Io: Here are the materials for the Glider, Ionie.
Here are the plans for the Lisse-Center, Mamie.
Here are the three pieces of the map.
Here are the three moon shards.
textes.Voici les trois éclats du Cœur, et trois: Here are the Heart's three shards, and three astral crystals.
textes.Voici mes dix pièces. Je pose la main su: Here are my ten coins. Do I put my hand on the ball?
Here are your three sulfur crystals.
Here are three blocks of iron ore.
Here are three logs of twisted wood.
Here are three hundred coins. I'll buy it.
Here are three mushrooms from the Twisted Wood.
Here are three storm crystals, Violette.
Here are three flakes of eternal frost.
textes.Voici trois fragments de météorite, Zéni: Here are three meteorite fragments, Zenith.
textes.Voici trois lots de pièces de vélo, Rust: Here are three lots of bike parts, Rustine!
textes.Voici trois paniers de légumes, Lentille: Here are three baskets of vegetables, Lentille!
Here are three feathers of the wind.
Here are three tufts of fever grass.
textes.Voici un cristal de soufre : c'est là qu: Here is a sulfur crystal: this is where fire is born.
Here are your five moon mushrooms.
Here are your five ember flowers.
Here are your four flown-away books.
textes.Voici vos trois graines lumineuses, Phot: Here are your three glowing seeds, Photon.
Here are your three pages, Madame Olga.
textes.Voici votre chapeau à plume, Monsieur le: Here is your feathered hat, Baron.
Here is your sun rosary, sister. The Duchess gave it back.
textes.Voilà ! Héroïque ! Bon, je t'ai fait un: There! Heroic! Well, I made you a bit taller. And with a cape. You didn't have a cape? Now you do.
textes.Voilà ! Le quinzième toit sera le bon. T: There! The fifteenth roof will be the right one. Here, these glasses: kaleidoscopes. The whole world turns into a rose window. It's useless, it's marvellous, and it doesn't explode. Well, I think.
textes.Voilà ! Voilà la bonne réponse ! C'est t: There! That's the right answer! It's always both, youngster, always. Gwenola! A mug for this sailor! It's on me… well, it's on him.
textes.Voilà la marchandise. Tout est forgé ici: Here's the merchandise. Everything's forged here, in the tree. You have {pieces} coins: choose wisely.
textes.Voilà qui me plaît. Cinq minutes d'avanc: Now that I like. Five minutes early is politeness. Ten is worry. I won't ask which are yours.
textes.Voilà un patient raisonnable ! Ça devien: Now there's a sensible patient! That's getting rare. You know my door, the front one. The back one is for people who don't want to be seen coming in.
textes.Voilà, Grand-père ! … C'est un nœud de l: There you go, Grandpa! … It's a shoelace knot.
There. That's exactly what I'm talking about.
textes.Voilà. C'est presque ça. Rentre chez toi: There. That's nearly it. Go home.
textes.Voir Caelan et Ilyria se marier. J'ai pa: To see Caelan and Ilyria married. I bet on after the millennium, but I'd be delighted to lose. I'm counting the springs, and I have a few left.
textes.Voir Clara danser sur une vraie scène, s: To see Clara dance on a real stage, on the mainland, with a red curtain and well-dressed people. I'll be in the front row, smelling of fish, and I won't care one bit.
To see Clara dance on a real stage, on the mainland. Me in the front row, in flip-flops, cheering louder than everyone. Even louder than Mum.
textes.Voir Croc ouvrir ce coffre. Le voir comp: To see Croc open that chest. To see him finally understand what his grandfather left here. That day, I'll stand him a rum. The good one, from the back.
textes.Voir Vénus se lever exactement la nuit q: To see Venus rise exactly on the night my tables predict. Not a night before, not a night after. Exactly. Just once, and I'll sleep in peace.
textes.Voir de mes yeux les abeilles d'en haut,: To see with my own eyes the bees up top, the ones that forage the Mother Tree. Thalion offered to carry me up. I'd rather eat a beehive. Well… I'd rather think about it.
textes.Voir de mes yeux, une seule fois, une cô: To see with my own eyes, just once, a coastline I've drawn. To check I put the bay in the right place. And to cry a little, if I did.
textes.Voir encore une fois le Feu Nouveau. Le: To see the New Fire one more time. The next one will be in seven years. I'll be seventy-two. I fully intend to carry a torch. Walking, this time.
textes.Voir entrer un grand navire dans la baie: To see a great ship sail into the bay at sunrise. A real one, three masts, all sails set. I'll count it. It'll be the finest number in my journal.
textes.Voir germer la graine d'Yggdrasil, la to: To see the Yggdrasil seed sprout, the very first shoot, with its two little leaves! And then to find my very own tree, my hazelnut's tree. I'd tell it: “Hello, it's me. Did you lose me?”
textes.Voir germer un nouvel Yggdrasil, et l'en: To see a new Yggdrasil sprout, and hear it whisper for the first time. And then, one evening, to go back down into the roots, sit beside Églantine, and talk about everything except the brambles.
textes.Voir l'automate joueur d'échecs d'Ambroi: See Ambroise Échec's chess-playing automaton (Fair stand, to the south)
textes.Voir l'avenir pour de vrai, une deuxième: To see the future for real, a second time. Just once. To know whether the first time wasn't a fluke, or one of Paulo's bouillabaisses with too much spice. A fortune-teller who doubts, traveller, is a lighthouse that blinks.
textes.Voir l'avenir, c'est facile. Le dire gen: Seeing the future is easy. Saying it kindly is an art. You don't want to know what we saw in Pyra's tea. Neither does she, for that matter.
textes.Voir la Cascade Arrabbiata tomber dans l: See the Arrabbiata Falls pour into the sea
textes.Voir la Cascade d'Encre tomber de la fal: See the Ink Waterfall tumble from the cliff
textes.Voir la baleine. Une fois. Je ne quitter: To see the whale. Once. I won't leave my post, mind you! But if it could pass right over the Gate, that would be very kind of it.
textes.Voir la mer de l'autre côté du monde. Mo: To see the sea on the other side of the world. My uncle says there's nothing out there. My uncle has never left his island.
textes.Voir la mer. Une fois. De loin d'abord,: See the sea. Once. From afar first, from the treetop, in Bourru's basket. With a skewer, for courage.
textes.Voir le Grand Cristal de mes propres yeu: To see the Great Crystal with my own eyes. Even through a porthole, even from afar, even for a second. I don't need to touch it. Just to know I didn't make it up.
textes.Voir le Roi des mares avant papy ! Et lu: See the Pond King before Grandpa! And ask him to bring Papa back. Or at least a letter. Grandpa says fish can go anywhere under the ground. So the King can go all the way to the sea, right?
textes.Voir le Sans-Pitié glisser de la grève j: To see the Merciless slide from the shore into the water, one spring-tide morning, with the whole port pushing and singing. And to hear the hull creak just right. The creak of a happy ship.
textes.Voir le volcan cracher sa sauce: See the volcano spit out its sauce
textes.Voir les gonds de la Porte aux Quatre Sc: To see the hinges of the Gate of the Four Seals. To touch that metal nobody knows, to hear it sing. And forge one blade from it, just one. Or a crêpe pan for Gwenola. We'll see which it prefers.
textes.Voir les pierres peintes du désert : les: To see the painted stones of the desert: the hunters, the animals, and the great round door. To paint them before the sand covers them. Painting a painting, can you imagine? Someone, a thousand years ago, had the same urge as me.
textes.Voir les trois soleils réunis sur l'aute: To see the three suns united on the altar of the highlands, as the ancients used to say. I don't know who will do it. But I'd like to be there, with my sistrum, and sing.
textes.Voir ma voile se gonfler. La mienne. Sor: To see my sail fill. Mine. Sail out of the bay, round the point, and see Carène as nothing more than a little brown smudge on the coast. And then come back. I think I'll come back. I think.
textes.Voir nager les carpes de la Place des Ho: Watch the carp swim in the Hologram Square
textes.Voir neiger. Une fois. Une vraie neige,: To see it snow. Once. Real snow, falling from the sky and not from a globe I shake. Fifteen years I've been selling snow, and I don't even know if it's cold. I imagine it cold. Like Bruno's ice creams.
textes.Voir revenir les vraies lumières du Bois: To see the Wood's true lights come back, the ones that left the night I was born. They say they're coming back. If it's true, I'd like to see them dance above my lanterns. All together.
textes.Voir s'ouvrir une fleur de lune, une seu: To see a moonflower open, just one, one night, on my hill. They say it only opens by moonlight and smells of sugar and rain. I'd spend the whole night watching it, sitting in the grass.
textes.Voir un jour le Serpent à Plumes voler a: To see the Feathered Serpent fly over Yaxché one day, just once, with all its green feathers. I wouldn't ask for anything. I'd watch.
textes.Voir un jour un apprenti réussir un sort: To see an apprentice one day pull off a spell I never managed to cast. My money's on Oscar: with all his getting everything wrong in such odd ways, he's bound to invent something eventually.
textes.Voir une fois, une seule, quelque chose: To see, once, just once, something real to report. Climb up to Mère-Lune's and tell her: “Reported.” She'd be pleased.
textes.Voir une vraie perle de lumière. Bleue,: To see a real pearl of light. Blue, shining all by itself, with no paint and no lies. I'd have it set in a mount forged by Hector, he has the finest hand on the island. And I'd never sell it. Not even for its weight in gold. Especially not for its weight in gold.
textes.Voler ! Zéphyrine dirait que t'as pas be: Flying! Zéphyrine would say you don't need a potion. I say it's more fun with one. I'll give it a go. It might make your socks float.
textes.Voler ? Mais c'est le plus facile ! Il s: Fly? But that's the easiest thing! All you need is wings. Ah. You haven't got any. Right, I'll note it in my book: spell number three hundred and five.
textes.Voler ? Presque ! Léviter. C'est mieux :: Fly? Almost! Levitate. It's better: you don't bump into seagulls. To learn, you must first feel the wind in your hand. The wind loses feathers when it turns too fast: bring me three. They land where it blows the hardest: on the western hill, at the edge of the northern cliffs, and on the eastern cliff, above the sea.
textes.Voler, une fois, au-dessus du cratère, e: To fly, once, over the crater, and see the mountain from above, the way my crows see it. Croâ says he'll carry me. Croâ says a lot of things.
textes.Volontiers. Avec mes dés à moi, monsieur: Gladly. With my own dice, Monsieur Malaterre.
textes.Volontiers. Elle ne guérit rien, mais el: Gladly. It doesn't cure anything, but it smells so nice.
textes.Volé ? Le mot est fort. Disons que tout: Stolen? That's a strong word. Let's say everything I sell has… travelled a lot. And its former owners aren't looking for it any more. They have other worries. Like swimming.
textes.Vos balayeurs m'ont encore écrit !: Your sweepers have written to me again!
textes.Vos bougainvilliers, Rose ! Encore plus: Your bougainvillea, Rose! Even lovelier than yesterday.
textes.Vos livres envolés… je peux aider ?: Your runaway books… can I help?
textes.Vos navets… ils bougent, Père Gaubert ?: Your turnips… are they moving, Père Gaubert?
textes.Vos vingt boîtes du mois, madame Bricole: Your twenty boxes for the month, Madame Bricolette.
Your stars only come out at night.
Your stars have moved since yesterday.
textes.Votre atelier n'a plus de toit ?: Your workshop has lost its roof?
textes.Votre automate a bien dormi, Ambroise ?: Did your automaton sleep well, Ambroise?
textes.Votre automate saura partager. Il est tr: Your automaton will learn to share. It's very intelligent.
textes.Votre baguette, bien croustillante, comm: Your baguette, nice and crusty, just how Raymond likes them. You're his favourite customer without knowing it.
textes.Votre bouture grandit, Léa. Elle a déjà: Your cutting is growing, Léa. It's already eaten its stake.
Your coffee, then. On the house.
textes.Votre caillou est devenu une clochette d: Your pebble has become a little silver bell!
Your map is coming along, captain.
textes.Votre chaussette, non. Le cristal, si !: Your sock, no. The crystal, yes!
textes.Votre coup, Ambroise. Il vous reste huit: Your move, Ambroise. You have eight seconds left.
textes.Votre croissant est prêt, bien doré, com: Your croissant is ready, nice and golden, just how you like them. I put it aside before the Lord came by.
textes.Votre galette, Majesté ! Toute chaude !: Your cracker, Majesty! Nice and warm!
textes.Votre grand-père a reçu mon pot ?: Did your grandfather get my jar?
textes.Votre machine à remonter le temps… J'y r: Your time machine… I think about it sometimes. In the evening, on the bench.
textes.Votre monnaie. Comptez-la, je sais que v: Your change. Count it, I know you like that. … Is it right? Of course it is.
textes.Votre monnaie. Je sais, vous faites conf: Your change. I know, you trust. Count it anyway. To please me.
textes.Votre petite explosion vous attend toujo: Your little explosion is still waiting for you, nice and warm. I've stored it far from Gaston's coffee.
textes.Votre phare a un problème ?: Is something wrong with your lighthouse?
textes.Votre piano tousse toujours, Prudence ?: Is your piano still coughing, Prudence?
textes.Votre pion a bougé tout seul, Moulay Bra: Your piece moved all by itself, Moulay Brahim.
textes.Votre secret est toujours à l'abri ? Mon: Is your secret still safe? My pencil is put away. But it's twitching, I warn you.
textes.Votre serré, {surnom}. Je vous ai vu arr: Your short black, {surnom}. I saw you coming from a mile off: it was already in the cup.
Your tea, Moulay Brahim. And your piece.
textes.Votre tisane, Sauge. Froide, s'il vous p: Your herbal tea, Sauge. Cold, please.
Wanting to is already halfway there. The other half is a mushroom. Ask me when your heart is ready.
textes.Vous ! Ne croyez pas que je ne sais pas: You! Don't think I don't know what you did.
You! Yes, you. Nothing. Have a nice day.
textes.Vous ! Vous êtes dans la Gazette de ce m: You! You're in this morning's Gazette. Page four. “A mysterious visitor”.
textes.Vous ! Vous êtes un ange. Hugo et moi, n: You! You're an angel. Hugo and I owe you everything.
textes.Vous allez finir par ne rien posséder du: You'll end up owning nothing at all.
textes.Vous allez me rembourser, j'espère !: You're going to pay me back, I hope!
textes.Vous allez noter quelque chose. Voilà. E: You're going to write something down. There. It's come true.
textes.Vous avez aidé {qn} ! {Il} me l'a racont: You helped {qn}! {Il} told me all about it. I won't forget it, {surnom}.
textes.Vous avez assez bu pour aujourd'hui. Un: You've had enough to drink for today. A glass of water, and off to bed!
textes.Vous avez combien de chats ?: How many cats do you have?
textes.Vous avez commencé un livre ? Même un pe: Have you started a book? Even a little one? I've put one aside for you. With pictures, and a sturdy cover.
You said that two winters ago.
textes.Vous avez encore des pièces en trop dans: Have you still got leftover pieces in your pockets? Bring them. I'll find where they go.
textes.Vous avez encore votre toit, professeur: Do you still have your roof, Professor?
textes.Vous avez eu l'occasion de lui parler, d: Have you had a chance to talk to them since?
textes.Vous avez fait la connaissance de {qn},: You've made the acquaintance of {qn}, I hear. What do you think?
textes.Vous avez frappé {qn} ? Ça ne se fait pa: You hit {qn}? That's just not done. Everyone's talking about it.
textes.Vous avez frappé {qn} ?! On m'a tout rac: You hit {qn}?! I've heard everything. You've got some nerve coming to talk to me.
textes.Vous avez frappé {qn}, à ce qu'on dit. J: You hit {qn}, so they say. I'm not saying it was deserved. I'm not saying it wasn't.
Word is you spoiled {qn}. Anyone who's kind to my folks is welcome at my place.
You look rushed off your feet.
textes.Vous avez offert des fleurs à votre ami,: Have you given flowers to your friend since? No? The lavender is waiting. It's patient, but not eternal.
textes.Vous avez offert {objet} à {qn} ? Tout l: You gave {objet} to {qn}? Everyone knows {il} can't stand that. I'm still laughing.
textes.Vous avez raison de ne pas juger trop vi: You're right not to judge too quickly.
textes.Vous avez toujours le marque-page que je: Do you still have the bookmark I gave you? Show me. … Good. I'm keeping an eye on you.
textes.Vous avez toujours votre souvenir ? Bien: Do you still have your keepsake? Good. I shan't buy it from you. I did think about it, I confess, but no.
textes.Vous avez tous la même tête…: You all have the same face…
textes.Vous avez une petite mine, vous. Vous av: You look a bit peaky. Did you sleep badly?
textes.Vous avez vu le jet, là-bas ?: Did you see the spout, over there?
textes.Vous avez vu le voleur de croissants ?: Did you see the croissant thief?
textes.Vous avez vu passer le voleur ?: Did you see the thief go by?
textes.Vous chantez tous les trois : « ♪ Tourne: You all three sing: “♪ Sunflower, sunflower, the moon watches you sleep… ♪”. It's a bit off-key, but very pretty.
textes.Vous chaussez les lunettes. Tout devient: You put on the glasses. Everything turns into coloured stars. You bump into a tree. You take them off.
You'd be looking under the throne, Majesty.
textes.Vous croyez ? Alors surtout, ne vérifiez: You think so? Then whatever you do, don't check. Keep it just like that, nice and warm, without looking. An idea you believe is new is almost as good as a new idea. Believe me.
You were dancing with me. I saw.
textes.Vous dites ça depuis cent ans. Je ne vou: You've been saying that for a hundred years. I still don't believe you.
textes.Vous dites ça maintenant. Attendez qu'el: You say that now. Wait until it finds your letterbox.
textes.Vous et votre Zéphyr… Voler avec un plan: You and your Zéphyr… Flying with a floor is cheating. But it's cheating I'd quite like to try.
textes.Vous et votre goût de l'aventure ! La fi: You and your taste for adventure! The blue vial made my kettle grow a moustache. Shall I keep it for you?
textes.Vous faites votre lit quand on vous rega: You make your bed when someone's watching? Well, I'm watching you. Just kidding. Or am I?
textes.Vous feriez ça ? Hugo a perdu son allian: You'd do that? Hugo lost his wedding ring playing in the waves, near the beach hut. It must be buried in the wet sand. You'd need a shovel… and a lot of luck.
textes.Vous jetez ? Bon. Alors rendez-moi un se: You throw things away? Fine. Then do me a favour: throw them off the top of the cliff. Crane side. I'll take care of the rest.
textes.Vous l'avez fait exprès ?: Did you do that on purpose?
textes.Vous l'avez fini, ce roman, Colette ?: Did you finish that novel, Colette?
textes.Vous l'avez toujours, votre caillou ? Ga: Do you still have your pebble? Take good care of it. It's good for nothing, and that's what makes it irreplaceable.
textes.Vous levez la coupe bien haut. On croit: You raise the cup high. You almost hear, far away, the whole Games Clearing applauding.
textes.Vous m'avez acheté %d objet, pour %d piè: You've bought %d item from me, for %d coins.
textes.Vous m'avez acheté %d objets, pour %d pi: You've bought %d items from me, for %d coins.
textes.Vous m'avez avoué avoir peur du noir. Je: You admitted to me you're afraid of the dark. I haven't told anyone. Tonight, I'll light up a little earlier.
textes.Vous m'avez crue, pour l'île. Je m'en so: You believed me, about the island. I remember it every time I look west.
textes.Vous m'avez dit qu'on ne peut pas tout p: You told me you can't forgive everything. I made a list of what I forgive Hugo for. It's long. It's tiny, actually.
textes.Vous m'avez dit que le Zéphyr vous faisa: You told me the Zéphyr scared you a little. Me too, sometimes. That makes two of us. That's already a crew.
textes.Vous m'avez dit que vous jouiez « un peu: You told me you play “a little”. I still haven't decided whether that was modesty or a trick.
textes.Vous m'avez dit que vous trouviez %s trè: You told me you found %s very nice.
textes.Vous m'avez dit que vous trouviez %s un: You told me you found %s a bit weird.
You told me that last week.
textes.Vous m'avez fait %d cadeau, le dernier :: You've given me %d gift, the last one: %s.
textes.Vous m'avez fait %d cadeaux, le dernier: You've given me %d gifts, the last one: %s.
textes.Vous m'aviez dit : une amitié. J'y repen: You told me: a friendship. I often think about it. It has no gears. And it keeps turning all the same.
textes.Vous m'aviez dit : « Ça dépend. » J'y pe: You told me: “It depends.” I think about it every evening, on the balcony. It depends… on me, mostly.
textes.Vous m'aviez dit que vous vous essuyez l: You told me you wipe your feet when you remember. I have put down three more doormats. Do remember.
textes.Vous m'aviez dit que ça dépendait de quo: You told me it depended on what. I thought about it for a whole winter. You were right.
textes.Vous m'aviez dit « les deux ». Margot a: You told me “both”. Margot worked out that it was the best answer. She wrote down your name.
textes.Vous m'aviez dit « ça dépend ». Alors je: You told me “it depends”. So I'm keeping a colourful surprise for you. Only colourful.
textes.Vous me garderez une bouture ?: Will you save me a cutting?
textes.Vous mettez les oreilles de renard. Vous: You put on the fox ears. You feel like you can hear a little better. Somewhere, a rabbit is laughing.
textes.Vous n'allez pas me ressortir ça chaque: You're not going to bring that up every evening, are you?
textes.Vous n'avez pas vérifié votre idée, j'es: You haven't checked your idea, I hope? Keep it warm. I'm keeping one too. Tightly shut.
You don't have a mailbag any more.
textes.Vous n'aviez pas encore goûté mes galett: You hadn't tried my crackers yet. Still not? Keep your innocence. But buy one anyway, as a decoration.
textes.Vous ne dormez pas ? … Je connais. Je n': You don't sleep? … I know the feeling. I'll say no more. A cup of moon tea, perhaps. The management offers it to insomniacs.
textes.Vous ne lisez pas. … Je vais m'asseoir u: You don't read. … I'm going to sit down for a moment. Well. It doesn't matter. It's never too late. Start with a short book. With pictures.
textes.Vous ne me croyez toujours pas, pour l'î: You still don't believe me, about the island? Next clear night, the telescope is yours. Ten minutes.
textes.Vous ne rêvez jamais de voler, vous. Res: You never dream of flying. Stay that way. We need sensible people on this bench.
textes.Vous ne… tu ne joues pas ? Alors pourquo: You don't… you don't play? Then why come into the Shark's Tooth? For the music? There isn't any. For me? … How flattering.
textes.Vous offrez des fleurs, parfois ? Et à q: Do you ever give flowers? And to whom, if it's not prying?
textes.Vous ouvrez la boîte. Il n'y a rien deda: You open the box. There is nothing inside. The maker kept his word.
textes.Vous ouvrez le parapluie. L'hélice se me: You open the umbrella. The propeller starts to spin, your hair flies away… and you don't.
textes.Vous pourriez m'apprendre à soigner ?: Could you teach me to heal?
textes.Vous qui adorez les surprises, regardez: You who love surprises, look behind you… No, nothing. Not yet. In twenty seconds, maybe.
textes.Vous qui aimez les cartes postales : j'e: You who love postcards: I've got a new one, with the lighthouse at sunset. Victor doesn't have that one. Ha!
textes.Vous qui aimez les choses jolies, revene: You who love pretty things, come back when the wind's from the south. It rains bubbles over the harbour.
textes.Vous qui aimez les orages, regardez le c: You who love storms, look at the sky tonight. There's electricity in the air. And in my coils.
textes.Vous qui aimez les perles, venez voir ma: You like pearls, so come and see my window. I have a new one. Round, honest. It looks like you.
textes.Vous qui avez eu une idée nouvelle… elle: You who had a new idea… is it still yours? Nobody had it in the meantime? I was worried.
textes.Vous qui avez le vertige… vous avez appr: You with your vertigo… have you tamed a few steps since? I'm working on it too. Gently.
textes.Vous qui chantez devant les gens… un jou: You who sing in front of people… will you show me how it's done one day? Just the first note.
textes.Vous qui chantez seulement seul… j'ai pe: You who only sing alone… I thought of you last night. Windows shut.
textes.Vous qui croyez aux légendes, écoutez ce: You who believe in legends, listen to this: a fisherman told me about a blue light last night. Another one! They're multiplying!
textes.Vous qui croyez aux signes : une mouette: You believe in signs: a pure white seagull landed on our balcony this morning. That's a good sign, isn't it? Say yes.
textes.Vous qui croyez à « certaines » légendes: You who believe in “some” legends: I found a new one this morning. Help me sort it out.
textes.Vous qui jetez tout : vous avez pensé à: You who throw everything away: have you thought about the cliff, crane side? I'll be waiting at the bottom.
textes.Vous qui n'avez pas de porte, sachez qu': You who have no door: know that at the palace, there are a hundred and twelve. I could lend you one.
textes.Vous qui n'avez pas le vertige, vous ave: You with no vertigo, did you look out of the cable car window? Tell me about the view. Nobody ever tells me enough about it.
textes.Vous qui n'avez pas peur du noir… la nui: You who aren't afraid of the dark… night is falling. Make the most of it. It's the finest hour.
textes.Vous qui n'offrez de fleurs à personne…: You who give flowers to nobody… take this one. If nobody gives you any, I'll start.
textes.Vous qui ne croyez pas au toujours… je n: You who don't believe in forever… I don't hold it against you. Not much. Neither does the engine.
textes.Vous qui ne croyez pas aux signes, dites: You don't believe in signs, so tell me the seagull on our balcony this morning didn't mean anything. Say it, please.
textes.Vous qui ne faites pas confiance aux mac: You who don't trust machines… You're still right. Hm. Unfortunately.
textes.Vous qui ne jouez pas aux échecs… toujou: You who don't play chess… still as wise as ever? Stay that way. It's rare, in Cliquetis.
textes.Vous qui pardonnez tout, je pense à vous: You forgive everything, so I think of you when I look at the sea from the balcony. I'm trying to do as you do.
textes.Vous qui pensez que tout existe déjà : P: You who think everything's been invented: Philibert has filed another patent. A button. It already existed. You'd agree.
textes.Vous qui préférez les chats… Boulon a fa: You who prefer cats… Boulon pretended not to see you this morning. He's sulking. It'll pass.
textes.Vous qui préférez les chiens : Boulon vo: You who prefer dogs: Boulon saved you a nut. It's a bit chewed. It's a present.
textes.Vous qui préférez les pierres : j'ai reç: You prefer stones: I received a garnet this morning. Not perfect. Real. Come and look at it in the light.
textes.Vous qui préférez les robots : Boulon a: You who prefer robots: Boulon has learned a new trick. He gives his left paw. He'd never done that before.
textes.Vous qui rêvez souvent de voler… si Achi: You who often dream of flying… if Achille ever comes down, I'm warning you. You'll go after me.
textes.Vous qui savez attendre : le lac vous a: You who know how to wait: the lake saw you go by this morning. It said nothing. That's a good sign.
textes.Vous qui trouvez mes galettes délicieuse: You who find my crackers delicious… I've got a batch fresh and hot. I'll watch you eat one, it makes me happy.
textes.Vous qui vous essuyez toujours les pieds: You who always wipe your feet: know that the doormat in the hall awaits you. I had it brushed for you.
textes.Vous qui vous soignez tout seul… montrez: You who patch yourself up… show me that knee anyway. I won't tell a soul.
textes.Vous qui êtes du matin : comment était l: You, the morning person: how was the dawn today? Pink? I missed it, as always. Tell me.
textes.Vous qui êtes du soir : vous avez vu la: You, the evening person: did you see the first star yesterday? It was a planet all right. It winked at you, I saw it.
textes.Vous qui êtes souvent en retard : vous a: You who are often late: did you get the alarm clock I gave you in spirit? It rings loudly, normally.
textes.Vous regardez l'heure. Il est… dans un m: You check the time. It's… in a moment. Or a little while ago. You put the watch away.
textes.Vous remontez le canard. Il fait « coin-: You wind up the duck. It goes “quack-quack-click” and waddles in your hand.
textes.Vous revenez voir le ciel ? Il est magni: Back to see the sky? It's magnificent tonight. It always is.
textes.Vous revenez vous faire confettiser ? Br: Back for another confetti blast? Well done!
textes.Vous savez garder un secret ? Moi non, m: Can you keep a secret? I can't, but maybe you can. Every Thursday, I sit down at Madame Rita's. She reads my cards for free, and I tell her everything that goes on at the hotel. Everything. So her amazing predictions… half of them, {surnom}, are me. The other half, I don't know where she gets them. And that scares me a little.
textes.Vous savez garder un secret, {surnom} ?: Can you keep a secret, {surnom}? I know perfectly well that it's Tic who keeps putting off the wedding. Seven times. I don't hold it against him: he's afraid of something, and I love him with it. At the back of the Bazaar, under a sheet, there's a wedding dress bought thirty-one years ago. The only item in the shop that isn't for sale. The label says: “Useful”.
textes.Vous secouez le grelot : ding-ding ! Vou: You shake the bell: ding-ding! Suddenly you really want to swap something for something else.
textes.Vous soufflez de toutes vos forces. Sile: You blow with all your might. Absolute silence. Somewhere, a fish lifts its head.
textes.Vous tombez à pic ! Je préside le jury d: You've come just in time! I chair the Fair's jury, and every member of the jury has an invention in the competition. It's a small problem. I need the opinion of someone impartial: you. Go and see Prudence's mechanical piano, Basile's bubble machine and Ambroise's automaton. Talk to them, look closely, then come back and tell me what you think.
textes.Vous tournez la manivelle. Une brise dél: You turn the crank. A delightful breeze cools your head. You have an idea! … No, it's gone.
textes.Vous trouviez la ville trop calme ? J'ai: You found the town too quiet? I've had paper lanterns ordered. Three. It's a start.
textes.Vous vendez beaucoup de lavande, Rose ?: Do you sell a lot of lavender, Rose?
textes.Vous voilà en avance, comme toujours. As: Here you are early, as always. Sit down, we'll wait for the hour together. It always comes in the end.
textes.Vous voulez l'entendre encore ?: Would you like to hear it again?
Would you like to hear it again?
textes.Vous voulez la suite ?: Would you like to hear the rest?
textes.Vous voulez que je vous parle de qui ?: Who would you like me to tell you about?
textes.Vous voulez un secret ? Je ne suis jamai: Do you want a secret? I've never been inside the Rune Crypt. Never. Every afternoon, I go up to the door, I look into the dark, and I leave. Dark without stars, I can't bear it. The master of light is afraid of the dark. There. Maybe that's why I became master of light. Don't tell Oscar.
textes.Vous vous glissez sous la couette bleue: You slip under the blue quilt of the Cottage. The wisteria smells lovely. Somewhere, a frog croaks. Zzz…
textes.Vous vous rappelez ? Je dis que je ne li: Remember? I say I don't read the wishes in the yellow postbox. I'm lying, {surnom}. I read them all. And I try to grant the little ones, in secret: an ice cream, a letter, a flower on a doorstep. There's one I can't manage to grant. Victor's handwriting: “To see it snow, just once.” Here, in Port-Azur. I'm trying to work out how.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Anouk, la guéris: You fainted… Anouk, the healer of Carène, treated you with seaweed and honey.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Aurore, la guéri: You fainted… Aurore, the healer, lays a glowing hand on your forehead. “There. All in order. Have a cup of stellar tea, Heavy-Foot.”
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Dagna vous a tra: You fainted… Dagna dragged you to the Forgefer terrace.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Des Atlantes vou: You fainted… Atlanteans brought you back under the dome, in front of the palace.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Des aventuriers: You fainted… Some adventurers carried you back to the Grand-Place, and Mamie Rissole fed you a slice of pie. You feel better right away.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Des chasseurs ma: You fainted… Maya hunters carried you to Yaxché.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Des démons vous: You fainted… Demons carried you to the Great Square, and Mère Brasille gave you a spicy-pepper broth. It wakes you up!
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Des fées vous on: You fainted… Fairies healed you with dew and songs.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Des pirates vous: You fainted… Pirates picked you up and dropped you off at the Doc's, who stitched you up without asking questions.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Des pêcheurs vou: You fainted… Fishermen brought you back by dugout canoe to Aztlán.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Le docteur Roux: You fainted… Doctor Roux treated you. You're now in Port-Azur's square.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Le professeur Bo: You fainted… Professor Boum revived you with a little shock (a very little one). You're now on the Cliquetis promenade.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Mère Sauge vous: You fainted… Mother Sage made you drink a tea that smelled of thyme. You're now in Cauldron Square, in Arcanelle.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Néferet vous a s: You fainted… Néferet healed you at the temple of Per-Hâpy.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Pivoine, la rena: You fainted… Pivoine, the fox herbalist, had you sniff a vial of mist. You're now at the Moon Circle.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Un berger vous a: You fainted… A shepherd brought you back out into the open air, in front of the Wind Sheepfold.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Un caravanier de: You fainted… A passing caravaneer pulled you out of the tomb and gave you something to drink.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Vous voici de re: You fainted… You're back in the village.
You fainted… You're back in the village. A fisherman brought your boat back to the jetty.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Vous vous réveil: You fainted… You wake up on a couch in Pallet Square, under a patchwork blanket. Lentille hands you a bowl of soup: “Pay what you like. Drink.”
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… Zineb, la patron: You fainted… Zineb, the owner of the Fondouk, made you drink a very sweet tea. You're now in Lantern Square.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… et réveillé au p: You fainted… and woke up at the foot of the ladder.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… et réveillé sur: You fainted… and woke up on the Wind Landing, at the edge of the floating island.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… et réveillé à l': You fainted… and woke up at the entrance of the hall. The red light of the Heart still beats.
textes.Vous vous êtes évanoui… et vous vous rév: You fainted… and you wake up in your bed, at the Wisteria Cottage. Someone tucked you in. Probably Pétronille. Or a very kind neighbor.
textes.Vous voyez ce petit point, là-haut, qui: See that little dot up there, doing figures of eight? That's my brother, Achille. He invented steam-powered wings. He's been flying for eight days. He doesn't know how to land. I'm Adèle. I'm waiting for him.
textes.Vous étiez perdu, la dernière fois. Vous: You were lost, last time. Less so now, it seems. Noted.
textes.Vous êtes allé sur l'île flottante. Je l: You've been to the floating island. I wrote it in my notebook, with your name. It's my only proof.
textes.Vous êtes au mouillage chez nous, c'est: You're moored with us, that's noted. Line forty-two. You haven't broken anything since. Keep it up.
textes.Vous êtes sage. Les échecs, ce sont troi: You're wise. Chess is three hundred defeats before the first victory. And sometimes, the victory is won by someone else in your place.
You've come to see me %d times.
textes.Vous, c'est de face, je m'en souviens. N: You're a front-view type, I remember. Don't move… Click! In my mind. The best photo of my holiday.
textes.Vous, l'amateur de romans d'amour… j'en: You, the romance lover… I have one to recommend to you. I won't tell you why I know it so well.
textes.Vous, l'habitué du Zéphyr : il y a une p: You, the Zéphyr regular: there's a window seat free tomorrow. But no spitting. Léonce has already done that.
textes.Vous, vous avez un peu le vertige. Alors: You get a little vertigo. So you don't lean out. Have I told you already? I'll say it again. Don't lean out.
textes.Vous, vous ne démontez rien. Je peux lai: You don't take anything apart. I can leave my tools next to you. That's rare, in Cliquetis.
textes.Vous. Oui, vous. Essuyez vos pieds, je v: You. Yes, you. Wipe your feet, if you please.
textes.Vous… pardon, tu sais lire une carte ?: Can you… pardon me, can you read a map?
textes.Vous… vous me croyez, pour l'île flottan: You… you believe me, about the floating island, in the west?
textes.Vous… y êtes allé ? Vraiment ? Attendez,: You… have been there? Really? Wait, my notebook. The trees, what are they like? And underneath, is it rock? Sorry. I'm shaking a little. Nobody had ever told me that.
textes.Voyageur ! Approche, n'aie pas peur des: Traveller! Come closer, don't be afraid of the hats.
textes.Voyons, voyons… Tout est garanti, sauf c: Let's see, let's see… Everything is guaranteed, except what isn't. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Vrai ?! Toi aussi ?! … Alors on n'a qu'à: Really?! You too?! … Then we'll just be scared together! That way we'll be less scared! Here, it brings good luck.
textes.Vraiment ? Ah, ça me fait plaisir ! Ils: Really? Ah, that makes me happy! They're less than fifty years old, you know. Well, most of them. I'll save you the one at the back, it's the softest.
textes.Vraiment ? Alors nous sommes cousins d'h: Really? Then we're herb cousins. You'll bring me yours.
textes.Vraiment ? Alors viens demain matin, au: Really? Then come tomorrow morning, to the end of the beach. We'll start with floating. Floating is like dancing lying down. You'll see, the sea holds you up.
textes.Vraiment ? Une vraie ? … C'est merveille: Really? A real one? … That's wonderful. I'm very happy for you. And a teeny bit jealous. Well, very. But mostly happy. Did you check? No, don't tell me.
textes.Vraiment ? … Écoute celui-là, alors. Tac: Really? … Listen to this one, then. Tac. And this one. Tac. Which one's ready? Take your time. Liars answer fast.
textes.Vu d'en haut, l'île ressemble à une feui: From above, the island looks like a leaf lying on the sea, with a stone in the middle. Stoneheart. We fly over it at a hundred and sixty metres. Below, it's flat as a table and round as a plate.
textes.Vziiiou ! Toi ! Avec le Glisseur d'Ionie: Vzziiiou! You! With Ionie's Glider! Finally, an opponent! Right. First, I need to see if you can handle yourself in the air. Go to the Zero-Gravity Garden, in the west, and do the glowing ring course. Set a record, any record: it's just to see if you can aim. Then… the real race. In the sky. Rings of light all around the island: under the plateau, between the islets, through the waterfalls of light, and back to the Spaceport. Me in my saucer, you in your Glider. First to arrive wins. Second pays for the ice creams. I love ice cream.
textes.Vérifie vite. Et pas un mouton, cette fo: Check fast. And no sheep this time.
textes.Whoooo ! Le tapis t'emporte à reculons,: Whoooo! The belt carries you backwards, much faster than you can run. You have to switch it: the levers are at the console, near the entrance.
textes.Wilfried a donné un bras pour l'envelopp: Wilfried gave an arm for the Zéphyr's envelope. I never forget it. At every take-off, I give him a wave. And he has the noisiest dog in the sky.
textes.Wilfried est un homme bon, avec un bras: Wilfried is a good man, with a brass arm and a dog that has a heart. We weren't made to live together. We're very well made for raising Léonce.
textes.Wouah ! Il est magnifique ! Cette fois,: Whoa! It's gorgeous! This time I'm paying you!
textes.Xan ? Pour descendre dans Xibalba ? Comm: Xan? To go down into Xibalba? Like the Twins?! … All right! But I'm hungry. I'm too hungry to lend you a mosquito. Ix Chab makes the best corn cakes in the square. Will you bring me one?
textes.Xan file vers les trônes et pique chaque: Xan flies toward the thrones and stings each Lord, one after another…
textes.Xan va très bien ! Et Miou, il a toujour: Xan is doing great! And Miou, does he still have his crooked ear?
textes.Xan, tu obéis bien, d'accord ? Et tu rev: Xan, you'll behave, all right? And you'll come back! (He pats the gourd.) Goodbye, Xan…
textes.Xibalba, le royaume des Seigneurs de la: Xibalba, the kingdom of the Lords of Death.
textes.Xóchitl ! Tes fleurs me regardent encore: Xóchitl! Your flowers are watching me again.
textes.Xóchitl ! Tes fleurs se vendent très bie: Xóchitl! Your flowers are selling very well!
textes.Xóchitl et moi, nous avons grandi sur le: Xóchitl and I grew up on the same canal. She smelled of flowers, I smelled of ink. She brings me flowers for the class. I teach her to read the days. She prefers the flowers.
textes.Xóchitl fait pousser des fleurs et du ma: Xóchitl grows flowers and maize on the water. The jaguars of Smoking Mountain took one of her animals. I promised her I'd hunt them. I keep my promises. When the high priest allows it.
textes.Xóchitl fait pousser des fleurs sur l'ea: Xóchitl grows flowers on the water, and she laughs louder than Nenetl's drum. I make her pots for her flowers. With eyes. She says her flowers look surprised. They have every reason to.
textes.Xóchitl fait pousser les plus belles fle: Xóchitl grows the most beautiful flowers on the lake. I resell them. She doesn't much like that. But we've known each other for thirty years. That's what you call a lasting business relationship.
textes.Xóchitl, la jardinière des chinampas, a: Xóchitl, the gardener of the chinampas, needs five bouquets of cempasúchil, the orange flowers that guide the souls of the dead, for the temple altars.
textes.Xóchitl. Les jaguars ne sont pas revenus: Xóchitl. The jaguars haven't come back?
textes.Yannick ! J'ai fini votre route jusqu'au: Yannick! I've finished your route to the elves.
textes.Yannick est le garçon le plus sympathiqu: Yannick is the friendliest lad in Port-Azur. He calls me “captain”, and he always has a pedalo for me. The same one. I think he keeps it for me.
textes.Yannick est un bon pote et un loueur cat: Yannick is a good mate and a disastrous boat-hirer. He rents pedalos to people who can't swim. I bring them back. One customer in ten, I've counted.
textes.Yannick loue des bateaux à des gens qui: Yannick rents boats to people who can't swim, and he thinks it's “cool”. One day I'll speak to the mayor about it. I've been saying that for three seasons, I know.
Yannick rents boats to people who can't swim. One day I'll have to mention it to the mayor.
textes.Yannick rêve de faire le tour de l'archi: Yannick dreams of sailing round the archipelago. I'm drawing him the route. He took me out in a pedalo once; we don't talk about it.
textes.Yasmine a des doigts de gabier et une tê: Yasmine has a topman's fingers and a captain's head. In fifteen years, she'll command a ship. I just pray it won't be the one chasing us.
textes.Yasmine monte sur mes canons comme sur d: Yasmine climbs on my cannons as if they were horses. I chase her off, she comes back. Rosa says she'd make a good captain of the guard. … Rosa talks a lot of nonsense.
textes.Yasmine, c'est ma copine. Elle est toujo: Yasmine's my friend. She's always the captain, and I'm always the sailor. It's not fair. But without her, boarding is rubbish.
textes.Yasmine, c'est ma fierté et mon souci. E: Yasmine is my pride and my worry. She refuses fish, she bosses the whole harbour around, and she wants to go to sea. Like her father. I don't sleep easy, but I laugh every day.
textes.Yasmine, ma nièce, capitaine de la Zahra: Yasmine, my niece, captain of the Zahra when she's moored. She has her mother's voice and her grandmother's orders. I'm her first sailor, and I obey.
textes.Yaya ! J'ai fait le crabe toute seule ce: Yaya! I did the crab all by myself this morning, on the beach!
textes.Yaya ! Je t'ai gardé le plus chaud !: Yaya! I saved you the warmest one!
textes.Yaya a voulu m'apprendre le pas du crabe: Yaya tried to teach me the crab step. I tried. Without stopping nodding. She laughed for an hour, sitting in the sand. I helped her up. I said: “Again?” I never got the step. I got the laugh. That's better.
textes.Yaya a voulu m'apprendre à danser « plus: Yaya tried to teach me to dance “smaller”, elbows tucked in, so I'd stop knocking people over. A week of lessons. On exam night, I lasted two tracks. On the third, my arm flew out and Yaya landed in Tchoum's arms. She never said whether I'd failed. She looked happy.
textes.Yaya donnait son cours à cinq heures, et: Yaya gave her class at five, and so did I my show, on the other side of the fountain. One day, I did the crab step backwards while falling over, and all the kids came over to my side. Yaya was left with the cat. The next day she'd moved her class to four. I moved my show too.
textes.Yaya et moi, on se partage la place du v: Yaya and I share the village square in the afternoons: she dances, I clown around. The kids come to me, the cat stays with her. I admire her. Don't tell her.
textes.Yaya jurait que le chat de la petite mai: Yaya swore the cat from the little house danced better than us. Nobody believed her. So I hid behind the fountain for a whole lesson. I've got the photo: the cat, one paw raised, right on the crab step. It's framed at Yaya's, above her bed.
textes.Yaya m'a amenée ici : je lui dois tout c: Yaya brought me here: I owe her every good thing that's happened to me in two years. She dances like a happy crab, and I always save her the warmest croissant.
textes.Yaya m'a appris le pas du crabe le premi: Yaya taught me the crab step the first night, my bag still in my hand. Since then I go to her class every day, next to the cat. He's better than me, but I'm improving.
textes.Yaya prétend que le chat du village dans: Yaya claims the village cat dances better than us. I've seen it. She's right.
textes.Yaya venait chaque semaine à la boulange: Yaya used to come to the bakery every week. I'd be dancing behind the counter and the change would go flying everywhere. One day, she put down her coins, did the crab step all the way to the door and told me: “Tonight, village beach. No arguments.” I didn't argue.
textes.Yaya, bouge pas, la lune est juste derri: Yaya, don't move, the moon is right behind you.
Yaya is my sister in everything but blood. She dances, I photograph: we've been doing that since we were six, on the same street. She's right about the cat, by the way.
textes.Yaya, le crabe amoureux, c'est moi qui l: Yaya, I'm the one who invented the lovestruck crab.
textes.Yaya. … Elle danse bien. Très bien. Elle: Yaya. … She dances well. Very well. She laughs loud. Louder than Raoul. … That's all. That's already a lot.
textes.Yggdrasil a quatre salles, comme les qua: Yggdrasil has four halls, like the four seasons. And a crown right at the top.
textes.Yggdrasil, l'Arbre-Monde, ne donne plus: Yggdrasil, the World Tree, hasn't produced any seeds for a hundred years: nasty plants have overrun its trunk. Queen Oriane would like the seed sleeping at the very top of the tree.
textes.Yo ! Bienvenue à la teuf ! Mets-toi deva: Yo! Welcome to the party! Get in front of the speakers, that's where it's at!
textes.Yo ! On répète pour le concert de samedi: Yo! We're rehearsing for Saturday's concert. We're missing a singer. Can you sing?
textes.Yo ! Première teuf ? Alors règle numéro: Yo! First party? Then rule number one: earplugs near the speakers. Rule number two: have fun.
textes.Yo ! Yannick, location de bateaux, de pé: Yo! Yannick, boat hire, pedalos and good vibes. Fancy a ride?
textes.Your weapon ! Of course. Une lame qui a: Your weapon! Of course. A blade that has seen the world is worth all the treasures there are. Will you show it to me? I shan't touch it. I'll only press my nose to it.
textes.Youssef ? Il voit des baleines partout,: Youssef? He sees whales everywhere, tells me about them every day, and breaks my bowls turning round to smile at me. He's sweet. A bit of a fibber. Sweet all the same.
textes.Youssef ? Une tête de mule. Il voit des: Youssef? Stubborn as a mule. He sees whales everywhere and says I scare the fish away. I love him like a son. Don't tell him.
textes.Youssef dit qu'il a vu une baleine passe: Youssef says he saw a whale swim past the Skala. Youssef sees whales everywhere.
textes.Youssef veut sa barque, la Baleine. Il p: Youssef wants his boat, the Whale. He pays coin by coin, he's a quarter of the way there. I start the hull at half. That's the rule. Even for him.
textes.Youssef, mon voisin de quai. Bon pêcheur: Youssef, my neighbour on the quay. A good fisherman, I'll admit, but he sees whales everywhere. And he says my Zahra is cross-eyed. She's cross-eyed just the right amount.
textes.Ysolde a dit que les pierres aiment pas: Ysolde said the stones don't like being alone in the dark. So I brought them my checked blanket, the one from my bed. She put it on the smallest stone. Now I'm a bit cold at night, but the little stone isn't. It's better that way. It's older than me.
textes.Ysolde est la fille d'Aube, ma plus viei: Ysolde is the daughter of Aube, my oldest friend, who guarded the Circle before her. She has her mother's eyes and her silence. I find her too lonely. She finds I talk too much.
Ysolde frightens me a little, I admit. She always appears behind you. But she loves her stones the way I love my stars, and that I understand. I say thank you for every shard.
textes.Ysolde parle peu, comme moi. Avec elle,: Ysolde doesn't talk much, like me. With her, you can stay quiet for a long time without it being awkward. She's teaching me the names of the stones. Slowly. The stones have to agree.
textes.Ysolde regarde le passé avec ses pierres: Ysolde looks at the past with her stones, I look at the future with my ball. We meet in the middle, in the present, and we never quite know what to say to each other. She finds me chatty. I find her too lonely.
textes.Ysolde, elle fait un peu peur. Elle est: Ysolde's a bit scary. She's always behind you, even when she was in front. I think she never sleeps. But she kept my blanket for the little stone. So maybe she's nice.
textes.Yum Kab ! Il reste du miel sur la cuillè: Yum Kab! Is there any honey left on the spoon?
textes.Yum Kab est doux comme son miel et têtu: Yum Kab is as gentle as his honey and as stubborn as his bees. In the evening we play knucklebones. He loses. He laughs. He plays again. He's the ideal opponent, and the most restful friend in the jungle.
textes.Yum Kab m'apporte le miel du balché, la: Yum Kab brings me the honey for the balché, the festival drink, and the wax for the offerings. He's the only man in Yaxché who makes me laugh during a ceremony. I don't know whether I should thank him for it.
textes.Yum Kab parle à ses abeilles. Elles lui: Yum Kab talks to his bees. They answer him, he says. By buzzing.
Yum Kab talks to his bees. They answer him, he says. By buzzing. I don't know. But he's the gentlest man in Yaxché. I bring him meat. He brings me honey.
textes.Yum Kab vend son miel moins cher que moi: Yum Kab sells his honey cheaper than I sell mine. I don't have any honey, but it's a matter of principle. If he goes any lower, nobody will dare sell anything sweet at the market.
Yum Kab sells his honey cheaper than I sell mine. I don't have any honey. But it's a matter of principle.
textes.Yum Kab, c'est le plus gentil de tout Ya: Yum Kab is the nicest person in all of Yaxché! His bees don't have stingers, and he lets me lick the honey spoon every day. He says I'm as sticky as honey. It's true, after the spoon.
textes.Yum Kab. Le miel du balché est prêt ?: Yum Kab. Is the honey for the balché ready?
textes.Yum Kab. Ton miel, toujours trop bon mar: Yum Kab. Your honey, still too cheap?
Yum Kab. A hive, in the big ceiba.
textes.Yvon, le pêcheur du lac, a peur des gren: Yvon, the lake fisherman, has been afraid of the giant frogs for forty years. There are more and more of them: they steal his fish, his bait and, once, his boat. He'd like someone to chase a few of them away.
textes.Z / S : avancer, reculer • Q / D : bar: Z / S: forward, reverse  •  Q / D: steer  •  approach a jetty or a beach to disembark
textes.Z / S : plus vite / plus lent (S arrête): Z / S: faster / slower (S stops), Q / D: turn, Space: climb, Ctrl: descend, E: land.
textes.Z / S : vitesse (S : sur place), Q / D :: Z / S: speed (S: hover), Q / D: turn, Space / Ctrl: climb / descend, E: land.
W to go up, S to go down.
textes.ZONE DE STOCKAGE\nCaisses à pousser. Ne:
STORAGE AREA
Crates to push. Do not push the robots.
textes.Zigomar ! Je peux être ton apprentie, ma: Zigomar! Can I be your apprentice now?
textes.Zigomar ! Les fusées seront prêtes pour: Zigomar! Will the rockets be ready for the festival?
textes.Zigomar ! Rien de neuf pour moi, hein ?: Zigomar! Nothing new for me, right?
textes.Zigomar a fait exploser trois de mes lan: Zigomar has blown up three of my lanterns, but he also invented the lanterns that fly away. For the Night of Lanterns, he's my partner in crime: the light's mine, the rockets are his. Together, we throw a party.
textes.Zigomar a transformé une de mes lanterne: Zigomar turned one of my lanterns into a rocket once. It flew up over the square, and everyone applauded. Since then, at every festival, we send lanterns flying. It's become a tradition!
textes.Zigomar est mon cousin. Il invente des c: Zigomar is my cousin. He invents things that explode, and he always wants to help me. He built me a jet-powered postbag. I've forgiven him. I don't want him to invent anything for me ever again.
textes.Zigomar fait exploser des choses en m'en: Zigomar blows things up while sending me hearts. He's tiring, noisy and eyebrowless. He's also the only one who's ever given me a firework. I don't know what to make of it yet.
textes.Zigomar m'a fabriqué un « sac postal à r: Zigomar built me a “jet-powered postbag” to deliver faster. On the first try, the bag caught fire above the port, and I crossed the Harbour backwards, smoking like a chimney. All the letters arrived, a bit toasted. People thought they smelled nicely of bread. Zigomar said it was a success.
textes.Zigomar m'a laissée allumer une fusée, u: Zigomar let me light a rocket once, on the pier. A tiny one. It went up really high, went “pop”, and drew a wonky star. Zigomar said it was the most beautiful wonky star he'd ever seen. I kept the stick in my treasure box.
textes.Zigomar m'envoie des fusées en forme de: Zigomar sends me heart-shaped rockets. The last one exploded in the shape of a… kidney. He says it was on purpose. It was very sweet. Don't tell him.
textes.Zigomar prépare les fusées de la Nuit de: Zigomar is making the rockets for the Night of Lanterns. For his rockets he needs sulphur crystals, from the sulphur springs, outside the city. I'm not allowed to go there. You're allowed, aren't you?
textes.Zigomar, c'est le plus grand inventeur d: Zigomar is the greatest inventor in the archipelago. His workshop has almost no roof left, and he has almost no eyebrows left. That proves he works hard. One day, I'll be his apprentice. Officially.
textes.Zigomar, l'inventeur et artificier, n'a: Zigomar, the inventor and fireworks maker, has run out of sulphur for his Night of Lanterns rockets. He needs three sulphur crystals from the hot springs.
textes.Zigomar. Plus de fusée en forme de cœur,: Zigomar. No more heart-shaped rockets, all right?
textes.Zineb fait semblant de râler parce que j: Zineb pretends to grumble because I pay her in paintings. But she hung them up herself, each on its own nail. The Fondouk is my home now. And she's a bit like my aunt.
textes.Zineb tient le Fondouk et vend son thé à: Zineb runs the Fondouk and sells her own tea. She says the fourth glass must be paid for. I give it away. We've been arguing for years. I don't know what I'd do without her.
textes.Zineb. Mon hôtesse. Elle garde ma chambr: Zineb. My hostess. She keeps my room, even when the courtyard is full. She brings tea up at midnight. … I have nothing else to say.
textes.Zip, zoum, scintille ! Ton Albatros a fa: Zip, zoom, sparkle! Your Albatros has molted: here is the Star Glider. It zips along like a happy thought. Don't exceed the speed of light, it's very frowned upon around here.
textes.Zohra ! Elle discute mon prix tous les v: Zohra! She haggles over my price every Friday, as if I were a thief. Then she takes my saffron, and nobody else's. A woman of taste. And of bad faith.
textes.Zohra ? Elle crie, elle juge, elle se fâ: Zohra? She shouts, she judges, she gets cross with the entire sea when Friday comes round, and she'd hold a lamp for three nights for a friend. I made her the finest dish of my life.
textes.Zohra a le premier étal, juste sous mon: Zohra has the first stall, right under my platform, and she refuses my sea bream. She says their flesh is stressed. Stressed! My sea bream! I like her anyway. That's serious.
textes.Zohra cherche des dorades pour son tajin: Zohra is looking for sea bream for her tajine. She won't take mine: she says they've heard too much shouting.
textes.Zohra commande tout le monde depuis qu'e: Zohra has been bossing everyone around since she learned to talk. Me first. She shouts, she judges, she's always right. The best sister in the port, but don't tell her.
textes.Zohra m'a commandé un tablier brodé de d: Zohra ordered an apron embroidered with sea bream. “Calm ones, mind. Not stressed ones.” I embroidered six sleeping sea bream, eyes half closed. She wore it to the auction, planted herself under Saïd's platform and shouted at him: “That's what a happy sea bream looks like!” Saïd shouted louder. But he looked at the apron.
textes.Zohra se moque de l'œil qui louche. Moi,: Zohra makes fun of the cross-eyed eye. Me, I stand up for Ali. I say it's on purpose, to see both reefs at once. Ali's the one who told me that; I don't know if he was joking. But one misty night, that eye brought me back into the channel all by itself. So maybe it is cross-eyed on purpose.
textes.Zohra veut faire son grand tajine du ven: Zohra wants to make her big Friday tajine. No sea bream, no tajine. She's in such a mood…
textes.Zohra, c'est mon amie, et la plus grande: Zohra is my friend, and the biggest chatterbox in Tazira. A secret told to Zohra in the morning is on every boat by evening. But she brings the best fish. You forgive a lot to a friend who brings fish.
textes.Zohra, la poissonnière, veut faire son g: Zohra, the fishmonger, wants to make her big Friday tagine. She needs two fine sea bream, caught by someone other than the fish-market men.
textes.Zohra, la reine du tajine ! Elle m'a tou: Zohra, the queen of tagine! She taught me everything. Well, she watched me do it, and she wept for joy. A woman who weeps over your cooking, you don't forget that.
textes.Zoé dort dans ma cabane d'essai depuis t: Zoé has been sleeping in my test hut for three weeks. She's put shells everywhere and leaves the door open for the crabs. But she says it's the most beautiful hut in the world. That counts.
textes.Zoé laisse toujours la porte ouverte. Un: Zoé always leaves the door open. One morning, there were three crabs in her hammock. She named them Kick, Bass and Mistral, and she talks to them. I say a hut is for closing. She says a hut is for opening. We don't agree. I still gave a bit of banana to Bass. He looked hungry.
textes.Zoé m'a demandé si on pouvait aller voir: Zoé asked if we could go and see Atlantis together. I stopped swimming. I said “one day”, in a tiny little voice. She didn't push: she floated on her back next to me, humming. That evening I gave her a pearly shell. It meant: one day, yes.
textes.Zoé m'aide à percer mes coquillages, l'a: Zoé helps me drill my shells in the afternoons. She holds the sea-urchin spine, I hold the shell. One day she drilled one so pretty that I put it in the middle of a necklace and sold it. Zoé sulked for an hour: she wanted to keep it. So I made her another one. Just for her. With a crab.
textes.Zoé nage comme elle danse : partout à la: Zoé swims the way she dances: everywhere at once, with lots of splashing and a big smile. She wants to go to Atlantis with me. That scares me, and it does me good.
textes.Zoé ne devait rester qu'un week-end. Ell: Zoé was only supposed to stay one weekend. She had no room left. I lent her my test hut for two nights, the one that leans. Three weeks later, there are shell garlands, a hammock and a sign saying “Zoé's Place”. I knock before going into my own hut now.
textes.Zoé vient à mon cours sur la place tous: Zoé comes to my class on the square every day at four. She settles in next to the cat and does everything he does. He stretches, she stretches. He yawns, she yawns. Yesterday he did the crab step and she followed. I'm not quite sure who's teaching whom any more.
textes.Zoé, aujourd'hui, on apprend à remonter: Zoé, today we learn to come up gently.
textes.Zoé, c'est la touriste qui reste. Arrivé: Zoé is the tourist who stayed. She came for a weekend and never looked at the boat timetable again. For a DJ, there's no finer compliment.
textes.Zoé, c'est ma deuxième élève sérieuse, a: Zoé is my second serious pupil, after the cat. She learns fast, she falls over laughing, and she comes back the next day. That's all you can ask of a dancer.
textes.Zoé, c'est mon témoin pour le dauphin, e: Zoé is my witness for the dolphin, and the best dancer to ever land on this beach since… since never. She tells me to jump, so I jump. She's always right.
Zoé, the door. Close the door.
textes.Zoé, le genou plié ! Comme le chat !: Zoé, bend the knee! Like the cat!
textes.Zut ! Bon, ça fait toujours sept sur dou: Drat! Well, that's still seven out of twelve!
textes.Zut ! J'étais si bien caché !: Darn! I was so well hidden!
textes.Zut. Je m'entraîne depuis trois semaines: Darn. I've been practicing for three weeks… Don't tell anyone, okay?
textes.Zzz… (Il renifle, sans ouvrir les yeux.): Zzz… (He sniffs, without opening his eyes.) … Honorine? (He opens one eye.) Oh! It's you! Thank you! I wasn't sleeping, you know. I was smelling. It's the best bread on the island. Tell her thank you. Tell her I wasn't sleeping.
textes.Zzz… gratte-moi le dos… plus à gauche…: Zzz… scratch my back… more to the left…
Zzz… huh? Old Flint not sleeping.
textes.Zébuline ! Le pot de cannelle, c'est enc: Zébuline! The cinnamon jar, was that you again?
textes.Zébuline ! Ma fille ! Des épices sont ar: Zébuline! My girl! Spices have arrived!
textes.Zébuline est ma voisine d'étal. Elle me: Zébuline has the stall next to mine. She sells me fire cinnamon, she laughs loudly, and she worries about Pépin from morning to night. She pretends not to know about the broken brioches. She knows.
textes.Zébuline m'a demandé la recette de ma po: Zébuline asked me for the recipe of my courage potion. I told her: “Infernal chili.” She waited for the rest. There was no rest. She thought I was joking. I wasn't joking. The courage is swallowing a spoonful of her chili. The rest is water, so you can do it.
textes.Zébuline me fournit le piment infernal p: Zébuline supplies me with infernal chili for my courage potions. She talks a lot, she laughs loudly, and she labels her jars with a single word. One. No date. It pains me.
textes.Zébuline, c'est ma fille. Elle a eu le m: Zébuline's my daughter. She was seasick from the cradle, so she sells what the sea brings: spices from the islands. She has my temper and her mother's patience. Luckily.
textes.Zébuline, ma voisine d'étal, vend des ép: Zébuline, my stall neighbour, sells spices. Pepper, mostly. On my side of the stall, mostly. She smiles a lot. I sneeze a lot. We're even. I think.
textes.Zébuline. Tes étiquettes. Il manque la d: Zébuline. Your labels. The date is missing.
textes.Zélie a dessiné un plan d'atterrissage a: Zélie drew up a landing plan using the port's fishing nets. One night, we stretched the biggest one between two masts, on the quay. Achille came down, took aim, and missed it by ten metres. He went past shouting “sorry!”. Zélie took notes. She says next time we'll use three nets.
textes.Zélie a piloté mon Zéphyr dix ans sans u: Zélie flew my Zéphyr for ten years without a scratch. She wants my gas recipe. She won't get it, but I rather like that she wants it.
textes.Zélie a refusé qu'Achille se pose sur le: Zélie refused to let Achille land on the Zéphyr. She was probably right, and I still hold it against her a little. But she lends me her binoculars. You can't hold a grudge for long against someone who lends you their binoculars.
textes.Zéphyr ! Tu me dois deux plumes et une c: Zéphyr! You owe me two feathers and a crate.
textes.Zéphyr ! Tu t'es perdu, aujourd'hui ?: Zéphyr! Did you get lost today?
textes.Zéphyr ! Tu te souviens de mon île, aujo: Zéphyr! Do you remember my island today?
textes.Zéphyr ? Il dit qu'il vole plus vite que: Zéphyr? He says he flies faster than the wind. The wind says otherwise. He shows off all the time, but when he gets lost, it's my fireflies that bring him home.
textes.Zéphyr ? Mon tout premier client, et le: Zéphyr? My very first customer, and the worst payer in the sky. He carries my crates of nectar up to the cloud fairies, and he pays me in feathers.
textes.Zéphyr dit qu'il vole plus vite que le v: Zéphyr says he flies faster than the wind. The wind says otherwise.
textes.Zéphyr fait trois fois le tour de l'Arbr: Zéphyr flies three times around the Tree before breakfast. Three times, all my drops on the ground. He calls it exercise. I call it extra work.
textes.Zéphyr m'a appris qu'elle avait perdu sa: Zéphyr told me she'd lost her wand and that she hides her hands when he flies by. I said nothing. A branch of Yggdrasil is never truly lost: it waits for someone to come and fetch it. It isn't always the fairy who goes.
textes.Zéphyr m'a rapporté la graine de cactus: Zéphyr brought me back the dwarf cactus seed. He arrived all proud… with a chunk of cactus stuck in his bottom. He said it was for transport. I pulled the spines out one by one. He went “fffwoosh” at every spine. There were thirty-two.
textes.Zéphyr me paie en plumes du grand oiseau: Zéphyr pays me in feathers from the great bird Ventaile. He says they're very rare. Me, I've got a drawer full of rare feathers and not a single coin. I tried selling some to Grommelot for his fireplace. He said they burn badly.
textes.Zéphyr porte mes lettres à Brindille. J': Zéphyr carries my letters to Brindille. I need him, and he knows it. Once, he read my letter out loud during the journey, “to practise reading fast”. Every seagull in the archipelago knows my advice to my sister. I didn't speak to him for a whole season. He didn't notice.
textes.Zéphyr porte nos lettres entre les îles,: Zéphyr carries our letters between the islands, faster than anyone. He's a braggart, touchy, and always one excuse behind. I wouldn't trade messengers for anything in the world.
textes.Zéphyr refuse de voyager d'un battement: Zéphyr refuses to travel in the blink of an eye, like the rest of us: he says it's cheating. One day, I set off for the elves' island at the same time as him. I waited for him over a cup of herbal tea. He arrived two hours later, out of breath, saying he'd taken a shortcut.
textes.Zéphyr, c'est lui qui m'a montée ici, da: Zéphyr is the one who carried me up here, in my hazelnut. So he's sort of my godfather. A godfather who can't remember where he found me, but a godfather all the same.
Zéphyr. My flowers, this morning. Again.
textes.Zéphyr. Tu as livré mes lettres ?: Zéphyr. Did you deliver my letters?
textes.Zéphyrine ! Il y aura du vent, cette nui: Zéphyrine! Will there be wind tonight?
textes.Zéphyrine ! J'ai une nouvelle potion rat: Zéphyrine! I've got a new botched potion for you!
textes.Zéphyrine ! Regarde comme je saute haut: Zéphyrine! Look how high I can jump!
textes.Zéphyrine Plume m'apprendra la lévitatio: Zéphyrine Plume will teach me levitation if I bring her three wind feathers. Then I'll have to ring the bell at the top of the Leaning Tower.
textes.Zéphyrine dit que le vent du nord lui a: Zéphyrine says the north wind spoke to her. The north wind doesn't speak. It whistles. That's different.
textes.Zéphyrine est gentille, bavarde, et touj: Zéphyrine is kind, chatty, and always up in the air, literally. We will never agree about the wind. It's restful, in a way. You always know where you stand.
textes.Zéphyrine est la seule personne de l'île: Zéphyrine is the only person on the island who talks faster than me. We're the ones up high. She visits me on my roof, levitating, with cake. The best of neighbours. The noisiest, too.
textes.Zéphyrine est très gentille, mais depuis: Zéphyrine is very kind, but since the bedsheet business, she looks at me as if I'm about to fly out of the window. Which could happen, mind you. Not on purpose.
textes.Zéphyrine, c'est ma meilleure cliente !: Zéphyrine is my best customer! She buys a botched potion from me every week and drinks it in front of everyone. Nobody else dares. She's the bravest person on the island.
textes.Zéphyrine, elle vole ! Pour de vrai, san: Zéphyrine can fly! For real, without a bedsheet! She says I mustn't jump off the dormitory. But she jumps off everything. It's not fair. I like her anyway. A lot.
textes.Zéro, le vieux balayeur de la Place des: Zéro, the old sweeper of the Hologram Square and the very first android of Neopolis, has lost his voice: his Z-Series voice chip gave out, and they stopped making them thirty years ago. Little Mio, his best friend, would so love to hear him tell his stories again.

textes.« ALERTE : DURITE ENDOMMAGÉE. CECI N'ÉTA: “ALERT: HOSE DAMAGED. THIS WAS NOT IN THE SPREADSHEET.” The screen turns bright red: OPTIMUS-LISSE switches to “VERY CROSS (POLITELY)” mode.
textes.« AU SECOURS ! » Un apprenti sorcier tou: “HELP!” An apprentice wizard circles his cauldron. On a chair, a frog glares at him, furious.
textes.« Alors l'Homme-Oiseau s'envola, le deux: “Then the Bird-Man took flight, the second, to seek the land beyond the waves.”
textes.« Au commencement, l'Œil du Soleil s'ouv: “In the beginning, the Eye of the Sun opened over the great waters, and the sea was warm.”
textes.« BIP. BONJOUR. INVITÉ. » Un petit robot: “BEEP. HELLO. GUEST.” A little copper robot rolls toward you, a tray in hand.
textes.« BONJOUR, VISITEUR NON AUTORISÉ. VOTRE: “GOOD DAY, UNAUTHORISED VISITOR. YOUR PRESENCE IS NOT OPTIMAL. LAUNCHING PROTOCOL: COURTEOUS DEMOLITION.” The ground shakes: the GREAT DIGGER unfolds, bucket raised, tracks creaking!
textes.« Bienvenue au Bureau de vente Lisse & F: “Welcome to the Lisse & Son Sales Office! The Lisse-Center: four hundred shops, zero squatters!”
textes.« Bonjour » ! Le classique ! Le meilleur: “Hello”! The classic! The best! A parrot that says hello is a house that smiles! You're a good sort, you are, it shows.
textes.« Bruits de pluie, face A et face B »: “Rain Sounds, Side A and Side B”
textes.« Cent ans que la ronce m'étouffait. Cen: “A hundred years the bramble choked me. A hundred years without a seed. You gave me back my breath, little traveller.” The spirit opens its hands of light: a golden seed, veined with fire, rests there. “Take it to the fairies. In a thousand years, it will be a world.” A circle of light appears on the Crown: it will take you back to the glade.
textes.« Chaque île boit à mes racines. Prends: “Every island drinks from my roots. Take care of them, and they will take care of you.”
textes.« Chère maison, je te quitte pour une pl: “Dear house, I'm leaving you for a bigger one. It's not you, it's me. Well, mostly it's the mice.”
textes.« Crr… » fait le coffre en se léchant le: “Grr…” says the chest, licking its chops. The Great Book had warned you.
textes.« Des daurades d'hier ! » Paulo l'a dit: “Day-old sea bream!” Paulo said it to Lola, and Lola said it to the whole quay. Me, Rosalie, three generations of stallholders! Since then, I have dinner at his place every evening, at the middle table. I eat slowly, I look at him, and I say “Delicious”. He doesn't know where to put himself. That's my revenge. It's very tasty.
textes.« Dors, petit marteau, dors, / la forge: “Sleep, little hammer, sleep, / the forge still keeps its watch, / the stone keeps you warm, / sleep, little hammer.”
textes.« Débarqué de la mer » : votre titre est: “Landed from the sea”: your headline is ready! It's waiting for a photo. Are you free tomorrow?
textes.« Débarqué de la mer, un jeune aventurie: “Landed from the sea, a young adventurer turns the archipelago upside down!” No: “Archipelago can't believe it!” Too long. I'll find it. Your arrival is a real front page.

textes.« Entre, entre ! » Quelqu'un verse du th: “Come in, come in!” Someone pours tea from very high up, without spilling a drop.
textes.« Et c'est l'histoire d'un caillou… » To: “And so there's this pebble…” The whole room bursts out laughing before the end.
textes.« Et la Tortue, la dernière, porta les A: “And the Turtle, the last, carried the Elders to the shore. When the four speak in this order, the stone listens.”
textes.« Gros-Louis prend le large » ! Ça te va: “Gros-Louis takes to the open sea”! Will that do?
textes.« Halte-là ! » … Ah non, c'est juste une: “Halt!” … Oh no, it's just armor on a dummy. Its knight is right next to it.
textes.« Ici a vécu Gaspard, inventeur de la so: “Gaspard lived here, inventor of the hot cold soup. He went to let the king taste it. He never came back. Neither did the king, by the way.”
textes.« Ici les Anciens ont enchaîné Nâga, le:
"Here the Ancients chained Nâga, the Serpent of the Abyss.
Three guardians, three eyes, one amulet:
